The speaker uses an outdoor-gear e-commerce site as a running example, walking from asset prep all the way to production optimization.

For assets, the recommended approach is **Capture, Convert, Create**: scan real objects with iPhone, convert existing files, or build from scratch in tools like Blender; you can also use generative AI apps such as Tripo3D and Meshy.ai to produce a model from photos or a text prompt. Export to **USDZ**, which packages geometry, materials, textures, and animations into a single file. To embed, point at a file with the `src` attribute or a `` child with a MIME type, and place an `` inside `` as a fallback for older browsers; use the **ready promise** to show a spinner until loaded and handle failures in catch; for browsers without native support, load a **polyfill** (though features like visionOS stereoscopic rendering cannot be polyfilled).

For interaction, the simplest path is **`stagemode="orbit"`**, a single attribute that lets users freely rotate the model, spring back when released, and rescale to avoid clipping. For precise control, use the **`entityTransform`** property with `DOMMatrix.rotateSelf` (after disabling orbit), and animate transitions smoothly with `requestAnimationFrame` plus easing; baked-in animations are driven with `play()` and `playbackRate` (a negative value reverses). Finally, wrap `<model>` in an `<a rel="ar">` to enable **AR Quick Look**. Before shipping, compress files with the built-in **usdcrush** (the example drops from 7.9 MB to 1.9 MB with no quality loss) and batch-generate thumbnails with **usdrecord**; both tools ship with macOS.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Safari engineer Aleksei opens by noting the **Model element** debuted on visionOS and now expands to **iOS, iPadOS, and macOS**, with the same markup and element working everywhere. Unlike the existing `model-viewer` JavaScript library, `<model>` is native, rendered directly by the platform, requires no extra library, and is an emerging W3C web standard. He frames the talk with an outdoor-gear e-commerce site, organized into asset prep, building features one at a time, and production optimization.

deepdive_en.title: Prepare the USDZ model asset
deepdive_en.body: The recommended path for getting 3D assets is **Capture, Convert, Create**: scan with iPhone, convert files, or build in Blender, plus generative AI apps like Tripo3D and Meshy.ai that turn photos or text prompts into models. The speaker generates a usable camping mallet model from a few photos in minutes and exports **USDZ**, a zipped Universal Scene Description that packages geometry, materials, textures, and animations into one file and is the recommended format.

deepdive_en.title: Loading and fallbacks
deepdive_en.body: This section previews how to embed a model, know when it's ready to display, and handle fallbacks. The speaker will cover loading, image fallback, the ready promise, and polyfills in turn.

deepdive_en.title: Load a model
deepdive_en.body: Like ``, you point the element at a file with the **`src` attribute** and the browser handles the rest with no plugins; you can also use a `` child with `type="model/vnd.usdz+zip"`. This mirrors the familiar image and video tag patterns, keeping the learning curve low.

deepdive_en.title: Image fallback
deepdive_en.body: The simplest fallback is placing an **`` inside the `` element**: older Safari versions and browsers that don't support Model element render the image instead, so visitors still get a sense of the product. This continues HTML's progressive-enhancement tradition.

deepdive_en.title: Ready promise
deepdive_en.body: 3D models can be tens of megabytes and take time to load, so the **`model.ready`** promise resolves once the model is actually loaded and ready to display. In practice show a spinner while loading, hide it on resolve, and in the **catch** block show fallback content if something unexpected happens.

deepdive_en.title: Polyfill fallback
deepdive_en.body: A **polyfill** retrofits a new standard's API via JavaScript so features work even before native support lands; the W3C Model element samples load the polyfill library when the native element isn't defined on `window`. The speaker cautions you to test both the polyfill and the native element, and notes some features (like Apple Vision Pro stereoscopic display) can't be polyfilled.

deepdive_en.title: Model background
deepdive_en.body: The Model element renders in its own virtual space, so it won't pick up the page's background.

deepdive_en.title: Model background
deepdive_en.body: To match your page design, set **`background-color`** directly on the `model` via CSS. Note the background is always rendered opaque, so even a color with transparency gets converted to opaque.

deepdive_en.title: Stage mode
deepdive_en.body: **`stagemode="orbit"`** lets visitors freely rotate the model side to side, with a gentle spring back to the original angle when tilted up or down, staying interactive while always looking its best. The attribute also rescales the model slightly to ensure no parts get clipped during rotation.

deepdive_en.title: Interactions
deepdive_en.body: This section frames letting visitors interact with and explore the model as a natural next step, previewing custom transforms and animation playback.

deepdive_en.title: Custom transforms
deepdive_en.body: The **`entityTransform`** property sets exact viewing angles via JavaScript; the speaker adds "Side" and "Reset" buttons to demonstrate. You must first disable orbit (remove `stagemode` or set it to `none`), and watch for clipping or disappearance when rotating, adjusting position if needed. The implementation creates a **`DOMMatrix`** and calls `rotateSelf` (the example rotates 135 degrees around Y for a side view), assigns it to `model.entityTransform`, and captures the initial transform up front to reset.

deepdive_en.title: Transition animation
deepdive_en.body: Switching transforms directly snaps instantly, so to make the transition smooth you animate the rotation with **`requestAnimationFrame`**. First set up state: the current angle, the animation duration (500 ms in the example, snappy yet smooth), and a reference to cancel any in-flight animation.

deepdive_en.title: Transition animation
deepdive_en.body: The `animateTo` function first cancels any running animation to avoid conflicts, captures the starting angle and start time, then a step function computes progress each frame, eases the rotation (cubic ease-out in the example), and updates `entityTransform` with a new `DOMMatrix`, requesting the next frame until done. Finally the buttons call animateTo: side view animates to 135 degrees, reset to 0, smoothly rotating and gliding back.

deepdive_en.title: Animation playback
deepdive_en.body: Models can also play built-in animations, typically authored in tools like Blender or Maya and baked into the USDZ file.

deepdive_en.title: Animation playback
deepdive_en.body: The Model element plays the first animation track, and a couple of lines of JavaScript control **`playbackRate`**, with a negative value running it in reverse. The speaker implements a `play` function that sets playbackRate then calls `play()`, using 5 and -5 for faster forward and reverse playback.

deepdive_en.title: AR and spatial
deepdive_en.body: This section brings models into the real environment and spatial computing, previewing AR Quick Look and the visionOS experience.

deepdive_en.title: AR Quick Look
deepdive_en.body: Wrap `<model>` in an `<a>` tag with **`rel="ar"`** pointing at the same resource, and on iOS and iPadOS customers get a full **AR Quick Look** experience. On **visionOS**, stereoscopic rendering gives models real depth so customers can pull the product out of the page to examine it; visionOS also supports immersive website environments, covered in the "Explore immersive website environments" session.

deepdive_en.title: Optimize assets for production
deepdive_en.body: Before shipping, run the command-line tool **usdcrush**, which in the example shrinks the boot model from 7.9 MB to 1.9 MB with no quality change, looking identical side by side in Safari. If you have a 3D file but no image, **usdrecord** generates a thumbnail or fallback image directly (with options like output format or a custom camera) and can be scripted across an entire catalog. Both tools ship with macOS as part of a larger USD tool suite, detailed in WWDC24's "What's new in USD and MaterialX."

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Action items: create your own 3D model from a text prompt or existing photos, add `<model>` pointing at a USDZ file, optimize assets with the USD tools, and try it across platforms to see how the element adapts. The team is actively advancing the Model spec at the **W3C** and encourages developers to join the Immersive Web Community Group with feedback and use cases, plus review "Immersive website environments" and WWDC25's "What's new for the spatial web."

title: Create web extensions for Safari
gloss: 為 Safari 建立 Web 擴充功能
takeaway: 從零打造一個 Safari Web 擴充功能，涵蓋 manifest、內容封鎖、修改網頁、儲存資料、打包發佈，並透過 native messaging 與 App 溝通。
chapters: Adding custom UI to your extension
Including the UI in the extension manifest
Wiring up the static declarativeNetRequest rules
Handling adding hosts to the settings
Declaring optional host permissions for all sites
Adding storage permission to the web extension manifest.json
Package your web extension into an app for Xcode

points.text: 可以**不需 Xcode**，直接從 manifest.json 開始建立並測試 Safari Web 擴充功能。
透過 **declarativeNetRequest** 權限可封鎖、修改與重新導向網路請求，並支援動態規則。
使用 **content scripts** 搭配 **scripting** 權限可動態註冊腳本以修改網頁內容。
以 **storage** API 持久化設定，並用 **background script** 在更新時還原狀態。
打包成 App 後可透過 **nativeMessaging** 與原生程式溝通，例如以 LocalAuthentication 做生物辨識驗證。

audience: 適合**想開發或移植 Safari Web 擴充功能的網頁與 App 開發者**，特別是初次接觸者。
gloss_en: Create web extensions for Safari
takeaway_en: Build a Safari web extension from scratch, covering the manifest, content blocking, modifying pages, storing data, packaging for distribution, and communicating with an app via native messaging.

points_en.text: You can build and test Safari web extensions starting straight from manifest.json, **without Xcode**.
The **declarativeNetRequest** permission lets you block, modify, and redirect network requests, with support for dynamic rules.
Use **content scripts** together with the **scripting** permission to dynamically register scripts that modify page content.
Persist settings with the **storage** API, and use a **background script** to restore state on update.
Once packaged into an app, the extension can communicate with native code via **nativeMessaging**, for example using LocalAuthentication for biometric authentication.

audience_en: For **web and app developers who want to build or port Safari web extensions**, especially first-timers.
summary: Safari 團隊工程師 Kiara 帶領從零打造一個 **Safari web extension**，並完整走過開發、測試與發佈流程——而且不需要 Xcode、甚至不需要 Mac。核心訊息是：web extension 本質上就是 HTML、CSS 與 JavaScript，且 Apple 正與 W3C **WebExtensions** 工作組推動跨瀏覽器標準化，因此為其他瀏覽器寫的擴充功能能直接帶到 Safari。她實作的範例「Shiny OnTrack」可封鎖讓人分心的網站，提供允許瀏覽 10 分鐘的 **Light mode** 與一進站就轉址的 **Full mode**。

開發從 **manifest.json**（擴充功能的「身分證」，含 name、description、version）起步，加入 SVG 圖示與 UI——可用 action button 的 popup，本例改用完整的 **options page** 來顯示封鎖清單。內容封鎖靠 **declarativeNetRequest** API：先在 manifest 宣告權限，再以 ID／priority／action／condition 定義規則，本例因事先不知封鎖哪些站而採**動態規則**（`updateDynamicRules`）。要把錯誤頁換成自訂頁面則用 **redirect rule**，並改用 `declarativeNetRequestWithHostAccess` 搭配 **optional host permissions**，在執行時以 `permissions.request` 向使用者請求單一網站存取——權限模型以使用者隱私為核心。Light mode 的 10 分鐘倒數計時則透過**動態註冊的 content scripts**（`scripting.registerContentScripts`）注入頁面。

為了讓資料在重新載入後仍存在，改用 **storage** API 的 local storage 把封鎖清單與模式寫入磁碟；又因註冊的 content scripts 不會跨擴充功能更新存活，加入 **background page** 監聽 `onInstalled` 事件，在更新後從 storage 重讀並重新註冊。發佈方面，**App Store Connect** 的 **Safari Web Extension Packager** 可在任何瀏覽器上把資源打包成內含 app，再透過 **TestFlight** 發測試版、最終送審上架。最後示範以 **native messaging** 讓擴充功能與內含 app 協作：擴充功能送訊息給 App Extension，由原生 app 用 **LocalAuthentication**（`LAContext.evaluatePolicy`）要求 Touch ID／Face ID 生物辨識後回傳結果，藉此保護擴充功能的設定。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: Safari 團隊工程師 Kiara 開場，說明 **web extension** 就是 HTML／CSS／JavaScript，且 Apple 與 W3C 工作組推動跨瀏覽器標準化，讓既有擴充功能可帶到 Safari。她將從零打造一個封鎖分心網站的擴充功能（含 Light 與 Full 兩種模式），並涵蓋打包發佈與和內含 app 協作。

deepdive.title: Get started
deepdive.body: 建議先下載本場 sample code project 跟著做。開始時在編輯器（Xcode 或任何編輯器皆可）建立一個資料夾來放擴充功能的所有檔案。

deepdive.title: Manifest file
deepdive.body: 每個擴充功能都需要 **manifest** 檔——JSON 格式，像擴充功能的「身分證」，包含 name、description、version 等資訊，告訴瀏覽器這個擴充功能是什麼、能做什麼。

deepdive.title: Adding an extension icon
deepdive.body: 新增 images 資料夾放圖示，並在 manifest 的 `icons` 指定。本例用 **SVG**，Safari 會完美處理縮放，使其在工具列或 Extensions Settings 等不同位置都正確顯示。

deepdive.title: Adding an action button
deepdive.body: 多數擴充功能需要 UI。一種方式是 **action button**：在 manifest 用 `action.default_popup` 指定 popup.html，點擊工具列按鈕時 Safari 會顯示該 popup。

deepdive.title: Adding custom UI to your extension
deepdive.body: 因為封鎖清單放在 popup 會顯得擁擠，改用擴充功能的 **options page**——一個完整頁面讓使用者設定擴充功能。

deepdive.title: Including the UI in the extension manifest
deepdive.body: 在 manifest 用 `options_ui.page`（後續改為 `options_page`）指定 options 頁面的 HTML 檔，Safari 便知道如何使用該資源。

deepdive.title: Hello World
deepdive.body: 先用最簡單的 Hello World 頁面測試。在 Safari 的 Advanced 設定勾選「Show features for web developers」啟用開發者面板，允許未簽章擴充功能後選取資料夾即可載入；重新載入後出現 Settings 按鈕並開啟 options 頁面。

deepdive.title: Block content
deepdive.body: 進入封鎖內容的核心——使用 **declarativeNetRequest** API，讓擴充功能能封鎖、修改或轉址網路請求，這正是過濾廣告與追蹤器的能力來源。

deepdive.title: Adding declarativeNetRequest permission
deepdive.body: 權限是擴充功能向 Safari 宣告所需存取的方式。要使用內容封鎖，需在 manifest 的 `permissions` 加入 **declarativeNetRequest**。

deepdive.title: Blocking network requests
deepdive.body: 一條規則包含 ID、priority、action 型別與符合條件。範例規則以 `urlFilter: "||webkit.org"` 與 `action.type: "block"` 封鎖對 webkit.org 的所有導覽。

deepdive.title: Modifying network requests
deepdive.body: 規則有兩種定義方式：在 manifest 內定義的**靜態規則**（已知規則時很合適），以及執行時用 JavaScript 加入的**動態規則**。本例因事先不知要封鎖哪些站，採動態方式。

deepdive.title: Updating dynamic rules
deepdive.body: 用 `browser.declarativeNetRequest.updateDynamicRules({ addRules: [...] })` 在執行時加入規則。把這段邏輯放在 utilities 資料夾的 rules.js。

deepdive.title: Wiring up the static declarativeNetRequest rules
deepdive.body: 在 rules.js 中加入 helper 把 host 映射成唯一整數 ID（`hostToRuleID`），再以 ID、type 為 block、`urlFilter` 比對 host 建立規則，並透過 `updateDynamicRules` 加入。

deepdive.title: Adding block rules dynamically
deepdive.body: 在 host.js 的 `addHost` 中，當使用者把網站加入清單且為 full 模式時建立封鎖規則。在 Safari 重新載入後把 webkit.org 加入清單，前往該站即被封鎖。

deepdive.title: Handling adding hosts to the settings
deepdive.body: 示範把網站加入封鎖清單後的封鎖效果，但內建錯誤頁不理想，於是改用轉址規則導向自訂頁面，引出下一段的 redirect。

deepdive.title: Redirecting network requests
deepdive.body: **redirect rule** 與 block rule 類似，但 `action.type` 為 redirect，並以 `extensionPath` 指定使用者導向的自訂頁面（如 /blocked.html）。

deepdive.title: Declaring optional host permissions
deepdive.body: 封鎖請求不需頁面存取，但**轉址需要**。因此改用 `declarativeNetRequestWithHostAccess` 權限，並以 **optional host permissions** 在執行時才請求網站存取。

deepdive.title: Declaring optional host permissions for all sites
deepdive.body: host permissions 由 scheme、host、path 組成的 match pattern 陣列定義。因任何站都可能被加入，採用可比對所有 URL 的 `*://*/*` 模式。Safari 的權限模型以使用者隱私為核心，由使用者決定授權哪些站。

deepdive.title: Add the redirect rule
deepdive.body: 在 rules.js 建立 redirect 規則，type 為 redirect 並帶自訂頁面路徑；資源頁面放進擴充功能資料夾。如此不再封鎖導覽，而是轉址到自訂頁面。

deepdive.title: Dynamically ask for host permissions
deepdive.body: 用 `browser.permissions.request` 在執行時向使用者請求網域與子網域的存取。在 Safari 加入 webkit.org 時會先跳出授權提示，允許並重新整理後導覽即被轉址到自訂頁面。

deepdive.title: Modify webpages
deepdive.body: 為實作 Light mode 允許瀏覽 10 分鐘並顯示倒數，需要把內容直接注入頁面，這正是 **content scripts** 的用途。

deepdive.title: Defining content scripts
deepdive.body: content scripts 讓擴充功能能讀取與修改網頁內容。可在 manifest 以檔案與 match pattern **靜態**宣告（已知目標站時合適），本例因事先未知改採動態。

deepdive.title: Dynamically registering content scripts
deepdive.body: 用 registered content scripts API 動態註冊，運作如靜態 script 但多了 ID 與 persistence flag；將 flag 設為 true 可讓 script 在 Safari 重啟後仍存在。

deepdive.title: Adding the scripting permission
deepdive.body: 要使用此 API，需在 manifest 加入 **scripting** 權限，並在 utilities 新增 scripting.js。

deepdive.title: Registering content scripts
deepdive.body: 在 scripting.js 定義 content script（ID、計時器的 js、樣式 css、涵蓋網域與子網域的 match pattern、`persistAcrossSessions: true`），再以 `browser.scripting.registerContentScripts` 註冊。

deepdive.title: Adding a host
deepdive.body: 在 `addHost` 中，當使用者加入網站時為其註冊顯示計時器的 content script；full 模式下轉址會在頁面載入前觸發，故總是可註冊。Light 模式下加入 webkit.org 後前往該站，頁面上會顯示 10 分鐘計時器。

deepdive.title: Web extensions storage APIs
deepdive.body: 目前資料存在記憶體中，重新載入即遺失，故改用 **storage** API。Safari 支援 session storage（適合不需跨重啟的暫存）與 local storage（寫入磁碟），封鎖清單需保留故選 local。

deepdive.title: Adding storage permission to the web extension manifest.json
deepdive.body: 要使用 storage API，需在 manifest 的 `permissions` 加入 **storage**。

deepdive.title: Saving data with storage
deepdive.body: 在 utilities 新增 storage.js，定義更新／取得 hosts 與儲存／取得 block mode 的 helper（`browser.storage.local.set`／`get`）。

deepdive.title: Persisting hosts to storage
deepdive.body: 在 `addHost` 中，使用者加入新站時更新 storage 內的 hosts 清單，讓封鎖清單之後總能完整呈現所有已加入的站。

deepdive.title: Reading from storage
deepdive.body: 在 options.js 啟動時從 storage 讀取既有 hosts 與 block mode，並用以渲染封鎖清單。

deepdive.title: Switching block modes
deepdive.body: 切換模式時將變更存入 storage；若為 full 模式則為所有站建立轉址規則，否則移除所有規則。改成 Full 並加站後重新載入，變更仍在。

deepdive.title: Adding a background script
deepdive.body: 註冊的 content scripts 能跨 Safari 重啟，但**不跨擴充功能更新**。因此需要 background page 或 service worker 來得知更新；講者偏好可存取 DOM 的 background page，在 manifest 以 `background.scripts` 指定。

deepdive.title: Background script
deepdive.body: 在 background.js 註冊 `runtime.onInstalled` 事件，當偵測到更新（reason 為 update）時從 storage 讀取 hosts 並重新註冊 content scripts，修復更新後遺失 script 的問題。

deepdive.title: Package and distribute
deepdive.body: 可用 **App Store Connect** 上傳、送審與管理擴充功能，且能在任何瀏覽器上進行、無需 Mac。它會替你建立內含 app，再用 **Safari Web Extension Packager** 上傳資源並在數分鐘內完成打包。

deepdive.title: Communicate with your app
deepdive.body: 標準 WebExtension API 之外，擴充功能還能透過 **native messaging** 取用平台原生功能，讓擴充功能與內含 app 協作。

deepdive.title: Package your web extension into an app for Xcode
deepdive.body: 在 Terminal 執行 `xcrun safari-web-extension-packager --copy-resources` 會建立並開啟一個含 app 與 web extension 的 Xcode 專案，供後續收發訊息。

deepdive.title: Adding the nativeMessaging permission
deepdive.body: 要使用 native messaging，需在擴充功能 manifest 的 `permissions` 加入 **nativeMessaging**。

deepdive.title: Sending a native message
deepdive.body: 在 background page 用 `browser.runtime.sendNativeMessage` 送出訊息（例如 requestBioAuth），回傳結果會告知驗證是否成功。

deepdive.title: Handling native messages
deepdive.body: 在 packager 產生的 **SafariWebExtensionHandler** 中解析訊息的 requestBioAuth key，再以 **LocalAuthentication** 的 `LAContext.evaluatePolicy(.deviceOwnerAuthenticationWithBiometrics)` 請求生物辨識。

deepdive.title: Replying to a native message
deepdive.body: 驗證完成後，原生 app 透過 `reply` 把含 success 結果的 `NSExtensionItem` 以 `context.completeRequest` 回傳給擴充功能。在 Safari 加入網站前會先要求 Touch ID 驗證，通過後才加入清單。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 總結整個從零打造到發佈的流程，鼓勵下載 sample code 把玩 API，到 MDN 查閱跨瀏覽器文件，並透過 Feedback Assistant 或 bugs.webkit.org 回報問題。

summary_en: Safari engineer Kiara builds a **Safari web extension** from the ground up and walks through development, testing, and distribution — with no Xcode and not even a Mac required. The core message: web extensions are just HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, and Apple is standardizing across browsers through the W3C **WebExtensions** group, so an extension built for another browser can come straight to Safari. Her sample, "Shiny OnTrack," blocks distracting sites with a **Light mode** that allows 10 minutes of browsing and a **Full mode** that redirects the moment you navigate there.

Development starts with the **manifest.json** (the extension's "ID card" with name, description, version), then adds an SVG icon and UI — either an action button popup or, as here, a full **options page** to show the blocklist. Content blocking uses the **declarativeNetRequest** API: declare the permission, then define rules with ID/priority/action/condition. Since the sites aren't known up front, the example uses **dynamic rules** (`updateDynamicRules`). To replace the error page with a custom one, it switches to a **redirect rule** and to `declarativeNetRequestWithHostAccess` with **optional host permissions**, requesting per-site access at runtime via `permissions.request` — a permission model built around user privacy. The Light-mode 10-minute countdown is injected via **dynamically registered content scripts** (`scripting.registerContentScripts`).

To survive reloads, the extension moves data into local **storage** so the blocklist and mode persist to disk; and because registered content scripts don't survive extension updates, a **background page** listens for `onInstalled` to re-read storage and re-register scripts after an update. For distribution, **App Store Connect**'s **Safari Web Extension Packager** packages resources into a containing app from any browser, then **TestFlight** distributes betas before App Store submission. Finally, **native messaging** lets the extension collaborate with its containing app: the extension sends a message that the native app handles with **LocalAuthentication** (`LAContext.evaluatePolicy`) to require Face ID/Touch ID before changes, protecting the extension's settings.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Safari engineer Kiara opens, noting that a **web extension** is just HTML/CSS/JavaScript and that Apple and the W3C group are standardizing across browsers, so existing extensions can come to Safari. She'll build a distraction-blocking extension (Light and Full modes) and cover packaging, distribution, and collaborating with a containing app.

deepdive_en.title: Get started
deepdive_en.body: Recommends downloading the session's sample code project to follow along. To begin, create a folder in your editor (Xcode or any editor) to hold all the extension's files.

deepdive_en.title: Manifest file
deepdive_en.body: Every extension needs a **manifest** file — JSON-formatted, like an ID card — containing the name, description, and version, telling the browser what the extension is and what it can do.

deepdive_en.title: Adding an extension icon
deepdive_en.body: Add an images folder for the icon and reference it via `icons` in the manifest. The example uses an **SVG**; Safari handles scaling perfectly so it shows correctly in the toolbar, Extensions Settings, and elsewhere.

deepdive_en.title: Adding an action button
deepdive_en.body: Most extensions need UI. One option is an **action button**: in the manifest, set `action.default_popup` to popup.html so Safari shows the popup when the toolbar button is clicked.

deepdive_en.title: Adding custom UI to your extension
deepdive_en.body: Because a blocklist would look cramped in a popup, the extension uses an **options page** instead — a full page where users configure settings.

deepdive_en.title: Including the UI in the extension manifest
deepdive_en.body: Specify the options page HTML via `options_ui.page` (later `options_page`) in the manifest so Safari knows how to use the resource.

deepdive_en.title: Hello World
deepdive_en.body: Test with a simple Hello World page first. In Safari's Advanced settings, check "Show features for web developers" to enable the developer pane, allow unsigned extensions, then select the folder to load it; after reloading, a Settings button appears and opens the options page.

deepdive_en.title: Block content
deepdive_en.body: Gets into the core of content blocking using the **declarativeNetRequest** API, which lets the extension block, modify, or redirect network requests — the power behind ad and tracker filtering.

deepdive_en.title: Adding declarativeNetRequest permission
deepdive_en.body: Permissions are how an extension tells Safari what it needs. To block content, add the **declarativeNetRequest** permission to the manifest's `permissions`.

deepdive_en.title: Blocking network requests
deepdive_en.body: A rule has an ID, priority, action type, and condition. The example rule blocks all navigations to webkit.org using `urlFilter: "||webkit.org"` and `action.type: "block"`.

deepdive_en.title: Modifying network requests
deepdive_en.body: Rules can be defined two ways: **static rules** in the manifest (good when rules are known) and **dynamic rules** added at runtime via JavaScript. Since the sites aren't known up front, the example goes dynamic.

deepdive_en.title: Updating dynamic rules
deepdive_en.body: Use `browser.declarativeNetRequest.updateDynamicRules({ addRules: [...] })` to add rules at runtime, placing this logic in rules.js inside a utilities folder.

deepdive_en.title: Wiring up the static declarativeNetRequest rules
deepdive_en.body: In rules.js, a helper maps the host to a unique integer ID (`hostToRuleID`), then builds a rule with that ID, type block, and a `urlFilter` matching the host, added via `updateDynamicRules`.

deepdive_en.title: Adding block rules dynamically
deepdive_en.body: In host.js's `addHost`, create the block rule when a user adds a site in full mode. After reloading in Safari and adding webkit.org, navigating there is blocked.

deepdive_en.title: Handling adding hosts to the settings
deepdive_en.body: Shows the blocking effect after adding a site, but the built-in error page isn't ideal, motivating a switch to redirect rules pointing at a custom page.

deepdive_en.title: Redirecting network requests
deepdive_en.body: A **redirect rule** resembles a block rule but with `action.type` of redirect and an `extensionPath` specifying the custom page (e.g. /blocked.html) the user lands on.

deepdive_en.title: Declaring optional host permissions
deepdive_en.body: Blocking requests doesn't need page access, but **redirecting does**. So the manifest switches to `declarativeNetRequestWithHostAccess` and uses **optional host permissions** to request site access at runtime.

deepdive_en.title: Declaring optional host permissions for all sites
deepdive_en.body: Host permissions are an array of match patterns (scheme, host, path). Since any site might be added, the example uses `*://*/*` to match all URLs. Safari's permission model centers on user privacy — the user decides which sites to grant.

deepdive_en.title: Add the redirect rule
deepdive_en.body: Create the redirect rule in rules.js with type redirect and the custom page path, with the page resources in the extension folder. Now navigations are redirected rather than blocked.

deepdive_en.title: Dynamically ask for host permissions
deepdive_en.body: Use `browser.permissions.request` to ask the user for access to the domain and subdomains at runtime. Adding webkit.org in Safari now prompts for access; allowing and refreshing redirects the navigation to the custom page.

deepdive_en.title: Modify webpages
deepdive_en.body: To implement Light mode's 10-minute browsing with a countdown, content must be injected directly into the page — the job of **content scripts**.

deepdive_en.title: Defining content scripts
deepdive_en.body: Content scripts let an extension read and modify page content. They can be declared **statically** in the manifest with files and match patterns (good for known sites); the example goes dynamic since sites aren't known up front.

deepdive_en.title: Dynamically registering content scripts
deepdive_en.body: Use the registered content scripts API to register dynamically; it works like static scripts but adds an ID and persistence flag — set the flag to true so scripts survive Safari restarts.

deepdive_en.title: Adding the scripting permission
deepdive_en.body: To use this API, add the **scripting** permission to the manifest and create scripting.js in utilities.

deepdive_en.title: Registering content scripts
deepdive_en.body: In scripting.js, define the content script (ID, the timer's js, styling css, match patterns covering the domain and subdomains, `persistAcrossSessions: true`), then register it with `browser.scripting.registerContentScripts`.

deepdive_en.title: Adding a host
deepdive_en.body: In `addHost`, register a timer content script when a user adds a site; in full mode the redirect fires before the page loads, so scripts can always be registered. In Light mode, adding webkit.org and visiting shows a 10-minute timer on the page.

deepdive_en.title: Web extensions storage APIs
deepdive_en.body: Data currently lives in memory and is lost on reload, so the extension moves to the **storage** API. Safari supports session storage (for transient data) and local storage (written to disk); the blocklist needs to persist, so local is the right call.

deepdive_en.title: Adding storage permission to the web extension manifest.json
deepdive_en.body: To use the storage API, add the **storage** permission to the manifest's `permissions`.

deepdive_en.title: Saving data with storage
deepdive_en.body: Add storage.js in utilities defining helpers to update/get hosts and save/get the block mode using `browser.storage.local.set`/`get`.

deepdive_en.title: Persisting hosts to storage
deepdive_en.body: In `addHost`, update the stored hosts list when a user adds a new site, so the blocklist always renders the full set of added sites afterward.

deepdive_en.title: Reading from storage
deepdive_en.body: In options.js at startup, read the existing hosts and block mode from storage and use them to render the blocklist.

deepdive_en.title: Switching block modes
deepdive_en.body: When switching modes, save the change to storage; if full mode, create redirect rules for all sites, otherwise remove all rules. After switching to Full, adding a site, and reloading, the changes persist.

deepdive_en.title: Adding a background script
deepdive_en.body: Registered content scripts survive Safari restarts but **not extension updates**. So a background page or service worker is needed to detect updates; the speaker prefers a background page (DOM access), specified via `background.scripts` in the manifest.

deepdive_en.title: Background script
deepdive_en.body: In background.js, register the `runtime.onInstalled` event; when an update is detected (reason update), read hosts from storage and re-register content scripts, fixing the lost-script problem after updates.

deepdive_en.title: Package and distribute
deepdive_en.body: Use **App Store Connect** to upload, submit, and manage the extension — from any browser, no Mac required. It creates the containing app for you, then the **Safari Web Extension Packager** uploads resources and packages the extension in minutes.

deepdive_en.title: Communicate with your app
deepdive_en.body: Beyond standard WebExtension APIs, the extension can reach native platform features via **native messaging**, letting the extension and its containing app work together.

deepdive_en.title: Package your web extension into an app for Xcode
deepdive_en.body: Running `xcrun safari-web-extension-packager --copy-resources` in Terminal creates and launches an Xcode project containing the app and web extension, ready to send and receive messages.

deepdive_en.title: Adding the nativeMessaging permission
deepdive_en.body: To use native messaging, add the **nativeMessaging** permission to the extension's manifest `permissions`.

deepdive_en.title: Sending a native message
deepdive_en.body: In the background page, send a message (e.g. requestBioAuth) with `browser.runtime.sendNativeMessage`; the reply indicates whether authentication succeeded.

deepdive_en.title: Handling native messages
deepdive_en.body: In the packager-generated **SafariWebExtensionHandler**, parse the message's requestBioAuth key, then request biometrics via **LocalAuthentication**'s `LAContext.evaluatePolicy(.deviceOwnerAuthenticationWithBiometrics)`.

deepdive_en.title: Replying to a native message
deepdive_en.body: After authentication, the native app replies via `reply`, returning an `NSExtensionItem` with the success result through `context.completeRequest`. In Safari, adding a site now prompts for Touch ID first, and only adds it after passing.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Wraps up the full build-to-distribution journey, encouraging downloading the sample code to explore the APIs, consulting cross-browser docs on MDN, and filing feedback via Feedback Assistant or bugs.webkit.org.

title: Enhance the accessibility of your reading app
gloss: 強化你閱讀類 App 的無障礙體驗
takeaway: 運用文字導覽 API、連結群組與自訂 UITextInput，為 VoiceOver 與 Speak Screen 打造順暢、可選取且能自動翻頁的閱讀體驗。
chapters: Link text elements together with navigation APIs
Link text elements together with a linked group
Add actions to the editor rotor

points.text: 為 **VoiceOver**、**Speak Screen** 等輔助技術打造穩固的閱讀體驗，提供直覺的文字選取。
用 **accessibilityNextTextNavigationElement**／**accessibilityPreviousTextNavigationElement** 把段落串連，讓導覽依閱讀順序前後移動。
以 **accessibilityLinkedGroup** 在 SwiftUI 中把同一頁的文字元素群組起來。
插入 **causesPageTurn** 特徵並回應 **accessibilityScroll**，朗讀完畢後自動翻頁。
為自訂文字（如掃描頁面）採用 **UITextInput**，讓輔助技術能正確選取與讀取內容。

audience: **開發閱讀、文件或電子書類 App 的 UIKit／SwiftUI 工程師**，想完善無障礙閱讀體驗的人。
gloss_en: Enhance the accessibility of your reading app
takeaway_en: Use text navigation APIs, linked groups, and custom UITextInput to build a smooth, selectable reading experience with automatic page turns for VoiceOver and Speak Screen.

points_en.text: Build robust reading experiences for assistive technologies like **VoiceOver** and **Speak Screen**, with intuitive text selection.
Use **accessibilityNextTextNavigationElement**/**accessibilityPreviousTextNavigationElement** to chain paragraphs so navigation moves forward and backward in reading order.
Use **accessibilityLinkedGroup** in SwiftUI to group the text elements on a single page together.
Add the **causesPageTurn** trait and respond to **accessibilityScroll** to turn the page automatically once reading finishes.
Adopt **UITextInput** for custom text (such as scanned pages) so assistive technologies can correctly select and read the content.

audience_en: **UIKit/SwiftUI engineers building reading, document, or e-book apps** who want to perfect the accessible reading experience.

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: 由 Accessibility 團隊的 Josh 開場，點出**長篇閱讀內容**與一般 UI 導覽的本質差異：閱讀是在文字間「流暢移動」，而非在控制項之間跳轉。講者以一個 Chicago 旅遊導覽 app 為範例，貫穿全場示範如何讓使用 **VoiceOver** 與 **Speak Screen** 的人也能順暢閱讀。

deepdive.title: Characteristics
deepdive.body: 說明兩種內建輔助技術：**VoiceOver** 是給失明／弱視者的螢幕報讀器，朗讀游標所在處；**Speak Screen** 則從上到下朗讀整頁並同步高亮。講者據此訂出三個目標：**granular text navigation**（逐行／逐字導覽）、**continuous reading**（不被頁面打斷的連續閱讀）、與 **comprehensive text selection**（完整的文字選取）。

deepdive.title: Standard views
deepdive.body: 建議優先採用系統內建、開箱即無障礙的文字 view：UIKit 的 `UITextView`、SwiftUI 開啟 selection 的 `Text` 或 `TextEditor`、AppKit 的 `NSTextView`，它們皆採用較高保真度的 **`UITextInput`** 協定，免費提供逐行／字導覽與選取。講者在旅遊 app 中因版面需求，為每個段落各用一個 `UITextView`。

deepdive.title: Link text elements together with navigation APIs
deepdive.body: 當段落各自是獨立 view 時，VoiceOver 只能在單一段落內逐行移動，跨段落會卡住。iOS 18 的 text navigation API 透過 `accessibilityNextTextNavigationElement` 與 `accessibilityPreviousTextNavigationElement` 互相指向，就能讓游標越過一段落末尾接到下一段開頭。

deepdive.title: Link text elements together with a linked group
deepdive.body: 對 SwiftUI，iOS 27 起可改用 **`accessibilityLinkedGroup`** modifier 取得同樣效果：把多個可選取的 `Text` 用相同 id 與 `@Namespace` 連結即可。macOS 上對應的是 `accessibilitySharedTextUIElements`。

deepdive.title: Turn pages automatically after reading
deepdive.body: 分頁內容若要像有聲書般連續朗讀，需在最後一段套用 **`causesPageTurn`** trait，並實作 `accessibilityScroll`。如此當 Speak Screen 或 VoiceOver 讀到頁尾時會自動翻頁並 post `.pageScrolled` 通知，避免 read all 在頁底停住。

deepdive.title: Add actions to the editor rotor
deepdive.body: 為了讓「儲存選取」這類動作能被 VoiceOver 使用者發現，講者覆寫 `UITextView` 子類的 `accessibilityCustomActions`，建立 `UIAccessibilityCustomAction` 並設定其 `category` 為 edit category，使其出現在 VoiceOver 的 **edit rotor** 中而非一般動作清單。

deepdive.title: Custom text
deepdive.body: 說明何時無法使用標準 view：進階排版、跨 app 共用程式碼、或顯示掃描頁面等。講者把文字 view 換成手寫筆記掃描圖後，失去了 `UITextView` 免費提供的無障礙行為，連朗讀都沒有，引出採用 `UITextInput` 的必要。

deepdive.title: Adopt UITextInput
deepdive.body: 在 accessibility element 上完整實作 **`UITextInput`** 協定，可讓圖片中的文字與標準 view 一樣可逐行觸控探索、rotor 導覽與選取。重點包括在 `selectionRects` 用已知行高行寬計算選取矩形、`text(in:)` 回傳正確子字串、提供（此處子類化 `UITextInputStringTokenizer` 的）tokenizer，並加上 `UITextInteraction` 與回呼 input delegate 來補齊選取視覺。

summary: 這場由 Apple Accessibility 團隊主講，核心訊息是：**長篇閱讀內容**的無障礙體驗，和一般 UI 導覽是兩回事——閱讀重在文字之間流暢移動，而非在控制項間跳轉。講者 Josh 以一個 Chicago 旅遊導覽 app 為範例，鎖定 **VoiceOver** 與 **Speak Screen** 兩種輔助技術，訂出三個目標：逐行的細緻導覽、不被分頁打斷的連續朗讀，以及完整的文字選取。

第一條路是盡量採用系統內建、開箱即無障礙的標準文字 view：iOS 的 `UITextView`、SwiftUI 的 `TextEditor` 或開啟 selection 的 `Text`、macOS 的 `NSTextView`，它們都採用了 **`UITextInput`** 協定。在此基礎上再用 API 補強：跨段落導覽用 iOS 18 的 **text navigation APIs**（`accessibilityNextTextNavigationElement` 系列）或 SwiftUI iOS 27 的 **`accessibilityLinkedGroup`**；分頁連續朗讀靠 **`causesPageTurn`** trait 搭配 `accessibilityScroll` 自動翻頁；要讓選取後的動作（如「Save Recommendation」）被發現，則用帶 edit category 的 `UIAccessibilityCustomAction` 加進 VoiceOver 的 edit rotor。

當 app 必須使用**自訂繪製的文字**（例如進階排版、跨 app 共用程式碼，或顯示掃描頁面）時，會失去標準 view 免費提供的無障礙行為，連最基本的朗讀都沒有。此時應在 accessibility element 上完整實作 **`UITextInput`** 協定：管理文字幾何、在 `selectionRects` 計算選取矩形、在 `text(in:)` 回傳指定範圍的子字串，並提供 tokenizer 處理逐行／句／字導覽。搭配 `UITextInteraction` 再回呼 input delegate，就能補上選取把手與高亮等視覺體驗。

實務上的收尾建議是：開啟 VoiceOver 親自稽核自己的 app，試試 read all 手勢、用 lines rotor 導覽、並做文字選取。用標準 view 的人應採用 `causesPageTurn` 與 text navigation element API 取得跨頁順暢閱讀；用自訂文字的人則應完整採用 `UITextInput`。這些改善也會讓 iOS 26 的 **Accessibility Reader** 一併受惠。
summary_en: Presented by Apple's Accessibility team, the core message is that accessibility for **long-form reading content** is fundamentally different from navigating ordinary UI: reading is about moving fluidly through text, not jumping between controls. Using a Chicago travel-guide app, presenter Josh focuses on two assistive technologies, **VoiceOver** and **Speak Screen**, and sets three goals: granular line-by-line navigation, continuous reading uninterrupted by pagination, and comprehensive text selection.

The first approach is to reach for system text views that are accessible out of the box: `UITextView` on iOS, SwiftUI's `TextEditor` or a `Text` with selection enabled, and `NSTextView` on macOS — all of which adopt the **`UITextInput`** protocol. On top of that, extend with APIs: cross-paragraph navigation via iOS 18's **text navigation APIs** (`accessibilityNextTextNavigationElement` and friends) or SwiftUI's iOS 27 **`accessibilityLinkedGroup`**; continuous read-all across pages via the **`causesPageTurn`** trait paired with `accessibilityScroll`; and surfacing selection actions like "Save Recommendation" through a `UIAccessibilityCustomAction` placed in VoiceOver's edit rotor using the edit category.

When the app must use **custom-rendered text** (for advanced typography, shared code, or scanned pages), it loses the free accessibility that standard views provide — even basic reading. The fix is to fully adopt the **`UITextInput`** protocol on your accessibility elements: manage text geometry, compute selection rectangles in `selectionRects`, return the right substring in `text(in:)`, and supply a tokenizer for line/sentence/word/character navigation. Adding a `UITextInteraction` and calling the input delegate rounds out selection handles and highlights.

The practical takeaway is to audit your app with VoiceOver on — try the read-all gesture, navigate with the lines rotor, and select text. If you use standard views, adopt `causesPageTurn` and the text navigation element APIs for smooth cross-page reading; if you use custom text, adopt `UITextInput` in its entirety. These improvements also benefit iOS 26's **Accessibility Reader**.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Josh from the Accessibility team opens by contrasting **long-form reading content** with ordinary UI navigation: reading is about fluidly moving through text, not jumping between controls. A Chicago travel-guide app serves as the running example for making the experience great for **VoiceOver** and **Speak Screen** users.

deepdive_en.title: Characteristics
deepdive_en.body: Explains the two built-in assistive technologies: **VoiceOver** is the screen reader for blind/low-vision users that reads what the cursor highlights; **Speak Screen** reads the whole page top-to-bottom with synchronized highlighting. From these, three goals are set: **granular text navigation**, **continuous reading**, and **comprehensive text selection**.

deepdive_en.title: Standard views
deepdive_en.body: Recommends reaching first for system text views that are accessible out of the box — UIKit's `UITextView`, SwiftUI's selectable `Text` or `TextEditor`, AppKit's `NSTextView` — all adopting the higher-fidelity **`UITextInput`** protocol. The travel app uses a separate `UITextView` per paragraph due to its layout.

deepdive_en.title: Link text elements together with navigation APIs
deepdive_en.body: Because each paragraph is a separate view, VoiceOver gets stuck navigating line-by-line within one paragraph. iOS 18's text navigation APIs let each element return its next/previous accessible element via `accessibilityNextTextNavigationElement` and `accessibilityPreviousTextNavigationElement`, so the cursor crosses from one paragraph's end to the next paragraph's first line.

deepdive_en.title: Link text elements together with a linked group
deepdive_en.body: For SwiftUI, iOS 27 offers the **`accessibilityLinkedGroup`** modifier for the same effect: link multiple selectable `Text` elements with the same id and `@Namespace`. The AppKit equivalent on Mac is `accessibilitySharedTextUIElements`.

deepdive_en.title: Turn pages automatically after reading
deepdive_en.body: For paginated content to read continuously like an audiobook, apply the **`causesPageTurn`** trait to the last paragraph and implement `accessibilityScroll`. Speak Screen and VoiceOver then auto-advance pages at the end and post a `.pageScrolled` notification, preventing read-all from stopping at the page bottom.

deepdive_en.title: Add actions to the editor rotor
deepdive_en.body: To make a "Save Recommendation" action discoverable, the presenter overrides `accessibilityCustomActions` on a `UITextView` subclass and creates a `UIAccessibilityCustomAction` whose `category` is the edit category, so it appears in VoiceOver's **edit rotor** rather than the generic actions list.

deepdive_en.title: Custom text
deepdive_en.body: Covers when standard views aren't possible: advanced typography, shared code across apps, or displaying scanned pages. Swapping text views for scanned handwriting images loses the free accessibility `UITextView` provided — even basic reading — motivating adoption of `UITextInput`.

deepdive_en.title: Adopt UITextInput
deepdive_en.body: Fully implementing **`UITextInput`** on accessibility elements makes rendered or image text as accessible as a native text view: line touch-exploration, rotor/Speak Screen navigation, and selection. Key pieces include computing selection rectangles in `selectionRects` from known line geometry, returning the right substring in `text(in:)`, providing a tokenizer (here a `UITextInputStringTokenizer` subclass), and adding a `UITextInteraction` plus input-delegate callbacks for selection visuals.

title: Refine accessibility for custom controls
gloss: 為自訂控制項優化無障礙體驗
takeaway: 為自訂控制項補上 label、value、可調整特性與自訂動作，能讓 VoiceOver 使用者完整操作你的互動元件。
chapters: Customize accessibility for the interactive cat surface

points.text: 用 **accessibilityLabel**、**accessibilityValue** 與 **.adjustable** 特性，搭配 **accessibilityAdjustableAction** 讓滑桿類控制項可被輔助技術調整。
透過 **accessibilityActivationPoint** 設定啟用點，讓 VoiceOver 啟用控制項時落在正確位置。
使用 **AccessibilityNotification.Announcement** 在數值變化時播報，並做好節流避免過度通知。
對複雜控制項以 **accessibilityActions** 提供「上/下/左/右」等自訂動作，取代難以操作的連續手勢。
針對直接觸控的互動表面，用 **accessibilityDirectTouch([.requiresActivation])** 兼顧探索與操作。

audience: 在 SwiftUI 中打造**自訂控制項與互動元件**、想讓它們完整支援 VoiceOver 的開發者。
gloss_en: Refine accessibility for custom controls
takeaway_en: Adding labels, values, adjustable traits, and custom actions to your custom controls lets VoiceOver users fully operate your interactive elements.

points_en.text: Use **accessibilityLabel**, **accessibilityValue**, and the **.adjustable** trait together with **accessibilityAdjustableAction** so slider-style controls can be adjusted by assistive technologies.
Set an activation point with **accessibilityActivationPoint** so VoiceOver activates the control at the correct location.
Use **AccessibilityNotification.Announcement** to announce value changes, and throttle them to avoid excessive notifications.
For complex controls, provide custom actions like up/down/left/right via **accessibilityActions** instead of hard-to-perform continuous gestures.
For direct-touch interactive surfaces, use **accessibilityDirectTouch([.requiresActivation])** to balance exploration and operation.

audience_en: Developers building **custom controls and interactive elements** in SwiftUI who want full VoiceOver support.
summary: 這場由 Apple Accessibility 團隊主講，核心訊息是：**自訂控制項**讓人能用超越標準元件的手勢做出獨特操作，但若不補上無障礙支援，使用 **VoiceOver**、**Switch Control** 等輔助技術的人就會被擋在門外。講者以一個標準 SwiftUI slider 為起點，說明視覺形態其實隱含了大量資訊——控制項的用途、目前的值、可採取的動作與互動回饋——然後把這四點訂為讓任何控制項無障礙化的**指導原則**：purpose、value、actions、feedback。

第一個範例是咖啡機 app 的填充式滑桿。透過 `accessibilityElement()`、`accessibilityLabel`、`accessibilityValue` 表達用途與目前值，再加上 **`.adjustable`** trait 與 **`accessibilityAdjustableAction`**，VoiceOver 就能像操作內建 slider 一樣上下調整。要做更精細的調整，則靠 VoiceOver 的 **passthrough gesture**——用 **`accessibilityActivationPoint`** 把手勢起點對齊目前填充高度，並在值變動時用 **`AccessibilityNotification.Announcement`** 適時播報（以節流避免過於吵雜）。

進一步的複雜控制項則需要不同工具。等化器（Background Sounds 的二維 pad）有水平與垂直兩軸，單一的 adjustable 只能涵蓋一軸，因此改用 **`accessibilityActions`** 自訂動作（Move Up/Down/Left/Right），讓使用者透過熟悉的動作探索 2D 空間。最後的互動虛擬貓 surface 支援撫摸、輕點、捏等多種手勢，passthrough 並不適合，於是採用 **`accessibilityDirectTouch`** 直接觸控 API，搭配 **`.requiresActivation`** 與 **`.silentOnTouch`** 選項把觸控事件直接交給控制項。實務建議：打開 VoiceOver 親自體驗自己的 app，並盡量同時提供 custom actions，讓無法做直接觸控的人也有替代路徑。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: 由 Accessibility 團隊的 Khin 開場，說明**自訂 UI 控制項**讓人能用超越標準元件的手勢與互動做出獨特操作，但也因此更需顧及 **VoiceOver**、**Switch Control** 等輔助技術。核心理念：技術要對所有人都好用，讓每個人都能存取 app 真正想提供的功能。本場將先講指導原則，再套用到幾個複雜控制項上。

deepdive.title: Guiding principles
deepdive.body: 以一個標準 SwiftUI slider 拆解視覺形態隱含的資訊：軌道、把手與位置讓人一眼看懂這是連續值、目前值約一半、把手可拖曳且有即時回饋。對照 **VoiceOver** 的描述（「Brightness, 50%, adjustable」與調整提示），歸納出四個指導原則：讓控制項的 **purpose**、**value**、**actions** 與 **feedback** 都能被輔助技術取得。

deepdive.title: Improve accessibility for coffee dispenser
deepdive.body: 以咖啡機 app 的填充式滑桿為例，預設下 VoiceOver 只讀出「Button、6 ounces」，看不懂如何互動。解法是先 `accessibilityElement()`，用 **`accessibilityLabel`**（"Coffee Dispenser"）表達用途、**`accessibilityValue`** 報出目前盎司數，再加上 **`.adjustable`** trait 與 **`accessibilityAdjustableAction`**——closure 依 `.increment`／`.decrement` 方向各自處理，讓使用者用上下滑一次調整一盎司。

deepdive.title: Set the accessibility activation point
deepdive.body: 為了做到半盎司的精細調整，引入 VoiceOver 的 **passthrough gesture**：雙擊並按住後，手勢會從控制項的 **`accessibilityActivationPoint`** 開始，VoiceOver 把觸控事件直接傳給控制項。範例用 `UnitPoint(x: 0.5, y: 1 - coffee)` 把起點對齊目前填充高度，讓使用者往任一方向都有調整空間。

deepdive.title: Post accessibility announcements
deepdive.body: passthrough 過程中要給予回饋，做法是在 `onChange(of: coffee)` 時用 **`AccessibilityNotification.Announcement(...).post()`** 播報新值。但不是每次變動都播——範例會追蹤上次播報的值與時間，只有在值確實改變且距離上次至少 0.3 秒時才播報，避免過於吵雜，確保使用者聽到的是有意義的更新。

deepdive.title: Complex controls
deepdive.body: 進入更複雜的範例：iOS Background Sounds 設定裡的等化器，是一個可同時調整兩個維度（頻率與振幅）的二維 pad。問題在於 **`.adjustable`** trait 的 increment／decrement 只能涵蓋單一軸，對於有水平與垂直兩軸的控制項並不理想，因此需要改用其他機制。

deepdive.title: Add custom actions
deepdive.body: 解法是 **custom actions**：在 EqualizerPad 上用 **`accessibilityActions`** 加入四個有描述性名稱的動作（Move Up／Right／Down／Left），各自把單一軸移動固定步數並 clamp 在範圍內。custom actions 不限於單軸，可暴露任意自訂操作，VoiceOver 會把動作名稱讀出、雙擊即執行，讓人用熟悉的方式探索 2D 空間。

deepdive.title: Customize accessibility for the interactive cat surface
deepdive.body: 最後是支援撫摸、輕點、捏等多種手勢的互動虛擬貓 surface，預設 VoiceOver 只當成一張圖片。先用 `accessibilityLabel`（"Virtual Cat"）與 `accessibilityValue`（貓目前反應）表達用途與狀態；因為使用者可能反覆或多手勢操作，passthrough 不適合，改用 **`accessibilityDirectTouch`** 直接觸控。搭配 **`.requiresActivation`**（雙擊後才響應、避免誤觸）與 **`.silentOnTouch`**（讓控制項自己的音效不被 VoiceOver 蓋掉），並建議盡量同時提供 custom actions 作為替代路徑。

summary_en: Presented by Apple's Accessibility team, the central message is that **custom controls** let people do unique, creative things with gestures that go beyond standard elements — but without accessibility support, people relying on **VoiceOver**, **Switch Control**, and other assistive technologies are locked out of the very thing the app was built to do. Starting from a standard SwiftUI slider, the speaker shows how visual form implicitly conveys a control's purpose, current value, possible actions, and feedback, then turns those into the **guiding principles** for making any control accessible: purpose, value, actions, and feedback.

The first example is a coffee maker's fill-style slider. Using `accessibilityElement()`, `accessibilityLabel`, and `accessibilityValue` to express purpose and current value, plus the **`.adjustable`** trait and **`accessibilityAdjustableAction`**, VoiceOver can adjust it just like a built-in slider. For finer adjustment, VoiceOver's **passthrough gesture** is used — **`accessibilityActivationPoint`** aligns the gesture's start with the current fill level, and **`AccessibilityNotification.Announcement`** posts value updates, throttled so they aren't noisy.

More complex controls need different tools. The equalizer (Background Sounds' two-dimensional pad) has horizontal and vertical axes, and a single adjustable action only covers one axis, so **`accessibilityActions`** custom actions (Move Up/Down/Left/Right) let people explore the 2D space through familiar actions. The final interactive virtual cat surface supports patting, tapping, and pinching, where passthrough isn't a good fit, so it adopts the **`accessibilityDirectTouch`** API with the **`.requiresActivation`** and **`.silentOnTouch`** options to pass touch events straight to the control. The practical advice: turn on VoiceOver and try your own app, and provide custom actions wherever possible so people who can't perform direct touch still have a path.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Khin from the Accessibility team opens by noting that **custom UI controls** empower unique, creative interactions beyond standard elements, which makes assistive technologies like **VoiceOver** and **Switch Control** all the more important to support. The core belief: technology works best when it works for everyone, giving access to the very thing the app was built to do. The session first covers guiding principles, then applies them to several complex controls.

deepdive_en.title: Guiding principles
deepdive_en.body: Using a standard SwiftUI slider, the speaker breaks down the information implied by visual form: track, handle, and position make it clear this is a continuous value at about half, with a draggable handle and immediate feedback. Contrasting that with **VoiceOver**'s description ("Brightness, 50%, adjustable" plus an adjustment hint), they derive four guiding principles: make a control's **purpose**, **value**, **actions**, and **feedback** available to assistive technologies.

deepdive_en.title: Improve accessibility for coffee dispenser
deepdive_en.body: With the coffee maker's fill-style slider, by default VoiceOver only reads "Button, 6 ounces" and gives no sense of how to interact. The fix is `accessibilityElement()`, then **`accessibilityLabel`** ("Coffee Dispenser") for purpose, **`accessibilityValue`** for the current ounces, plus the **`.adjustable`** trait and **`accessibilityAdjustableAction`** — whose closure handles the `.increment`/`.decrement` direction so swiping up or down changes the amount one ounce at a time.

deepdive_en.title: Set the accessibility activation point
deepdive_en.body: For half-ounce precision, VoiceOver's **passthrough gesture** is introduced: after a double-tap-and-hold, the gesture begins at the control's **`accessibilityActivationPoint`** and VoiceOver sends touch events straight to the control. The example uses `UnitPoint(x: 0.5, y: 1 - coffee)` to align the start with the current fill level, giving room to adjust in either direction.

deepdive_en.title: Post accessibility announcements
deepdive_en.body: Feedback during the passthrough gesture is provided by posting **`AccessibilityNotification.Announcement(...).post()`** in `onChange(of: coffee)`. Not every change is announced, though — the example tracks the last spoken value and time, announcing only when the value has actually changed and at least 0.3 seconds have passed, keeping updates meaningful rather than noisy.

deepdive_en.title: Complex controls
deepdive_en.body: The session moves to more complex examples: the equalizer in iOS Background Sounds settings, a two-dimensional pad that adjusts two values (frequency and amplitude) at once. The problem is that the **`.adjustable`** trait's increment/decrement only covers a single axis, which isn't ideal for a control with both horizontal and vertical axes, motivating a different mechanism.

deepdive_en.title: Add custom actions
deepdive_en.body: The solution is **custom actions**: on the EqualizerPad, **`accessibilityActions`** adds four descriptively named actions (Move Up/Right/Down/Left), each moving a single axis by a fixed step clamped within range. Custom actions aren't limited to one axis and can expose any operation — VoiceOver reads each name aloud and a double-tap activates it — letting people navigate the 2D space using familiar actions.

deepdive_en.title: Customize accessibility for the interactive cat surface
deepdive_en.body: The final example is an interactive virtual cat surface supporting patting, tapping, and pinching, which VoiceOver treats only as an image by default. After `accessibilityLabel` ("Virtual Cat") and `accessibilityValue` (the cat's current reaction), passthrough isn't a good fit since people may repeat or combine gestures, so **`accessibilityDirectTouch`** is used. The **`.requiresActivation`** option (responds only after a double-tap, avoiding accidental activation) and **`.silentOnTouch`** option (so the control's own audio isn't talked over) are explained, with advice to also expose custom actions as an alternative path.

title: Prepare your tvOS apps for Dynamic Type
gloss: 讓你的 tvOS App 支援動態字型
takeaway: tvOS 也要支援 Dynamic Type,改用標準 text styles 與彈性 constraints,並在進入無障礙字級時切換成適配版面。
chapters: Dynamic Type with text styles in UIKit
Adapt layout in response to dynamic type
Provide a conditional layout for when larger sizes are turned on
UIKit adaptive layout that responds to content size changes

points.text: **Dynamic Type** 讓使用者自選文字大小,tvOS App 也應支援以提升閱讀與操作舒適度。
常見問題來自**寫死的字體大小與固定寬度 frame**;改用 .frame(maxWidth: .infinity) 等彈性 constraints。
採用**標準 text styles**:SwiftUI 用 .font(.caption) 等,UIKit 用 UIFont.preferredFont(forTextStyle:) 並開啟 adjustsFontForContentSizeCategory。
在 SwiftUI 監看 **@Environment(\.dynamicTypeSize)**,用 isAccessibilitySize 調整 containerRelativeFrame 的欄數或以 AnyLayout 切換 H/V Stack。
UIKit 用 **registerForTraitChanges** 監聽 UITraitPreferredContentSizeCategory,在無障礙字級時把 stack 軸向改為垂直。

audience: **開發 tvOS App、想兼顧無障礙與不同字級下版面正確性的開發者。**
gloss_en: Prepare your tvOS app for Dynamic Type
takeaway_en: tvOS apps should support Dynamic Type too—switch to standard text styles and flexible constraints, and adapt the layout when accessibility text sizes are in use.

points_en.text: **Dynamic Type** lets users choose their text size, and tvOS apps should support it to make reading and interaction more comfortable.
Common problems come from **hard-coded font sizes and fixed-width frames**; switch to flexible constraints like .frame(maxWidth: .infinity).
Adopt **standard text styles**: in SwiftUI use .font(.caption) and the like; in UIKit use UIFont.preferredFont(forTextStyle:) and enable adjustsFontForContentSizeCategory.
In SwiftUI, observe **@Environment(\.dynamicTypeSize)** and use isAccessibilitySize to adjust the column count in containerRelativeFrame, or switch between H/V Stacks with AnyLayout.
In UIKit, use **registerForTraitChanges** to observe UITraitPreferredContentSizeCategory and switch the stack axis to vertical at accessibility text sizes.

audience_en: **Developers building tvOS apps who want correct layouts across text sizes while supporting accessibility.**
summary: **tvOS 27** 首度帶來系統層級的 **Large Text（Dynamic Type）** 支援，讓使用者能在「設定 > 輔助使用 > 顯示 > 文字大小」把字級從 Large 一路調到 Accessibility XXXL，全平台每個 app 都受惠。由 Accessibility 團隊的 Isis 主講，重點是：tvOS 的 Dynamic Type 與 iOS 運作方式相同，標準的 `Label`、`Button`、tab bar 等元件會自動縮放，開發者的工作是找出並修正**自訂元件**。支援後還能在 App Store 的 **Accessibility Nutrition Labels** 標示 Larger Text，觸及特別尋找無障礙 app 的使用者。

常見問題有三類：避免**固定字級**（hard-coded font size）導致文字無法縮放、避免**固定寬高 constraint** 造成截斷或裁切，以及在元件放大後調整 padding 與 spacing。修法是把 hard-coded 字型換成語意化的 **text style**（SwiftUI 用 `.caption` 等；UIKit 用 `UIFont.preferredFont(forTextStyle:)` 並設 `adjustsFontForContentSizeCategory = true`），並把固定寬度改成 **flexible constraint**（SwiftUI 將 `frame(width:)` 改為 `frame(maxWidth: .infinity)`）。

光修固定值有時不夠，還需依文字大小**調整版面**。透過讀取 `@Environment(\.dynamicTypeSize)`，可在 accessibility size 時改變 `containerRelativeFrame` 的欄數（如電影海報從 6 欄改 4 欄），給每格更寬空間；更進一步可用 **`AnyLayout`** 在 `HStackLayout` 與 `VStackLayout` 間切換，讓 card 在大字級時改為垂直堆疊。UIKit 則改 `UIStackView.axis` 並用 `registerForTraitChanges` 監聽 `UITraitPreferredContentSizeCategory` 即時更新。行動方案：用標準 text style、系統性地以 Large Text 測試、必要時調整版面，並在 tvOS 的 Accessibility Nutrition Labels 標示支援。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: 由 Accessibility 團隊工程經理 Isis 開場，宣布 **tvOS 27** 首度支援系統層級的 Large Text 文字縮放。許多人需要或偏好不同字級，使用者可在「設定 > 輔助使用 > 顯示 > 文字大小」從 Large 調到 Accessibility XXXL；標準 UIKit／SwiftUI 元件會自動適應，且支援後可在 App Store 的 **Accessibility Nutrition Labels** 標示 Larger Text。

deepdive.title: Identify common issues
deepdive.body: 說明三類需檢查的問題：**固定字級** 讓文字無法縮放、不適應 Dynamic Type 的 hard-coded 尺寸或 constraint 會造成 **截斷或裁切**，以及元件放大後需調整 **padding 與 spacing**。以媒體 app 中「Signup information」caption 因 hard-coded 字級而不縮放為例。

deepdive.title: Adopt standard text styles
deepdive.body: 把 hard-coded 字型換成 **語意化 text style**（如 `.caption`），文字才會隨偏好縮放。示範把該 caption 改用 caption 樣式，字級開始動態成長。

deepdive.title: Use flexible constraints
deepdive.body: 改用 text style 後若仍截斷，是因固定寬度（300 點）不夠。將 `frame(width: 300)` 改為 **`frame(maxWidth: .infinity)`**，讓 SwiftUI 依內容使用所需寬度，文字便能完整顯示。

deepdive.title: Dynamic Type with text styles in UIKit
deepdive.body: UIKit 的作法類似但多一步：把 hard-coded font 換成 **`UIFont.preferredFont(forTextStyle:)`**，並設定 **`adjustsFontForContentSizeCategory = true`**，UIKit 才會在偏好變更時自動更新字級。

deepdive.title: Adapt your layout
deepdive.body: 有時修固定值不夠，需在大字級時**調整版面**同時保留預設尺寸的原版面。以六張電影海報的 collection view 為例，大字級下橫向放不下六個標題，需要適配。

deepdive.title: Adapt layout in response to dynamic type
deepdive.body: 讀取 **`dynamicTypeSize`** 環境值，在 `containerRelativeFrame` 修飾器中調整欄數：accessibility size 時顯示 4 欄而非 6 欄，給每格更寬尺寸與更多標題空間；更長文字可考慮 marquee 策略。

deepdive.title: Provide a conditional layout for when larger sizes are turned on
deepdive.body: 針對 content card（圖、標題、副標）在大字級下 padding 不足且易截斷，提供**條件式版面**：讀 `dynamicTypeSize` 判斷是否為 accessibility size，再用 **`AnyLayout`** 在 `VStackLayout` 與 `HStackLayout` 間切換，像一般 stack 一樣使用。

deepdive.title: UIKit adaptive layout that responds to content size changes
deepdive.body: UIKit 用 **`UIStackView`** 並依 `preferredContentSizeCategory.isAccessibilityCategory` 切換 `axis`（垂直／水平）。呼叫 **`registerForTraitChanges`** 傳入 `UITraitPreferredContentSizeCategory`，即可在執行期隨字級變化即時更新版面；大字級時改為垂直堆疊讓標題佔滿寬度。

summary_en: **tvOS 27** brings system-wide **Large Text (Dynamic Type)** support for the first time, letting users scale text from Large up to Accessibility XXXL in Settings > Accessibility > Display > Text Size, benefiting every app on the platform. Presented by Isis from the Accessibility team, the key point is that tvOS Dynamic Type works the same as iOS: standard `Label`, `Button`, and tab bar components scale automatically, so the developer's job is to find and fix **custom elements**. Once supported, you can indicate Larger Text in your App Store **Accessibility Nutrition Labels** to reach users seeking accessible apps.

There are three common issue types: avoid **hard-coded font sizes** that prevent text from scaling, avoid **fixed width/height constraints** that cause truncation or clipping, and adjust padding and spacing once elements grow. The fixes: replace hard-coded fonts with semantic **text styles** (SwiftUI `.caption` etc.; UIKit `UIFont.preferredFont(forTextStyle:)` with `adjustsFontForContentSizeCategory = true`), and replace fixed widths with **flexible constraints** (in SwiftUI, change `frame(width:)` to `frame(maxWidth: .infinity)`).

Fixing hard-coded values isn't always enough—you may need to **adapt layout** in response to text size. By reading `@Environment(\.dynamicTypeSize)`, you can change `containerRelativeFrame`'s column count at accessibility sizes (e.g., movie posters from 6 to 4 columns) for wider cells; going further, use **`AnyLayout`** to switch between `HStackLayout` and `VStackLayout` so cards stack vertically at large sizes. In UIKit, change `UIStackView.axis` and use `registerForTraitChanges` to observe `UITraitPreferredContentSizeCategory` for live updates. Action plan: use standard text styles, test systematically with Large Text, adapt layouts when needed, and indicate support in your tvOS Accessibility Nutrition Labels.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Isis, an engineering manager on the Accessibility team, opens by announcing **tvOS 27** brings system-wide Large Text scaling for the first time. Many people need or prefer different text sizes; users set them in Settings > Accessibility > Display > Text Size from Large up to Accessibility XXXL. Standard UIKit/SwiftUI components adapt automatically, and you can indicate Larger Text in App Store **Accessibility Nutrition Labels**.

deepdive_en.title: Identify common issues
deepdive_en.body: Covers three issue types to check: **hard-coded font sizes** that block scaling, hard-coded sizes/constraints that cause **truncation or clipping**, and the need to adjust **padding and spacing** as elements grow. Uses the example of a 'Signup information' caption in a media app that won't scale due to a hard-coded font size.

deepdive_en.title: Adopt standard text styles
deepdive_en.body: Replace hard-coded fonts with **semantic text styles** (like `.caption`) so text scales with preferences. Demonstrates switching the caption to the caption style, after which the size begins growing dynamically.

deepdive_en.title: Use flexible constraints
deepdive_en.body: If text still truncates after adopting a text style, the cause is a fixed width (300 points). Change `frame(width: 300)` to **`frame(maxWidth: .infinity)`** so SwiftUI uses as much width as the content needs and the text displays fully.

deepdive_en.title: Dynamic Type with text styles in UIKit
deepdive_en.body: The UIKit approach is similar with one extra step: replace hard-coded fonts with **`UIFont.preferredFont(forTextStyle:)`** and set **`adjustsFontForContentSizeCategory = true`** so UIKit updates the font size automatically when preferences change.

deepdive_en.title: Adapt your layout
deepdive_en.body: Sometimes fixing fixed values isn't enough—you need to **adapt the layout** at large sizes while preserving the original for default sizes. Uses a six-poster collection view that can't fit six titles horizontally at large text and needs adaptation.

deepdive_en.title: Adapt layout in response to dynamic type
deepdive_en.body: Read the **`dynamicTypeSize`** environment value and adjust the column count in the `containerRelativeFrame` modifier: show 4 columns instead of 6 at accessibility sizes for wider cells and more title room; consider a marquee strategy for even longer text.

deepdive_en.title: Provide a conditional layout for when larger sizes are turned on
deepdive_en.body: For content cards (image, title, subtitle) that lack padding and truncate at large sizes, provide a **conditional layout**: read `dynamicTypeSize` to detect accessibility sizes, then use **`AnyLayout`** to switch between `VStackLayout` and `HStackLayout`, using it like any normal stack.

deepdive_en.title: UIKit adaptive layout that responds to content size changes
deepdive_en.body: In UIKit, use **`UIStackView`** and switch `axis` (vertical/horizontal) based on `preferredContentSizeCategory.isAccessibilityCategory`. Call **`registerForTraitChanges`** passing `UITraitPreferredContentSizeCategory` to update the layout live as size changes; at large sizes it switches to a vertical stack so titles span the full width.

title: Meet the new MetricKit
gloss: 認識全新的 MetricKit
takeaway: 用全新以 async 串流為核心的 MetricKit 接收效能指標與診斷資料，並透過 State Reporting 加上自訂情境，更快找出並修正效能問題。
chapters: Send your metrics to the server
Send your diagnostic data to the server
Send encoded metric reports to the server

points.text: 用 `MetricManager` 的 **async 串流**（`metricReports`、`diagnosticReports`）接收效能指標與診斷，取代舊有的 delegate 模式。
指標報告可直接以 **`JSONEncoder` 編碼**並上傳到自家伺服器，方便集中分析。
診斷資料涵蓋**當機（crash）與卡頓（hang）**，並提供 `callStackTree`、終止原因與分類等細節。
透過 **State Reporting**（`StateReporter`、`@ReportableMetadata`）為指標加上自訂情境，把資料對應到 App 內的狀態與畫面。

audience: **重視 App 效能、想建立指標與當機監控管線的開發者**。
gloss_en: Meet the new MetricKit
takeaway_en: Receive performance metrics and diagnostics with the new async-stream-based MetricKit, and use State Reporting to add custom context so you can find and fix performance problems faster.

points_en.text: Receive performance metrics and diagnostics via `MetricManager`'s **async streams** (`metricReports`, `diagnosticReports`), replacing the old delegate pattern.
Metric reports can be encoded directly with **`JSONEncoder`** and uploaded to your own server for centralized analysis.
Diagnostics cover **crashes and hangs**, with details like `callStackTree`, termination reason, and classification.
Use **State Reporting** (`StateReporter`, `@ReportableMetadata`) to attach custom context to metrics, mapping data to in-app states and screens.

audience_en: **Developers who care about app performance and want to build a metrics and crash monitoring pipeline**.
summary: **MetricKit** 是 Apple 用來在真實裝置上監測 app 效能品質的框架，由 MetricKit 團隊的 Yonni 主講。效能優化是一個循環：收集資料、分析找問題、triage 找根因、修正、再回到收集。MetricKit 負責「收集」這一環，提供兩種資料：**metrics**（告訴你某面向是變好還變壞的整體趨勢）與 **diagnostics**（告訴你哪條 code path 造成問題）。**iOS 27** 把整個框架以現代、Swift-first 的全新 API 從頭重寫，所有新進展都僅限這套新 API（舊的 `MXMetricManager` 應遷移到新的 **`MetricManager`**）。

取得 metrics 很簡單：建立 `MetricManager`，在 app 啟動時就 `for await report in manager.metricReports` 訂閱，避免延遲訂閱造成資料遺失。每日 report 內含一個涵蓋全天的 entry 與數個數小時的細分 entry；每個 interval 內的 metrics 依 **metric group**（`.cpu`、`.memory`、`.display`、`.gpu`）組織。`MetricReport` 是 **Codable**，可直接用 `JSONEncoder` 編碼送到伺服器做跨裝置聚合分析；也可逐層 filter 到特定 group 再 switch 取出如 `peakMemory` 的值。iOS 27 新增 **Metal frame rate** metric。

Diagnostics 在 triage 階段特別有用：當 crash、hang 發生，系統在裝置上擷取診斷並立即透過 `manager.diagnosticReports` 送達 app。crash diagnostic 提供 backtrace、termination reason、exception type，iOS 27 還加上 **termination category**（標示該 crash 如何被計入 metrics，方便與趨勢對照）；新增 **memory exception diagnostics**。最強大的是 **context**：透過 **StateReporting** 框架以 `reportTransition(to:)` 回報 app 狀態（如不同 tab、實驗開關），MetricKit 便能把 metric 依狀態切分——例如 scroll hitch 在 Spending tab 僅 1 ms/s 但 Reports tab 飆到 71 ms/s，直接指出優化重點。每個 state 屬於一個 **domain**（同時只有一個 active state），可用 `@ReportableMetadata` 加結構化細節，並用 `encodingFormatKey = .byStateReportingDomain` 把報告依 domain 分組送出。最佳實務：domain 要窄、state 要代表穩定且有意義的階段、別過度細分。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: 由 MetricKit 團隊的 Yonni 開場，介紹框架與 **iOS 27** 新功能。效能優化是循環：收集→分析→triage→修正→再收集，MetricKit 負責**收集**。它提供 **metrics**（效能趨勢的整體訊號）與 **diagnostics**（指出問題 code path），iOS 27 以現代 Swift-first API 全新重寫，所有新進展皆專屬這套新 API。

deepdive.title: Metrics
deepdive.body: 說明 metrics 是 app 的持續健康訊號：launch time、hangs、animation 反映流暢度，CPU／GPU／disk／network 反映資源消耗。以 time to first draw 的 histogram 與由 hang 資料推導 hang rate 為例；iOS 27 可把每個 metric 依 app **state** 切分，並新增 **Metal frame rate** metric。

deepdive.title: Receive metrics from MetricKit
deepdive.body: 入口是 **`MetricManager`** 類別，透過 `for await report in manager.metricReports` 接收 report。應在 app 啟動時就建立並保持存活，避免延遲訂閱造成資料遺失，讓串流持續送達後續報告。

deepdive.title: Send your metrics to the server
deepdive.body: `MetricReport` 是 **Codable**，可用 `JSONEncoder` 直接把整份報告編碼成 JSON 送到伺服器，方便跨多裝置檢視 app 健康狀況。

deepdive.title: Access your performance metrics
deepdive.body: 若只想取特定資料，可遍歷 **`intervalEntries`**（含全天彙總與細分窗口），filter 到目標 **metric group**（如 `.memory`），再 switch 各 metric case 取值（範例只處理 `peakMemory`）。建議在 app 啟動時於 detached task 或專屬 service class 執行。接著進入分析階段：在伺服器聚合、建立 baseline 並監測趨勢。

deepdive.title: Diagnostics
deepdive.body: metrics 用於監測，**diagnostics** 用於 triage。當 crash 或 hang 發生，系統在裝置上擷取診斷並立即送達 app。多數 diagnostics 含 **backtrace**；crash diagnostic 還提供終止原因與 exception type，iOS 27 新增 **termination category** 對應 metrics 計入方式，可與異常終止趨勢相關聯。

deepdive.title: Receive diagnostics
deepdive.body: 透過 `manager.diagnosticReports` await 取得診斷報告，同樣應在 app 啟動時於 detached task 或專屬 service class 開始監聽。

deepdive.title: Send your diagnostic data to the server
deepdive.body: `DiagnosticReport` 與 metric report 一樣是 **Codable**，可用 `JSONEncoder` 編碼成 JSON，把所有診斷資訊送到分析伺服器。

deepdive.title: Access your diagnostic data
deepdive.body: 診斷報告為結構化，可 switch 不同 case 取用：crash case 取出 **backtrace、reason、category**，hang case 則另行處理。讓 app 能針對不同診斷類型分流並上傳。

deepdive.title: Context
deepdive.body: 前述資料是整體圖像；要調查個別問題需更細緻的 **context**。以費用報帳 app 為例，scroll hitch 的平均值（15 ms/s）橫跨 Reports 與 Spending 兩 tab，無法看出問題出在哪。可用 **StateReporting** 框架回報 app 狀態，讓 MetricKit 依狀態聚合 metric。

deepdive.title: Receive MetricKit data with states
deepdive.body: 建立 **`StateReportingDomain`**（reverse-DNS 字串）並在設定 `MetricManager` 時以 `enabledStateReportingDomains` 註冊，再用 `StateReporter.reporter(for:)` 的 **`reportTransition(to:)`** 回報轉換（如 "Reports"）。state 採 transition 模型，無 start/end 配對，只回報當下狀態。

deepdive.title: Define custom structured types
deepdive.body: 可用 **`@ReportableMetadata`** 巨集定義自訂 struct（如 `ViewConfiguration` 含 listSize、isSorted），建立帶 `stableMetadata:` 的 reporter，並在 `reportTransition` 時附上該結構，為每個狀態加上更細的結構化資訊。

deepdive.title: Send encoded metric reports to the server
deepdive.body: 送出時可把資料依 **state reporting domain** 分組：在 `JSONEncoder` 的 `userInfo` 設定 `MetricReport.encodingFormatKey` 為 **`.byStateReportingDomain`**，編碼後 state entries 與 interval entries 都會依 domain 與 state 分組。最佳實務：domain 要窄、state 代表穩定有意義的階段、避免過度細分，並用 Points of Interest instrument 驗證。

summary_en: **MetricKit** is Apple's framework for monitoring real-world app performance quality on real devices, presented by Yonni from the MetricKit team. Performance optimization is a loop: collect data, analyze to find problems, triage to find root cause, fix, and return to collecting. MetricKit handles the collection piece, providing two kinds of data: **metrics** (telling you whether an area is trending better or worse overall) and **diagnostics** (telling you which code path caused a problem). **iOS 27** rebuilds the framework from the ground up with a modern, Swift-first API; all new advances are exclusive to it (migrate the old `MXMetricManager` to the new **`MetricManager`**).

Getting metrics is simple: create a `MetricManager` and subscribe at app startup via `for await report in manager.metricReports` to avoid data loss from delayed subscription. Each daily report contains a full-day entry plus smaller multi-hour breakdown entries; within each interval, metrics are organized into **metric groups** (`.cpu`, `.memory`, `.display`, `.gpu`). `MetricReport` is **Codable**, so encode it with `JSONEncoder` and send it to a server for cross-device aggregation; or drill down by filtering to a group and switching over cases to read values like `peakMemory`. iOS 27 adds a **Metal frame rate** metric.

Diagnostics shine in the triage phase: when a crash or hang occurs, the system captures a diagnostic on device and delivers it immediately via `manager.diagnosticReports`. A crash diagnostic provides a backtrace, termination reason, and exception type, and iOS 27 adds a **termination category** (indicating how the crash was accounted for in metrics, to correlate with trends); it also adds **memory exception diagnostics**. The most powerful capability is **context**: via the **StateReporting** framework you report app states with `reportTransition(to:)` (e.g., different tabs, an experiment flag), so MetricKit can intersect metrics with state—for example scroll hitch was just 1 ms/s on the Spending tab but spiked to 71 ms/s on the Reports tab, pinpointing where to optimize. Each state belongs to a **domain** (only one active state at a time), can carry structured detail via `@ReportableMetadata`, and reports can be grouped by domain on send via `encodingFormatKey = .byStateReportingDomain`. Best practices: keep domains narrow, make states represent stable meaningful phases, and avoid over-granularity.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Yonni from the MetricKit team opens by introducing the framework and **iOS 27** updates. Optimization is a loop: collect → analyze → triage → fix → collect, with MetricKit handling **collection**. It provides **metrics** (an overall performance trend signal) and **diagnostics** (pinpointing the problem code path); iOS 27 rewrites it with a modern Swift-first API, and all new advances are exclusive to it.

deepdive_en.title: Metrics
deepdive_en.body: Explains metrics as the app's ongoing health signal: launch time, hangs, and animation reflect smoothness, while CPU/GPU/disk/network reflect resource consumption. Uses a time-to-first-draw histogram and a derived hang rate as examples; iOS 27 can intersect each metric with app **state** and adds a **Metal frame rate** metric.

deepdive_en.title: Receive metrics from MetricKit
deepdive_en.body: The entry point is the **`MetricManager`** class; receive reports via `for await report in manager.metricReports`. Set this up at app startup and keep it alive to avoid data loss from delayed subscription, so the stream keeps delivering subsequent reports.

deepdive_en.title: Send your metrics to the server
deepdive_en.body: `MetricReport` is **Codable**, so use `JSONEncoder` to encode the entire report to JSON and send it to a server, making it easy to examine app health across many devices.

deepdive_en.title: Access your performance metrics
deepdive_en.body: To access specific data, iterate **`intervalEntries`** (full-day aggregate plus breakdown windows), filter to the target **metric group** (e.g. `.memory`), then switch over metric cases to read values (the example handles only `peakMemory`). Do this in a detached task or dedicated service class at launch. Then enter analysis: aggregate on a server, establish a baseline, and monitor trends.

deepdive_en.title: Diagnostics
deepdive_en.body: Metrics are for monitoring; **diagnostics** are for triage. When a crash or hang occurs, the system captures a diagnostic on device and delivers it immediately. Most diagnostics include a **backtrace**; crash diagnostics also provide a termination reason and exception type, and iOS 27 adds a **termination category** matching how it's accounted for in metrics, to correlate with abnormal-termination trends.

deepdive_en.title: Receive diagnostics
deepdive_en.body: Await diagnostic reports via `manager.diagnosticReports`, again starting the listener at app launch in a detached task or dedicated service class.

deepdive_en.title: Send your diagnostic data to the server
deepdive_en.body: Like metric reports, `DiagnosticReport` is **Codable**, so encode it to JSON with `JSONEncoder` and send all the diagnostic information to your analytics server.

deepdive_en.title: Access your diagnostic data
deepdive_en.body: Diagnostic reports are structured, so switch over cases to pick what you need: the crash case extracts **backtrace, reason, and category**, while the hang case is handled separately, letting the app route and upload different diagnostic types.

deepdive_en.title: Context
deepdive_en.body: The data so far is the overall picture; investigating individual issues needs richer **context**. Using an expense app, the average scroll hitch (15 ms/s) blends the Reports and Spending tabs, hiding where the problem is. Report app states via the **StateReporting** framework so MetricKit can aggregate metrics by state.

deepdive_en.title: Receive MetricKit data with states
deepdive_en.body: Create a **`StateReportingDomain`** (a reverse-DNS string), register it via `enabledStateReportingDomains` when setting up `MetricManager`, then use `StateReporter.reporter(for:)`'s **`reportTransition(to:)`** to report transitions (e.g. "Reports"). States follow a transition model with no start/end pairs—you report the current condition.

deepdive_en.title: Define custom structured types
deepdive_en.body: Use the **`@ReportableMetadata`** macro to define a custom struct (e.g. `ViewConfiguration` with listSize, isSorted), create a reporter with `stableMetadata:`, and pass that struct in `reportTransition` to attach finer structured info to each state.

deepdive_en.title: Send encoded metric reports to the server
deepdive_en.body: On send, group data by **state reporting domain**: set `MetricReport.encodingFormatKey` to **`.byStateReportingDomain`** on the `JSONEncoder`'s `userInfo`, so encoded state and interval entries are grouped by domain and state. Best practices: keep domains narrow, make states stable and meaningful, avoid over-granularity, and validate with the Points of Interest instrument.

title: Live Activities essentials
gloss: Live Activities 核心要點
takeaway: 用 ActivityKit 從零打造、更新並最佳化 **Live Activity**，涵蓋 Dynamic Island、StandBy、新的 small 樣式與 App Intents 互動。
chapters: Start and update a Live Activity
Optimize for limited width in the Dynamic Island
Associate an intent with a button

points.text: 以 `ActivityAttributes` 與 `ContentState` 定義資料，並用 `ActivityConfiguration` 與 **Dynamic Island** 各區域建立 Live Activity 視圖。
透過 `Activity.request` 啟動、`activity.update` 更新內容，先以 `ActivityAuthorizationInfo` 確認已啟用。
新增對 **`activityFamily` small** 樣式的支援（`supplementalActivityFamilies([.small])`），可依 `activityFamily` 環境值客製化呈現。
用 `isDynamicIslandLimitedInWidth` 與 `showsWidgetContainerBackground` 等環境值，最佳化 Dynamic Island 窄版與 **StandBy** 背景。
以 `LiveActivityIntent` 加入互動，將 intent 綁定到 `Button(intent:)` 直接在 Live Activity 上操作。

audience: **想加入或精進 Live Activity 與 Dynamic Island** 的 iOS 開發者。
gloss_en: Live Activities essentials
takeaway_en: Build, update, and optimize a **Live Activity** from scratch with ActivityKit, covering Dynamic Island, StandBy, the new small style, and App Intents interaction.

points_en.text: Define data with `ActivityAttributes` and `ContentState`, and build the Live Activity views with `ActivityConfiguration` and the **Dynamic Island** regions.
Start with `Activity.request` and update content with `activity.update`, after confirming it's enabled via `ActivityAuthorizationInfo`.
Adds support for the **`activityFamily` small** style (`supplementalActivityFamilies([.small])`), letting you customize presentation based on the `activityFamily` environment value.
Use environment values like `isDynamicIslandLimitedInWidth` and `showsWidgetContainerBackground` to optimize the narrow Dynamic Island and the **StandBy** background.
Add interactivity with `LiveActivityIntent`, binding the intent to `Button(intent:)` to act directly on the Live Activity.

audience_en: iOS developers **looking to add or refine Live Activities and Dynamic Island**.

deepdive.title: Introduction
