audience: 適合**開發教育與考試類 App、需在 macOS 上提供安全評量環境的開發者**。
gloss_en: What's new in assessment on macOS
takeaway_en: New options in the Automatic Assessment Configuration framework let you set up precondition checks, accessibility restrictions, and the system experience for education apps on macOS to create a secure testing environment.

points_en.text: Use **precondition checks** to require conditions such as SIP, a managed device, or a single user before entering assessment, ensuring a secure environment.
Fine-tune **accessibility restrictions** to individually allow or disable assistive features like VoiceOver, Switch Control, and Zoom.
Use **system experience customization** to customize Menu Bar items, input restrictions (Dictation, autofill, Emoji keyboard), and the Dock's appearance.
Configure which directories and files can be accessed, and use **application launch restrictions** to limit which apps can launch and which scripts can run.

audience_en: For **developers building education and exam apps who need to provide a secure assessment environment on macOS**.
summary: 這場由 Apple Education Technologies 團隊主講，介紹 macOS 27 在 **Automatic Assessment Configuration**（AAC）框架上的強化。這個框架的用途，是替教育測驗或證照認證機構打造一個安全、鎖定的考試環境。要使用它，你的 app 必須先透過 Apple Developer portal 申請受限制的 **Automatic Assessment Configuration entitlement**。整場示範都圍繞一個範例考試 app，逐一展示各項 API 能力。

內容分成五大塊。第一是**系統前置條件檢查**（precondition checks）：在考試開始前，app 可要求 Mac 已啟用 System Integrity Protection、已 MDM 註冊、只有單一帳號登入且為指定帳號類型（如 standard），並要求關閉 Lockdown Mode 與 iCloud Private Relay，確保裝置處於難以竄改的硬化狀態。第二是**無障礙限制**：預設既有的輔助功能會在考試中持續運作以確保公平，但對於沒有核可需求的學生，可逐項以 `allowsAccessibility*` 屬性關閉如 Switch Control 等可載入使用者內容的功能（設為 true 只是允許、並非強制開啟）。第三是**系統體驗客製化**，可透過 `allowsMenuBar`、`allowedMenuBarItems`、`allowedAppleMenuItems` 篩選選單列；以 `allowsDictation`、`allowsAutoFill`、`allowsStructuralInput`、`allowsEmojiKeyboard` 關閉可能洩漏答案的輸入法；用 `allowsDock` 提供聚焦的 Dock；並以 `allowedDirectoriesAndFiles` 把 Finder 加為 participant 後限制可存取的目錄與檔案。

第四是**應用程式啟動限制**：把 `allowOnlyParticipantsToRun` 設為 true，系統會在考試開始時關閉所有非必要的 process，只留下主考試 app、明確允許的 participant 與必要系統 process；再以 `allowsUserScriptExecution = false` 阻擋 Shortcut 與 Automator 腳本執行，避免螢幕擷取、按鍵側錄或外傳資料等威脅。最後是**最佳實務**：讓框架替你處理安全工作而非自己重造輪子、只限制考試真正需要的最小範圍、把無障礙視為必要需求而非事後例外、用框架的 transition callback 來驅動 app 狀態（因為 session 不是在呼叫 begin/end 當下立即轉換）、並在每個 macOS beta 推出當天就用完整測試矩陣重新驗證並立即回報 Feedback。整體而言，AAC 用單一統一的 API，就能驗證系統安全前提、調整無障礙配套、客製使用者體驗並鎖定執行環境。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: 由 Education Technologies 團隊的工程師 Chris 開場，說明 **Automatic Assessment Configuration** 框架在 macOS 27 的強化，目的是替交付教育測驗或證照的機構打造安全、鎖定的環境。使用前須透過 Apple Developer portal 申請受限制的 **AAC entitlement**。本場將涵蓋五大主題：系統前置條件、無障礙限制、系統體驗客製化、應用程式啟動限制與最佳實務，全程以一個範例考試 app 示範。

deepdive.title: Precondition checks
deepdive.body: 說明在考試開始前做**系統前置條件檢查**對於確保 Mac 處於硬化狀態的重要性。app 可要求啟用 **System Integrity Protection**、已 **MDM 註冊**、只有單一帳號登入、且帳號為指定類型（如 standard）這四項，共同確保裝置難以竄改；另可要求關閉 **Lockdown Mode** 與 **iCloud Private Relay**，避免這些隱私安全功能干擾考試的基礎設施需求。

deepdive.title: Set up precondition checks
deepdive.body: 示範在 **`AEAssessmentConfiguration`** 物件上設定屬性來加入前置條件，此物件即定義一場 assessment session 參數的核心。範例程式碼要求登入帳號必須是 standard 帳號。若學生裝置不符合一項或多項要求，系統會顯示警示，告知必須先解決哪些問題才能繼續。

deepdive.title: Accessibility restrictions
deepdive.body: 說明 macOS 內建完整的無障礙功能，是讓視覺、聽覺、肢體或認知需求者公平參與考試的關鍵，毋須第三方輔助軟體。預設情況下選單列與 Dock 被隱藏，但既有已啟用的無障礙功能會在 session 中持續運作（如示範中的 **Switch Control**）。不過某些功能可載入使用者自訂內容，因此對沒有核可配套需求的學生關閉它們是重要的安全措施。

deepdive.title: Restrict accessibility features
deepdive.body: 示範一個允許所有無障礙功能、僅限制 **Switch Control** 的設定。重點提醒：把屬性設為 true 並不會「啟用」對應功能，只是允許它在使用者已開啟時於考試中可用。當 session 開始時，被限制的 Switch Control 會被自動結束，且在 session 期間無法再次啟動。

deepdive.title: System experience customization
deepdive.body: 介紹框架最強大的領域之一——**系統體驗客製化**，調整學生在考試中與 macOS 互動的方式。macOS 透過選單列、選單列項目（如 Wi-Fi、Volume）、Dock、Dictation 與 AutoFill 等輸入技術、以及 Finder 與開啟／儲存對話框等熟悉元素提供流暢環境，這些都是可被裁切調整的對象。

deepdive.title: Customize the Menu Bar items
deepdive.body: 示範以 **`allowsMenuBar`** 開啟選單列讓學生取用必要的 app 功能，並用 **`allowedMenuBarItems`** 定義允許清單（如 battery、clock、volume），移除可能成為資訊外洩管道的項目。這些 menu extra 不會被強制開啟，而是在原本就存在時才於 session 中持續可用；另以 **`allowedAppleMenuItems`** 客製 Apple 選單（範例只顯示 sleep，設空陣列則只留「About This Mac」）。

deepdive.title: Define input restrictions
deepdive.body: 說明哪些輸入法可能不慎提供提示或正確答案：**Dictation** 會自動產生正確拼字、emoji picker 提供可搜尋的符號庫、structural input 揭露字元組成線索，**AutoFill** 則可能從 Contacts 等來源帶入預載答案或參考資料。把 `allowsDictation`、`allowsAutoFill`、`allowsStructuralInput`、`allowsEmojiKeyboard` 設為 false，即可在 Edit 選單與支援這些功能的 UI 控制項中隱藏並阻止其使用。

deepdive.title: Enable dock appearance
deepdive.body: 示範把 **`allowsDock`** 設為 true 來啟用篩選過的 Dock 體驗，提供學生聚焦的工作區以便尋找與切換 app。考試中 Dock 只顯示被允許的 app，除了恆常存在的 Finder 與 Trash 錨點外，僅出現該 session 允許的 app；但即使 Finder 出現，除非明確加為 participant，否則仍無法存取。

deepdive.title: Set allowed directories and files
deepdive.body: 說明若考試 app 需與指定檔案互動，可允許存取 Finder 並使用標準開啟／儲存對話框。示範先把 **Finder 加為 participant**，再以 **`allowedDirectoriesAndFiles`** 將 Documents 目錄列入允許清單供學生儲存草稿。此設定也會同步篩選標準 Open/Save 面板中可見的目錄與檔案，學生只看得到被允許的目錄。

deepdive.title: Application launch restrictions
deepdive.body: 說明對考試完整性的最後一層控制——限制考試中可執行的 process。非必要的 process 可能被用來擷取螢幕內容、側錄按鍵、向外部傳輸資料或以其他方式破壞安全測試環境。因此你可能會想把允許執行的範圍限縮到只剩考試 app 與你允許的 participant app，並一併關閉 Shortcuts 與 Automator 動作的執行。

deepdive.title: Set application launch restrictions
deepdive.body: 示範把 **`allowOnlyParticipantsToRun`** 設為 true，告訴系統在考試開始時關閉非必要 process，只允許主考試 app、明確允許的 participant 與必要系統 process 執行。同時把 **`allowsUserScriptExecution`** 設為 false 以阻止 Shortcut 與 Automator 腳本。示範中考試前 Safari、Notes 與一個長時間執行的 Shortcut 都在運作，開始後只剩範例 app 與其 participant（Finder），其餘背景 process 皆被停止且無法存取。

deepdive.title: Best practices
deepdive.body: 整理每位開發者都應考量的最佳實務：善用框架深度系統整合替你保護環境，別自己重造等效功能而應採用框架 API 並刪除冗餘程式碼；只限制考試真正需要的最小範圍，從寬鬆開始再刻意收緊；把無障礙視為必要需求、從第一天起就設計支援輔助技術。此外要記得 session 轉換不是在呼叫 begin/end 當下立即發生，應註冊框架的 **transition callback** 來驅動 app 狀態；並在每個 macOS beta 推出當天就用完整測試矩陣重新驗證並立即回報 Feedback。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 總結建議的後續步驟：用系統預檢驗證裝置完整性、啟用無障礙功能提供公平的考試體驗、客製選單列項目／Dock／檔案系統以提供熟悉直覺的體驗、封鎖非必要 process 來保護執行環境，並以真實考試流程在 macOS 上測試你的方案。無論是課堂測驗 app 或全國標準化測驗平台，**AutomaticAssessmentConfiguration** 框架都能透過單一統一的 API 驗證安全前提、調整無障礙配套、客製體驗並鎖定執行環境。

summary_en: Presented by Apple's Education Technologies team, this session covers the enhancements to the **Automatic Assessment Configuration** (AAC) framework in macOS 27. The framework exists to create a secure, locked-down environment for organizations delivering education assessments or certifications. To use it, your app needs the restricted **Automatic Assessment Configuration entitlement**, requestable through the Apple Developer portal. The whole talk demonstrates the API capabilities through a sample assessment app.

The content breaks into five areas. First, **precondition checks**: before an exam begins, your app can require that System Integrity Protection is enabled, the Mac is MDM enrolled, only a single account is signed in, and that account is a specific type (such as standard), plus require Lockdown Mode and iCloud Private Relay to be disabled—together ensuring a hardened, tamper-resistant device. Second, **accessibility restrictions**: already-enabled features keep working during a session for fairness, but for students without an approved accommodation you can disable customizable features like Switch Control via the `allowsAccessibility*` properties (setting true only allows, it does not force-enable). Third, **system experience customization** via `allowsMenuBar`, `allowedMenuBarItems`, and `allowedAppleMenuItems` to filter the Menu Bar; `allowsDictation`, `allowsAutoFill`, `allowsStructuralInput`, and `allowsEmojiKeyboard` to disable answer-leaking input methods; `allowsDock` for a focused Dock; and `allowedDirectoriesAndFiles` (after adding Finder as a participant) to restrict file access.

Fourth, **application launch restrictions**: setting `allowOnlyParticipantsToRun` to true shuts down all non-essential processes at session start, leaving only the main app, allowlisted participants, and essential system processes, while `allowsUserScriptExecution = false` blocks Shortcuts and Automator scripts—mitigating screen capture, keystroke logging, and data exfiltration threats. Finally, **best practices**: let the framework do the security work rather than rolling your own, restrict only the minimum the assessment requires, treat accessibility as a requirement rather than an afterthought, drive app state off the framework's transition callbacks (sessions don't transition the instant you call begin/end), and re-validate against every macOS beta the day it drops with your full test matrix, filing Feedback immediately. Overall, AAC verifies security prerequisites, tailors accessibility, customizes the experience, and locks down the runtime through a single unified API.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Chris, an engineer on the Education Technologies team, opens by explaining the enhancements to the **Automatic Assessment Configuration** framework in macOS 27, which helps create a secure, locked-down environment for organizations delivering education assessments or certifications. Using it requires the restricted **AAC entitlement** from the Apple Developer portal. The session covers five areas—system preconditions, accessibility restrictions, system experience customization, application launch restrictions, and best practices—all demonstrated with a sample assessment app.

deepdive_en.title: Precondition checks
deepdive_en.body: Explains why running **system precondition checks** before an exam matters for ensuring the Mac is in a hardened state. An app can require that **System Integrity Protection** is enabled, the Mac is **MDM enrolled**, only a single account is signed in, and the account is a specific type (such as standard)—four checks that together ensure a tamper-resistant device. It can additionally require that **Lockdown Mode** and **iCloud Private Relay** are disabled so these privacy and security features don't interfere with the assessment's infrastructure requirements.

deepdive_en.title: Set up precondition checks
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates adding preconditions by setting properties on the **`AEAssessmentConfiguration`** object, which defines an assessment session's parameters. The example code requires the signed-in account to be a standard account. If a student's device fails one or more requirements, an alert is shown informing them which issues must be resolved before continuing.

deepdive_en.title: Accessibility restrictions
deepdive_en.body: Notes that macOS includes a comprehensive suite of accessibility features essential for equitable exam access without third-party assistive software. By default the Menu Bar and Dock are hidden, but currently enabled accessibility features keep working during the session (as shown with **Switch Control**). However, some features can be customized with user-generated content, so disabling them for students without an approved accommodation is an important security measure.

deepdive_en.title: Restrict accessibility features
deepdive_en.body: Shows a configuration that allows every accessibility feature except **Switch Control**. The key caveat: setting a property to true does not enable the corresponding feature—it merely allows it to be used during an assessment when the user has it on. When the session starts, the restricted Switch Control is automatically quit and cannot be relaunched for the duration of the session.

deepdive_en.title: System experience customization
deepdive_en.body: Introduces one of the framework's most powerful areas—**system experience customization**, tailoring how students interact with macOS during an assessment. The familiar macOS experience comes from the Menu Bar, Menu Bar items (Wi-Fi, Volume), the Dock, input technologies like Dictation and AutoFill, and filesystem interaction via Finder and the Open/Save dialogs—all of which can be tailored.

deepdive_en.title: Customize the Menu Bar items
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates enabling the Menu Bar with **`allowsMenuBar`** so students can access essential app functions, and using **`allowedMenuBarItems`** to define an allowlist (such as battery, clock, volume) while removing items that could leak content. These menu extras aren't forced on—they remain available only if already present. The Apple menu is also customized via **`allowedAppleMenuItems`** (the example shows only sleep; an empty array leaves only "About This Mac").

deepdive_en.title: Define input restrictions
deepdive_en.body: Explains which input methods could inadvertently provide hints or answers: **Dictation** auto-produces correct spelling, the emoji picker exposes a searchable symbol library, structural input reveals character composition clues, and **AutoFill** can inject pre-loaded answers or reference material from sources like Contacts. Setting `allowsDictation`, `allowsAutoFill`, `allowsStructuralInput`, and `allowsEmojiKeyboard` to false hides them in menus and prevents their use in UI controls that normally support them.

deepdive_en.title: Enable dock appearance
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates setting **`allowsDock`** to true for a filtered Dock that gives students a focused workspace to find and switch between apps. During the assessment the Dock shows only the allowed apps; beyond the always-present Finder and Trash anchors, only the session's allowed apps appear. Even though Finder is shown, it isn't accessible unless explicitly added as a participant.

deepdive_en.title: Set allowed directories and files
deepdive_en.body: Explains that if the app needs to interact with designated files, you can allow Finder access and use the standard Open/Save dialogs. The demo first adds **Finder as a participant**, then uses **`allowedDirectoriesAndFiles`** to allowlist the Documents directory for saving scratch work. The same setting filters the directories and files shown in the standard Open and Save panels, so students see only the allowlisted directory.

deepdive_en.title: Application launch restrictions
deepdive_en.body: Covers the final layer of control—restricting which processes may run during an assessment. Non-essential processes can capture screen content, log keystrokes, transmit data to external parties, or otherwise undermine the secure testing environment. Accordingly, you may want to restrict allowed processes to just your assessment app and allowlisted participants, and also shut down Shortcuts and Automator actions.

deepdive_en.title: Set application launch restrictions
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates setting **`allowOnlyParticipantsToRun`** to true, telling the system to shut down non-essential processes at session start so only the main app, explicitly allowlisted participants, and essential system processes run. It also sets **`allowsUserScriptExecution`** to false to block Shortcut and Automator scripts. In the demo, Safari, Notes, and a long-running Shortcut are running before the exam; afterward only the sample app and its participant (Finder) remain, with all user-initiated background processes stopped.

deepdive_en.title: Best practices
deepdive_en.body: Rounds up practices every developer should consider: let the framework's deep system integration secure the environment rather than rolling your own equivalents, adopting its APIs and deleting redundant code; restrict only the minimum the assessment requires, starting permissive and tightening deliberately; and treat accessibility as a requirement, designing for assistive technologies from day one. It also stresses that sessions don't transition the instant you call begin/end, so register for the framework's **transition callbacks** to drive app state, and re-validate on every macOS beta the day it drops, filing Feedback immediately.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Summarizes the recommended next steps: use system pre-checks to validate device integrity, enable accessibility features for an equitable experience, provide a familiar experience by customizing Menu Bar items, the Dock, and the file system, secure the runtime by blocking non-essential processes, and test with real exam workflows on macOS. Whether building a classroom quiz app or a nationwide standardized testing platform, the **AutomaticAssessmentConfiguration** framework verifies security prerequisites, tailors accessibility, customizes the experience, and locks down the runtime through a single unified API.

title: Run local agentic AI on the Mac using MLX
gloss: 用 MLX 在 Mac 上執行本機 agentic AI
takeaway: 在 Mac 上以 MLX-LM 啟動本機 OpenAI 相容伺服器，讓 AI agent 兼顧隱私、低延遲與離線運作，並可透過分散式推論擴展更大模型。
chapters: Set up MLX-LM and start the local server
Configure an agent to use your local MLX server

points.text: 在本機執行 AI agent，兼顧**隱私、低延遲與離線存取**，由 MLX 進展與 Mac 硬體共同支撐。
用 **mlx_lm.server** 啟動本機伺服器，提供與 **OpenAI 相容**的 `/v1/chat/completions` 端點。
把 agent（例如 **opencode**）的 baseURL 指向 `http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1` 即可改用本機模型。
說明如何**讓 agent 變快**，並透過並行處理提升吞吐。
以 **mlx.launch** 搭配 hostfile 與 jaccl backend 進行**分散式推論**，跑更大的模型。

audience: **想在 Mac 上自建本機 LLM／agent 服務的開發者與 ML 工程師**，重視隱私與離線運作的人。
gloss_en: Run local agentic AI on the Mac using MLX
takeaway_en: Launch a local OpenAI-compatible server with MLX-LM on the Mac so AI agents get privacy, low latency, and offline operation, and scale to larger models with distributed inference.

points_en.text: Run AI agents locally with **privacy, low latency, and offline access**, backed by MLX advances and Mac hardware.
Use **mlx_lm.server** to launch a local server that exposes an **OpenAI-compatible** `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint.
Point an agent's (for example, **opencode**) baseURL at `http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1` to switch to the local model.
Explains how to **make your agent faster** and increase throughput through concurrency.
Run **distributed inference** with **mlx.launch** plus a hostfile and the jaccl backend to run larger models.

audience_en: **Developers and ML engineers who want to self-host a local LLM/agent service on the Mac** and care about privacy and offline operation.
summary: 這場由 MLX 團隊主講，示範如何**完全在 Mac 本機上**跑起 agentic AI 工作流程——不靠雲端、不需 API key，資料全程留在自己的機器上。講者先區分傳統 chat 與 **agentic loop** 的差別：chat 是你發 prompt、模型回應，後續動作得自己來；agent 則由它自行與模型對話決定要做什麼，再呼叫工具（執行指令、讀檔、打 API），觀察結果後回到模型推理下一步，如此循環直到任務完成。這整個 loop 在 Apple silicon 上能在本機跑完，帶來隱私、零成本與隨時可用的好處。

核心是 **local agentic AI stack** 四層：底層是為 Apple silicon 打造的開源陣列框架 **MLX**（負責 Metal 加速與記憶體管理）；其上是 **MLX-LM**，可載入、執行、量化、微調來自 HuggingFace 的數千個模型；再上是 **MLX-LM Server**，一個 OpenAI 相容的 HTTP server，支援結構化 tool calling 與 reasoning 模型，是任何雲端 LLM API 的 drop-in 替代品；最頂層則是 agent 本身，凡是會講 OpenAI chat completions 協定的（Xcode、OpenCode、自訂腳本等）都能直接接上。設定只要三步：`pip install mlx-lm`、用支援 tool calling 的模型啟動 `mlx_lm.server`、再把 agent 的 base URL 指向本機 server。

最後講解 MLX 如何榨乾硬體效能、解決本機跑 agent 的三大挑戰。**Prompt processing**：agentic session 動輒數十萬 token 且多為輸入，M5 的 **Neural Accelerators** 讓矩陣乘法比 M4 快四倍，prompt 處理也近乎同步加速，且無需改任何程式。**Concurrency**：agent 常派多個 subagent 並行，MLX-LM Server 以 **continuous batching** 動態分組同時處理，避免請求排隊卡住。**Model size**：超大模型（如 1.6 兆參數的 DeepSeek）單機放不下時，MLX 的 distributed 支援可跨多台 Mac（Thunderbolt 或 Ethernet）分片模型；macOS 26.2 起的 **Thunderbolt RDMA** 讓四節點分散式推論最高快三倍。講者以從零打造 SwiftUI 繪圖 app、並在 Xcode 中修 bug 等實機 demo 收尾。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: MLX 團隊工程師 Angelos 開場，主旨是讓你**完全在 Mac 本機**建構並執行 agentic AI 工作流程——不靠雲端、不需 API key。強調過去一年 AI agent 從研究原型走入日常生產力工具，而 Apple silicon 讓整個流程能在本機完成，兼顧隱私、低延遲與無使用成本。

deepdive.title: The chat and agentic loop
deepdive.body: 對比兩種模式：傳統 **chat** 是你發 prompt、模型回應，要採取行動得自己來；**agent** 則由它與模型對話決定動作，再呼叫工具（執行指令、讀檔、打 API），觀察結果後回到模型推理下一步。這個「user→agent→model→tools」的循環就是 **agentic loop**，會持續到任務完成。講者展示本機 demo：請 agent 抓取 MLX repo 的近期 PR、摘要變更並標出需注意處，模型在本機推理、只有 git 指令會連網。

deepdive.title: Local agentic AI stack
deepdive.body: 拆解四層 stack：底層 **MLX**（為 Apple silicon 打造的開源陣列框架，負責低階運算、Metal 加速與記憶體管理）；其上 **MLX-LM**（載入、執行、量化、微調 HuggingFace 上數千模型，提供 CLI 與 Python API）；再上 **MLX-LM Server**（OpenAI 相容 HTTP server，支援 tool calling 與 reasoning 模型，是雲端 LLM API 的 drop-in 替代）；最頂為 agent。並指出 Ollama、LM Studio、vLLM 等熱門工具其實都建在 MLX 之上。

deepdive.title: Setting up your own agent
deepdive.body: 概述只要三步就能從零到完整本機 agentic 工作流程，接著逐步示範。

deepdive.title: Set up MLX-LM and start the local server
deepdive.body: 第一步 `pip install mlx-lm` 安裝所需一切；第二步用支援 tool calling 的模型啟動 `mlx_lm.server`（建議先用小模型測試），server 載入模型後即在 localhost 接受請求。

deepdive.title: Configure an agent to use your local MLX server
deepdive.body: 第三步把 agent 的 base URL 指向本機 server 即可，agent 不在意模型跑在 Mac 還是雲端。以 **OpenCode** 設定為例：定義一個 local provider、把 URL 設為 localhost、設定 server 預期的模型名稱，並要 OpenCode 一律使用此本機模型。

deepdive.title: Making agents fast
deepdive.body: 進入效能主題，說明 MLX 如何因應本機跑 agent 的關鍵挑戰。第一個挑戰是 **prompt processing**：agentic loop 每次收到 tool 輸出都得重新處理大量 context，且 session 動輒數十萬 token、多數非生成。M5 的 **Neural Accelerators** 讓矩陣乘法比 M4 快四倍，配合 MLX 專用 kernel 幾乎等比加速 prompt 處理，且**無需任何程式改動**，MLX 會自動選最佳 kernel。

deepdive.title: Concurrency and distributed inference
deepdive.body: 第二個挑戰 **concurrency**：agent 常派多個 subagent 並行（讀文件、搜程式、寫測試），形成多請求同時打本機模型。MLX-LM Server 以 **continuous batching** 動態把進來的請求分組在 GPU 上一起處理，新請求可中途加入而不需等待，避免排隊卡住。第三個挑戰 **model size**：超大模型單機放不下時，MLX 的 distributed 支援可跨多台 Mac 分片，既能跑更大模型也能並行加速 prompt 處理。

deepdive.title: Launch distributed inference with MLX
deepdive.body: 示範以 `mlx.launch` 搭配描述節點與連線型態的 hostfile 啟動分散式 server，模型會自動分片到所有裝置。並指出 macOS 26.2 起支援 **Thunderbolt RDMA**，提供低延遲、高頻寬通訊，使分散式推論最高快三倍（四節點）。延伸推薦「Explore distributed inference and training with MLX」一場。

deepdive.title: More examples
deepdive.body: 進階實機 demo：請 agent 在空白 Xcode 專案中從零打造一個 iPad 繪圖 app——agent 先看目錄結構、擬定計畫、寫程式並自行 build、邊修錯誤，兩分鐘就出第一版；再請它把筆刷改成圓角端點並重編。最後示範在 Xcode 的 Intelligence 設定中接上本機 MLX server（Locally Hosted provider、設定 port），讓模型直接讀專案、理解 build 錯誤並修復刻意植入的 bug。全程程式不離開 Mac。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 總結：今天展示了從 MLX 到 agent 的完整本機 stack，以及 Neural Accelerators、continuous batching、distributed inference 如何讓它變快。起步只需安裝 MLX-LM、啟動 server、把你愛用的 agent 指向它，且所有內容皆為開源、即刻可用。

summary_en: Presented by the MLX team, this session shows how to run agentic AI workflows **entirely on your Mac**—no cloud, no API keys, with your data never leaving the machine. The speaker contrasts traditional chat with the **agentic loop**: in chat you send a prompt and the model replies, but acting on it is on you; an agent talks to the model to decide what to do, calls tools (run commands, read files, hit APIs), observes results, and loops back until the task is done. On Apple silicon the whole loop runs locally, giving privacy, zero usage cost, and always-on availability.

The core is the four-layer **local agentic AI stack**: at the bottom, **MLX**, the open-source array framework for Apple silicon handling Metal acceleration and memory; above it, **MLX-LM** to load, run, quantize, and fine-tune thousands of HuggingFace models; then **MLX-LM Server**, an OpenAI-compatible HTTP server with structured tool calling and reasoning models that's a drop-in replacement for any cloud LLM API; and at the top, the agent itself—anything speaking the OpenAI chat completions protocol (Xcode, OpenCode, custom scripts) plugs in directly. Setup is three steps: `pip install mlx-lm`, launch `mlx_lm.server` with a tool-calling model, and point the agent's base URL at the local server.

Finally, the talk covers how MLX squeezes the hardware to solve three challenges of local agents. **Prompt processing**: agentic sessions run to hundreds of thousands of (mostly input) tokens, and M5's **Neural Accelerators** make matrix multiply 4x faster than M4, translating almost directly to prompt-processing speedup with no code changes. **Concurrency**: agents spawn parallel subagents, and MLX-LM Server uses **continuous batching** to dynamically group simultaneous requests so they don't stall in a queue. **Model size**: when a model (like the 1.6-trillion-parameter DeepSeek) won't fit on one machine, MLX's distributed support shards it across multiple Macs over Thunderbolt or Ethernet, and **Thunderbolt RDMA** (macOS 26.2) makes four-node distributed inference up to 3x faster. Live demos—building a SwiftUI drawing app from scratch and fixing an Xcode bug—close the session.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: MLX engineer Angelos opens with the goal of building and running agentic AI workflows **entirely on your Mac**—no cloud, no API keys. He notes AI agents have gone from research prototypes to everyday productivity tools, and Apple silicon lets the whole loop run locally with privacy, low latency, and no usage costs.

deepdive_en.title: The chat and agentic loop
deepdive_en.body: Contrasts two modes: in **chat** you send a prompt and the model replies, but acting is on you; an **agent** talks to the model to decide actions, calls tools (run commands, read files, hit APIs), observes results, and reasons about the next step. This user→agent→model→tools cycle is the **agentic loop**, repeating until the task is done. A local demo has the agent fetch recent PRs from the MLX repo, summarize changes, and flag what needs attention—reasoning locally, with only git commands hitting the network.

deepdive_en.title: Local agentic AI stack
deepdive_en.body: Breaks down the four layers: **MLX** at the bottom (open-source array framework for Apple silicon, handling low-level compute, Metal acceleration, memory); **MLX-LM** above (load, run, quantize, fine-tune thousands of HuggingFace models, with CLI and Python API); then **MLX-LM Server** (OpenAI-compatible HTTP server with tool calling and reasoning models, a drop-in for cloud LLM APIs); and the agent on top. Notes that Ollama, LM Studio, and vLLM all build on MLX.

deepdive_en.title: Setting up your own agent
deepdive_en.body: Overview that just three steps take you from zero to a fully local agentic workflow, which the session then walks through.

deepdive_en.title: Set up MLX-LM and start the local server
deepdive_en.body: Step one, `pip install mlx-lm` gets everything; step two, launch `mlx_lm.server` with a tool-calling model (start small to test), which loads the model and accepts requests on localhost.

deepdive_en.title: Configure an agent to use your local MLX server
deepdive_en.body: Step three: point the agent's base URL at the local server—the agent doesn't care whether the model runs on the Mac or the cloud. The **OpenCode** example defines a local provider, sets the URL to localhost, names the model the server expects, and tells OpenCode to use this local model for everything.

deepdive_en.title: Making agents fast
deepdive_en.body: Enters performance, explaining how MLX addresses the key challenges. First is **prompt processing**: the loop reprocesses large context every time it receives tool output, and sessions run to hundreds of thousands of mostly non-generated tokens. M5's **Neural Accelerators** make matrix multiply 4x faster than M4, and MLX's specialized kernels translate that almost directly to prompt-processing speedup—with **no code changes**, since MLX auto-selects the best kernel.

deepdive_en.title: Concurrency and distributed inference
deepdive_en.body: Second challenge, **concurrency**: agents spawn parallel subagents (reading docs, searching code, writing tests), hitting the local model with multiple simultaneous requests. MLX-LM Server uses **continuous batching** to dynamically group incoming requests on the GPU, letting new ones join mid-batch without waiting, so nothing stalls in a queue. Third challenge, **model size**: when a model won't fit on one machine, MLX's distributed support shards it across multiple Macs, running larger models and parallelizing prompt processing.

deepdive_en.title: Launch distributed inference with MLX
deepdive_en.body: Shows launching a distributed server with `mlx.launch` plus a hostfile describing nodes and connection type, with the model auto-sharded across devices. Notes **Thunderbolt RDMA** (macOS 26.2) provides low-latency, high-bandwidth communication, making distributed inference up to 3x faster on four nodes, and points to the companion session 'Explore distributed inference and training with MLX'.

deepdive_en.title: More examples
deepdive_en.body: Advanced live demos: the agent builds an iPad drawing app from scratch in a blank Xcode project—inspecting the directory, planning, writing code, building itself, and fixing errors, with a first version in two minutes—then adds rounded end caps and recompiles. Finally, in Xcode's Intelligence settings it connects to the running MLX server (a Locally Hosted provider with a port) so the model reads project files, understands build errors, and fixes a deliberately introduced bug—all without code leaving the Mac.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Wrap-up: the session showed the full local stack from MLX up to the agent, and how Neural Accelerators, continuous batching, and distributed inference make it fast. To start, install MLX-LM, launch the server, and point your favorite agent at it—everything shown is open-source and available now.

audience_en: Machine learning engineers familiar with MLX who want to **scale large-model inference and fine-tuning across multiple Macs**.
summary: 本場由 MLX 團隊深入講解如何用桌上的多台 Mac 組成 cluster，跨機器做**分散式推論與微調**。問題背景是：本機 LLM 越來越大、能力越強，但單機的記憶體、運算或頻寬終會成為瓶頸。講者先鋪陳完整的軟硬體 stack：機器間需要實體 interconnect 與傳輸協定，macOS 26.2 起支援 **Thunderbolt 5 上的 RDMA**（直接記憶體互傳、繞過大部分 CPU/OS 開銷）；其上是 Apple 開源的集合通訊函式庫 **JACCL**（提供 send 與 all-reduce 等通訊原語，且不限於 ML）；最頂是 **MLX** 與 **MLX LM**，負責跨 cluster 協調分散式工作。

接著以四台 M3 Ultra 實際組 cluster。**拓樸**會直接影響通訊時間：通訊時間由固定的 latency 與隨資料量成長的 transfer time 組成；JACCL 支援 **mesh**（每台直連每台，latency 最低）與 **ring**（只連兩個鄰居，省線省埠、可多線增頻寬但 latency 較高），並會依訊息大小與操作**自動選擇**最佳拓樸，因此建議全部連成 mesh。組好後在系統設定開啟 RDMA 並重開機；以 **`mlx.launch`** 搭配 JSON hostfile 透過 SSH 啟動各節點，hostfile 可用 **`mlx.distributed_config`** 自動產生（含 `--auto-setup` 自動設定 Thunderbolt 網路、`--backend jaccl`／`jaccl-ring` 決定 mesh 或 ring）。

最後是重頭戲：分散式推論與微調。把單機的 `mlx_lm.chat` 用 `mlx.launch --hostfile` 包起來即可跨 cluster 跑，模型自動分片——27B 的 Qwen 在四台上比單台快近三倍。模型太大時（如 1 兆參數的 Kimi）可用兩種策略分片：**pipeline parallelism**（按深度切，通訊單純但不加速）與 **tensor parallelism**（按寬度切，每層每 token 都通訊、可加速，故需 mesh 低延遲，且為預設）。微調走 **data-parallel**：每台複製模型、各吃不同 batch、再平均梯度，用 `mlx_lm.lora` 並把 `--batch-size` 乘上裝置數即可，實測四台快三倍以上。除了 CLI，分散式通訊也透過 **Python、Swift、C++ API** 開放（含直接呼叫 JACCL 的 all-sum），方便嵌入自己的 app。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: MLX 團隊研究員 Tatiana 開場：本機 LLM 持續變大變強，最終會撞到單機的記憶體、運算或頻寬上限。本場承接「Run local agentic AI on the Mac using MLX」，深入講如何用桌上的多台 Mac 跨機器擴展——跑更大的模型或加速推論與訓練。路線是先 CLI、再 Python API、最後 Swift 嵌入 app。

deepdive.title: Distributed communication
deepdive.body: 鋪陳通訊 stack：機器間需要實體 **interconnect** 與傳輸協定。macOS 26.2 起支援 **Thunderbolt 5 上的 RDMA**，直接把資料從一台的記憶體搬到另一台、繞過多數 CPU/OS 開銷，提供高頻寬低延遲。其上是 Apple 開源的集合通訊函式庫 **JACCL**，提供跨機器送資料與彙整結果的通訊原語（不限 ML）；最頂是用 JACCL 做分散式推論與訓練的 **MLX**。

deepdive.title: Setting up your cluster
deepdive.body: 以四台 M3 Ultra 組 cluster：用 Thunderbolt 5 線連接，而連法（拓樸）直接影響通訊時間。概述接下來的步驟——先談決定通訊時間的因素，再看 JACCL 支援哪些拓樸與取捨，接著在機器上啟用 RDMA，最後用 MLX 啟動分散式工作。

deepdive.title: Hostfile format for a 4-node MLX cluster
deepdive.body: 解析描述 cluster 的 JSON hostfile：每個節點一筆，`ssh` 是 `mlx.launch` 連線用的 hostname、`ips` 是 JACCL 初始協調用的本地網路 IP、`rdma` 是各 Thunderbolt peer 連線的 RDMA 裝置名稱清單。可手寫，但更建議用工具自動產生。

deepdive.title: Generate the cluster hostfile with mlx.distributed_config
deepdive.body: 用 **`mlx.distributed_config`** 自動產生 hostfile：傳入 hostname 清單與輸出路徑，可用 `--env` 內嵌環境變數（例如 `MLX_METAL_FAST_SYNCH=1` 加速 GPU↔CPU 同步，對分散式很關鍵）。`--auto-setup` 會自動關閉 Thunderbolt Bridge、把各連線設定為 RDMA；`--backend` 設 `jaccl` 為 mesh、`jaccl-ring` 為 ring。執行時會先檢查 SSH 可達、探測各埠連線拓樸，最後寫出 hostfile。

deepdive.title: Distributed inference and fine-tuning
deepdive.body: 進入重頭戲——分散式語言模型推論與微調，最簡單的入口是 CLI 與 **MLX LM**（建在 MLX 之上的開源套件，提供 CLI 與 Python API 在 Apple silicon 本機跑模型）。

deepdive.title: Run distributed LLM inference with mlx_lm.chat
deepdive.body: 單機用 `mlx_lm.chat` 指定模型與 max-tokens；要跨 cluster，只要用 **`mlx.launch --hostfile`** 包住、在 `--` 後接同樣的 `mlx_lm.chat`（但指向各節點上的遠端路徑），MLX LM 自動分片並協調。實測 27B 的 Qwen 在四台 M3 Ultra 上生成速度約為單台的三倍。注意每台都要裝好 MLX 等函式庫且可存取執行檔。

deepdive.title: Model parallelism strategies
deepdive.body: 處理模型太大（如 1 兆參數的 Kimi、8-bit 仍需約 1TB 記憶體）的兩種分片：**pipeline parallelism** 按深度切，每台持有一組層、資料循序通過，通訊單純（只在層組邊界交換 activation）但不加速；**tensor parallelism** 按寬度切，每台持有每層的一部分、同時處理同一 token，可加速但每層每 token 都要通訊，故低延遲很重要、必須用 mesh。

deepdive.title: Run distributed inference with pipeline parallelism
deepdive.body: tensor parallelism 是 MLX LM 預設策略；要改用 pipeline parallelism 只需在指令後加 `--pipeline`（並非所有模型都支援）。示範用 `mlx.launch` 在 cluster 上跑 1 兆參數的 Kimi（未加 `--pipeline`，即用 tensor parallelism）：mlx.launch 連上每台、MLX LM 載入並分片模型，一行指令就讓巨型模型在本機多台 Mac 上回答問題。

deepdive.title: Distributed fine-tuning
deepdive.body: 說明微調原理：單機把訓練資料切成 batch，每個 batch 算梯度並更新權重，重複多輪直到品質達標。要用多台加速，採 **data-parallel**——每台複製模型、各吃不同 batch、各自算梯度，再平均梯度讓更新涵蓋所有 batch，因此 N 台理論上可快 N 倍。

deepdive.title: Run distributed fine-tuning with mlx_lm.lora
deepdive.body: 與單機唯一差別是用 `mlx.launch` 啟動、指向各節點上的 `mlx_lm.lora`，資料分片由 MLX LM 處理，指令幾乎相同——把 `--batch-size` 乘上裝置數，讓每台每步仍處理相同樣本數。實測微調 9B 的 Qwen：單台約 180 tokens/秒、四台約 600 tokens/秒，超過三倍加速，等於把桌上裝置變成本機訓練 cluster。

deepdive.title: CLI, Python, Swift, and C++ APIs
deepdive.body: 前面以 CLT 為主，但 MLX 也透過彈性的 **Python、Swift、C++ API** 對分片與分散式操作提供細緻控制，可在 Python／C++ 實驗或用 Swift 嵌入 app。

deepdive.title: Distributed inference with the MLX LM Python API
deepdive.body: 用 Python API 做分散式推論：先以 `mx.distributed.init(backend="jaccl")` 初始化通訊群組，再定義平行策略（如 tensor parallelism），用 `sharded_load` 分片載入模型，之後就像單機一樣使用——MLX LM 在底層處理所有分散式通訊。

deepdive.title: Shard a layer with the MLX Python API
deepdive.body: 要更細緻控制可用 MLX 本身的低階原語：示範定義一個簡單 `nn.Linear` 後，以 `shard_linear`（strategy="all-to-sharded"）按欄分片，餵入資料即得分片運算結果。

deepdive.title: All-reduce across devices in Python, Swift, and C++
deepdive.body: 示範跨裝置的基礎集合操作 all-reduce：在 Python／Swift／C++ 中先用 JACCL 初始化 distributed group，再用對應 MLX 原語（如 `mx.distributed.all_sum`）對 tensor 做跨機器的集合求和。

deepdive.title: Standalone distributed sum with the JACCL C++ API
deepdive.body: 強調 **JACCL 可獨立使用**、不需 MLX，適用任何需要分散式通訊的應用（含非 ML）。示範純 C++ API：初始化 JACCL group 後，直接用 JACCL（而非 MLX）對 tensor 做跨機器集合求和。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 總結：本場走過讓 Apple silicon 分散式訓練與推論成真的完整 stack，從 Thunderbolt 上的 RDMA 一路到 MLX 與 MLX LM，並展示如何用最少的單機程式改動就從單台擴到多台，換來更快推論、能跑兆級參數模型與更快微調，且涵蓋 CLI、Python、Swift、C++。延伸推薦「Run local agentic AI on the Mac using MLX」與相關文件。

summary_en: The MLX team takes a deep dive into turning the Macs on your desk into a cluster for **distributed inference and fine-tuning**. The motivation: local LLMs keep getting larger and more capable, but a single machine's memory, compute, or bandwidth eventually becomes the limit. The talk first lays out the full stack: machines need a physical interconnect and a transport protocol, and macOS 26.2 adds **RDMA over Thunderbolt 5** (moving data directly between machines' memory, bypassing most CPU/OS overhead); on top sits **JACCL**, Apple's open-source collective communication library (send and all-reduce primitives, not limited to ML); and at the top, **MLX** and **MLX LM** orchestrate distributed work across the cluster.

It then builds a real cluster from four M3 Ultras. **Topology** directly affects communication time, which is made of fixed latency plus transfer time that grows with data size. JACCL supports a **mesh** (every machine directly connected to every other, lowest latency) and a **ring** (each node connects only to its two neighbors—fewer cables/ports, extra bandwidth via multiple cables, but higher latency), and it **automatically picks** the best topology per message size and operation, so connecting everything as a mesh is recommended. After enabling RDMA in Settings and rebooting, you launch nodes over SSH with **`mlx.launch`** plus a JSON hostfile, which **`mlx.distributed_config`** can generate for you (with `--auto-setup` to configure the Thunderbolt network and `--backend jaccl`/`jaccl-ring` to choose mesh or ring).

The payoff is distributed inference and fine-tuning. Wrapping single-device `mlx_lm.chat` in `mlx.launch --hostfile` runs it across the cluster with automatic sharding—a 27B Qwen runs nearly 3x faster on four machines than on one. For models too large for one machine (like the 1-trillion-parameter Kimi), two strategies shard it: **pipeline parallelism** (split by depth—simple communication but no speedup) and **tensor parallelism** (split by width—communicates every layer per token, speeds up inference, needs mesh low latency, and is the default). Fine-tuning uses **data-parallel** training: each machine replicates the model, takes a different batch, and gradients are averaged—done with `mlx_lm.lora` and `--batch-size` scaled by device count, giving over 3x speedup on four machines. Beyond the CLI, distributed communication is also exposed via **Python, Swift, and C++ APIs** (including JACCL all-sum directly) for embedding in your own apps.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: MLX research scientist Tatiana opens: local LLMs keep getting bigger and smarter, eventually hitting a single machine's memory, compute, or bandwidth limits. Building on 'Run local agentic AI on the Mac using MLX', this session dives into scaling across multiple Macs on your desk—running larger models or accelerating inference and training. The path: CLI first, then the Python API, then Swift for embedding in apps.

deepdive_en.title: Distributed communication
deepdive_en.body: Lays out the communication stack: machines need a physical **interconnect** and a transport protocol. macOS 26.2 adds **RDMA over Thunderbolt 5**, moving data directly from one machine's memory to another's and bypassing most CPU/OS overhead for high-bandwidth, low-latency transfer. Above it sits **JACCL**, Apple's open-source collective communication library with primitives for sending and combining data across the group (not ML-only); at the top is **MLX**, which uses JACCL for distributed inference and training.

deepdive_en.title: Setting up your cluster
deepdive_en.body: Builds a cluster from four M3 Ultras connected with Thunderbolt 5 cables, where wiring (topology) directly affects communication time. Outlines the steps: what determines communication time, which topologies JACCL supports and their trade-offs, enabling RDMA, and launching distributed jobs with MLX.

deepdive_en.title: Hostfile format for a 4-node MLX cluster
deepdive_en.body: Walks through the JSON hostfile describing the cluster: one entry per node, with `ssh` (the hostname mlx.launch uses), `ips` (the local-network IP JACCL uses for initial coordination), and `rdma` (a list of RDMA device names per Thunderbolt peer connection). You can write it by hand, but a helper can generate it.

deepdive_en.title: Generate the cluster hostfile with mlx.distributed_config
deepdive_en.body: Uses **`mlx.distributed_config`** to auto-generate the hostfile: pass the host list and an output path, optionally embedding env vars with `--env` (e.g., `MLX_METAL_FAST_SYNCH=1` for faster GPU↔CPU sync, critical for distributed work). `--auto-setup` disables the Thunderbolt Bridge and configures each link for RDMA; `--backend jaccl` means mesh, `jaccl-ring` means ring. The run checks SSH reachability, probes ports to map topology, and writes the hostfile.

deepdive_en.title: Distributed inference and fine-tuning
deepdive_en.body: Enters the main event—distributed LLM inference and fine-tuning—with the easiest entry point being the CLI and **MLX LM** (an open-source package on top of MLX providing CLI tools and a Python API to run models locally on Apple silicon).

deepdive_en.title: Run distributed LLM inference with mlx_lm.chat
deepdive_en.body: Single-device `mlx_lm.chat` takes a model and max-tokens; to go across the cluster, wrap it with **`mlx.launch --hostfile`** and after `--` pass the same `mlx_lm.chat` (pointing to the remote executable path on each node), with MLX LM sharding and coordinating automatically. A 27B Qwen generates roughly 3x faster on four M3 Ultras than on one. Note that all libraries like MLX must be installed and the executable accessible on every machine.

deepdive_en.title: Model parallelism strategies
deepdive_en.body: Handles models too large for one machine (the 1-trillion-parameter Kimi needs ~1TB even at 8-bit) with two sharding approaches: **pipeline parallelism** splits by depth—each machine holds a group of layers and data flows sequentially, with simple communication (only at boundaries) but no speedup; **tensor parallelism** splits by width—each machine holds part of every layer and all process the same token at once, speeding up inference but communicating every layer per token, making low latency (mesh) crucial.

deepdive_en.title: Run distributed inference with pipeline parallelism
deepdive_en.body: Tensor parallelism is MLX LM's default; switching to pipeline parallelism just appends `--pipeline` (not all models support it). The demo runs the 1-trillion-parameter Kimi on the cluster via `mlx.launch` without `--pipeline` (so tensor parallelism): mlx.launch connects to every machine, MLX LM loads and shards the model, and one command has a massive model answering questions across local Macs.

deepdive_en.title: Distributed fine-tuning
deepdive_en.body: Explains fine-tuning: on a single machine you split data into batches, compute gradients and update weights per batch, repeating for passes until quality is reached. To speed up with multiple machines, use **data-parallel** training—replicate the model on each Mac, give each a different batch, compute gradients locally, then average them so the update uses all batches, giving up to N-times speedup with N machines.

deepdive_en.title: Run distributed fine-tuning with mlx_lm.lora
deepdive_en.body: The only difference from single-device is launching with `mlx.launch` pointing to `mlx_lm.lora` on each node; MLX LM handles data sharding and the command is nearly identical—scale `--batch-size` by device count so each machine still processes the same samples per step. Fine-tuning a 9B Qwen runs ~180 tokens/sec on one M3 Ultra vs ~600 on the cluster, over 3x faster, turning desk devices into a local training cluster.

deepdive_en.title: CLI, Python, Swift, and C++ APIs
deepdive_en.body: The examples so far used the CLI, but MLX also exposes fine-grained control over sharding and distributed operations via flexible **Python, Swift, and C++ APIs**—for experimenting in Python/C++ or embedding models in apps with Swift.

deepdive_en.title: Distributed inference with the MLX LM Python API
deepdive_en.body: For distributed inference in Python: initialize the communication group with `mx.distributed.init(backend="jaccl")`, define the parallelism (e.g., tensor parallelism), shard-load the model with `sharded_load`, then use it exactly as on a single device—MLX LM handles all distributed communication under the hood.

deepdive_en.title: Shard a layer with the MLX Python API
deepdive_en.body: For finer control, use MLX's low-level primitives: after defining a simple `nn.Linear`, shard it column-wise with `shard_linear` (strategy="all-to-sharded"), then feed data to get the sharded computation result.

deepdive_en.title: All-reduce across devices in Python, Swift, and C++
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates the basic collective all-reduce: in Python/Swift/C++, initialize the distributed group via JACCL, then perform a collective sum across machines with the corresponding MLX primitive (e.g., `mx.distributed.all_sum`).

deepdive_en.title: Standalone distributed sum with the JACCL C++ API
deepdive_en.body: Stresses that **JACCL works on its own**, without MLX, for any distributed workload (including non-ML). The pure C++ example initializes a JACCL group and performs a collective sum across machines via JACCL directly rather than MLX.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Wrap-up: the session covered the full stack making distributed training and inference possible on Apple silicon, from RDMA over Thunderbolt up to MLX and MLX LM, and showed scaling from one device to many with minimal single-device code changes—yielding faster inference, trillion-parameter models, and faster fine-tuning across CLI, Python, Swift, and C++. It points to 'Run local agentic AI on the Mac using MLX' and the docs for advanced features.

title: Design immersive environments for visionOS apps and the spatial web
gloss: 為 visionOS App 與空間網頁設計沉浸式環境
takeaway: 用前期、製作、後期三階段的工作流,為 visionOS App、網站與 SharePlay 體驗打造擬真的沉浸式環境。

points.text: 教你為 App、網站與 **SharePlay** 體驗打造**擬真(photoreal)的 visionOS 環境**。
**Pre-production(前期)**:規劃環境概念、參考與設計方向。
**Production(製作)**:實際建構環境資產與場景。
**Post-production(後期)**:潤飾與最佳化沉浸式呈現效果。
內容同時涵蓋 App 與**空間網頁(spatial web)**的沉浸式環境設計。

audience: **為 visionOS 或空間網頁打造沉浸式環境的設計師與 3D 內容創作者。**
gloss_en: Design immersive environments for visionOS apps and the spatial web
takeaway_en: Use a three-phase workflow—pre-production, production, and post-production—to build photoreal immersive environments for visionOS apps, websites, and SharePlay experiences.

points_en.text: Learn to build **photoreal visionOS environments** for apps, websites, and **SharePlay** experiences.
**Pre-production**: plan the environment concept, references, and design direction.
**Production**: actually build the environment assets and scene.
**Post-production**: polish and optimize the immersive presentation.
The content covers immersive environment design for both apps and the **spatial web**.

audience_en: **Designers and 3D content creators building immersive environments for visionOS or the spatial web.**
summary: 這場由 Apple 人機介面設計師 Michael Breymann 主講，主題是如何為 visionOS app、網站與 SharePlay 體驗設計**沉浸式環境（immersive environments）**。他先點出 visionOS 的系統環境並非單純的背景圖：它是為空間運算打造的**寫實自然場景**，具備真正的**深度與視差（parallax）**，會隨視角改變而回應，再加上動態與**空間音訊（spatial audio）**，讓場景彷彿活著。整場以 Mount Hood、Moon、Jupiter、Yosemite、Thorsmork、Bora Bora 六個系統環境為例，貫穿 **pre-production、production、post-production** 三個階段的設計流程。

**Pre-production（前期）**強調先釐清意圖：為何要做這個環境、想呈現什麼特質、使用者會怎麼用這個空間。接著實地勘景，注意 visionOS 全沉浸時視野約 **81°**，思考主視角與轉身後看到的內容，並標記要替換的元素（如道路、雜亂植被）。無法親臨的場景（如月球）則仰賴 Apollo 任務照片等參考素材；團隊也用 Yosemite 的 **Digital Elevation Models** 做光照研究。規劃時要以**圖層（layers）**思維從背景到前景構圖，並預先想好動態與音訊。

**Production（製作）**核心是在源頭就拍到高品質照片。建議用三腳架、相機離地 1 公尺並水平、深景深，若可能再架一台離地 2 公尺的相機同步觸發以利後期補景；用涵蓋全視角的 rig 與鏡頭產出 360° 拼接全景，並拍**包圍曝光（bracketed exposures）**保留動態範圍。visionOS 環境在 **40 ppd（pixels per degree）**下清晰，理想目標是 **14,400 × 7,200** 的 360° 全景。此外用 photogrammetry／LiDAR 取得點雲做距離量測，並拍 Macbeth 色卡、鉻球與灰球當光照參考；若無法拍攝則用 DCC 工具製作算圖全景。

**Post-production（後期）**從清理全景開始，移除相機 rig、腳印、人物與干擾構圖的元素，再透過 digital matte painting 與 CG 算圖反覆精修，特別留意色彩平衡與光照一致性。為了營造視差，需把全景投到 UV 空間的 3D mesh，用次要照片與 CG 補上看不到的部分，並持續做 A/B 比對確保材質轉移品質；翻轉場景、套用極端 gamma／gain 可揪出色偏與資料流失。最後以**自訂 shader** 高效率地做出動態：UV flow maps 驅動雲與植物、scrolling mask 模擬雲影、flip book 紋理近似柔和陰影、hierarchical vertex animation 加上分層 sine 波讓樹幹與葉片擺動有層次。實務心法是**凡事有意圖、構圖要成立、用聲音與動態把場景綁在一起**，並勇於打破自己的設計、擁抱意外。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: 講者開宗明義說明 visionOS 的系統環境**不只是背景**，而是為空間運算設計的**寫實自然景觀**。以 Haleakala 為例，它不像平面媒體或全景圖那樣對視角無反應，而是提供真正的**深度與視差（parallax）**，再結合動態與音訊讓場景彷彿活著。整場將以六個系統環境為例，帶過 pre-production、production、post-production 三階段。

deepdive.title: Pre-production
deepdive.body: 前期先問三個問題：**為何**做這個環境、想帶出**哪些特質**、使用者會**如何使用**這個空間。講者以大尺寸觀影（雕塑地形、研究最佳中心觀看線）與 Keynote 環境（刻意無聲、聚光於舞台以利練習演講）說明意圖如何驅動設計。實地勘景時要考量 visionOS 全沉浸約 **81°** 視野的主視角與轉身視野，月球這類場景則靠 Apollo 照片，Yosemite 則用 **Digital Elevation Models** 做光照研究；並提醒以**圖層**思維構圖、預先規劃動態與音訊。

deepdive.title: Production
deepdive.body: 製作階段強調在源頭拍到可直接使用的高品質素材。技巧包含三腳架相機離地 1 公尺水平、深景深，並架第二台離地 2 公尺相機同步觸發供後期補景；用全視角 rig 產出 360° 拼接全景，拍**包圍曝光**保留從太陽到陰影的動態範圍。目標解析度為 **40 ppd**、約 **14,400 × 7,200** 的全景；另以 photogrammetry／LiDAR 點雲做距離量測（例如發現地形其實有坡度），並拍 Macbeth 色卡與鉻／灰球當光照參考，必要時改用算圖全景。

deepdive.title: Post-production
deepdive.body: 後期先**清理全景**：移除相機 rig、腳印、人物與過於搶眼的植被，再以 matte painting 與 CG 反覆精修並維持色彩與光照一致。為製造視差需把全景轉到 UV 空間的 **3D mesh**，用次要照片與 CG 補齊不可見區域，並以 A/B 比對、翻轉場景、極端 gamma／gain 檢查品質。動態與音訊是沉浸的關鍵：空間音訊放置 emitter（如河水流經岩石處），而 Bora Bora 的雲、棕櫚、海浪則用 **UV flow maps、scrolling mask 雲影、flip book 陰影、hierarchical vertex animation 加分層 sine 波**等技巧，在即時算圖預算內做出可信動態。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 收尾以設計心法作結：**凡事有意圖**，能解釋每個元素的增刪理由；**構圖要成立**，每個元素都該屬於它所在之處；並以**聲音與動態**把整個場景綁在一起。這套原則不分個人、小團隊或大工作室皆適用。最後的提醒是：別太執著於單一想法，試著去**打破自己的設計**、做點意外之舉並接受結果，最好的成果往往來自途中擁抱的驚喜。

summary_en: Presented by Apple human interface designer Michael Breymann, this session is about designing **immersive environments** for visionOS apps, websites, and SharePlay experiences. He opens by stressing that visionOS system environments are far more than backdrops: they are **photoreal natural landscapes** built for spatial computing, with true **depth and parallax** that respond to a change in perspective, and combined with motion and **spatial audio** the scene feels alive. The talk walks through the full design process across **pre-production, production, and post-production**, illustrated with six system environments: Mount Hood, the Moon, Jupiter, Yosemite, Thorsmork, and Bora Bora.

**Pre-production** is about getting clear on intent: why you're building the environment, what qualities you want to bring out, and how the viewer will use the space. You then scout the location, keeping in mind that visionOS shows roughly **81°** of field of view when fully immersed, considering the primary viewpoint and what's behind the viewer, and flagging elements to replace (roads, busy vegetation). Inaccessible scenes like the Moon rely on reference material such as Apollo photography, while Yosemite used **Digital Elevation Models** for a lighting study. Plan composition in terms of **layers** from background to foreground, and think early about motion and audio.

**Production** centers on capturing high-quality photography at the source. Tips include a tripod with the camera leveled 1 meter off the ground, deep depth of field, and a second camera at 2 meters triggered simultaneously to fill in the scene later; use a rig and lens covering all views to produce a stitched 360° panorama, and shoot **bracketed exposures** to preserve dynamic range. visionOS environments are sharp at **40 pixels per degree**, so an ideal 360° target is **14,400 × 7,200**. Capture photogrammetry/LiDAR point clouds for distance measurements, and shoot Macbeth charts plus chrome and gray spheres as lighting reference, or build a rendered panorama in a DCC tool when shooting isn't possible.

**Post-production** starts with cleanup of the panorama, removing the camera rig, footprints, people, and elements that interfere with the composition, then refining through digital matte painting and CG renders while watching color balance and lighting consistency. To create parallax you move the panorama onto a 3D mesh in UV space, filling unseen areas with secondary photography and CG, and constantly A/B comparing to retain quality; flopping the scene and pushing extreme gamma/gain values reveals color shifts and data loss. Finally, custom **shaders** deliver efficient motion: UV flow maps drive clouds and foliage, a scrolling mask fakes cloud shadows, flip book textures approximate soft shadows, and hierarchical vertex animation with layered sine waves makes trunks and leaflets sway with variety. The guiding principles: **be intentional, build a composition that works, and tie everything together with sound and motion** — and don't be afraid to break your own designs and embrace the surprises.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: The presenter states up front that visionOS system environments are **not just backdrops** but photoreal natural landscapes designed for spatial computing. Using Haleakala as an example, he contrasts them with flat media or panoramic images that don't respond to perspective, emphasizing the true **depth and parallax** they provide, which combined with motion and audio makes the scene feel alive. The talk will use six system environments to walk through the pre-production, production, and post-production stages.

deepdive_en.title: Pre-production
deepdive_en.body: Pre-production starts with three questions: **why** you're building this environment, what **qualities** you want to bring to life, and **how** the viewer will use the space. Examples include large-format media viewing (sculpting terrain, researching the optimal center line) and the Keynote environment (intentionally silent, lit on the stage for speech practice). Scouting must account for the roughly **81°** field of view at full immersion for both the primary and turn-around views; the Moon relied on Apollo photography while Yosemite used **Digital Elevation Models** for a lighting study. The advice is to compose in **layers** and plan motion and audio ahead of time.

deepdive_en.title: Production
deepdive_en.body: Production is about capturing directly usable, high-quality source imagery. Tips include a tripod with the camera leveled 1 meter off the ground and deep depth of field, plus a second camera at 2 meters triggered simultaneously to fill in the scene during post; use an all-view rig to produce a stitched 360° panorama and shoot **bracketed exposures** to capture the range from sun to shadow. The target is **40 ppd**, around **14,400 × 7,200**; photogrammetry/LiDAR point clouds aid distance measurement (e.g. discovering a slope), and Macbeth charts with chrome/gray spheres serve as lighting reference, with a rendered panorama as the fallback.

deepdive_en.title: Post-production
deepdive_en.body: Post-production begins with **cleaning up the panorama**: removing the camera rig, footprints, people, and overly dominant vegetation, then refining through matte painting and CG while keeping color and lighting consistent. To create parallax the panorama is moved onto a **3D mesh** in UV space, with secondary photography and CG filling unseen areas, validated via A/B comparison, scene flopping, and extreme gamma/gain checks. Motion and audio complete immersion: spatial audio emitters are placed (e.g. where the river flows around rocks), and Bora Bora's clouds, palms, and waves use techniques like **UV flow maps, a scrolling cloud-shadow mask, flip book shadows, and hierarchical vertex animation with layered sine waves** to achieve believable motion within the real-time render budget.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: The session closes with design principles: **be intentional** and able to justify every element you add or remove; **create a composition that works** where every element belongs; and tie the whole scene together with **sound and motion**. These apply equally to an individual, a small team, or a large studio. The final thought is to not get too attached to any one idea — try to **break your own designs**, do something unexpected, and be receptive to the surprises that often produce your best work.

title: What’s new in image understanding
gloss: 影像理解的新功能
takeaway: 用 Vision 的 tap-to-segment 以點選方式分割影像，並把影像當作輸入餵給 Foundation Models 產生說明或進行 image-based tool calling。
chapters: Generate an image caption with Foundation Models
Create a crop that highlights a prominent subject (watchOS / saliency)

points.text: 用 **tap-to-segment**（`GenerateIterativeSegmentationRequest`）以種子點產生物件遮罩，並可加點逐步修正結果。
**Foundation Models** 現可接收影像輸入，透過 `Prompt` 搭配 `Attachment(image)` 直接產生影像說明文字。
支援 **image-based tool calling**：自訂 `Tool` 以 `ImageReference` 解析影像，讓模型呼叫如植物辨識等工具。
Vision 現可在 **watchOS** 使用，並以 `GenerateObjectnessBasedSaliencyImageRequest` 依顯著主體自動裁切影像。

audience: **想在 App 中加入影像分割、影像理解或多模態模型功能的開發者**。
gloss_en: What's new in image understanding
takeaway_en: Segment images by tapping with Vision's tap-to-segment, and feed images as input to Foundation Models to generate captions or perform image-based tool calling.

points_en.text: Use **tap-to-segment** (`GenerateIterativeSegmentationRequest`) to produce object masks from seed points, refining the result step by step by adding more points.
**Foundation Models** can now accept image input, generating image captions directly via a `Prompt` paired with `Attachment(image)`.
Support **image-based tool calling**: define a custom `Tool` that resolves images via `ImageReference`, letting the model call tools such as plant identification.
Vision is now available on **watchOS**, and `GenerateObjectnessBasedSaliencyImageRequest` can automatically crop images based on their salient subject.

audience_en: **Developers who want to add image segmentation, image understanding, or multimodal model features to their app**.
summary: 由 Vision 框架團隊的 Megan Williams 主講，主題是今年 image understanding 的多項進展，讓 app 能打造前所未有的影像體驗。重點有四：Vision 全新的 **tap-to-segment** 互動式去背 API、**Foundation Models** 框架現在支援影像輸入（image inputs）、可讓 LLM 呼叫的 **image-based tool calling**，以及 Vision 現已登陸 **watchOS**。整體訊息是：分析影像不再只有 Vision 或只有大型語言模型可選，兩者可以互補搭配。

**Tap-to-segment** 讓你只要點一下就能隔離影像中任意物件，選取方式包含單點、bounding box、lasso、scribble，並能用增減點來精修 mask。技術上用 **`ImageRequestHandler`** 持有影像，建立 **`GenerateIterativeSegmentationRequest`**（以物件內一個點作 seed）執行後產生 PixelBuffer mask，可再加入新點重複執行精修。要注意：Vision 用左下為原點的 normalized 座標（0–1）、lasso 線寬至少為影像寬的 1%，且首次使用前需以 **`downloadAssets`** 下載模型並以 `assetStatus` 檢查就緒狀態。

**Foundation Models** 框架今年支援把影像當作 prompt 的 attachment，用 prompt builder 語法即可請模型生成圖片說明、室內設計建議、甚至看冰箱照片給食譜。更進一步是 **image-based tool calling**：自訂 tool 以 **`ImageReference`** 為參數（代表 chat session 中既有影像的參照），在 `call` 方法內透過 session 的 history transcript 把 reference 解析回 imageAttachment 再轉成 pixelBuffer 分析。Vision 直接提供兩個內建 tool——**barcode reader**（讀條碼／QR code）與 **OCR**（讀細密文字，支援 30+ 語言），只要 `import Vision` 並把 tool 設定到 session、為附加影像加上 label 即可。

最後，**Vision 登上 watchOS**。講者以野生動物 app 為例：手錶螢幕小、動物照片看不清，便用 **`GenerateObjectnessBasedSaliencyImageRequest`** 做 saliency 分析，從 observation 取得 salient 物件的 bounding box，挑最顯著的來裁切，讓使用者在手錶上看到放大且聚焦主體的畫面。Vision 支援 30 多種影像分析（臉部、姿態、偵測分類、軌跡與物件追蹤等），可用來打造自家 tool。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: Vision 框架團隊的 Megan 以一段「找不到議程、用 AI 從便利貼照片生成議程」的情境開場，點出今年 image understanding 的多項進展。她以**遺失議程**的小故事帶出 **Foundation Models** 今年支援影像輸入，並預告四大主題：tap-to-segment、Foundation Models 影像分析、image-based tools，以及 Vision 登上 watchOS。

deepdive.title: Segment images with tap-to-segment
deepdive.body: 示範 Vision 既有的 person segmentation 之外，新的 **tap-to-segment** 能去背任意物件（花瓶、桌遊、衣物、地板）。在咖啡廳照片中以單點隔離咖啡杯；複雜主體則改用 **bounding box**（同時取杯與盤）、**lasso**（可頌）或 **scribble**（一次塗過多個物件）。已有 mask 後還能加點納入盤子、或減點只保留咖啡而排除杯子。

deepdive.title: Segment images (tap-to-segment)
deepdive.body: API 流程：用 **`ImageRequestHandler`** 持有影像，建立 **`GenerateIterativeSegmentationRequest`**、以物件內一點作 seed，performRequest 後得到顯示物件像素的 PixelBuffer mask；加入新點重新執行即可精修。注意事項：Vision 採左下原點的 normalized 座標（0–1）、lasso 線寬至少為影像寬的 1%，首次去背前需用 **`downloadAssets`** 下載模型並以 `assetStatus` 確認就緒。

deepdive.title: Image inputs for Foundation Models
deepdive.body: 介紹用大型語言模型分析影像的新方式：除了生成圖片 caption，還能做室內設計建議、看冰箱照片產生食譜等描述性任務，可能性無窮。比較傳統 **Vision**（固定的電腦視覺 API、為特定任務微調、快到能即時處理影格）與 **Foundation Models**（versatile，幾乎能回答任何要求），並指出兩者可透過 tool calling 互補。

deepdive.title: Generate an image caption with Foundation Models
deepdive.body: 用 Foundation Models 的 **prompt builder** 語法生成圖片說明：一段帶處理指示的文字 prompt，把影像當 **attachment** 加進 prompt，再請模型回應即可得到 caption。API 非常簡單，鼓勵開發者用自己的 prompt 嘗試各種描述性任務。

deepdive.title: Image-based tool calling
deepdive.body: 先複習 tool calling：模型遇到自己答不了的問題（如天氣）時會呼叫外部 tool 取得結果再回答。今年 tool calling **支援影像參數**：例如植物辨識，模型不把整張圖當參數，而是傳一個影像的**參照**給自訂 tool，由 tool 分析後回傳植物名稱，模型再據此回應。

deepdive.title: Create an image-based tool
deepdive.body: 自訂 tool 需符合 Foundation Models 的 tool protocol 並定義輸入參數，這裡用 **`ImageReference`** 表示參數需指向 chat session 中既有影像。在 `call` 方法內取出 imageReference 後須**解析**：因為 reference 只在其產生的 transcript 脈絡中有效，要透過 session 的 history 屬性取得 transcript，把 reference 還原成 imageAttachment，再轉成 pixelBuffer 分析。

deepdive.title: Use Vision tools
deepdive.body: Vision 直接提供現成 tool。以活動傳單為例，未啟用 tool 時模型讀得到地點與日期卻讀不出 QR code；啟用 Vision 的 **barcode reader tool** 後模型即可呼叫它取得網址。Vision 提供兩個 tool：barcode reader 與 **OCR**（適合細密文字、支援 30+ 語言）。使用時只需 `import Vision`、把 tool 設定到 session，並**為附加影像加 label** 供模型指定要傳給 tool 的影像。

deepdive.title: Vision on watchOS
deepdive.body: 今年 Vision 可用於更多地方，包含 **watchOS**。以本地野生動物 app 為例：手錶螢幕小、動物照片難看清，可用 Vision 的 saliency 分析找出影像中的興趣主體，再裁切讓主體更突出。

deepdive.title: Create a crop that highlights a prominent subject (watchOS / saliency)
deepdive.body: 程式做法：建立 **`GenerateObjectnessBasedSaliencyImageRequest`**、對影像 performRequest 得到 saliency observation，從中取得偵測到的 salient 物件 bounding box，挑最顯著的物件作裁切。更新後 app 只顯示影像中最突出的部分，在手錶上呈現放大聚焦的視圖。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 回顧：tap-to-segment 可互動式去背任意物件；Foundation Models 現支援影像輸入帶來全新分析方式；可建立使用 Vision 等框架的 tool 強化影像分析；Vision 也能在所有平台（含 watchOS）強化 app。可下載 watchOS 與 tap-to-segment 範例 app，並參考「Discover Swift enhancements in the Vision framework」與「What's new in the Foundation Models framework」。

summary_en: Presented by Megan Williams of the Vision framework team, this session covers this year's advances in image understanding for building incredible app experiences. There are four highlights: Vision's new interactive **tap-to-segment** API, **Foundation Models** framework now supporting image inputs, **image-based tool calling** that lets LLMs invoke tools, and Vision arriving on **watchOS**. The overarching message: analyzing images is no longer an either/or choice between Vision and large language models—the two complement each other.

**Tap-to-segment** lets you isolate any object in an image with a single tap, supporting selection by point, bounding box, lasso, and scribble, with refinement by adding or subtracting points. Technically, hold the image in an **`ImageRequestHandler`**, build a **`GenerateIterativeSegmentationRequest`** with a seed point inside the object, and perform it to get a PixelBuffer mask, then add points and re-run to refine. Keep in mind Vision uses normalized coordinates with origin at lower-left (values 0–1), lasso stroke width should be at least 1% of image width, and you must download the model with **`downloadAssets`** (checking `assetStatus`) before the first segmentation.

**Foundation Models** now supports including an image as an attachment in your prompt; with the prompt builder syntax you can generate image captions, interior-decorating suggestions, or even a recipe from a photo of your fridge. Going further, **image-based tool calling** lets a custom tool take an **`ImageReference`** argument (a reference to an existing image in the chat session); inside the tool's `call` method you resolve the reference back to an imageAttachment via the session's history transcript, then convert it to a pixelBuffer for analysis. Vision ships two built-in tools—a **barcode reader** (barcodes/QR codes) and **OCR** (fine or dense text in 30+ languages)—and using them is just `import Vision`, configuring the session with the tools, and giving attached images a label.

Finally, **Vision comes to watchOS**. The presenter's wildlife app has tiny photos hard to see on the small screen, so she uses **`GenerateObjectnessBasedSaliencyImageRequest`** for saliency analysis, pulls the bounding boxes of salient objects from the observation, and crops to the most prominent one for a zoomed-in, subject-focused view. Vision supports over 30 types of image analysis (facial analysis, pose estimation, detection and classification, trajectory analysis, object tracking) you can wrap into your own tools.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Megan of the Vision framework team opens with a scenario—her agenda is missing, so she uses AI to generate one from a photo of her sticky notes—introducing this year's image-understanding advances. The **missing agenda** story leads into Foundation Models now supporting image inputs, and she previews four topics: tap-to-segment, Foundation Models image analysis, image-based tools, and Vision on watchOS.

deepdive_en.title: Segment images with tap-to-segment
deepdive_en.body: Beyond existing person segmentation, the new **tap-to-segment** can isolate any object (vase, board game, clothing, even the floor). In a cafe photo she isolates a coffee cup with a single point; for complex subjects she uses a **bounding box** (cup plus plate), a **lasso** (a croissant), or a **scribble** (multiple objects at once). With a mask in hand she adds a point to include the plate, or subtracts one to keep just the coffee, excluding the cup.

deepdive_en.title: Segment images (tap-to-segment)
deepdive_en.body: API flow: hold the image in an **`ImageRequestHandler`**, create a **`GenerateIterativeSegmentationRequest`** with a seed point inside the object, and perform it to get a PixelBuffer mask of the object's pixels; add a point and re-run to refine. Notes: Vision uses normalized coordinates with origin at lower-left (0–1), lasso width should be at least 1% of image width, and the model must be downloaded via **`downloadAssets`** (check `assetStatus`) before first use.

deepdive_en.title: Image inputs for Foundation Models
deepdive_en.body: A new way to analyze images with LLMs: beyond captions, it handles descriptive tasks like interior-decorating advice or generating a recipe from a fridge photo—the possibilities are endless. She contrasts traditional **Vision** (fixed CV APIs, fine-tuned per task, fast enough for real-time video) with **Foundation Models** (versatile, able to do almost anything asked), noting the two combine via tool calling.

deepdive_en.title: Generate an image caption with Foundation Models
deepdive_en.body: Generating a caption uses Foundation Models' **prompt builder** syntax: a text prompt with processing instructions, the image included as an **attachment**, then asking the model to respond yields a caption. The API is very simple, and developers are encouraged to try their own descriptive prompts.

deepdive_en.title: Image-based tool calling
deepdive_en.body: A refresher on tool calling: when the model can't answer (e.g., weather) it invokes an external tool, gets a result, and responds. This year tool calling **supports image arguments**: for plant identification the model passes a **reference** to an image to a custom tool rather than the whole image, the tool analyzes it and returns the plant name, and the model responds with the right information.

deepdive_en.title: Create an image-based tool
deepdive_en.body: A custom tool conforms to the Foundation Models tool protocol and defines input arguments—here an **`ImageReference`**, signaling the argument must reference an existing image in the session. Inside `call`, the imageReference must be **resolved**: because a reference is valid only within the transcript that generated it, you use the session's history property to get the transcript, resolve the reference back to an imageAttachment, then convert it to a pixelBuffer for analysis.

deepdive_en.title: Use Vision tools
deepdive_en.body: Vision provides ready-made tools. With an event flyer, the model without tools reads the date and location but not the QR code; enabling Vision's **barcode reader tool** lets the model call it to get the website. Vision offers two tools: the barcode reader and **OCR** (good for fine, dense text in 30+ languages). Usage is just `import Vision`, configure the session with the tools, and **label attached images** so the model can specify which image to pass.

deepdive_en.title: Vision on watchOS
deepdive_en.body: Vision is now available in more places, including **watchOS**. With a local-wildlife app, photos are hard to see on the small watch screen, so Vision's saliency analysis identifies the subject of interest so the image can be cropped to feature it more prominently.

deepdive_en.title: Create a crop that highlights a prominent subject (watchOS / saliency)
deepdive_en.body: The code creates a **`GenerateObjectnessBasedSaliencyImageRequest`**, performs it on the image to get a saliency observation, reads the bounding boxes of detected salient objects, and uses the most prominent one for the crop. The updated app shows only the most salient portion, giving a zoomed-in view on the watch.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Recap: tap-to-segment interactively segments any object; Foundation Models now supports image inputs for new kinds of analysis; you can build tools using frameworks like Vision to improve image analysis; and Vision enhances apps on all platforms including watchOS. Download the watchOS and tap-to-segment sample apps, and watch 'Discover Swift enhancements in the Vision framework' and 'What's new in the Foundation Models framework'.

title: Build intelligent Siri experiences with App Schemas
gloss: 用 App Schemas 打造智慧 Siri 體驗
takeaway: 用 **App Intents 與 App Schemas** 把 App 的內容與動作交給 Siri 與 Apple Intelligence，並支援跨 App 的螢幕感知與內容傳遞。
chapters: Contributing message content to Apple Intelligence
An interface that locates entities using arbitrary string input
Adopting a schema domain in UnicornChat
Working across apps - Exporting content to another app

points.text: 用 **App Entities** 建模資料、`IndexedEntity` 建立索引，讓 Siri 與 Apple Intelligence 能存取你的內容。
採用 **App Schemas** 領域（如 `.messages.message`）即可獲得系統內建的智慧能力，無需自行設計介面。
以 `EntityStringQuery` 用任意字串解析實體，並透過 `#Predicate` 與 SwiftData 查詢比對。
跨 App 運作：用 `appEntityIdentifier` 做**螢幕感知（onscreen awareness）**與視圖註記，讓 Siri 知道畫面上有什麼。
透過 `IntentValueQuery` 與 `IntentValueRepresentation`（搭配 `Transferable`）在 App 之間匯出與匯入內容。

audience: **想讓 App 內容與動作深度整合進 Siri 與 Apple Intelligence** 的 iOS 開發者。
gloss_en: Build intelligent Siri experiences with App Schemas
takeaway_en: Use **App Intents and App Schemas** to hand your app's content and actions to Siri and Apple Intelligence, with support for cross-app onscreen awareness and content transfer.

points_en.text: Model your data with **App Entities** and index it with `IndexedEntity` so Siri and Apple Intelligence can access your content.
Adopt an **App Schemas** domain (such as `.messages.message`) to gain the system's built-in intelligence without designing the interface yourself.
Resolve entities from arbitrary strings with `EntityStringQuery`, matching via `#Predicate` and SwiftData queries.
Works across apps: use `appEntityIdentifier` for **onscreen awareness** and view annotation, so Siri knows what's on screen.
Export and import content between apps with `IntentValueQuery` and `IntentValueRepresentation` (paired with `Transferable`).

audience_en: iOS developers **who want to deeply integrate their app's content and actions into Siri and Apple Intelligence**.
summary: 這場由 Swift Intelligence Frameworks 團隊的 Dan Niemeyer 主講，主題是如何用 **App Intents** 把 app 帶到 Siri。在 27 系列中，由 Apple Intelligence 驅動的 Siri 變得更強大、更具情境、更個人化，而 App Intents 正是這一切的基礎。今年 Siri 在三方面躍進：能存取你 app 的 **entity**（真正有意義的內容），能用你 app 的 **intent** 採取行動，還能理解**螢幕上的情境**。整場以一個與虛構獨角獸聊天的範例 app **UnicornChat** 貫穿示範。

一切的核心是 **AppEntity**——對 app 內既有內容的結構化描述，說明「那是什麼、如何被辨識、哪些屬性重要」。但光建模還不夠，entity 必須符合 **AppSchema**，Siri 才知道它屬於哪一類（如 messages、contacts、documents）。要讓 Siri 找到正確的 entity，主要途徑是採用 **IndexedEntity**，把內容索引進系統的語意索引，支援以「意義」而非字串比對來搜尋（用 `indexingKey` 告訴 Spotlight 哪些屬性可搜尋）；當資料量太大、在伺服器上或變動太頻繁而無法事先索引時，則改用 **EntityStringQuery**，由 app 自行比對。有了 entity 之後，再把它與**動作**結合：定義 **App Intent** 就能讓動作出現在 Shortcuts、Spotlight、Widgets 等系統各處；而要讓 Siri 直接執行，動作需採用 **app schema**（schema 是 App Intent 的特化），並把多個 schema 歸入 **AppSchema domain**（如 messages）。示範中 UnicornChat 採用 messages domain 的 **sendMessage** schema，把 schema 參數對應到既有送訊流程，Siri 即可在不開啟 app 的情況下完成「傳訊息給 Glow」。

下半場談**跨 app 工作流程**，例如「把 Bubbles 的這則回覆 email 給我太太」，由兩項能力組成：**onscreen awareness** 與 **content transfer**。螢幕情境用 **UserActivity**（畫面上只有一個主要項目時）或 **View annotations**（`appEntityIdentifier`，畫面上有多個有意義項目時）把可見內容連到 entity；內容傳輸則靠 **Transferable** 搭配 **IntentValueRepresentation** 把 entity 匯出（例如把 ContactEntity 匯出為 IntentPerson）。內容進入你的 app 時有兩條路：用 **IntentValueQuery** 把傳入值解析到既有 entity，或用 `IntentValueRepresentation` 的 **importing** 建立全新 entity。最後是最佳實務與測試：Xcode 會在你採用 sendMessage 卻漏掉相關的 **draftMessage** schema 時以建置錯誤與 fix-it 提示你補齊；測試則建議由 **AppIntentsTesting**（隔離驗證商業邏輯）開始，再依序到 **Shortcuts**、**Spotlight**，最後用 **Siri** 做端對端驗證。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: 由 Swift Intelligence Frameworks 團隊的軟體工程師 Dan Niemeyer 開場，說明如何用 Apple Intelligence 驅動的新能力把 app 帶到 **Siri**。今年 Siri 更強大、更具情境也更個人化，而 **App Intents** 是讓這一切成真的基礎。本場將涵蓋 Siri 與 App Intents 的新功能、Siri 如何理解內容並採取行動，以及跨 app 的使用情境與最佳實務。

deepdive.title: What's new in Siri
deepdive.body: 說明 Siri 由 **Apple Intelligence** 驅動後在三方面變強：能存取 app 的 **entity** 回答如「我下一場會議何時何地」這類問題；能用 app 的 **intent** 採取行動如「把最新報告寄給 Mary」；還能理解**螢幕情境**如「解釋這段文字」。開發者參與 Apple Intelligence 的方式就是透過 App Intents 框架，本場將以範例 app **UnicornChat**（一個與虛構獨角獸聊天的 messaging app）貫穿示範。

deepdive.title: Contributing content with App Entities
deepdive.body: 所有體驗的核心是 **AppEntity**——對 app 內既有內容的結構化表示，描述「那是什麼、如何被辨識、哪些屬性重要」（如標題、日期、文字），它不是新的資料模型而是描述既有內容的方式。但光建模不足以讓 Siri 找到或談論它，entity 還必須符合 **AppSchema**，Siri 才知道它代表哪一類概念。UnicornChat 中的 Contact、Conversation、Message 都建模為符合 schema 的 entity，因此 Siri 能理解「顯示 Flare 的最後一則訊息」這類請求。

deepdive.title: Entity resolution and IndexedEntity
deepdive.body: **Entity resolution** 是 Siri 把使用者所說的話解析成 app 內真實 entity 的過程，例如把「Glow」解析為特定獨角獸 contact 並填入其屬性值。但人們常以概念與描述而非精確名稱表達，因此 Siri 需要語意搜尋，而這正是 **IndexedEntity** 所提供的——它把 entity 索引進系統語意索引，讓 Siri 依意義比對、理解 entity 間關係，甚至能對內容回答問題。

deepdive.title: Contributing message content to Apple Intelligence
deepdive.body: 示範把 schematized entity 進一步符合 **IndexedEntity** 協定來取得語意比對能力。以 **`indexingKey`** 告訴 Spotlight 哪些屬性（如 message body）應可被搜尋，索引後 Siri 就能搜尋、推理並用內容回答問題，例如「顯示與 Flare 關於電影的訊息」這類非字串比對的語意查詢。IndexedEntity 帶來最佳的 Siri 體驗：語意比對、更少追問、更自然的語言理解。

deepdive.title: An interface that locates entities using arbitrary string input
deepdive.body: 說明當資料量太大、位於伺服器或變動太頻繁而無法事先索引時，可改用 **EntityStringQuery**。此時 Siri 把使用者輸入交給你的 app，由 app 自行負責尋找並回傳符合的 entity，雖然失去語意理解，但能完全掌控搜尋與比對方式。範例的 `ContactQuery` 以 `localizedStandardContains` 對 Person 名稱做比對後回傳對應 entity。

deepdive.title: Making actions available
deepdive.body: 說明 **App Intents** 是 app 對系統暴露動作的方式，但動作分兩種待遇。定義一個 app intent 後，動作會出現在 Shortcuts、Spotlight、Widgets 等系統各處，讓人們即使不用 Siri 也能發現並觸發。而要讓 Siri 能直接執行，動作需採用 **schema**（schema 是 App Intent 的特化），schema 定義 Siri 理解的動作種類、預期結構與如何對應到自然語言。

deepdive.title: Adopting a schema domain in UnicornChat
deepdive.body: 示範在 UnicornChat 端對端採用一個 domain。個別 schema 定義個別動作，但 app 通常需要完整的一組，因此 schema 被歸入 **AppSchema domain**（如 mail、photos、messages）。在 Xcode 中輸入 schema 名稱時可用自動完成挑選，這裡選 messages domain 的 **sendMessage** schema，把 schema 參數對應到既有送訊流程：處理參數、傳入 UnicornChat 介面送出、再把新訊息以 entity 回傳，Siri 即可在不開啟 app 下完成「傳訊息給 Glow」。

deepdive.title: Moving content across apps
deepdive.body: 切入跨 app 工作流程，說明許多真實請求會橫跨多個 app——從一個 app 開始、在另一個延續、最後在別處完成，例如「Hey Siri，把 Bubbles 的這則回覆 email 給我太太」。這類體驗結合兩項能力：理解人們正在看什麼（**onscreen awareness**），以及把內容移到另一個 app（**content transfer**），接下來會分別說明。

deepdive.title: Working across apps: onscreen awareness
deepdive.body: 說明 **onscreen awareness** 把畫面上可見的內容連到系統能理解的結構化資訊，核心仍是 **app entity**——當 view 與 entity 關聯後，Siri 能解析「這則訊息」「那段對話」這類指涉而毋須使用者明確命名。註解螢幕內容有兩種 API：畫面上只有一個主要項目（如檢視文件或撰寫訊息）時用 **UserActivity**；同時有多個有意義項目（如對話中的訊息或清單項目）時用 **View annotations**。

deepdive.title: Working across apps - View annotations
deepdive.body: 示範以 **View annotations** 把清單中每一列連到對應的 entity。範例對每個 message row 用 **`appEntityIdentifier`** 標註其 MessageEntity，明確把螢幕內容連到同一批用於 intent 的 entity，讓使用者能說「編輯這則訊息」或「轉發最後一則」，Siri 直接從 view 解析 entity。

deepdive.title: Working across apps - Exporting content to another app
deepdive.body: 說明 **content transfer** 讓其他 app 能對你的 entity 採取行動，做法是用 **Transferable** 搭配 **IntentValueRepresentation** 匯出 entity，告訴系統如何以其他 app 能理解的形式表示你的內容。範例把 ContactEntity 匯出為 IntentPerson，匯出後系統就能把內容傳入其他 app 的動作，支援如「打給這位聯絡人」的情境；你的 app 毋須知道後續發生什麼，只需準確描述內容。

deepdive.title: Working across apps - IntentValueQuery
deepdive.body: 說明內容傳入你的 app 時有兩種可能：指涉既有事物，或代表全新事物。若是比對既有內容，用 **IntentValueQuery**，概念上類似 entity query 但範圍限於 intent 參數。範例的 `ContactEntityQuery` 接收其他 app 傳來的 IntentPerson，依顯示名稱比對到既有的 ContactEntity，適用於內容已存在或要從既有資料中挑選的情況。

deepdive.title: Working across apps - IntentValueRepresentation
deepdive.body: 說明若傳入內容應在你的 app 中建立全新事物，則用 **`IntentValueRepresentation`** 的 **importing**，把傳入值轉換成全新的 app entity。範例在需要時用 IntentPerson 建立一隻新的獨角獸並加入 ContactManager。匯入內容時的原則是：若內容已存在就 resolve、不存在就 import，許多 app 會視 intent 與工作流程兩者並用。

deepdive.title: Best practices
deepdive.body: 示範一個關鍵最佳實務：在採用 **sendMessage** schema 後嘗試建置，Xcode 會出現建置錯誤，提示你尚未採用相關的 **draftMessage** schema——因為某些 Siri 情境（尤其需要確認時）需要多個 schema 才能提供完整體驗。這不只是編譯錯誤而是設計提示，點進去 Xcode 會提供 **fix-it** 產生 draftMessage 的範例採用（intent 定義、必要參數與 stub），你只需填入 app 專屬部分（連接 entity、注入相依、處理輸入、開啟建立訊息畫面，並因會變更 UI 狀態而在 main actor 執行）。

deepdive.title: Testing your integration
deepdive.body: 說明採用 schema 後測試變得關鍵，建議的循序路徑：先用新的 **AppIntentsTesting** 框架在完全隔離（不涉及 Siri）下呼叫 intent、傳入參數並驗證結果，這是最快也最可靠地驗證商業邏輯的方式；接著到 **Shortcuts** 驗證 intent 的形狀與呈現；再到 **Spotlight** 確認 entity 已正確索引、可被發現與連結；最後用 **Siri** 做涵蓋自然語言、entity resolution、螢幕情境與跨 app 工作流程的端對端測試。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 總結具體後續步驟：把 entity 建模並索引到 Spotlight 讓 Siri 找得到內容、採用符合 app 核心體驗的 **app schema domain**、採用 **Transferable** 以啟用內容匯入匯出，並依 AppIntentsTesting → Shortcuts → Spotlight → Siri 的順序儘早且頻繁地測試。這些 API 今日皆已可用，且設計成能隨 app 與 Siri 的演進而擴展——把 app 帶到 Siri 不只是加上語音支援，更是讓 app 在整個系統中更快、更易存取、更好用。

summary_en: Presented by Dan Niemeyer of the Swift Intelligence Frameworks team, this session shows how to bring your app to Siri using **App Intents**. In the 27 releases, Siri—powered by Apple Intelligence—is more capable, more contextual, and more personal, and App Intents are the foundation that makes that possible. This year Siri advances in three ways: it can access your app's **entities** (the meaningful content inside your app), take action using your app's **intents**, and understand **on-screen context**. The whole talk is grounded in a sample app, **UnicornChat**, for chatting with fictional unicorn characters.

Everything centers on the **AppEntity**—a structured description of content your app already works with, describing what the thing is, how it's identified, and which properties matter. But modeling alone isn't enough; an entity must conform to an **AppSchema** so Siri knows what category it represents (messages, contacts, documents). The primary way to let Siri find the right entity is adopting **IndexedEntity**, which indexes content into the system semantic index for meaning-based search (with `indexingKey` telling Spotlight which properties are searchable); when data is too large, lives on a server, or changes too frequently to pre-index, use **EntityStringQuery** and match it yourself. Once entities exist, combine them with **actions**: defining an **App Intent** surfaces an action across Shortcuts, Spotlight, Widgets, and more, while making it executable by Siri requires an **app schema** (a specialization of App Intents), grouped into **AppSchema domains** like messages. The demo adopts the messages domain's **sendMessage** schema, mapping its parameters onto UnicornChat's existing send flow so Siri completes "send a message to Glow" without opening the app.

The second half covers **cross-app workflows**, such as "email my wife this reply from Bubbles," built from two capabilities: **on-screen awareness** and **content transfer**. On-screen context uses **UserActivity** (when one primary item is visible) or **View annotations** (`appEntityIdentifier`, when multiple meaningful items are visible) to connect what's shown to entities; content transfer uses **Transferable** with **IntentValueRepresentation** to export an entity (e.g., a ContactEntity as an IntentPerson). When content arrives in your app there are two paths: use **IntentValueQuery** to resolve incoming values to an existing entity, or use **importing** on `IntentValueRepresentation` to create something new. Finally, best practices and testing: Xcode surfaces a build error and fix-it when you adopt sendMessage but miss the related **draftMessage** schema, and testing should start with **AppIntentsTesting** (isolated logic validation), then **Shortcuts**, **Spotlight**, and finally end-to-end with **Siri**.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
