deepdive_en.body: Dan Niemeyer, a software engineer on the Swift Intelligence Frameworks team, opens by explaining how to bring your app to **Siri** using new capabilities powered by Apple Intelligence. This year Siri is more capable, more contextual, and more personal, and **App Intents** are the foundation that makes that possible. The session covers what's new with Siri and App Intents, how Siri understands content and takes action, and cross-app use cases plus best practices.

deepdive_en.title: What's new in Siri
deepdive_en.body: Explains the three ways Siri, powered by **Apple Intelligence**, becomes more powerful: it can access your app's **entities** to answer questions like "when and where is my next meeting," take action using your app's **intents** like "send my latest report to Mary," and understand **on-screen context** like "explain this text." Developers participate in Apple Intelligence through the App Intents framework, and the talk uses the sample app **UnicornChat**—a messaging app for chatting with fictional unicorns—throughout.

deepdive_en.title: Contributing content with App Entities
deepdive_en.body: At the center of every experience is the **AppEntity**—a structured representation of content already inside your app, describing what the thing is, how it's identified, and which properties matter (title, date, text); it's not a new data model but a way to describe existing content. Modeling alone isn't enough for Siri to find or talk about it—the entity must also conform to an **AppSchema** so Siri knows what kind of thing it is. In UnicornChat, Contact, Conversation, and Message are all entities conforming to schemas, letting Siri understand requests like "show my last message from Flare."

deepdive_en.title: Entity resolution and IndexedEntity
deepdive_en.body: **Entity resolution** is how Siri resolves what the user says into real entities inside your app—for example resolving "Glow" to a specific unicorn contact and filling in its property values. But people often speak in concepts and descriptions rather than exact names, so Siri needs semantic search, which is exactly what **IndexedEntity** enables—indexing entities into the system semantic index so Siri can match by meaning, understand relationships, and even answer questions over your content.

deepdive_en.title: Contributing message content to Apple Intelligence
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates conforming a schematized entity to the **IndexedEntity** protocol to gain semantic matching. The **`indexingKey`** tells Spotlight which properties (like the message body) should be searchable; once indexed, Siri can search, reason over, and use content to answer questions—such as "show the messages with Flare about movies," a semantic query rather than a string match. IndexedEntity delivers the best Siri experience: semantic matching, fewer follow-ups, and more natural language understanding.

deepdive_en.title: An interface that locates entities using arbitrary string input
deepdive_en.body: Explains that when a dataset is too large, lives on a server, or changes too frequently to pre-index, you can use **EntityStringQuery**. Siri hands you the person's input, and your app is responsible for finding and returning matching entities—you lose semantic understanding but gain full control over how you search and match. The example `ContactQuery` matches Person names with `localizedStandardContains` and returns the corresponding entities.

deepdive_en.title: Making actions available
deepdive_en.body: Explains that **App Intents** are how your app exposes actions to the system, but not all actions are treated the same. Defining an app intent surfaces the action across the system in places like Shortcuts, Spotlight, and Widgets, so people can discover and trigger it even without Siri. To make an action executable by Siri, it must adopt a **schema** (a specialization of App Intents) that defines the action kinds Siri understands, the structure it expects, and how it maps to natural language.

deepdive_en.title: Adopting a schema domain in UnicornChat
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates wiring a domain end-to-end in UnicornChat. Individual schemas define individual actions, but apps usually need a full set, so schemas are grouped into **AppSchema domains** (mail, photos, messages). In Xcode, autocomplete helps pick a schema; here the **sendMessage** schema from the messages domain is chosen and its parameters mapped onto the existing send flow: process the parameters, pass them into UnicornChat's interface to send, and return the new message as an entity—so Siri completes "send a message to Glow" without opening the app.

deepdive_en.title: Moving content across apps
deepdive_en.body: Introduces cross-app workflows, noting that many real requests span multiple apps—starting in one, continuing in another, and finishing elsewhere, like "Hey Siri, email my wife this reply from Bubbles." These experiences combine two capabilities: understanding what people are looking at (**on-screen awareness**) and moving that content into another app (**content transfer**), each covered in turn.

deepdive_en.title: Working across apps: onscreen awareness
deepdive_en.body: Explains that **on-screen awareness** connects what's visible to structured information the system understands, with the **app entity** at its core—when views are associated with entities, Siri can resolve references like "this message" or "that conversation" without people naming them. There are two annotation APIs: use **UserActivity** when one primary thing is on screen (viewing a document, composing a message), and use **View annotations** when multiple meaningful items are visible (messages in a conversation, items in a list).

deepdive_en.title: Working across apps - View annotations
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates **View annotations** connecting each list row to its corresponding entity. The example annotates each message row with its MessageEntity via **`appEntityIdentifier`**, explicitly linking what's on screen to the same entities used for intents, so users can say "edit this message" or "forward the last one" and Siri resolves the entity directly from the view.

deepdive_en.title: Working across apps - Exporting content to another app
deepdive_en.body: Explains that **content transfer** lets other apps act on your entities by exporting them with **Transferable** and an **IntentValueRepresentation**, telling the system how to represent your content in a form other apps understand. The example exports a ContactEntity as an IntentPerson; once exported, the system can pass that content into other apps' actions, enabling cases like "call this contact." Your app doesn't need to know what happens next—it just describes its content accurately.

deepdive_en.title: Working across apps - IntentValueQuery
deepdive_en.body: Explains that when content comes into your app there are two possibilities: it refers to something existing, or represents something new. To match existing content, use **IntentValueQuery**—conceptually similar to entity query but scoped to intent parameters. The example `ContactEntityQuery` receives an IntentPerson from another app and matches it by display name to an existing ContactEntity, ideal when the content already exists or you want to select from existing data.

deepdive_en.title: Working across apps - IntentValueRepresentation
deepdive_en.body: Explains that when incoming content should create something new, use **importing** on **`IntentValueRepresentation`** to convert the incoming value into a brand-new app entity. The example creates a new unicorn from an IntentPerson when needed and appends it to ContactManager. The principle when importing content: if it already exists, resolve it; if not, import it—and many apps use both depending on the intent and workflow.

deepdive_en.title: Best practices
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates a key best practice: after adopting the **sendMessage** schema, building produces an error because the related **draftMessage** schema hasn't been adopted—some Siri scenarios (especially when confirmation is required) need multiple schemas for a complete experience. This isn't just a compiler error but a design hint; clicking in, Xcode offers a **fix-it** generating a sample draftMessage adoption (intent definition, required parameters, stub). You then fill in app-specific pieces—connect entities, inject dependencies, process input, open the message creation view, and run on the main actor since it mutates UI state.

deepdive_en.title: Testing your integration
deepdive_en.body: Explains that once schemas are adopted, testing becomes critical, and recommends a sequence: start with the new **AppIntentsTesting** framework to invoke intents in full isolation (no Siri), passing parameters and validating results—the fastest, most reliable way to validate business logic; then **Shortcuts** to validate the shape and presentation of the intent; then **Spotlight** to confirm entities are indexed, discoverable, and linkable; and finally **Siri** for end-to-end testing of natural language, entity resolution, on-screen context, and cross-app workflows.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Summarizes the concrete next steps: model and index your entities to Spotlight so Siri can find your content, adopt the **app schema domains** matching your core experiences, adopt **Transferable** to enable content import and export, and test early and often in the order AppIntentsTesting, Shortcuts, Spotlight, then Siri. All these APIs are available today and are designed to scale as Siri evolves—bringing your app to Siri isn't just adding voice support, it makes your app faster, more accessible, and easier to use across the system.

title: What’s new in the Foundation Models framework
gloss: Foundation Models 框架的新功能
takeaway: Foundation Models framework 新增影像理解、Private Cloud Compute、第三方模型整合與 Dynamic Profiles，打造更強大的 agentic App。
chapters: Routing between craft analysis and brainstorm
Describing the profile for craft app
Describing the profile for craft app

points.text: 新的 **on-device 模型** 提供更大的 context size，並可用 **tokenCount** 預估輸入長度。
支援 **影像理解（Vision）**，可在 respond 中透過 **Attachment** 附加 UIImage 等影像類型發問。
可存取 **Private Cloud Compute**，並透過模型抽象層整合第三方與開源模型。
以 **DynamicProfile** 為 agentic App 動態組合 instructions、tools 與模型設定，並支援模式切換。
提供 **fm 命令列工具**、Evaluations framework 與 **Foundation Models Python SDK** 等開發配套。

audience: 想在 App 中加入 **裝置端生成式 AI 與 agentic 功能** 的 Apple 平台開發者。
gloss_en: What's new in the Foundation Models framework
takeaway_en: The Foundation Models framework adds image understanding, Private Cloud Compute, third-party model integration, and Dynamic Profiles to build more powerful agentic apps.

points_en.text: The new **on-device model** offers a larger context size, and you can estimate input length with **tokenCount**.
Supports **image understanding (Vision)**: attach images such as UIImage via an **Attachment** in respond to ask questions about them.
Access **Private Cloud Compute**, and integrate third-party and open source models through a model abstraction layer.
Use **DynamicProfile** to dynamically compose instructions, tools, and model settings for agentic apps, with support for mode switching.
Ships developer tooling including the **fm command-line tool**, the Evaluations framework, and the **Foundation Models Python SDK**.

audience_en: Apple platform developers who want to add **on-device generative AI and agentic features** to their apps.
summary: 繼去年推出 Foundation Models 框架（guided generation、snapshot streaming、tool protocol）後，今年的重點是「深入並超越 OS 的整合、更多元的模型，以及打造 agentic 體驗的新基礎元件」。最大的消息是 **Foundation Models 框架正式開源**，同時推出會在 OS 版本之間持續更新的 **Foundation Models framework utilities** 套件，提供新興與實驗性的建構積木。框架本身也帶來全新、從頭打造、在邏輯與工具呼叫上更強的**裝置端模型**，並沿用 iOS 26.4 起的 contextSize 與 tokenCount API 讓 App 依硬體調整。

模型能力大幅擴張。裝置端模型新增**視覺（Vision）能力**：只要在 prompt builder 中插入 Attachment 影像即可詢問圖片內容，可由 UIImage、NSImage、CGImage、Core Image、CoreVideo Pixel Buffer 或檔案 URL 建立，支援任意尺寸與比例（但越大越耗 token 與延遲）。需要更多算力時，可用全新的 **PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel**——與 Apple Intelligence 同源的大型模型，具 32,000 token 上下文與**推理（reasoning）**能力，透過 contextOptions 的 reasoningLevel 控制思考深度；它無需帳號設定、驗證或 API key，完全私密（不儲存 prompt 且可供獨立研究者驗證），並讓框架登陸 watchOS。此外開放**模型抽象層**（LanguageModel protocol），既有的 SystemLanguageModel 與 PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel 皆符合此協定，並開源 CoreAILanguageModel 與 MLXLanguageModel；Anthropic 與 Google 也將發佈 Swift 套件提供前沿伺服器模型，用法只需 import、初始化模型再傳入 session，下游程式碼不變。使用第三方模型需自理驗證與計費，務必以 OAuth 取得 token 並存於 KeyChain，並可用 session／response 的 usage 屬性追蹤 token 用量（含 cache 與 reasoning token）。

在系統工具方面，框架內建多個由 **Vision 框架**支援的原生工具：**BarcodeReaderTool** 讀取條碼、**OCRTool** 從影像擷取結構化文字；以及由 **Spotlight** 支援的 search tool，可實作完全本機的 **RAG（Retrieval-Augmented Generation）**。Agentic 體驗的核心則是全新的宣告式 API **dynamic profiles**：以 DynamicProfile 協定宣告 body，其中的 Profile 由 instructions 與 tools 組成，可在單一 LanguageModelSession 內依 App 狀態（如 craftAnalysis 與 brainstorm 兩種模式）切換，並用 modifier 指定不同模型（如 .model(PCC)）與 .reasoningLevel，同時保留對話歷史；框架負責在任一時刻將 DynamicProfile 解析為單一 active Profile 並處理轉換。另推出 **Evaluations 框架**量化智慧功能品質，讓你在調整 prompt 時以統計方式衡量準確度。

最後是 Mac 生產力與開源。macOS 27 帶來全新的 **fm 命令列工具**，可在終端機存取裝置端模型與 PCC，支援 fm chat 互動、也能接入 shell script 做文件摘要、資訊擷取或依影像內容生成檔名。**Foundation Models SDK for Python** 讓資料科學家以幾行 Python 存取同一個裝置端模型、檢查可用性並產生結構化回應。開源方面，utilities 套件提供 transcript 管理的 profile modifier、載入程序知識的 skill API，以及支援 Chat Completions 標準的 language model；框架核心開源後也能在 Linux 等任何 Swift 執行環境運作。整體而言，搭配 Anthropic、Google、CoreAI 與 MLX，你將能「在任何地方執行任何模型」。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: Erik 與 Zhen 回顧去年 Foundation Models 框架的 guided generation、snapshot streaming 與 tool protocol，並定調今年主題：深入與超越 OS 的整合、更多元模型，以及 agentic 新基礎元件。最重磅消息是**框架正式開源**，並推出會在 OS 版本間持續更新的 **Foundation Models framework utilities** 套件提供實驗性建構積木。

deepdive.title: New on-device model
deepdive.body: 介紹全新、從頭打造的**裝置端模型**，在智慧度、邏輯與工具呼叫上全面更強，並持續改進 guardrails 以減少 iOS 26.4 起已降低的誤判。此模型是今年諸多模型更新的起點，後續再疊加視覺能力與伺服器模型。

deepdive.title: Context size and token counting
deepdive.body: 說明 iOS 26.4 起推出的 **contextSize** 與 **tokenCount** API，可檢視模型上下文大小並計算 instructions、prompt 與 transcript 的 token 數（範例顯示 contextSize 為 8192）。建議用這些 API 讓 App 依執行硬體調整行為。

deepdive.title: Vision: image understanding
deepdive.body: 裝置端模型新增**視覺能力**，API 是既有 prompt builder 的自然延伸：在 prompt 中插入影像 **Attachment** 並搭配文字，模型即可回答關於圖片的問題（示範詢問桌上 origami 照片）。這解鎖了全新類別的應用。

deepdive.title: Attachable image types
deepdive.body: 列出可建立影像 attachment 的型別：**UIImage**、**NSImage**、**CGImage**、Core Image 型別、**CoreVideo Pixel Buffer** 與檔案 URL。模型支援任意尺寸與比例、無需裁切或填補，但需留意較大影像會消耗更多 token 並增加延遲。

deepdive.title: Private Cloud Compute
deepdive.body: 推出全新 **PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel**——與 Apple Intelligence 同源的大型模型，具 **32,000 token** 上下文與**推理**能力，透過 contextOptions 的 **reasoningLevel** 控制思考深度。使用無需帳號設定、驗證或 API key，完全私密（不儲存 prompt、可供獨立驗證），並讓框架登陸 watchOS；首次下載量低於 200 萬的開發者免雲端 API 費用，iCloud+ 訂閱用戶額度更高。

deepdive.title: Model abstraction layer
deepdive.body: 開放**模型抽象層**，核心是新的 **LanguageModel** 協定，讓本機與伺服器模型都能支撐 LanguageModelSession。既有的 **SystemLanguageModel** 與 **PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel** 已符合此協定，並額外開源 **CoreAILanguageModel** 與 **MLXLanguageModel**，可在 Mac 的 Apple Neural Engine 與 GPU 上執行各式本機模型。

deepdive.title: Partner model integrations
deepdive.body: **Anthropic** 與 **Google** 將發佈 Swift 套件提供前沿伺服器模型。用法極簡：以 Swift Package Manager import 套件、初始化想用的模型，再於建立 session 時傳入，下游程式碼維持不變。但須注意第三方伺服器模型通常需自行處理驗證與計費。

deepdive.title: Inspecting usage
deepdive.body: 提醒安全實務：勿在 App binary 儲存私鑰，應以 **OAuth** 取得 access token 並存於 **KeyChain**。第三方模型多為**按 token 計費**，因此 session 與 response 新增 **usage** 屬性，可得知輸入／輸出 token 數，並區分讀自 cache 的 token 與用於 reasoning 的 token。

deepdive.title: System tools: Vision and Spotlight
deepdive.body: 介紹內建系統工具：由 **Vision 框架**支援的 **BarcodeReaderTool**（讀條碼）與 **OCRTool**（從影像擷取結構化文字），增強模型對視覺資訊的推理；以及由 **Spotlight** 支援的 search tool，用於實作完全本機的 **RAG**，是社群最常被要求的功能之一。

deepdive.title: Dynamic Profiles for agentic apps
deepdive.body: 由 Zhen 介紹 agentic 體驗的新基礎元件 **dynamic profiles**。以 crafts App 為例：先在 craft analysis 模式分析 origami 照片並透過 tool call 記錄結果，再切換到 brainstorm 模式運用 PCC 的推理能力建議創作點子。傳統做多 session 與情境調度需大量 boilerplate，dynamic profiles 改以宣告式方式解決。

deepdive.title: Routing between craft analysis and brainstorm
deepdive.body: 示範未使用 dynamic profiles 前的命令式做法：以 @Observable 物件儲存 mode，於 craftAnalysis 與 brainstorm 分支各自建立帶不同 instructions、tools 的 LanguageModelSession，並沿用 dropFirstInstructions 後的 transcript 保留歷史。範例還包含讓模型自行呼叫的 **SwitchModeTool**，以及用 withObservationTracking 在 mode 改變時更新 session。

deepdive.title: Describing the profile for craft app
deepdive.body: 展示 dynamic profiles 最簡形式：宣告 struct 並符合 **DynamicProfile** 協定，body 回傳一個由 **Instructions** 與工具（如 RecordImageAnalysisTool）組成的 **Profile**，再用 `LanguageModelSession(profile:)` 初始化 session。這把當下情境中應存在的 instructions 與 tools 以宣告式描述出來。

deepdive.title: Composing models and configurations
deepdive.body: 說明除了管理情境，還可為不同任務指定不同模型與設定並保留對話歷史。crafts App 的 craftAnalysis 與 brainstorm 各有不同 instructions／tools，前者用 **SystemLanguageModel** 即可，後者以 modifier 指定 **PCC** 並設定 deep reasoning，最終得到動態配置 model、tools 與 instructions 的單一 session。

deepdive.title: Describing the profile for craft app
deepdive.body: 以更完整的 **CraftProfile** 範例呈現：body 內依 states.mode 以 switch 在 craftAnalysis 與 brainstorm 分支回傳不同 Profile，brainstorm 分支再鏈上 `.model(privateCloudCompute)` 與 `.reasoningLevel(.deep)`。關鍵概念是 DynamicProfile 在任一時刻只解析為單一 active Profile，開發者用條件選擇，轉換由框架處理。

deepdive.title: Evaluations framework
deepdive.body: 因語言模型本質上非確定性、行為難預測，推出全新的 **Evaluations 框架**量化智慧功能的品質。它讓開發者在調整 prompt 時以統計方式衡量準確度、理解變更的影響，進而更有信心交付 App。

deepdive.title: The fm command line tool
deepdive.body: macOS 27 把模型帶到命令列：全新 **fm** 工具可在終端機存取裝置端模型與 PCC，內建 helper 列出支援功能。示範以 **fm chat** 詢問 origami 的 valley fold 含義，並能接入 shell script 做文件摘要、資訊擷取，或依影像內容生成描述性檔名。

deepdive.title: Foundation Models Python SDK
deepdive.body: 預告 **Foundation Models SDK for Python**，讓 Python 生態的資料科學家與研究者直接存取與 Swift 框架同一個裝置端模型，能檢查模型可用性並以幾行程式碼從 prompt 產生結構化回應。

deepdive.title: Open source and framework utilities
deepdive.body: 介紹 **Foundation Models framework utilities** 開源套件，提供探索 LLM 新興實務的建構積木：transcript 管理的 profile modifier、載入程序知識的 **skill API**，以及支援 **Chat Completions** 標準的 language model。此套件會隨工具與趨勢演進而持續成長。

deepdive.title: Foundation Models SDK for Python
deepdive.body: 以 Python 程式碼示範 SDK 用法：import 套件、建立 SystemLanguageModel、以 is_available() 檢查可用性，再建立 LanguageModelSession 並 await session.respond 產生回應。涵蓋 Swift 框架的核心功能，可快速從 prompt 走到結構化結果。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: Erik 與 Zhen 收尾，強調本場只是冰山一角，建議觀看 Evaluations、Private Cloud Compute、強化版 Xcode instrument 與 dynamic profiles 等深入場次。下一步可探索範例 App 學習 dynamic profiles，並開始熟悉 Evaluations 框架。

summary_en: Following last year's Foundation Models framework (guided generation, snapshot streaming, the tool protocol), this year focuses on integrations into and beyond the OS, a wider variety of models, and new primitives for agentic experiences. The headline news is that the **Foundation Models framework is going open source**, alongside a new **Foundation Models framework utilities** package that updates between OS releases to deliver emerging and experimental building blocks. The framework also ships a new, ground-up **on-device model** that is better at logic and tool calling, and continues to use the contextSize and tokenCount APIs (from iOS 26.4) so apps can adapt to their hardware.

Model capabilities expand significantly. The on-device model gains **Vision**: just insert an image Attachment into the prompt builder to ask about a picture, created from UIImage, NSImage, CGImage, Core Image, CoreVideo Pixel Buffers, or file URLs, with any size or aspect ratio supported (though larger images cost more tokens and latency). For more horsepower, the new **PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel** is the same large model that powers Apple Intelligence, with a 32,000-token context window and **reasoning**, controlled via reasoningLevel on contextOptions. It needs no account setup, authentication, or API keys, is fully private (no prompts stored, independently verifiable), and brings the framework to watchOS. The framework also opens a **model abstraction layer** (the LanguageModel protocol); SystemLanguageModel and PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel already conform, and CoreAILanguageModel and MLXLanguageModel are open-sourced. Anthropic and Google are publishing Swift packages for frontier server models—just import, initialize, and pass the model into the session, with downstream code unchanged. Third-party server models require your own auth and billing, so use OAuth and store tokens in KeyChain, and track token usage via the new usage property on sessions and responses (including cached and reasoning tokens).

For system tools, the framework adds native tools backed by the **Vision framework**: **BarcodeReaderTool** to read barcodes and **OCRTool** to extract structured text from images, plus a **Spotlight**-powered search tool for fully local **RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)**. The core of agentic experiences is the new declarative **dynamic profiles** API: declare a DynamicProfile with a body whose Profile is composed of instructions and tools, switch within a single LanguageModelSession based on app state (e.g. craftAnalysis vs. brainstorm modes), and use modifiers to specify different models (e.g. .model(PCC)) and .reasoningLevel while preserving conversation history. A DynamicProfile resolves to a single active Profile at any moment; you pick it with conditionals and the framework handles the transition. The new **Evaluations framework** quantifies the quality of your intelligence features so you can measure accuracy statistically as you tweak prompts.

Finally, Mac productivity and open source. macOS 27 brings the new **fm command-line tool** to access the on-device model and PCC from the terminal, supporting interactive fm chat and shell-script integration for document summaries, information extraction, or generating file names from image content. The **Foundation Models SDK for Python** lets data scientists access the same on-device model in a few lines of Python, check availability, and generate structured responses. On open source, the utilities package provides profile modifiers for transcript management, a skill API for procedural knowledge loading, and a language model that speaks the Chat Completions standard; with the framework core open-sourced it can run anywhere Swift runs, including Linux servers. Together with Anthropic, Google, CoreAI, and MLX, you'll be able to run any model, anywhere.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Erik and Zhen recap last year's guided generation, snapshot streaming, and tool protocol, then frame this year's themes: integrations into and beyond the OS, a wider variety of models, and new agentic primitives. The biggest news is that the **framework is going open source**, alongside a new **Foundation Models framework utilities** package that updates between OS releases with experimental building blocks.

deepdive_en.title: New on-device model
deepdive_en.body: Introduces a new, ground-up **on-device model** that is better across the board, especially at logic and tool calling, with continued guardrail refinements that reduce the false positives already lowered in iOS 26.4. This model is the starting point for the many model updates that follow, layering on vision and server models.

deepdive_en.title: Context size and token counting
deepdive_en.body: Covers the **contextSize** and **tokenCount** APIs introduced in iOS 26.4 for inspecting the model's context size and counting tokens in instructions, prompts, and transcripts (the example shows a contextSize of 8192). The advice is to use these going forward so apps adapt to the hardware they run on.

deepdive_en.title: Vision: image understanding
deepdive_en.body: The on-device model gains **Vision**, with an API that is a natural extension of the existing prompt builders: insert an image **Attachment** alongside text and the model can answer questions about the image (demoed with a photo of origami). This unlocks entire new categories of applications.

deepdive_en.title: Attachable image types
deepdive_en.body: Lists the types an image attachment can be created from: **UIImage**, **NSImage**, **CGImage**, Core Image types, **CoreVideo Pixel Buffers**, and file URLs. The model supports any size and aspect ratio with no cropping or padding, but larger images consume more tokens and add latency.

deepdive_en.title: Private Cloud Compute
deepdive_en.body: Introduces the new **PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel**, the same large model that powers Apple Intelligence, with a **32,000-token** context window and **reasoning**, controlled via the **reasoningLevel** argument on contextOptions. It requires no account setup, authentication, or API keys and is fully private (no prompts stored, independently verifiable), and it brings the framework to watchOS; developers with under 2 million first-time downloads pay no cloud API costs, and iCloud+ subscribers get higher limits.

deepdive_en.title: Model abstraction layer
deepdive_en.body: Opens up the **model abstraction layer**, built on a new **LanguageModel** protocol that lets both local and server models back a LanguageModelSession. **SystemLanguageModel** and **PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel** already conform, and two more implementations are open-sourced: **CoreAILanguageModel** and **MLXLanguageModel**, for running many local models on the Apple Neural Engine and your Mac's GPU.

deepdive_en.title: Partner model integrations
deepdive_en.body: **Anthropic** and **Google** are publishing Swift packages providing frontier server models. Usage is simple: import the package with Swift Package Manager, initialize the model you want, and pass it when creating the session, with downstream code unchanged. Note that third-party server models typically require you to handle both authentication and billing.

deepdive_en.title: Inspecting usage
deepdive_en.body: Stresses security practices: never store private keys in your app binary, fetch access tokens via **OAuth**, and store them in **KeyChain**. Since third-party models are usually billed per token, sessions and responses gain a **usage** property reporting input and output token counts, distinguishing tokens read from cache and tokens used for reasoning.

deepdive_en.title: System tools: Vision and Spotlight
deepdive_en.body: Introduces built-in system tools: the **Vision framework**-backed **BarcodeReaderTool** (read barcodes) and **OCRTool** (extract structured text from images), which strengthen the model's reasoning about visual information, plus a **Spotlight**-powered search tool for implementing fully local **RAG**, one of the most requested features.

deepdive_en.title: Dynamic Profiles for agentic apps
deepdive_en.body: Zhen introduces **dynamic profiles**, the new primitive for agentic experiences. In the crafts app, a session starts in craft analysis mode to analyze origami photos and record findings via a tool call, then switches to brainstorm mode using PCC's reasoning to suggest creative projects. Doing this with multiple sessions and orchestration involves a lot of boilerplate, which dynamic profiles solve declaratively.

deepdive_en.title: Routing between craft analysis and brainstorm
deepdive_en.body: Shows the imperative approach before dynamic profiles: an @Observable object stores the mode, and craftAnalysis and brainstorm branches each create a LanguageModelSession with different instructions and tools, reusing the transcript (after dropFirstInstructions) to keep history. The example includes a **SwitchModeTool** the model can call and uses withObservationTracking to update the session when mode changes.

deepdive_en.title: Describing the profile for craft app
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates the simplest dynamic profile: declare a struct conforming to **DynamicProfile** with a body returning a **Profile** composed of **Instructions** and tools (e.g. RecordImageAnalysisTool), then initialize the session with `LanguageModelSession(profile:)`. This declaratively describes the instructions and tools that should be present in the context at that moment.

deepdive_en.title: Composing models and configurations
deepdive_en.body: Explains that beyond managing context, you can specify different models and configurations per task while keeping conversation history. The crafts app's craftAnalysis and brainstorm each have their own instructions and tools; the former is fine with **SystemLanguageModel**, while the latter uses modifiers to specify **PCC** with deep reasoning, yielding a single session with dynamically configured model, tools, and instructions.

deepdive_en.title: Describing the profile for craft app
deepdive_en.body: Shows a fuller **CraftProfile** example: the body switches on states.mode to return different Profiles for craftAnalysis and brainstorm, with the brainstorm branch chaining `.model(privateCloudCompute)` and `.reasoningLevel(.deep)`. The key concept is that a DynamicProfile resolves to a single active Profile at any time; you pick it with conditionals and the framework handles the transition.

deepdive_en.title: Evaluations framework
deepdive_en.body: Because language models are inherently non-deterministic and hard to predict, the new **Evaluations framework** measures the quality of your intelligence features. It helps app developers quantify accuracy as they tweak prompts, understand the statistical impact of changes, and deliver with confidence.

deepdive_en.title: The fm command line tool
deepdive_en.body: macOS 27 brings the models to the command line with the new **fm** tool, which accesses the on-device model and PCC from the terminal and lists its supported features via a helper. The demo uses **fm chat** to ask what a valley fold means in origami, and shows plugging fm into shell scripts to summarize documents, extract information, or generate descriptive file names from image content.

deepdive_en.title: Foundation Models Python SDK
deepdive_en.body: Previews the **Foundation Models SDK for Python**, giving data scientists and researchers in the Python ecosystem direct access to the same on-device model as the Swift framework, with the ability to check availability and generate structured responses in a few lines of code.

deepdive_en.title: Open source and framework utilities
deepdive_en.body: Introduces the open-source **Foundation Models framework utilities** package, a collection of building blocks for exploring emerging LLM practices: profile modifiers for transcript management, a **skill API** for procedural knowledge loading, and a language model that interfaces with servers using the **Chat Completions** standard. The package is designed to grow as tools and trends evolve.

deepdive_en.title: Foundation Models SDK for Python
deepdive_en.body: Walks through the Python SDK in code: import the package, create a SystemLanguageModel, check availability with is_available(), then create a LanguageModelSession and await session.respond to generate a response. It carries the core features of the Swift framework, taking you from prompt to structured result quickly.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Erik and Zhen wrap up, noting this session only scratches the surface and pointing to deep dives on the Evaluations framework, Private Cloud Compute, the enhanced Xcode instrument, and dynamic profiles. Suggested next steps are to explore the sample app to learn about dynamic profiles and to start getting familiar with the Evaluations framework.

title: Build agentic app experiences with the Foundation Models framework
gloss: 用 Foundation Models 框架打造 agentic App 體驗
takeaway: 透過 DynamicProfile、動態指令、transcript 管理與多 agent 編排（baton-pass、phone-a-friend、skills），用 Foundation Models 打造可隨階段切換模型與行為的 agentic 體驗。
chapters: Initialize your session with your dynamic profile
Read and write session properties in a profile
Define a tool that throws an error
Set the transcript error handling policy

points.text: 新的 **DynamicProfile** 與 **DynamicInstructions** 能依 App 階段動態切換**指令、模型（on-device 或 PCC）、溫度與推理層級**。
提供 **historyTransform**、rollingWindow、lifecycle modifiers 與 **@SessionProperty** 來管理 transcript 歷史與自訂工作階段狀態。
多 agent 編排模式：**baton-pass**（交棒切換模式）、**phone-a-friend**（委派子 session）與 **Skills**（依需求注入知識）。
可用 **toolCallingMode**（.required/.disallowed）控制工具呼叫並跳出迴圈，並以 **transcriptErrorHandlingPolicy** 決定錯誤後保留或還原 transcript。
最後涵蓋 **效能、準確度與評估**（evaluations），協助衡量 agentic 流程的品質。

audience: **已熟悉 Foundation Models 基礎、想進一步打造多階段 agentic 流程**的進階 AI 功能開發者。
gloss_en: Build agentic app experiences with Foundation Models
takeaway_en: Use DynamicProfile, dynamic instructions, transcript management, and multi-agent orchestration (baton-pass, phone-a-friend, skills) to build agentic experiences with Foundation Models that switch models and behavior by stage.

points_en.text: The new **DynamicProfile** and **DynamicInstructions** let you dynamically switch **instructions, model (on-device or PCC), temperature, and reasoning level** based on your app's stage.
Provides **historyTransform**, rollingWindow, lifecycle modifiers, and **@SessionProperty** to manage transcript history and customize session state.
Multi-agent orchestration patterns: **baton-pass** (handing off between modes), **phone-a-friend** (delegating to a sub-session), and **Skills** (injecting knowledge on demand).
Use **toolCallingMode** (.required/.disallowed) to control tool calls and break out of loops, and **transcriptErrorHandlingPolicy** to decide whether to keep or restore the transcript after an error.
Finally covers **performance, accuracy, and evaluations** to help you measure the quality of your agentic flows.

audience_en: Advanced AI feature developers who **already know the Foundation Models basics and want to build multi-stage agentic flows**.
summary: 本場介紹 **Foundation Models framework** 的新一組 API——**Dynamic profiles**，用來解決 agentic 體驗的兩大難題：在長時間 session 中做 **context management**（修剪或摘要 transcript 以守住模型的 context window），以及在多模型間建立**邊界**（依能力與成本選用最適模型）。Apple 把這些設計成低階且彈性的 primitive，並同步推出開源 Swift 套件 **Foundation Models framework utilities**，內含建構 agentic 體驗的可重用元件，會在 OS 版本之間持續更新。

**`DynamicProfile`** 讓你在同一個 `LanguageModelSession` 內切換模型。每個 **Profile** 代表一種設定狀態或 agent，由 instructions、tools 與 modifiers（控制 model、temperature、samplingMode、reasoningLevel 等）組成。範例 Origami 手作 app 依 brainstorm／planning／reviewing 三個階段，分別搭配 **PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel**（需廣博知識與創意，溫度設 1、reasoning 設 deep）與 **SystemLanguageModel**（省下伺服器呼叫）。可重用的指令與工具用 **`DynamicInstructions`** 打包並可組合巢狀；由於 profile 的 body 每次 prompt 都會重新求值，切換 mode 就像「換帽子」般切換 agent。

切換模型也意味著要管理 **transcript**：可用 **`historyTransform`**（prompt 前對 history 做局部、不永久變更的轉換，例如丟掉 tool call 以省 context）或內建的 **history** session property（會跨所有 profile 生效、且有損）來修剪、聚焦或在轉到較不私密模型時 redact PII。**Lifecycle modifiers**（如 `onResponse`）讓你在 session 各時點插入命令式程式，搭配自訂的 **session properties**（用 `@SessionPropertyEntry` 宣告、跨工具與 profile 共享）可在每次回應後摘要並保存。

orchestration 介紹兩種模式：**baton-pass**（協作——多個 profile 共享完整 transcript，靠工具切換 active 變數來交棒，接棒者產出最終回答）與 **phone-a-friend**（諮詢——工具 spawn 一個 transcript 獨立的短命子 session，回傳結果後消失，由父 profile 給最終答案）；utilities 套件另提供 Skills 型別。新增的 **Tool calling mode**（allowed／disallowed／required）讓你控制何時呼叫工具；用 required 時要自備跳出條件（用變數條件化，或讓 final-answer tool 丟錯中止迴圈）。丟錯或取消預設會 **revertTranscript**，新的 **`transcriptErrorHandlingPolicy`** 可改為 **preserveTranscript** 並手動修整可變的 transcript。最後提醒：改寫 history 會使 **KV cache** 失效進而增加延遲，也可能讓模型混淆而影響準確度，務必用 Foundation Models Instrument 量測、並用 **Evaluations framework** 以資料驅動驗證。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: Erik 與 Oliver 開場，點出 **Dynamic profiles** 要解的兩個問題：長 session 的 **context management**（修剪或摘要 transcript 守住 context window），以及用多模型時依**能力與成本**建立邊界。強調這領域週週在變，故把 API 設計成彈性 primitive，並宣布開源 Swift 套件 **Foundation Models framework utilities**，收納新興或實驗性的 agentic 模式、在 OS 版本間更新。

deepdive.title: The example app and agents
deepdive.body: 以手作 app **Origami** 為貫穿範例：可做摺紙與鉤針教學，使用者上傳照片發想點子、回饋後生成教學、過程中再上傳進度照取得技巧建議。各階段共享 context 但優先順序不同，可受益於不同模型、指令與設定——這些設定就是 **agents**，代表 app 行事、各有目標與能力。

deepdive.title: Declaring a dynamic profile
deepdive.body: **`DynamicProfile`** 讓你在 `LanguageModelSession` 內宣告多個 **Profile**（各代表一種設定狀態或 agent），由 instructions、tools 與 modifiers 組成。先聚焦 brainstorming 階段：給它說明目標的指令與一個產生標題的工具，並在使用者做摺紙時額外加入相關指令與工具。

deepdive.title: Dynamic instructions
deepdive.body: 引入 **`DynamicInstructions`**：把相關的 tools 與 instructions 打包成可在程式各處重用的單一元件（如 `OrigamiExpert` 收納摺紙知識與工具），且可組合——巢狀於另一個 DynamicInstructions 的 body 內會把指令與工具串接起來。

deepdive.title: DynamicInstructions
deepdive.body: 示範以 `DynamicInstructions` 建立 `BrainstormFacilitator` 來承載 profile 的指令，藉此把 brainstorming profile 的宣告整理乾淨。

deepdive.title: Configuring models per phase
deepdive.body: 說明各階段可配不同模型：brainstorming 需廣博手作知識與創意，故用 **PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel** 並把 temperature 設為 1 以鼓勵更有創意的回應。

deepdive.title: DynamicProfile
deepdive.body: 把三個階段補齊：planning 同樣用 PCC 並把 **reasoningLevel** 設為 deep（生成教學較複雜）；reviewing 改用 **SystemLanguageModel** 以省下不必要的伺服器呼叫。至此完成整個手作 DynamicProfile 的宣告。

deepdive.title: Initialize your session with your dynamic profile
deepdive.body: 用新的 `LanguageModelSession` initializer 帶入 DynamicProfile 即可。重點：profile 的 body 每次 prompt 都會重新求值，所以隨 app 在各 mode 間移動，session 的人格也隨之改變——像換帽子或切換 agent，可在 brainstorming／planning／reviewing 間流轉。

deepdive.title: Transcript management and history transforms
deepdive.body: 切換模型時各模型 context 上限不同，可能需修剪多餘 entry 以守住上限；此外移除不相關 entry 可提升模型專注，轉到較不私密的模型時也可 redact 私密資訊。transcript 是 session 對模型 context 的表示，DynamicInstructions 可改 instructions entry，其餘 entry 則透過名為 history 的視窗處理（如丟掉 tool call 即為簡單的修剪法）。

deepdive.title: Transcript management
deepdive.body: 示範 **`historyTransform`**：可套在 profile 上、在 prompt 模型前轉換 history，正是過濾非必要 entry 的時機（範例套在 reviewing profile 上以守住 on-device 模型的 context 上限）。重點：transform 不會永久變更 session transcript，只是 prompt 前的局部轉換，故不怕弄丟日後可能有用的 context。

deepdive.title: Custom modifiers
deepdive.body: 因 historyTransform 內容繁雜，可用 custom modifier 把複雜度藏起來：宣告一個符合 `DynamicProfileModifier` 的新型別並套用該 historyTransform。

deepdive.title: Custom modifiers
deepdive.body: 再以 `DynamicProfile` 的 extension 把此 modifier 開放重用，任何想減少 context 的新 Profile 都能套用。並指出 utilities 套件已內建多個好用 modifier，值得參考。

deepdive.title: History management modifiers
deepdive.body: 除了 transform，還有更具狀態的作法：在 session 某些時點需摘要較早的 entry 以回收 context，於每次模型回應後做能形成清楚的生命週期邊界。引出用一組新 modifier 在每次回應後執行摘要操作。

deepdive.title: Lifecycle modifiers and session properties
deepdive.body: **Lifecycle modifiers** 讓你在 profile 宣告中直接跑命令式程式、取得 profile 進度，可用於更新 session 外部狀態（如 UI 反映進度）或內部狀態（如切換 craft profile 的 mode、改 history）。並預告搭配 session properties 一起用。

deepdive.title: Lifecycle modifiers
deepdive.body: 用 `onResponse` modifier 在回應邊界改寫 history（前述的摘要時機）；同時帶出另一概念 session properties——此處用到框架內建的 history property。

deepdive.title: Declare a custom session property
deepdive.body: **Session properties** 讓你定義可被任何 Tool 或 Profile 存取的狀態。history 是框架內建的 property（會擷取 session history、可作為 historyTransform 的替代），但它有損且變更會跨所有 profile 生效；要做無損且針對特定 profile 的轉換則應用 historyTransform。亦可用 `@SessionPropertyEntry` 巨集在 `SessionPropertyValues` 的 extension 內宣告自訂 property（皆可變、需有初始值）。

deepdive.title: Read and write session properties in a profile
deepdive.body: 示範用自訂的 summary property 在 `onResponse` 時儲存對話摘要：各 Profile 可讀取其值並把摘要放進指令，讓模型掌握被丟掉的 entry 之 context；任何 profile 都能寫入、且變更跨整個 session 可見。小結：用 lifecycle modifier 在特定時點跑程式、用 history property 為所有 profile 更新 history、用自訂 session property 儲存共享狀態。

deepdive.title: Orchestration: baton-pass
deepdive.body: Erik 接手講 orchestration 的兩種模式。**baton-pass** 是協作：有兩個以上各用不同模型的 profile、一個控制 active profile 的變數，並給每個 profile 一個能設定該變數的工具，三者組成此模式。

deepdive.title: Orchestration: baton-pass
deepdive.body: 舉例：在 brainstorming 時問「怎麼摺紙鶴」，brainstorm profile 會呼叫工具把棒子交給 tutorial profile，tool output 表示交接成功，由 tutorial profile 完成最終回答。關鍵屬性：完整 transcript history 對兩個 profile 皆可見，且接棒者能一路把答案送到終點。

deepdive.title: Orchestration: phone-a-friend and skills
deepdive.body: **phone-a-friend** 是諮詢，同樣靠 tool calling，關鍵差異是工具不切換變數，而是 spawn 一個短命 session。

deepdive.title: Orchestration: phone-a-friend
deepdive.body: 舉例：問「適合小孩的有趣專案」時，模型可能判斷需要一個標題、呼叫 phone-a-friend 工具去諮詢 title profile——該工具 spawn 一個 transcript 獨立的新 session、prompt 它、把回應當 tool output 送回，子 session 隨即消失，由父 session 給最終回答。關鍵屬性：各 profile 的 transcript 彼此隔離，且父 profile 永遠負責最終答案。

deepdive.title: The skills pattern
deepdive.body: 指出 baton-pass 與 phone-a-friend 外還有其他選項，例如 utilities 套件提供的 **Skills** 型別，是 procedural context loading 的常見模式。

deepdive.title: Tool calling mode
deepdive.body: 介紹新的 **Tool calling mode** 來控制工具呼叫時機，有三個選項：allowed、disallowed、required。

deepdive.title: Tool calling mode
deepdive.body: 逐一說明：預設 **allowed**（既有行為，模型可呼叫工具也可直接回應，最常見）；**disallowed** 禁止呼叫工具（如使用者進入工具明顯無關的畫面時）；**required** 只能呼叫工具（適合把所有動作都表示成 tool call 的 agentic 系統）。用 profile 時以 modifier 指定，否則可在 `respond(to:)` 的 GenerationOptions 設定。

deepdive.title: Escaping a tool call loop
deepdive.body: 強調 required 時模型形同處於 while loop，**必須自備跳出條件**。一種作法是用變數條件化 tool call mode（例如要求呼叫工具直到模型呼叫 database 工具為止）。

deepdive.title: Define a tool that throws an error
deepdive.body: 更強硬的第二種作法：給模型一個會丟錯的 final-answer 工具，丟錯會中止 tool calling 迴圈並立即把控制權交還給你。

deepdive.title: Transcript error handling
deepdive.body: 預設情況下，工具丟錯或取消回應時 session transcript 會回滾到先前狀態。但若進階情境想允許中途取消後再續跑，就需在錯誤後保留 transcript，框架為此新增了相關 API。

deepdive.title: Set the transcript error handling policy
deepdive.body: 用 profile 時以 modifier 設定 **`transcriptErrorHandlingPolicy`**，否則直接設在 session 上。兩個選項：`.revertTranscript` 與 `.preserveTranscript`；用 preserve 時若要續用 session，得自行把 transcript 還原到良好狀態。

deepdive.title: Transcript mutation
deepdive.body: 為配合上述，session 的 **transcript property 現在可變**。但只能在 session 的 `isResponding` 為 false 時修改——在回應期間嘗試變更 transcript 屬程式設計錯誤。

deepdive.title: Performance, accuracy, and evaluations
deepdive.body: 談變更 transcript 對效能與準確度的影響。**KV cache** 是重要最佳化，會被 transcript 變更失效：一般 append 可保留 cache、降低 time-to-first-token，但改寫 history（移除 entry、改工具、改 instructions）通常觸發 cache 失效、增加延遲，唯一確定方式是用升級版 **Foundation Models Instrument** 量測。準確度上，改寫 history 可能讓模型混淆（如先前未用工具就產生標題，之後加了工具仍可能依樣行事），故進入細緻的 transcript 修改時更應用 **Evaluations framework** 建立 eval set 量化效果，做資料驅動的最佳化。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 收尾回顧：dynamic profiles 可操控模型行為與管理 transcript，並走過 phone-a-friend、baton-pass、tool calling mode、手動 transcript 管理與 KV cache。鼓勵試玩 sample app、在 revamped Xcode instrument 中測試 PCC，並擁抱 Foundation Models framework utilities。

summary_en: This session introduces a new set of **Foundation Models framework** APIs—**Dynamic profiles**—that solve two problems for agentic experiences: **context management** in long-running sessions (trimming or summarizing the transcript to stay within the model's context window) and establishing **boundaries** across multiple models (choosing the best one by capability and cost). Apple designs these as low-level, flexible primitives and ships an open-source Swift package, **Foundation Models framework utilities**, with reusable components for building agentic experiences, updated between OS releases.

**`DynamicProfile`** lets you switch models within a single `LanguageModelSession`. Each **Profile** represents a configuration state or agent, made up of instructions, tools, and modifiers (controlling model, temperature, samplingMode, reasoningLevel, and more). The Origami craft example uses three phases—brainstorm/planning/reviewing—pairing **PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel** (broad knowledge and creativity, temperature 1, reasoning deep) with **SystemLanguageModel** (to save server calls). Reusable instructions and tools are packaged with **`DynamicInstructions`**, which is composable and nestable; since a profile's body is re-evaluated on every prompt, switching mode swaps the session's persona like changing hats.

Switching models means managing the **transcript**: use **`historyTransform`** (a local, non-permanent transformation applied before prompting—e.g., dropping tool calls to save context) or the built-in **history** session property (lossy and applied across all profiles) to trim, focus, or redact PII when moving to a less private model. **Lifecycle modifiers** (like `onResponse`) let you run imperative code at points in the session, and combined with custom **session properties** (declared with `@SessionPropertyEntry`, shared across tools and profiles) you can summarize and persist state after each response.

Orchestration covers two patterns: **baton-pass** (collaboration—multiple profiles share the full transcript and hand off by toggling an active variable, with the receiver producing the final answer) and **phone-a-friend** (consultation—a tool spawns a short-lived child session with an isolated transcript, returns its result, then disappears, with the parent giving the final answer); the utilities package also offers a Skills type. The new **Tool calling mode** (allowed/disallowed/required) controls when tools run; with required you must provide an exit condition (conditionalize on a variable, or give a final-answer tool that throws to abort the loop). Throwing or cancelling defaults to **revertTranscript**, but the new **`transcriptErrorHandlingPolicy`** can switch to **preserveTranscript** with manual cleanup of the now-mutable transcript. The talk closes by warning that rewriting history invalidates the **KV cache** (raising latency) and can confuse the model (hurting accuracy), so measure with the Foundation Models Instrument and validate data-driven with the **Evaluations framework**.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Erik and Oliver open by framing the two problems **Dynamic profiles** solve: **context management** in long sessions (trimming or summarizing the transcript to fit the context window) and establishing boundaries by **capability and cost** when using multiple models. Noting the field changes week to week, they designed the APIs as flexible primitives and announce the open-source Swift package **Foundation Models framework utilities** for emerging, experimental agentic patterns, updated between OS releases.

deepdive_en.title: The example app and agents
deepdive_en.body: The running example is the craft app **Origami**, which makes origami and crochet tutorials: users upload photos to brainstorm ideas, give feedback, get a generated tutorial, and upload progress photos for technique advice. Each stage shares context but has different priorities, benefiting from different models, instructions, and options—these configurations are **agents** that act on the app's behalf with a particular goal and capabilities.

deepdive_en.title: Declaring a dynamic profile
deepdive_en.body: **`DynamicProfile`** lets you declare multiple **Profiles** (each a configuration state or agent) in a `LanguageModelSession`, made of instructions, tools, and modifiers. Focusing on the brainstorming phase: it gets instructions explaining its goal and a tool to generate titles, plus extra origami-specific instructions and tools when the user works on an origami project.

deepdive_en.title: Dynamic instructions
deepdive_en.body: Introduces **`DynamicInstructions`**: it packages related tools and instructions into a single reusable component (e.g., `OrigamiExpert` holding origami knowledge and tools), and it's composable—nesting it inside another DynamicInstructions body concatenates the instructions and tools.

deepdive_en.title: DynamicInstructions
deepdive_en.body: Shows building `BrainstormFacilitator` with `DynamicInstructions` to hold the profile's instructions, cleaning up the brainstorming profile declaration.

deepdive_en.title: Configuring models per phase
deepdive_en.body: Explains configuring different models per phase: brainstorming needs broad craft knowledge and creativity, so it uses **PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel** with temperature set to 1 to encourage more creative responses.

deepdive_en.title: DynamicProfile
deepdive_en.body: Completes the three phases: planning also uses PCC with **reasoningLevel** set to deep (generating a tutorial is complex), while reviewing switches to **SystemLanguageModel** to save unnecessary server calls—finishing the full craft DynamicProfile declaration.

deepdive_en.title: Initialize your session with your dynamic profile
deepdive_en.body: Use the new `LanguageModelSession` initializer with the DynamicProfile. Key point: the profile's body is re-evaluated on every prompt, so as the app moves between modes the session's persona changes—like swapping hats or switching agents—flowing from brainstorming to planning to reviewing.

deepdive_en.title: Transcript management and history transforms
deepdive_en.body: Switching models means different context limits, possibly needing to trim entries to stay within them; removing irrelevant entries also improves focus, and you can redact private info when moving to a less private model. The transcript is the session's representation of the model's context—DynamicInstructions can change the instructions entry, while the rest is handled via a window called history (dropping tool calls being one easy trim).

deepdive_en.title: Transcript management
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates **`historyTransform`**: applied to a profile to transform history before prompting, the right time to filter unnecessary entries (the example applies it to the reviewing profile to fit the on-device model's context). Crucially, transforms don't permanently mutate the session transcript—they're local, pre-prompt transformations—so you don't lose context that may matter later.

deepdive_en.title: Custom modifiers
deepdive_en.body: Since a historyTransform can get complex, custom modifiers hide that complexity: declare a new type conforming to `DynamicProfileModifier` and apply the historyTransform.

deepdive_en.title: Custom modifiers
deepdive_en.body: Expose the modifier for reuse via an extension on `DynamicProfile` so any new Profile that wants to reduce context can use it. Notes the utilities package already includes several useful modifiers worth reviewing.

deepdive_en.title: History management modifiers
deepdive_en.body: Beyond transforms, a more stateful approach: at certain points you summarize earlier entries to reclaim context, and doing it after each response creates a clear lifecycle boundary—leading to a new set of modifiers that run summarization after each response.

deepdive_en.title: Lifecycle modifiers and session properties
deepdive_en.body: **Lifecycle modifiers** let you run imperative code directly in a profile declaration with access to the profile's progress—useful for updating state external to the session (reflecting progress in UI) or internal state (changing the craft profile's mode, modifying history). Previews using them with session properties.

deepdive_en.title: Lifecycle modifiers
deepdive_en.body: Uses the `onResponse` modifier to mutate history at the response boundary (the earlier summarization moment), while introducing session properties—here the framework's built-in history property.

deepdive_en.title: Declare a custom session property
deepdive_en.body: **Session properties** define state accessible from any Tool or Profile. history is a built-in property (capturing session history, an alternative to historyTransform), but it's lossy and its changes apply across all profiles; for lossless, profile-targeted transformations prefer historyTransform. You can also declare custom properties with the `@SessionPropertyEntry` macro in an extension on `SessionPropertyValues` (all mutable, all needing an initial value).

deepdive_en.title: Read and write session properties in a profile
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates storing a conversation summary in a custom summary property on `onResponse`: each Profile can read it and include the summary in its instructions so it has context on dropped entries; any profile can write, and changes are visible across the session. Recap: use lifecycle modifiers to run code at specific points, the history property to update history for all profiles, and custom session properties to store shared state.

deepdive_en.title: Orchestration: baton-pass
deepdive_en.body: Erik takes over orchestration with two patterns. **baton-pass** is collaboration: two or more profiles each using different models, a variable controlling which profile is active, and a tool on each profile to set that variable—together making up the pattern.

deepdive_en.title: Orchestration: baton-pass
deepdive_en.body: Example: while brainstorming, asking how to fold a crane has the brainstorm profile call a tool to pass the baton to the tutorial profile; tool output signals a successful handoff, and the tutorial profile produces the final answer. Key attributes: the full transcript history is visible to both profiles, and the receiver can carry it across the finish line.

deepdive_en.title: Orchestration: phone-a-friend and skills
deepdive_en.body: **phone-a-friend** is consultation, also relying on tool calling, but the key difference is the tool doesn't toggle a variable—it spawns a short-lived session.

deepdive_en.title: Orchestration: phone-a-friend
deepdive_en.body: Example: asked for a fun kids' project, the model may reason it needs a title and call its phone-a-friend tool to consult the title profile—the tool spawns a new session with an independent transcript, prompts it, returns the response as tool output, and the child session disappears, with the parent giving the final answer. Key attributes: each profile's transcript is isolated, and the parent is always responsible for the final answer.

deepdive_en.title: The skills pattern
deepdive_en.body: Notes that beyond baton-pass and phone-a-friend there are other options, such as the utilities package's **Skills** type, a popular pattern for procedural context loading.

deepdive_en.title: Tool calling mode
deepdive_en.body: Introduces the new **Tool calling mode** to control when tool calls happen, with three options: allowed, disallowed, and required.

deepdive_en.title: Tool calling mode
deepdive_en.body: Explains each: default **allowed** (existing behavior—the model may call a tool or respond directly, the most common case); **disallowed** prevents tool calls (e.g., when the user is in a part of the app where tools are irrelevant); **required** means only tool calls (good for agentic systems representing all actions as tool calls). With profiles, set it via a modifier; otherwise via GenerationOptions on `respond(to:)`.

deepdive_en.title: Escaping a tool call loop
deepdive_en.body: Stresses that with required, the model is essentially in a while loop and you **must provide an exit condition**. One option is conditionalizing the tool call mode on a variable (e.g., requiring tool calls until the model calls the database tool).

deepdive_en.title: Define a tool that throws an error
deepdive_en.body: A more forceful second option: equip the model with a final-answer tool that throws an error—throwing aborts the tool-calling loop and immediately returns control to you.

deepdive_en.title: Transcript error handling
deepdive_en.body: By default, when a tool throws or a response is cancelled, the session transcript rolls back to its previous state. But for advanced cases where you want to cancel partway and then resume, you need to keep the transcript after an error, and the framework adds new API for this.

deepdive_en.title: Set the transcript error handling policy
deepdive_en.body: With profiles, set **`transcriptErrorHandlingPolicy`** via a modifier, otherwise directly on the session. The two options are `.revertTranscript` and `.preserveTranscript`; with preserve, it's on you to put the transcript back into a good state if you intend to keep using the session.

deepdive_en.title: Transcript mutation
deepdive_en.body: To support this, the session's **transcript property is now mutable**—but you can only modify it when the session's `isResponding` is false; mutating during a response is a programmer error.

deepdive_en.title: Performance, accuracy, and evaluations
deepdive_en.body: Discusses the performance and accuracy impact of mutating the transcript. The **KV cache** is a key optimization invalidated by transcript mutations: appending generally preserves it and minimizes time-to-first-token, but rewriting history (removing entries, changing tools, updating instructions) typically triggers invalidation and raises latency—the only way to be sure is measuring with the upgraded **Foundation Models Instrument**. For accuracy, rewriting history can confuse the model (e.g., having generated titles without a tool, it may keep doing so after a tool is added), so for nuanced modifications use the **Evaluations framework** to build eval sets and quantify effects for data-driven optimization.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Wrap-up: dynamic profiles steer model behavior and manage the transcript, having covered phone-a-friend, baton-pass, tool calling mode, manual transcript management, and KV caches. They encourage trying the sample app, testing PCC in the revamped Xcode instrument, and embracing Foundation Models framework utilities.

title: Debug and profile agentic app experiences with Instruments
gloss: 用 Instruments 除錯與分析代理式 App 體驗
takeaway: 用 Xcode 強化版的 FoundationModels instrument 錄製追蹤、檢視代理流程行為並最佳化其效能。
chapters: Inspect and diagnose an agentic experience

points.text: 使用 Xcode 中強化的 **FoundationModels instrument**，檢視並診斷**代理式（agentic）流程**的行為與效能。
建立適合 **LLM App 開發的心態**，理解非確定性流程需要不同的觀察與除錯方式。
用 **Instruments** 錄製追蹤（trace），並透過其 UI 逐步檢視代理執行的每個環節。
解讀**效能指標（performance metrics）**，找出延遲與瓶頸並加以最佳化。

audience: **正在用 Foundation Models 打造代理式或 LLM 功能**、需要除錯與最佳化效能的開發者。
gloss_en: Debug and profile agentic app experiences with Instruments
takeaway_en: Use Xcode's enhanced FoundationModels instrument to record traces, inspect agentic flow behavior, and optimize its performance.

points_en.text: Use the enhanced **FoundationModels instrument** in Xcode to inspect and diagnose the behavior and performance of **agentic flows**.
Build the right **mindset for LLM app development**, understanding that non-deterministic flows need a different approach to observation and debugging.
Record a trace with **Instruments** and step through every part of the agent's execution in its UI.
Interpret **performance metrics** to find latency and bottlenecks and optimize them.

audience_en: Developers **building agentic or LLM features with Foundation Models** who need to debug and optimize performance.
summary: 用 **Foundation Models** 框架打造的功能和傳統開發最大的不同，在於 LLM 的輸出是**非決定性的（probabilistic）**：同樣的輸入可能得到完全不同的回應，傳統的單元測試（斷言輸出等於固定字串）因此失效，你必須改為評估回應的品質與意圖。更棘手的是，強大的 agentic 功能往往倚賴**多模型協作**與**工具呼叫（tool calls）**，每多一個步驟就多一份延遲、也多一個可能失敗的環節，而失敗常常是「靜默」的——模型持續接受輸入、持續呼叫工具，卻從不拋出錯誤，讓問題極難追查。這正是本場次主角、Xcode 中強化版 **Foundation Models instrument** 要解決的觀測性（observability）問題。

講者以自製的 Craft 手作筆記 App 為例，示範一個互動式腦力激盪功能：使用者先與模型對話發想要做的手作，決定後 App 再切換到教學模式產生詳細步驟。這個功能用到兩組 instructions（brainstorming 與 tutorial generation）與兩個工具（**GenerateCraftIdeaTool** 與 **SwitchToTutorialModeTool**），都跑在 Private Cloud Compute 的伺服器模型上。透過 Product → Profile 選 Foundation Models 範本錄製 trace 後，timeline 的 **Instructions lane** 立刻揭露 bug：整個 session 只有一組 instructions 在作用，模式切換根本沒發生。

深入右側的 tree view（依 sessions、requests、model inferences、instructions、prompts、responses 階層展開）後，根因浮現：prompt 引用了 switchToTutorialMode 工具，但該工具其實沒有被掛進這組 instructions 的 toolset，模型因此卡在 brainstorm 迴圈裡。回到 Xcode 在 **BrainstormDynamicInstructions** 補上缺漏的工具、重新錄製，Instructions lane 就正確顯示兩組 instructions 接力，確認修復成功。

最後場次帶到效能優化的三個關鍵指標：**Time to First Token**（從送出 prompt 到開始產生回應的時間，太高代表使用者盯著空白畫面，可縮短 prompt 來改善）、**Tokens per Second**（整體產生速度，用來比較不同 prompt 設定並抓回歸）、以及 **Total Latency**（送出到收到完整回應的總時間，最能被使用者感受，建議用串流盡早呈現部分結果）。實務帶走的重點：先跑 trace，讓 model inference 節點的 token 與耗時數據告訴你時間花在哪，再對症下藥；安裝 Xcode 27 並把裝置更新到最新 OS 即可開始使用，且此 instrument 支援任何搭配 Foundation Models 使用的模型。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: 開場點出 **Foundation Models** API 讓 App 直接取用裝置端與伺服器端的生成式 AI，最好的體驗會依情境**動態調整**而非靜態。**DynamicInstructions** 讓你精準指定模型每次請求可存取的 instructions 與工具，並在每次請求前重新評估——這份彈性帶來回應性，卻也讓功能更難除錯。本場次目標就是教你用 Instruments 找出並修正這類問題。

deepdive.title: LLM app development mindset
deepdive.body: 點明用 LLM 開發的三大挑戰：**probabilistic output**（同 prompt 可能有不同輸出，使傳統斷言式單元測試失效）、**model-to-model communication**（多模型協作時資料如何可靠流動與優雅復原），以及 **observability**（多模型管線出錯時難以定位）。並拆解 LLM 應用核心迴圈：使用者送 prompt、模型推理並呼叫工具、工具執行、模型彙整結果產生回應，這個迴圈是理解整個 instrument 的基礎。

deepdive.title: Inspect and diagnose an agentic experience
deepdive.body: 以 Craft App 的腦力激盪功能為實例：使用者與模型對話發想手作，決定後切換到教學模式產生步驟。功能用到 brainstorming 與 tutorial generation 兩組 instructions、**GenerateCraftIdeaTool** 與 **SwitchToTutorialModeTool** 兩個工具，皆跑在 Private Cloud Compute 伺服器模型上，為後續用 Instruments 診斷鋪陳場景。

deepdive.title: Recording a trace with Instruments
deepdive.body: 示範從 Product → Profile 讓 Xcode 在本機建置 App，於範本選擇器挑 **Foundation Models** 範本並 Record。特別提醒此 instrument 會擷取 prompt 與 response 資料、可能含敏感資訊，雖然正式環境關閉 logging，但 trace 期間會開啟，故 trace 檔需妥善保存。實測時模型選了 Paper Butterfly 卻沒進入教學模式、只給更多點子，顯示出 bug。

deepdive.title: Navigating the Instruments UI
deepdive.body: 介紹 Instruments 介面：上方 tracks 在時間軸顯示活動、每個 track 含多條 lane，下方 detail view 顯示所選範圍摘要，點選後右側 inspector 展開細節。Foundation Models instrument 有 6 條 lane，其中 **Instructions lane** 顯示某組 instructions 與工具作用多久——此例只見一組 instructions 全程作用，揭露模式交接出錯；**Model Inference lane** 以黃色（處理輸入 prompt）與橘色（產生回應）長條呈現耗時。配合 tree view 逐層展開可追出 instruction set 從未改變的原因：prompt 引用了 switchToTutorialMode 但該工具未掛進這組 instructions，且這是無錯誤拋出的**靜默失敗**。

deepdive.title: Performance metrics
deepdive.body: 在 model inference 節點檢視 metrics 與 duration，帶出三個效能指標：**Time to First Token**（開始回應前的等待，縮短 prompt 可降低）、**Tokens per Second**（產生速度，用於跨設定比較與抓回歸）、**Total Latency**（端到端總時間，使用者最有感，建議用串流提前呈現部分結果）。這些數字是定位時間與資源去向、決定優化方向的起點。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 建議除錯之後接著探索評估，可觀看「Meet the Evaluations framework」用結構化評估衡量並改善 prompt 品質。實作前置：安裝 **Xcode 27**、把要 profile 的裝置更新到最新 OS；此 instrument 支援任何搭配 Foundation Models 使用的模型，並建議搭配 agentic 相關場次與框架文件深入。

summary_en: Building features with the **Foundation Models** framework differs fundamentally from traditional development because LLM output is **probabilistic**: the same input can yield completely different responses, so traditional unit tests that assert against a fixed string break down, and you must instead evaluate the quality and intent of a response. Powerful agentic features compound this by relying on **model-to-model communication** and **tool calls**, where every extra step adds latency and a new place to fail—and failures are often silent, with the model accepting input and calling tools yet never throwing an error, making bugs very hard to catch. This is exactly the observability problem the enhanced **Foundation Models instrument** in Xcode is built to solve.

The speaker demonstrates with a homegrown Craft journaling app: an interactive brainstorming feature where the user converses with the model to refine craft ideas, then the app switches to tutorial mode to generate detailed steps. The feature uses two instruction sets (brainstorming and tutorial generation) and two tools (**GenerateCraftIdeaTool** and **SwitchToTutorialModeTool**), all running on the Private Cloud Compute server model. After recording a trace via Product → Profile with the Foundation Models template, the **Instructions lane** in the timeline immediately reveals the bug: only one instruction set was active for the whole session, so the mode switch never happened.

Digging into the tree view on the right (organized as sessions, requests, model inferences, instructions, prompts, and responses) surfaces the root cause: the prompt references the switchToTutorialMode tool, but that tool was never added to this instruction set's toolset, trapping the model in the brainstorm loop. Returning to Xcode to add the missing tool in **BrainstormDynamicInstructions** and re-recording makes the Instructions lane correctly show two instruction sets handing off, confirming the fix.

The session closes on three key performance metrics: **Time to First Token** (how long until the model begins responding—high values leave people staring at a blank screen, reducible by shortening the prompt), **Tokens per Second** (overall generation speed, useful for benchmarking prompt configurations and catching regressions), and **Total Latency** (full request-to-response time, the number people feel most, best mitigated with streaming to surface partial results sooner). The practical takeaway: run a trace first and let the model inference node's token and duration data show where time goes, then fix accordingly; install Xcode 27, update your device to the latest OS, and note this instrument supports any model you use with Foundation Models.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: The opening notes that **Foundation Models** APIs give your app direct access to on-device and server-based generative AI, and that the best experiences adapt to context rather than being static. **DynamicInstructions** lets you specify exactly which instructions and tools the model can access, re-evaluating before every request—flexibility that drives responsiveness but also makes features harder to debug. The session's goal is to teach you to identify and fix those issues with Instruments.

deepdive_en.title: LLM app development mindset
deepdive_en.body: This chapter frames the three challenges of building with LLMs: **probabilistic output** (the same prompt can produce different results, breaking assertion-style unit testing), **model-to-model communication** (reliably flowing data between models and recovering gracefully), and **observability** (locating failures in a multi-model pipeline). It also breaks down the core LLM loop—prompt, reasoning plus tool call, tool action, final response—which is the basis for everything the instrument shows.

deepdive_en.title: Inspect and diagnose an agentic experience
deepdive_en.body: Using the Craft app's brainstorming feature as a concrete case: the user converses with the model to refine craft ideas, then the app switches to tutorial mode. The feature relies on two instruction sets (brainstorming and tutorial generation), the **GenerateCraftIdeaTool** and **SwitchToTutorialModeTool**, all running on the Private Cloud Compute server model—setting the stage for diagnosis with Instruments.

deepdive_en.title: Recording a trace with Instruments
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates recording via Product → Profile, letting Xcode build locally, choosing the **Foundation Models** template, and clicking Record. It warns that this instrument captures prompt and response data that may contain sensitive information—logging is off in production but on during a trace, so trace files must be kept safe. In the run, the model picks Paper Butterfly but fails to enter tutorial mode and just offers more ideas, exposing the bug.

deepdive_en.title: Navigating the Instruments UI
deepdive_en.body: Introduces the UI: tracks show activity on the timeline with multiple lanes each, the detail view below summarizes the selected range, and clicking opens the inspector on the right. The Foundation Models instrument has six lanes; the **Instructions lane** shows how long an instruction set and its tools were active—here only one set ran the whole session, revealing the broken handoff—while the **Model Inference lane** uses yellow bars (input prompt processing) and orange bars (response generation). The tree view then traces why the instruction set never changed: the prompt references switchToTutorialMode but that tool wasn't configured with these instructions, and it was a **silent failure** that threw no error.

deepdive_en.title: Performance metrics
deepdive_en.body: Inspecting metrics and duration on the model inference node introduces three performance measures: **Time to First Token** (the wait before a response begins, reducible by shortening the prompt), **Tokens per Second** (generation speed, used to benchmark configurations and catch regressions), and **Total Latency** (end-to-end time people feel most, best improved with streaming to surface partial results). These numbers are the starting point for understanding where time and resources go and pointing toward the right fix.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Recommends exploring evaluation after debugging—watch "Meet the Evaluations framework" to measure and improve prompt quality with structured evaluation. To get started, install **Xcode 27** and update the device you profile on to the latest OS; the instrument supports any model used with the Foundation Models framework, and pairs with related agentic sessions and the full documentation.

title: LLM search using Core Spotlight
gloss: 使用 Core Spotlight 的 LLM 搜尋
takeaway: 結合 SpotlightSearchTool 與 LanguageModelSession，可把基本搜尋升級為以 App 索引為依據的檢索增強（RAG）系統。
chapters: Ask the model with a Foundation Models session
Provide full items with an index delegate
Track the query token for refresh
Reference resolution with a contact resolver
Define an evaluation dataset with ModelSampleProtocol

points.text: 把 **SpotlightSearchTool** 加入 **LanguageModelSession** 的 tools，即可讓模型以 App 的 Core Spotlight 索引為依據回答問題。
透過 **CSSearchableIndexDelegate** 提供完整項目，並追蹤 query token 來刷新逐步顯示的結果。
用 **GuidanceProfile** 調整搜尋導引層級，裝置端模型 context 較小時宜採用 focused 導引。
可實作 **ContactResolver** 做指代解析，並以 **CustomStage** 自訂搜尋管線階段。
使用 **Evaluations** 框架與 **ModelSampleProtocol**、**TrajectoryExpectation** 建立資料集，量化評估回應品質。

audience: 適合**想在 App 中以裝置端模型打造 RAG 搜尋體驗、並善用 Spotlight 索引的開發者**。
gloss_en: LLM search using Core Spotlight
takeaway_en: Combining SpotlightSearchTool with LanguageModelSession lets you upgrade basic search into a retrieval-augmented (RAG) system grounded in your app's index.

points_en.text: Add **SpotlightSearchTool** to a **LanguageModelSession**'s tools so the model can answer questions grounded in your app's Core Spotlight index.
Provide full items via **CSSearchableIndexDelegate**, and track the query token to refresh results as they're shown incrementally.
Use **GuidanceProfile** to tune the search guidance level; favor focused guidance when the on-device model's context is small.
Implement a **ContactResolver** for reference resolution, and use **CustomStage** to customize stages of the search pipeline.
Use the **Evaluations** framework with **ModelSampleProtocol** and **TrajectoryExpectation** to build datasets and quantitatively assess response quality.

audience_en: For **developers who want to build a RAG search experience in their app using on-device models and make good use of the Spotlight index**.
summary: 這場由 Spotlight 工程團隊主講，主題是把 app 既有的搜尋升級成一套**檢索增強（RAG）**的對話式體驗：不再自己拼搜尋字串，而是把 app 內容開放給語言模型推理並生成回應。講者以一個「健行步道」app 為例——它已經把州立公園與步道、完成日期、個人筆記等內容索引進 **Core Spotlight**。一開始只用 Foundation Models 的 **LanguageModelSession** 提問，模型只會憑自身世界知識作答；要讓答案紮根在 app 自己的資料上，就得透過 **tool-calling** 讓模型去查 Spotlight 索引。

核心新 API 是 **SpotlightSearchTool**，它採用 Foundation Models 的 Tool 協定，一行就能讓模型直接搜尋 app 的 Core Spotlight 索引（支援 iOS、iPadOS、macOS、visionOS）。導入分三件事：先**設定工具**（預設搜尋 Spotlight 索引，或用 configuration 指定 file source 等來源）並把它加進 session；接著補強模型在搜尋期間看得到的**額外脈絡**——因為索引裡像文字、HTML 等高度壓縮的資料模型讀不回來，所以要在 index delegate 新增的 **searchableItems(forIdentifiers:)** 裡用 id 取回完整的 **CSSearchableItem** 並補上屬性；最後**呈現結果**，可直接訂閱 `tool.searchResults` 這個 async sequence，逐批拿回結果，並用每筆 reply 的 **queryToken** 判斷何時該刷新 UI（因為一次回應模型可能多次呼叫工具）。

工具還能依所選模型與內容客製。**GuidanceProfile** 能把模型可用的搜尋能力縮小到 app 真正需要的範圍（例如關掉 people、指定要考慮的 attributes），on-device 模型 context 較小時更適合用 focused guidance。**ContactResolver** 提供世界知識做指代消解，把「我」或某人對應到可比對索引 metadata 的身分資訊。針對複雜請求，**custom pipeline stage** 讓模型不只下單純查詢，而是組合查詢與運算（計數、建表、求平均等）；stage 是 **@Generable** 的，模型會按 prompt 即時生成，例如示範中用情感分析算出每段健行的「快樂分數」再排序。Pipeline stage 也可能透過 reply 回傳 count、table、text、statistic 等資料型別，每筆都附上 LLM 生成的 label 供 UI 自由運用。

最後講者用 **Evaluations** 框架說明如何衡量這套體驗的品質。重點放在 **result coverage**：給定一份已索引進 Core Spotlight 的資料集，模型生成的回應有沒有涵蓋我們預期它該找到的項目。流程是先用 **ModelSampleProtocol** 定義含自然語言 input、期望 output 與預期 item identifiers 的資料集（沒有真實資料時可用 Sample Generation API 大量擴充種子樣本），再以 **TrajectoryExpectation** 宣告期望軌跡（例如必須呼叫一次 SpotlightSearchTool 做查詢），最後在測試裡索引資料、跑評估，並對 coverage 等 metric 設定門檻。整場的核心訊息很清楚：我們不再寫搜尋查詢，而是提供內容，把其餘交給智慧處理。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: 講者 Jennifer 開場點出今年用 **Foundation Models** 搭配 **Core Spotlight** 把搜尋帶到新層次：只要把 app 內容開放給大型語言模型推理與生成，就能打造對話式體驗。她以自己的健行步道 app 為貫穿範例——已能瀏覽州立公園與步道、並在完成後寫下個人筆記，現在希望能直接問模型關於去過或該嘗試的健行。

deepdive.title: Ask the model with a Foundation Models session
deepdive.body: 示範最基本的起點：在 app 裡引入 **LanguageModelSession**，就能對模型提出廣泛問題，但它只會憑自身**世界知識**作答。講者強調她其實只想要關於 app 已知步道的答案，這就帶出後續用 Spotlight 為答案紮根的需求。

deepdive.title: Grounding answers with Spotlight tool-calling
deepdive.body: 說明 Foundation Models 的 **Tool 協定**如何擴充模型能力：工具宣告自己的 arguments、output 與用途說明，模型決定要用時就生成呼叫參數、再用其 output 生成回應。據此推出能讓模型對 app 的 Core Spotlight 索引下搜尋的 **SpotlightSearchTool**，並提醒前提是 app 已透過 Core Spotlight 捐贈可搜尋內容。

deepdive.title: Configure and add SpotlightSearchTool
deepdive.body: 概述採用 SpotlightSearchTool 的三個面向：為想要的搜尋類型**設定工具**、在搜尋進行時補上**額外脈絡**以取得最佳回應、以及在 UI 中以不同方式**呈現結果**。以「我去過哪些健行？」這類需要按完成日期、地點等屬性搜尋的問題作為動機。

deepdive.title: Set up SpotlightSearchTool
deepdive.body: 設定工具與直接做 Spotlight 查詢差別不大：import **CoreSpotlight** 與 **FoundationModels** 後，一行 `SpotlightSearchTool()` 就能搜尋 app 索引。也可傳入 configuration 自訂來源，例如指定 **.files** 來搜尋 app sandbox 內的檔案路徑。

deepdive.title: Add SpotlightSearchTool to a session
deepdive.body: 選定模型（**SystemLanguageModel** 或透過 Model Provider API 自選）後，把 tool 實例加進 **LanguageModelSession** 即可開始取得回應。講者拆解其「魔法」其實是一條 tool-calling 軌跡：模型決定使用工具、生成查詢、Spotlight 執行並回傳結果集描述、模型再據此推理生成最終回應。

deepdive.title: Implement an index delegate
deepdive.body: 點出問題：索引裡像文字內容與 HTML 採高度壓縮表示，可被搜尋卻無法還原成模型讀得懂的形式。因此為 **CSSearchableIndexDelegate** 新增 **searchableItems(forIdentifiers:)**，讓工具能依 unique identifier 取回完整 **CSSearchableItem**，以便在數百萬筆結果中有效率地管理回應。

deepdive.title: Displaying results and partial replies
deepdive.body: 說明兩種呈現方式：session 回應是對結果集的簡潔描述，適合 assistant 風格介面直接顯示；而搜尋結果本身也可直接從 SpotlightSearchTool 取得，對大型結果集的清單式顯示最適合。搜尋會以批次回傳結果。

deepdive.title: Provide full items with an index delegate
deepdive.body: 延伸 index delegate 的用途：這也是替模型補上**不適合捐贈做搜尋、但有助推理的 metadata** 的好時機，在 delegate 回傳 item 時為其設定額外屬性供模型參考。讓模型在生成回應時能看到原本壓縮、無法還原的細節。

deepdive.title: Track the query token for refresh
deepdive.body: 搜尋 reply 是一連串 async sequence 事件，每筆可能含一批結果直到工具呼叫完成。由於同一次回應模型可能多次呼叫 SpotlightSearchTool，因此要用每筆 reply 的 **queryToken** 判斷何時開新的顯示區段、何時刷新 UI，確保介面與模型同步。

deepdive.title: Customizing with guidance profiles
deepdive.body: 概述三種客製方式：**guidance profile** 縮小工具的搜尋能力範圍、提供**世界知識**協助指代消解、以及實作 **custom pipeline stage** 改善模型對 app 內容的推理。SpotlightSearchTool 預設把全套搜尋能力交給模型做 guided generation，但 profile 可只保留 app 需要的部分。

deepdive.title: Set a dynamic guidance profile
deepdive.body: 用 **GuidanceProfile** 選擇性開啟 people、dates 等能力，甚至指定模型該考慮的確切 attribute 清單；健行 app 不捐贈人際關係，就可略過作者／收件人的搜尋引導。建立工具時以 profile 設 **.dynamic** guide level；on-device 模型 context 受限時，則建議用 **.focused** 處理較簡單的搜尋能力。

deepdive.title: Implement a ContactResolver
deepdive.body: 示範用 **ContactResolver** 提供索引裡沒有的脈絡來做**指代消解**：當使用者問到同行的某人時，模型需要知道那是誰。resolver 回傳與使用者身分相關的聯絡資訊（顯示名稱、email、暱稱等），來源可以是帳號 profile、Contacts 框架或登入 session，再設給 `tool.contactResolver`。

deepdive.title: Reference resolution with a contact resolver
deepdive.body: 進一步說明 resolver 回傳的聯絡資訊會被拿去比對索引中的 metadata，協助工具把結果過濾到正確的集合。例如 app 若有捐贈人際關係，使用者就能詢問同行夥伴，而模型靠 resolver 把「那個人」對應到實際身分。

deepdive.title: Custom pipeline stages
deepdive.body: 針對很複雜的請求，模型可能放棄單純查詢，改用 **pipeline search**：把對索引的查詢與對結果集的運算結合以求最高效率。以「今年走了幾條步道、每月平均幾英里」為例，模型可拆成搜尋已完成健行、按月計數建表、再對所有計數求平均等階段。

deepdive.title: Define a custom stage
deepdive.body: 示範自訂的 **HappinessStage**：以 CSSearchableItem 為 input、回傳 scored 版本為 output，分數可由對 notes 屬性跑情感分析、或結合五星評等等自訂邏輯算出。stage 是 **@Generable**，可用 **@Guide** 屬性（如 threshold）告訴模型偏好哪些結果，最後加進工具 configuration 的 customStages 即可註冊。

deepdive.title: Handle a reply data types
deepdive.body: 說明模型可能在 reply 中回傳 pipeline stage 的 output data 作為另一種部分結果。資料型別涵蓋 **items、scoredItems、groupedItems、count、table、statistic、text** 等，app 可顯示其中部分或全部；每筆 reply 還附帶 LLM 生成的 **label** 描述內容，讓 UI 有最大彈性。

deepdive.title: Evaluating response quality
deepdive.body: 在這麼多客製選項下，講者用 **Evaluations** 框架來廣泛驗證模型在 app 中的回應品質：不只能評估工具呼叫是否得當、回應是否有意義，還能快速反覆調整 app 的可搜尋內容搭配不同 guidance profile。本場聚焦以 **result coverage** 衡量健行對話體驗。

deepdive.title: Define an evaluation dataset with ModelSampleProtocol
deepdive.body: 用採用 **ModelSampleProtocol** 的 **TrailRequest** 定義資料集，包含自然語言 input、模型回應 output、軌跡的 expectation，以及一組預期工具應回傳的 item identifiers。沒有真實資料時可用 **Sample Generation API** 從種子樣本（以 JSON 序列化的 query 與預期 id）大量擴充出多種變化。

deepdive.title: Define the trajectory expectation
deepdive.body: 說明如何宣告期望軌跡：對這些樣本，回應軌跡應包含一次呼叫 SpotlightSearchTool 做查詢的動作，於是用 **TrajectoryExpectation** 搭配 **ToolExpectation**（如 unordered、針對 query 參數做 keyOnly 比對）來表達。同時概覽會把「最終回應涵蓋多少預期項目」納入考量的評估流程。

deepdive.title: Run the evaluation test —
deepdive.body: 在測試 target 中載入步道 items 與 samples、把 items 捐贈進 Core Spotlight、並為此評估設定 SpotlightSearchTool，然後執行 evaluation。跑完後對任一納入的 metric（如 **ResultCoverage**）設定期望，例如以 `#expect(coverageMean >= 0.5)` 要求跨查詢的結果涵蓋率至少達 50%。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 鼓勵下載健行步道 app 範例程式碼實際操作、嘗試加入自己的自訂功能，並參考 evaluations agentic 深入講座為 app 建立自己的評估套件。結語點題：我們不再寫搜尋查詢，而是提供內容，讓智慧完成其餘的事。

summary_en: Presented by the Spotlight engineering team, this session is about upgrading an app's basic search into a retrieval-augmented, conversational experience: instead of hand-writing search queries, you make your app's content available to a language model to reason over and generate responses. The running example is a hiking-trails app that has already indexed state parks, trails, completion dates, and personal notes into **Core Spotlight**. Starting with just a Foundation Models **LanguageModelSession**, the model answers only from its own world knowledge; to ground answers in the app's own data, you use **tool-calling** to let the model search the Spotlight index.

The key new API is **SpotlightSearchTool**, which adopts the Foundation Models Tool protocol so that, in a single line, a model can search your app's Core Spotlight index (available on iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and visionOS). Adoption is three things: **configure the tool** (search the Spotlight index by default, or use a configuration to specify sources like file paths) and add it to a session; **add context** the model can see during the search — because compact representations like text and HTML can't be recovered for the model, you implement the new **searchableItems(forIdentifiers:)** on your index delegate to return the full **CSSearchableItem** by id and attach extra attributes; and **display results** by subscribing to `tool.searchResults`, an async sequence that delivers results in batches, using each reply's **queryToken** to know when to refresh the UI (since one response may call the tool multiple times).

The tool can be customized for the chosen model and content. A **GuidanceProfile** scopes the model's search capabilities to only what the app needs (e.g. disabling people, listing specific attributes); on-device models with smaller context are better served by focused guidance. A **ContactResolver** supplies world knowledge for reference resolution, mapping a person reference to identity info that can be matched against index metadata. For complex requests, a **custom pipeline stage** lets the model combine queries with computation (counting, table-building, averaging); stages are **@Generable**, generated on demand from the prompt — the demo computes a sentiment-based "happiness score" per hike and sorts. Pipeline stages can also return data types like count, table, text, and statistic via replies, each carrying an LLM-generated label for flexible UI.

Finally the **Evaluations** framework is used to measure the experience's quality, focused on **result coverage**: given a dataset indexed in Core Spotlight, how well does the model's response cover the items we expect it to find.
