You define a dataset with **ModelSampleProtocol** (natural-language input, expected output, and expected item identifiers — expandable from seed samples with the Sample Generation APIs when real data is scarce), declare the expected path with a **TrajectoryExpectation** (e.g. one SpotlightSearchTool query call), then index the data, run the evaluation, and assert thresholds on metrics like coverage. The closing message is clear: we no longer write search queries — we provide the content and let intelligence do the rest.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Jennifer opens by noting that this year **Foundation Models** plus **Core Spotlight** take search to a new level: simply make your app's content available to a large language model for reasoning and response generation to build conversational experiences. She frames it with her hiking-trails app — which already browses state parks and trails and lets her write personal notes after a hike — and her wish to ask a model about hikes she's done or should try.

deepdive_en.title: Ask the model with a Foundation Models session
deepdive_en.body: She shows the simplest starting point: introducing a **LanguageModelSession** lets the app ask broad questions, but the model answers only from its own **world knowledge**. She stresses she really only wants answers about the trails her app knows about, motivating the need to ground answers using Spotlight.

deepdive_en.title: Grounding answers with Spotlight tool-calling
deepdive_en.body: Explains the Foundation Models **Tool protocol**: a tool declares its arguments, output, and instructions; when the model decides to use it, it generates the call arguments and uses the output for response generation. This leads to **SpotlightSearchTool**, which lets a model search the app's Core Spotlight index, with the prerequisite that the app already donates searchable content to Core Spotlight.

deepdive_en.title: Configure and add SpotlightSearchTool
deepdive_en.body: Outlines the three aspects of adopting SpotlightSearchTool: **configure** the tool for the kind of search wanted, add **context** while the search is active for the best response, and **display results** in the UI in different ways. The motivating question — "What hikes have I gone on?" — requires searching by attributes like completion date and location.

deepdive_en.title: Set up SpotlightSearchTool
deepdive_en.body: Configuring the tool isn't far from a direct Spotlight query: after importing **CoreSpotlight** and **FoundationModels**, one line of `SpotlightSearchTool()` is ready to search the app's index. A custom configuration can also be supplied, e.g. specifying a **.files** source to search file paths in the app's sandbox.

deepdive_en.title: Add SpotlightSearchTool to a session
deepdive_en.body: After choosing a model (the **SystemLanguageModel** or one via the new Model Provider APIs), add the tool instance to a **LanguageModelSession** to start getting responses. She breaks down the "magic" as a tool-calling trajectory: the model decides to use the tool, generates a query, Spotlight executes and returns a description of the result set, and the model reasons over it to generate its final response.

deepdive_en.title: Implement an index delegate
deepdive_en.body: Names the problem: index data like text content and HTML is stored in a highly compact representation that can be searched but not recovered for the model to read. So a new **searchableItems(forIdentifiers:)** is added to **CSSearchableIndexDelegate** to recover the full **CSSearchableItem** by unique identifier, letting the model efficiently manage responses over potentially millions of results.

deepdive_en.title: Displaying results and partial replies
deepdive_en.body: Describes two display paths: the session response is a concise description of the result set, ideal to show directly in an assistant-style interface, while the searchable items are also available directly on SpotlightSearchTool — best for list-style display, especially when the result set is large. Search replies pass back results in batches.

deepdive_en.title: Provide full items with an index delegate
deepdive_en.body: Extends the index delegate's role: it's also the right moment to attach **metadata that doesn't make sense to donate for search but is useful for the model to reason about**, setting additional attributes on the item when the delegate returns it. This lets the model see details that were otherwise compacted and unrecoverable.

deepdive_en.title: Track the query token for refresh
deepdive_en.body: Search replies arrive as an async sequence of events, each possibly including a batch of results until the tool call completes. Because the model may call SpotlightSearchTool more than once for a single response, use each reply's **queryToken** to decide when to start a new display section and when to refresh the UI so it stays in sync with the model.

deepdive_en.title: Customizing with guidance profiles
deepdive_en.body: Overviews three customization paths: a **guidance profile** to scope the tool's search capabilities, providing **world knowledge** to help reference resolution, and implementing **custom pipeline stages** to improve reasoning over app content. SpotlightSearchTool gives its full capability set to the model for guided generation, but a profile narrows it to what the app needs.

deepdive_en.title: Set a dynamic guidance profile
deepdive_en.body: Use a **GuidanceProfile** to selectively enable capabilities like people and dates, even specifying the exact attribute list the model should consider; since the hiking app donates no person relationships, author/recipient search can be skipped. Create the tool with a **.dynamic** guide level using the profile; for on-device models with restricted context, prefer **.focused** for simpler search capabilities.

deepdive_en.title: Implement a ContactResolver
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates a **ContactResolver** to provide context not in the index for **reference resolution**: when a user asks about another participant, the model needs to know who that is. The resolver returns contact info tied to the user's identity (display name, emails, nicknames) sourced from an account profile, the Contacts framework, or a sign-in session, then is set on `tool.contactResolver`.

deepdive_en.title: Reference resolution with a contact resolver
deepdive_en.body: Further explains that the resolver's contact info is matched against metadata in the index to filter results to the right set. For example, if the app donated person relationships, a user could ask about trail companions, and the resolver maps "that person" to a concrete identity.

deepdive_en.title: Custom pipeline stages
deepdive_en.body: For really complex requests the model may forgo a simple query in favor of a **pipeline search**: combining index queries with computation over the result set for maximal efficiency. The example "how many trails this year, and average miles per month" can be broken into searching completed hikes, a counting stage that builds a table by month, then a stage averaging the counts.

deepdive_en.title: Define a custom stage
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates a custom **HappinessStage**: input is CSSearchableItem and output a scored version, with the score computed by sentiment analysis over the notes attribute or custom logic like five-star ratings. The stage is **@Generable**, using **@Guide** properties (e.g. threshold) to inform which results to prefer, and is registered by adding it to the tool configuration's customStages.

deepdive_en.title: Handle a reply data types
deepdive_en.body: Explains the model may send back a pipeline stage's output data in a reply as another kind of partial result. The data types span **items, scoredItems, groupedItems, count, table, statistic, and text**, and the app can display some or all; each reply also carries an LLM-generated **label** describing the content for maximum UI flexibility.

deepdive_en.title: Evaluating response quality
deepdive_en.body: With so many customization options, she turns to the **Evaluations** framework to verify response quality broadly: not only how well the model calls the tool and how meaningful the response is, but also rapidly iterating on searchable content paired with different guidance profiles. This session focuses on **result coverage** for the hiking conversational experience.

deepdive_en.title: Define an evaluation dataset with ModelSampleProtocol
deepdive_en.body: A **TrailRequest** adopting **ModelSampleProtocol** defines the dataset with natural-language input, the model-response output, a trajectory expectation, and a set of expected item identifiers the tool should return. Without real data, the **Sample Generation APIs** expand seed samples (query and expected ids serialized as JSON) into many variations.

deepdive_en.title: Define the trajectory expectation
deepdive_en.body: Shows how to declare the expected path: for these samples the response trajectory should include one call to SpotlightSearchTool to perform a query, expressed with a **TrajectoryExpectation** plus a **ToolExpectation** (e.g. unordered, key-only match on the query argument). It also previews an evaluation flow that accounts for how many expected items appear in the final response.

deepdive_en.title: Run the evaluation test —
deepdive_en.body: In the test target, load the trail items and samples, donate the items to Core Spotlight, and configure SpotlightSearchTool for the evaluation, then run it. After the run, set expectations on any included metric such as **ResultCoverage**, e.g. `#expect(coverageMean >= 0.5)` to require at least 50% coverage across queries.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Encourages downloading the hiking-trails sample code, trying your own custom functionality, and building an evaluation suite with inspiration from the evaluations agentic deep dive. The closing line: we're not writing search queries anymore — we provide the content and let intelligence do the rest.

title: Principles of great design
gloss: 卓越設計的原則
takeaway: 以目的、能動性、責任、熟悉感、彈性、簡潔、工藝與愉悅這幾項基本原則，作為打造優秀 Apple 平台體驗的設計準則。

points.text: 深入探討 Apple 平台的**基本設計原則**，建立判斷好設計的共同語言。
從**目的（Purpose）與能動性（Agency）**出發，讓設計服務使用者的意圖。
強調**責任（Responsibility）、熟悉感（Familiarity）與彈性（Flexibility）**，兼顧信任與適應力。
以**簡潔（Simplicity）、工藝（Craft）與愉悅（Delight）**收尾，追求細節品質與情感體驗。

audience: **設計師與在意產品體驗的開發者**，想建立紮實設計判斷力的人。
gloss_en: Principles of great design
takeaway_en: Use the fundamental principles of purpose, agency, responsibility, familiarity, flexibility, simplicity, craft, and delight as the design guidelines for building great Apple platform experiences.

points_en.text: Dive deep into the **fundamental design principles** for Apple platforms, building a shared language for judging good design.
Start from **purpose and agency** so design serves the user's intent.
Emphasize **responsibility, familiarity, and flexibility**, balancing trust and adaptability.
Close with **simplicity, craft, and delight**, pursuing detail quality and emotional experience.

audience_en: **Designers and developers who care about product experience** and want to build solid design judgment.
summary: 這場由 Apple Design Evangelists Linda 與 Doug 主講的設計專題，回到最根本的問題：什麼是設計？他們的答案是「**帶著意圖去製作（making something with intention）**」——聚焦對人最重要的事，做出真正有價值的東西。每加一個功能，都在向使用者索取時間、注意力與信任，因此設計常常是「決定不做什麼」。整場圍繞八個可在 Apple 平台上打造優秀體驗的**基礎設計原則**，並強調沒有公式或唯一正解，原則之間甚至會互相拉扯，最終要靠你的知識與直覺找到最佳路徑。

八大原則依序為：**Purpose**（在動筆寫程式前先想清楚要做的東西有沒有目的）、**Agency**（把控制權交給人、提供選擇與不阻擋使用者；並以 **forgiveness** 讓人能 undo、在破壞性操作前確認來支撐自主性）、**Responsibility**（以使用者最佳利益行事，從隱私這項人權出發，只在對的時機要求必要資料並透明說明用途，並認真思考功能如何被濫用、AI 可能產生不準確或有害結果，必要時加上預覽／確認／免責，甚至移除風險過高的功能）。

接著是 **Familiarity**（建立在人們既有的知識上，善用恰到好處的 metaphor、保持行為與位置的 consistency）、**Flexibility**（承認人們以各自獨特的方式使用產品，支援不同情境與裝置、照顧不同能力與無障礙需求，並允許個人化）、**Simplicity**（簡單不等於極簡，而是 frictionless 與 intuitive，靠 concise 的用語與 clear 的階層；有時讓介面更簡單反而需要補上 context）、**Craft**（對細節的執著，用高品質的字型、色彩、圖像、流暢動畫與可靠 SDK，並持續迭代與維護），最後是 **Delight**（從你希望使用者感受到的情緒出發，是把所有原則都做對後自然湧現的成果）。建議以 **Human Interface Guidelines** 與新的設計原則頁面作為起點。

deepdive.title: Intro
deepdive.body: Design Evangelists Linda 與 Doug 開場，拋出「什麼是設計」的問題。他們主張設計不只是外觀或行為，而是 **making something with intention**——聚焦對人最重要的事。每個功能都在索取時間、注意力與信任，因此選擇做什麼，往往是決定不做什麼。

deepdive.title: Purpose
deepdive.body: 第一個原則 **Purpose**：在畫下任何草圖或寫下任何程式碼之前，先思考你要做的東西是否有目的。並強調這些原則沒有公式或唯一正解，偏重某一原則時可能在另一原則上有所取捨，最終要靠知識與直覺找到最佳路徑。

deepdive.title: Agency
deepdive.body: **Agency** 是把人放在掌控位置：提供選擇、讓介面不阻擋使用者想做的事，給予自主探索的空間。也談 **forgiveness**——人會誤觸、誤刪，要讓 undo 容易，並在破壞性操作前確認；謹慎使用 interruption，只在快要鑄成大錯時介入，讓人安心探索。

deepdive.title: Responsibility
deepdive.body: **Responsibility** 是以人的最佳利益行事，起點是隱私這項人權：不要一啟動就丟權限提示、只要求必要資料並透明說明用途。也要保護安全，認真自問功能如何被濫用、誰會受害；負責任地加入 AI 時須預期模型可能產生不準確或有害內容（如過敏食譜），用預覽／確認／免責減緩，風險過高則移除。

deepdive.title: Familiarity
deepdive.body: **Familiarity** 建立在人們既有的知識上：善用 **metaphor**（如垃圾桶代表刪除），但別太字面也別太抽象；保持 **consistency**——外觀相同者行為應相同、相同動作放在相同位置（如 Mac 視窗永遠在左上角關閉），讓人能預測接下來會發生什麼。

deepdive.title: Flexibility
deepdive.body: **Flexibility** 承認人們以如同自身一樣獨特的方式使用產品：支援不同情境（在家用喇叭、跑步用 AirPods、開車免持），為每種裝置發揮其獨特優勢；照顧年齡、語言、熟練度與無障礙等不同能力，並在無法滿足所有人時允許 **個人化**（如重排或隱藏控制項）。

deepdive.title: Simplicity
deepdive.body: **Simplicity** 是去蕪存菁讓核心目的凸顯，但簡單不等於極簡——把功能全藏起來只是看起來極簡。簡單的設計 frictionless 且 intuitive，靠 **concise**（平實用語、減少步驟）與 **clear**（用 hierarchy、間距、對比建立階層）。有時讓介面更簡單反而要**補上 context**（如顯示剩餘時間），剛剛好就是簡單。

deepdive.title: Craft
deepdive.body: **Craft** 是對細節的執著，讓人感受到你真的在乎。粗製濫造的軟體（按鈕卡頓、捲動抖動、圖示錯位、旋轉後版面亂掉）讓人質疑成果品質；精心打磨則帶來信心。要素包括高品質字型、適應明暗的色彩、清晰圖像、流暢動畫與可靠安全的 SDK，並靠 **iteration** 與持續**維護**讓設計具備 longevity。

deepdive.title: Delight
deepdive.body: **Delight** 難以定義卻一眼可辨：令人滿足、豐富，並建立真實的情感連結。它不是事後灑彩帶或加花飾，而是先**界定你希望使用者感受到的情緒**（放鬆、自信、興奮）再透過設計強化。Delight 是把前述所有原則都做對後自然湧現的結果。最後建議以 **Human Interface Guidelines** 與新的設計原則頁面作為起點。

summary_en: Presented by Apple Design Evangelists Linda and Doug, this design talk returns to the most basic question: what is design? Their answer is **making something with intention**—focusing on what's most important to people so you build something they truly value. Every feature you add asks for the user's time, attention, and trust, so design is often a matter of deciding what not to include. The talk centers on eight foundational **design principles** for building great experiences on Apple platforms, stressing there's no formula or single right way—principles can even pull against each other, and ultimately you use your knowledge and intuition to find the best path.

The eight principles, in order: **Purpose** (before sketching or coding, ask whether what you're making has purpose); **Agency** (put people in control with choices and an interface that never stands in the way, supported by **forgiveness**—make undo easy and double-check destructive actions); and **Responsibility** (act in people's best interest, starting with privacy as a human right—ask for necessary data only at the right moment and be transparent about its use, think hard about how features could be misused and how AI might produce inaccurate or harmful results, adding previews/confirmations/disclaimers or removing features whose risks outweigh their value).

Then **Familiarity** (build on what people know with well-judged metaphors and consistent behavior and placement); **Flexibility** (recognize people use your design in ways as unique as they are—support different contexts and devices, cater to a range of abilities and accessibility needs, and allow personalization); **Simplicity** (simple isn't minimal but frictionless and intuitive, achieved through concise language and clear hierarchy—sometimes simplicity even means adding context); **Craft** (an uncompromising attention to detail using high-quality fonts, colors, graphics, fluid animation, and reliable SDKs, sustained through iteration and maintenance); and finally **Delight** (start from the emotion you want people to feel—it's the natural result of getting all the principles right). They recommend the **Human Interface Guidelines** and the new design principles page as a starting point.

deepdive_en.title: Intro
deepdive_en.body: Design Evangelists Linda and Doug open with the question 'what is design?' They argue design isn't just look or behavior but **making something with intention**—focusing on what's most important to people. Every feature asks for time, attention, and trust, so choosing what to build is often deciding what not to include.

deepdive_en.title: Purpose
deepdive_en.body: The first principle, **Purpose**: before drawing a sketch or writing a line of code, think about whether what you're making has purpose. They stress there's no formula or single right answer—leaning into one principle may mean compromising another, and you find the best path with knowledge and intuition.

deepdive_en.title: Agency
deepdive_en.body: **Agency** puts people in control: offer choices, let the interface not stand in the way, and give autonomy to explore. It also covers **forgiveness**—people mis-tap and mis-delete, so make undo easy and confirm before destructive actions; use interruptions sparingly, only when a big mistake is imminent, so people feel free to explore.

deepdive_en.title: Responsibility
deepdive_en.body: **Responsibility** means acting in people's best interest, starting with privacy as a human right: don't throw permission prompts on launch, ask only for what's necessary, and be transparent about its use. Keep people safe by asking how features could be misused and who could be harmed; when adding AI, anticipate inaccurate or harmful output (like an allergy-triggering recipe), mitigate with previews/confirmations/disclaimers, or remove features when risks outweigh value.

deepdive_en.title: Familiarity
deepdive_en.body: **Familiarity** builds on what people already know: use **metaphors** (a trash can for delete) that are neither too literal nor too abstract, and keep **consistency**—things that look the same should behave the same, and the same action should live in the same place (a Mac window always closes top-left)—so people can predict what happens next.

deepdive_en.title: Flexibility
deepdive_en.body: **Flexibility** recognizes people use your design in ways as unique as they are: support different contexts (speakers at home, AirPods on a run, hands-free while driving) and play to each device's strengths; cater to differences in age, language, expertise, and accessibility; and when you can't satisfy everyone, allow **personalization** (rearranging or hiding controls).

deepdive_en.title: Simplicity
deepdive_en.body: **Simplicity** strips away the unnecessary so the core purpose shines, but simple isn't minimal—hiding everything just looks minimal. Simple designs are frictionless and intuitive through being **concise** (plain language, fewer steps) and **clear** (hierarchy via order, spacing, contrast). Sometimes making an interface simpler means **adding context** (like remaining time); simplicity is having exactly enough.

deepdive_en.title: Craft
deepdive_en.body: **Craft** is attention to detail that shows you care. Shoddy software (laggy buttons, jittery scrolling, misaligned icons, broken rotation layouts) makes people question the results; meticulous craft inspires confidence. Ingredients: high-quality fonts, light/dark-adapting colors, clear graphics, fluid animation, and reliable secure SDKs, achieved through **iteration** and ongoing **maintenance** for longevity.

deepdive_en.title: Delight
deepdive_en.body: **Delight** is hard to define but instantly recognizable: satisfying, enriching, and emotionally connecting. It's not confetti tacked on at the end but starts by **identifying the emotion** you want people to feel (relaxed, confident, excited) and reinforcing it through design. Delight is the natural result of getting all the other principles right. They close by recommending the **Human Interface Guidelines** and the new design principles page.

title: Communicate your brand identity on iOS
gloss: 在 iOS 上傳達品牌識別
takeaway: 用字體、色彩、元件與互動表達品牌個性，同時保留 iOS 使用者熟悉的操作慣性。

points.text: 在**元件（Components）**層面客製外觀時，仍要維持系統行為與使用者的操作預期。
透過**內容（Content）**呈現語氣與個性，是傳達品牌的重要一環。
善用**色彩（Color）與字體（Typography）**建立一致而獨特的視覺識別。
以**圖示（Iconography）**強化品牌印象，在熟悉與獨特之間取得平衡。

audience: 想在 iOS 上**強化品牌識別、又不犧牲系統一致性**的設計師與開發者。
gloss_en: Communicate your brand identity on iOS
takeaway_en: Express your brand's personality through typography, color, components, and interactions while preserving the operating conventions iOS users are familiar with.

points_en.text: When customizing the look of **Components**, still maintain system behavior and users' operating expectations.
Conveying tone and personality through **Content** is an important part of expressing your brand.
Make good use of **Color and Typography** to build a consistent yet distinctive visual identity.
Reinforce brand impression with **Iconography**, striking a balance between the familiar and the unique.

audience_en: Designers and developers who want to **strengthen brand identity on iOS without sacrificing system consistency**.
summary: Design Evangelist Sarah 在這場 session 探討如何在 iOS app 上表達**品牌識別**，同時維持使用者熟悉的原生操作體驗。她提出的核心心法是：在重要之處保持熟悉、在需要之處才做客製，而品牌不只是視覺（字體、色彩、圖示），更是一種感受。她特別提醒，即使你的產品在網站、行銷、實體店或其他平台都有呈現，也不應預設讓各處長得一模一樣——iPhone 使用者期待 app 看起來、用起來都像 iOS。

她借用 iOS 26 **Liquid Glass** 的概念，把介面分成兩層：負責全域導航與動作的 **UI layer**（如 tab bar、top toolbar），以及承載 app 獨特功能的 **content layer**。品牌最適合表達的地方是 content layer，而 UI layer 應盡量沿用 iOS 既有的熟悉元件。透過 Gentler Streak、Slack、Moonlitt 等案例，她說明導航元件應維持原生、僅在最有影響力或最能凸顯內容之處才客製元件，並提醒像 context menu 這類常被忽略的標準元件（SwiftUI 開箱即用）能省下大量自建與維護成本。

在 content layer，她鼓勵把它當成畫布：Crumbl 用每週更換的全螢幕影片、Moonlitt 用 edge-to-edge 漸層與 3D 元素營造沉浸感；文案的 voice and tone 也是品牌的一環。她強調 app 是動態體驗，**Zoom Transitions**（NYT Cooking）與 spring 動畫（Gentler Streak）能強化層級與互動，但延遲或掉幀會傷害觀感。色彩方面，建議把品牌色移入 content area / scroll view，讓 Liquid Glass 控制項動態取色，並像 Slack 一樣節制地用 **accent / tint color** 來傳達層級、狀態與選取；同時務必支援 Dark Mode。

字體上，自訂字型（如 Crumbl Sans）可用於記憶點時刻，但必須支援並測試 **Dynamic Type**，讓文字放大時換行而非截斷；若不想自製，**San Francisco** 系列（SF Pro、SF Compact、SF Mono、New York、SF Rounded）已能營造豐富層級。圖示方面，自訂 iconography（如 NYT Cooking）應可辨識、一致且能縮放到小尺寸並尊重各平台慣例，而 **SF Symbols**（超過 7,000 個、內建於 Xcode、像字型一樣縮放）是免費好選擇。最後談到 logo 應低調不佔空間（NYT Cooking 僅在 Home tab 顯示並隨捲動淡出）。整體原則：讓品牌服務於體驗，別讓它凌駕系統行為或混淆熟悉慣例。

deepdive.title: Intro
deepdive.body: Design Evangelist **Sarah** 開場點出核心問題：如何在表達品牌識別的同時，維持 iOS 熟悉典範的完整性。她說明品牌既有美學面（精煉的 typography、富表現力的 color、iconography 視覺語言），也是一種「感受」。她提醒不應讓 app 與網站、行銷、其他平台長得一模一樣，因為 iPhone 使用者期待 app 看起來、用起來都像 iOS，本場會分享在系統範圍內細緻表達品牌的方法。

deepdive.title: Components
deepdive.body: 借用 iOS 26 **Liquid Glass** 概念，把介面分為負責導航與動作的 **UI layer**（tab bar、top toolbar）與承載獨特功能的 **content layer**。以 Gentler Streak（識別鮮明但導航全原生）、Slack（自訂 top toolbar 但按鈕尺寸與 popover 行為仍很 iOS）、Moonlitt（自訂月相日曆元件但採用 Liquid Glass 與 concentric edges）為例，主張僅在最有影響力處才客製元件，其餘用標準元件；並特別舉 SwiftUI 開箱即用的 **context menu** 說明過度客製功能性元件反而顯得不原生或過時。

deepdive.title: Content
deepdive.body: 把 content layer 當成品牌的畫布，涵蓋影像、影片與文字。以 Crumbl 每週更換的全螢幕影片、Moonlitt edge-to-edge 漸層與動態 3D 月相為例，強調內容要有明確目的並可營造沉浸感；文案的 voice and tone 也能塑造品牌與情緒（並推薦觀看 UX writing 的相關 session）。她進一步指出 app 是動態體驗，NYT Cooking 用 SwiftUI 的 **Zoom Transitions** 連結點擊目標與轉場、Gentler Streak 用 spring 動畫讓內容生動，但延遲或掉幀會傷害使用者觀感。

deepdive.title: Color
deepdive.body: 說明 iOS 26 前 app 常在 toolbar/tab bar 用實色背景，反而壓縮內容區並產生 letterbox。建議把品牌色移入 content area / scroll view，讓 Liquid Glass 控制項動態取色並隨捲動消失。強調色彩應創造意義（層級、分組、互動），多用於控制項與動作的 **accent / tint color**；以 Slack 節制用色（未讀徽章、選取狀態等）為例，並提醒 iPhone 是個人裝置，務必支援 **Dark Mode**，連 widget 也是品牌延伸的觸點。

deepdive.title: Typography
deepdive.body: 說明 typography 可富表現力但必須維持功能性。以 Crumbl 自製的 **Crumbl Sans** 用於大標題等記憶點為例，強調自訂字型最須注意的是縮放：必須支援並測試 **Dynamic Type**，讓字級放大時換成多行而非截斷標籤。介紹系統字型 **San Francisco**（支援逾 150 種語言）及其變體 SF Pro、SF Compact、SF Mono、New York，並舉 Gentler Streak 全用系統字型（含 SF Rounded）也能做出層級與獨特感。

deepdive.title: Iconography
deepdive.body: 說明自訂 iconography 可用於 app 各處，以 NYT Cooking 銳利邊緣、線條變體、能縮放到小尺寸且尊重各平台分享慣例的圖示為佳例，強調圖示應可辨識、一致、目的明確而非過度風格化。推薦免費的 **SF Symbols**（逾 7,000 個、像字型般動態縮放、內建於 Xcode、具無障礙與在地化支援）。最後談 logo 應低調，以 NYT Cooking 僅在 Home tab 顯示並隨捲動淡出為範例，總結品牌應服務體驗、別凌駕系統行為。

summary_en: Design Evangelist Sarah explores how to express **brand identity** in an iOS app while preserving the familiar, native experience users expect. Her core philosophy: be familiar where it matters and bespoke where needed—and remember that branding is not just visuals (typography, color, iconography) but also a feeling. She cautions that even if your product appears on a website, in marketing, in a retail store, or on other platforms, you shouldn't default to making everything identical—iPhone users expect apps to look and feel like iOS.

Borrowing the iOS 26 **Liquid Glass** concept, she divides the interface into two layers: the **UI layer** for global navigation and actions (tab bars, top toolbars) and the **content layer** that holds the features making an app unique. The content layer is the best place to express brand, while the UI layer should lean on familiar iOS components. Through examples like Gentler Streak, Slack, and Moonlitt, she argues that navigation should stay native and components should be customized only where they have the biggest impact, noting that often-overlooked standard components like context menus (free out of the box in SwiftUI) save significant build and maintenance cost.

In the content layer, she encourages treating it as a canvas: Crumbl uses weekly-changing full-bleed videos and Moonlitt uses edge-to-edge gradients and 3D elements for immersion; copy's voice and tone are part of the brand too. She stresses that apps are dynamic experiences—**Zoom Transitions** (NYT Cooking) and spring animations (Gentler Streak) reinforce hierarchy and interaction, but lag or dropped frames hurt perception. For color, she recommends moving brand color into the content area / scroll view so Liquid Glass controls pick it up dynamically, and using **accent / tint color** sparingly (as Slack does) to convey hierarchy, state, and selection—while always supporting Dark Mode.

On typography, custom fonts (like Crumbl Sans) work for memorable moments but must support and be tested for **Dynamic Type**, wrapping rather than truncating as text scales; if you'd rather not build your own, the **San Francisco** family (SF Pro, SF Compact, SF Mono, New York, SF Rounded) already creates rich hierarchy. For iconography, custom icons (like NYT Cooking's) should be recognizable, consistent, scale to small sizes, and respect platform conventions, while **SF Symbols** (over 7,000, built into Xcode, scaling like a font) is a great free option. Finally, logos should be understated (NYT Cooking shows its logo only on the Home tab, fading on scroll). The overriding principle: brand should serve the experience, not override system behavior or confuse familiar conventions.

deepdive_en.title: Intro
deepdive_en.body: Design Evangelist **Sarah** opens with the central question: how to express brand identity while keeping the integrity of familiar iOS paradigms. She notes branding has an aesthetic side (refined typography, expressive color, the visual language of iconography) but is also a feeling. She cautions against making an app identical to its website, marketing, or other platforms, since iPhone users expect apps to look and feel like iOS, and previews practical guidance for expressing brand within the bounds of the OS.

deepdive_en.title: Components
deepdive_en.body: Borrowing the iOS 26 **Liquid Glass** concept, she splits the interface into the **UI layer** for navigation and actions (tab bars, top toolbars) and the **content layer** holding unique features. Using Gentler Streak (distinct identity but fully native navigation), Slack (custom top toolbar but iOS-like button sizes and popover behavior), and Moonlitt (custom lunar calendar component with Liquid Glass and concentric edges), she argues for customizing components only where impact is highest and using standard components elsewhere—citing SwiftUI's out-of-the-box **context menu** to show that over-customizing utilitarian components can feel non-native or dated.

deepdive_en.title: Content
deepdive_en.body: She frames the content layer as the brand's canvas, spanning imagery, video, and words. Using Crumbl's weekly full-bleed videos and Moonlitt's edge-to-edge gradients and dynamic 3D moon, she stresses content needs clear purpose and can feel immersive; copy's voice and tone also shape brand and emotion (with a pointer to the UX writing session). She further notes apps are dynamic experiences—NYT Cooking uses SwiftUI's **Zoom Transitions** to connect tap target and transition state, and Gentler Streak uses spring animations to make content pop, but lag or dropped frames damage perception.

deepdive_en.title: Color
deepdive_en.body: She explains that before iOS 26 apps often used solid backgrounds on toolbars and tab bars, which letterboxed and shrank the content area. The recommendation is to move brand color into the content area / scroll view so Liquid Glass controls pick it up dynamically and scroll away. Color should create meaning (hierarchy, grouping, interaction) and is best applied as **accent / tint color** on controls and actions; she cites Slack's sparing use (unread badges, selected states) and reminds that the iPhone is a personal device, so supporting **Dark Mode** is essential, with widgets being another brand touchpoint.

deepdive_en.title: Typography
deepdive_en.body: She explains typography can be expressive but must stay functional. Using Crumbl's custom **Crumbl Sans** for memorable large headers, she stresses the key concern with custom fonts is scaling: you must support and test **Dynamic Type** so labels drop to multiple lines rather than truncate as size increases. She introduces the system font **San Francisco** (supporting over 150 languages) and its variants SF Pro, SF Compact, SF Mono, and New York, citing Gentler Streak's use of system fonts entirely (including SF Rounded) to achieve variety and a distinct feel.

deepdive_en.title: Iconography
deepdive_en.body: She explains custom iconography can be used throughout an app, citing NYT Cooking's sharp-edged, line-weight icons that scale well to small sizes and respect each platform's sharing conventions, and stresses icons should be identifiable, consistent, and purposeful rather than heavily stylized. She recommends the free **SF Symbols** (over 7,000 symbols, scaling like a font, built into Xcode, with accessibility and localization support). She closes on logos being understated—NYT Cooking shows its logo only on the Home tab, fading on scroll—concluding that brand should serve the experience rather than override system behavior.

title: Design no-code games with Reality Composer Pro 3
gloss: 用 Reality Composer Pro 3 設計無程式碼遊戲
takeaway: 用 Reality Composer Pro 3 的 ScriptGraph 不寫程式就能做出 3D 互動內容與遊戲,必要時再用程式碼接收事件做進階整合。

points.text: **ScriptGraph** 讓你在 Reality Composer Pro 3 裡用**節點視覺化、不寫程式**就能建立 3D 互動內容與遊戲。
課程以實作示範**從零打造一款遊戲**的完整流程。
「Advanced techniques」展示進階用法,讓 no-code 內容也能更靈活。
可用程式碼透過 **scene.subscribe(forEventName:)** 接收 ScriptGraph 發出的自訂事件(如 "squirrelTalk")。
事件可搭配 RealityView 的 **Attachment** 把 SwiftUI 視圖綁到 3D 內容上呈現。

audience: **想用 Reality Composer Pro 3 製作 3D 遊戲或互動內容、但不想寫大量程式的設計師與創作者。**
gloss_en: Design no-code games with Reality Composer Pro 3
takeaway_en: Use ScriptGraph in Reality Composer Pro 3 to build interactive 3D content and games without writing code, then drop into code to receive events for advanced integration when needed.

points_en.text: **ScriptGraph** lets you build interactive 3D content and games in Reality Composer Pro 3 **visually with nodes, no code required**.
The session walks through the complete process of **building a game from scratch** with a hands-on demo.
The "Advanced techniques" section shows advanced usage that makes no-code content even more flexible.
From code, receive custom events emitted by ScriptGraph (such as "squirrelTalk") via **scene.subscribe(forEventName:)**.
Events can pair with RealityView's **Attachment** to bind SwiftUI views onto 3D content for presentation.

audience_en: **Designers and creators who want to build 3D games or interactive content with Reality Composer Pro 3 without writing much code.**
summary: Apple 創意總監 Saschka Unseld 示範如何在 **Reality Composer Pro 3** 裡，完全不寫程式地用 **ScriptGraph** 從零打造一款 RealityKit 遊戲。ScriptGraph 是 Reality Composer Pro 的節點式視覺化腳本系統，採用 **event-driven** 邏輯：監聽 Pinch、Drag 等事件，用節點做運算，再透過 Set 節點修改 entity 的 component。最棒的是能直接在編輯器與 Vision Pro 上即時測試與迭代。

全場以一隻睡著守著堅果的小松鼠為主軸，玩家可以伸手把堅果偷走並拖動，引導松鼠回家。建構流程從讓堅果可拖曳開始：先加上 **Input Target**、**Collision**、**Hover Effect** component，再建一個 dragNut ScriptGraph，用 `On Drag` 事件驅動 `Set Transform`。接著用 Multiply 與 public **Input variable**（dragSpeed）微調手感，並透過 **Override** 讓同一份邏輯在不同 Nut 上有各自設定。為了更有重量感，再加入 **Physics Body**，改用 `Add Force`、計算 dragDelta，並在拖曳時用 `Set PhysicsBodyComponent` 關掉重力、調高 linear damping。

進階段落示範如何用 **Prototyped Subgraph** 整理並重用邏輯（例如「偵測 bool 變化」），以及用 **Custom Node Library** 建立帶參數的 **Custom Event**（nutIsDragged），讓 Nut 的 ScriptGraph 把世界座標傳給松鼠的 ScriptGraph 來驅動旋轉。松鼠生氣的表情則透過 `Set Material Parameter` 切換 Shader Graph 裡的材質。最後要做 SwiftUI 對話泡泡時，因為 ScriptGraph 的 Scene Event 也能從 Swift 收送，講者改用 `Run with Xcode`，由 Reality Composer Pro 3 自動產生 Xcode 專案，並用 Coding Intelligence 產生訂閱 `squirrelTalk` event、以 SwiftUI Attachment 顯示泡泡的程式碼。
整體要點是：ScriptGraph 讓設計師能快速 mock up 並反覆迭代互動感受，無需寫程式即可完成大部分遊戲邏輯，而在需要 SwiftUI 介面或自訂行為時，又能無縫橋接到 Swift。延伸資源包含下載 Reality Composer Pro 3 與 Apple Developer 網站上的完整 Squirrel 範例專案。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: 創意總監 Saschka Unseld 開場，強調快速 mock up 與反覆迭代對創意工作的重要性，並表示 **Reality Composer Pro 3** 讓他不寫一行程式就能從零做出 RealityKit 遊戲。本場聚焦於 ScriptGraph，適合想快速把點子做出來的創作者。

deepdive.title: Meet ScriptGraph
deepdive.body: 介紹 **ScriptGraph** 是 Reality Composer Pro 的節點式視覺化腳本，透過 **event-driven** 邏輯運作：監聽 Pinch、Drag 與自訂事件來驅動動畫與互動。最大優勢是可直接在編輯器與 **Vision Pro** 上即時測試與迭代。

deepdive.title: A wish...
deepdive.body: 以「願望」起點說明遊戲構想：一隻守著堅果睡著、卻沒注意夜幕將至的小松鼠。玩家可在 Vision Pro 上伸手偷走堅果並自由拖動，藉此引導松鼠回家。

deepdive.title: Build the game
deepdive.body: 開始建構：為堅果加上 **Input Target**、**Collision**、**Hover Effect** component 使其可注視與高亮，再建立 dragNut ScriptGraph，用 `On Drag` 事件觸發 `Set Transform`，把 Scene Location 接到 translation。接著用 Play 與 Preview on Device 在 Vision Pro 即時測試。

deepdive.title: Advanced techniques
deepdive.body: 進階技巧：用 `Multiply by Number` 與 public **Input variable** dragSpeed 微調手感、以 **Override** 讓不同 Nut 各有設定；加入 **Physics Body** 後改用 `Add Force` 並計算 dragDelta，拖曳時以 `Set PhysicsBodyComponent` 關閉重力、提高 linear damping。再以 **Prototyped Subgraph** 重用邏輯，並用 **Custom Node Library** 建立帶 nutPosition 參數的 **Custom Event** nutIsDragged，跨 entity 傳遞並驅動松鼠旋轉與材質切換。

deepdive.title: Squirrel Talk
deepdive.body: 為松鼠加上 SwiftUI 語音泡泡。因 ScriptGraph 的 **Scene Event** 也能從 Swift 收送，講者切到 `Run with Xcode`，讓 Reality Composer Pro 3 自動產生 Xcode 專案，並用 `Send Scene Event`（squirrelTalk，帶 sayThis 字串）通知 Swift。再以 Coding Intelligence 產生訂閱該 event 並用 SwiftUI **Attachment** 顯示泡泡的程式碼。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 總結 ScriptGraph 如何幫助快速勾勒點子、迭代互動感受並實現願望，並預告還能加入松鼠行走跳躍、可拖曳的葉子與 visionOS ornament 等。鼓勵下載 Reality Composer Pro 3 與 Apple Developer 網站上的完整 Squirrel 範例專案。

summary_en: Apple Creative Director Saschka Unseld shows how to build a RealityKit game from scratch in **Reality Composer Pro 3** without writing a single line of code, using **ScriptGraph** — its node-based visual scripting. ScriptGraph works through **event-driven** logic: listen to events like Pinch and Drag, run logic on the data with nodes, then write back to an entity's components with Set nodes. The standout is being able to test and iterate live, both in the editor and on Vision Pro.

The session centers on a sleeping squirrel guarding a nut; the player reaches out, steals the nut, and drags it to guide the squirrel home. Making the nut draggable starts with adding **Input Target**, **Collision**, and **Hover Effect** components, then a dragNut ScriptGraph using `On Drag` to drive `Set Transform`. A `Multiply` node and a public **Input variable** (dragSpeed) tune the feel, with **Overrides** letting one graph behave differently per nut. For weight, a **Physics Body** is added, switching to `Add Force`, computing a dragDelta, and using `Set PhysicsBodyComponent` to disable gravity and raise linear damping while dragging.

Advanced techniques cover **Prototyped Subgraphs** for cleaning up and reusing logic (e.g. detecting a bool change), and a **Custom Node Library** for a parameterized **Custom Event** (nutIsDragged) so the nut's graph passes its world position to the squirrel's graph to drive rotation. The squirrel's upset face is driven via `Set Material Parameter` toggling a Shader Graph texture. For a SwiftUI speech bubble, because ScriptGraph Scene Events can also be sent and received from Swift, the presenter switches to `Run with Xcode` — Reality Composer Pro 3 generates the Xcode project — and uses Coding Intelligence to write code that subscribes to the `squirrelTalk` event and shows the bubble as a SwiftUI Attachment.

The takeaway: ScriptGraph lets designers quickly mock up and iterate on how interactions feel, covering most game logic with no code, while bridging seamlessly to Swift when a SwiftUI interface or custom behavior is needed. Follow-ups include downloading Reality Composer Pro 3 and the full Squirrel sample project from the Apple Developer website.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Creative Director Saschka Unseld opens by stressing how fast mock-ups and iteration matter for creative work, noting that **Reality Composer Pro 3** lets him build a RealityKit game from scratch without a single line of code. The session is aimed at creatives who want to quickly bring an idea to life with ScriptGraph.

deepdive_en.title: Meet ScriptGraph
deepdive_en.body: Introduces **ScriptGraph** as Reality Composer Pro's node-based visual scripting that works through **event-driven** logic: listening to Pinch, Drag, and custom events to drive animation and interaction. The key advantage is testing and iterating live in the editor and on **Vision Pro**.

deepdive_en.title: A wish...
deepdive_en.body: Frames the game as starting from a wish: a little squirrel asleep guarding a nut, unaware night is falling. On Vision Pro the player can reach out, steal the nut, and freely drag it to guide the squirrel back home.

deepdive_en.title: Build the game
deepdive_en.body: Building begins: the nut gets **Input Target**, **Collision**, and **Hover Effect** components to be gaze-able and highlighted, then a dragNut ScriptGraph uses `On Drag` to trigger `Set Transform`, wiring Scene Location into translation. It's tested live via Play and Preview on Device on Vision Pro.

deepdive_en.title: Advanced techniques
deepdive_en.body: Advanced techniques: a `Multiply by Number` node plus a public **Input variable** dragSpeed tune feel, with **Overrides** per nut; adding a **Physics Body** switches to `Add Force` with a computed dragDelta, and `Set PhysicsBodyComponent` disables gravity and raises linear damping while dragging. **Prototyped Subgraphs** reuse logic, and a **Custom Node Library** defines a **Custom Event** nutIsDragged (with nutPosition) to pass data across entities and drive the squirrel's rotation and material change.

deepdive_en.title: Squirrel Talk
deepdive_en.body: Adds a SwiftUI speech bubble for the squirrel. Since ScriptGraph **Scene Events** can be sent/received from Swift, the presenter switches to `Run with Xcode` — Reality Composer Pro 3 auto-generates the project — and uses `Send Scene Event` (squirrelTalk, carrying a sayThis string). Coding Intelligence then writes the code to subscribe to the event and show the bubble as a SwiftUI **Attachment**.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Wraps up on how ScriptGraph helps sketch ideas, iterate on interaction feel, and realize a wish, previewing additions like the squirrel walking and jumping, draggable leaves, and a visionOS ornament. Encourages downloading Reality Composer Pro 3 and the full Squirrel sample project from the Apple Developer website.

title: Meet the Music Understanding framework
gloss: 認識 Music Understanding 框架
takeaway: 用全新的 Music Understanding 框架在裝置端分析音訊的六個面向（調性、節奏、結構、樂器、響度、節奏感），打造音樂相關的智慧功能。

points.text: 全新的 **Music Understanding** 框架可在**裝置端（on device）**分析音訊的六個面向：調性、節奏、結構、樂器活動、響度與節奏感。
用 `MusicUnderstandingSession` 載入 `AVURLAsset` 後呼叫 `analyze()`，結果集中在 `SessionResult`，並以 `TimedValue` 與 `RangedValue` 標註時間點與時間範圍。
調性分析提供 `KeySignature`（`Tonic`、`Mode`），節奏分析提供 beats、bars 與 `beatsPerMinute`。
提供 **串流 API**（如 `loudnessResults`）與自訂 `AudioProvider`，可即時逐段取得分析結果並更新 UI。

audience: **開發音樂、健身、影音剪輯或任何需要分析音訊內容 App 的開發者**。
gloss_en: Meet the Music Understanding framework
takeaway_en: Use the new Music Understanding framework to analyze audio on device across six dimensions (key, rhythm, structure, instrumentation, loudness, and groove) to build smart music features.

points_en.text: The new **Music Understanding** framework analyzes audio **on device** across six dimensions: key, rhythm, structure, instrument activity, loudness, and groove.
Load an `AVURLAsset` with `MusicUnderstandingSession` and call `analyze()`; results are gathered in `SessionResult`, with `TimedValue` and `RangedValue` annotating points and ranges in time.
Key analysis provides `KeySignature` (`Tonic`, `Mode`), and rhythm analysis provides beats, bars, and `beatsPerMinute`.
Offers a **streaming API** (such as `loudnessResults`) and a custom `AudioProvider`, letting you obtain analysis results segment by segment in real time and update the UI.

audience_en: **Developers building music, fitness, video editing, or any app that needs to analyze audio content**.
summary: 由 Computational Music 團隊的 Conner 主講，介紹全新的 **Music Understanding** 框架——一套在所有 Apple 平台上提供「裝置端音樂智慧」的能力。它替你包辦所有訊號處理與模型推論，開發者不需具備 signal processing 或 machine learning 背景即可使用；而且因為完全 **on-device** 執行，分析的音訊保有隱私、可離線運作。Apple 內部的 Final Cut Pro 團隊已用它打造節拍偵測（beat detection）與 iPad 版的 montage 自動剪輯功能。

框架可從六大面向分析音樂：**key**（調性）、**rhythm**（節奏）、**structure**（結構）、**pace**（律動感）、**instrument activity**（樂器活動）與 **loudness**（響度）。使用上，app 透過 **MusicUnderstandingSession** 與框架互動，以 `AVAsset` 或自訂的 audio provider 初始化，呼叫 `analyze()` 並 await 結果。預設會分析全部類型；若只需特定面向，可改用 `analyze(for:)` 以避免不必要的運算、換取最佳效能。結果集中在 **SessionResult** 結構中，每個面向都是 optional 欄位。

API 大量使用兩種帶時間的泛型型別：**TimedValue**（值對應一個 `CMTime`）與 **RangedValue**（值對應一個 `CMTimeRange`）。各面向各自回傳專屬結果：KeyResult 以 RangedValue 將 **KeySignature**（tonic + mode）對應到時間區段；RhythmResult 給出每個 beat、bar 的 `CMTime` 陣列與全曲 `beatsPerMinute`；StructureResult 拆成 sections／segments／phrases 三層；PaceResult 給能量律動；InstrumentActivityResult 同時提供「樂器是否出現」的 ranges 與「強度隨時間變化」的 activity；LoudnessResult 則用業界標準 **LUFS** 提供 integrated／momentary／shortTerm 與 peak。

進階用法上，框架另提供 **loudness 的 streaming API**，以 `AsyncSequence` 每 100ms 推送一次結果，搭配符合 `AsyncSequence` 的自訂 **AudioProvider**（產出 `AVReadOnlyAudioPCMBuffer`、以 nil 收尾）即可邊讀邊算。所有結果皆 `Codable`，用 `JSONEncoder` 即可匯出 JSON。實務應用很廣：把畫面同步到 beat／loudness／pace 做影片剪輯、依 tempo 或 key 整理音樂庫驅動 DJ app、或預先計算分析資料讓遊戲隨音樂律動。建議下載官方範例 app 「Music Understanding Lab」做為起點。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: Conner 開場介紹 **Music Understanding** 是一套跨 Apple 平台、完全 on-device 的音樂分析框架，替開發者包辦所有 signal processing 與 model inference。強調分析音訊保有隱私且可離線；並以 Apple 自家 **Final Cut Pro** 的 beat detection 與 iPad montage 自動剪輯為實際採用案例。

deepdive.title: Musical features
deepdive.body: 說明框架分析的六大面向：key、rhythm、structure、pace、instrument activity、loudness。並建立樂理層級觀念：beats 組成 bars、bars 組成 phrases、phrases 組成 segments、segments 組成 sections（如 chorus、verse、intro、bridge）；同時區分全曲 **bpm**（脈動）與聽感上的快慢 **pace**。

deepdive.title: Framework integration
deepdive.body: 介紹高階整合方式：app 透過 **MusicUnderstandingSession** 互動，以 `AVAsset` 或自訂 audio provider 初始化，呼叫 `analyze` 並 await 結果。預設分析所有類型；為求最高效能可指定只分析感興趣的類型，避免不必要的運算。

deepdive.title: Music Understanding Lab
deepdive.body: 示範官方範例 app **Music Understanding Lab**（可於 developer.apple.com 取得）。選一首歌後，app 將分析結果轉成視覺體驗，每個面向都有獨立 tile；播放時 Rhythm 與 Structure tile 會隨歌曲更新，playhead 讓使用者跟著音樂走。

deepdive.title: Initialize the session
deepdive.body: 解說 Select Song 按鈕的實作：用 SwiftUI `fileImporter` 取得檔案 URL，建立 `AVURLAsset` 時務必把 **AVURLAssetPreferPreciseDurationAndTimingKey** 設為 true 以取得最準確的結果。接著用 asset 建立 session，呼叫 `analyze()` 並 await 回傳。

deepdive.title: Inside SessionResult
deepdive.body: 說明 **SessionResult** 結構：每個分析面向都有專屬欄位且皆為 optional。使用一般 `analyze()` 時全部結果都會有值；若用 `analyze(for:)` 鎖定特定面向，未要求的欄位會是 nil。

deepdive.title: TimedValue
deepdive.body: 介紹 **TimedValue**：將一個值與一個 `CMTime` 關聯起來，是框架中表達「某時間點的值」的標準泛型型別。

deepdive.title: RangedValue
deepdive.body: 介紹 **RangedValue**：與 TimedValue 類似，但是把值關聯到一段 `CMTimeRange`，用來表達「某時間區段內的值」。

deepdive.title: Key analysis
deepdive.body: 示範 Key tile（範例曲為 D flat major）。Key 分析回傳 **KeyResult**，內含一組 ranges，以 RangedValue 將 **KeySignature** 對應到特定時間區段。

deepdive.title: KeySignature
deepdive.body: 說明 **KeySignature** 由 **tonic** 與 **mode** 兩部分組成，共同描述歌曲所環繞的調性。

deepdive.title: Using tonic
deepdive.body: 解釋 **tonic** 可以是任一標準半音音高（如 C、G），代表歌曲建構所環繞的根音（root note）。

deepdive.title: Using mode
deepdive.body: 解釋 **mode** 只有 major 或 minor 兩種，標示調性的大小調屬性。

deepdive.title: Rhythm analysis
deepdive.body: 示範 Rhythm tile：左側顯示 bpm、右側指示燈隨每個 beat 亮起。**RhythmResult** 提供每個 beat 與 bar 的 `CMTime` 陣列，以及全曲 `beatsPerMinute`；bpm 為 optional，因為若處理的音訊不足以找到至少兩個 beat，bpm 會是 nil。

deepdive.title: StructureResult
deepdive.body: 說明 Structure tile 以三列矩形呈現歌曲結構階層。**StructureResult** 含 sections、segments、phrases 三個屬性，各為 `CMTimeRange` 陣列；播放時當前的 section／segment／phrase 會高亮顯示。

deepdive.title: Analyzing pace
deepdive.body: 示範 Pace tile，描述音樂帶給聽者的快慢感：較有能量的段落值較高、UI 上以較高的長條呈現。**PaceResult** 僅有一個屬性，內含一組 ranged values。

deepdive.title: InstrumentActivityResult
deepdive.body: 示範 instrument activity tile，可用色塊時間區段或詳細活動曲線（0 到 1）呈現。**InstrumentActivityResult** 有 ranges（每個 Instrument 對應 `CMTimeRange` 陣列，判斷是否出現）與 activity（對應 `TimedValue<Float>`，表達隨時間的演奏強度，適合驅動音訊反應式動畫）。

deepdive.title: LoudnessResult
deepdive.body: 說明 Loudness tile 以業界標準 **LUFS** 衡量人耳感知音量。**LoudnessResult** 支援 integrated（全曲平均單一值）、momentary（400ms 視窗、偵測突發尖峰）與 shortTerm（3 秒視窗、較平滑的趨勢），每 100ms 一筆；另有以分貝表示的 peak 最高音量。

deepdive.title: Streaming API for loudness
deepdive.body: 介紹 loudness 的 streaming API：透過 `AsyncSequence` 在每 100ms 分析後即時送出結果，適合即時顯示而非等整曲分析完。

deepdive.title: Streaming API for loudness
deepdive.body: 示範用法：照常初始化 session，但開兩個 task——一個消費即時送來的 loudness 結果並更新音量、另一個呼叫 `analyze(for: [.loudness])` 開始分析，兩者並行。

deepdive.title: Audio Provider
deepdive.body: 說明 **AudioProvider** 需符合 `AsyncSequence`，產出 `AVReadOnlyAudioPCMBuffer` 物件；送完所有音訊緩衝後，必須再送一個 nil 以標示完成。

deepdive.title: Encode to JSON
deepdive.body: 說明所有 Music Understanding 結果皆 `Codable`。要匯出 JSON 只需建立 `JSONEncoder` 並 encode session 結果，對應 Lab 右上角的 Share 按鈕匯出完整分析資料。

deepdive.title: Suggestion for using pace
deepdive.body: 示範 Video tile 如何結合 **structure** 與 **pace** 製作隨音樂同步的影片：先依 section 時間區段切分，再用各段 pace（每分鐘事件率，除以 60 得每個 clip 時長）決定 clip 數量；高能量段用較短較快的 clip、低能量段用較長較慢的 clip，使畫面切換貼合歌曲能量。

summary_en: Presented by Conner from the Computational Music team, this session introduces **Music Understanding**, a new framework that brings on-device musical intelligence to every Apple platform. It handles all the signal processing and model inference for you, so no machine-learning or DSP expertise is required, and because everything runs **on-device** the audio you analyze stays private and works offline. Apple's own Final Cut Pro team already uses it to power beat detection and the iPad montage auto-edit feature.

The framework analyzes music across six dimensions: **key**, **rhythm**, **structure**, **pace**, **instrument activity**, and **loudness**. Apps interact through a **MusicUnderstandingSession**, initialized with an `AVAsset` or a custom audio provider, then call `analyze()` and await the results. By default all types are analyzed; for best performance you can use `analyze(for:)` to request only the dimensions you need. Everything comes back in a single **SessionResult** struct where each dimension is an optional field.

Two time-aware generic types recur throughout the API: **TimedValue** (a value at a `CMTime`) and **RangedValue** (a value over a `CMTimeRange`). Each dimension has its own result: KeyResult maps a **KeySignature** (tonic + mode) to time ranges; RhythmResult gives `CMTime` arrays for beats and bars plus a global `beatsPerMinute`; StructureResult breaks the song into sections/segments/phrases; PaceResult expresses energy; InstrumentActivityResult provides both presence ranges and per-instrument intensity activity; and LoudnessResult reports integrated/momentary/shortTerm and peak values in the industry-standard **LUFS** scale.

For advanced use, the framework offers a **streaming loudness API** that delivers results via an `AsyncSequence` every 100ms, paired with a custom **AudioProvider** that conforms to `AsyncSequence`, yields `AVReadOnlyAudioPCMBuffer` objects, and sends a final nil to signal completion. All results are `Codable`, so a `JSONEncoder` exports them to JSON in a couple of lines. The practical possibilities are broad: sync visuals to beat, loudness, or pace for video editing; organize music libraries by tempo or key for a DJ app; or precompute analysis to animate a game to music. Download the sample app "Music Understanding Lab" to kickstart your own work.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Conner introduces **Music Understanding** as a cross-platform, fully on-device music analysis framework that handles all signal processing and model inference for you. He stresses that analyzed audio stays private and works offline, and cites Apple's own **Final Cut Pro** beat detection and iPad montage auto-edit as real adopters.

deepdive_en.title: Musical features
deepdive_en.body: Covers the six analysis dimensions: key, rhythm, structure, pace, instrument activity, and loudness. He builds up the musical hierarchy: beats form bars, bars form phrases, phrases form segments, and segments form sections (chorus, verse, intro, bridge), while distinguishing a song's steady **bpm** from its perceived **pace**.

deepdive_en.title: Framework integration
deepdive_en.body: Explains the high-level model: apps interact via a **MusicUnderstandingSession**, initialized with an `AVAsset` or a custom audio provider, then call `analyze` and await results. All types are analyzed by default; for top performance you can specify only the types you care about to avoid unnecessary computation.

deepdive_en.title: Music Understanding Lab
deepdive_en.body: Demos the official sample app **Music Understanding Lab** (available on developer.apple.com). After picking a song, the app turns analysis into a visual experience with a dedicated tile per dimension; during playback the Rhythm and Structure tiles update and a playhead ties it to the music.

deepdive_en.title: Initialize the session
deepdive_en.body: Walks through the Select Song button: use the SwiftUI `fileImporter` to get a URL, build an `AVURLAsset` and be sure to set **AVURLAssetPreferPreciseDurationAndTimingKey** to true for the most accurate results, then create the session and call `analyze()`, awaiting the return.

deepdive_en.title: Inside SessionResult
deepdive_en.body: Describes the **SessionResult** struct: every analyzed feature has its own optional field. The general `analyze()` populates all results, while the targeted `analyze(for:)` returns only what you asked for and leaves the rest nil.

deepdive_en.title: TimedValue
deepdive_en.body: Introduces **TimedValue**, which associates a value with a single `CMTime`, the standard generic type for expressing a value at a point in time.

deepdive_en.title: RangedValue
deepdive_en.body: Introduces **RangedValue**, similar to TimedValue but associating a value with a `CMTimeRange` to express a value over a span of time.

deepdive_en.title: Key analysis
deepdive_en.body: Demos the Key tile (the sample song is D flat major). Key analysis returns a **KeyResult** containing an array of ranges that map a **KeySignature** to a specific time range via RangedValue.

deepdive_en.title: KeySignature
deepdive_en.body: Explains that a **KeySignature** is made of a **tonic** and a **mode**, which together describe the key the song is built around.

deepdive_en.title: Using tonic
deepdive_en.body: The **tonic** can be any standard chromatic pitch (like C or G) and represents the root note around which the song is built.

deepdive_en.title: Using mode
deepdive_en.body: The **mode** is either major or minor, indicating the tonal quality of the key.

deepdive_en.title: Rhythm analysis
deepdive_en.body: Demos the Rhythm tile: bpm on the left, beat indicators that light up on the right. **RhythmResult** provides `CMTime` arrays for every beat and bar plus a global `beatsPerMinute`; bpm is optional because if not enough audio has been processed to find at least two beats, it will be nil.

deepdive_en.title: StructureResult
deepdive_en.body: Explains the Structure tile's three rows of rectangles for the structural hierarchy. **StructureResult** has sections, segments, and phrases properties, each an array of `CMTimeRange`; during playback the current section, segment, and phrase are highlighted.

deepdive_en.title: Analyzing pace
deepdive_en.body: Demos the Pace tile, which conveys how fast the music feels: more energetic parts get higher values shown as taller bars. **PaceResult** has a single property holding an array of ranged values.

deepdive_en.title: InstrumentActivityResult
deepdive_en.body: Demos instrument activity tiles, shown as color-coded time ranges or as a detailed activity graph (values 0 to 1). **InstrumentActivityResult** has ranges (each Instrument to an array of `CMTimeRange`, for simple presence) and activity (each Instrument to `TimedValue<Float>`, expressing intensity over time and great for audio-reactive animation).

deepdive_en.title: LoudnessResult
deepdive_en.body: Explains the Loudness tile measured in the industry-standard **LUFS**. **LoudnessResult** supports integrated (a single whole-song average), momentary (400ms window, for short spikes), and shortTerm (3-second window, smoother trend), sampled every 100ms, plus a peak maximum level in decibels.

deepdive_en.title: Streaming API for loudness
deepdive_en.body: Introduces the streaming loudness API, which delivers results via an `AsyncSequence` for every 100ms of audio analyzed, suitable for live display rather than waiting for the full track.

deepdive_en.title: Streaming API for loudness
deepdive_en.body: Shows the usage: initialize the session as before, then set up two tasks in parallel, one consuming streamed loudness results to update an audio level, the other calling `analyze(for: [.loudness])` to begin analysis.

deepdive_en.title: Audio Provider
deepdive_en.body: Explains that an **AudioProvider** conforms to `AsyncSequence` and yields `AVReadOnlyAudioPCMBuffer` objects; once all buffers are sent it must send a final nil to signal completion.

deepdive_en.title: Encode to JSON
deepdive_en.body: Notes that all Music Understanding results are `Codable`. Exporting to JSON just means creating a `JSONEncoder` and encoding the session results, which backs the Lab's Share button that exports all analysis data.

deepdive_en.title: Suggestion for using pace
deepdive_en.body: Demos how the Video tile combines **structure** and **pace** to build a music-synced video: it identifies section time ranges, then uses each section's pace (an events-per-minute rate, divided by 60 to get time per clip) to decide how many clips to show, retiming longer/slower clips for low-energy parts and shorter/faster clips for high-energy parts.

title: Integrate MusicKit into your app
gloss: 將 MusicKit 整合進你的 App
takeaway: 用 **MusicKit** 把 Apple Music 帶進 App，涵蓋授權、訂閱檢查、音樂選取、播放控制與目錄請求。
chapters: Presents the Apple Music subscription offer
Adds subscription button to main view

points.text: 完成專案設定與**授權**，並以 `MusicSubscription.current` 與 `subscriptionUpdates` 檢查訂閱狀態。
用 `musicSubscriptionOffer` 呈現 Apple Music 訂閱提示，讓尚未訂閱者可以升級。
透過新的 **`.musicPicker()`** 修飾器讓使用者挑選歌曲，再以 `ArtworkImage` 顯示封面。
使用 `ApplicationMusicPlayer.shared` 控制播放、暫停與上一首／下一首，並讀取 `queue.currentEntry` 顯示資訊。
以 `MusicCatalogResourceRequest` 依 ID 取得目錄歌曲，並可用 `.findEquivalents` 取得對應版本。

audience: **想在 App 中整合 Apple Music 播放與目錄功能**的 iOS 開發者。
gloss_en: Integrate MusicKit into your app
takeaway_en: Use **MusicKit** to bring Apple Music into your app, covering authorization, subscription checks, music selection, playback control, and catalog requests.

points_en.text: Complete project setup and **authorization**, then check subscription status with `MusicSubscription.current` and `subscriptionUpdates`.
Present an Apple Music subscription prompt with `musicSubscriptionOffer` so non-subscribers can upgrade.
Let users pick songs with the new **`.musicPicker()`** modifier, then show artwork with `ArtworkImage`.
Control play, pause, and previous/next with `ApplicationMusicPlayer.shared`, and read `queue.currentEntry` to display info.
Fetch catalog songs by ID with `MusicCatalogResourceRequest`, and use `.findEquivalents` to get matching versions.

audience_en: iOS developers **who want to integrate Apple Music playback and catalog features into their app**.
summary: MusicKit 團隊的 Cathy 與 Alan 示範如何把 **MusicKit** 整合進 app，並以一個健身（騎車）app 作為貫穿範例，讓使用者在運動時挑選並播放音樂。**MusicKit** 是專為 Apple 平台設計的 Swift 框架，圍繞 Swift concurrency 與 SwiftUI 打造，能存取與播放 Apple Music 目錄與使用者媒體庫。整合前的設定包括：在 developer portal 的 App ID 勾選 MusicKit 以自動產生 developer token、確認 Xcode 登入同一帳號，並在 Signing & Capabilities 加入 **Media Library** capability 以提供音樂存取的說明文字。

授權與訂閱方面，用 **MusicAuthorization** 的非同步 request 方法取得使用者許可。Apple Music 訂閱並非必要（無訂閱僅能存取已購買或同步的音樂），但可用 **`.musicSubscriptionOffer`** view modifier 讓使用者不離開 app 即可訂閱，並透過 `MusicSubscriptionOffer.Options`（含 messageIdentifier，如 `.playMusic`）客製化。app 以 `@State` 追蹤 `MusicSubscription`，並在授權後用 `.task` 取得當前值並監聽 `subscriptionUpdates`，僅在 `canBecomeSubscriber` 時顯示訂閱按鈕。選曲則靠 **`.musicPicker`** modifier——它在單一介面整合 Apple Music 目錄與媒體庫，不需訂閱（無訂閱時只顯示媒體庫內容），並可將 selection 改為陣列以支援多選。

播放由 Alan 接手：MusicKit 提供 **SystemMusicPlayer**（控制系統 Music app、背景持續播放）與 **ApplicationMusicPlayer**（在 app 內播放、可完整讀寫 queue）兩種 player。queue 由可播放的 music items 組成，呼叫 `play()`／`pause()` 控制，並可用 `prepareToPlay()` 預先緩衝以縮短輸出延遲；`affectsListeningHistory` 決定是否出現在 Recently Played。兩個 player 的 state 與 queue 都是 observable，可直接用於 SwiftUI——範例以 `ArtworkImage` 顯示封面、用 currentEntry 的 title／subtitle 顯示資訊，並以 `skipToNextEntry`／`skipToPreviousEntry` 切歌。最後是 **catalog requests**：用 **`MusicCatalogResourceRequest`** 依 ID 抓取歌曲，加上 `.findEquivalents` option 處理跨地區／清淨版的資源等價，呼叫 `response()` 取回強型別的 `MusicItemCollection`（支援 `nextBatch()` 分頁），用以在運動畫面提供可一鍵播放的推薦歌曲。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: MusicKit 工程師 Cathy 開場，介紹 **MusicKit** 是專為 Apple 平台、圍繞 Swift concurrency 與 SwiftUI 設計的 Swift 框架，可存取與播放 Apple Music 目錄與媒體庫。她與 Alan 將在一個健身 app 中走過授權、music item 與 music picker、播放，以及 catalog requests。

deepdive.title: Project setup and authorization
deepdive.body: 專案設定包含在 developer portal 的 App ID（App Services 分頁）勾選 **MusicKit** 以自動產生 developer token，並確認 Xcode 登入同一帳號。授權用 **MusicAuthorization** 的非同步 request 方法，系統會跳出許可提示；在 Signing & Capabilities 加入 **Media Library** capability 並填寫說明，該文字會出現在提示底部。

deepdive.title: Presents the Apple Music subscription offer
deepdive.body: Apple Music 訂閱非必要，但無訂閱只能存取已購買或同步的音樂。用 **`.musicSubscriptionOffer`** view modifier（接受 `isPresented` binding）讓使用者不離開 app 即可訂閱；透過 `MusicSubscriptionOffer.Options` 設定 Performance Partner Program 資訊與 messageIdentifier（本例為 `.playMusic`）來客製 UI 與潛在抽成。

deepdive.title: Adds subscription button to main view
deepdive.body: 在主畫面以 `@State` 宣告 `MusicSubscription` 狀態，僅在使用者尚未訂閱且 `canBecomeSubscriber` 時顯示訂閱按鈕。用授權成功時觸發的 `.task` 取得 `MusicSubscription.current` 並持續監聽 `subscriptionUpdates` 以即時更新狀態。

deepdive.title: Music items and music picker
deepdive.body: **MusicItem** 是使用 MusicKit API 的基礎，為 model 層的 value type。每個 item 有 **Attributes**（如 Album 的 title、contentRating）、**Relationships**（如 Album 的 tracks）與較弱關聯的 **Associations**（如 otherVersions）。除了 Album 還有 Genre、Station、Playlist 等型別。

deepdive.title: Add .musicPicker() modifier
deepdive.body: 用 **`.musicPicker`** SwiftUI view modifier 在單一統一介面同時呈現 Apple Music 目錄與媒體庫。需加上是否顯示的 toggle 與 selected song 狀態（預設 nil）。picker 不需訂閱（無訂閱時只顯示媒體庫），並可把 selection 改為陣列以支援多選整張專輯或播放清單。

deepdive.title: Music players and playback
deepdive.body: 由 Alan 接手介紹兩種 player：**SystemMusicPlayer**（控制系統 Music app、背景／結束後持續播放、queue 唯讀）與 **ApplicationMusicPlayer**（在 app 內播放、queue 可完整讀寫）。queue 由可播放 music items 組成，`play()`／`pause()` 控制，`prepareToPlay()` 預先緩衝以縮短延遲，`affectsListeningHistory` 決定是否進 Recently Played；state 與 queue 皆 observable 可直接用於 SwiftUI。

deepdive.title: Artwork
deepdive.body: 從 player 的 queue 取得正在播放的歌曲，若其有 artwork 則用 MusicKit 的 **`ArtworkImage`** SwiftUI view 顯示封面，否則顯示 placeholder 的 RoundedRectangle。

deepdive.title: Current entry info
deepdive.body: 用 queue 的 `currentEntry` 顯示目前歌曲的 title 與（若有）subtitle，分別套用 title3.bold 與 secondary 樣式。

deepdive.title: Playback controls (play, pause)
deepdive.body: 讀取 `ApplicationMusicPlayer` 的 state，以 `playbackStatus == .playing` 判斷是否播放中，按鈕在播放時呼叫 `pause()`、否則在 Task 中呼叫 `play()`。

deepdive.title: Playback controls (next, previous)
deepdive.body: Back 按鈕呼叫 `skipToPreviousEntry`、Next 按鈕呼叫 `skipToNextEntry` 來切換上一首／下一首；切歌後 `ArtworkImage` 會即時反映新歌的封面。

deepdive.title: Catalog requests
deepdive.body: **catalog requests** 讓 app 直接查詢 Apple Music、提供與使用者媒體庫無關的內容（如為 app 策展的歌曲）。MusicKit 提供多種結構化請求（依 filter 取得、搜尋、策展與個人化內容等），詳見文件。

deepdive.title: Music catalog resource request
deepdive.body: **`MusicCatalogResourceRequest`** 是針對特定資源的結構化請求，可設 options、指定要一併取得的 relationships／associations 與回傳數量上限。呼叫非同步 `response()` 取回 `MusicCatalogResourceResponse`，內含強型別的 `MusicItemCollection`，支援以 `hasNextBatch` 與 `nextBatch()` 分頁。範例 `fetchSongs` 依 ID 抓歌、加上 `.findEquivalents` 處理跨地區／清淨版等價，並以 `item(for:)` 取出 featured 與其餘歌曲。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 總結建議：採用 music picker view modifier 提供統一熟悉的選曲體驗，善用 Apple Music 目錄豐富內容（如為 app 加入背景音樂），並探索其他 MusicKit API（瀏覽與修改媒體庫見「Explore more content with MusicKit」；Android／web 整合見「Meet Apple Music API and MusicKit」）。

summary_en: MusicKit team members Cathy and Alan show how to integrate **MusicKit** into an app, using a fitness (cycling) workout app as the running example so people can pick and play music during workouts. **MusicKit** is a Swift framework for Apple platforms, designed around Swift concurrency and SwiftUI, that accesses and plays the Apple Music catalog and a person's media library. Setup before integration includes checking MusicKit on your App ID in the developer portal to auto-generate a developer token, confirming Xcode is signed into the same account, and adding the **Media Library** capability in Signing & Capabilities with a usage description.

For authorization and subscriptions, use **MusicAuthorization**'s async request method to get permission. An Apple Music subscription isn't required (without one, only purchased or synced music is accessible), but the **`.musicSubscriptionOffer`** view modifier lets people subscribe without leaving the app, customized via `MusicSubscriptionOffer.Options` (including a messageIdentifier like `.playMusic`). The app tracks a `MusicSubscription` with `@State`, fetching the current value and listening for `subscriptionUpdates` in a `.task` after authorization, showing the subscribe button only when `canBecomeSubscriber`. Selection uses the **`.musicPicker`** modifier — a single unified interface over the catalog and library that needs no subscription (showing only library content without one) and supports multi-selection by making the selection an array.

Alan takes over playback: MusicKit offers **SystemMusicPlayer** (controls the system Music app, keeps playing in the background) and **ApplicationMusicPlayer** (plays from your app, with full read/write queue access). A queue is a collection of playable music items, controlled with `play()`/`pause()`, with `prepareToPlay()` to buffer ahead and reduce latency, while `affectsListeningHistory` governs whether it appears in Recently Played. Both players' state and queue are observable for direct use in SwiftUI — the example shows the cover with `ArtworkImage`, the title/subtitle from currentEntry, and skips via `skipToNextEntry`/`skipToPreviousEntry`. Finally, **catalog requests**: use **`MusicCatalogResourceRequest`** to fetch songs by ID with the `.findEquivalents` option for cross-region/clean equivalency, calling `response()` to get a strongly-typed `MusicItemCollection` (paginated via `nextBatch()`), used to offer one-tap recommended songs on the workout screen.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: MusicKit engineer Cathy opens, introducing **MusicKit** as a Swift framework for Apple platforms designed around Swift concurrency and SwiftUI that accesses and plays the Apple Music catalog and media library. She and Alan will walk through authorization, music items and the music picker, playback, and catalog requests in a fitness app.

deepdive_en.title: Project setup and authorization
deepdive_en.body: Setup includes checking **MusicKit** on the App ID (App Services tab) in the developer portal to auto-generate a developer token, and confirming Xcode is signed into the same account. Authorization uses **MusicAuthorization**'s async request method, which prompts the user; add the **Media Library** capability in Signing & Capabilities with a description that appears at the bottom of the prompt.

deepdive_en.title: Presents the Apple Music subscription offer
deepdive_en.body: A subscription isn't required, but without one only purchased or synced music is accessible. Use the **`.musicSubscriptionOffer`** view modifier (taking an `isPresented` binding) to let people subscribe without leaving the app; configure `MusicSubscriptionOffer.Options` with Performance Partner Program info and a messageIdentifier (here `.playMusic`) to customize the UI and potential commissions.

deepdive_en.title: Adds subscription button to main view
deepdive_en.body: In the main view, declare a `MusicSubscription` state with `@State` and show the subscribe button only when the user isn't subscribed and `canBecomeSubscriber`. Use a `.task` triggered when authorization succeeds to fetch `MusicSubscription.current` and keep listening to `subscriptionUpdates` for live updates.

deepdive_en.title: Music items and music picker
deepdive_en.body: A **MusicItem** is the building block for MusicKit APIs, a value type in the model layer. Each has **Attributes** (e.g. an Album's title, contentRating), **Relationships** (e.g. an Album's tracks), and more loosely-tied **Associations** (e.g. otherVersions). Beyond Album there are Genre, Station, Playlist, and more.

deepdive_en.title: Add .musicPicker() modifier
deepdive_en.body: Use the **`.musicPicker`** SwiftUI view modifier to surface the Apple Music catalog and the library in a single unified interface. Add a toggle for whether it's shown and a selected song state (nil by default). The picker needs no subscription (showing only library content without one) and supports multi-selection by making the selection an array to pick whole albums or playlists.

deepdive_en.title: Music players and playback
deepdive_en.body: Alan introduces the two players: **SystemMusicPlayer** (controls the system Music app, keeps playing in the background/after quit, read-only queue) and **ApplicationMusicPlayer** (plays from your app, full read/write queue). A queue is a collection of playable music items, controlled by `play()`/`pause()`, with `prepareToPlay()` to buffer ahead and `affectsListeningHistory` governing Recently Played; state and queue are observable for direct SwiftUI use.

deepdive_en.title: Artwork
deepdive_en.body: Get the currently playing song from the player's queue, and if it has artwork, display the cover with MusicKit's **`ArtworkImage`** SwiftUI view; otherwise show a placeholder RoundedRectangle.

deepdive_en.title: Current entry info
deepdive_en.body: Use the queue's `currentEntry` to display the current song's title and (if present) subtitle, styled with title3.bold and secondary respectively.

deepdive_en.title: Playback controls (play, pause)
deepdive_en.body: Read `ApplicationMusicPlayer`'s state, derive whether it's playing via `playbackStatus == .playing`, and have the button call `pause()` when playing or `play()` in a Task otherwise.

deepdive_en.title: Playback controls (next, previous)
deepdive_en.body: The Back button calls `skipToPreviousEntry` and the Next button calls `skipToNextEntry` to change tracks; after skipping, `ArtworkImage` reflects the new song's cover instantly.

deepdive_en.title: Catalog requests
deepdive_en.body: **Catalog requests** let the app query Apple Music directly and provide content independent of the user's library (such as curated songs for your app). MusicKit offers several structured requests (filtered fetches, search, curated and personalized content); see the docs for the full list.

deepdive_en.title: Music catalog resource request
deepdive_en.body: **`MusicCatalogResourceRequest`** is a structured request for a specific resource; you can set options, specify relationships/associations to also fulfill, and a result limit. Calling the async `response()` returns a `MusicCatalogResourceResponse` containing a strongly-typed `MusicItemCollection`, paginated via `hasNextBatch` and `nextBatch()`. The `fetchSongs` example fetches by ID, adds `.findEquivalents` for cross-region/clean equivalency, and uses `item(for:)` to pull the featured and remaining songs.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Closing advice: adopt the music picker view modifier for a unified, familiar picking experience, leverage the rich Apple Music catalog (e.g. add background music to your app), and explore other MusicKit APIs (browsing/modifying the library in "Explore more content with MusicKit"; Android/web integration in "Meet Apple Music API and MusicKit").

title: Discover generated subtitles and subtitle styles
gloss: 認識自動產生字幕與字幕樣式
takeaway: 運用自動產生字幕讓影片內容更易讀，並讓使用者在 App 中即時預覽與套用字幕樣式。

points.text: 新的 **自動產生字幕** 功能可轉錄口語音訊，甚至翻譯，提升影片內容的無障礙程度。
說明字幕的 **產生方式、可用性與支援條件**，協助評估如何整合到既有影片流程。
透過 **MediaAccessibility** 的 MACaptionAppearanceCopyProfileIDs 取得可用字幕樣式設定檔。
以 **setCaptionPreviewProfileID** 在 AVPlayerLayer 上即時預覽字幕樣式，並可停止預覽。
使用 **MACaptionAppearanceSetActiveProfileID** 套用使用者選定的字幕外觀。

audience: 開發 **影片播放或媒體製作 App**、想加入字幕產生與樣式自訂的開發者。
gloss_en: Discover generated subtitles and subtitle styles
takeaway_en: Use generated subtitles to make video content more readable, and let users preview and apply subtitle styles in real time within your app.

points_en.text: The new **generated subtitles** feature can transcribe spoken audio, and even translate it, improving the accessibility of your video content.
Explains how subtitles are **generated, their availability, and supported conditions**, helping you assess how to integrate them into an existing video pipeline.
Retrieve available subtitle style profiles via **MediaAccessibility**'s MACaptionAppearanceCopyProfileIDs.
Use **setCaptionPreviewProfileID** on an AVPlayerLayer to preview subtitle styles in real time, and to stop previewing.
Use **MACaptionAppearanceSetActiveProfileID** to apply the caption appearance the user selected.

audience_en: Developers building **video playback or media production apps** who want to add subtitle generation and style customization.
summary: AVFoundation 團隊工程師 James 介紹兩項讓影片內容更無障礙的字幕功能。第一項是 **Apple AI-generated subtitles**（產生字幕）：在裝置上、播放當下即時、本地產生字幕，協助當原始內容沒有觀眾需要的字幕語言時補上缺口。它有兩種用途——從音訊以 on-device Speech-To-Text 模型產生字幕（**Speech transcription**），以及從既有字幕用 on-device 翻譯模型產生另一種語言字幕（**Language translation**）。最棒的是開發者**無需實作任何東西**即可在播放時自動啟用；authored（人工製作）字幕仍為優先且不變，產生字幕只是額外提供更多語言。

支援範圍涵蓋 HTTP Live Streaming（直播、隨選影片、體育等）與檔案型內容（app 內建或下載），內容類型從專業電影影集到使用者自拍與社群影片皆可。語言／裝置方面，自 iOS／macOS／tvOS／visionOS 27 起可由英文音訊產生英文字幕，並可在 iOS／macOS 由英文字幕產生多種語言字幕。要讓使用者用到，app 需提供字幕選擇 UI：iOS 的 **AVPlayerViewController** 與 macOS 的 **AVPlayerView** 已完整實作（含播放控制）；若想加進既有播放 UI 但不要播放控制，可用 **AVLegibleMediaOptionsMenuController**；也可自行實作客製控制項。

第二項是 **subtitle style preview**（字幕樣式預覽）。多年來 Settings app 已可選擇與自訂字幕樣式（如使用者自建的 Bold Yellow），但在觀看影片時就近切換更方便、更無障礙。此功能讓使用者直接在播放時的字幕選單裡切換樣式，並即時預覽效果。實作選項包括：iOS 的 AVPlayerViewController／macOS 的 AVPlayerView（完整實作）、AVLegibleMediaOptionsMenuController（加進既有 UI），以及較底層的 **AVPlayerLayer**（自行驅動）與需自行渲染的 **AVCaptionRenderer**。AVPlayerLayer 流程是：以 `MACaptionAppearanceCopyProfileIDs` 取得各樣式的 profile ID 填入 UI、選取時用 `setCaptionPreviewProfileID` 顯示預覽（傳 nil 文字會顯示本地化系統文字，並用 position 避開控制項）、結束時 `stopShowingCaptionPreview`，最後以 `MACaptionAppearanceSetActiveProfileID` 套用所選樣式。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: AVFoundation 工程師 James 開場，說明人們因無障礙需求、輔助理解、或環境吵雜等各種原因使用字幕。**Apple AI-generated subtitles** 可在裝置上、播放當下本地即時產生。本場先示範產生字幕如何在 app 中呈現，再介紹讓使用者在播放時自訂字幕樣式的 subtitle style preview。

deepdive.title: Media authoring
deepdive.body: 回顧媒體製作流程：先拍攝與剪輯影音，再人工製作 **authored subtitles**（每種語言一份，也可有多語音軌），最終媒體把影像、音訊與 authored 字幕包在一起。即使有多語字幕，觀眾仍可能沒有看得懂的語言，這正是產生字幕補足缺口之處。

deepdive.title: Subtitle generation methods
deepdive.body: 產生字幕有兩種用途：**Speech transcription**——音訊經 on-device Speech-To-Text 模型產生字幕；**Language translation**——既有字幕（如英文）經 on-device 翻譯模型產生另一語言（如義大利文）。產生字幕僅額外提供語言，**authored 字幕仍優先且不變**。

deepdive.title: Availability and support
deepdive.body: 好消息是開發者**無需實作**即可在播放時自動啟用產生字幕。支援多種場景：HTTP Live Streaming（直播、隨選影片、體育直播）與檔案型內容（app 內建或下載）；內容類型含專業電影影集與使用者自拍、社群影片。自 iOS／macOS／tvOS／visionOS 27 起可由英文音訊產生英文字幕，iOS／macOS 還可由英文字幕產生多語字幕。

deepdive.title: Presenting subtitles in your app
deepdive.body: 強調 app 應在播放時提供字幕選擇 UI。選項包括：iOS 的 **AVPlayerViewController** 與 macOS 的 **AVPlayerView**（完整實作字幕選擇與播放控制，無需額外處理）；**AVLegibleMediaOptionsMenuController**（提供字幕選擇但不含播放控制，適合加進既有 UI）；或自行實作客製控制項以配合 app 風格。

deepdive.title: Subtitle style preview
deepdive.body: 字幕的呈現方式同樣重要。Settings app 多年來可選擇與自訂字幕樣式（如自建的 Bold Yellow——黃字加邊框更易讀），但在觀看影片時就近切換更方便無障礙。**subtitle style preview** 讓使用者直接在播放時的字幕選單切換樣式並即時預覽效果。

deepdive.title: Implement subtitle style preview
deepdive.body: 實作選項：iOS 的 AVPlayerViewController／macOS 的 AVPlayerView（完整實作）、AVLegibleMediaOptionsMenuController（加進既有 UI），以及較底層、需自行驅動的 **AVPlayerLayer** 與需自行渲染的 **AVCaptionRenderer**。AVPlayerLayer 流程：用 `MACaptionAppearanceCopyProfileIDs` 取得各樣式 profile ID 填入 UI、選取時 `setCaptionPreviewProfileID` 顯示預覽（傳 nil 文字顯示本地化系統文字、用 position 避開控制項）、結束 `stopShowingCaptionPreview`，最後 `MACaptionAppearanceSetActiveProfileID` 套用。

deepdive.title: Demo
deepdive.body: 示範同時使用兩項功能：觀看一支英文字幕的露營影片，從 Subtitles 選單的 Language 切換到標記 sparkle 與「Translated」的義大利文**產生字幕**；再從 Style 選單嘗試 Large Text，現有字幕被替換成義大利文 placeholder 預覽，最後套用自建的 Bold Yellow 樣式。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 建議：實際探索產生字幕（如看旅遊影片並開啟）、確保 app 有字幕選擇 UI，並實作 subtitle style preview，讓需要調整字幕樣式的使用者能在觀看時就近完成。

summary_en: AVFoundation engineer James covers two subtitle features that make video content more accessible. The first is **Apple AI-generated subtitles**: created live, locally on the device as media plays, to fill the gap when the original content lacks the subtitle language a viewer needs. There are two use cases — generating subtitles from audio via an on-device Speech-To-Text model (**Speech transcription**) and generating another language from existing subtitles via an on-device translation model (**Language translation**). Best of all, developers **don't need to implement anything** — they're available automatically during playback; authored subtitles remain preferred and unchanged, with generated subtitles simply offering more languages.

Support spans HTTP Live Streaming (live streams, video on demand, sports) and file-based content (app-bundled or downloaded), across content from professional movies and series to user-captured and social media videos. For languages and devices, starting in iOS/macOS/tvOS/visionOS 27 English subtitles can be generated from English audio, and on iOS/macOS multiple languages can be generated from English subtitles. To let users access them, the app should provide a subtitle-selection UI: iOS's **AVPlayerViewController** and macOS's **AVPlayerView** fully implement it (with player controls); to add it to existing player UI without controls, use **AVLegibleMediaOptionsMenuController**; or implement custom controls.

The second feature is **subtitle style preview**. The Settings app has long let people select and customize subtitle styling (like a user-made Bold Yellow), but changing it while watching is more convenient and accessible. This feature lets users switch styles right from the playback subtitle menu, with a live preview of each. Implementation options include iOS's AVPlayerViewController / macOS's AVPlayerView (fully implemented), AVLegibleMediaOptionsMenuController (for existing UI), and the lower-level **AVPlayerLayer** (you drive it) and **AVCaptionRenderer** (you render it). The AVPlayerLayer flow: fetch each style's profile ID with `MACaptionAppearanceCopyProfileIDs` to populate the UI, show a preview on selection with `setCaptionPreviewProfileID` (passing nil text shows localized system text, and position avoids controls), stop with `stopShowingCaptionPreview`, and apply the chosen style with `MACaptionAppearanceSetActiveProfileID`.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: AVFoundation engineer James opens, noting people use subtitles for accessibility, comprehension, or noisy environments. **Apple AI-generated subtitles** are created live and locally on-device as media plays. The session first shows how generated subtitles appear in your app, then the subtitle style preview that lets users customize styling during playback.

deepdive_en.title: Media authoring
deepdive_en.body: Reviews the media creation flow: filming and editing video and audio, then manually creating **authored subtitles** (one per language, with possible multiple audio languages), with the final media bundling video, audio, and authored subtitles. Even with multiple languages, a viewer may lack one they understand — exactly where generated subtitles fill the gap.

deepdive_en.title: Subtitle generation methods
deepdive_en.body: Generated subtitles have two use cases: **Speech transcription** — audio runs through an on-device Speech-To-Text model to produce subtitles; **Language translation** — existing subtitles (e.g. English) run through an on-device translation model to produce another language (e.g. Italian). Generated subtitles only add languages; **authored subtitles remain preferred and unchanged**.

deepdive_en.title: Availability and support
deepdive_en.body: The good news: developers **don't need to implement anything** — generated subtitles are available automatically during playback. Supported scenarios include HTTP Live Streaming (live streams, video on demand, live sports) and file-based content (app-bundled or downloaded), across professional movies/series and user-captured/social videos. From iOS/macOS/tvOS/visionOS 27, English subtitles can be generated from English audio; iOS/macOS can also generate multiple languages from English subtitles.

deepdive_en.title: Presenting subtitles in your app
deepdive_en.body: Stresses providing a subtitle-selection UI during playback. Options include iOS's **AVPlayerViewController** and macOS's **AVPlayerView** (fully implementing selection and player controls), **AVLegibleMediaOptionsMenuController** (selection without player controls, good for existing UI), or custom controls to match the app's style.

deepdive_en.title: Subtitle style preview
deepdive_en.body: How subtitles look matters too. The Settings app has long let people select and customize subtitle styles (like a custom Bold Yellow — yellow text with extra border for readability), but changing it while watching is more convenient and accessible. **Subtitle style preview** lets users switch styles right in the playback subtitle menu with a live preview.

deepdive_en.title: Implement subtitle style preview
