deepdive_en.body: New toolbar APIs specify trade-offs when space is limited: apply **`visibilityPriority(.high)`** to the important Undo/Redo group to keep it visible, put rare actions in a **`ToolbarOverflowMenu`**, and use **`topBarPinnedTrailing`** placement so Share is never hidden.

deepdive_en.title: Minimize toolbar on scroll with toolbarMinimizeBehavior
deepdive_en.body: Use **`toolbarMinimizeBehavior(.onScrollDown, for: .navigationBar)`** so the system automatically collapses the navigation bar when scrolling down, freeing space when browsing many stickers.

deepdive_en.title: Document-based apps
deepdive_en.body: Julia introduces the new **Document API**, expanding on the existing `FileDocument`/`ReferenceFileDocument` foundation. Document-based apps (like Pages, Xcode) get Cmd+N/Cmd+O, an edited indicator, and autosaving for free; this session focuses on three improvements: document creation context, read/write performance, and direct URL access.

deepdive_en.title: Document creation sources with context parameter
deepdive_en.body: Use **`DocumentCreationSource`** to declare multiple sources (blank, photo), each with a `NewDocumentButton` in the launch scene; SwiftUI passes the chosen source to the creation closure via a **context parameter**.

deepdive_en.title: Use the context to create a document
deepdive_en.body: Check the context in the initializer: if the source is photo, the document opens with the photo picker already presented, so the user is one tap from placing stickers on a photo.

deepdive_en.title: Document app declaration
deepdive_en.body: Opt into the document architecture with a **`DocumentGroup`** as the first Scene in the app body, using an **`@Observable`** `StickerDocument` class to describe the document type; Observation means views update only when a dependent property changes.

deepdive_en.title: Implement document writing
deepdive_en.body: Conform the document to the **`WritableDocument`** protocol for writing, with three requirements: a list of writable formats, a snapshot method returning the content, and a Writer. The goal is to make reading and writing fast and efficient.

deepdive_en.title: Implement document writing: list writable formats
deepdive_en.body: First requirement: declare **`writableDocumentTypes`** (e.g. a custom `.stickerDocument` defined via `UTType(exportedAs:)`), listing the formats the app can write.

deepdive_en.title: Implement document writing: provide snapshot
deepdive_en.body: Second requirement: implement **`snapshot(contentType:)`** returning current content; the example is `@MainActor` and returns `sending PageSnapshot`, a snapshot of the document at a single point in time.

deepdive_en.title: Implement document writing: represent the snapshot
deepdive_en.body: Use a custom **`PageSnapshot`** struct to represent content—the background image, sticker coordinates (`StickerPlacements`), and the stickers themselves—containing everything needed for writing.

deepdive_en.title: Implement document writing: provide a DocumentWriter
deepdive_en.body: Third requirement: provide a Writer conforming to the **`DocumentWriter`** protocol, given the requested contentType (e.g. stickerDocument); it knows how to write the document to disk in a specified format.

deepdive_en.title: DocumentWriter: Snapshot
deepdive_en.body: `DocumentWriter` has a notion of Snapshot, serving as the content type used during writing.

deepdive_en.title: DocumentWriter: PageSnapshot as Snapshot
deepdive_en.body: Assign the previously defined **`PageSnapshot`** as the Writer's `Snapshot` associated type, fitting the writing requirement perfectly.

deepdive_en.title: DocumentWriter protocol implementation
deepdive_en.body: `DocumentWriter`'s only requirement is the **`write`** method: it is **nonisolated and async**, performing expensive disk writes in the background to keep the app responsive, and by diffing current vs. previous snapshots it **writes only the parts that changed**.

deepdive_en.title: Progress reporting during writing
deepdive_en.body: Even after optimization, disk operations can take time, so SwiftUI provides a **`progress`** parameter to report writing progress using Foundation's **`Subprogress`** API.

deepdive_en.title: Implement document reading with ReadableDocument protocol
deepdive_en.body: Conform the document type to **`ReadableDocument`** for reading, the twin of WritableDocument: both require a supported-formats list, WritableDocument provides a snapshot while ReadableDocument applies it; the former's companion is DocumentWriter, the latter's is DocumentReader doing the disk heavy lifting.

deepdive_en.title: Add PNG to supported formats list
deepdive_en.body: To save pages as images for people without the app, first add **`.png`** to the **`writableContentTypes`** list.

deepdive_en.title: Add content type checks
deepdive_en.body: Since the app now handles multiple formats, add **content type checks** in the `write` method for each supported type (using `contentType.conforms(to:)` to branch between stickerDocument and png).

deepdive_en.title: Writing multiple formats including PNG
deepdive_en.body: The PNG branch uses **Core Graphics** (`CGContext`) to flatten stickers and the background photo into a single image written to the URL. Adding another content type lets you write more formats with any framework.

deepdive_en.title: Presentation and interaction
deepdive_en.body: Begins the presentation-and-interaction segment, covering reorderable containers, swipe actions, and the item-binding pattern for confirmationDialog/alert.

deepdive_en.title: Reorderable list with reorderContainer
deepdive_en.body: Use the **reorderable container** API: add **`reorderable()`** to ForEach and **`reorderContainer(for:)`** to the List, calling a helper in the closure to apply ordering changes; SwiftUI handles the drag interaction and animation automatically.

deepdive_en.title: Apply changes to a reorderable list's data source
deepdive_en.body: The helper (`difference.apply`) uses the open-source **swift-collections** `OrderedDictionary` under the hood to commit ordering changes, computing the destination offset from `destination.position` and moving keys.

deepdive_en.title: Reorderable grid with LazyVGrid
deepdive_en.body: The reorderable API works with any container: move the same List code to a **`LazyVGrid`** with the reordering code unchanged, getting the same interactive reordering in a different container.

deepdive_en.title: Swipe actions on List
deepdive_en.body: Apply **`swipeActions`** to a List item with a Delete button to swipe-remove stickers from the list.

deepdive_en.title: Swipe actions on any view
deepdive_en.body: From iOS 27, **swipe actions work on any view**, not just List: move the ForEach into a `LazyVStack` and add **`swipeActionsContainer()`** to coordinate swipe actions across items in that scroll view.

deepdive_en.title: Confirmation dialog with item binding
deepdive_en.body: **`confirmationDialog`** now supports the same **item-binding** pattern as sheets: pass an `item: $stickerToDelete` binding, and setting the value (e.g. tapping Delete in a context menu) presents the dialog.

deepdive_en.title: Alert with item binding
deepdive_en.body: The same item-binding pattern also applies to **`alert`**: pass an `item:` binding, and setting the value presents the alert.

deepdive_en.title: Data flow and performance
deepdive_en.body: Steven takes over on data flow and performance. Many improvements take effect with no code changes; being thoughtful about data flow is key to keeping an app responsive and smooth.

deepdive_en.title: AsyncImage with URLRequest and custom URLSession
deepdive_en.body: **`AsyncImage`** now supports standard **HTTP caching** by default (respecting server cache headers), enabled for every app so scrolling back to the top no longer reloads. Pass a custom **`URLRequest`** (specifying cachePolicy) or use **`asyncImageURLSession`** to supply a custom `URLSession` configured with a `URLCache`.

deepdive_en.title: @State converted to macro for lazy initialization
deepdive_en.body: **`@State` becomes a macro**: classes stored in State are now **lazy**, initialized once per view lifetime; previously a new instance was created and discarded on each reinitialization. This is back-ported to iOS 17/macOS 14 and aligned releases where `@Observable` debuted.

deepdive_en.title: @State macro init assignment error
deepdive_en.body: The State macro can be source-breaking: if a `@State` variable has both a default value and is assigned in `init`, Xcode reports a use-before-initialization error.

deepdive_en.title: Fixed @State macro init assignment error
deepdive_en.body: The fix is to **remove the unnecessary default value assignment** (leave `@State private var page: StickerPage` for the init to assign), clearing the error.

deepdive_en.title: @ContentBuilder
deepdive_en.body: Deeply nested views often hit the 'compiler unable to type-check in reasonable time' error, caused by Section/Group/ForEach each having multiple builder overloads to try. The new **`@ContentBuilder`** unifies common builders into one, leaving a single straightforward path and **dramatically improving type-checking (compile) performance**; it's an evolution of ViewBuilder usable with any minimum deployment target.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Summarizes the action plan: rebuild your project with Xcode 27 for the 2027 releases and review the refreshed look; if you have a document-based app, adopt the new Document API; and try the **SwiftUI agent skills** shipped with Xcode 27 (SwiftUI Specialist and What's New In SwiftUI), exportable to markdown via `xcrun agent skills export` for other tools.

title: Code-along: Build powerful drag and drop in SwiftUI
gloss: 程式碼共做：在 SwiftUI 打造強大的拖放功能
takeaway: 透過打造接龍遊戲，學會 SwiftUI 全新的**拖放與重排序 API**：`reorderable`、`dragContainer` 與 `dropDestination`。
chapters: Add reorder container to the GameView
Add dragContainer to customize the reorderContainer modifier.
Add dragPreviewsFormation to customize how the dragged cards appear
Add dropPreviewsFormation to customize how dragged cards appear over a destination
Add a drag configuration to allow move.
Add a drop destination modifier and configure it

points.text: 用 **`reorderable()`** 搭配 `reorderContainer(for:)` 即可在集合內重排序，並以 `apply(difference:)` 套用變更。
以 `dragContainer(for:)` 客製化拖曳來源，支援一次**拖曳多張卡片**的堆疊。
透過 `dragPreviewsFormation(.stack)` 與 `dropPreviewsFormation(.stack)` 控制拖曳與放置時的預覽外觀。
用 `DragConfiguration(allowMove: true)` 設定拖曳行為，允許移動而非僅複製。
以 `dropDestination(for:)` 接收放置，並用 `dropConfiguration` 計算目的地與是否允許 `.move` 操作。

audience: **想在 SwiftUI 中實作進階拖放與清單重排序**的 iOS 開發者。
gloss_en: Code-along: Build powerful drag and drop in SwiftUI
takeaway_en: By building a game of Solitaire, learn SwiftUI's new **drag-and-drop and reordering APIs**: `reorderable`, `dragContainer`, and `dropDestination`.

points_en.text: Use **`reorderable()`** together with `reorderContainer(for:)` to reorder within a collection, applying changes with `apply(difference:)`.
Customize the drag source with `dragContainer(for:)`, supporting stacks that **drag multiple cards** at once.
Control the preview appearance during dragging and dropping with `dragPreviewsFormation(.stack)` and `dropPreviewsFormation(.stack)`.
Configure drag behavior with `DragConfiguration(allowMove: true)` to allow moving rather than just copying.
Receive drops with `dropDestination(for:)`, using `dropConfiguration` to compute the destination and whether to allow `.move` operations.

audience_en: iOS developers who **want to implement advanced drag and drop and list reordering in SwiftUI**.
summary: 自 iOS 16 起，SwiftUI 就以 **draggable** 與 **dropDestination** 兩個 modifier 搭配 **Transferable** 協定提供拖放能力，但這場 code-along 帶來 2027 版本三大新進化：全新的**重新排序（reordering）API**、可一次拖曳多個項目的 **Drag Container API**，以及能精細控制資料在拖曳與放置時如何傳輸的**設定（configuration）API**。講者以從零打造一局「接龍（Solitaire）」為主軸，示範如何在既有的 reorderable 之上層層疊加自訂行為，就算你不做接龍也能套用。

重新排序的核心是兩個 modifier：在 ForEach 上加 **reorderable()** 讓每張卡可被拖曳並在原位留下佔位符，在容器上加 **reorderContainer(for:)** 並在 closure 收到 difference 後更新資料。要讓多個牌堆共享同一個排序容器，可把 reorderContainer 加在包住所有 PileView 的 HStack，並用 **Card.Group** 這類型別唯一識別每一堆；當同一容器有多個 reorderable，需用 collectionID 區分。一個巧妙細節：接龍不能重排蓋著的牌，講者不靠進階 API，而是把卡片陣列切成兩個 ForEach——蓋著的牌那段不加 reorderable，翻開的牌那段才加，乾淨地擋掉不該被拖的牌。

要一次拖多張牌，reorderContainer 雖隱含自帶 dragContainer 與 dropDestination，但可自行加上 **dragContainer(for:)**（型別需與容器一致）並在 closure 回傳該卡上方整疊的 transferable 資料。拖曳與放置時的外觀則用 **dragPreviewsFormation(.stack)** 與 **dropPreviewsFormation(.stack)** 統一，後者建議下在 GameView 根層以確保整個遊玩區一致。注意 dragContainer 為 iOS、iPadOS、visionOS 27 新增，三個 formation modifier 則於 macOS 26 起可用。

最後用 **Drag Configuration API** 補上把新牌移入牌堆的規則。預設拖曳資料以複製（copy）傳輸，但卡牌應該是「移動」而非複製，故在來源卡上加 **dragConfiguration(DragConfiguration(allowMove: true))** 表達移動意圖；由於目的地的 reorderContainer 預設只接受容器內的移動，需自行補一個 **dropDestination(for:)** 讀取 reorderDestination 並呼叫遊戲邏輯插入新牌，再用 **dropConfiguration** 在 closure 中做三件事：依拖曳位置算出目標牌堆、只允許 move 傳輸、並驗證該移動是否合法（不合法回傳 forbidden 讓 SwiftUI 擋下）。實務帶走的重點：先用 reorderable／reorderContainer 把基本排序跑起來，再以 drag/drop 的 container 與 configuration modifier 逐步客製，就能做出順手又有規則的拖放體驗。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: 回顧 iOS 16 起 SwiftUI 透過 **draggable** 與 **dropDestination** 提供拖放，資料只要符合 **Transferable** 協定即可在系統間拖曳並被其他 App 接受（如把 card 型別 conform Transferable）。本場次宣告三大擴充：reordering API、可拖多項的 Drag Container API，以及可設定資料傳輸方式的 configuration API，並以打造接龍遊戲為示範主線，附可下載的範例專案。

deepdive.title: Reordering
deepdive.body: 說明 App 內容通常有既定順序、但使用者想自行重排。示範拖曳一張牌時，它會從 view hierarchy 被「抬起」、原位留下空白佔位符，拖過其他牌時它們會讓出空間、佔位符也更新到放下後的位置。講者策略是先不套遊戲規則把 reordering 跑通，再回頭加入規則。

deepdive.title: Add reorderable to the preview
deepdive.body: 先在檔案底部的 Preview（綠底四張牌）試水溫：在建立卡片的 **ForEach** 加 **reorderable()**，在 HStack 加 **reorderContainer**，指定 item 型別為 **CardValue**（與 ForEach 一致），closure 收到 difference 後更新 cards 陣列。完成後即可在 Preview 把梅花 A 從左拖到尾端重排。

deepdive.title: Add reorder container to the GameView
deepdive.body: 為了讓所有牌堆同屬一個排序容器，把 **reorderContainer** 加到包住所有 PileView 的 HStack，沿用 **CardValue** 為 item 型別。因為有多個牌堆，需用 **Card.Group** 型別唯一識別每一堆，並在 closure 處理跨多堆的 difference，呼叫 game.moveCards(difference:) 更新資料。

deepdive.title: Add reorderable to PileView
deepdive.body: 到 **PileView** 在卡片的 ForEach 加 **reorderable**；由於同一容器內有多個 reorderable，需提供唯一識別（collectionID: Card.Group.pile(index)）。如此即可把方塊 4 拖放到有黑桃 5 的牌堆，完成跨堆重排。

deepdive.title: Drag multiple items
deepdive.body: 處理接龍不能重排蓋著牌的需求。講者不用進階 API，而是把 cards 陣列以 firstFaceUpIndex 切成兩個 **ForEach**：前段是蓋著的牌、不加 reorderable，後段是翻開的牌、加上 reorderable（並以 id: \.value 識別）。如此翻開的牌可重排、拖蓋著的牌則無反應；這些 API 在所有支援拖放的 Apple 平台皆可用。

deepdive.title: Add dragContainer to customize the reorderContainer modifier.
deepdive.body: 為了一次拖多張牌，雖然 reorderContainer 隱含自帶 dragContainer 與 dropDestination，仍在其下方自行宣告 **dragContainer(for: CardValue.self)** 以客製行為，型別須與容器一致。closure 收到 item identifier 後，呼叫遊戲邏輯（game.cardStack(startingAt:)）找出疊在該牌上方的整疊卡並回傳其 transferable 資料；如此拖梅花 4 時其上的方塊 3 會一起被帶走。

deepdive.title: Add dragPreviewsFormation to customize how the dragged cards appear
deepdive.body: 多張牌一起拖時預設會收成一疊（pile，首張在上）。講者用 **dragPreviewsFormation** 改變外觀，可選 pile、list、stack 等，選 **.stack** 因為它精簡又有疊牌的手感，拖梅花 4 時卡片便排成整齊的一疊。

deepdive.title: Add dropPreviewsFormation to customize how dragged cards appear over a destination
deepdive.body: 拖到牌堆上方時外觀會還原成預設，因為此時受 reorderContainer 的 dropDestination 之 drop formation 影響。講者用 **dropPreviewsFormation(.stack)** 統一，並把它下在 **GameView** 根層以套用到 App 內所有 dropDestination，使拖曳外觀在整個遊玩區一致。注意 dragContainer 為 iOS／iPadOS／visionOS 27 新增，三個 modifier 皆於 macOS 26 起可用。

deepdive.title: Drag configuration
deepdive.body: 說明加上拖曳能力時要先想「資料如何移動」。預設 SwiftUI 建議以複製（copy）傳輸，適合跨 App 移動或插入新資料，但接龍中把牌拖進牌堆不該產生複本，而應從牌庫「移動」過去。由於這些 view 是與 reorderContainer 分離的拖曳來源與 dropDestination，需改用新的 **Drag Configuration API** 才能達成。

deepdive.title: Add a drag configuration to allow move.
deepdive.body: 在 **RemainderView** 目前翻開的卡片已有拖曳 modifier、預設以 copy 傳輸。講者加上 **dragConfiguration(DragConfiguration(allowMove: true))** 表達此卡的意圖是以 move 傳輸，但實際如何傳輸仍由 dropDestination 決定。

deepdive.title: Add a drop destination modifier and configure it
deepdive.body: 因為 reorderContainer 預設只接受容器內的移動，要接受新項目須自行在 dragContainer 下加 **dropDestination(for: CardValue.self)**，讀取 session 的 **reorderDestination** 並呼叫 game.insertCards 插入新牌（堆間移動仍由 reorderContainer closure 處理）。再加 **dropConfiguration** 做三件事：依 session.location 算出目標牌堆並建立 Destination、只表達 move 意圖、用 game.validateMove 驗證合法性，不合法回傳 .forbidden 讓 SwiftUI 擋下。如此方塊 6 只在規則允許時才能拖到黑桃 7 上，非法移動（如方塊 Q）則彈回牌庫。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 總結：本案從只有 reorderable 與 reorderContainer 起步，再以堆疊 drag/drop modifier 完整客製出一局接龍。鼓勵開發者即使不做接龍，也可考慮為 App 內容加入重排、用 Drag Container API 支援一次拖多項，並以 drag/drop 設定微調，讓 App 的拖放體驗更順手好用。

summary_en: Since iOS 16, SwiftUI has offered drag and drop via the **draggable** and **dropDestination** modifiers backed by the **Transferable** protocol, but this code-along introduces three major advances in the 2027 releases: a new **reordering API**, a **Drag Container API** for dragging multiple items at once, and **configuration APIs** for fine-grained control over how data transfers during drags and drops. The speaker builds a game of Solitaire from scratch to show how to layer custom behavior on top of basic reordering—techniques that apply even if you aren't building Solitaire.

Reordering centers on two modifiers: add **reorderable()** to a ForEach so each card can be lifted and leaves a placeholder, and add **reorderContainer(for:)** to the container, updating your data from the difference in the closure. To share one reorder container across multiple piles, place reorderContainer on the HStack wrapping all PileViews and use a type like **Card.Group** to uniquely identify each pile; when a container holds multiple reorderables, distinguish them with a collectionID. A neat detail: since face-down cards can't be reordered in Solitaire, rather than reaching for advanced API the speaker slices the cards array into two ForEach views—one for face-down cards without reorderable, one for face-up cards with it—cleanly preventing the wrong cards from being dragged.

To drag multiple cards at once, although reorderContainer implicitly provides its own dragContainer and dropDestination, you can add your own **dragContainer(for:)** (matching the container's type) and return the transferable data for the whole stack above a card in the closure. Drag and drop appearance is unified with **dragPreviewsFormation(.stack)** and **dropPreviewsFormation(.stack)**, the latter best declared on the GameView root for consistency across the playing area. Note that dragContainer is new on iOS, iPadOS, and visionOS 27, while the three formation modifiers are available on macOS 26 and newer.

Finally, the **Drag Configuration API** adds the rules for moving new cards into piles. By default drag data transfers by copy, but a card should move rather than be copied, so the source card gets **dragConfiguration(DragConfiguration(allowMove: true))** to express move intent; because the destination reorderContainer accepts only moves within the container by default, you add a **dropDestination(for:)** that reads the reorderDestination and calls game logic to insert new cards, then a **dropConfiguration** whose closure does three things: compute the target pile from the drag location, allow only move transfers, and validate whether the move is legal (returning forbidden lets SwiftUI block it). The practical takeaway: get basic reordering working with reorderable/reorderContainer first, then customize step by step with the drag/drop container and configuration modifiers to build a rule-aware, delightful drag-and-drop experience.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Recaps that since iOS 16 SwiftUI has provided drag and drop through **draggable** and **dropDestination**, with data conforming to the **Transferable** protocol so it can be dragged across the system and accepted by other apps (e.g. conforming a card type to Transferable). The session announces three expansions—a reordering API, a Drag Container API for multiple items, and configuration APIs for data transfer—using a Solitaire game as the running example, with a downloadable sample project.

deepdive_en.title: Reordering
deepdive_en.body: Explains that app content usually has an order but people want to rearrange it. Demonstrates that dragging a card lifts it from the view hierarchy, leaving an empty placeholder, and that other cards make space as you drag over them while the placeholder updates to the drop location. The strategy is to get reordering working without game rules first, then add the rules back in.

deepdive_en.title: Add reorderable to the preview
deepdive_en.body: Tries it out in the bottom-of-file Preview (four cards on green): add **reorderable()** to the **ForEach** creating the cards, add **reorderContainer** to the HStack, specify the item type as **CardValue** (matching the ForEach), and update the cards array from the difference in the closure. The preview can then reorder the ace of clubs from the left to the end.

deepdive_en.title: Add reorder container to the GameView
deepdive_en.body: To put all piles in one reorder container, the **reorderContainer** is added to the HStack containing every PileView, reusing **CardValue** as the item type. Because there are multiple piles, the **Card.Group** type uniquely identifies each, and the closure handles a difference across piles by calling game.moveCards(difference:).

deepdive_en.title: Add reorderable to PileView
deepdive_en.body: In **PileView**, **reorderable** is added to the cards' ForEach; since multiple reorderables share one container, each needs a unique identifier (collectionID: Card.Group.pile(index)). This enables dragging the four of diamonds onto the pile with the five of spades for cross-pile reordering.

deepdive_en.title: Drag multiple items
deepdive_en.body: Handles the rule that face-down cards can't be reordered. Instead of advanced API, the speaker slices the cards array at firstFaceUpIndex into two **ForEach** views: the first holds face-down cards without reorderable, the second holds face-up cards with it (identified by id: \.value). Face-up cards reorder while face-down cards don't respond; these APIs are available on all Apple platforms that support drag and drop.

deepdive_en.title: Add dragContainer to customize the reorderContainer modifier.
deepdive_en.body: To drag multiple cards, even though reorderContainer implicitly provides its own dragContainer and dropDestination, a **dragContainer(for: CardValue.self)** is declared below it to customize behavior, matching the container's type. Its closure receives an item identifier and calls game logic (game.cardStack(startingAt:)) to find the cards stacked above and return their transferable data, so dragging the four of clubs brings the three of diamonds along.

deepdive_en.title: Add dragPreviewsFormation to customize how the dragged cards appear
deepdive_en.body: By default dragged cards collapse into a pile (first card on top). The speaker uses **dragPreviewsFormation** to change the appearance—options include pile, list, and stack—choosing **.stack** because it's compact and has the feel of stacked cards, so the four of clubs forms a neat stack when dragged.

deepdive_en.title: Add dropPreviewsFormation to customize how dragged cards appear over a destination
deepdive_en.body: Over the piles the appearance reverts to default because the cards then use the reorderContainer's dropDestination drop formation. The speaker unifies it with **dropPreviewsFormation(.stack)** declared on the **GameView** root so it applies to every dropDestination, keeping the dragged appearance consistent across the playing area. Note dragContainer is new on iOS/iPadOS/visionOS 27, and all three modifiers are available on macOS 26 and newer.

deepdive_en.title: Drag configuration
deepdive_en.body: Explains thinking about how a card's value should move when adding drag. SwiftUI defaults to transfer by copy, which suits moving data between apps or inserting something new, but in Solitaire dragging a card into a pile shouldn't create a copy—it should move from the deck. Because these views are a separate drag source and dropDestination from the reorderContainer, the new **Drag Configuration API** is needed.

deepdive_en.title: Add a drag configuration to allow move.
deepdive_en.body: In **RemainderView** the current face-up card already has drag modifiers and defaults to transfer by copy. The speaker adds **dragConfiguration(DragConfiguration(allowMove: true))** to express the intent that this card transfers by move, though the dropDestination ultimately decides how the data is transferred.

deepdive_en.title: Add a drop destination modifier and configure it
deepdive_en.body: Because the reorderContainer accepts only moves within the container by default, accepting new items requires a **dropDestination(for: CardValue.self)** below the dragContainer that reads the session's **reorderDestination** and calls game.insertCards (moves between piles stay handled by the reorderContainer closure). A **dropConfiguration** then does three things: compute the target pile from session.location and build a Destination, express move-only intent, and validate legality with game.validateMove, returning .forbidden so SwiftUI blocks invalid drops. Thus the six of diamonds can land on the seven of spades only when allowed, while an illegal move like the queen of diamonds returns to the deck.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Wraps up: the app started with just reorderable and reorderContainer, then composed drag/drop modifiers on top to fully build Solitaire. Even if you aren't building Solitaire, consider letting people reorder content, supporting multi-item drags with the Drag Container API, and fine-tuning with drag/drop configurations to make your app's drag and drop a delight to use.

title: Use SwiftUI with AppKit and UIKit
gloss: 在 AppKit 與 UIKit 中使用 SwiftUI
takeaway: 藉助 Observation 框架，把 SwiftUI 視圖、手勢、選單與場景漸進式地嵌入既有的 AppKit 或 UIKit App。
chapters: Adding ColorMenu to the Main Menu

points.text: 用 **@Observable** 模型讓 AppKit 與 SwiftUI 共享同一份狀態，達成漸進式採用。
透過 **NSHostingView** 將 SwiftUI 視圖（如自訂色彩選擇器）嵌入 AppKit 介面。
以 **NSGestureRecognizerRepresentable** 把 NSGestureRecognizer（如 Force Click）橋接進 SwiftUI。
使用 **NSHostingMenu** 把 SwiftUI 定義的選單放進 macOS 主選單列。
透過 **NSHostingSceneRepresentation** 動態加入 MenuBarExtra、Settings 等 SwiftUI 場景。

audience: 維護既有 **AppKit 或 UIKit App**、想逐步導入 SwiftUI 的 macOS／iOS 開發者。
gloss_en: Use SwiftUI with AppKit and UIKit
takeaway_en: Leverage the Observation framework to incrementally embed SwiftUI views, gestures, menus, and scenes into an existing AppKit or UIKit app.

points_en.text: Use an **@Observable** model to share the same state between AppKit and SwiftUI, enabling incremental adoption.
Embed SwiftUI views (such as a custom color picker) into an AppKit interface via **NSHostingView**.
Bridge an NSGestureRecognizer (such as Force Click) into SwiftUI with **NSGestureRecognizerRepresentable**.
Use **NSHostingMenu** to place a SwiftUI-defined menu into the macOS main menu bar.
Dynamically add SwiftUI scenes like MenuBarExtra and Settings via **NSHostingSceneRepresentation**.

audience_en: macOS/iOS developers maintaining an existing **AppKit or UIKit app** who want to adopt SwiftUI incrementally.
summary: 這場由 UI Frameworks 團隊的 David Nadoba 主講，核心訊息是：**SwiftUI 從一開始就被設計成能與 AppKit、UIKit 共存**，就像 Swift 與 Objective-C 一樣，因此你可以**漸進式採用**，不必整個 app 重寫或從零開始。講者強調連 Apple 自己也走這條路（Logic Pro 的外掛、Xcode 的 Coding Assistant），而且在 2026 的新設計下，即使你用 NSSlider、NSSwitch 這類 AppKit 控制項，底層其實也是用 SwiftUI 與 **Liquid Glass** 來繪製。全程以一個能透過網路控制檯燈的 AppKit app（含一個三滑桿的自訂顏色選擇器）作為範例。

起點是**先用 @Observable，連 SwiftUI 都還沒登場**。原本當 hue 改變時要手動對其他滑桿設 `needsDisplay = true` 才會重繪；只要把 model 標上 **@Observable**，AppKit 會追蹤在 `draw`、`drawKnob`、`drawBar` 等繪製方法中存取了哪些屬性，並在它們變動時自動重繪。除了 `NSView.draw(_:)`，**updateConstraints()、layout()、updateLayer()** 與對應的 NSViewController 方法也都支援；UIKit 涵蓋更廣，延伸到 UIButton、UICollectionViewCell 等。此功能可透過 Info.plist 的 **NSObservationTrackingEnabled**（macOS 15）與 **UIObservationTrackingEnabled**（iOS 18）回溯部署，2026 版起預設開啟。

接著是**何時改用 SwiftUI 與如何嵌入 NSView 階層**。當畫法與互動會整個改變時（例如把三個直線滑桿改成圓環式顏色選擇器），就是換用 SwiftUI 的好時機——可沿用同一個 @Observable ColorModel，並用 **Canvas** 這個 immediate-mode 繪圖 API（類似 drawRect，也能用 withCGContext 沿用既有 CoreGraphics 程式碼）。要放回既有 NSView 階層，就把 SwiftUI view 包進 **NSHostingView**（它是 NSView 子類）。此外可用 **NSGestureRecognizerRepresentable** 把既有的 NSGestureRecognizer 子類（示範中的 ForceClickGestureRecognizer，偵測 trackpad 用力按的 force click）直接以 `.gesture` 加到 SwiftUI view，與既有的 DragGesture 共存無需改動。

最後兩段把 SwiftUI 帶進**主選單與 Scene**。force click 並非所有輸入裝置都支援，所以講者用 SwiftUI 寫了含 Button、keyboardShortcut 與 palette 風格 Picker 的 **ColorMenu** view，再用 **NSHostingMenu**（NSMenu 子類）包起來、設成 NSMenuItem 的 submenu 加進既有主選單。完整的 SwiftUI **Scene** 也能從既有 app delegate 動態加入：用 **NSHostingSceneRepresentation** 包住 MenuBarExtra 與 Settings 兩個 scene，在 `applicationWillFinishLaunching` 呼叫 `addSceneRepresentation`，並透過其 environment 的 `openSettings()` 從 @IBAction 程式化開啟設定視窗。結語提醒：app 不需要全部變成 SwiftUI 才能受惠，先試 @Observable、在新元件採用 SwiftUI，就是很好的第一步。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: David Nadoba 開場說明 **SwiftUI 自設計之初就能與 AppKit／UIKit 良好共存**，適合漸進式採用而不必重寫。他舉 Logic Pro 外掛、Xcode 27 的 Coding Assistant 為例，並指出即便你用 NSSlider、NSSwitch 等 AppKit 控制項，底層也已用 **SwiftUI** 與 **Liquid Glass** 繪製。本場聚焦 macOS（概念通用於各平台），以一個能控制桌上環形燈的 AppKit app 為範例。

deepdive.title: Observation in AppKit
deepdive.body: 拆解現有顏色選擇器的痛點：三個滑桿以自訂 track 漸層與 knob 繪製，移動 hue 的 knob 時其他滑桿的外觀也需更新，但 AppKit 不會自動重繪。目前必須在 hue 改變時手動對 saturation、brightness 滑桿設 **needsDisplay = true**，且每個值與外部變動都得照做。

deepdive.title: Observation in AppKit
deepdive.body: 提出解法：在 Swift class 加上 **@Observable** 巨集，所有可變屬性即納入觀察系統。滑桿是 NSSliderCell 子類，只要在 **drawKnob** 等繪製方法中存取新 ColorModel 的屬性，AppKit 就會追蹤存取並在屬性變動時自動重繪，不再需要手動 needsDisplay。除了 draw，**updateConstraints()、layout()、updateLayer()** 與 NSViewController 對應方法也支援；UIKit 更延伸到 UIButton、UICollectionViewCell 等，並可用 Info.plist 旗標回溯部署到 macOS 15／iOS 18。

deepdive.title: Hosting SwiftUI in AppKit
deepdive.body: 講者構想一個全新的圓環式顏色選擇器：hue 為外圈色環、saturation 與 brightness 為內側兩個半圓、正中央以圓形預覽結果色。由於整個繪圖與互動都會改變，他認為這正是改用 SwiftUI 的好時機，並可沿用先前 NSSlider 版本相同的 @Observable ColorModel。

deepdive.title: Circular color picker
deepdive.body: 在 view 的 body 使用 **Canvas**——一個 immediate-mode 繪圖 API，類似 AppKit／UIKit 的 drawRect：每次重繪都以新的 GraphicsContext 呼叫你的 closure，直接下 stroke、fill、transform、filter 等繪製指令。也可透過 **withCGContext** 沿用既有 CoreGraphics 繪圖程式碼，並引用 WWDC21 的 Canvas 介紹與 WWDC26 的 Metal Shader 講座。

deepdive.title: Hosting SwiftUI in AppKit
deepdive.body: 因為顏色選擇器仍嵌在多處 NSView 階層中，講者把 SwiftUI view 包進 **NSHostingView**（NSView 的子類）即可放回原處。關鍵在於 model 早已改為 @Observable，所以幾乎不需其他改動；並指向 WWDC 2022 的「Use SwiftUI with AppKit／UIKit」做深入了解。

deepdive.title: AppKit gestures in SwiftUI
deepdive.body: 在展示新選擇器前，他想加一個功能：用一次 **force click**（在 trackpad 上用力按）把 brightness 與 saturation 快速重設為 100%。他在 app 其他地方已有對應的 **NSGestureRecognizer**，希望直接沿用到新的 SwiftUI view。

deepdive.title: Mix NSGestureRecognizer with SwiftUI
deepdive.body: 用 **NSGestureRecognizerRepresentable** 把既有手勢辨識器帶入 SwiftUI：在 makeNSGestureRecognizer 回傳 **ForceClickGestureRecognizer**（偵測 pressure stage 2），在 handleNSGestureRecognizerAction 把 saturation、brightness 重設為 1 並包進 withAnimation。回到 HSBColorPicker 後用 **.gesture** 修飾子加上去，與既有 DragGesture 共存無需其他改動；他也提到 NSViewRepresentable 等其他 representable 協定。

deepdive.title: SwiftUI in the main menu
deepdive.body: 由於 Magic Mouse、MacBook Neo 的 trackpad 等裝置無法做 force click，需要另一種存取方式：帶 keyboard shortcut 的選單項目。app 主選單用的是 AppKit 的 **NSMenu**，講者接著說明如何用 SwiftUI 加入這個新選單項目。

deepdive.title: Adding ColorMenu to the Main Menu
deepdive.body: 建立符合 View 協定、可存取共享 ColorModel 的 **ColorMenu**：body 中放 Button（含 label 與重設 action，並用 withAnimation 動畫化）、加上 **keyboardShortcut**，以及一個 **palette 風格的 Picker** 精準選常用色。再用 **NSHostingMenu**（NSMenu 子類，可設 title）包住此 view，建立 NSMenuItem、設為其 submenu 並加進 mainMenu。

deepdive.title: SwiftUI scenes in AppKit
deepdive.body: 最後一步：用既有 app delegate 把完整的 **SwiftUI Scene** 帶進 app。講者想讓使用者能快速調整燈的顏色或亮度，因此打算加入一個 menu bar extra，而 SwiftUI 的 **MenuBarExtra** scene 只需幾行就能做到。

deepdive.title: Adding SwiftUI scenes dynamically
deepdive.body: 用 **NSHostingSceneRepresentation** 包住 SwiftUI scene，讓既有 AppKit app 能動態加入；在 NSApplicationDelegate 的 **applicationWillFinishLaunching** 呼叫 **addSceneRepresentation** 傳入 scenes 即可。再用 **Settings** scene 放一個 Toggle 控制 MenuBarExtra 的插入與移除，並透過該 representation environment 的 **openSettings()**，從 @IBAction 程式化開啟設定視窗。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 總結混用 SwiftUI 與 AppKit 的多種方式，並強調正確做法取決於你的 app 與問題。建議：先試 **@Observable** 讓 model 與 NSView 自動同步；在實作或重寫元件時考慮 SwiftUI；把既有 gesture recognizer 子類加到 SwiftUI view；新 scene 直接用 SwiftUI 起手。所有 API 在 2026 或更早版本即可使用，且 app 不需全面 SwiftUI 才能受惠。

summary_en: Presented by David Nadoba of the UI Frameworks team, the core message is that **SwiftUI was designed from the start to work alongside AppKit and UIKit** — much like Swift with Objective-C — so you can **adopt it incrementally** without rewriting your whole app or starting from scratch. He notes Apple itself follows this path (Logic Pro plugins, Xcode's Coding Assistant), and that with the 2026 design even AppKit controls like NSSlider and NSSwitch are rendered using SwiftUI and **Liquid Glass** under the hood. The running example is an AppKit app that controls a desk ring lamp over the network, with a custom three-slider color picker.

The starting point is **@Observable, before any SwiftUI at all**. Previously, when hue changed you had to manually set `needsDisplay = true` on the other sliders to redraw them; just adding **@Observable** to the model makes AppKit track which properties are accessed inside draw methods like `draw`, `drawKnob`, and `drawBar`, and redraw automatically when they change. Beyond `NSView.draw(_:)`, **updateConstraints(), layout(), updateLayer()** and the NSViewController equivalents also support it; UIKit goes further to UIButton, UICollectionViewCell, and more. It can be back-deployed via the Info.plist keys **NSObservationTrackingEnabled** (macOS 15) and **UIObservationTrackingEnabled** (iOS 18), and is on by default from the 2026 releases.

Next is **when to move to SwiftUI and how to embed it in an NSView hierarchy**. When the drawing and interaction will change completely (e.g. turning three linear sliders into a circular color picker), it's a great time to switch — reusing the same @Observable ColorModel and SwiftUI's **Canvas**, an immediate-mode drawing API (like drawRect, and able to reuse existing CoreGraphics code via withCGContext). To place it back in an existing NSView hierarchy, wrap the SwiftUI view in **NSHostingView** (an NSView subclass). You can also use **NSGestureRecognizerRepresentable** to add an existing NSGestureRecognizer subclass (the demo's ForceClickGestureRecognizer, detecting a firm trackpad force click) directly to a SwiftUI view via `.gesture`, coexisting with the existing DragGesture without other changes.

The last two parts bring SwiftUI into the **main menu and Scenes**. Since force click isn't available on every input device, he builds a SwiftUI **ColorMenu** view with a Button, keyboardShortcut, and a palette-style Picker, then wraps it in **NSHostingMenu** (an NSMenu subclass) as a submenu added to the existing main menu. Full SwiftUI **Scenes** can be added dynamically from an existing app delegate too: wrap MenuBarExtra and Settings scenes in **NSHostingSceneRepresentation**, call `addSceneRepresentation` in `applicationWillFinishLaunching`, and use its environment's `openSettings()` from an @IBAction to open Settings programmatically. The closing reminder: an app needn't be entirely SwiftUI to benefit — trying @Observable and adopting SwiftUI for new components are great first steps.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: David Nadoba opens by explaining that **SwiftUI was designed from the beginning to work great alongside AppKit and UIKit**, ideal for incremental adoption without rewriting everything. He cites Logic Pro plugins and Xcode 27's Coding Assistant, and notes that even AppKit controls like NSSlider and NSSwitch are now rendered using **SwiftUI** and **Liquid Glass** under the hood. The talk focuses on macOS (concepts apply to all platforms), using an AppKit app that controls a desk ring lamp.

deepdive_en.title: Observation in AppKit
deepdive_en.body: He walks through the current color picker's pain point: three sliders with a custom track gradient and knob, where moving the hue knob must also update the other sliders' appearance, but AppKit doesn't redraw them automatically. Today he must manually set **needsDisplay = true** on the saturation and brightness sliders whenever hue changes, and similarly for every value and external change.

deepdive_en.title: Observation in AppKit
deepdive_en.body: The fix: add the **@Observable** macro to a Swift class so all mutable variables participate in observation. The sliders are NSSliderCell subclasses, and simply accessing the new ColorModel's properties inside draw methods like **drawKnob** lets AppKit track the access and redraw automatically when they change — no more manual needsDisplay. Besides draw, **updateConstraints(), layout(), updateLayer()** and NSViewController equivalents support it; UIKit extends to UIButton, UICollectionViewCell, and more, with Info.plist flags to back-deploy to macOS 15 / iOS 18.

deepdive_en.title: Hosting SwiftUI in AppKit
deepdive_en.body: He envisions a new circular color picker: hue as an outer color ring, saturation and brightness as two inner semicircles, with a circular preview of the resulting color in the middle. Because the whole drawing and interaction will change, he sees this as a great time to move to SwiftUI, reusing the same @Observable ColorModel from the NSSlider-based picker.

deepdive_en.title: Circular color picker
deepdive_en.body: In the view's body he uses **Canvas** — an immediate-mode drawing API like AppKit/UIKit's drawRect: each redraw calls your closure with a fresh GraphicsContext where you issue strokes, fills, transforms, and filters directly. Existing CoreGraphics drawing code can be reused via **withCGContext**, and he references WWDC21's Canvas intro and WWDC26's Metal Shaders session.

deepdive_en.title: Hosting SwiftUI in AppKit
deepdive_en.body: Since the picker is still embedded in many NSView hierarchies, he wraps the SwiftUI view in **NSHostingView** (an NSView subclass) to drop it back in. Because the model was already moved to @Observable, that's essentially all that's needed; he points to WWDC 2022's "Use SwiftUI with AppKit/UIKit" for a deeper tour.

deepdive_en.title: AppKit gestures in SwiftUI
deepdive_en.body: Before showing the new picker he wants one more feature: reset brightness and saturation to 100% with a single **force click** (a firm press on the trackpad). He already has an **NSGestureRecognizer** for this used elsewhere in the app and wants to reuse it in the new SwiftUI view.

deepdive_en.title: Mix NSGestureRecognizer with SwiftUI
deepdive_en.body: Using **NSGestureRecognizerRepresentable**, he brings the existing recognizer into SwiftUI: makeNSGestureRecognizer returns his **ForceClickGestureRecognizer** (recognizing pressure stage 2), and handleNSGestureRecognizerAction resets saturation and brightness to 1 inside withAnimation. Back in HSBColorPicker he adds it with the **.gesture** modifier, coexisting with the existing DragGesture without other changes; he also mentions other representables like NSViewRepresentable.

deepdive_en.title: SwiftUI in the main menu
deepdive_en.body: Because devices like the Magic Mouse and MacBook Neo trackpad can't do a force click, another access path is needed: a menu item with a keyboard shortcut. The app's main menu uses AppKit's **NSMenu**, and he explains how to add the new menu item using SwiftUI.

deepdive_en.title: Adding ColorMenu to the Main Menu
deepdive_en.body: He creates a **ColorMenu** conforming to View with access to the shared ColorModel: the body has a Button (with label and reset action wrapped in withAnimation), a **keyboardShortcut**, and a **palette-style Picker** to precisely select common colors. He then wraps it in **NSHostingMenu** (an NSMenu subclass with a title), creates an NSMenuItem, sets the color menu as its submenu, and adds it to the mainMenu.

deepdive_en.title: SwiftUI scenes in AppKit
deepdive_en.body: The final step: bring complete **SwiftUI Scenes** to the app using the existing app delegate. He wants to give people quick access to change the lights' color or brightness via a menu bar extra, which SwiftUI's **MenuBarExtra** scene makes possible in just a few lines.

deepdive_en.title: Adding SwiftUI scenes dynamically
deepdive_en.body: He wraps SwiftUI scenes in **NSHostingSceneRepresentation** so an existing AppKit app can add them dynamically, calling **addSceneRepresentation** in the NSApplicationDelegate's **applicationWillFinishLaunching**. A **Settings** scene adds a Toggle to control inserting/removing the MenuBarExtra, and the representation's environment exposes **openSettings()**, used from an @IBAction to open the settings window programmatically.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: He sums up the various ways to mix SwiftUI and AppKit, noting the right approach depends on your app and problem. Recommendations: try **@Observable** to keep model and NSViews in sync; consider SwiftUI when implementing or rewriting a component; add existing gesture recognizer subclasses to SwiftUI views; start new scenes with SwiftUI. All APIs are available on the 2026 releases or earlier, and an app needn't be entirely SwiftUI to benefit.

title: What’s new in SwiftData
gloss: SwiftData 的新功能
takeaway: SwiftData 新增分區擷取、以 Codable 持久化自訂與第三方型別，以及 ResultsObserver 與 HistoryObserver 來觀察資料變動與同步歷史。
chapters: // Use observation to update map bounds
// Using HistoryObserver to sync with a server

points.text: 新的**分區擷取**：在 **@Query** 中用 sectionBy 直接依屬性分組，搭配 ForEach 走訪 sections 渲染分區 List。
可用 **@Attribute(.codable)** 與 Codable 巢狀型別持久化**自訂及第三方型別**（如 MKMapItem.Identifier）。
**ResultsObserver** 讓你在 SwiftUI 之外觀察查詢結果變動（例如更新地圖邊界）。
**HistoryObserver** 搭配 withContinuousObservation 追蹤資料變更歷史，適合與伺服器同步。

audience: **使用 SwiftData 做資料持久化**、需要分區顯示、自訂型別儲存或與後端同步的 App 開發者。
gloss_en: What's new in SwiftData
takeaway_en: SwiftData adds sectioned fetching, persisting custom and third-party types with Codable, and ResultsObserver and HistoryObserver for observing data changes and sync history.

points_en.text: New **sectioned fetching**: use sectionBy in **@Query** to group directly by a property, then iterate sections with ForEach to render a sectioned List.
Use **@Attribute(.codable)** with nested Codable types to persist **custom and third-party types** (such as MKMapItem.Identifier).
**ResultsObserver** lets you observe changes to query results outside of SwiftUI (for example, to update map bounds).
**HistoryObserver** with withContinuousObservation tracks the history of data changes, ideal for syncing with a server.

audience_en: App developers **using SwiftData for data persistence** who need sectioned display, custom type storage, or backend syncing.
summary: 本場由 SwiftData 團隊工程師 Thomas 介紹 Apple 2027 版本中 SwiftData 的新功能，並以多年來持續開發、用於追蹤旅行計畫的範例 app **SampleTrips** (採 SwiftData 持久化、SwiftUI 介面) 貫穿全場。第一個主題是 **sectioned fetching**：`@Query` 新增 `sectionBy` 參數，只要傳入從 model root 指向字串的 KeyPath (例如 `\.destination`)，即可把結果依該屬性分組。Query 的 wrapped value 仍是 `[Trip]`，但透過底線前綴的 `_trips` 可取得 `sections`，搭配巢狀 `ForEach` 與 `Section`，並以每個 section 的 `id` (KeyPath 對應值) 當作標題，輕鬆做出依目的地分組的清單。

第二個主題是儲存自訂型別。範例想把 MapKit 搜尋到的座標與 **MKMapItem.Identifier** 存入 Trip model，但因為 `MKMapItem.Identifier` 是無法標註 `@Model`、SwiftData 也無法自動檢視的 class，啟動時會丟出「Class property within Persisted Struct/Enum is not supported」的 fatal error。解法是 Apple 2027 新增的 **`.codable` attribute**：由於該型別符合 **Codable**，將屬性標為 `@Attribute(.codable)` 即可讓 SwiftData 委派序列化、儲存其編碼後的表示。但要注意 codable 內容對 SwiftData 是不透明的，無法用於 Predicate 過濾或 Sort Descriptor 排序，型別結構改變也不會觸發 migration，因此它是儲存「你不擁有的型別」的逃生艙，自有型別仍應建模為 SwiftData model 以享有排序、過濾與索引。

第三個主題是監看資料變化的全新 API。`@Query` 雖好，但僅限 SwiftUI 視圖;Apple 2027 推出 **ResultsObserver**,可在 app 任何地方 (非 SwiftUI、甚至 SceneKit 遊戲) 運作，同樣支援 filtering、sorting 與 sectioning,透過 **Swift Observation** 反應變化。範例用 `MapCameraController` 持有 `ResultsObserver<Trip, Never>`,以 `withContinuousObservation(options: [.didSet])` 在 trip 變動時重算地圖的 `MapCameraBounds`,並把回傳的 **ObservationTracking token** 存於 class 以維持觀察生命週期。

最後是 **HistoryObserver**。SwiftData 每次儲存都會記錄一筆 history transaction (包含變更內容、來源 author 與唯一 token),可用於與外部伺服器同步或反應 app extension 等外部變更。HistoryObserver 讓你輕鬆反應 persistent history 的新交易,並可依 model 型別與 transaction author 過濾;它只有一個可觀察屬性 **eventCounter**,有新交易時遞增。範例的 `ServerSync` 以 `authors: ["App"]` 建立 observer (避免把伺服器來的變更又回傳),在觀察閉包中存取 `eventCounter` 讓 Observation 追蹤,再呼叫 `processChanges()` 透過 `ModelContext.fetchHistory` 取得並上傳變更。總結:用 sections 客製 fetch、用 codable 儲存他人框架型別、用 ResultsObserver 在 SwiftUI 外反應查詢結果變化、用 HistoryObserver 反應 persistent history 變化。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: SwiftData 團隊工程師 **Thomas** 開場,介紹 Apple 2027 版本帶來的 SwiftData 新功能,並建議 SwiftData 新手先看 code-along「Add persistence with SwiftData」。他預告三大主題:用 `Query` 在 SwiftUI 視圖中分段擷取資料、在 model 中儲存自訂型別的強化,以及觀察 model 與 history 變化的全新 API。

deepdive.title: Sectioned fetching
deepdive.body: 以範例 app **SampleTrips** 說明 SwiftUI 與 SwiftData 的緊密整合:在視圖加上 `@Query` 即可擷取依 start date 排序的所有 trips 並用於 list。Thomas 提出需求 — 想把 trips 依目的地分組,讓同地點的旅行相鄰顯示,引出 Apple 2027 中 **Query 對 sectioning 的支援**。

deepdive.title: Sectioning your fetches
deepdive.body: 建立 sectioned query 只需把從 Trip model root 指向字串的 KeyPath 傳給 Query 新的 **`sectionBy`** 參數 (此處用 `\.destination`),wrapped value 仍是 `[Trip]`。要分段顯示時,透過底線前綴的 **`_trips`** 存取 query 的 `sections` 屬性,用 `ForEach` 走訪各 section,每個 section 的 **`id`** (即 KeyPath 對應值,如目的地) 當作 `Section` 標題,內層再以 `ForEach` 走訪該 section 的 trips 建立 `TripListItem`。

deepdive.title: Using custom types
deepdive.body: 聚焦於 SampleTrips 核心的 **Trip** model (含 name、destination、起訖日期)。Thomas 想加入 MapKit 找地點的功能,為每個 location 取得名稱、座標與 **MKMapItem.Identifier** 並存入 model,但加上這些屬性後啟動 app 會丟出 fatal error「Class property within Persisted Struct/Enum is not supported」,因為 SwiftData 載入時會自動為 model 產生 schema,而未標 `@Model` 的 class 無法被自動檢視。

deepdive.title: Using Codable
deepdive.body: 由於 `MKMapItem.Identifier` 來自 MapKit、無法修改或標 `@Model`,但它符合 **Codable**,Apple 2027 可將 attribute 標為 **`.codable`** 讓 SwiftData 委派序列化並儲存編碼表示 (示範 `@Attribute(.codable) var mapItemIdentifier`),app 即可正常啟動。需注意 codable 內容對 SwiftData 不透明:無法用於 **Predicate** 過濾或 **Sort Descriptor** 排序,型別結構變動也不觸發 migration (Codable 實作須前後相容)。它是儲存非自有型別的「逃生艙」,自有型別仍應建模為 SwiftData model 以享有排序、過濾與索引。

deepdive.title: Observing data stores with ResultsObserver
deepdive.body: 回顧 `@Query` 會在視圖出現時擷取資料並持續監看 store 變化使視圖重繪,但僅限 SwiftUI。Apple 2027 推出 **ResultsObserver**,如同 Query 般擷取並觀察 store,卻能在 app 任何地方運作 (獨立於 SwiftUI、甚至 SceneKit 遊戲),透過 **Swift Observation** 反應變化,並支援既有的 filtering、sorting 與 sectioning。講者以資料流圖說明:把 Query 換成 ResultsObserver、View 換成任意程式碼即可。

deepdive.title: // Use observation to update map bounds
deepdive.body: 示範用 **`MapCameraController`** 為地圖計算合適的 **`MapCameraBounds`**。它建立一個不帶 predicate 或 sectioning 的 `ResultsObserver<Trip, Never>` 以涵蓋所有 trips,並用 **`withContinuousObservation(options: [.didSet])`** 在每次 trip 變動時重算 bounds。回傳的 **ObservationTracking token** 存於 class 以維持整個生命週期的觀察;實際操作中刪除 Toronto 行程後,observer 偵測到變化並讓控制器重算地圖相機範圍。

deepdive.title: // Using HistoryObserver to sync with a server
deepdive.body: 對應到與外部伺服器同步的程式碼:`ServerSync` 以 **`HistoryObserver(authors: ["App"], modelContainer:)`** 建立 observer,只關注 app 自身的變更以避免把伺服器來的變更又回傳。它同樣用 `withContinuousObservation(options: .didSet)` 並把 token 存於 class,在觀察閉包中存取 **`eventCounter`** 讓 Swift Observation 知道要追蹤什麼,再呼叫 `processChanges()`。

deepdive.title: Observing history with HistoryObserver
deepdive.body: 先複習 SwiftData 在每次儲存時記錄 **history transaction** (含變更內容、來源 author 與唯一 token,可配合 `ModelContext.fetchHistory` 取得較新交易),並推薦觀看 WWDC 2024「Track Model Changes with SwiftData History」。新的 **HistoryObserver** 讓你輕鬆反應 persistent history 的新交易,可依 model 型別與 transaction author 過濾,其唯一可觀察屬性 **`eventCounter`** 在有新交易時遞增,程式碼可觀察它並用 `ModelContext.fetchHistory` 取得最新變更上傳伺服器。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: Thomas 總結四大新功能:用 **sections** 客製 SwiftData fetch、用 **codable** attribute 儲存來自其他框架的型別、用 **ResultsObserver** 在 SwiftUI 視圖外反應查詢結果變化,以及用 **HistoryObserver** 反應 SwiftData persistent history 的變化,並感謝觀看。

summary_en: SwiftData engineer Thomas introduces the new SwiftData features in Apple's 2027 releases, using **SampleTrips** — a long-running sample app for tracking planned adventures (SwiftData for persistence, SwiftUI for UI) — throughout. The first topic is **sectioned fetching**: `@Query` gains a `sectionBy` parameter that takes a KeyPath from the model root to a string (e.g. `\.destination`) to group results by that property. The query's wrapped value is still `[Trip]`, but the underscore-prefixed `_trips` exposes a `sections` property; combined with nested `ForEach` and `Section`, using each section's `id` (the KeyPath value) as the header, you get a list grouped by destination.

The second topic is storing custom types. The example wants to persist coordinates and an **MKMapItem.Identifier** from MapKit search in the Trip model, but because `MKMapItem.Identifier` is a class that can't be annotated `@Model` and can't be inspected by SwiftData, the app throws a fatal error at launch: 'Class property within Persisted Struct/Enum is not supported.' The fix is the new **`.codable` attribute** in Apple's 2027 releases: since the type conforms to **Codable**, marking the property `@Attribute(.codable)` tells SwiftData to delegate serialization and store the encoded representation. Note that codable contents are opaque to SwiftData — they can't be used in Predicates for filtering or Sort Descriptors for sorting, and shape changes won't trigger a migration — so it's an escape hatch for types you don't own, while your own types should be modeled as SwiftData models for sorting, filtering, and indexing.

The third topic is new APIs for observing data changes. `@Query` is great but limited to SwiftUI views; Apple's 2027 releases introduce **ResultsObserver**, which works anywhere in your app (outside SwiftUI, even a SceneKit game), supports the same filtering, sorting, and sectioning, and reacts to changes via **Swift Observation**. The example has a `MapCameraController` hold a `ResultsObserver<Trip, Never>`, using `withContinuousObservation(options: [.didSet])` to recalculate the map's `MapCameraBounds` whenever a trip changes, and stores the returned **ObservationTracking token** on the class to keep the observation alive.

Finally, **HistoryObserver**. Every save records a history transaction (with what changed, the source author, and a unique token), useful for syncing with external servers or reacting to changes made outside the app such as in an app extension. HistoryObserver makes it easy to react to new transactions in the persistent history and can filter by model type and transaction author; it has a single observable property, **eventCounter**, which increments when new transactions arrive. The example's `ServerSync` creates the observer with `authors: ["App"]` (to avoid replaying server-originated changes back to the server), accesses `eventCounter` inside the observation closure so Observation tracks it, and calls `processChanges()` to fetch and upload via `ModelContext.fetchHistory`. The takeaways: tailor fetches with sections, store other frameworks' types with codable, react to query-result changes outside SwiftUI with ResultsObserver, and react to persistent-history changes with HistoryObserver.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: SwiftData engineer **Thomas** opens by introducing the new SwiftData features in Apple's 2027 releases and recommends newcomers watch the code-along 'Add persistence with SwiftData' first. He previews three topics: fetching data in sections with `Query` in SwiftUI views, enhancements for storing custom types in your model, and new APIs for observing model and history changes.

deepdive_en.title: Sectioned fetching
deepdive_en.body: Using the sample app **SampleTrips**, Thomas shows how tightly SwiftUI and SwiftData integrate: adding `@Query` to a view fetches all trips sorted by start date for use in a list. He motivates the need to group trips by destination so trips to the same place appear together, introducing **Query's support for sectioning** in Apple's 2027 releases.

deepdive_en.title: Sectioning your fetches
deepdive_en.body: Creating a sectioned query just means passing a KeyPath from the Trip model root to a string into Query's new **`sectionBy`** parameter (here `\.destination`); the wrapped value is still `[Trip]`. To display sections, access the query's `sections` property via the underscore-prefixed **`_trips`**, iterate with `ForEach`, use each section's **`id`** (the KeyPath value, e.g. destination) as the `Section` header, and use an inner `ForEach` over the section's trips to build a `TripListItem` for each.

deepdive_en.title: Using custom types
deepdive_en.body: The focus turns to SampleTrips' central **Trip** model (name, destination, start/end dates). Thomas wants to add MapKit location lookup, storing each location's name, coordinates, and **MKMapItem.Identifier** in the model, but adding these properties makes the app throw the fatal error 'Class property within Persisted Struct/Enum is not supported,' because SwiftData auto-generates a schema at load time and can't inspect classes not annotated with `@Model`.

deepdive_en.title: Using Codable
deepdive_en.body: Since `MKMapItem.Identifier` comes from MapKit and can't be modified or marked `@Model` but conforms to **Codable**, Apple's 2027 releases let you mark an attribute **`.codable`** so SwiftData delegates serialization and stores the encoded representation (demoed as `@Attribute(.codable) var mapItemIdentifier`), letting the app launch cleanly. Keep in mind codable contents are opaque to SwiftData: they can't be used in **Predicates** for filtering or **Sort Descriptors** for sorting, and shape changes don't trigger a migration (the Codable implementation must be forward- and backward-compatible). It's an escape hatch for types you don't own; model your own types as SwiftData models to get sorting, filtering, and indexing.

deepdive_en.title: Observing data stores with ResultsObserver
deepdive_en.body: Recapping that `@Query` fetches when the view appears and continuously monitors the store to re-render the view, but only in SwiftUI. Apple's 2027 releases introduce **ResultsObserver**, which fetches and observes the store like Query but works anywhere in your app (independent of SwiftUI, even a SceneKit game), reacting to changes via **Swift Observation** and supporting the same filtering, sorting, and sectioning. The presenter shows the data-flow diagram with Query replaced by ResultsObserver and the View replaced by any code you like.

deepdive_en.title: // Use observation to update map bounds
deepdive_en.body: The demo uses a **`MapCameraController`** to compute fitting **`MapCameraBounds`** for a map. It creates a `ResultsObserver<Trip, Never>` with no predicate or sectioning to cover all trips, and uses **`withContinuousObservation(options: [.didSet])`** to recalculate the bounds whenever a trip changes. The returned **ObservationTracking token** is stored on the class to keep the observation alive for its lifetime; deleting the Toronto trip in the demo triggers the observer and recalculates the map camera bounds.

deepdive_en.title: // Using HistoryObserver to sync with a server
deepdive_en.body: This corresponds to syncing with an external server: `ServerSync` creates an observer with **`HistoryObserver(authors: ["App"], modelContainer:)`**, interested only in the app's own changes so it doesn't replay server-originated changes back to the server. Like the camera controller it uses `withContinuousObservation(options: .didSet)` and stores the token on the class, accessing **`eventCounter`** inside the closure so Swift Observation knows what to track before calling `processChanges()`.

deepdive_en.title: Observing history with HistoryObserver
deepdive_en.body: A quick recap that SwiftData records a **history transaction** on each save (with what changed, the source author, and a unique token usable with `ModelContext.fetchHistory` to fetch newer transactions), with a pointer to WWDC 2024's 'Track Model Changes with SwiftData History.' The new **HistoryObserver** makes it easy to react to new transactions in the persistent history, can filter by model type and transaction author, and exposes a single observable property, **`eventCounter`**, which increments when new transactions arrive so code can observe it and use `ModelContext.fetchHistory` to fetch and upload the latest changes.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Thomas summarizes the four new features: tailor SwiftData fetches with **sections**, use **codable** attributes to store types from other frameworks, use **ResultsObserver** to react to query-result changes outside SwiftUI views, and use **HistoryObserver** to react to changes in SwiftData's persistent history, then thanks the audience.

title: Code-along: Add persistence with SwiftData
gloss: 程式碼實作：用 SwiftData 加入持久化
takeaway: 跟著實作把現有 App 加上 SwiftData 持久化：以 @Model 定義模型與關聯，再用 @Query 在 SwiftUI 中動態查詢資料。

Enable interoperability between your schema and SwiftUI views

Search for trips and activities by name
Capture and report errors from ActivityItemView

points.text: 跟著實作為現有 App 加上持久化：用 **@Model** 把 Activity、Trip 等類別轉成持久化模型。
以 **@Relationship**（含 deleteRule 與 inverse）定義 Trip、TripImage、Activity 之間的關聯。
在 SwiftUI 中用 **@Query** 搭配 **#Predicate** 與 **FetchDescriptor** 動態查詢、排序與限制筆數，並支援依名稱搜尋。

audience: **想為 SwiftUI App 加入本地持久化**、正要上手或深入 SwiftData 的開發者。
gloss_en: Code-along: Add persistence with SwiftData
takeaway_en: Follow along to add SwiftData persistence to an existing app: define models and relationships with @Model, then query data dynamically in SwiftUI with @Query.

points_en.text: Follow along to add persistence to an existing app: use **@Model** to turn classes like Activity and Trip into persistent models.
Use **@Relationship** (including deleteRule and inverse) to define the relationships between Trip, TripImage, and Activity.
In SwiftUI, use **@Query** with **#Predicate** and **FetchDescriptor** to dynamically query, sort, and limit results, with support for searching by name.
Use **ModelContainer** to configure the container and seed data, and catch and report save errors in the view.
Use **withContinuousObservation** to observe property changes, update dateEdited, and handle side effects in tandem.

audience_en: **Developers who want to add local persistence to a SwiftUI app** and are just getting started with or going deeper into SwiftData.
summary: 這場 code-along 由 SwiftData 工程師 Matthew Turk 主講，以一個名為 Wishlist 的旅遊清單 app 為範例，示範如何把原本只存在記憶體裡的動態資料，改造成跨 Apple 平台、可永久保存的持久層。原始 app 透過 SwiftUI environment 注入一個 **DataSource** 類別，所有 trip、goal、搜尋結果都在記憶體中即時過濾與排序;這對小範例可行,但會持續占用 RAM,而且 app 一關閉、新增的資料就全部消失,回到預載內容。SwiftData 正是為解決這類問題而生:把 app 狀態連到持久化儲存,並透過 **ModelContext** 來存取。

改造的第一步是辨識相關狀態(trip collections、goal 狀態、搜尋結果),並把這些資料型別重構成 SwiftData 的 schema。具體做法是 import SwiftData,把 **@Observable** 換成 **@Model**(SwiftData 會自動產生 observable conformance)。過程中要逐一修正編譯錯誤:`creationDate` 必須改成 `var` 才能由資料庫填值、所有 model 屬性都必須是 **Codable** 才能序列化成資料庫欄位。原本以 enum 定義的 **Goal** 因為是封閉值集合,無法當持久 model,要改成 class,並用 SwiftData 的 **model inheritance** 拆出 TripGoal 與 ActivityGoal 子類別。

接著定義 model 之間的關係。每個 Trip 對多個 Activity 屬於 to-many relationship,以宣告陣列加上 **@Relationship(deleteRule: .cascade)** 來表達,刪除 trip 時連帶清掉其 activities。圖片處理也重新設計:用 `thumbnailData` 把低解析縮圖以原始 bytes 內嵌資料庫,完整解析圖則透過 external file reference 存成獨立的 **TripImage** model。由於 SwiftUI view 可直接綁定 SwiftData model,TripEditModel 與 DataSource 等檔案得以刪除,移除了數百行狀態管理、儲存、過濾、排序與搜尋的程式碼。

view 層則改用 **@Query** 搭配 **#Predicate**,等同於對 model context 呼叫 fetch,但能在結果變動時自動更新 UI。講者強調用 predicate 在資料庫端就篩選(像直接請圖書館員只拿你要的書),比起把全部抓回來再丟掉,能在記憶體與磁碟 I/O 間取得最佳平衡;查詢可在 view 的 initializer 內依參數動態建構(如 TripCollectionView 依季節、SearchResultsListView 依搜尋字串)。最後以 view modifier 捕捉並呈現執行期錯誤(如磁碟空間不足),並用 2027 版本新增的 **withContinuousObservation**(Continuous Observation)重新讓 `dateEdited` 即時更新,取代與 SwiftData 不相容的 didSet property observers。整體 takeaway:先設計出 app 狀態的恰當表示並宣告 Model schema,再用 predicate 寫精準查詢平衡記憶體與儲存,並持續調整 SwiftUI view 以與 SwiftData 達到最佳互通。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: 由 SwiftData 團隊工程師 **Matthew Turk** 開場,目標是把現有 SwiftUI app 的動態資料連到跨 Apple 平台的現代持久層。範例 app **Wishlist** 用清單管理旅遊計畫,把 trips 分成各季節主題的 collection。影片會逐步走過專案檔案,辨識可做為 model 與 schema 的型別,定義 model 間關係,並以效能、互通性與擴充性為考量更新 view。

deepdive.title: Identify relevant state
deepdive.body: 示範現有資料流:view 透過 SwiftUI environment 取得 **DataSource**,所有 trip、goal、搜尋結果都在記憶體中即時過濾排序。問題在於這仰賴 RAM 處理與儲存,並非穩定的保存位置——關閉 app 再開,新增的 "Northern Lights" trip 就消失、重設回預載內容。這正是 **SwiftData** 透過 model context 連到持久儲存所要解決的問題。

deepdive.title: Define your schemas
deepdive.body: 確立相關狀態(trip collections、goal 狀態、搜尋結果)後,下一步是在程式碼中找到這些資料結構,並重構成帶 SwiftData schema 的 model。這會為後續用持久化的 **ModelContext** 取代記憶體中的 DataSource、進而寫出高效資料庫查詢來驅動 view 鋪路。

deepdive.title: Convert Activity to a persistent model with @Model
deepdive.body: 以 **Activity** 為例,持久化第一步是 import SwiftData 並把 **@Observable** 換成 **@Model**,SwiftData 會自動產生 observable conformance。講者也指出 name 與 isComplete 上的 didSet observers 會在屬性變動時更新 `dateEdited`,但 property observer 與 computed property 不一定相容,因此先移除這些 didSet 區塊、保留 dateEdited,稍後再用別的技術補回。

deepdive.title: Add Codable conformance to TripCollection
deepdive.body: 輪到 **Trip** class,同樣 import SwiftData 並換 macro。檢視編譯錯誤:`creationDate` 必須改成 **var**,SwiftData 才能在執行期以資料庫載入的值填入;另一錯誤指出所有 model 屬性都必須 **Codable**,因為 SwiftData 要把屬性序列化成資料庫欄位。於是跳到 **TripCollection** 宣告處明確加上 Codable conformance,讓季節主題能納入 schema 並持久化。

deepdive.title: Define model relationships
deepdive.body: 說明 goal tracking:原本 **Goal** 是 enum,因 enum 定義的是封閉值集合而無法做持久 model,須改成可儲存屬性、可任意實例化的 **class**。重新設計後保留 name、kind、targetCount,並新增 `completedCount` 與 `isComplete` 儲存屬性(達標時存 true),方便日後查詢時區分已完成與待完成 goal。再以 **model inheritance** 把 kind 的差異拆成 **TripGoal** 與 **ActivityGoal** 子類別。

deepdive.title: Set up model relationships between Trip, TripImage, and Activity
deepdive.body: 把原本用 dictionary 與迴圈近似的 to-many 關係,改成正式的 model relationship:在 Trip 宣告 activities 陣列並加上 **@Relationship(deleteRule: .cascade, inverse: \Activity.trip)**,刪 trip 時連帶清除其 activities。圖片方面新增 `thumbnailData` 內嵌低解析縮圖原始 bytes,完整圖則以 external file reference 存成獨立的 **TripImage** model;photoURL 經 refactor 重新命名為 photo,並以 multi-cursor 一次更新多個檔案。

deepdive.title: Enable interoperability between your schema and SwiftUI views
deepdive.body: 因為 SwiftUI view 能直接綁定 SwiftData model 並即時傳遞編輯,**TripEditModel** 已無存在必要;DataSource 的所有職責也由 ModelContext、query 與 relationship 自動處理,可直接刪除。講者強調這一步移除了專案中數百行的狀態管理、儲存、過濾、排序、關係走訪與搜尋程式碼。

deepdive.title: Update the view layer
deepdive.body: schema 與 model container 就位後,自動儲存預設啟用。接下來要為每個呈現 model 的子 view 加上精準、針對性的查詢,再用 SwiftUI view modifier 捕捉與呈現執行期可能發生的錯誤(如磁碟空間不足或不支援的 predicate),最後補回缺少的 property observer 讓 UI 事件正確傳遞資料與副作用。WindowGroup 上的 **.modelContainer** scene modifier 則告訴 SwiftUI 採用新 schema。

deepdive.title: Fetch achieved and upcoming goals
deepdive.body: 對比兩種取資料方式:抓全部 goal 再丟掉不要的,記憶體用得少但 I/O 多(像請圖書館員把每本書都搬來);用 **#Predicate** 則像事先告訴館員你要什麼,只取所需。在 GoalsView 中 import SwiftData,把 dataSource environment 換成兩個 **@Query**:一個依 dateAchieved 反向排序抓已達成 goal,另一個抓剩餘的待完成 goal,並能在結果變動時自動更新 view。

deepdive.title: Fetch recent trips
deepdive.body: 同樣的概念套用到 **RecentTripsPageView**:import SwiftData,以 **@Query** 搭配 FetchDescriptor 取代 dataSource,依 creationDate 反向排序並設 `fetchLimit: 5`,取得最近 5 筆 trip 直接餵進 ForEach。這展示 SwiftData 如何以針對性查詢取代全域變數、降低持續的記憶體占用。

deepdive.title: Dynamically construct a query in the initializer of TripCollectionView
deepdive.body: **TripCollectionView** 要依季節分段 trip,每個 tripCollection 對應一個 view 實例,但 view 在 init 前並不知道要顯示哪個季節,因此先宣告 query 再於 initializer 內動態建構。重點是 predicate 直接從 initializer 捕捉 tripCollection 參數,於送往資料庫前完成過濾,結果再進入 ForEach。

deepdive.title: Search for trips and activities by name
deepdive.body: 第三個分頁的 **SearchResultsListView** 由上層 view 持有搜尋欄與文字並傳入 initializer。同樣把 dataSource 換成 query 宣告,依參數建構 predicate:搜尋字串為空時 fallback 抓最近 3 筆 trip;否則以 `localizedStandardContains` 比對 trip 與隸屬於 trip 的 activity 名稱並排序。List 的 overlay 則改用 `trips.isEmpty` 與 `activities.isEmpty` 直接判斷,無結果時顯示 **ContentUnavailableView**。

deepdive.title: Capture and report errors from ActivityItemView
deepdive.body: **ActivityItemView** 的 `updateGoalAchievements` 會在使用者完成 activity 時更新進度且可能丟出錯誤。講者把錯誤捕捉到 state 變數,送進 telemetry 系統以利日後改進 app,並在合理時以 **.alert** 呈現,告知使用者如何從錯誤中恢復。這處理了持久層的錯誤案例。

deepdive.title: Update dateEdited and propagate side effects on property changes
deepdive.body: 重現先前移除 didSet 造成的 bug:依 "Date Edited" 排序時勾選 activity,卻不會移到最上方。改用 2027 版本 Observation 框架新增的 **withContinuousObservation** 在 ActivityItemView 的 initializer 設定觀察:當 name 或 isComplete 改變時更新 `dateEdited`,觸發 query 自動更新清單;同時順帶更新 Trip 的 `isComplete`——當所有 activity 都完成時整個 trip 視為完成。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 總結整套流程:先思考 app 狀態的恰當表示並宣告構成 schema 的 **Model** 型別,接著用 predicate 寫針對性查詢來平衡記憶體與磁碟儲存,並持續調整 SwiftUI view 以與 SwiftData 達到最佳互通。講者最後勾掉今天的最後一項 activity、贏得 badge 作結。

summary_en: In this code-along, SwiftData engineer Matthew Turk uses a travel-planning app called Wishlist to show how to take in-memory, dynamic SwiftUI data and turn it into a persistent layer that works across all of Apple's platforms. The original app injects a **DataSource** class through the SwiftUI environment, filtering and sorting every trip, goal, and search result in memory on demand. That works for a small example but keeps an elevated memory footprint and, crucially, loses any newly added data the moment the app closes, resetting to preinstalled content. This is precisely the problem **SwiftData** solves by connecting app state to persistent storage via a **ModelContext**.

The first step is to identify the relevant state (trip collections, goal statuses, search results) and refactor those types into SwiftData schemas. Concretely, you import SwiftData and replace **@Observable** with **@Model** (SwiftData auto-generates observable conformance). Build errors guide the rest: `creationDate` must become a `var` so the database can populate it, and every model property must be **Codable** to be serialized into columns. The enum-based **Goal** can't be a persistent model because an enum is a closed set of values, so it becomes a class, and **model inheritance** splits it into TripGoal and ActivityGoal subclasses.

Next come relationships. Each Trip-to-many-Activity is a to-many relationship, declared as an array annotated with **@Relationship(deleteRule: .cascade)** so deleting a trip cascades to its activities. Image handling is redesigned too: `thumbnailData` inlines a low-resolution thumbnail's raw bytes in the database, while the full-resolution image is stored as an external file reference behind a dedicated **TripImage** model. Because SwiftUI views bind directly to SwiftData models, files like TripEditModel and DataSource are deleted, removing hundreds of lines of state management, storage, filtering, sorting, and search code.

The view layer then switches to **@Query** with **#Predicate**, equivalent to calling fetch on a model context but auto-updating the UI when results change. Turk stresses filtering at the database with a predicate (like asking a librarian only for the books you want) to balance memory against disk I/O, and shows queries built dynamically in a view's initializer (by season in TripCollectionView, by search text in SearchResultsListView). Finally, view modifiers capture and surface runtime errors like low disk space, and the new **withContinuousObservation** (Continuous Observation, added in the 2027 releases) restores live `dateEdited` updates that the SwiftData-incompatible didSet observers used to provide. The takeaway: model your state into a proper schema, write targeted predicate-based queries to balance memory and storage, and keep tuning SwiftUI views for interoperability with SwiftData.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: SwiftData engineer **Matthew Turk** opens with the goal of connecting an existing SwiftUI app's dynamic data to a modern, cross-platform persistence layer. The sample app **Wishlist** organizes travel plans in lists, grouping trips into seasonal collections. The video walks the project files to identify types for models and schemas, define relationships between them, and update the views with an eye toward performance, interoperability, and extensibility.

deepdive_en.title: Identify relevant state
deepdive_en.body: The current data flow is demoed: views pull a **DataSource** from the SwiftUI environment, and all trips, goals, and search results are filtered and sorted in memory on demand. The problem is that this relies on RAM for both processing and storage, which isn't stable—close and relaunch the app and the new "Northern Lights" trip is gone, reset to preinstalled content. This is exactly what **SwiftData** addresses by connecting state to persistent storage through a model context.

deepdive_en.title: Define your schemas
deepdive_en.body: Having identified the relevant state (trip collections, goal statuses, search results), the next move is to find where those data structures live in the code and refactor them as models with SwiftData schemas. This sets up replacing the in-memory DataSource with a persistent **ModelContext** to drive the views with efficient database queries.

deepdive_en.title: Convert Activity to a persistent model with @Model
deepdive_en.body: Using **Activity** as the example, the first persistence step is to import SwiftData and replace **@Observable** with **@Model**; SwiftData auto-generates observable conformance. Turk notes the didSet observers on name and isComplete that update `dateEdited`, but since property observers and computed properties aren't always compatible, he removes the didSet blocks for now (leaving dateEdited) and restores the behavior later with a different technique.

deepdive_en.title: Add Codable conformance to TripCollection
deepdive_en.body: The **Trip** class is next—same import-and-swap-macro treatment. Build errors reveal that `creationDate` must become a **var** so SwiftData can populate it at runtime from the database, and that all model properties must be **Codable** so SwiftData can serialize them into columns. He jumps to the **TripCollection** declaration and adds Codable conformance explicitly so the trip's seasonal theme is included in the schema and persisted.

deepdive_en.title: Define model relationships
deepdive_en.body: Goal tracking is explained: **Goal** was an enum, but because an enum defines a closed set of values it can't be a persistent model—it needs to be a **class** that stores properties and can be instantiated freely. The redesign keeps name, kind, and targetCount and adds stored `completedCount` and `isComplete` (true once the target is met), which helps later when querying to separate completed from upcoming goals. **Model inheritance** then splits the kind differences into **TripGoal** and **ActivityGoal** subclasses.

deepdive_en.title: Set up model relationships between Trip, TripImage, and Activity
deepdive_en.body: The to-many relationships previously approximated with dictionaries and loops become proper model relationships: Trip declares an activities array annotated with **@Relationship(deleteRule: .cascade, inverse: \Activity.trip)** so deleting a trip clears its activities. For images, a new `thumbnailData` inlines low-resolution raw bytes in the database, while the full image is stored via an external file reference behind a dedicated **TripImage** model; photoURL is refactor-renamed to photo, updating multiple files at once with multi-cursor editing.

deepdive_en.title: Enable interoperability between your schema and SwiftUI views
deepdive_en.body: Because SwiftUI views bind directly to SwiftData models and propagate edits in real time, **TripEditModel** is no longer needed; DataSource's responsibilities are all handled automatically by ModelContext, queries, and relationships, so both can be deleted. Turk highlights that this step removes hundreds of lines of state management, storage, filtering, sorting, relationship traversal, and search code.

deepdive_en.title: Update the view layer
deepdive_en.body: With the schemas and model container in place, automatic saving is enabled by default. Next, each subview that presents models gets efficient, targeted queries; SwiftUI view modifiers then capture and surface possible runtime errors like low disk capacity or unsupported predicates; and finally, missing property observers are added back so UI events propagate the right data and side effects. The **.modelContainer** scene modifier on WindowGroup tells SwiftUI to use the new schema.

deepdive_en.title: Fetch achieved and upcoming goals
deepdive_en.body: Two fetching approaches are contrasted: fetching all goals then discarding the irrelevant ones uses less memory but incurs more I/O (like asking a librarian to grab every book), whereas using a **#Predicate** is like asking upfront for exactly what you want. In GoalsView, import SwiftData and replace the dataSource environment with two **@Query** declarations—one fetching achieved goals sorted by dateAchieved in reverse, the other fetching the remaining upcoming goals—both auto-updating the view when results change.

deepdive_en.title: Fetch recent trips
deepdive_en.body: The same idea applies to **RecentTripsPageView**: import SwiftData and replace dataSource with an **@Query** using a FetchDescriptor that sorts by creationDate in reverse with `fetchLimit: 5`, yielding the five most recent trips fed straight into a ForEach. This demonstrates how SwiftData replaces global variables with targeted queries that reduce ongoing memory use.

deepdive_en.title: Dynamically construct a query in the initializer of TripCollectionView
deepdive_en.body: **TripCollectionView** segments trips by season, with one view instance per tripCollection, but the view doesn't know which season it'll show until initialized—so the query is declared and then constructed dynamically in the initializer. The key point is that the predicate captures the tripCollection parameter directly from the initializer before heading to the database, with results flowing into the ForEach.

deepdive_en.title: Search for trips and activities by name
deepdive_en.body: The third tab's **SearchResultsListView** receives the search field and text from its superview's initializer. Again dataSource is replaced with query declarations whose predicates are built from the parameters: an empty search string falls back to the three most recent trips, otherwise it matches trip names and trip-owned activity names with `localizedStandardContains` and sorts them. The List's overlay uses direct `trips.isEmpty` and `activities.isEmpty` checks to show a **ContentUnavailableView** when there are no results.

deepdive_en.title: Capture and report errors from ActivityItemView
deepdive_en.body: **ActivityItemView**'s `updateGoalAchievements` updates progress as people complete activities and can throw errors. Turk captures those errors in a state variable, passes them to a telemetry system to improve the app, and—when reasonable—presents an **.alert** letting people know how to recover. That handles the persistence layer's error case.

deepdive_en.title: Update dateEdited and propagate side effects on property changes
deepdive_en.body: The bug from removing didSet is reproduced: sorting by "Date Edited" and checking off an activity doesn't move it to the top. The fix uses **withContinuousObservation**, added to the Observation framework in the 2027 releases, set up in ActivityItemView's initializer: whenever name or isComplete changes, it updates `dateEdited`, triggering the query to refresh the list; it also updates the Trip's `isComplete` as a side effect when all activities are complete.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: The workflow is summarized: start by considering the appropriate representation of your app's state and declaring the **Model** types that make up your schema, then write targeted queries using predicates to balance memory use against on-disk storage, and stay current on adjusting SwiftUI views for optimal interoperability with SwiftData. Turk closes by checking off the day's last activity and earning his badge.

title: WidgetKit foundations
gloss: WidgetKit 基礎入門
takeaway: 掌握 WidgetKit 的基本概念，從 StaticConfiguration、支援尺寸、深層連結到隨系統調整的著色渲染模式，打造融入系統的 Widget。

points.text: 以 **StaticConfiguration** 搭配 provider 與 SwiftUI 視圖建立 Widget，並用 **containerBackground** 設定背景。
透過 **supportedFamilies** 宣告支援的 Widget 尺寸，例如 systemMedium。
使用 **widgetURL** 加入深層連結，讓使用者點按 Widget 直接進入 App 對應內容。
搭配 **widgetAccentedRenderingMode** 控制著色渲染模式，使 Widget 隨系統外觀調整。

audience: 適合**第一次開發 Widget、想學會 WidgetKit 基礎的 SwiftUI 開發者**。
gloss_en: WidgetKit foundations
takeaway_en: Master the basics of WidgetKit—from StaticConfiguration, supported sizes, and deep links to accented rendering that adapts to the system—to build widgets that blend into the system.

points_en.text: Build a widget with **StaticConfiguration** together with a provider and a SwiftUI view, and set the background using **containerBackground**.
Declare the widget sizes you support, such as systemMedium, via **supportedFamilies**.
Use **widgetURL** to add a deep link so tapping the widget takes the user directly to the corresponding content in your app.
Use **widgetAccentedRenderingMode** to control the accented rendering mode so the widget adapts to the system appearance.

audience_en: Ideal for **SwiftUI developers building a widget for the first time who want to learn the WidgetKit foundations**.
summary: 本場由系統體驗團隊工程師 Jonathan Long 主講，從零開始介紹 **WidgetKit** 的基礎觀念與第一個 widget 的建構流程。Widget 之所以令人印象深刻有三個特質：**glanceable**（一眼可懂）、**relevant**（內容隨時間、習慣與位置而相關）以及 **personalizable**（可依個人喜好設定）。無論 app 是用 SwiftUI 或 UIKit 開發，widget 本身都以 SwiftUI 建構，並透過獨立的 **widget extension** 行程提供給系統。由於 extension 與主 app 是分離的行程，必須透過 **app group** 的 shared container（例如共享資料庫或 user defaults）來傳遞資料。

Widget 的內容核心是 **timeline**，由多個 **timeline entry** 組成，每個 entry 攜帶在特定時間點渲染畫面所需的資料。講者以讀書會 app 的 reading goals widget 為例，說明 widget 的兩種設定方式：可由使用者設定的 **AppIntentConfiguration**，以及最單純、自動帶入目前書籍的 **StaticConfiguration**。StaticConfiguration 需要 kind（唯一識別碼）、timeline provider 與回傳 View 的 closure，並以 **containerBackground** modifier 標示背景，讓系統在著色或透明 tint 環境下能替換為玻璃材質。Timeline provider 須提供三種狀態：snapshot（gallery 預覽）、placeholder（同步、不需資料的暫位畫面，常用 SwiftUI 的 redacted modifier）以及 timeline entry。

Timeline 的更新由 **reload policy** 決定，分為 **atEnd**（entry 用盡時重載，適合 reading goals widget）、**afterDate**（指定特定時間重載，適合 reading schedule widget）以及 **never**（不自動重載，適合只在互動後更新的 reading log widget，可用 WidgetCenter 的 reload API 或 push notification 觸發）。最佳實務包括盡量提供多筆 entry、留意系統會依使用習慣分配更新預算（budget）並節流前景的頻繁重載。需要密集更新與提醒能力的短暫內容（如體育賽事）則應改用 **Live Activities**。

後半段聚焦於整合與適應。透過 **supportedFamilies** modifier 可支援多種尺寸（包含 macOS、iOS、iPadOS 27 新增的 system extra large portrait），iOS widget 也能出現在 CarPlay 與 macOS remote widget。整合手段包括 **widgetURL** 做 deep link、以 App Intents 做可設定 widget、以及用 button 與 toggle 加入互動元素（透過 App Intent 由系統代為執行）。最後強調要在 full color、tinted 與 clear 等各種環境測試 widget；當 accented rendering mode 無法正確著色圖片時（如書封變成白色方塊），可用 **widgetAccentedRenderingMode(.fullColor)** 保留原始色彩。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: 由系統體驗團隊工程師 **Jonathan Long** 開場，說明 widget 能在使用者最常造訪的便利位置提供相關內容，並橫跨 iOS、iPadOS、watchOS、visionOS 與 macOS 等多個平台。本場將涵蓋 **WidgetKit** 的基礎、如何建構第一個 widget、如何更好地整合 app 與 widget，以及如何在系統環境（如 tinted 環境）改變時讓 widget 自動適應。

deepdive.title: Fundamentals
