These focused intents exist only for tests: they create exactly the data a test needs (no leftover state causing flakiness), jump directly to any view without UI navigation, and can even wrap functionality you **haven't yet adopted App Intents** for (internal navigation, data management, state manipulation) to test it through AppIntentsTesting.

deepdive_en.title: Make an intent test-only
deepdive_en.body: The recipe: mark the intent `static let isDiscoverable = false` (so the system never exposes it anywhere) and wrap it in an `#if DEBUG` compiler directive (so only tests can access it). The example is **SeedSampleEventsIntent** from the earlier string-query test, which creates a known set of events in the calendar.

deepdive_en.title: Testing Spotlight indexing
deepdive_en.body: The session moves to system integrations beyond the app. **Spotlight** lets people search the whole system from one place; once entities are indexed they appear in results without opening the app. The scenario—a commander urgently asking when the Dark Matter Symposium is, but Spotlight surfaces nothing—exposes a bug: indexing code was commented out during development and never re-enabled, undetected because the app's behavior didn't change. The fix is to uncomment it, plus a test to prevent recurrence.

deepdive_en.title: Test Spotlight indexing
deepdive_en.body: The regression test uses `spotlightQuery("Supernova Viewing Party")` to talk to Spotlight: first assert the result is empty, then create the event with **CreateEventIntent**, then query again and assert exactly one result with a matching title. Once passing, it runs on every commit and will immediately catch any future break in the Spotlight integration.

deepdive_en.title: Testing view annotations
deepdive_en.body: A **view annotation** tells the system which entity your view is currently showing, so **Siri** can understand what's on screen and act on it. CometCal reports the on-screen **EventEntity** every time you navigate to an event, so even when a wormhole yanks the phone away you can ask "Siri, what time is this event?". If the annotation is broken, Siri has no idea—motivating the bug to fix.

deepdive_en.title: Test view annotations
deepdive_en.body: The test navigates to an event with **OpenEventIntent**, and because it lives in an XCUITest bundle uses **XCUI Automation** (`app.staticTexts[...]` with `waitForExistence`) to confirm the right event renders. It then calls `viewAnnotations()` to retrieve the on-screen annotations the system reports, asserts there is exactly one, and uses the ViewAnnotation's `entity` property with dynamic member lookup to assert the title. The test first fails; in EventDetailView the bug is that the **calendar id was used as the identifier**—changed to the event id, the test passes and Siri can correctly answer the event's time and location.

deepdive_en.title: The App Intents testing workflow
deepdive_en.body: An overview of folding AppIntentsTesting into your workflow: first implement the foundational types—actions, data, queries—and write AppIntentsTesting coverage for them as **unit tests** for your App Intents integration; then integrate more deeply with the system (annotate views, donate to Spotlight, pass data between apps) and cover those as **integration tests**. With coverage at every layer, still test manually with **Siri** and **Shortcuts** to experience the intents as people would.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: The wrap-up: **AppIntentsTesting** is a single framework for testing your intents, entities, enums, queries, and system integrations—all out-of-process and automated. The speaker encourages downloading the **CometCal** sample project to try it and explore the full test suite, consulting the documentation for the complete API, and points to a talk on building Siri experiences with App Intents.

title: Best practices for integrating visual intelligence in your app
gloss: 在 App 中整合視覺智慧的最佳實務
takeaway: 用 **Visual Intelligence** 搭配 App Intents 與 Vision 特徵比對，讓使用者以相機影像在你的 App 中探索內容。
chapters: Define the content you want to return as an App Entity
Build a catalog of albums with precomputed feature prints
Search the catalog for albums matching the captured image
Create an open intent to land users on the right screen
Use UnionValue to return multiple visual search result types
Expand the IntentValueQuery to return the UnionValue
Provide a link to in-app search
Request calendar access and fetch upcoming concerts
Filter for upcoming events that match known artists in our catalog

points.text: 把可回傳的內容定義成 **`AppEntity`**，並用 `IntentValueQuery` 接收 `SemanticContentDescriptor` 回傳視覺搜尋結果。
以 Vision 的 `GenerateImageFeaturePrintRequest` 預先計算**特徵指紋（feature print）**，再用 `distance(to:)` 比對拍攝影像。
用 `OpenIntent` 讓搜尋結果直接開啟到正確畫面，並用 `@UnionValue` 回傳多種結果類型（如專輯與演唱會）。
透過 `@AppIntent(schema: .visualIntelligence.semanticContentSearch)` 提供「**在 App 中繼續搜尋**」的入口。
整合系統 store 與 **EventKit**，請求行事曆權限抓取演唱會並監聽 `EKEventStoreChanged` 更新。

audience: **想讓 App 內容能透過相機與視覺智慧被探索**的 iOS／iPad／Mac 開發者。
gloss_en: Best practices for integrating visual intelligence in your app
takeaway_en: Use **Visual Intelligence** together with App Intents and Vision feature matching to let users discover content in your app from camera imagery.

points_en.text: Define returnable content as an **`AppEntity`**, and use `IntentValueQuery` to receive a `SemanticContentDescriptor` and return visual search results.
Precompute a **feature print** with Vision's `GenerateImageFeaturePrintRequest`, then compare it against the captured image using `distance(to:)`.
Use `OpenIntent` to open search results directly to the right screen, and `@UnionValue` to return multiple result types (such as albums and concerts).
Provide a "**continue searching in the app**" entry point via `@AppIntent(schema: .visualIntelligence.semanticContentSearch)`.
Integrate the system store with **EventKit**, requesting calendar access to fetch concerts and listening for `EKEventStoreChanged` updates.

audience_en: iOS/iPad/Mac developers who want **their app's content to be discoverable through the camera and visual intelligence**.
summary: 本場由 System Experience 團隊的 ML 工程師 David 主講，示範如何讓你的 App 接入 **Visual Intelligence**。今年除了新增加入聯絡人、儲存多筆行事曆事件、醫療裝置讀數記錄等能力，更把 Visual Intelligence 帶到 iPadOS 與 macOS。主講以一款音樂探索 App 為例：使用者只要對專輯封面拍照或截圖、按下「反白搜尋」，就能在 Visual Intelligence 裡看到比對到的專輯與相關演唱會，甚至擷取演唱會貼文後自動把事件加進行事曆，再回到 App 中看到對應內容。

整合的核心建立在 **App Intents** 與 **VisualIntelligence** 兩個框架之上，分四步走。首先把要回傳的內容定義成 **App Entity**（例如 AlbumEntity），並透過 displayRepresentation 提供標題、副標與縮圖，因為結果列只有約三行文字與一張縮圖的空間。接著實作 **IntentValueQuery**，它的 values(for:) 會收到系統傳來、內含擷取影像的 **SemanticContentDescriptor**；範例用 **Vision** 框架的 **GenerateImageFeaturePrintRequest** 先為目錄中的專輯預先計算 **feature print**，查詢時再對輸入影像產生 feature print 並以距離門檻比對、依相似度排序回傳。最後用 **OpenIntent** 讓使用者點選結果時直接落在正確畫面。

同一套程式碼幾乎不需修改即可跨 iOS、iPadOS、macOS 運作，但要留意平台差異：iOS 多半透過相機拍攝實體物件，Mac 與 iPad 則以截圖為主，且 Mac 的輸入 pixel buffer 可能大上許多，必要時應考慮縮放。想一次回傳多種結果型別（專輯與演唱會）時，可用 **@UnionValue** 列舉包裝；若想讓使用者延伸搜尋，採用 **semanticContentSearch** schema 帶著同樣的影像情境跳進 App 內完整搜尋畫面並預先填入結果。

除了「提供結果給 Visual Intelligence」，另一個整合方向是「從 Visual Intelligence 接收資料」——透過 **system store integrations**。Visual Intelligence 擷取的事件會寫入系統儲存，App 端只要照常用 **EventKit**（行事曆）、**Contacts**（聯絡人）、**HealthKit**（醫療讀數）讀取即可自動取得這些資料。範例用 EKEventStore 請求權限、篩出與目錄藝人相符的近期活動，並監聽 .EKEventStoreChanged 讓新事件自動出現。實務重點是：結果要快且依相關性排序、善用兩種整合點覆蓋使用者跨裝置的情境。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: David 開場說明 **Visual Intelligence** 自推出以來讓人們快速了解周遭環境或 iPhone 螢幕上的內容，今年更新增加入聯絡人、儲存多筆行事曆事件、醫療裝置記錄等能力，並擴展到 **iPad 與 macOS**。他以自己想做的音樂探索 App 為例，預告整場將從定義內容、實作查詢、跨平台到 system store 整合逐步建構。

deepdive.title: Defining your content
deepdive.body: 整合 Image Search 同時用到 **App Intents** 與 **VisualIntelligence** 框架。第一步是用 **App entities**（App 中的「名詞」）定義要回傳的內容，本例先定義代表專輯的 entity，作為搜尋結果的回傳型別。

deepdive.title: Define the content you want to return as an App Entity
deepdive.body: 在程式中定義 **AlbumEntity**，加入標準的 defaultQuery 與 typeDisplayRepresentation，並以 id、name、artistName、封面縮圖資料描述內容。**displayRepresentation** 決定結果如何呈現——這是使用者第一眼看到的東西，空間只有約三行文字與縮圖，因此應放最關鍵的辨識資訊（專輯名與藝人），並建議使用縮圖尺寸而非全解析度圖。

deepdive.title: Implementing a query
deepdive.body: 定義好 entity 後，靠 **IntentValueQuery** 讓 Visual Intelligence 查詢 App。它是一個輕量查詢協定，若先前已為 Siri 採用 App Intents 可能已有此查詢；與一般查詢的關鍵差異在於輸入是內含擷取影像資訊的 **SemanticContentDescriptor**。

deepdive.title: Adopt IntentValueQuery to return results
deepdive.body: 採用 **IntentValueQuery** 協定並實作 values(for:)，輸入為 SemanticContentDescriptor。實作中從 input 取出 **pixelBuffer**，傳給 catalog.search 取得相符專輯，再以 VisualSearchResult.album 包裝回傳。

deepdive.title: Build a catalog of albums with precomputed feature prints
deepdive.body: 本例選擇在裝置上以本地目錄搜尋，並使用 **Vision** 框架的預訓練電腦視覺模型。每筆目錄項目存有一個 **feature print**（影像的精簡數值表示），透過 **GenerateImageFeaturePrintRequest** 產生；關鍵是預先為目錄中所有專輯算好 feature print，避免在查詢當下才計算而拖慢速度。

deepdive.title: Search the catalog for albums matching the captured image
deepdive.body: 查詢時先用 **VideoToolbox** 把 pixelBuffer 轉成 CGImage，再為它產生 feature print，與目錄中預算好的 feature print 逐一以 **distance** 比較，套用最大距離門檻濾掉不相似的結果，最後依相似度排序回傳前幾筆。建議限制回傳數量以確保相關性，找不到時回傳空陣列由系統處理。

deepdive.title: Opening results
deepdive.body: 為了讓使用者點選結果後落在 App 正確畫面，需要一個 **OpenIntent**。當使用者在 Image Search 結果中點選某張專輯時，系統會帶著選取的 entity 呼叫此 intent。

deepdive.title: Create an open intent to land users on the right screen
deepdive.body: **OpenAlbumIntent** 採用 OpenIntent，以 @Parameter 接收 AlbumEntity，在 perform 中導向專輯詳情頁。若已為其他功能採用 App Intents 而有同一 entity 的 OpenIntent，可直接重用；並建議保持輕量，因為它在 App 進入前景時執行，沉重載入應留到畫面出現後。

deepdive.title: Mac and iPad adoption
deepdive.body: 今年 Visual Intelligence 也登上 iPadOS 與 macOS，且 IntentValueQuery、entities、OpenIntent 等同一套程式碼幾乎不需改動即可跨平台。差異在於入口：iOS 多用相機拍實體物件，Mac 與 iPad 主要透過截圖；此外 Mac 的輸入 pixel buffer 可能遠大於 iPhone，必要時應考慮縮放。

deepdive.title: Use UnionValue to return multiple visual search result types
deepdive.body: 由於一個 App 只能有一個接受 SemanticContentDescriptor 的 IntentValueQuery，要回傳多種型別時用 **@UnionValue** 列舉，為每種 entity（album 與 concert）各一個 case。有了兩種 entity，也需要為每種各自準備一個 **OpenIntent**。

deepdive.title: Expand the IntentValueQuery to return the UnionValue
deepdive.body: 更新查詢以回傳 union 型別：先搜出最相符的專輯，再用這些專輯的藝人名找出附近的演唱會，把兩者合併成單一結果清單。這示範了如何超越單純像素比對，依情境衍生出完全不同類型（演唱會）的結果。

deepdive.title: Returning multiple result types
deepdive.body: 鼓勵開發者思考 App 適不適合回傳多種結果，以及除了像素相符之外還能回傳哪些內容。本例透過影像相似度找到專輯，再用藝人名串接出附近演唱會，展現依情境發揮創意的回傳設計。

deepdive.title: Continuing search in your app
deepdive.body: 若使用者沒有立刻找到想要的結果，應提供延伸到 App 內繼續搜尋的途徑，這可用 **semanticContentSearch** schema 達成。

deepdive.title: Provide a link to in-app search
deepdive.body: 建立符合 **semanticContentSearch** schema 的 intent，系統會自動提供 semanticContent 屬性（即先前帶有 pixel buffer 的 SemanticContentDescriptor）。在 perform 中導向 App 內搜尋畫面並預先填入結果，讓使用者按下「More results」即進入完整搜尋體驗，可呈現比結果列更深入的篩選與分類。

deepdive.title: System store integrations
deepdive.body: 除了提供結果給 Visual Intelligence，App 也能透過 **system store integrations** 接收資料。Visual Intelligence 的其他動作會把資料寫入系統儲存，作為共享系統資料的橋樑：事件以 **EventKit** 讀取、聯絡人以 **Contacts**、醫療裝置讀數以 **HealthKit**。若 App 已從這些框架讀資料，Visual Intelligence 會自動成為新的輸入來源。

deepdive.title: Request calendar access and fetch upcoming concerts
deepdive.body: 本例的 **UpcomingConcertManager** 使用 EKEventStore，透過 requestFullAccessToEvents 請求行事曆讀取權限，授權後才抓取近期活動並更新授權狀態。

deepdive.title: Filter for upcoming events that match known artists in our catalog
deepdive.body: 以 predicateForEvents 查詢未來約 90 天內的事件，再篩出標題與目錄中藝人名相符的活動，讓 App 只關注與使用者音樂興趣相關的演唱會。

deepdive.title: Observe newly created events
deepdive.body: 加入對 **.EKEventStoreChanged** 通知的監聽，透過 NotificationCenter 的 async 通知序列，讓包含由 Visual Intelligence 建立在內的新事件能自動重新抓取並出現在 App 中。相同模式也適用於 Contacts（CNContactStore）與 HealthKit（HKHealthStore）。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 總結 Visual Intelligence 提供兩個強大整合點：透過 **Image Search** 提供結果、透過 **system store integrations** 接收資料；並隨著它登上 iOS、iPadOS、macOS 讓整合觸及跨裝置的使用者。建議查閱開發者文件，並延伸觀看 App Intents 與 Vision 框架的相關場次。

summary_en: Presented by David, an ML engineer on the System Experience team, this session shows how to bring your app into **Visual Intelligence**. This year Apple adds new capabilities like adding to contacts, saving multiple calendar events, and medical-device logging, and extends Visual Intelligence to iPadOS and macOS. Using a music-discovery app as the example, a user can photograph or screenshot album artwork, tap Highlight to Search, and see matching albums and nearby concerts inside Visual Intelligence — and even capture a concert post so the event lands in the calendar and shows up automatically back in the app.

The integration is built on the **App Intents** and **VisualIntelligence** frameworks in four steps. First, model the content you return as an **App Entity** (e.g. AlbumEntity) with a displayRepresentation supplying title, subtitle, and thumbnail, since the result row only affords about three lines of text and one image. Next, implement an **IntentValueQuery** whose values(for:) receives a **SemanticContentDescriptor** holding the captured image; the example uses the **Vision** framework's **GenerateImageFeaturePrintRequest** to precompute **feature prints** for the catalog, then at query time generates a feature print for the input and ranks candidates by distance under a threshold. Finally, an **OpenIntent** takes users straight to the right screen when they tap a result.

The same code runs across iOS, iPadOS, and macOS with minimal change, but mind the platform differences: iOS users mostly capture physical objects with the camera while Mac and iPad lean on screenshots, and the Mac input pixel buffer can be much larger, so consider resizing. To return more than one result type (albums and concerts) wrap them in a **@UnionValue** enum, and to let users keep searching, adopt the **semanticContentSearch** schema to carry the same image context into your full in-app search experience with pre-populated results.

Beyond providing results, the other direction is receiving data via **system store integrations**. Visual Intelligence writes extracted data into system stores that your app reads normally with **EventKit** (events), **Contacts**, and **HealthKit** (medical readings) — so an app that already reads those frameworks gains Visual Intelligence as a new input source for free. The example requests calendar access with EKEventStore, filters for upcoming events matching catalog artists, and observes .EKEventStoreChanged so new events appear automatically. The practical takeaways: return results fast and ranked, and use both integration points to cover users across their devices.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: David opens by noting how **Visual Intelligence** lets people learn about their surroundings or what's on their iPhone screen, with this year adding contacts, multiple calendar events, and medical-device logging plus expansion to **iPad and macOS**. He frames the whole session around building a music-discovery app, walking from defining content through implementing a query, cross-platform support, and system store integrations.

deepdive_en.title: Defining your content
deepdive_en.body: Image Search integration uses both the **App Intents** and **VisualIntelligence** frameworks. The first step is defining the content to return using **App entities** — the nouns of your app — here an album entity that serves as the result type.

deepdive_en.title: Define the content you want to return as an App Entity
deepdive_en.body: An **AlbumEntity** is defined with a standard defaultQuery and typeDisplayRepresentation, plus id, name, artistName, and cover-art thumbnail data. Its **displayRepresentation** controls how each result appears — the first thing people see, with room for only about three lines of text and a thumbnail — so put the key identifying info (album name and artist) there and prefer thumbnail-sized images over full-resolution assets.

deepdive_en.title: Implementing a query
deepdive_en.body: After defining the entity, an **IntentValueQuery** lets Visual Intelligence query the app. It's a lightweight query protocol you may already have from adopting App Intents for Siri; the key difference for Visual Intelligence is the input — a **SemanticContentDescriptor** carrying information about the captured image.

deepdive_en.title: Adopt IntentValueQuery to return results
deepdive_en.body: Adopt the **IntentValueQuery** protocol and implement values(for:) with a SemanticContentDescriptor input. The body grabs the **pixelBuffer** from the input, passes it to catalog.search to get matching albums, and returns them wrapped as VisualSearchResult.album.

deepdive_en.title: Build a catalog of albums with precomputed feature prints
deepdive_en.body: The example searches on device against a local catalog using the **Vision** framework's pretrained models. Each catalog entry stores a **feature print** — a compact numerical representation of an image — produced via **GenerateImageFeaturePrintRequest**; crucially these are precomputed for every album so no computation happens at query time, keeping the query fast.

deepdive_en.title: Search the catalog for albums matching the captured image
deepdive_en.body: At query time the pixelBuffer is converted to a CGImage with **VideoToolbox**, a feature print is generated for it, and it's compared against the precomputed prints by **distance** under a maximum threshold, then sorted by similarity and returned top-N. Apple recommends limiting the result count for relevance and returning an empty array when there are no good matches, which the system handles.

deepdive_en.title: Opening results
deepdive_en.body: To land people on the right screen after they tap a result, you need an **OpenIntent**. When a user taps an album in the Image Search results, the system calls this intent with the selected entity.

deepdive_en.title: Create an open intent to land users on the right screen
deepdive_en.body: **OpenAlbumIntent** adopts OpenIntent, takes an AlbumEntity via @Parameter, and navigates to the album detail page in perform. If you already have an OpenIntent for the entity from adopting App Intents, reuse it; keep it lightweight since it runs as the app comes to the foreground, deferring heavy loading until after the view appears.

deepdive_en.title: Mac and iPad adoption
deepdive_en.body: Visual Intelligence comes to iPadOS and macOS this year, and the same IntentValueQuery, entities, and OpenIntent code works across platforms with minimal change. The differences are entry points — iOS favors camera capture of physical objects while Mac and iPad lean on screenshots — and the Mac input pixel buffer can be much larger than on iPhone, so consider resizing.

deepdive_en.title: Use UnionValue to return multiple visual search result types
deepdive_en.body: Since an app can have only one IntentValueQuery accepting a SemanticContentDescriptor, returning multiple types uses a **@UnionValue** enum with a case per entity (album and concert). With two entity types you also need a separate **OpenIntent** for each.

deepdive_en.title: Expand the IntentValueQuery to return the UnionValue
deepdive_en.body: The query is updated to return the union type: search for the top matching albums first, then use those albums' artists to find nearby concerts, and combine both into one results list — showing how to go beyond pixel matching to derive a completely different kind of result.

deepdive_en.title: Returning multiple result types
deepdive_en.body: Consider whether returning multiple result types makes sense, and what content your app can return beyond pixel matches. The example finds albums by image similarity and then surfaces nearby concerts via artist names, illustrating creative, context-driven result design.

deepdive_en.title: Continuing search in your app
deepdive_en.body: If people don't immediately find what they want, provide an easy way to continue the search inside the app, which the **semanticContentSearch** schema enables.

deepdive_en.title: Provide a link to in-app search
deepdive_en.body: Create an intent conforming to the **semanticContentSearch** schema; the system supplies the semanticContent property automatically — the same SemanticContentDescriptor with the pixel buffer. In perform, navigate to an in-app search view pre-populated with results so tapping More results drops users into the full search experience with filters and categories beyond the results sheet.

deepdive_en.title: System store integrations
deepdive_en.body: Besides providing results, an app can receive data through **system store integrations**. Visual Intelligence's other actions write data to system stores that bridge to shared system data: events via **EventKit**, contacts via **Contacts**, medical-device readings via **HealthKit**. An app that already reads those frameworks gets Visual Intelligence as a new input source automatically.

deepdive_en.title: Request calendar access and fetch upcoming concerts
deepdive_en.body: The **UpcomingConcertManager** uses EKEventStore, requesting calendar read access via requestFullAccessToEvents, and only after authorization fetches upcoming events and updates the authorization status.

deepdive_en.title: Filter for upcoming events that match known artists in our catalog
deepdive_en.body: It queries events in roughly the next 90 days with predicateForEvents, then filters for those whose title matches an artist name in the catalog, so the app focuses only on concerts relevant to the user's music interests.

deepdive_en.title: Observe newly created events
deepdive_en.body: A notification observer on **.EKEventStoreChanged** via NotificationCenter's async sequence re-fetches so that new events — including ones created by Visual Intelligence — appear automatically. The same pattern applies to Contacts (CNContactStore) and HealthKit (HKHealthStore).

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: The recap: Visual Intelligence offers two integration points — providing results via **Image Search** and receiving data via **system store integrations** — and now reaches users across iOS, iPadOS, and macOS. Apple points to the developer documentation and related App Intents and Vision sessions to go further.

title: Meet the Evaluations framework
gloss: 認識 Evaluations 框架
takeaway: 在機率性的 AI 世界裡，用 Evaluations 框架以資料集、metrics 與 model judge 系統化評估模型驅動功能的品質。

Run with Swift Testing and an optimization target
Running the evaluation and reading the report
Synthesize more samples with a SampleGenerator
More evaluators: word count and genre
Add app context with a ModelJudgePrompt

points.text: 在機率性世界中，**單元測試不足以驗證模型行為**，需要專門的 Evaluations 框架。
用 **Evaluation** 搭配 **ModelSample** 資料集定義要評估的功能，並可用 SampleGenerator 合成更多樣本。
透過 **Metric** 與 **Evaluator** 定義通過／失敗條件，並用 MetricsAggregator 跨樣本彙總統計。
可用 **.evaluates** 與 Swift Testing 整合，設定 optimization target 並以 hill-climbing 迭代 instructions。
以 **ModelJudgeEvaluator** 進行質性評分，並用 ScoreDimension 與 ModelJudgePrompt 細分維度。

audience: 正在打造 **模型驅動或生成式 AI 功能**、需要系統化衡量輸出品質的開發者。
gloss_en: Meet the Evaluations framework
takeaway_en: In a probabilistic AI world, use the Evaluations framework to systematically assess the quality of model-driven features with datasets, metrics, and a model judge.

points_en.text: In a probabilistic world, **unit tests alone aren't enough to verify model behavior**; a dedicated Evaluations framework is needed.
Use **Evaluation** with a **ModelSample** dataset to define the feature to evaluate, and use SampleGenerator to synthesize more samples.
Define pass/fail criteria with **Metric** and **Evaluator**, and use MetricsAggregator to aggregate statistics across samples.
Integrate with Swift Testing via **.evaluates**, set an optimization target, and iterate on instructions with hill-climbing.
Use **ModelJudgeEvaluator** for qualitative scoring, and break it down by dimension with ScoreDimension and ModelJudgePrompt.

audience_en: Developers building **model-driven or generative AI features** who need to systematically measure output quality.
summary: 這場由 Yada 與 Rob 主講，介紹全新的 **Evaluations framework**——用來衡量「由模型驅動的功能」品質的測試工具。承接去年的 **Foundation Models framework**，講者點出生成式 AI 打破了傳統軟體測試的根本契約：同一輸入不再保證產生同一輸出，因此 **unit test 不足以驗證機率性行為**。我們需要新的測試形式，回答諸如「功能多常產生非預期結果」、「在什麼情況下會產生不安全結果」這類問題。

全片以一個書籍管理 app **Book Tracker** 的 **BookTaggingService**（依使用者書評自動產生標籤）為範例，示範建立 evaluation 的五個步驟：定義要衡量的程式（`subject(from:)`）、定義輸入資料（**`ModelSample`**，含 prompt 與 expected）、定義量測（**`Metric`** 與 **`Evaluator`** closure 回傳 passing／failing）、彙總量測（`aggregateMetrics(using:)`），最後用 **Swift Testing** 的 `@Test` 搭配 **`.evaluates`** trait 設定 optimization target 跑起來。Xcode 提供專屬的 evaluation report，可逐一檢視每個 sample 的 prompt、量測與模型完整回應。

接著談如何擴大規模。好的 evaluation 需要數千筆、且涵蓋不同類型、長度、體裁與夾雜個人意見的 dataset；框架內建 **`SampleGenerator`**（`makeSamples`）可用模型合成更多樣本。量化指標之外，講者引入 **model judge**：用一個「至少和受評模型一樣強」的模型（此處用 **Private Cloud Compute** 的模型）對輸出做主觀評分。**`ModelJudgeEvaluator`** 與量化 evaluator 共用相同協定與 `Metric` 型別，可自由混用；rationale（評分理由）是關鍵,讓你看見判斷依據。

當 judge 的判斷與你不一致時，代表問題問得太籠統。解法是拆成多個 **`ScoreDimension`**（例如把模糊的 quality 拆成 relevance 與 usefulness），並用 **`ModelJudgePrompt`** 補上 app 脈絡（告訴 judge 這是個人書庫而非評論平台）。整套流程的精神是 **hill-climbing**：讀 rationale、改 instructions、重跑、看分數變化，把它放在開發核心就成了 **evaluation-driven development**。最佳實務是從 20–30 筆小 dataset 起步、能用程式量的就用量化指標、只能用文字描述的才用 model judge，並從單次執行的 rationale 學習下一步。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: Yada 與 Rob 開場介紹 **Evaluations framework**，並回顧去年的 **Foundation Models framework**。核心論點是生成式 AI **打破了「同一輸入產生同一輸出」的測試契約**，導致 unit test 不足以驗證行為。未經驗證的行為會侵蝕使用者信任，因此需要一種更穩健、能回答「多常出錯」「何時產生不安全結果」的新測試形式。

deepdive.title: Demo app Book Tacker: a manual evaluation
deepdive.body: 以 **Book Tracker** app 的 **BookTaggingService** 為例，用 `#Playground` macro 對《Pride & Prejudice》與《Dracula》兩篇書評手動試跑。講者用人類判斷列出期望（標籤數不該過多、不要書名當標籤、避免多字詞標籤、要能辨識文學 genre），這其實就是**第一次人工 evaluation**——但人類判斷無法規模化。

deepdive.title: Building your first evaluation
deepdive.body: 說明自動化的入口只需 `import Evaluations` 並實作 **`Evaluation`** 協定。建立與執行一個 evaluation 有五個步驟：定義受測程式、定義輸入資料、定義量測方式、彙總量測、建立測試來執行。

deepdive.title: Define an Evaluation
deepdive.body: 在 `subject(from:)` 中呼叫 `BookTaggingService` 並回傳其輸出作為評估的 **subject**。用 **`ModelSample`** 包裝先前的書評作為輸入，並同時定義 **expected**（理想標籤）。接著用 **`Metric`**（如 `TagCount`）與 **`Evaluator`** closure 檢查標籤數是否落在 3–8 之間，回傳 passing 或 failing。

deepdive.title: Run with Swift Testing and an optimization target
deepdive.body: Evaluations 整合 **Swift Testing**，可在測試 target 內執行。在 `@Suite` 中實例化 evaluation 並加上 notes 以便日後比較不同執行；再用 `@Test` 搭配新的 **`.evaluates`** trait 取得結果 bundle，對 `tagCount` 的平均值用 `#expect` 斷言。此處設定 **optimization target 為 80%**——低於此即視為功能退步,失敗測試正是好訊號。

deepdive.title: Running the evaluation and reading the report
deepdive.body: 跑測試後（如預期）未通過,`TagCount` 只有 50% 通過率。講者示範用 Xcode 的 **evaluation report**:從 report navigator 點進 Evaluations,雙擊列展開,看到《Pride & Prejudice》失敗而《Dracula》通過,並在 assistant editor 的細節面板檢視 prompt、各項量測與模型完整回應。

deepdive.title: Constrain output with a Generable @Guide
deepdive.body: 為了改善表現,講者回看 `@Generable` 的 `BookTags` 型別,在 `tags` 屬性的 **`@Guide`** 上加入 **`.count(3...8)`** range,指示模型只產生 3 到 8 個標籤。這是一次 hill-climbing 假設,改完重跑驗證。

deepdive.title: Building robust datasets
deepdive.body: 改完後測試通過、`TagCount` 達 100%,但出現怪行為:服務**永遠產生 8 個標籤**。講者指出一開始只有兩筆樣本、量測太少無法看出趨勢,好的 evaluation 需要數千筆樣本並涵蓋多樣性。

deepdive.title: Define the dataset with ModelSample
deepdive.body: 說明 dataset 要刻意製造多樣性:不同 genre、不同長度的書評、fiction 與 non-fiction 的不同分類、以及小說／短篇／散文等不同體裁。並刻意夾雜個人意見,測量服務能否忽略它們;若想教模型用你的風格寫標籤,就在 expected 值放入更多個人風格。

deepdive.title: Synthesize more samples with a SampleGenerator
deepdive.body: 人工建資料同樣無法規模化。框架內建 **`SampleGenerator`**,可直接對 `ModelSample` 陣列呼叫 **`makeSamples`**,指定 prompt 與 `targetCount`,用你選的模型合成更多樣本(範例為 sentence-completion 配對)。更進階用法請見另一場「Create robust evaluations for agentic apps」。

deepdive.title: More evaluators: word count and genre
deepdive.body: 把 dataset 擴充到整個書庫後重跑,測試仍通過、平均仍 100%,但 8 個標籤的怪行為持續存在。這促使講者新增更多 evaluator 來更細緻地追蹤行為,而不只看是否落在範圍內。

deepdive.title: Define a Metric and Evaluator
deepdive.body: 新增 **`TagTotal`** metric 記錄實際標籤數量,並用 scoring 值(而非 pass/fail)記錄,以便看出**分布**而非只看是否合規。同樣的模式可用來檢查標籤是否含空白(多字詞)以及是否含已知 genre。

deepdive.title: Refining metrics and evaluators
deepdive.body: 示範字數檢查:逐一檢查每個標籤是否含空白,有就回傳 `wordCount.failing`。genre 檢查同樣直接:向 `BookTaggingService` 取得 `knownGenres`,比對每個生成標籤是否命中。

deepdive.title: Aggregate metrics across samples
deepdive.body: Evaluator 一次只跑一個 sample,但可在 `aggregateMetrics(using:)` 中用 **`MetricsAggregator`** 跨所有樣本看趨勢。範例計算 `tagCount` 的平均,並用 `group` 對 `tagTotal` 計算標準差、平均與變異數,得到「服務多常正確」的比率與標籤總數的分布。

deepdive.title: Iterate the feature's instructions (hill-climbing)
deepdive.body: evaluation 逐漸完整,已能用五個 aggregate metric 衡量原本五個期望中的三個,report 呈現標籤分布、範圍合規與含 genre 的豐富樣貌。講者透過迭代 `BookTaggingService` 的 instructions 持續改善。

deepdive.title: Evaluation-driven development and hill-climbing
deepdive.body: 展示從最初到多次迭代後的 instructions 變化,並用「每次改動都對應新增一個 evaluation 期望來驗證」的方式追蹤每次變更。把這個 **hill-climbing** 回饋迴圈放到開發流程的核心,就是 **evaluation-driven development**。

deepdive.title: Model judges: qualitative metrics
deepdive.body: 由 Yada 接手講 **model judge**,用來規模化衡量**質化指標**。以《Alice in Wonderland》為例:量化指標全過,但 'overrated'、'pretentious' 描述的是讀者感受而非書,'whodunit' 甚至是錯的 genre——模型只抓住評論的字面語言而沒理解書。指標通過卻給錯訊號,因此需要請模型來幫忙評分。

deepdive.title: Building a model judge
deepdive.body: **Model judge 是用一個語言模型來替你的功能輸出評分**,給出像人一樣的主觀評價,但能一致套用到整個 dataset。受評功能 `BookTaggingService` 在 on-device 模型跑以求快速與本地;judge 則應**至少和受評模型一樣強**,此處改用 **Private Cloud Compute** 的更強模型。

deepdive.title: Build a model judge
deepdive.body: model judge 有幾個關鍵元件:instruction(告訴模型要評什麼)、feature input(書評 prompt)、feature output(生成標籤)、與 scoring guide。框架替你處理大部分,你只需專注 scoring guide。範例用 **`ModelJudgeEvaluator`** 定義 1–4 的 `TagQuality` 量表(偶數級距避免落在中性中間值),並指定 Private Cloud Compute 為 judge。

deepdive.title: Refining with score dimensions
deepdive.body: 跑出來每個 sample 都得 3 或 4 分,《Alice in Wonderland》得 3 分。但細看 rationale,judge 只標出部分不相關標籤——因為**依我們寫的量表,judge 其實是對的**:每個標籤都連到使用者寫的東西。問題在於量表太籠統、同時問了兩個不同的問題,需要拆開。

deepdive.title: Split into score dimensions
deepdive.body: 把籠統的問題拆成不同的 **`ScoreDimension`**。先定義 **Relevance**:每個標籤是否描述書本身的特質、主題或調性,而非細節或讀者的個人反應,並把這段寫成 dimension 的 description 與 1–4 的 scale。

deepdive.title: Add dimensions to the judge
deepdive.body: 用同樣方式定義 **Usefulness**,再把 relevance 與 usefulness 兩個 dimension 一起加進 **`ModelJudgeEvaluator`**。但光有 dimension 不夠——它們告訴 judge 要量什麼,卻沒告訴它如何理解你的 app。

deepdive.title: Add app context with a ModelJudgePrompt
deepdive.body: 用 **`ModelJudgePrompt`** 補上 app 脈絡:在 instructions 告訴 judge 這是個人書庫 app(而非評論平台,以免把讀者的批評當成有效書本描述),用 `evaluationTarget` 格式化回應,並用 `reference` 把 expectedTags 當作比對參考傳入。

deepdive.title: Reviewing dimension results
deepdive.body: 補上脈絡後重跑,原本的 Quality 換成 relevance 與 usefulness 兩個分數。以《Alice in Wonderland》為例,兩段 rationale 把診斷分開:Relevance 指出哪種標籤錯了,Usefulness 指出錯標籤如何在瀏覽上失敗,給出清楚的改進方向。

deepdive.title: Best practices
deepdive.body: 收尾的最佳實務:從 20–30 筆的小而聚焦 dataset 起步;先想清楚你要模型怎麼表現;能用程式量的特質就用量化指標(rule of thumb:能在程式裡量就是量化,只能用文字描述就需要 `ModelJudgeEvaluator`);model judge 也從簡單開始,定義 dimension、跑、讀 rationale——一次執行學到的比數小時規劃還多;用 rationale 驅動下一步改動。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 請觀眾查閱文件與 sample code,並推薦延伸場次:「Improve your prompts by hill climbing with Evaluations」與「Create robust evaluations for agentic apps」。

summary_en: Presented by Yada and Rob, this session introduces the new **Evaluations framework** for measuring the quality of model-driven features. Building on last year's **Foundation Models framework**, the speakers note that generative AI breaks software testing's fundamental contract: the same input no longer guarantees the same output, so **unit tests are insufficient** to verify probabilistic behavior. We need a new form of testing that answers questions like how often a feature produces unexpected results and under what circumstances it produces unsafe ones.

The whole talk uses **Book Tracker**'s **BookTaggingService** (which auto-tags books from a user's review) as the running example, walking through the five steps to build an evaluation: define the code under test (`subject(from:)`), define the input data (**`ModelSample`** with prompt and expected), define measurements (**`Metric`** and an **`Evaluator`** closure returning passing/failing), aggregate them (`aggregateMetrics(using:)`), and finally run it with **Swift Testing**'s `@Test` plus the new **`.evaluates`** trait to set an optimization target. Xcode provides a dedicated evaluation report to inspect each sample's prompt, measurements, and the model's full response.

Next comes scaling. A good evaluation needs thousands of samples spanning different types, lengths, forms, and sprinkled-in personal opinions; the framework's built-in **`SampleGenerator`** (`makeSamples`) synthesizes more. Beyond quantitative metrics, the speakers introduce the **model judge**: a model at least as capable as the one under test (here a **Private Cloud Compute** model) that scores outputs subjectively. A **`ModelJudgeEvaluator`** conforms to the same protocol and produces the same `Metric` type as quantitative evaluators, so they mix freely; the rationale is essential — it shows you why the judge scored what it did.

When the judge disagrees with you, your question is too broad. The fix is to split it into multiple **`ScoreDimension`**s (e.g. break a vague "quality" into relevance and usefulness) and add app context with a **`ModelJudgePrompt`** (telling the judge this is a personal library, not a review platform). The spirit of the whole loop is **hill-climbing**: read the rationale, change the instructions, re-run, watch the scores move — and centering development on it is **evaluation-driven development**. Best practices: start with 20–30 samples, use quantitative metrics for anything measurable in code and model judges only for what you can only describe in words, and learn your next change from the rationales.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Yada and Rob open by introducing the **Evaluations framework** and recapping last year's **Foundation Models framework**. The core argument is that generative AI **breaks the "same input, same output" testing contract**, making unit tests insufficient. Unverified behavior erodes user trust, so a more robust new form of testing is needed — one that answers how often a feature errs and when it produces unsafe results.

deepdive_en.title: Demo app Book Tacker: a manual evaluation
deepdive_en.body: Using Book Tracker's **BookTaggingService**, they run a `#Playground` macro against two reviews — Pride & Prejudice and Dracula. Listing expectations by human judgment (not too many tags, no book title, avoid multi-word tags, recognize literary genres) is in fact a **first manual evaluation** — but human judgment doesn't scale.

deepdive_en.title: Building your first evaluation
deepdive_en.body: Automating it requires only `import Evaluations` and conforming to the **`Evaluation`** protocol. Building and running an evaluation has five steps: define the code under test, the input data, the measurements, the aggregation, and finally a test to run it.

deepdive_en.title: Define an Evaluation
deepdive_en.body: In `subject(from:)` they call `BookTaggingService` and return its output as the evaluation's **subject**. **`ModelSample`** wraps the earlier reviews as input, with **expected** ideal tags defined too. A **`Metric`** (`TagCount`) and an **`Evaluator`** closure then check whether the tag count is within 3–8, returning passing or failing.

deepdive_en.title: Run with Swift Testing and an optimization target
deepdive_en.body: Evaluations integrates with **Swift Testing**, runnable in test targets. They instantiate the evaluation in a `@Suite` with notes for later comparison, then use `@Test` with the new **`.evaluates`** trait to get a results bundle and assert against `tagCount`'s mean with `#expect`. The **optimization target is 80%** — dipping below means a regression, and a failing test is great signal.

deepdive_en.title: Running the evaluation and reading the report
deepdive_en.body: The test (as expected) fails with `TagCount` passing only 50%. They demo Xcode's **evaluation report**: open Evaluations from the report navigator, double-click a row, and see Pride & Prejudice failing while Dracula passes, inspecting prompt, measurements, and full model response in the assistant editor's detail panel.

deepdive_en.title: Constrain output with a Generable @Guide
deepdive_en.body: To improve results, they revisit the `@Generable` `BookTags` type and add **`.count(3...8)`** to the `tags` property's **`@Guide`**, instructing the model to produce only 3 to 8 tags. This is a hill-climbing hypothesis, re-run to verify.

deepdive_en.title: Building robust datasets
deepdive_en.body: The change makes the test pass at 100% `TagCount`, but reveals a strange behavior: the service now **always produces 8 tags**. With only two samples there were too few measurements to spot trends — a good evaluation needs thousands of samples and real variety.

deepdive_en.title: Define the dataset with ModelSample
deepdive_en.body: A dataset should be deliberately diverse: different genres, review lengths, fiction vs non-fiction categories, and forms like novels, short stories, and essays. Personal opinions are sprinkled in to test whether the service ignores them; to teach the model your style, put more personal style into the samples' expected values.

deepdive_en.title: Synthesize more samples with a SampleGenerator
deepdive_en.body: Human data creation doesn't scale either. The built-in **`SampleGenerator`** is called directly on a `ModelSample` array via **`makeSamples`**, with a prompt and `targetCount`, synthesizing more samples with a model of your choice (the example uses sentence-completion pairs). Advanced uses are covered in "Create robust evaluations for agentic apps."

deepdive_en.title: More evaluators: word count and genre
deepdive_en.body: After expanding the dataset to the whole library, the test still passes at 100% but the always-8-tags behavior persists. This motivates adding more evaluators to track behavior more finely rather than just checking the count range.

deepdive_en.title: Define a Metric and Evaluator
deepdive_en.body: A new **`TagTotal`** metric records the actual number of tags using a scoring value (not pass/fail), so you can see the **distribution** rather than mere compliance. The same pattern checks whether tags contain spaces (multi-word) and whether they include a known genre.

deepdive_en.title: Refining metrics and evaluators
deepdive_en.body: The word-count check inspects each tag for a space, returning `wordCount.failing` if found. The genre check is equally direct: fetch `knownGenres` from `BookTaggingService` and compare each generated tag for a match.

deepdive_en.title: Aggregate metrics across samples
deepdive_en.body: Evaluators run one sample at a time, but `aggregateMetrics(using:)` with a **`MetricsAggregator`** spots trends across all samples. The example computes the mean of `tagCount` and uses `group` to compute standard deviation, mean, and variance of `tagTotal`, yielding a how-often-correct ratio and the tag-total distribution.

deepdive_en.title: Iterate the feature's instructions (hill-climbing)
deepdive_en.body: The evaluation fills out, now measuring three of the five original expectations via five aggregate metrics, with the report showing tag distribution, range compliance, and genre presence. The speakers keep improving by iterating the `BookTaggingService` instructions.

deepdive_en.title: Evaluation-driven development and hill-climbing
deepdive_en.body: They show how the instructions evolved across runs, tracking each change by the new expectation added to verify it. Centering development on this **hill-climbing** feedback loop is **evaluation-driven development**.

deepdive_en.title: Model judges: qualitative metrics
deepdive_en.body: Yada takes over to cover the **model judge** for scaling **qualitative metrics**. With Alice in Wonderland: every quantitative metric passes, yet 'overrated' and 'pretentious' describe the reader's feelings, not the book, and 'whodunit' is the wrong genre — the model latched onto the review's language without understanding the book. Metrics pass but give the wrong signal, so a model is asked to help.

deepdive_en.title: Building a model judge
deepdive_en.body: **A model judge is a language model used to score your feature's output**, giving a person-like subjective rating applied consistently across the dataset. The feature `BookTaggingService` runs on-device for speed and locality; the judge should be **at least as capable** as the model under test, here a more capable **Private Cloud Compute** model.

deepdive_en.title: Build a model judge
deepdive_en.body: A model judge has key components: instruction (what to evaluate), feature input (the review prompt), feature output (the generated tags), and the scoring guide. The framework handles most of it, so you focus on the scoring guide. The example uses a **`ModelJudgeEvaluator`** with a 1–4 `TagQuality` scale (an even count avoids a neutral middle) and specifies Private Cloud Compute as the judge.

deepdive_en.title: Refining with score dimensions
deepdive_en.body: Every sample scores 3 or 4; Alice in Wonderland gets a 3. But reading the rationale, the judge flagged only some irrelevant tags — because **by the scale we wrote, the judge is right**: every tag connects to something the user wrote. The scale was too broad, asking two different questions at once, and needs splitting.

deepdive_en.title: Split into score dimensions
deepdive_en.body: The broad question is split into separate **`ScoreDimension`**s. First, **Relevance**: whether each tag describes a quality, theme, or tone of the book itself rather than incidental details or the reader's personal reactions — written as the dimension's description with a 1–4 scale.

deepdive_en.title: Add dimensions to the judge
deepdive_en.body: **Usefulness** is defined the same way, and both relevance and usefulness dimensions are added to the **`ModelJudgeEvaluator`**. But dimensions alone aren't enough — they tell the judge what to measure, not how to think about your app.

deepdive_en.title: Add app context with a ModelJudgePrompt
deepdive_en.body: A **`ModelJudgePrompt`** supplies app context: the instructions tell the judge this is a personal library app (not a review platform, so a reader's criticism isn't treated as a valid descriptor), `evaluationTarget` formats the response, and `reference` passes the expectedTags for comparison.

deepdive_en.title: Reviewing dimension results
deepdive_en.body: After adding context and re-running, the single Quality is replaced by separate relevance and usefulness scores. For Alice in Wonderland, two rationales separate the diagnosis: Relevance says what kind of tag is wrong, Usefulness says how the wrong tags fail at browsing — giving a clear path forward.

deepdive_en.title: Best practices
deepdive_en.body: Closing best practices: start with a focused 20–30 sample dataset; spec out how you want the model to behave; use heuristics for quantifiable traits (rule of thumb: measurable in code = quantitative; only describable in words = needs a `ModelJudgeEvaluator`); start simple with the judge — define a dimension, run it, read the rationales; and use rationales to drive your next change (too-uniform scores mean the question is too broad).

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Viewers are pointed to the documentation and sample code, plus two follow-up sessions: "Improve your prompts by hill climbing with Evaluations" and "Create robust evaluations for agentic apps."

title: Create robust evaluations for agentic apps
gloss: 為 agentic App 建立穩健的評估
takeaway: 運用 Evaluations 框架以 makeSamples 產生合成資料、驗證樣本，並用 TrajectoryExpectation 評估工具呼叫的順序與引數，打造穩健的 agentic 評估。

points.text: 用 **makeSamples** 與自訂 **SampleGenerator** 產生多樣化的**合成資料**，解決評估資料集不足的問題。
透過 **validator** 閉包驗證樣本，並可分別存取 valid 與 **invalidSamples**，再比較不同評估結果。
以 **TrajectoryExpectation** 與 **ToolExpectation** 評估工具呼叫，支援 ordered／unordered 與 disallowed。
引數比對提供 **.exact、.naturalLanguage、.keyOnly、.range、.contains** 等 matcher，可依語意而非字面匹配。
用 **ToolCallEvaluator** 搭配 Metric（allPass／percentagePass）建立完整的工具呼叫評估流程。

audience: **建構 agentic 或工具呼叫型 AI 功能**、需要系統化評估模型行為與品質的開發者。
gloss_en: Create robust evaluations for agentic apps
takeaway_en: Use the Evaluations framework to generate synthetic data with makeSamples, validate samples, and assess the order and arguments of tool calls with TrajectoryExpectation to build robust agentic evaluations.

points_en.text: Use **makeSamples** with a custom **SampleGenerator** to generate diverse **synthetic data**, solving the problem of insufficient evaluation datasets.
Validate samples with a **validator** closure, access valid and **invalidSamples** separately, and compare different evaluation results.
Evaluate tool calls with **TrajectoryExpectation** and **ToolExpectation**, supporting ordered/unordered and disallowed.
Argument matching offers matchers like **.exact, .naturalLanguage, .keyOnly, .range, .contains**, matching by meaning rather than literal text.
Use **ToolCallEvaluator** with a Metric (allPass/percentagePass) to build a complete tool-call evaluation flow.

audience_en: **Developers building agentic or tool-calling AI features** who need to systematically evaluate model behavior and quality.
summary: 本場由 Evaluations 團隊的 Ada 與 Kyle 主講，聚焦 **Evaluations 框架**的進階用法，目標是為智慧型（intelligence-powered）功能打造穩固且可擴充的評估。框架是 Xcode 27 的新成員，支援 macOS、iOS、watchOS 與 visionOS。內容延續 hill-climbing 流程中的 Develop 與 Evaluate 步驟，分兩大主題：用合成資料擴充評估資料集，以及為含 **tool calling** 的代理式（agentic）工作流建立評估。

第一部分以 BookTracker（依書評自動產生標籤的個人書庫 App）說明「資料集問題」：手寫的 13 筆樣本只能看見功能表現的一小角，評估結果可能漂亮卻具誤導性。框架提供純程式碼的合成資料 API：最簡單的 **makeSamples** 需要 prompt、初始 dataset 與 targetCount（含初始樣本在內的最終總量），回傳一串非同步產生的新樣本；預設使用裝置端模型。需要更多控制時改用 **SampleGenerator**，可透過 **sessionProvider** 指定模型（例如 context 較大的 **PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel**）與系統指令；框架自動處理 batch size，並在 context window 用盡時重新呼叫 sessionProvider，因此指令必須自足。還能設定 **samplingStrategy**（random 或 sliding window）決定如何挑選 in-context 範例，並用 **validator** 閉包逐筆驗證（如書評至少 100 字、3–8 個標籤、全小寫），有效樣本進 samples、失敗的自動歸入 invalidSamples。
把資料集從 13 筆擴到 100 筆後，用 Xcode 27 新的 **Evaluations Report** 與 **Compare** 功能比較，分數如預期下滑——這揭示原本只是因資料不夠全面才顯得表現良好。分數變化可能來自 prompt/指令問題、功能本身的缺口、評估設計，或資料仍不夠代表性，可繼續用合成資料 API 增量或補邊界案例。

第二部分由 Kyle 講 **tool 評估**：模型可能給出聽起來合理卻沒呼叫正確工具的答案，因此要驗證「怎麼做」而非只看「做出什麼」。核心是 **TrajectoryExpectation**，它檢查一段 LanguageModelSession transcript 中工具呼叫的種類與順序。可用 unordered／ordered 表達是否在意順序、用 **disallowed** 指定不該出現的工具，並以多種 argument matcher 比對參數：**.exact**、**.naturalLanguage**（比對意圖而非字串）、.keyOnly、.range、.contains 等。完整評估用 **ToolCallEvaluator** 把 LanguageModelSession 與工具組合、取得回應並擷取結構化 transcript 來計分。由於 TrajectoryExpectation 也是 Generable，同樣能用 SampleGenerator 合成 tool 評估樣本，但須在指令中說明可用工具、順序與情境，並以 validator 確認每筆都有 expectation、至少含一個工具、且工具名皆屬已定義集合。把書籤標籤評估（檢查產出）與 tool 評估（檢查路徑）放進同一套件，即可對功能建立端到端信心。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: Ada 與 Kyle 介紹 **Evaluations 框架**——在 Swift App 中評估智慧型功能、追蹤長期改善並確保上線品質的方式，為 **Xcode 27** 新增、支援 macOS／iOS／watchOS／visionOS。本場聚焦如何處理評估的複雜度與可擴充性，分為合成資料與 tool 評估兩大主題，並建議先看「Meet the Evaluations framework」與 hill climbing 兩部影片。

deepdive.title: The dataset problem in BookTracker
deepdive.body: 以 **BookTracker**（依書評自動產生標籤的個人書庫 App）為例，Book 類別含 title、author、review、tags、rating，並有 13 筆 sampleBooks。講者指出這 13 筆只能呈現功能表現的一小角——書籍、類型與書寫方式千變萬化，小資料集無法涵蓋，評估結果可能看似亮眼卻誤導。

deepdive.title: Generating synthetic data with makeSamples
deepdive.body: 提出以合成資料解決資料集問題。框架以純程式碼定義樣本生成，支援文字資料並透過 **@Generable** 巨集產生結構化合成資料，可自建生成流程、由命令列執行或接進既有工作流。

deepdive.title: Generate synthetic data with makeSamples
deepdive.body: **makeSamples** 需要三項：prompt、dataset 與 targetCount。範例 prompt 要求模型產生涵蓋多元類型、年代、文化與讀者樣貌的書評；dataset 傳入 13 筆 sampleBooks，以新的 **ModelSample** 把書評當 prompt、標籤當 expected。targetCount 設 100，但因為它是「含初始樣本的最終總量」，模型實際只會新生成 87 筆。

deepdive.title: Configure a custom SampleGenerator
deepdive.body: 預設用裝置端模型生成已適用多數情況，但若想自帶模型或自訂指令，框架提供 **SampleGenerator** 給予完整控制。本章引入超越 prompt／dataset／targetCount 的進階配置入口。

deepdive.title: Customizing generation with SampleGenerator
deepdive.body: 重點是 **sessionProvider**——回傳 LanguageModelSession 的閉包，用來決定驅動生成的模型與系統指令；範例採 context 較大的 **PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel** 並寫入規則（書評至少 100 字、3–8 個小寫標籤等）。框架自動管理 batch size，生成開始時呼叫一次 sessionProvider 並跨批次重用以維持 context；若 context window 中途耗盡會擲錯並重新取得一個全新（無前文）session，因此指令必須自足。

deepdive.title: Sampling strategies
deepdive.body: **samplingStrategy** 控制如何從初始 dataset 挑選展示給模型的 in-context 範例。**random** 隨機挑不重複的子集，適合初始樣本無特定順序時；**sliding window** 依序逐步走過樣本並跳過重複，適合資料有意義順序時。本例因初始樣本無意義順序而用 random，也是預設值故無需明寫。

deepdive.title: Validating synthetic samples
deepdive.body: 即使在 sessionProvider 指令裡寫了規則，也不保證輸出真的遵守，因此用 **validator** 閉包逐筆接受或拒絕生成樣本。validator 是「逐筆隔離」驗證、無法看到其他樣本，所以多元性與跨樣本的長度分布等需要更多判斷，無法只靠它檢查。

deepdive.title: Validate generated samples
deepdive.body: 把規則拆成可系統化檢查的項目：書評至少 100 字（以 Frankenstein 為例示範長度檢查）、標籤數量介於 3 到 8 之間、所有標籤皆為小寫。這三項已定義為 SampleGenerator 的驗證 metric，用來確認樣本符合預期結構。

deepdive.title: Access valid and invalid results
deepdive.body: 生成過程中通過驗證的樣本收進 generator 的 **samples** 屬性，未通過者自動歸入 **invalidSamples**；兩者即時更新，可在迭代中（檢查進度）或迴圈結束後存取。結果可直接用於 App 或在本地存成資料集。

deepdive.title: Comparing evaluation results
deepdive.body: Xcode 27 新增 **Evaluations Report** 視覺化結果。先看 13 筆樣本的 BookTaggingEvaluation（相關性與實用性分數很高），再用 **Compare** 與 100 筆新資料集比較，分數如預期下滑。這代表先前的好表現只是因為沒用更全面的資料集測試。

deepdive.title: Tool calling and tool evaluations
deepdive.body: Kyle 接手 **tool 評估**。當 App 變複雜、需要多個步驟才能完成像搜尋這樣的任務時就會用到工具；模型可能給出聽起來合理卻沒呼叫正確工具的答案，最終輸出看似正確但取得路徑不對。tool 評估讓你驗證「怎麼做」——正確的工具、正確的參數、正確的順序，並檢查中途有無非預期的工具呼叫。

deepdive.title: Define a tool's Generable argument
deepdive.body: BookTracker 加入 library assistant，串接 **searchBooks**、**getBookDetails**、**findSimilarBooks** 多個自訂工具。以 SearchBooksTool 為例，它符合 Tool 協定、有名稱與描述，參數是 **@Generable** struct 且全為 optional，讓模型依使用者意圖決定填哪些篩選（例如「找 gothic 書」填 tag、「找開心的」生成 mood 搜尋）。

deepdive.title: A basic trajectory expectation
deepdive.body: tool 評估的主角是 **TrajectoryExpectation**，它檢查一段 session transcript 中每個工具呼叫的種類與順序——像檢視規劃路線時做過的決策清單。最簡單的例子：prompt「Find books tagged gothic」期望一次 searchBooks 呼叫，用 **unordered** 表示不在意何時發生、只在意它發生。

deepdive.title: Match arguments by intent (naturalLanguage)
deepdive.body: 可在 expectation 加 arguments 進一步約束。**.exact** 比對精確值（如 tag「gothic」），但精確比對未必合適——prompt「Find something cheerful」時模型可能傳 uplifting／happy／cheerful，此時用 **.naturalLanguage** 比對意圖而非字串，並提供判定 criteria。框架另有 .contains、.oneOf、.pattern、.range 等多種 matcher。

deepdive.title: Expect tool calls in order
deepdive.body: 多步驟任務需要順序。用 **ordered** 指定模型必須先呼叫 searchBooks、再呼叫 getBookDetails；若代理先取詳情就還沒有 bookId，那是個 bug，而 TrajectoryExpectation 因為檢查的是「過程」而非只看終點，能抓到這種錯。

deepdive.title: Disallow specific tool calls
deepdive.body: 有時「不該做什麼」同樣重要。當 prompt 含「別找相似書」之類意圖時，模型應遵守，**disallowed** 參數指定不得出現在 transcript 中的工具；若代理仍呼叫了 findSimilarBooks，即判定失敗。

deepdive.title: Build a tool call evaluation
deepdive.body: 把各種 trajectory expectation 整合進完整評估：定義一組各含 prompt 與 TrajectoryExpectation 的樣本，用 **ToolCallEvaluator** 計分。ToolCallEvaluator 會把 LanguageModelSession 與工具結合、取得回應並擷取結構化 transcript，結果顯示在 Xcode assistant 中與其他結果並陳。

deepdive.title: Trajectory expectations
deepdive.body: 本章彙整 TrajectoryExpectation 的能力——它在 transcript 中找出所有工具呼叫，再逐一對照你寫進評估的 ordered／unordered／disallowed 與 argument matcher，全面驗證代理的決策路徑而非只看最終輸出。

deepdive.title: Synthesize tool-evaluation samples
deepdive.body: 由於 ModelSample 與 **TrajectoryExpectation 也是 Generable**，可像先前一樣用 SampleGenerator 合成更多 tool 評估樣本。關鍵差異是模型不知道你定義了哪些工具或順序需求，因此 sessionProvider 的指令須明列可用工具、用途、順序期望與其他必要情境，並用既有 dataset 當初始樣本、targetCount 設 100。

deepdive.title: Validate tool-evaluation samples
deepdive.body: 為 tool 評估樣本指定驗證 metric：每筆都必須有 expectations、至少參照一個工具（ordered 與 unordered 數量相加大於 0），且所有被參照的工具名都屬於已定義的有效集合（searchBooks、getBookDetails、findSimilarBooks）。如此即可合成並驗證 tool 評估樣本。

deepdive.title: Building a tool call evaluation
deepdive.body: 回到整合視角：稍早建的書籤標籤評估檢查「模型產出什麼」（標籤數、類型涵蓋、品質分數），tool 評估檢查「模型怎麼達成」（正確工具、參數、順序）。把兩者放進同一評估套件執行，即可對功能建立端到端的信心。

deepdive.title: Synthetic data for tool evaluations
deepdive.body: 再次強調合成資料 API 在 tool 評估上的威力：因 TrajectoryExpectation 為 Generable，可大幅簡化原本複雜的 tool 評估資料集擴充；資料越具代表性，分數就越貼近真實。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 結語鼓勵把這些做法應用到自己的 App 與評估資料集：試著製作合成資料、評估 App 中的自訂工具，並查閱範例 App 與開發者文件中的相關文章，將檢查「產出」與檢查「路徑」結合以提升評估的穩固度。

summary_en: Presented by Ada and Kyle from the Evaluations team, this session covers advanced use of the **Evaluations framework** to build robust, scalable evaluations for intelligence-powered features. New in Xcode 27, the framework supports macOS, iOS, watchOS, and visionOS. Continuing the hill-climbing process's Develop and Evaluate steps, it has two themes: growing your evaluation dataset with synthetic data, and building evaluations for agentic workflows that involve **tool calling**.

The first part uses BookTracker — a personal library app that auto-tags books from reviews — to frame the dataset problem: 13 hand-written samples give only a narrow window, so results can look great yet mislead. The framework exposes code-first synthetic-data APIs. The simplest, **makeSamples**, takes a prompt, an initial dataset, and a targetCount (the final total including your starting samples) and returns an async stream of new samples, using the on-device model by default. For more control, **SampleGenerator** lets you set a **sessionProvider** to choose the model (e.g. the larger-context **PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel**) and system instructions; the framework manages batch size and re-calls sessionProvider if the context window is exhausted mid-run, so instructions must be self-contained. You can also set a **samplingStrategy** (random or sliding window) for in-context examples and a **validator** closure to check each sample in isolation (review ≥100 chars, 3–8 tags, all lowercase); valid samples go to samples and failures to invalidSamples automatically.

After expanding from 13 to 100 samples, the new Xcode 27 **Evaluations Report** and **Compare** show the scores drop as expected — revealing the earlier feature only looked good because it wasn't tested comprehensively. Score changes could signal prompt/instruction issues, gaps in the feature, the evaluation design, or a dataset that's still not representative, which you can keep improving with the synthetic-data APIs.

In the second part Kyle covers **tool evaluations**: a model can give a reasonable-sounding answer without ever calling the right tool, so you must verify the how, not just the what. The core is a **TrajectoryExpectation**, which checks the kind and order of tool calls in a LanguageModelSession transcript. Use unordered/ordered to express whether sequence matters, **disallowed** to forbid tools, and argument matchers — **.exact**, **.naturalLanguage** (matching intent not exact string), .keyOnly, .range, .contains and more. A full evaluation uses **ToolCallEvaluator** to combine a LanguageModelSession with the tools, get a response, and capture the structured transcript for scoring. Because TrajectoryExpectation is Generable, you can synthesize tool-evaluation samples with SampleGenerator too — but your instructions must spell out available tools, order, and context, and a validator should confirm each sample has expectations, references at least one tool, and uses only defined tool names. Running tag evaluations (checking output) and tool evaluations (checking the path) in one suite gives end-to-end confidence in the feature.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Ada and Kyle introduce the **Evaluations framework** — a way to assess intelligence features in Swift apps, track improvements, and ensure production quality — new in **Xcode 27** and supporting macOS/iOS/watchOS/visionOS. The session targets complexity and scalability, split into synthetic data and tool evaluations, and points to the "Meet the Evaluations framework" and hill-climbing videos for fundamentals.

deepdive_en.title: The dataset problem in BookTracker
deepdive_en.body: Using **BookTracker** (auto-tags books from reviews), the Book class holds title, author, review, tags, and rating, with 13 sampleBooks. The presenters stress those 13 samples give only a narrow view — books, genres, and review styles vary enormously — so a small dataset can't capture the variety and results may look great yet mislead.

deepdive_en.title: Generating synthetic data with makeSamples
deepdive_en.body: Synthetic data is proposed as the answer. The framework defines sample generation entirely in code, supports text data, and uses the **@Generable** macro to produce structured synthetic data, so you can build a pipeline, run it from the command line, or plug it into existing workflows.

deepdive_en.title: Generate synthetic data with makeSamples
deepdive_en.body: **makeSamples** needs three things: a prompt, a dataset, and a targetCount. The example prompt asks for diverse reviews across genres, eras, cultures, and reader personas; the dataset is the 13 sampleBooks wrapped as **ModelSample** (review as prompt, tags as expected). targetCount is 100, but since it's the final total including starting samples, the model actually generates 87 new ones.

deepdive_en.title: Configure a custom SampleGenerator
deepdive_en.body: The on-device model suits most cases, but to bring your own model or customize instructions the framework provides **SampleGenerator** for full control over generation, introducing configurations beyond prompt/dataset/targetCount.

deepdive_en.title: Customizing generation with SampleGenerator
deepdive_en.body: The key is **sessionProvider** — a closure returning a LanguageModelSession that sets which model drives generation and the system instructions; the example uses the larger-context **PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel** with rules (review ≥100 chars, 3–8 lowercase tags, etc.). The framework auto-manages batch size and reuses one session across batches, but if the context window is exhausted mid-run it throws and gets a fresh session with no prior context — so instructions must be self-contained.

deepdive_en.title: Sampling strategies
deepdive_en.body: **samplingStrategy** controls how in-context examples are picked from the initial dataset. **random** selects a non-duplicate subset, good when initial samples have no meaningful order; **sliding window** steps through samples sequentially, skipping duplicates, for ordered datasets. The example uses random — also the default, so it isn't stated explicitly — since its samples aren't meaningfully ordered.

deepdive_en.title: Validating synthetic samples
deepdive_en.body: Rules in the sessionProvider instructions don't guarantee compliant output, so a **validator** closure accepts or rejects each generated sample. The validator runs per-sample in isolation with no view of other samples, so diversity and cross-sample length distribution need more judgment and can't be checked by it alone.

deepdive_en.title: Validate generated samples
deepdive_en.body: Rules are turned into systematically checkable items: review at least 100 characters (demoed with Frankenstein), tag count between 3 and 8, and all tags lowercase. These three validation metrics are defined on the SampleGenerator to confirm samples meet the expected structure.

deepdive_en.title: Access valid and invalid results
deepdive_en.body: During a run, samples passing validation collect in the generator's **samples** property while failures go automatically to **invalidSamples**; both update in real time and can be accessed mid-iteration (to check progress) or after the loop. Results can be used directly in the app or saved locally as a dataset.

deepdive_en.title: Comparing evaluation results
deepdive_en.body: Xcode 27 adds an **Evaluations Report** to visualize results. The 13-sample BookTaggingEvaluation scores high on relevance and usefulness, but the **Compare** button against the 100-sample dataset shows the scores drop as expected — proving the earlier strong performance only reflected an insufficiently comprehensive dataset.

deepdive_en.title: Tool calling and tool evaluations
deepdive_en.body: Kyle takes over for **tool evaluations**. As an app grows complex and needs multiple steps to complete a task like search, tools come in; a model may give a reasonable-sounding answer without calling the right tool, so the output can look correct while the path is wrong. Tool evaluations verify the how — correct tools, correct arguments, correct order — and check for unexpected tool calls along the way.

deepdive_en.title: Define a tool's Generable argument
deepdive_en.body: BookTracker adds a library assistant chaining **searchBooks**, **getBookDetails**, and **findSimilarBooks**. SearchBooksTool conforms to the Tool protocol with a name and description, and its arguments are a **@Generable** struct of all-optional fields, letting the model choose filters by intent (e.g. "find gothic books" populates tag; "something cheerful" generates a mood search).

deepdive_en.title: A basic trajectory expectation
deepdive_en.body: The main component is a **TrajectoryExpectation**, which checks the kind and order of each tool call in a session transcript — like reviewing the list of decisions you made planning a route. The simplest case: prompt "Find books tagged gothic" expects one searchBooks call, with **unordered** meaning you don't care when it happens, just that it does.

deepdive_en.title: Match arguments by intent (naturalLanguage)
deepdive_en.body: Arguments refine the expectation. **.exact** matches a precise value (tag "gothic"), but exact isn't always right — for "Find something cheerful" the model might pass uplifting/happy/cheerful, so **.naturalLanguage** matches intent rather than the exact string, with judging criteria. Other matchers include .contains, .oneOf, .pattern, and .range.

deepdive_en.title: Expect tool calls in order
deepdive_en.body: Multistep tasks need order. **ordered** requires searchBooks before getBookDetails; if an agent gets details first it has no bookId yet — a bug — and TrajectoryExpectation catches it because it checks the journey, not just the destination.

deepdive_en.title: Disallow specific tool calls
deepdive_en.body: Sometimes what an agent shouldn't do matters just as much. When a prompt says something like don't look for similar books, the model should comply; the **disallowed** parameter names tools that must not appear in the transcript, and if the agent calls findSimilarBooks anyway it's a failure.

deepdive_en.title: Build a tool call evaluation
deepdive_en.body: The trajectory expectations come together in a full evaluation: define a dataset of samples each with a prompt and a TrajectoryExpectation, and score them with **ToolCallEvaluator**. It combines a LanguageModelSession with the tools, gets a response, captures the structured transcript, and surfaces results in the Xcode assistant alongside the rest.

deepdive_en.title: Trajectory expectations
deepdive_en.body: This chapter ties together what trajectory expectations do — they find all tool calls in the transcript and run each against the ordered/unordered/disallowed rules and argument matchers you wrote, verifying the agent's decision path rather than just the final output.

deepdive_en.title: Synthesize tool-evaluation samples
deepdive_en.body: Because ModelSample and **TrajectoryExpectation are Generable**, you can synthesize more tool-evaluation samples with SampleGenerator as before. The key difference: the model doesn't know your tools or order requirements, so the sessionProvider instructions must list available tools, their purpose, order expectations, and other context, using the existing dataset as initial samples with a targetCount of 100.

deepdive_en.title: Validate tool-evaluation samples
deepdive_en.body: Validation metrics for tool-evaluation samples: each must have expectations, must reference at least one tool (ordered plus unordered count greater than 0), and all referenced tool names must belong to the defined valid set (searchBooks, getBookDetails, findSimilarBooks). That covers synthesizing and validating tool-evaluation samples.

deepdive_en.title: Building a tool call evaluation
deepdive_en.body: Back to the integrated view: the earlier book-tagging evaluation checks what the model produces (tag count, genre coverage, quality scores), while tool evaluations check how it gets there (right tools, arguments, order). Running both in the same evaluation suite builds end-to-end confidence in the feature.

deepdive_en.title: Synthetic data for tool evaluations
deepdive_en.body: The session reiterates the power of synthetic-data APIs for tool evaluations: because TrajectoryExpectation is Generable, expanding an otherwise complex tool-evaluation dataset is much easier, and the more representative the data, the more the scores reflect reality.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: The closing encourages applying these ideas to your own apps and datasets: make your own synthetic data, evaluate your app's custom tools, and check the sample app and developer documentation, combining checks on output with checks on the path to make evaluations more robust.

title: Build a responsive camera app that launches quickly
gloss: 打造啟動快速且反應靈敏的相機 App
takeaway: 用 AVFoundation 的延遲啟動、反應式擷取與確定性檔案寫入，打造瞬間啟動、不錯失畫面的相機 App。
chapters: Adopt AVProVideoStorage for deterministic file write speeds

points.text: 用**延遲啟動（deferred start）**讓相機**瞬間啟動**：先顯示預覽，再延後啟動非必要的輸出，避免錯失關鍵畫面。
可採**自動**或**手動**延遲啟動，透過 **automaticallyRunsDeferredStart**、isDeferredStartEnabled 與 **runDeferredStartWhenNeeded** 控制時機。
啟用**反應式擷取（responsive capture）**與穩定預覽，讓 **AVCapturePhotoOutput** 能立即拍照。
監控 **hardwareCost** 與 **systemPressureState** 維持持續效能，必要時改用低成本設定。
用 **AVProVideoStorage** 達成確定性的檔案寫入速度，妥善管理專業影片儲存空間。

audience: **開發相機或影音擷取 App**、在意啟動速度、拍攝反應與錄影效能的開發者。
gloss_en: Build a responsive camera app that launches quickly
takeaway_en: Use AVFoundation's deferred start, responsive capture, and deterministic file writing to build a camera app that launches instantly and never misses the shot.

points_en.text: Use **deferred start** to launch the camera **instantly**: show the preview first, then defer starting non-essential outputs to avoid missing the key moment.
Use **automatic** or **manual** deferred start, controlling the timing via **automaticallyRunsDeferredStart**, isDeferredStartEnabled, and **runDeferredStartWhenNeeded**.
Enable **responsive capture** and a stable preview so **AVCapturePhotoOutput** can take photos immediately.
Monitor **hardwareCost** and **systemPressureState** to maintain sustained performance, switching to lower-cost settings when necessary.
Use **AVProVideoStorage** to achieve deterministic file-write speeds and properly manage professional video storage.

audience_en: Developers **building camera or audio/video capture apps** who care about launch speed, capture responsiveness, and recording performance.
summary: 這場由相機效能團隊主講，核心訊息：相機 app 的「快」最關鍵的指標，是**第一張 preview 畫面多快出現在螢幕上**——慢一點點，使用者就會錯過瞬間（講者以掉落的骨牌示範）。整場聚焦四大主題：加速啟動、流暢渲染 preview、在嚴苛環境下維持效能，以及高位元率錄影的確定性寫檔。啟動序列分四階段：app 啟動、設定並啟動 session、初始化 AV capture output、preview 開始串流。

啟動最佳化的關鍵思維是把工作分成「**preview 顯示前必需**」與「**preview 跑起來後再做**」兩階段。UI 上只先建立 camera preview 與 shutter button，其餘（image well、mode picker 等）等啟動完成後淡入。`AVCaptureSession` 因為協調所有物件要最先建立，但它的建立、`startRunning`、`stopRunning` 都會**阻塞主執行緒**，必須 dispatch 到背景並只 commit 一次設定。最耗時的是**初始化 outputs**——只有 preview layer 或單一 output 是 preview 必需的；因此 iOS 26 新增 **Deferred Start API**：在不需於啟動時用到的 output 上設 `isDeferredStartEnabled = true`，把它們延後到 preview 出現後再初始化。實測啟動時間可**減半（2 倍快）**。

Deferred Start 有自動與手動兩種模式。**自動模式**（以 iOS 26+ SDK 重編譯後預設啟用，`automaticallyRunsDeferredStart = true`）由系統在 preview 出現後挑最佳時機初始化，並透過 `sessionWillRunDeferredStart` 與 `sessionDidRunDeferredStart` 兩個 delegate callback 通知；**手動模式**（設為 false）由 app 自行在準備好時呼叫 `runDeferredStartWhenNeeded`，適合需先讀偏好設定、或用 `AVCaptureVideoDataOutput` 自行渲染 preview 的情況（此時要追蹤第一張 frame 是否已呈現）。但延後 photo output 有個代價：preview 變快但首拍時間不變，因此要在 `AVCapturePhotoOutput` 設 **`isResponsiveCaptureEnabled = true`**，在開始拍攝與處理間加入緩衝，讓使用者即使 output 尚未就緒也能捕捉到瞬間。

渲染 preview 兩種選擇：`AVCaptureVideoPreviewLayer`（最簡單、低延遲、自動處理 HDR tone mapping，但無逐幀存取；用 iOS 26+ 重編譯自動納入 deferred start）與 `AVCaptureVideoDataOutput`（可逐幀處理、套 UI overlay、整合 Metal，但需手動採用 deferred start）。維持效能方面，用 **hardware cost** 與 **system pressure cost** 兩個 0–1 的 API 評估設定是否可持續（超過 1 即不支援），並觀察 `AVCaptureDevice` 的 **systemPressureState** 在壓力升高時降 frame rate、節流 GPU/ANE、減少 UI 工作；可用 frameRateOverride 與 binned format 降低成本。最後是 iOS 27 新增的 **`AVProVideoStorage`**——一個系統共用、預先配置的儲存資源，搭配既有錄影 API（在 `AVCaptureMovieFileOutput` 或 asset writer 設 `usesProVideoStorage`）為 ProRes 等高位元率編碼提供**確定性的寫檔速度**，避免掉幀。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: 相機效能團隊工程師 Jake 開場，點出啟動慢使用者一定有感，而讓相機「感覺快」的單一最重要因素是 **preview 畫面多快出現**。以中間放紅色骨牌的掉落示範說明：preview 太慢就會錯過瞬間。預告四大主題：加速啟動、渲染 preview 的最佳實務、維持效能的 API，以及高位元率錄影的確定性寫檔。

deepdive.title: Fast Launch
deepdive.body: 拆解啟動四階段：**app 啟動**（linker 載入、static initializer、建立 UI scene）、**設定並啟動 session**、**初始化 AV capture outputs**、**preview 開始串流**。建議把 UI 工作分兩階段：preview 必需的（camera preview、shutter button）先做，image well 與 mode picker 等啟動後再淡入；任何在 preview 渲染前建立的資源都會拖慢啟動。

deepdive.title: Adopt deferred start
deepdive.body: 初始化 outputs 是啟動最耗時的部分，但 preview 只需 preview layer 或單一 output。iOS 26+ 的 **Deferred Start API** 讓 app 把非啟動必需的 output 延後到 preview 出現後初始化——在每個 output（與 preview layer）上設 `isDeferredStartEnabled`，除渲染 preview 的 output 外全部延後。

deepdive.title: Automatic deferred start delegate
deepdive.body: 說明自動模式：以 iOS 26+ SDK 重編譯的 app 預設用自動模式（`automaticallyRunsDeferredStart` 為 true），系統在 preview 出現後不久挑最佳時機初始化延後的 output，並發出兩個 delegate callback：`sessionWillRunDeferredStart`（初始化前，適合建立背景資源）與 `sessionDidRunDeferredStart`（完成後，所有 output 就緒）。

deepdive.title: Adopt automatic deferred start
deepdive.body: 示範採用：先建立處理 delegate callback 的類別，在設定時於 `AVCaptureSession` 設 `automaticallyRunsDeferredStart = true`（iOS 26+ 重編譯已自動設好），對所有非啟動必需的 output（如 photo output）啟用 deferred start、用 preview layer 渲染 preview，掛上 delegate 後 commit 設定並 `startRunning`。

deepdive.title: Adopt manual deferred start
deepdive.body: 介紹手動模式，適合想先讀偏好設定或先設定 UI 再做重初始化的 app，或用 `AVCaptureVideoDataOutput` 自行渲染 preview 的情況。把 `automaticallyRunsDeferredStart` 設為 false，並在渲染 preview 的 output 上停用 deferred start，由 app 在啟動工作完成後自行呼叫 `runDeferredStartWhenNeeded`。

deepdive.title: Manage runDeferredStartWhenNeeded
deepdive.body: 示範手動模式的時機掌控：用 `AVCaptureVideoDataOutput` 自行渲染時，追蹤第一張 frame 是否已呈現（範例用 CAMetalLayer）。一旦第一張 frame 呈現，就設定非關鍵 UI 並呼叫 session 的 `runDeferredStartWhenNeeded` 啟動延後的 output；之後便無需特別處理。

deepdive.title: Enable responsive capture
deepdive.body: 點出延後 photo output 的代價：preview 變快但首拍時間不變，因為系統得先初始化完 photo output 才能拍。解法是在 `AVCapturePhotoOutput` 設 **`isResponsiveCaptureEnabled = true`**，在開始拍攝與處理間加入緩衝，讓使用者即使 output 尚未完全就緒也能捕捉到瞬間（綠機因此拍到骨牌、紫機則錯過）。

deepdive.title: Steady preview
deepdive.body: preview 跑起來後維持穩定 framerate 與節奏很重要，否則相機會卡。最簡單的渲染方式是 **`AVCaptureVideoPreviewLayer`**：為渲染 preview 最佳化、自動處理 HDR tone mapping、低 CPU/GPU 負擔、低延遲，但代價是無逐幀存取。需要更多控制（逐幀處理、自訂 overlay、整合 Metal 與分析 frame 資料）則改用 **`AVCaptureVideoDataOutput`**，但需自行採用手動 deferred start 才能拿到同樣的啟動加速。渲染時每幀工作要短以避免掉幀。

deepdive.title: Sustained performance
deepdive.body: 隨著加入更多相機或輸入裝置，設定的效能成本上升。介紹 **hardware cost** API（0–1，回報 session 硬體實際使用比例，超過 1 表示系統無法支援），影響因素包含相機數量、active format（1080p vs 4K）、frame rate（假設 format 的最大 frame rate，可用 frameRateOverride 降低）與是否用 binned format（分組像素、較省頻寬）。

deepdive.title: Monitor for system pressure
deepdive.body: 介紹 **system pressure cost** API（0–1，代表目前設定的成本，超過 1 即不可持續），並建議觀察 `AVCaptureDevice` 的 **systemPressureState**：壓力升高時降低裝置 frame rate、節流 GPU 或 Apple Neural Engine、減少 UI 工作。建議在初始設定後使用這些 API——commit 設定後確認 hardware cost 不超過裝置能力，再註冊 state 變化處理器隨系統狀態調整。

deepdive.title: Deterministic file writing
deepdive.body: 說明傳統檔案 I/O 因系統要兼顧多項操作、記憶體碎片與儲存磨損而**非確定性**，而 ProRes 等高位元率錄影需要持續的高頻寬 I/O 才能不掉幀。引出 iOS 27 新增、用來解決此問題的 `AVProVideoStorage`。

deepdive.title: Manage pro video storage
deepdive.body: **`AVProVideoStorage`** 是追蹤並管理預先配置儲存的系統級共用資源，搭配既有錄影 API：在 `AVCaptureMovieFileOutput`（或用 video data output 錄影時的 asset writer）設 `usesProVideoStorage` 即可,由系統處理配置與 I/O，讓高位元率編碼的寫檔速度保持一致。相機設定新增讓使用者控制配置多少儲存，並提供 remaining capacity 與 open settings 方法。

deepdive.title: Adopt AVProVideoStorage for deterministic file write speeds
deepdive.body: 示範採用流程：先以 `isProVideoStorageSupported` 確認支援、用 `shared` 取得單例，建立 movie file output、session、connection 並選 format，用 `isProVideoStorageSupported`（在 output 上）確認相容，錄影前確認儲存非忙於 resize 或處理檔案請求，最後開啟 pro video storage 並開始錄影。錄影寫入預配置儲存、結束後再搬到指定位置；同樣適用於 `AVAssetWriter`。最後建議搭配高品質 photo output 採用 deferred start、用 instruments 量測效能，並在真實嚴苛環境（如大熱天）測試。

summary_en: Presented by the camera performance team, the central message is that the single most important factor in a camera app feeling fast is **how quickly the first preview frame appears on screen**—a small delay and the user misses the moment (demoed with falling dominoes). The session covers four topics: accelerating launch, rendering preview smoothly, sustaining performance under stress, and deterministic file writing for high-bit-rate recording. The launch sequence has four stages: app launch, session configure and start, AV capture output initialization, and preview streaming.

The key launch idea is to split work into what's **needed before preview displays** and what can wait **after preview is running**. In the UI, create only the camera preview and shutter button first, fading in the rest (image well, mode picker) after launch. `AVCaptureSession` must be created first since it coordinates everything, but its creation, `startRunning`, and `stopRunning` all **block the main thread**, so dispatch off-main and commit configuration once. The most expensive step is **initializing outputs**—only a preview layer or single output is needed for preview—so iOS 26 adds the **Deferred Start API**: set `isDeferredStartEnabled = true` on outputs not needed at launch to postpone them until after preview appears. Measured launch time can be **halved (2x faster)**.

Deferred Start has automatic and manual modes. **Automatic** (default when recompiled against the iOS 26+ SDK, `automaticallyRunsDeferredStart = true`) lets the system pick the best time after preview appears, with `sessionWillRunDeferredStart` and `sessionDidRunDeferredStart` delegate callbacks; **manual** (set to false) has the app call `runDeferredStartWhenNeeded` when ready—useful for reading preferences first or rendering preview yourself with `AVCaptureVideoDataOutput` (tracking when the first frame is presented). Deferring the photo output has a catch: preview is faster but time-to-first-capture stays the same, so set **`isResponsiveCaptureEnabled = true`** on `AVCapturePhotoOutput` to buffer between starting a capture and processing, letting people grab the moment even before the output is fully ready.

For rendering preview there are two choices: `AVCaptureVideoPreviewLayer` (simplest, low-latency, automatic HDR tone mapping, but no per-frame access; auto-opted into deferred start when recompiled for iOS 26+) and `AVCaptureVideoDataOutput` (per-frame processing, UI overlays, Metal integration, but needs manual deferred start). To sustain performance, use the **hardware cost** and **system pressure cost** APIs (both 0–1; above 1 is unsupported) to check whether a configuration is sustainable, and observe `AVCaptureDevice`'s **systemPressureState** to reduce frame rate, throttle GPU/ANE, and minimize UI work as pressure rises; frameRateOverride and binned formats lower cost. Finally, iOS 27 adds **`AVProVideoStorage`**—a system-wide, pre-allocated storage resource that works with existing recording APIs (set `usesProVideoStorage` on `AVCaptureMovieFileOutput` or an asset writer) to deliver deterministic write speeds for high-bit-rate codecs like ProRes, avoiding dropped frames.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Camera performance engineer Jake opens, noting people notice slow launches and that the single most important factor in feeling fast is **how quickly preview appears**. A falling-dominoes demo (with a red domino in the middle) shows that slow preview misses the moment. Previews the four topics: accelerating launch, preview rendering best practices, performance-sustaining APIs, and deterministic file writing for high-bit-rate recording.

deepdive_en.title: Fast Launch
deepdive_en.body: Breaks launch into four stages: **app launch** (linker load, static initializers, UI scene creation), **configure and start the session**, **initialize AV capture outputs**, and **preview streaming**. Split UI work into two phases—create preview-critical UI (camera preview, shutter button) first, fade in image well and mode picker after; any resource created before preview renders slows launch.

deepdive_en.title: Adopt deferred start
deepdive_en.body: Initializing outputs is the most expensive launch step, but preview only needs a preview layer or single output. The iOS 26+ **Deferred Start API** lets apps postpone non-launch outputs until after preview appears—set `isDeferredStartEnabled` on each output (and the preview layer), deferring all except the one rendering preview.

deepdive_en.title: Automatic deferred start delegate
deepdive_en.body: Explains automatic mode: apps recompiled against iOS 26+ default to it (`automaticallyRunsDeferredStart` true), with the system initializing deferred outputs shortly after preview appears and firing two delegate callbacks: `sessionWillRunDeferredStart` (before init, good for background resources) and `sessionDidRunDeferredStart` (after, all outputs ready).

deepdive_en.title: Adopt automatic deferred start
deepdive_en.body: Shows adoption: create a delegate-handling class, set `automaticallyRunsDeferredStart = true` on `AVCaptureSession` during configuration (already true if recompiled for iOS 26+), enable deferred start on non-launch outputs (e.g., the photo output) while rendering preview with the preview layer, attach the delegate, commit, and `startRunning`.

deepdive_en.title: Adopt manual deferred start
deepdive_en.body: Introduces manual mode for apps that want to read preferences or set up UI before heavy init, or that render preview with `AVCaptureVideoDataOutput`. Set `automaticallyRunsDeferredStart` to false and disable deferred start on the preview-rendering output, then call `runDeferredStartWhenNeeded` once startup work is done.

deepdive_en.title: Manage runDeferredStartWhenNeeded
deepdive_en.body: Shows timing control in manual mode: when rendering preview yourself, track whether the first frame is presented (the example uses a CAMetalLayer). Once it is, set up non-critical UI and call the session's `runDeferredStartWhenNeeded` for the postponed outputs; no special handling is needed afterward.

deepdive_en.title: Enable responsive capture
deepdive_en.body: Notes the catch of deferring the photo output: preview is faster but time-to-first-capture stays the same, since the system must finish initializing it before capturing. The fix is `isResponsiveCaptureEnabled = true` on `AVCapturePhotoOutput`, which buffers between starting a capture and processing so people can grab the moment even if the output isn't fully ready (the green phone catches the dominoes; the purple one misses).

deepdive_en.title: Steady preview
deepdive_en.body: Once preview runs, a steady framerate and cadence matter or the camera feels laggy. The simplest renderer is **`AVCaptureVideoPreviewLayer`**: optimized for preview, automatic HDR tone mapping, low CPU/GPU overhead, low latency—at the cost of no per-frame access. For more control (per-frame processing, custom overlays, Metal, frame analysis), use **`AVCaptureVideoDataOutput`**, but adopt manual deferred start to keep the launch gains. Keep per-frame work short to avoid drops.

deepdive_en.title: Sustained performance
deepdive_en.body: As more cameras or inputs are added, the configuration's performance cost grows.
