The result is a tightly packed, staggered layout that preserves each item's natural proportions. You start with `display: grid-lanes`, add `grid-template-columns` and `gap`; swap columns for `grid-template-rows` to turn a waterfall into a brick wall.

Grid Lanes deliberately reuses existing Grid syntax and mental models. You can adjust column ratios with the `fr` unit, let the browser pick the column count with `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(...))`, and span an item across columns with `grid-column: span 2` or an explicit `grid-column: 2 / span 2` (you control column placement but not the row—Grid Lanes decides that). Inside a card, `grid-template-columns: subgrid` brings **Subgrid** in so child content aligns with the parent layout, and you can nest grids and grid-lanes inside one another freely.

Advanced control comes from **flow-tolerance**. By default the browser always drops the next item into the shortest column, but when two columns differ by only a few pixels this can flip visual order against tab order, hurting **accessibility**. flow-tolerance (default `1em`) is the dial that loosens this rule: if the taller column is still within the shorter column plus tolerance, the item stays put, avoiding left-right ping-ponging. When results surprise you, **Web Inspector** has full Grid Lanes support—overlaying column and row lines, per-item order numbers, and the gaps between items. Overall Grid Lanes replaces what used to require JavaScript with a few lines of CSS, and adapts the layout to your content rather than the other way around.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Safari engineer Brandon introduces **Grid Lanes**, a new web layout mode that lets items of any size flow naturally into available space. He frames it as the familiar **masonry layout**: vertically it reads like a waterfall, and flipped it becomes a brick wall of items flowing across rows. The key message is that there's no need to wait—it ships in **Safari 26.4** and is available behind a flag in other browsers.

deepdive_en.title: CSS Flexbox and Grid
deepdive_en.body: He steps back to note that every layout mode answers two questions: where items go and how much space they get. **Flexbox** offers one axis and a single lane with wrapping; **Grid** offers two dimensions, placing items into intersecting cells. The problem is that differing aspect ratios leave large empty areas in Grid, and stretching, zoom-cropping, or scaling all damage images—motivating a middle ground.

deepdive_en.title: CSS Grid Lanes
deepdive_en.body: He defines **Grid Lanes** as sitting between Grid and Flex: it structures only one direction and leaves the other free, but unlike Flex it distributes content across multiple lanes. Items are placed one by one into whichever column leaves them closest to the top, so earlier items sit higher and later ones fill below, producing a tightly packed staggered layout that preserves proportions. It works with any content—images or text, where text wraps and the browser sizes heights, and headlines can span columns.

deepdive_en.title: Build a Grid Lanes container
deepdive_en.body: The demo section begins, building a Grid Lanes container from scratch as the foundation for adding column definitions and properties step by step.

deepdive_en.title: Create a Grid Lanes Container
deepdive_en.body: Declare the container with `display: grid-lanes`, the first step that activates the entire layout mode.

deepdive_en.title: Create a Grid Lanes Container
deepdive_en.body: Add `grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr)` to define the tracks. He explains that **`fr`** (fractional unit) divides the container's available space into fractions—here three equal columns.

deepdive_en.title: Create a Grid Lanes Container
deepdive_en.body: Add `gap: 10px` for spacing between items, identical to Grid usage, completing a basic Grid Lanes container in three lines of CSS.

deepdive_en.title: Implement brick variation
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates converting the waterfall into a brick-wall variation, where the key is simply switching the structured direction.

deepdive_en.title: Implement a Brick Variation
deepdive_en.body: Replace `grid-template-columns` with `grid-template-rows`, instantly flipping the layout from a vertical waterfall into a horizontally flowing brick wall.

deepdive_en.title: Implement a Brick Variation
deepdive_en.body: He stresses the one catch: you pick one direction, not both—you cannot structure columns and rows simultaneously, which is the essential difference from two-dimensional Grid.

deepdive_en.title: Experiment with different layouts
deepdive_en.body: Shows that these three lines of CSS can yield surprisingly varied layouts, encouraging developers to experiment.

deepdive_en.title: Experiment with different layouts
deepdive_en.body: Starting from three equal columns, he shows columns need not be equal—using `1fr 2fr 1fr` makes the center column take twice the space of the sides.

deepdive_en.title: Experiment with different layouts
deepdive_en.body: Switching to `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(200px, 1fr))` lets the browser decide the column count: **`auto-fill`** packs in as many columns as fit, while **`minmax()`** keeps each at least 200px but lets it grow to fill space.

deepdive_en.title: Experiment with different layouts
deepdive_en.body: He extends the idea into a repeating pattern of narrow and wide columns via `minmax`, showing the flexibility achievable with minimal CSS.

deepdive_en.title: Experiment with different layouts
deepdive_en.body: He wraps up the experimentation by noting what he loves most is the expressiveness—rich variety from a few lines of CSS—and invites viewers to explore.

deepdive_en.title: Control individual items
deepdive_en.body: The focus shifts from the overall layout to shaping individual items, noting Grid Lanes can also control how a single item renders.

deepdive_en.title: Control Individual Items
deepdive_en.body: Back at a three-equal-column container, he shows that giving one item more space is done with properties that already exist in Grid.

deepdive_en.title: Control Individual Items
deepdive_en.body: Using `grid-column: span 2`, an item stretches across two columns and the rest of the layout adjusts around it automatically.

deepdive_en.title: Control Individual Items
deepdive_en.body: Switching to `grid-column: 2 / span 2` places the item precisely starting in column 2 and spanning columns 2 and 3. Key note: you control **column** placement, but Grid Lanes decides the **row** for you.

deepdive_en.title: Integrate Subgrid
deepdive_en.body: He demonstrates a two-column recipe card containing an image and text—content that by default does not participate in the parent Grid Lanes layout.

deepdive_en.title: Integrate Subgrid
deepdive_en.body: Adding `display: grid-lanes` and `grid-template-columns: subgrid` to the card lets its contents join the parent layout as their own items: the image takes one column, the text the other, each sized to its content.

deepdive_en.title: Integrate Subgrid
deepdive_en.body: He stresses arbitrary nesting: a regular Grid inside a Grid Lanes container or vice versa. The same tools and syntax carry over, so **Subgrid** and Grid Lanes integrate seamlessly.

deepdive_en.title: Flow Tolerance
deepdive_en.body: He introduces **flow-tolerance**. By default the browser always places the next item in the shortest column, but when columns differ by only a few pixels this can make rows read left-to-right then right-to-left, mismatching tab order and hurting **accessibility**. flow-tolerance loosens the rule: for each new item it asks whether the taller column is less than the shorter plus tolerance—if so the item stays, otherwise it drops into the shorter column. The default is `1em`, and he advises tuning it to your content.

deepdive_en.title: Improve item positioning
deepdive_en.body: Continuing the flow-tolerance idea, he shows how adjusting the tolerance value improves where items land so visual order better matches expectations.

deepdive_en.title: Improve item positioning
deepdive_en.body: Setting `flow-tolerance` to a concrete value (such as `2.1em`), he compares how different tolerances affect the arrangement to find what works for the content.

deepdive_en.title: Web Inspector
deepdive_en.body: He explains that when the browser's flexibility produces unexpected results, you can debug with **Web Inspector**. It fully supports Grid Lanes—turning on the overlay shows column and row lines, order numbers projected over each item, and the gaps between items.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: He concludes that Grid Lanes replaces JavaScript-dependent layouts with a few lines of CSS and adapts to your content. He recommends the WebKit team's **Grid Lanes Field Guide** with interactive demos, encourages trying it in projects and sending feedback, and points to 'What's new in WebKit for Safari 27.'

title: Rediscover the HTML select element
gloss: 重新認識 HTML select 元素
takeaway: 透過 appearance: base-select 與新的 CSS 偽元素，全面自訂網頁 select 選單的外觀與下拉內容。

points.text: 新的 **appearance: base-select** 解鎖對原生 select 表單控制項的完整樣式控制。
可用 **::picker(select)** 與 **:open** 狀態自訂下拉面板的邊框、陰影與圖示。
透過 **option::checkmark** 與 option:checked 自訂選項勾選標記與選取樣式。
選項可放入 **圖片** 並以 grid 版面排列，超越純文字選單。
用 **selectedcontent** 元素自訂按鈕顯示，並為不支援的瀏覽器準備 fallback。

audience: 需要 **深度自訂網頁表單下拉選單** 樣式與互動的前端 Web 開發者。
gloss_en: Rediscover the HTML select element
takeaway_en: Use appearance: base-select and new CSS pseudo-elements to fully customize the appearance and dropdown content of web select menus.

points_en.text: The new **appearance: base-select** unlocks full styling control over the native select form control.
Use **::picker(select)** with the **:open** state to customize the dropdown panel's border, shadow, and icons.
Use **option::checkmark** and option:checked to customize the option checkmark and selected styling.
Options can contain **images** and be laid out with grid, going beyond plain-text menus.
Use the **selectedcontent** element to customize the button display, and prepare a fallback for browsers that don't support it.

audience_en: Front-end web developers who need to **deeply customize the styling and interaction of web form dropdowns**.
summary: 這場由 Safari 工程師主講，介紹 web 上 HTML `<select>` 元素的重大升級——**Customizable select**（可自訂下拉選單）。過去要做出超越預設樣式的下拉選單，得靠大量 JavaScript 函式庫或一堆 `<div>`，無障礙也很棘手。現在從 **Safari 27 與 Chrome 135** 起，只用 HTML 與 CSS 就能完全自訂 `<select>`，同時保留語意化 HTML 的好處：鍵盤導覽、螢幕閱讀器支援與基本無障礙都是開箱即用。講者以替攝影師客戶打造作品集網站、做出排序與篩選選單為例貫穿全場。

啟用的關鍵是新的 **`appearance: base-select`**：套在 `<select>` 上即從原生控制項（在 Apple 平台稱 pull-down button）切換成可大量自訂的較小樣式集，並開始繼承 body 的 font-family。接著可自訂按鈕本身的 background、border、padding；用新的 **`::picker-icon`** 偽元素改箭頭（設 content 與 width），並用 **`:open`** 偽類在下拉開啟時改變顏色。要自訂下拉選單則用 **`::picker(select)`** 選取選單、同樣設 `appearance: base-select` 以脫離原生選單，再調整 padding、margin、border、box-shadow；用 `:checked` 強調已選 option，並用 **`::checkmark`** 偽元素自訂預設打勾（一樣設 content 與 width）。

Customizable select 最強之處是能**超越純文字選項**——option 內可放任何內容：images、videos、emojis、SVG。講者在每個 option 放 SVG 加 label 做出分類瀏覽（圖片 alt 留空以免螢幕閱讀器重複念出標籤），用 `:checked` 凸顯選中項。當符號讓下拉太長時，改用 **grid layout**（`grid-template` 定義行列、`gap` 定義間距）排成整齊網格——這正是重用其他 CSS 能力的好處。

若想讓選中 option 的豐富內容（如 SVG）也出現在按鈕中，需要兩個工具：把一個 `<button>` 放進 `<select>` 作為第一個子元素來**取代內建按鈕**（過去 HTML 不允許），以及用新的 **`<selectedcontent>`** 元素在按鈕內顯示選中 option 的豐富內容。最後強調**漸進增強（progressive enhancement）**：不支援此功能的瀏覽器會回退到原生彈出選單，因為重用了語意化 `<select>`，內建無障礙特性依然保留。講者也提到用 Safari 的 **Grid Lanes** 排版圖片，並建議用 Safari Technology Preview 或 Beta 試用、務必在不支援的瀏覽器與輔助工具上測試。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: Safari 工程師 Tim 開場，點出 web 開發者長年在下拉選單上的掙扎：超越預設 `<select>` 得靠重量級 JavaScript 或一堆 `<div>`，無障礙也難處理。介紹 **Customizable select**——從 **Safari 27 與 Chrome 135** 起只用 HTML 與 CSS 就能完全自訂，並以替攝影師客戶打造作品集網站、加入排序篩選為示範。

deepdive.title: Basic markup
deepdive.body: 回顧 `<select>` 加 label 的 HTML 標記。強調原生 `<select>` 開箱即具基本無障礙：可用鍵盤導覽 option、與螢幕閱讀器良好搭配，無需外部函式庫，並用它建立頁面的 Sort by 按鈕。

deepdive.title: Style the select button
deepdive.body: 說明可點擊以顯示選單的部分即「按鈕」，將從這最基本的部分開始自訂樣式。

deepdive.title: Native form control
deepdive.body: 展示原生控制項（在 Apple 平台稱 pull-down button）——它匹配平台上其他控制項給使用者熟悉感，但放到攝影網站上會顯得格格不入，引出 Customizable select 的需求。

deepdive.title: appearance: base-select
deepdive.body: 自訂第一步是套用 **`appearance: base-select`**，從原生控制項切換成較小、可自訂的樣式集。因先前在 body 設了 Gill Sans，按鈕現在會繼承 body 字型，與旁邊的 label 一致。

deepdive.title: Style the select button
deepdive.body: 進一步調整按鈕的 background、border 與 padding，讓它更貼合網站設計。

deepdive.title: Picker icon
deepdive.body: 用新的 **`::picker-icon`** 選擇器改箭頭：設 content 屬性換成新字符、設 width 調整大小。

deepdive.title: Picker icon open state
deepdive.body: 用 **`:open`** 偽類在下拉選單開啟時為按鈕設不同顏色，並把箭頭更新成符合開啟狀態的文字色。

deepdive.title: Customize the drop-down
deepdive.body: 介紹下拉選單本身的可樣式化部件：用 **`::picker(select)`** 樣式化選單、用 option 上的 **`::checkmark`** 樣式化打勾。

deepdive.title: Picker select
deepdive.body: 用 **`::picker(select)`** 並設 `appearance: base-select` 來脫離原生選單、取得乾淨起點，準備自訂下拉。

deepdive.title: Picker select spacing
deepdive.body: 用 padding 與 margin 安排下拉選單的間距。

deepdive.title: Picker select border and shadow
deepdive.body: 處理下拉選單的 border 與 box-shadow。

deepdive.title: Custom option styles
deepdive.body: 強調已選 option 讓使用者清楚自己選了什麼：在 `:checked` 的 option 設粗體字、把其他 option 變灰。

deepdive.title: Picker option checkmark
deepdive.body: 用 **`::checkmark`** 選擇器設 content 與 width 改變預設打勾，做法與 `::picker-icon` 類似。

deepdive.title: Go beyond text options
deepdive.body: 介紹 Customizable select 能超越純文字選項，option 內可放 images、videos、emojis 等任何內容，並以加入熱門攝影分類瀏覽的功能為例。

deepdive.title: Images in option
deepdive.body: 在每個 option 放 SVG 與 label 讓使用者更易探索分類；圖片 alt 留空，避免螢幕閱讀器重複念出標籤（如 Flowers）。

deepdive.title: Custom option highlight
deepdive.body: 因移除了打勾，用 `:checked` 選擇器改變顏色，更醒目地凸顯選中的 option。

deepdive.title: Grid layout in drop downs
deepdive.body: 符號讓下拉太長、版面不合視窗時，改用 **grid layout**：`grid-template` 定義行列數、`gap` 定義格間距，把下拉排成整齊網格，這也展現重用其他 CSS 能力的好處。

deepdive.title: Select with image options
deepdive.body: 整合前述樣式做出含圖片選項的 select，呈現分類瀏覽的完整效果。

deepdive.title: The selectedcontent element
deepdive.body: 想讓選中 option 的 SVG 也出現在按鈕中——但內建按鈕只顯示文字，引出 **`<selectedcontent>`** 元素來顯示選中 option 的豐富內容。

deepdive.title: Select menu
deepdive.body: 說明 select 自帶一個供點擊以開啟下拉的按鈕，作為自訂按鈕內容的鋪陳。

deepdive.title: Select menu button
deepdive.body: 把一個 `<button>` 放進 `<select>` 作為第一個子元素來**取代內建按鈕**（過去 HTML 不允許），即可在按鈕內放自訂內容，如 label 或 `<selectedcontent>`。

deepdive.title: SelectedContent Element
deepdive.body: **`<selectedcontent>`** 的特別之處是它會顯示選中 option 的豐富內容，例如 Everything 標籤旁的 SVG，讓按鈕反映選取結果。

deepdive.title: Fallback for unsupported browsers
deepdive.body: 強調**漸進增強**：不支援的瀏覽器仍可用，使用者拿到原生彈出選單。這正是重用 `<select>` 的好處——因為是語意化元素，內建無障礙特性依然保留。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 總結 select 元素與網站融為一體、並提到加了用 Customizable select 做的徑向色彩選擇器、用 Safari 的 **Grid Lanes** 排版圖片。功能將隨 Safari 27 推出，可用 Safari Technology Preview 或 Beta 試用,並務必在不支援的瀏覽器與輔助工具上測試,參考 webkit.org 的最佳實務。

summary_en: Presented by a Safari engineer, this session covers a major upgrade to the HTML `<select>` element on the web: **Customizable select**. Previously, going beyond the default required heavy JavaScript libraries or piles of `<div>`s, and accessibility was tricky. Now, starting in **Safari 27 and Chrome 135**, you can fully customize `<select>` using just HTML and CSS while keeping the benefits of semantic HTML—keyboard navigation, screen reader support, and basic accessibility are there out of the box. The presenter runs through building sort and filter menus for a photographer client's portfolio site.

The key is the new **`appearance: base-select`**: applied to `<select>`, it switches from the native control (called a pull-down button on Apple platforms) to a smaller, customizable set of styles and inherits the body font-family. You can then style the button's background, border, and padding; change the arrow with the new **`::picker-icon`** pseudo-element (setting content and width); and use the **`:open`** pseudo-class to change colors when the drop-down is open. To customize the drop-down, use **`::picker(select)`** with `appearance: base-select` to opt out of the native menu, then adjust padding, margin, border, and box-shadow; emphasize the selected option with `:checked` and customize the default checkmark with the **`::checkmark`** pseudo-element (also content and width).

The most powerful aspect is going **beyond text-only options**—an option can hold any content: images, videos, emojis, SVG. The presenter places an SVG and label in each option for category browsing (leaving image alt empty so screen readers don't read the label twice) and highlights the selection with `:checked`. When symbols make the drop-down too long, a **grid layout** (`grid-template` for rows/columns, `gap` for spacing) arranges it neatly—exactly the benefit of reusing other CSS features.

To get the selected option's rich content (like its SVG) into the button, two tools are needed: place a `<button>` as the first child of `<select>` to **replace the built-in button** (previously disallowed in HTML), and use the new **`<selectedcontent>`** element to show the selected option's rich content inside the button. Finally, it stresses **progressive enhancement**: unsupported browsers fall back to the native pop-up, and because the semantic `<select>` is reused, built-in accessibility features remain. The presenter also mentions using Safari's **Grid Lanes** to lay out images, and recommends trying it in Safari Technology Preview or Beta and testing in unsupported browsers and with assistive tools.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Safari engineer Tim opens, noting web developers' long struggle with drop-downs: going beyond the default `<select>` meant heavy JavaScript or many `<div>`s, with tricky accessibility. Introduces **Customizable select**—fully customizable with just HTML and CSS starting in **Safari 27 and Chrome 135**—demoed by building sort and filter controls for a photographer client's portfolio site.

deepdive_en.title: Basic markup
deepdive_en.body: Reviews the `<select>` markup with its label, stressing that the native `<select>` has basic accessibility out of the box: keyboard navigation of options and good screen reader support with no external libraries, used to build the page's Sort by button.

deepdive_en.title: Style the select button
deepdive_en.body: Identifies the clickable part that shows the menu as the 'button', the most basic part to start styling.

deepdive_en.title: Native form control
deepdive_en.body: Shows the native control (a pull-down button on Apple platforms)—it matches other platform controls for familiarity but feels out of place on the photo site, motivating Customizable select.

deepdive_en.title: appearance: base-select
deepdive_en.body: The first customization step is applying **`appearance: base-select`**, switching from the native control to a smaller, customizable style set. Since Gill Sans was set on the body, the button now inherits the body font, matching the adjacent label.

deepdive_en.title: Style the select button
deepdive_en.body: Adjusts the button's background, border, and padding to better match the site's design.

deepdive_en.title: Picker icon
deepdive_en.body: Uses the new **`::picker-icon`** selector to change the arrow: set the content property to a new glyph and a width to size it.

deepdive_en.title: Picker icon open state
deepdive_en.body: Uses the **`:open`** pseudo-class to set different button colors when the drop-down is open, updating the arrow to match the open state's text color.

deepdive_en.title: Customize the drop-down
deepdive_en.body: Introduces the drop-down's styleable parts: **`::picker(select)`** for the menu and **`::checkmark`** on the option for the check.

deepdive_en.title: Picker select
deepdive_en.body: Uses **`::picker(select)`** with `appearance: base-select` to opt out of the native menu for a clean slate before customizing the drop-down.

deepdive_en.title: Picker select spacing
deepdive_en.body: Arranges the drop-down's spacing with padding and margin.

deepdive_en.title: Picker select border and shadow
deepdive_en.body: Handles the drop-down's borders and box-shadow.

deepdive_en.title: Custom option styles
deepdive_en.body: Emphasizes the selected option so the choice is clear: set bold font on the `:checked` option and gray out the others.

deepdive_en.title: Picker option checkmark
deepdive_en.body: Uses the **`::checkmark`** selector with content and width to change the default checkmark, similar to `::picker-icon`.

deepdive_en.title: Go beyond text options
deepdive_en.body: Introduces going beyond text-only options—an option can hold any content like images, videos, and emojis—exemplified by adding browsing of popular photography categories.

deepdive_en.title: Images in option
deepdive_en.body: Places an SVG and label in each option so customers can explore categories; image alt is left empty to avoid screen readers announcing the label (e.g., Flowers) twice.

deepdive_en.title: Custom option highlight
deepdive_en.body: Since the checkmark was removed, uses the `:checked` selector to change colors and highlight the selected option more prominently.

deepdive_en.title: Grid layout in drop downs
deepdive_en.body: When symbols make the drop-down too long for the window, a **grid layout** (`grid-template` for rows/columns, `gap` for spacing) arranges it into a neat grid, showing the benefit of reusing other CSS features.

deepdive_en.title: Select with image options
deepdive_en.body: Combines the prior styling into a select with image options, showing the complete category-browsing result.

deepdive_en.title: The selectedcontent element
deepdive_en.body: Wants the selected option's SVG in the button too—but the built-in button shows only text—introducing the **`<selectedcontent>`** element to display the selected option's rich content.

deepdive_en.title: Select menu
deepdive_en.body: Notes that select comes with a button people click to open the drop-down, setting up custom button content.

deepdive_en.title: Select menu button
deepdive_en.body: Places a `<button>` as the first child of `<select>` to **replace the built-in button** (previously disallowed in HTML), letting you put custom content inside, like labels or `<selectedcontent>`.

deepdive_en.title: SelectedContent Element
deepdive_en.body: What's special about **`<selectedcontent>`** is that it shows the selected option's rich content—like the SVG next to the Everything label—so the button reflects the selection.

deepdive_en.title: Fallback for unsupported browsers
deepdive_en.body: Stresses **progressive enhancement**: unsupported browsers stay usable, giving customers the native pop-up. That's a benefit of reusing `<select>`—being a semantic element, built-in accessibility features remain.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Wraps up with the select elements blending into the site, plus a radial color picker built with Customizable select and images laid out with Safari's **Grid Lanes**. The features arrive in Safari 27; try them in Safari Technology Preview or Beta, test in unsupported browsers and with assistive tools, and see webkit.org for best practices.

title: Build with the new Apple Foundation Model on Private Cloud Compute
gloss: 在 Private Cloud Compute 上使用全新 Apple Foundation Model 開發
takeaway: 只需一行改用 PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel，即可在保護隱私的前提下取用前沿級模型，並享有更大 context、推理層級控制與用量限制處理。
chapters: Switch to the PCC server model (one-line change)
Structured output and tools work the same

points.text: **Private Cloud Compute（PCC）** 讓你存取**前沿級模型**同時保護使用者隱私，只需把模型換成 **PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel**（一行變更）。
**結構化輸出（@Generable）與工具呼叫**在 PCC 上用法完全相同；可用 model.isAvailable 檢查可用性。
可透過 **ContextOptions(reasoningLevel:)** 設定 .light/.moderate/.deep 推理層級；PCC 的 **contextSize 達 32768**，遠大於裝置端。
用 **quotaUsage** 處理**用量限制**：偵測接近上限、超出，並可顯示 limitIncreaseSuggestion 引導使用者。

audience: **想在 App 中使用更強大模型、又需兼顧隱私**的開發者，尤其需要大 context 或深度推理的情境。
gloss_en: Build with the new Apple Foundation Model on Private Cloud Compute
takeaway_en: With a single line switching to PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel, you can access frontier-class models while protecting privacy, gaining a larger context, reasoning-level control, and quota handling.

points_en.text: **Private Cloud Compute (PCC)** lets you access **frontier-class models** while protecting user privacy; just swap the model for **PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel** (a one-line change).
**Structured output (@Generable) and tool calling** work exactly the same on PCC; use model.isAvailable to check availability.
Set the reasoning level to .light/.moderate/.deep via **ContextOptions(reasoningLevel:)**; PCC's **contextSize reaches 32768**, far larger than on-device.
Use **quotaUsage** to handle **usage limits**: detect approaching the cap or exceeding it, and show limitIncreaseSuggestion to guide the user.

audience_en: **Developers who want to use more powerful models in their apps while balancing privacy**, especially in scenarios needing large context or deep reasoning.
summary: 這場由 Louis 主講的 session 介紹如何在 app 中透過 **Private Cloud Compute (PCC)** 使用一個強大的全新伺服器端 LLM。去年 Apple 以 **Foundation Models** 框架開放了 on-device LLM,今年不僅讓 on-device 模型更強(支援圖片輸入、更好的指令遵循與自訂 tool 呼叫),還新增了一個跑在 PCC 上的伺服器模型,用來處理更複雜的使用情境——例如需要對大量使用者輸入做推理的助理、或大量 tool 呼叫與大型輸出的功能,甚至可從 watchOS 呼叫。

PCC 最大的價值在於兼顧能力與隱私:它以端對端隱私設計,確保使用者資料絕不被儲存、僅用於當次請求,且經獨立研究者驗證。因為 PCC 與 OS 及 iCloud 整合,開發者完全不需處理 authentication 或 API key,使用者只要有支援 **Apple Intelligence** 的裝置即可;對開發者也沒有 token 費用,每位使用者有每日額度,可升級 **iCloud+** 取得更高上限。此功能開放給下載量低於 2M 的 app,可即日於開發者網站申請。

整合極為簡單:原本用 Foundation Models 呼叫 on-device LLM 只需 3 行(建立 session、呼叫 respond),要切換到 PCC 伺服器模型只要改 1 行——把 model 換成 **PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel()**。框架提供統一的 Swift API,**@Generable** 的結構化輸出與 **Tool** 呼叫在兩種模型上用法完全相同,可輕鬆切換而不必改寫程式碼。同樣地,PCC 也僅在 Apple Intelligence 裝置上可用,務必檢查 availability 並優雅處理不可用情況。on-device 與 PCC 的差異包括:前者離線可用、無請求限制、context 為 4K;後者需網路連線、有每日額度、context 達 32K 且支援 reasoning。

PCC 的 reasoning 讓模型在產生回應前先「思考」,即在 transcript 的獨立區段生成額外文字,分為 **.light**、**.moderate**、**.deep** 三級,可透過 respond 的 `ContextOptions` 設定;reasoning 文字會占用 token 與 context size,可觀察 transcript 顯示進度。新增的 `contextSize` 屬性可程式化讀取模型 context 大小。講者強調選擇模型或 reasoning 等級應依資料而非感覺,因此推出全新的 **Evaluations** 框架(整合於 Xcode)來評估你的功能品質。最後是 usage limit 處理:請求以使用者的 iCloud 帳號計算,應檢查 model 的 `quotaUsage`(`isLimitReached`、`isApproachingLimit`、`limitIncreaseSuggestion`),用持續存在的 UI(如按鈕下方的 label,而非 alert)告知使用者並提供提升額度的選項;Xcode 的 scheme Debug Options 還能模擬額度狀態以便測試。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: 主講人 **Louis** 開場說明這支影片要教你如何透過 **Private Cloud Compute** 在 app 中使用強大的全新伺服器 LLM。去年的 **Foundation Models** 框架帶來 on-device LLM,今年該模型更強(支援圖片輸入、更好的指令遵循與 tool 呼叫),並針對更複雜需求新增 PCC 伺服器模型,可建構會對大量輸入做推理的助理、或需大量 tool 呼叫與大型輸出的功能,甚至能從 watchOS 呼叫。

deepdive.title: What is Private Cloud Compute
deepdive.body: **Private Cloud Compute** 原本驅動系統功能,把複雜任務送到 Apple 伺服器,現在也開放給 app 使用,讓你存取強大伺服器 LLM 而不犧牲隱私。它以端對端隱私設計,使用者資料絕不被儲存、只用於當次請求,並經獨立研究者驗證。因與 OS 及 iCloud 整合,無需 authentication 或 API key,使用者只要有 Apple Intelligence 裝置即可;對開發者沒有 token 費用,每位使用者有每日額度,可升級 **iCloud+** 提高上限,且開放給下載量低於 2M 的 app 申請。

deepdive.title: Integrating PCC with Foundation Models
deepdive.body: 進入如何用 **Foundation Models** 框架整合 PCC 的環節。重點是整套整合都建立在去年既有的 Foundation Models API 之上,讓既有 app 能以最小改動取得伺服器模型的能力。

deepdive.title: Prompt the on-device model
deepdive.body: 回顧既有用法:用 Foundation Models 呼叫 on-device LLM 只需 3 行——建立 **LanguageModelSession**,再呼叫 `respond(to:)` 傳入 prompt(例如請它摘要一篇文章)。這作為對照,凸顯接下來切換到 PCC 有多容易。

deepdive.title: Switch to the PCC server model (one-line change)
deepdive.body: 只要改 1 行就能切到 PCC 伺服器模型:在 LanguageModelSession 的初始化傳入 `model: PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel()`。改完這行,你就在和一個更大、context 更大、推理能力更強的模型對話,其餘程式碼維持不變。

deepdive.title: Structured output and tools work the same
deepdive.body: 框架提供統一的 Swift API,不論呼叫哪個模型都一致。用 **@Generable** 取得結構化輸出(例如含 oneLineSummary 與 keyPoints 的 ArticleSummary)、或呼叫 **Tool**(如 FindRelatedArticlesTool),在 PCC 模型上的用法與 on-device 完全相同,讓你能輕鬆在兩者間切換而不必改寫程式碼。

deepdive.title: Check availability
deepdive.body: 與 on-device 模型一樣,PCC 也只在 Apple Intelligence 裝置上可用。務必檢查 availability API 並優雅處理 Apple Intelligence 不可用的情況,範例以 `model.isAvailable` 在 view 中決定要顯示發送請求的 UI 還是 fallback。

deepdive.title: Deciding between on-device and PCC
deepdive.body: 比較 on-device System 模型與 PCC 模型:兩者皆保有隱私,但 on-device 可離線、無請求限制、context 為 4K;PCC 需網路連線、有每日額度、context 達 32K 且支援 reasoning。選哪個模型是撰寫功能時的重要決定。

deepdive.title: Reasoning levels and context size
deepdive.body: 解釋 reasoning:一般 LLM 讀 prompt 後直接生成回應,而 reasoning 讓模型先「思考」,在 transcript 的獨立區段生成額外文字。PCC 提供三級:**.light** 蒐集一些額外脈絡、**.moderate** 推理稍深、**.deep** 的推理文字甚至可能比實際回應還長。但要記得 reasoning 是額外生成的文字,會用掉 token 並計入 context size 上限。

deepdive.title: Set a reasoning level
deepdive.body: 示範在對 session 呼叫 respond 時透過 `ContextOptions(reasoningLevel:)` 設定 reasoning 等級(.light/.moderate/.deep)。session 的 transcript 會包含 reasoning 區段,可觀察 transcript 顯示進度——對可能耗時較久的 **.deep** 等級尤其有用。

deepdive.title: Read the context size
deepdive.body: 介紹方便的 `contextSize` 屬性,可程式化取得模型的 context 大小:`SystemLanguageModel().contextSize` 在 26.0 為 4096、27.0(較新裝置)為 8192,而 `PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel().contextSize` 為 32768。這讓你能依模型實際容量做決策。

deepdive.title: Evaluating and combining models
deepdive.body: 強調選擇 on-device 或 PCC、以及決定 reasoning 等級,應依資料而非「憑感覺」。你可能會驚訝今年更新後的 on-device 模型在某些任務表現得多好,但唯有評估才能確知。為此推出全新、整合於 Xcode 的 **Evaluations** 框架(詳見 "Meet the Evaluations framework");並可將 on-device 與伺服器模型搭配使用(詳見 "Build agentic app experiences with Foundation Models")。

deepdive.title: Handling usage limits
deepdive.body: 說明使用 PCC 時妥善處理 usage limit 的重要性:請求以使用者的 iCloud 帳號計算。以一個用 PCC 摘要文章(含文字與圖片)的 app 為例,當使用者達到上限時請求會丟出錯誤,若只是把錯誤顯示在 UI 上對使用者並不友善、也不夠 actionable,因此需要更好的處理方式。

deepdive.title: Handle usage limits
deepdive.body: 具體做法是檢查 model 的 `quotaUsage`:用 `isLimitReached` 判斷是否超限並以自訂 UI(如按鈕下方的 label)處理,超限時顯示按鈕讓使用者管理額度(例如升級帳號);也可用 `isApproachingLimit` 偵測接近上限。應整合進既有 UI、避免用會被關閉的 alert,改以持續存在的狀態(如停用發送按鈕、顯示低調 label)呈現。Xcode 的 scheme Debug Options 提供 "Simulate Apple Foundation Models Availability",可模擬 Quota Usage Limit Reached 與 Nearing Usage Limit 兩種狀態以便測試。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 總結整合 PCC 的概觀,並鼓勵想使用此新伺服器模型者即日於開發者網站申請。建議從 "What's new in the Foundation Models framework" 開始了解全貌,並可參考 "Debug and profile agentic app experiences with Instruments" 以理解模型在執行期的行為。

summary_en: In this session, Louis shows how to access a powerful new server-side LLM in your apps via **Private Cloud Compute (PCC)**. Last year Apple opened up an on-device LLM through the **Foundation Models** framework; this year the on-device model is even better (image input, improved instruction following, better custom tool calling), and a new server model running on PCC is added for more complex use cases—assistants that reason over large user input, or features that make many tool calls with large outputs—and it can even be called from watchOS.

PCC's key value is combining capability with privacy: it's designed for end-to-end privacy, ensuring user data is never stored and only used for the request, independently verified by researchers. Because PCC is integrated into the OS together with iCloud, developers don't deal with authentication or API keys—users just need a device that supports **Apple Intelligence**. There are no token costs to the developer; each user gets a daily limit and can upgrade to **iCloud+** for higher limits. The feature is available for apps with under 2M downloads, and you can apply on the developer website today.

Integration is remarkably simple: prompting the on-device LLM with Foundation Models takes just 3 lines (create a session, call respond), and switching to the PCC server model takes just 1 line—swap in **PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel()**. The framework offers a unified Swift API, so structured output with **@Generable** and **Tool** calling work the same on both models, letting you switch without rewriting code. Like the on-device model, PCC is only available on Apple Intelligence devices, so you must check availability and gracefully handle when it's unavailable. Differences: on-device works offline, has no request limits, and a 4K context; PCC needs an internet connection, has a daily limit, a 32K context, and supports reasoning.

PCC's reasoning lets the model "think" before responding by generating extra text in a separate transcript segment, across three levels—**.light**, **.moderate**, **.deep**—set via `ContextOptions` on respond; reasoning text consumes tokens and counts toward context size, and you can observe the transcript to show progress. A new `contextSize` property reads a model's context size programmatically. Louis stresses choosing a model or reasoning level based on data, not vibes, introducing the new **Evaluations** framework integrated into Xcode to assess your feature's quality. Finally, on usage limits: requests count against the user's iCloud account, so check the model's `quotaUsage` (`isLimitReached`, `isApproachingLimit`, `limitIncreaseSuggestion`) and surface it with persistent UI (a label under the button, not an alert) that offers a way to raise the limit; Xcode's scheme Debug Options can even simulate the quota states for testing.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: **Louis** opens by explaining the video teaches how to use a powerful new server LLM in your apps via **Private Cloud Compute**. Last year's **Foundation Models** framework brought an on-device LLM; this year that model is stronger (image input, better instruction following and tool calling), and a new PCC server model is added for more complex needs—assistants that reason over large input, or features with many tool calls and large outputs—even callable from watchOS.

deepdive_en.title: What is Private Cloud Compute
deepdive_en.body: **Private Cloud Compute** already powers system features by sending complex tasks to Apple's servers, and is now opened to apps, giving access to a powerful server LLM without compromising privacy. It's designed for end-to-end privacy—user data is never stored, only used for the request—and independently verified. Integrated with the OS and iCloud, it needs no authentication or API keys; users just need an Apple Intelligence device. There are no token costs to developers, each user gets a daily limit, **iCloud+** raises it, and the feature is open to apps with under 2M downloads.

deepdive_en.title: Integrating PCC with Foundation Models
deepdive_en.body: This section turns to integrating PCC using the **Foundation Models** framework. The point is that the whole integration builds on last year's existing Foundation Models API, letting existing apps gain server-model capability with minimal changes.

deepdive_en.title: Prompt the on-device model
deepdive_en.body: A recap of existing usage: prompting the on-device LLM with Foundation Models takes just 3 lines—create a **LanguageModelSession** and call `respond(to:)` with your prompt (e.g., asking it to summarize an article). This serves as the baseline that highlights how easy switching to PCC is.

deepdive_en.title: Switch to the PCC server model (one-line change)
deepdive_en.body: Switching to the PCC server model takes just 1 line: pass `model: PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel()` when initializing the LanguageModelSession. With that single change you're talking to a much larger model with larger context and stronger reasoning, while the rest of the code stays the same.

deepdive_en.title: Structured output and tools work the same
deepdive_en.body: The framework offers a unified Swift API regardless of which model you call. Getting structured output with **@Generable** (e.g., an ArticleSummary with oneLineSummary and keyPoints) or calling a **Tool** (like FindRelatedArticlesTool) works exactly the same on the PCC model as on-device, letting you switch between them without rewriting code.

deepdive_en.title: Check availability
deepdive_en.body: Just like the on-device model, PCC is only available on Apple Intelligence devices. You must check the availability API and gracefully handle when Apple Intelligence isn't available; the example uses `model.isAvailable` in a view to decide whether to show the request UI or a fallback.

deepdive_en.title: Deciding between on-device and PCC
deepdive_en.body: A comparison of the on-device System model and the PCC model: both offer privacy, but on-device works offline, has no request limits, and a 4K context; PCC needs an internet connection, has a daily per-user limit, a 32K context, and supports reasoning. Choosing which model to use is an important decision when writing a feature.

deepdive_en.title: Reasoning levels and context size
deepdive_en.body: Reasoning is explained: a normal LLM reads the prompt and generates a response, while reasoning lets the model "think" first by generating extra text in a separate transcript segment. PCC offers three levels: **.light** gathers some extra context, **.moderate** reasons a little deeper, and **.deep** may produce reasoning text even longer than the response. But reasoning is extra generated text, so it uses tokens and counts toward the context size limit.

deepdive_en.title: Set a reasoning level
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates setting the reasoning level via `ContextOptions(reasoningLevel:)` (.light/.moderate/.deep) when calling respond on a session. The session's transcript includes the reasoning segment, which you can observe to show progress—especially useful with the potentially slower **.deep** level.

deepdive_en.title: Read the context size
deepdive_en.body: Introduces the convenient `contextSize` property to get a model's context size programmatically: `SystemLanguageModel().contextSize` is 4096 on 26.0 and 8192 on 27.0 (newer devices), while `PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel().contextSize` is 32768. This lets you make decisions based on a model's actual capacity.

deepdive_en.title: Evaluating and combining models
deepdive_en.body: Stresses deciding between on-device and PCC, and the reasoning level, based on data rather than vibes. You may be surprised how well this year's updated on-device model performs at certain tasks, but only evaluation tells for sure. Hence the new **Evaluations** framework integrated into Xcode (see "Meet the Evaluations framework"), and you can even use on-device and server models together (see "Build agentic app experiences with Foundation Models").

deepdive_en.title: Handling usage limits
deepdive_en.body: Explains the importance of handling usage limits well with PCC: requests are counted against the user's iCloud account. Using an app that summarizes an article (text and images) with PCC as the example, when a user hits a limit the request throws an error—just showing that error in the UI isn't a great experience since it isn't actionable, so a better approach is needed.

deepdive_en.title: Handle usage limits
deepdive_en.body: The concrete approach is to check the model's `quotaUsage`: use `isLimitReached` and handle it with custom UI (like a label under the button), showing a button that lets the user manage their limit (e.g., upgrade their account) when exceeded; you can also detect `isApproachingLimit`. Integrate this with existing UI and avoid a dismissible alert—instead use persistent state (disable the request button, show a subtle label). Xcode's scheme Debug Options provide "Simulate Apple Foundation Models Availability" to simulate Quota Usage Limit Reached and Nearing Usage Limit for testing.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Wraps up the overview of integrating PCC and encourages those who want the new server model to apply on the Developer website today. It suggests starting with "What's new in the Foundation Models framework" for an overview, and "Debug and profile agentic app experiences with Instruments" to understand model behavior at runtime.

title: Explore immersive website environments in visionOS
gloss: 探索 visionOS 的沉浸式網站環境
takeaway: 用 JavaScript 的新 Immersive API 搭配 model 元素，把網站訪客帶進 Apple Vision Pro 的虛擬環境中。
chapters: Adding the environment model on the page for inline preview
Request the immersive transition on the model
Update the entity transform and the layout on immersive state updates
Request an immersive transition on the escape room model
Handle the request result and show a loading animation
Dock the video in the environment with the fullscreen API

points.text: JavaScript 的新 **Immersive API** 可把網站訪客**帶進 Apple Vision Pro 的虛擬環境**中。
用 **<model>** 元素搭配 **environmentmap** 載入環境，先在頁面內做**內嵌預覽（inline preview）**。
透過 **entityTransform** 與 **DOMMatrix** 調整模型位置與座位視角，打造合適的眼平視角。
用 **document.immersiveEnabled** 偵測可用性，呼叫 **requestImmersive** 切換沉浸狀態，並監聽 **immersivechange** 更新版面。
最佳化體驗：用 **usdcrush** 壓縮 USDZ、用 fullscreen API 嵌入影片，並控制載入動畫與影像。

audience: **想為 Vision Pro 打造沉浸式網頁體驗**、在網站中嵌入 3D 環境的網頁開發者。
gloss_en: Explore immersive website environments in visionOS
takeaway_en: Use JavaScript's new Immersive API together with the model element to transport website visitors into virtual environments on Apple Vision Pro.

points_en.text: JavaScript's new **Immersive API** can **transport website visitors into virtual environments** on Apple Vision Pro.
Use the **<model>** element with **environmentmap** to load an environment, starting with an **inline preview** within the page.
Adjust the model's position and seated viewing angle via **entityTransform** and **DOMMatrix** to create an appropriate eye-level perspective.
Detect availability with **document.immersiveEnabled**, call **requestImmersive** to toggle the immersive state, and listen for **immersivechange** to update the layout.
Optimize the experience: compress USDZ with **usdcrush**, embed video with the fullscreen API, and control loading animations and images.

audience_en: Web developers who **want to build immersive web experiences for Vision Pro** and embed 3D environments in their websites.
summary: 由 visionOS Safari 團隊的 Jean 主講，這場介紹如何用全新的 **JavaScript Immersive API** 在 Apple Vision Pro 的 Safari 中，把網站訪客帶進虛擬環境，成為說故事與吸引顧客的全新方式。兩個貫穿範例：售票網站讓訪客選位時先看到 inline 預覽，再「走進劇院」站在自己選的座位；以及一款 visionOS 密室逃脫遊戲的行銷網站，把訪客送進昏暗密室，TV 螢幕播放神秘影片誘導下載。整套 API 的核心是 HTML **`<model>` 元素**（指定 USDZ 3D 資產，並可加 **`environmentmap`** 360 度 HDR 環境貼圖提供照明與反射）。

**Immersive API 刻意模仿大家熟悉的 Fullscreen API**：用 `model.requestImmersive()` 請求 model 進入沉浸式（必須由使用者互動觸發，如點按按鈕），並有 `document.immersiveEnabled` 偵測支援、`document.immersiveElement` 查詢當前沉浸元素、`immersivechange` 事件、CSS 偽類客製版面等對應能力。與 Fullscreen 不同的是，它把 model 帶到瀏覽器邊界之外、同時保留網頁可見，且兩者可同時作用。Inline 預覽透過設定 model 的 **`entityTransform`**（DOMMatrix）來客製——先用 identity matrix 移除預設縮放、向下平移到人眼高度，再依座位 JSON 的位移與角度建出對應視角。

進入沉浸式時要注意 inline 與 immersive 有**不同參考座標系**（原點與比例不同：inline 原點在 layer 中央依 CSS，immersive 原點在使用者腳下、真實世界比例），因此 transform 需依沉浸狀態重算，並監聽 `immersivechange` 同步更新版面與顯示 exit 按鈕（Vision Pro 也可用 Digital Crown 隨時退出）。密室範例則把 model 設 `display: none` 隱藏 inline、直到請求才下載資產以省頻寬，並在等待時顯示 loading 動畫。最後是優化體驗：用 **Fullscreen API 把影片 dock** 到環境中的螢幕（搭配 Blender 外掛加 RealityKit 標註做 video docking 與光溢出）、用 `model.play()` 播放門開啟動畫、用 Scene Understanding 標註讓 Safari 視窗在環境投下陰影；效能上則減少頂點與實體數、用 low-poly mesh、把光照 bake 進材質、用 **`usdcrush`** 壓縮 USDZ。此外 image 元素加 `controls` 屬性即可在 visionOS 把全景／空間照片環繞展開。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: visionOS Safari 團隊的 Jean 開場，展示如何用沉浸式環境提升網站。以售票網站（選位後可走進劇院站在選定座位）與密室逃脫行銷網站（被送進昏暗密室、TV 播神秘影片誘導下載）兩個範例，預告本場將涵蓋 API 概覽、inline 預覽、進入沉浸式、以及優化。

deepdive.title: Meet the immersive API
deepdive.body: 概覽 **Immersive API**：一切始於 HTML **`<model>` 元素**，用來在網站顯示 3D 模型。

deepdive.title: Basic model element
deepdive.body: 最基本用法：`<model src="teapot.usdz">`，指定 USDZ 3D 資產即可在網頁顯示模型。

deepdive.title: Model element with environment map
deepdive.body: 加上 **`environmentmap`** 屬性（一張 360 度 HDR 影像捕捉場景周圍光照），可為茶壺等光滑物件帶來戲劇性的反射與照明。資產可用 Blender 等任何能匯出 USDZ 的工具製作。

deepdive.title: Preview environments inline
deepdive.body: 說明 **inline 預覽**是把環境介紹給訪客的好開端，能在頁面中先呈現環境的一個視角作為第一步。

deepdive.title: Adding the environment model on the page for inline preview
deepdive.body: 在空的 HTML div 加入 `<model>`，提供劇院 USDZ 與其 lighting map。預設模型會縮放以塞進元素邊界，因此一開始顯示的是從外部看的整座劇院。

deepdive.title: Reset the model entity transform
deepdive.body: 要擺脫預設塞入行為，需客製 **`entityTransform`**（控制位置、旋轉、縮放）：取得 model、等待 `ready` 後，建立 **identity matrix** 並設給 entityTransform，移除所有變換。

deepdive.title: Translate the model down
deepdive.body: 因劇院模型原點在地板，移除變換後地板位於 layer 中央；目標是以人眼高度呈現環境，故用 `translateSelf(0, -1.0, 0)` 把模型**向下平移 1 公尺**到坐姿眼高。

deepdive.title: Build the seat transform
deepdive.body: 為讓預覽視角對應實際選位，準備座位 JSON（每座位含原點位移與朝向角度，採右手 Y-up 座標）。在 `buildTransform` 中依座位的 x/y/z 與 ry 套用旋轉與平移，再加眼高平移，讓視角符合該座位。

deepdive.title: Go immersive
deepdive.body: Inline 預覽在 macOS、iOS 也適用，但真正的魔法是讓買票者**走進劇院**，釋放 visionOS 等空間平台的全部潛力。

deepdive.title: Detect feature availability
deepdive.body: 先用 **`document.immersiveEnabled`** 檢查目前瀏覽器是否支援沉浸式呈現，據此才顯示沉浸式按鈕，確保按鈕只在實際支援處出現。

deepdive.title: Request the immersive transition on the model
deepdive.body: 在使用者互動（如點按沉浸式按鈕）中呼叫 **`model.requestImmersive()`** 請求進入沉浸式——此操作必須回應使用者互動才能觸發。

deepdive.title: Build immersive transform
deepdive.body: 注意 inline 與 immersive 有**不同參考座標系**（原點與比例不同）。在 `buildTransform` 加第二個 immersive 參數：沉浸時加些微旋轉讓主視覺（舞台）不被 Safari 視窗擋住，眼高平移則只在 inline 時套用。

deepdive.title: Update the entity transform and the layout on immersive state updates
deepdive.body: 因 entityTransform 取決於沉浸狀態，須在進出沉浸時重算。監聽 model 的 **`immersivechange`** 事件，依 `document.immersiveElement` 判斷當前狀態重算 transform，並用 CSS class 切換更新頁面版面（調整介面、顯示 exit 按鈕）。Vision Pro 使用者也可用 Digital Crown 隨時退出。

deepdive.title: Hide the inline preview
deepdive.body: 密室範例為保留驚喜，把 `<model>` 設 **`display: none`** 隱藏 inline layer；這不影響請求沉浸式，且有實際好處——資產在沉浸請求真正發生前不會下載或解碼，對重型環境模型可省下大量頻寬與記憶體。

deepdive.title: Request an immersive transition on the escape room model
deepdive.body: 只需在按鈕的 click 事件呼叫 **`escapeRoom.requestImmersive()`** 即可請求密室模型進入沉浸式，程式碼出乎意料地少。

deepdive.title: Handle the request result and show a loading animation
deepdive.body: 因模型未預先 inline 載入，沉浸請求可能需時（重型資產更甚）。用 try／finally 在請求前 `showLoadingAnimation()`、完成後 `hideLoadingAnimation()`，給訪客「正在進行」的回饋。

deepdive.title: Optimize the experience
deepdive.body: 進入讓密室「活起來」的細節：影片、動畫、陰影投射等小細節讓簡單體驗大放異彩。

deepdive.title: Dock the video in the environment with the fullscreen API
deepdive.body: 用 **video docking** 把影片放進環境中的螢幕（TV／投影／看板），而非 inline 播放，還能讓影片光線溢出到場景材質。需在 USDZ 加 RealityKit 標註（講者用自製 Blender 外掛標記 TV 為 docking region），再對影片 `requestFullscreen()` 即自動送到正確位置並隱藏 Safari 視窗。

deepdive.title: Play the model animation
deepdive.body: 讓神秘的門滑開：在 Blender 預先做好開門動畫，監聽影片 `ended` 事件，先 `exitFullscreen()` 取消 dock、再 **`escapeRoom.play()`** 播放模型動畫。可用 `currentTime` 在動畫時間軸導覽，串成多階段環境變換。

deepdive.title: Compress your USDZ with usdcrush
deepdive.body: 效能優化：減少頂點數（不匯出原點處看不到的 mesh）、減少實體數（合併桌面與裝飾）、適時用 low-poly mesh、保持 shader 簡單（把光照 bake 進材質做 unlit）；最後用 **`usdcrush`** 命令列工具壓縮 USDZ 紋理，直接縮短載入時間。Safari 視窗的陰影投射則需 Scene Understanding 標註並用專用 low-poly mesh。

deepdive.title: Image controls
deepdive.body: 另一個可組合的 API：在 `` 元素加 **`controls`** 屬性，瀏覽器即提供原生控制項——在 visionOS 可把全景照片全螢幕環繞展開，也支援用 Vision Pro 或 iPhone 拍的空間照片。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 總結行動方案：用 Apple Vision Pro 試玩 webkit.org 的線上 demo、建立你的第一個網站環境（參考 session 附的 API 規格資源）、並在 bugs.webkit.org 提交功能需求或錯誤回報。並推薦觀看「Design immersive environments for visionOS apps and the spatial web」。

summary_en: Presented by Jean from the visionOS Safari team, this session shows how to use the new **JavaScript Immersive API** to transport website visitors into virtual environments in Apple Vision Pro's Safari—a new way to tell stories and engage customers. Two running examples: a ticket-sales site that gives an inline preview as visitors pick a seat, then lets them 'enter the theater' and stand at their chosen spot; and a marketing site for a visionOS escape-room game that drops visitors into a dim chamber where a TV plays a mysterious video to drive downloads. The API centers on the HTML **`<model>` element** (specifying a USDZ 3D asset, optionally with an **`environmentmap`** 360-degree HDR map for lighting and reflections).

The **Immersive API deliberately mirrors the familiar Fullscreen API**: call `model.requestImmersive()` to go immersive (must be triggered by user interaction, like a button tap), with `document.immersiveEnabled` to detect support, `document.immersiveElement` to query the current immersive element, an `immersivechange` event, and CSS pseudo-classes for layout. Unlike Fullscreen, it transports the model beyond the browser bounds while keeping the page visible, and both can be active simultaneously. Inline previews are customized via the model's **`entityTransform`** (a DOMMatrix)—first an identity matrix to remove default scaling, a downward translate to eye level, then per-seat translation and rotation from a seat JSON to match the chosen viewpoint.

When going immersive, note that inline and immersive use **different reference frames** (different origins and scales: inline's origin is at the layer center per CSS, immersive's is at the user's feet at real-world scale), so the transform must be recomputed per immersive state, listening to `immersivechange` to update layout and show an exit button (Vision Pro users can also exit anytime with the Digital Crown). The escape-room example sets the model to `display: none` to hide the inline preview and avoid downloading the asset until requested, showing a loading animation while waiting. Finally, optimizing the experience: use the **Fullscreen API to dock video** onto a screen in the environment (with RealityKit annotations added via a Blender plugin for video docking and light spill), `model.play()` to play a door-opening animation, and a Scene Understanding annotation so the Safari window casts a shadow; for performance, reduce vertex and entity counts, use low-poly meshes, bake lighting into materials, and compress USDZ with **`usdcrush`**. An `` element with the `controls` attribute also lets you wrap panoramas/spatial photos around the viewer on visionOS.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Jean from the visionOS Safari team opens by showing how to elevate websites with immersive environments. Using a ticket site (enter the theater and stand at your chosen seat) and an escape-room marketing site (dropped into a dim chamber with a mysterious TV video driving downloads), the session previews an API overview, inline previews, going immersive, and optimization.

deepdive_en.title: Meet the immersive API
deepdive_en.body: Overviews the **Immersive API**: it all starts with the HTML **`<model>` element** for displaying 3D models on a website.

deepdive_en.title: Basic model element
deepdive_en.body: The most basic usage: `<model src="teapot.usdz">`, specifying a USDZ 3D asset to display a model on the page.

deepdive_en.title: Model element with environment map
deepdive_en.body: Adding the **`environmentmap`** attribute (a 360-degree HDR image capturing the scene's lighting) brings dramatic reflections and lighting to shiny objects like a teapot. Assets can be made with any tool that exports USDZ, such as Blender.

deepdive_en.title: Preview environments inline
deepdive_en.body: Explains that **inline previews** are a great first step to introduce an environment to visitors, presenting a viewpoint of the environment within the page.

deepdive_en.title: Adding the environment model on the page for inline preview
deepdive_en.body: Add a `<model>` to an empty HTML div with the theater USDZ and its lighting map. By default the model scales to fit the element bounds, so it initially shows the whole theater from the outside.

deepdive_en.title: Reset the model entity transform
deepdive_en.body: To remove the default fitting, customize the **`entityTransform`** (position, rotation, scale): get the model, await `ready`, create an **identity matrix**, and assign it to entityTransform, removing all transformations.

deepdive_en.title: Translate the model down
deepdive_en.body: Because the theater model's origin is on its floor, after removing transforms the floor sits at the layer center; to present at human eye level, use `translateSelf(0, -1.0, 0)` to **translate the model down 1 meter** to seated eye height.

deepdive_en.title: Build the seat transform
deepdive_en.body: To match the preview viewpoint to the actual seat, prepare a seat JSON (each seat's origin offset and orientation angle, in right-handed Y-up coordinates). In `buildTransform`, apply the seat's rotation and translation from x/y/z and ry plus the eye-level translation so the view matches that seat.

deepdive_en.title: Go immersive
deepdive_en.body: Inline previews also work on macOS and iOS, but the real magic is letting the buyer **step inside the theater**, unlocking the full potential of spatial platforms like visionOS.

deepdive_en.title: Detect feature availability
deepdive_en.body: First check **`document.immersiveEnabled`** to see whether the current browser supports immersive presentations, and only then show the immersive button so it appears only where actually supported.

deepdive_en.title: Request the immersive transition on the model
deepdive_en.body: Call **`model.requestImmersive()`** within a user interaction (like tapping the immersive button) to request going immersive—this must happen in response to user interaction.

deepdive_en.title: Build immersive transform
deepdive_en.body: Note that inline and immersive have **different reference frames** (different origins and scales). Add a second immersive parameter to `buildTransform`: when immersive, add a slight rotation so the main focus (the stage) isn't hidden behind the Safari window, and apply the eye-level translation only when inline.

deepdive_en.title: Update the entity transform and the layout on immersive state updates
deepdive_en.body: Since entityTransform depends on immersive state, recompute it when entering/exiting immersive. Listen to the model's **`immersivechange`** event, recompute the transform based on `document.immersiveElement`, and toggle a CSS class to update the page layout (adjust UI, show an exit button). Vision Pro users can also exit anytime with the Digital Crown.

deepdive_en.title: Hide the inline preview
deepdive_en.body: The escape-room example keeps the surprise by setting the `<model>` to **`display: none`** to hide the inline layer; this doesn't prevent requesting immersive and has a practical benefit—the asset isn't downloaded or decoded until the immersive request actually happens, saving significant bandwidth and memory for heavy environment models.

deepdive_en.title: Request an immersive transition on the escape room model
deepdive_en.body: Simply call **`escapeRoom.requestImmersive()`** in the button's click event to request the escape-room model go immersive—it takes surprisingly little code.

deepdive_en.title: Handle the request result and show a loading animation
deepdive_en.body: Since the model isn't preloaded inline, the immersive request may take time (more so for heavy assets). Use try/finally to `showLoadingAnimation()` before the request and `hideLoadingAnimation()` after, giving visitors feedback that something is happening.

deepdive_en.title: Optimize the experience
deepdive_en.body: Moves to the details that bring the escape room alive: video, animations, and shadow casting—small touches that make a simple experience go a long way.

deepdive_en.title: Dock the video in the environment with the fullscreen API
deepdive_en.body: Use **video docking** to place the video on a screen in the environment (TV/projector/billboard) instead of inline, and let its light spill onto scene materials. This needs RealityKit annotations in the USDZ (the speaker uses a custom Blender plugin to tag the TV as the docking region); calling `requestFullscreen()` on the video then transports it to the right location and hides the Safari window.

deepdive_en.title: Play the model animation
deepdive_en.body: To make the mysterious door slide open: author the door-opening animation in Blender, listen for the video's `ended` event, call `exitFullscreen()` to undock, then **`escapeRoom.play()`** to play the model animation. Use `currentTime` to navigate the timeline for multi-stage environment transformations.

deepdive_en.title: Compress your USDZ with usdcrush
deepdive_en.body: Performance: reduce vertex count (don't export meshes invisible from the origin), reduce entity count (merge the desk with its decorations), use low-poly meshes where appropriate, and keep shaders simple (bake lighting into materials for unlit); finally use the **`usdcrush`** command-line tool to compress USDZ textures, directly cutting load time. Safari window shadow casting needs a Scene Understanding annotation with a dedicated low-poly mesh.

deepdive_en.title: Image controls
deepdive_en.body: Another composable API: add the **`controls`** attribute to an `` element and the browser provides native controls—on visionOS this lets you make a panorama fullscreen and wrap it around you, and it also supports spatial photos captured on Vision Pro or iPhone.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Summarizes the action plan: try the online demos on webkit.org with Apple Vision Pro, build your first website environment (using the API specs attached to the session), and file feature requests or bug reports at bugs.webkit.org. Also recommends watching 'Design immersive environments for visionOS apps and the spatial web'.

title: Dive into lazy stacks and scrolling with SwiftUI
gloss: 深入 SwiftUI 的 lazy stacks 與捲動
takeaway: 理解 LazyVStack／LazyHStack 如何估算尺寸與延遲載入子視圖，並善用 scroll transition、prefetch 與程式化捲動打造流暢的捲動體驗。
chapters: Setting up lazy stack subview in onAppear
Lazy stack subview ready before onAppear
Using onGeometryChange in lazy stack subview
Using custom layout in lazy stack subview

points.text: 深入解析 **LazyVStack** 與 **LazyHStack** 如何估算尺寸並延遲載入子視圖，是流暢捲動的關鍵。
建議**在資料層而非視圖層做過濾**（例如以 @Query 的 #Predicate），避免子視圖數量在出現後才改變。
用 **scrollTransition** 製作捲動特效，並以 **onScrollGeometryChange** 與 **onScrollTargetVisibilityChange** 觀測捲動狀態。
在 **initializer** 而非 onAppear 設定子視圖狀態與載入工作，可在出現前就準備好內容、減少跳動。
透過 **ScrollPosition** 搭配 scrollTo 做程式化捲動，並避免在視圖出現後改變版面。

audience: 適合**已熟悉 SwiftUI、想深入優化長列表與捲動效能的開發者**。
gloss_en: Dive into lazy stacks and scrolling with SwiftUI
takeaway_en: Understand how LazyVStack / LazyHStack estimate sizes and lazily load subviews, and make good use of scroll transitions, prefetching, and programmatic scrolling to build a smooth scrolling experience.

points_en.text: A deep dive into how **LazyVStack** and **LazyHStack** estimate sizes and lazily load subviews—the key to smooth scrolling.
Recommends **filtering at the data layer rather than the view layer** (for example with @Query's #Predicate) to avoid the subview count changing after they appear.
Use **scrollTransition** for scroll effects, and observe scroll state with **onScrollGeometryChange** and **onScrollTargetVisibilityChange**.
Set subview state and kick off loading work in the **initializer** rather than onAppear, so content is ready before it appears and there's less jumping.
Do programmatic scrolling with **ScrollPosition** and scrollTo, and avoid changing layout after a view appears.

audience_en: **Developers already familiar with SwiftUI who want to dig deeper into optimizing long lists and scrolling performance.**
summary: 這場由 UI Frameworks 工程師 Rens 主講，是對 SwiftUI **lazy stacks** 與捲動的深度複習。**LazyVStack** 與 **LazyHStack** 是任何需要長篇、自訂捲動內容的 app 的核心元件，其威力來自簡單性——能與 reorderable、swipe actions 等其他元件自由組合。講者以一個摺紙（Origami）教學 app 貫穿全場，逐步拆解 lazy stack 的內部運作：它只會評估、渲染**可見區域**內的 view，把離畫面的 view 移除，因此比 VStack 更有效率；但代價是離畫面 view 的高度與寬度都是**估算**的，捲動位置（content offset）也因此不精確、會隨著學到更多 view 而變動。

接著講者示範了**版面與佈局**的注意事項：LazyVStack 的理想寬度取自第一個 subview，LazyHStack 的理想高度亦然，所以遇到可變高度（如多行字幕）應**固定高度**；用 `pinnedViews` 可釘住 section header。在效能反模式上，`scrollTransition` 不要把原本不可見的 view 推進可見區（lazy stack 會誤判而提早消失）；判斷按鈕顯示與否應避免用絕對 content offset，改用 **`onScrollTargetVisibilityChange`** 這類以**相對可見性**為基準的 API。更關鍵的洞見是：一個 view struct 不一定對應一個 lazy stack subview——body 裡多個頂層 view 會各自被載入；而在 leaf view 裡用條件式（如依 `detailLevel`、optional unwrapping）產生**動態數量的 subview** 會害 lazy stack 為了維持 index 而把 view 留得比預期久，正解是在**資料層過濾**（例如 SwiftData `Query` 的 `#Predicate`）。

後半段談 **prefetching**：lazy stack 會在 view 真正出現前先做部分渲染工作，把成本分散到多個 frame，避免捲動掉幀（hitch）。因此你應在 **initializer** 而非 `onAppear` 就把 view 設定到合理狀態，否則 prefetch 的成果會被丟棄;`task` 或搭配 cache 的 observable loader 也能讓資料更早載入。同時要記得離畫面的 view 狀態最終會被釋放，重要狀態（如 highlight）應移到 model 或用 **`@Binding`** 提升到外層。最後在**程式化捲動**上，`ScrollPosition` 可捲到尚未載入的 view；要捲得順暢，務必讓每個 ForEach 元素**穩定對應單一 subview**、在資料層過濾、並避免 view 出現後才用 `onGeometryChange` 改變佈局（必要時改用 custom **`Layout`**）。理解這些機制，才能把 lazy stack 用到極致。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: UI Frameworks 工程師 Rens 開場，指出 **lazy stacks** 是任何顯示長篇、自訂捲動內容的 SwiftUI app 的核心元件，其威力來自**簡單性**——能與其他元件自由組合，例如 2027 的 reorderable 拖拉重排、以及 list 之外的 swipe actions。本場將深入講解 lazy stack 如何運作、能做什麼、又該避免什麼。

deepdive.title: Origami app
deepdive.body: 介紹貫穿全場的範例：一個顯示摺紙教學步驟的 **Origami app**，目前只示範摺天鵝的步驟。

deepdive.title: Layout
deepdive.body: 說明主畫面結構：`ScrollView` 內放 `LazyVStack`，再對每個步驟放一個 `StepView`。**LazyVStack** 與 VStack 不同——它不評估或渲染不可見的 view，只由上到下擺放直到填滿可見區，捲動時再依需要加入/移除 view，因此更有效率。代價是離畫面 view 的高度需**估算**（依已擺放 view 的平均尺寸與剩餘數量），寬度則取自第一個 subview；估算不精確，使得整體高度與**捲動位置**會隨捲動變動，例如 iPhone 轉向後捲回頂端時 lazy stack 必須沿途修正估算的上方空間並同步調整 content offset。

deepdive.title: Horizontally scrolling showcase
deepdive.body: 為了讓使用者分享成品照片，新增一個 **Showcase** view：內含水平 `ScrollView` 加 `LazyHStack`，於是出現 LazyHStack 巢狀在外層 LazyVStack 的結構。這種巢狀對效能有利（不是每個人都會捲到這些額外 view）。LazyHStack 的理想高度同樣取自第一個 subview，所以若每張照片有可變行數的說明文字，較長的會被裁掉——最佳解是**固定 view 高度**（例如設 line limit 並預留空間）。

deepdive.title: Showcase section
deepdive.body: 改把照片以較大尺寸直向排在步驟下方，並放進一個 **Section**。透過 LazyVStack 的 **`pinnedViews: [.sectionHeaders]`** 參數，捲動時 Showcase 的 section header 會釘在頂端。

deepdive.title: Scroll effect
deepdive.body: 示範一個**反模式**：用 `.scrollTransition` 對照片加上 `rotationEffect` 與 `scaleEffect`。由於 lazy stack 只依 view 的**原始位置**載入，這種 transform 把 view 推出了原本的 frame，導致 lazy stack 誤以為它離畫面而提早消失——示範中粉紅天鵝太早不見。

deepdive.title: Scroll effect
deepdive.body: 給出正確做法：改用不會把 view 推出可見區的 `scaleEffect`（依 `phase.value` 縮放但不位移），運作正常。原則是：對 lazy stack 內的 view 套 scroll transition 時，**別讓原本不可見的 view 被 transform 推進可見區**，因為 lazy stack 不會察覺。

deepdive.title: Scroll to Showcase button
deepdive.body: 新增一顆「捲到 Showcase」按鈕，希望只在接近頂端時顯示。第一版用 `.onScrollGeometryChange` 取**絕對 content offset**，捲超過 100 點就隱藏按鈕。雖然能動，但因 lazy stack 的 content offset 是估算的，按鈕消失的確切位置會隨估算改變而飄移。

deepdive.title: Scroll to Showcase button
deepdive.body: 給出較佳做法：改用以**相對可見性**為基準的 **`.onScrollTargetVisibilityChange`**，當可見區內的 subview 可見性改變時觸發。按鈕的顯示只取決於哪些 subview 可見（threshold 設 0.8），避開了估算 content offset 的不穩定。

deepdive.title: Subview loading
deepdive.body: 提出本段核心觀念：lazy stack 在 view 即將進入可見區時才載入它，但它個別載入的 subview **不一定**直接對應你在程式碼裡定義的 view struct。

deepdive.title: One resolved subview
deepdive.body: 回到最初的簡單 `ContentView`：此時 `StepView` 與 LazyVStack 看到的 subview 是 **1 對 1** 的。`ScrollView` 內有 LazyVStack，LazyVStack 內有 ForEach，而 ForEach 會 resolve 成每個步驟一個 StepView——這些通常就是 lazy stack 載入的 subview。

deepdive.title: Multiple resolved subviews
deepdive.body: 示範較複雜的情況：當 `StepView` 的 body 在頂層放了 `StepDiagram` 與 `StepInstructions` 兩個 view 且未包在 VStack 裡時，每個 StepView 會 **resolve 成兩個 view**。LazyVStack 會**分別**評估與載入這兩者（但仍需先評估 StepView 才能建立任一個)。

deepdive.title: Dynamic number of subviews
deepdive.body: 示範要小心的情況：`StepView` 依 `detailLevel` 環境值決定是否顯示，於是每個 StepView 會 resolve 成**一個或零個 subview**。雖然內容仍是 lazy 載入，但因為 lazy stack 用 **index** 定址可見 subview，它必須把較早的 StepView 留著（以防 detailLevel 改變而影響 index）。結論：在 ForEach 中大量建立的 leaf view 裡，**避免產生動態數量的 subview**。

deepdive.title: Filtering on the view level
deepdive.body: 進一步說明前述反模式的代價：若 StepView body 還用了像 `writingStyle` 這種不相關的環境值，當它改變時，連已捲離畫面的 view 都可能被重新評估 body，造成不必要的 view update，且 lazy stack 不會釋放這些 StepView 的狀態。

deepdive.title: Filtering on the data level
deepdive.body: 給出正解：**在資料層過濾**。若使用 SwiftData，就用 `#Predicate` 過濾 `Query`（這裡把 `detailLevel` 放進 predicate）。如此 LazyVStack 能立即得知 subview 數量，不必為了計算數量或 index 而建構 view。

deepdive.title: Optional unwrapping
deepdive.body: 提醒在 view body 裡 **unwrap optional** 也有同樣效果：這裡用 `if let token` 解開 `apiToken` 環境值，body 只在 token 非 nil 時回傳內容——這同樣造成動態數量的 subview。

deepdive.title: Optional unwrapping
deepdive.body: 給出較佳結構：token 可由 `NetworkClient` model 物件處理；若未驗證，應在**更上層**的 view 顯示 `ContentUnavailableView`，而不是一開始就放 lazy stack。也提到 lazy stack 因只保留少量資料在記憶體，不需做完整 diff，只對可見 view 做最小變更檢查。

deepdive.title: Prefetching
deepdive.body: 介紹 **prefetching**：當捲動方向到達已擺放內容的邊緣時，lazy stack 會在 view 上畫面前就先做部分渲染工作。捲動時 ScrollView 必須在 frame deadline 內穩定畫出每一幀，若擺放新 view 的工作超時就會**掉幀（hitch）**;prefetching 會先檢查是否有足夠時間，預先評估 body 與佈局（甚至預先處理巢狀 LazyHStack），把工作分散到多個 frame，等 view 真正出現時大半工作已完成。

deepdive.title: Loading more content
deepdive.body: 示範 `onAppear` 的合理用途之一——**無限捲動**：最後一個 `ProgressView` 加上 `.onAppear`，當它出現時 `pager.fetchPage()` 抓取下一頁照片。

deepdive.title: Setting up lazy stack subview in onAppear
deepdive.body: 示範**反模式**：在每個 view 的 `onAppear` 裡才用 `viewModel.configure(with: id)` 做設定，使得 view 的尺寸與大部分內容在擺放後才劇烈改變。如此 prefetching 先做的工作會被丟棄、出現時得重做，lazy stack 還可能載入比需要更多的 view，影響捲動。

deepdive.title: Lazy stack subview ready before onAppear
deepdive.body: 給出正解：在 **initializer** 就把 view 設好（用 `State(initialValue:)` 建立帶 id 的 viewModel），讓 view 在出現前就處於合理狀態。也補充：body 通常先被呼叫、`onAppear` 稍後才在擺放時呼叫；若捲動方向反轉，body 甚至可能因 prefetching 被呼叫但 `onAppear` 從未被呼叫。

deepdive.title: Loading diagram with task modifier
deepdive.body: 示範用 **`task`** modifier 在 view 出現時從網路遠端載入 diagram（`diagram = await diagramLoader.loadDiagram(id:)`）。這可行，但仍是在出現時才開始載入。

deepdive.title: Loading diagram in initializer
deepdive.body: 示範如何善用 prefetching 讓資料**更早**載入：用一個連到 cache 的 `DiagramLoader` observable 物件，在其 **initializer** 中（cache 沒命中時）就立刻開始載入 diagram，因此會比等到出現時稍早抓到，提高出現時已就緒的機率。

deepdive.title: Highlight @State variable
deepdive.body: 示範**狀態保存**的陷阱：`StepView` 用 `@State var isHighlighted`。離畫面的 view 雖會保留數次更新以備捲回，但最終會從記憶體刪除、連帶刪除其 state——所以一旦捲走，highlight 狀態就遺失。結論：別把需在捲動後存活的資料放在 view state。

deepdive.title: Highlight @Binding
deepdive.body: 給出正解：把重要狀態移到 model 物件，或用 **`@Binding`** 提升到外層 view。這裡 `ContentView` 持有 `@State var highlighted: Set<Step.ID>`，StepView 透過 `@Binding` 共享，highlight 就不會因捲動而遺失。

deepdive.title: Programmatic scrolling
deepdive.body: 進入**程式化捲動**主題，並給出讓 lazy stack 內捲動順暢的建議。

deepdive.title: Programmatically scroll to showcase
deepdive.body: 示範用 **`ScrollPosition`** binding 程式化捲到 showcase 的 section header（`scrollPosition.scrollTo(id:)`）。即使目標 view 不在畫面上也能捲到——lazy stack 會估算其位置，並在動畫捲動的每一幀更新該估算。

deepdive.title: Dynamic number of views
deepdive.body: 重申**動態數量 subview** 對程式化捲動也有效能衝擊。若每個 ForEach 元素都**穩定 resolve 成單一 subview**，lazy stack 就能直接查 ForEach 找到要捲到的 ID 而不必建構任何 view，捲動最有效率。

deepdive.title: Filter at the data level
deepdive.body: 再次強調：捲到接近結尾的 subview 時，若 lazy stack 能快速數出 subview 數量會更順——所以別在 view body 用條件式過濾，要在**資料層過濾**（例如用 `Query` 的 predicate）。

deepdive.title: Using onGeometryChange in lazy stack subview
deepdive.body: 示範另一個讓捲動變不順的常見模式：用 **`onGeometryChange`** 把量到的字幕高度存進 state（`subtitleHeight`），再於另一次佈局 pass 用它算 diagram 的 frame。lazy stack 先量到 view 的原始高度，但高度在出現後才改變、把其他內容往下推，使捲動不可靠。

deepdive.title: Using custom layout in lazy stack subview
deepdive.body: 給出正解：當無法只靠 SwiftUI 佈局基本元件時，改用**自訂 `Layout`**（這裡是 `StepLayout`）來一次算好佈局，避免 view 出現後才改變高度。並指向「Compose custom layouts with SwiftUI」場次深入了解。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 總結全場：涵蓋 lazy stack 的佈局、view struct 不一定對應單一 subview 及其影響、prefetching 如何提升捲動效能、以及程式化捲到離畫面 view。最佳實務包括：避免依賴估算且不穩的絕對 content size/offset、別在 leaf view 用條件式過濾資料、盡量在 `onAppear` 前設好 subview、以及別在 view 出現後改變佈局。

summary_en: Presented by UI Frameworks Engineer Rens, this session is a deep refresher on SwiftUI **lazy stacks** and scrolling. **LazyVStack** and **LazyHStack** are essential for any app showing long, custom scrolling content, and their power comes from simplicity — they compose freely with other components like reorderable and swipe actions. Using an Origami tutorial app throughout, the talk dissects how lazy stacks work internally: they only evaluate and render views in the **visible region**, removing off-screen views, which makes them more efficient than a VStack. The cost is that off-screen view heights and widths are **estimated**, so the scroll position (content offset) is imprecise and shifts as the stack learns more about new views.

The session then covers **layout** caveats: a LazyVStack's ideal width comes from its first subview, as does a LazyHStack's ideal height, so variable heights (e.g. multi-line captions) should be **fixed**; `pinnedViews` pins section headers. On performance anti-patterns, a `scrollTransition` must not push normally-invisible views into the visible rect (the lazy stack thinks they're off-screen and they vanish too early); deciding button visibility should avoid absolute content offset in favor of relative-visibility APIs like **`onScrollTargetVisibilityChange`**. A key insight: one view struct doesn't always map to one lazy stack subview — multiple top-level views in a body are each loaded; and using conditionals in leaf views (e.g. by `detailLevel` or optional unwrapping) to produce a **dynamic number of subviews** keeps views alive longer than expected, since the stack addresses subviews by index. The fix is to **filter at the data level** (e.g. a SwiftData `Query` with a `#Predicate`).

The second half explains **prefetching**: lazy stacks perform part of a view's rendering work before it appears, spreading the cost across frames to avoid scroll hitches. So you should configure a view to a reasonable state in its **initializer** rather than `onAppear`, or the prefetched work is discarded; a `task` or a cache-backed observable loader can load data earlier too. Remember that off-screen view state is eventually released, so important state (like highlight) should move to a model or be lifted via **`@Binding`**. Finally, on **programmatic scrolling**, `ScrollPosition` can scroll to a not-yet-loaded view; for smoothness, ensure each ForEach element **resolves to a single stable subview**, filter at the data level, and avoid changing layout after a view appears with `onGeometryChange` (use a custom **`Layout`** instead). Understanding these mechanisms lets you get the most out of lazy stacks.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: UI Frameworks Engineer Rens opens by noting that **lazy stacks** are essential to any SwiftUI app showing long, custom scrolling content, and that their power comes from **simplicity** — they compose freely with other components, such as 2027's reorderable drag-and-reorder and swipe actions outside of List. The session will dive into how lazy stacks work, what you can do with them, and what to avoid.

deepdive_en.title: Origami app
deepdive_en.body: Introduces the running example: an **Origami app** showing instructions for folding origami pieces, currently demonstrating only the steps to make a swan.

deepdive_en.title: Layout
deepdive_en.body: Explains the main view: a `ScrollView` containing a `LazyVStack` with a `StepView` per step. Unlike a VStack, a **LazyVStack** doesn't evaluate or render invisible views — it lays them out top to bottom until the visible rect is filled, adding/removing views as you scroll, making it more efficient. The cost is that off-screen view heights are **estimated** (from the average size of placed views and remaining count), the width comes from the first subview, and because estimates are imprecise the overall height and **scroll position** shift while scrolling — e.g. after an iPhone orientation change, scrolling back to the top forces the stack to correct the estimated space above and adjust content offset accordingly.

deepdive_en.title: Horizontally scrolling showcase
deepdive_en.body: To let users share photos of their creations, a **Showcase** view is added: a horizontal `ScrollView` with a `LazyHStack`, producing a LazyHStack nested inside the outer LazyVStack. This nesting is good for performance (not everyone scrolls to these extra views). A LazyHStack's ideal height also comes from its first subview, so if each photo had a variable-line caption, longer ones would be cut off — the best fix is to **fix view heights** (e.g. set a line limit and reserve space).

deepdive_en.title: Showcase section
deepdive_en.body: The photos are instead placed larger and vertically below the steps, inside a **Section**. Using the LazyVStack's **`pinnedViews: [.sectionHeaders]`** parameter, the Showcase section header sticks to the top while scrolling.

deepdive_en.title: Scroll effect
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates an **anti-pattern**: applying `.scrollTransition` with `rotationEffect` and `scaleEffect` to the photos. Because the lazy stack loads views based on their **original position**, this transform pushes views out of their frame, making the stack believe they're off-screen so they disappear too early — the pink swan vanishes prematurely in the demo.

deepdive_en.title: Scroll effect
deepdive_en.body: Shows the correct approach: a `scaleEffect` that doesn't push views out of the visible rect (scaling by `phase.value` without displacement), which works fine. The principle: when applying a scroll transition to views in a lazy stack, **don't let normally-invisible views get pushed into the visible rect**, because the lazy stack won't be aware of it.

deepdive_en.title: Scroll to Showcase button
deepdive_en.body: Adds a "scroll to Showcase" button that should only be visible near the top. The first version uses `.onScrollGeometryChange` to read the **absolute content offset**, hiding the button when scrolled past 100 points. It works, but because the lazy stack's content offset is estimated, the exact point where the button disappears shifts as estimates change.

deepdive_en.title: Scroll to Showcase button
deepdive_en.body: Shows the better approach: use the relative-visibility based **`.onScrollTargetVisibilityChange`**, whose closure fires when the visibility of subviews in the visible region changes. The button's visibility depends only on which subviews are visible (threshold 0.8), avoiding the instability of estimated content offset.

deepdive_en.title: Subview loading
deepdive_en.body: Raises the key idea for this segment: lazy stacks load a view when it's about to enter the visible region, but the individual subviews they load do **not** always correspond directly to the view structs you define in code.

deepdive_en.title: One resolved subview
deepdive_en.body: Returns to the simple `ContentView`: here `StepView` instances and the subviews the LazyVStack sees are **1-to-1**. The `ScrollView` has a LazyVStack, which has a ForEach, and the ForEach resolves to one StepView per step — usually exactly the subviews the lazy stack loads.

deepdive_en.title: Multiple resolved subviews
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates a more complex case: when `StepView`'s body has two top-level views, `StepDiagram` and `StepInstructions`, not wrapped in a VStack, each StepView **resolves to two views**. The LazyVStack evaluates and loads both **separately** (though StepView still has to be evaluated to create either).

deepdive_en.title: Dynamic number of subviews
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates a case to watch out for: `StepView` checks a `detailLevel` environment value to decide visibility, so each StepView resolves to **one or zero subviews**. Although contents are still loaded lazily, because the lazy stack addresses visible subviews by **index**, it must keep earlier StepViews alive in case detailLevel changes and shifts the indices. Conclusion: in leaf views created many times in a ForEach, **avoid a dynamic number of subviews**.

deepdive_en.title: Filtering on the view level
deepdive_en.body: Elaborates on the cost of that anti-pattern: if the StepView body also uses an unrelated environment value like `writingStyle`, a change to it can trigger body evaluations even for views scrolled off-screen, causing unnecessary view updates, and the lazy stack won't release these StepViews' state.

deepdive_en.title: Filtering on the data level
deepdive_en.body: Gives the fix: **filter at the data level**. With SwiftData, filter the `Query` with a `#Predicate` (here placing `detailLevel` in the predicate). This makes the subview count immediately clear to the LazyVStack, which no longer has to construct views just to compute counts or indices.

deepdive_en.title: Optional unwrapping
deepdive_en.body: Warns that **unwrapping an optional** in a view body has the same effect: here `if let token` unwraps an `apiToken` environment value and the body only returns content when it's non-nil — also producing a dynamic number of subviews.

deepdive_en.title: Optional unwrapping
deepdive_en.body: Shows a better structure: the token could be handled by a `NetworkClient` model object; if unauthenticated, a view **higher up** the hierarchy should show a `ContentUnavailableView` rather than placing the lazy stack at all. Also notes that since lazy stacks keep little data in memory, they don't perform a full diff — only a minimal check for changes in visible views.

deepdive_en.title: Prefetching
deepdive_en.body: Introduces **prefetching**: when scrolling reaches the edge of placed content, the lazy stack performs part of a view's rendering work before it's on screen. While scrolling, the ScrollView must draw frames within a deadline; if placing new views overruns it, a frame is dropped — a visible **hitch**. Prefetching checks whether there's enough time to pre-evaluate a view's body and layout (even a nested LazyHStack), spreading the work across frames so most of it is done by the time the view appears.

deepdive_en.title: Loading more content
deepdive_en.body: Shows a legitimate use of `onAppear` — **infinite scrolling**: the final `ProgressView` has an `.onAppear` that calls `pager.fetchPage()` to fetch the next page of photos when it appears.

deepdive_en.title: Setting up lazy stack subview in onAppear
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates an **anti-pattern**: configuring each view only in `onAppear` via `viewModel.configure(with: id)`, so the view's size and most of its content change dramatically after placement. The work prefetching did is thrown away and redone on appear, the lazy stack may load more views than needed, and scrolling suffers.

deepdive_en.title: Lazy stack subview ready before onAppear
deepdive_en.body: Gives the fix: set up the view in the **initializer** (building the viewModel with `State(initialValue:)` from the id) so it's in a reasonable state before appearing. Also notes body is generally called first and `onAppear` only later when placed; if scroll direction reverses, body may be called via prefetching while `onAppear` is never called.

deepdive_en.title: Loading diagram with task modifier
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates using the **`task`** modifier to remotely load a diagram from the internet when the view appears (`diagram = await diagramLoader.loadDiagram(id:)`). This works but still starts loading only on appear.

deepdive_en.title: Loading diagram in initializer
deepdive_en.body: Shows how to leverage prefetching to load data **earlier**: a cache-backed `DiagramLoader` observable object starts loading the diagram in its **initializer** (when the cache misses), so it's fetched slightly sooner and is more likely to be ready by the time the view appears.

deepdive_en.title: Highlight @State variable
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates a **state-preservation** pitfall: `StepView` uses `@State var isHighlighted`. Off-screen views are kept for a few updates in case they scroll back, but are eventually deleted from memory along with their state — so once scrolled away, the highlight is lost. Conclusion: don't keep data that must survive scrolling in view state.

deepdive_en.title: Highlight @Binding
deepdive_en.body: Gives the fix: move important state to a model object, or lift it to an outer view via **`@Binding`**. Here `ContentView` holds `@State var highlighted: Set<Step.ID>` and StepView shares it through a `@Binding`, so the highlight isn't lost on scroll.
