deepdive_en.title: Programmatic scrolling
deepdive_en.body: Moves into **programmatic scrolling**, offering tips to make scrolling work well in lazy stacks.

deepdive_en.title: Programmatically scroll to showcase
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates using a **`ScrollPosition`** binding to programmatically scroll to the showcase's section header (`scrollPosition.scrollTo(id:)`). This works even when the target view isn't on screen — the lazy stack estimates its position and updates that estimate on every frame of an animated scroll.

deepdive_en.title: Dynamic number of views
deepdive_en.body: Reiterates that a **dynamic number of subviews** also hurts programmatic scrolling. If each ForEach element **reliably resolves to a single subview**, the lazy stack can query the ForEach to find the ID to scroll to without constructing any views — the most performant case.

deepdive_en.title: Filter at the data level
deepdive_en.body: Stresses again that scrolling to a subview near the end is smoother if the lazy stack can quickly count subviews — so don't filter with a conditional in the view body; **filter at the data level** (e.g. a predicate on a `Query`).

deepdive_en.title: Using onGeometryChange in lazy stack subview
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates another common pattern that hurts scrolling: using **`onGeometryChange`** to store a measured subtitle height in state (`subtitleHeight`), then using it in another layout pass to compute the diagram's frame. The lazy stack measures the view's original height, but it changes after appearing and pushes other content down, making scrolling unreliable.

deepdive_en.title: Using custom layout in lazy stack subview
deepdive_en.body: Gives the fix: when SwiftUI's layout primitives aren't enough, use a custom **`Layout`** (here `StepLayout`) to compute the layout in one pass and avoid changing height after the view appears. Points to the "Compose custom layouts with SwiftUI" session for more.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Wraps up the whole session: covering lazy stack layout, how view structs don't always resolve to a single subview and the consequences, how prefetching improves scrolling performance, and programmatic scrolling to off-screen views. Best practices include avoiding the estimated, unstable absolute content size/offset, not filtering data with conditionals in leaf views, setting up subviews before `onAppear` where possible, and not changing layout after subviews appear.

title: Compose advanced graphics effects with SwiftUI
gloss: 用 SwiftUI 組合進階圖形效果
takeaway: 結合 SwiftUI 的 layerEffect、Metal shader 與 TimelineView、對齊指南等版面 API，把複雜視覺拆解成可組合、可動畫的圖形效果。
chapters: Writing layer effect shader in Metal
SwiftUI layer effect with offset parameter
SwiftUI layer effect with full-width offset
SwiftUI layer effect with noise sampling
SwiftUI layer effect with static visual
SwiftUI layer effect with animated visual

points.text: 示範如何把設計**拆解（design breakdown）**成可組合的 SwiftUI 版面與圖形 API。
以 **layerEffect** 搭配 Metal 的 `[[stitchable]]` shader 套用自訂效果（如背景扭曲）。
透過 noise texture 取樣與 **domain warping** 在 shader 中產生豐富的視覺變化。
用 **TimelineView(.animation)** 把經過時間傳入 shader，驅動動畫化的視覺。
以 **ScrollViewReader** 做時間同步逐字稿，並用 **alignmentGuide** 讓時間戳浮動對齊。

audience: **想為 SwiftUI App 打造客製化視覺與動畫效果的開發者**，對 shader 與圖形組合有興趣的人。
gloss_en: Compose advanced graphics effects with SwiftUI
takeaway_en: Combine SwiftUI's layerEffect, Metal shaders, and layout APIs like TimelineView and alignment guides to break complex visuals down into composable, animatable graphics effects.

points_en.text: Demonstrates how to do a **design breakdown** into composable SwiftUI layout and graphics APIs.
Apply custom effects (such as background distortion) using **layerEffect** paired with Metal's `[[stitchable]]` shaders.
Produce rich visual variation in the shader through noise texture sampling and **domain warping**.
Use **TimelineView(.animation)** to pass elapsed time into a shader, driving animated visuals.
Build a time-synced transcript with **ScrollViewReader**, and use **alignmentGuide** to float the timestamps into alignment.

audience_en: **Developers who want to craft custom visuals and animation effects for their SwiftUI apps** and are interested in shaders and graphics composition.
summary: 由 UI Frameworks 團隊的 Haotian 主講,核心觀念是:**SwiftUI 的進階效果不在於複雜,而在於「組裝」**。他把 SwiftUI app 比喻成一條 **pipeline**——資料流經一連串標準「管子」(modifier 與 API),每個管子各自就能運作,而你可以串接、分支或合流它們,創意就發生在這裡。整場以一個 podcast app 為例,把陽春的逐字稿畫面,改造成像 Apple Music live lyrics 那樣有動態封面與時間同步捲動字幕的效果。

前景與背景兩條主線。背景用 **shader** 把封面圖轉成視覺特效:先用 **`.blur`** 柔化,再用 **`.layerEffect`**(三種 shader effect 中最具彈性、可取樣整層的一種)套上 Metal 寫的 `backgroundWarp` shader。從單純取樣、加上 **`float2` offset**、引入 **NoiseTexture**(以 RGB 的紅綠通道當作每像素的 organic offset),到二次取樣的 **domain warping** 產生流動的有機團塊;最後因為 shader 是 stateless,改用 **`TimelineView(.animation)`** 每幀傳入 elapsed 時間,讓畫面動起來。

前景是時間同步的逐字稿。用 `ScrollView` + `LazyVStack` 排出每行 `Text`,用 playback 的 timestamp 判斷 current line(粗體高亮、其餘淡出),再以 **`onChange`** 搭配 **`ScrollViewReader`** 的 `scrollTo(anchor: .center)` 讓目前行置中。浮動時間戳則用 **alignment** 觀念解決:把 timestamp 放進 **`.overlay`**,改用 `.bottomLeading` 對齊,再用 **`alignmentGuide`** 把 subview 的 bottom 覆寫成它自己的 top,純語意地讓子視圖上緣貼齊容器下緣,完全不用手動 offset。
實務收尾:這些效果全來自簡單管子的組合,且跨 Apple 裝置皆可運作。同一條 pipeline 換掉輸入(用陀螺儀取代音訊)、換掉 shader(用漣漪取代扭曲)、換掉前景(用自由 canvas 取代 scroll view),就能得到完全不同的成果——API 一樣,**你餵進什麼、怎麼串接,才是你的創意**。建議下載 sample project 動手調整 shader、noise 與速度。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: Haotian 提出全片主軸:SwiftUI 進階效果其實是一條 **pipeline**——資料流經一系列標準管子,各自可運作,而你能串接、分支或合流它們。**「advanced」在於組裝,而非複雜度**。路線圖為:拆解設計、打造進階效果、再以 creative pipeline 應用到自己的 app。

deepdive.title: Design breakdown
deepdive.body: 以自製 podcast app 為例,要把陽春逐字稿變成像 Apple Music live lyrics 的樣子。重點是現有 UI **已含所有需要的資料**(封面、播放資訊、逐字稿),問題不在缺資料,而在如何用 pipeline **轉換**它:封面接 shader pipe 再合流 time pipe 做動態視覺;逐字稿接同一條 time pipe 做時間同步捲動。

deepdive.title: Cover art and shader effects
deepdive.body: 從封面開始。原料就是一張封面圖,因為它會墊在逐字稿後面,需要先處理讓它不搶戲,再施加 shader 魔法。

deepdive.title: Cover art image
deepdive.body: 最基本的起點:`Image("CoverArt")`,直接顯示原始封面圖作為後續所有變換的素材。

deepdive.title: Blurred cover art image
deepdive.body: 用 **`.blur(radius: 30)`** 柔化封面,讓它退到背景不與前景的逐字稿競爭。接著解釋 shader 是什麼:向量圖被 GPU 點陣化成像素後,可在 GPU 上跑一支 shader 程式決定每個像素的顏色,且**每像素平行、彼此無感知**地獨立執行。

deepdive.title: Applying layer effect in SwiftUI
deepdive.body: 介紹三種 shader effect:**colorEffect**(改每像素顏色,適合黑白化)、**distortionEffect**(改取樣位置,適合幾何變形如 shear)、**layerEffect**(最具彈性,提供整層 layer 可取樣鄰近或整片像素,適合 blur)。此用例選 **layerEffect**,並在 `GeometryReader` 中套上 `ShaderLibrary.backgroundWarp()`。

deepdive.title: Writing layer effect shader in Metal
deepdive.body: 對應的 Metal 端 `backgroundWarp` 標上 `[[stitchable]]`,先只做 `layer.sample(position)` 原位取樣,得到一張和原圖一樣的影像——但這就是可往上堆疊的 shader 起點。

deepdive.title: Metal shader with offset parameter
deepdive.body: 為 shader 增加一個 **`float2 offset`** 參數,改成 `layer.sample(position + offset)`——告訴 SwiftUI「我要這個位置的顏色去跟隨另一個位置」,讓取樣位置可被位移。

deepdive.title: SwiftUI layer effect with offset parameter
deepdive.body: 在 SwiftUI 端對應傳入 `.float2(.init(x: 0, y: 0))`。當 offset 為零時影像不變;增加 offset 時每個像素都以相同位移取樣,整體均勻平移。

deepdive.title: SwiftUI layer effect with full-width offset
deepdive.body: 把 offset 改為 `.float2(.init(x: proxy.size.width, y: 0))`,以整個視圖寬度位移。但因為是**均勻 offset**,只會得到固定模式的平移,缺乏 organic 變化,需要某種能隨像素變動的東西。

deepdive.title: SwiftUI layer effect with noise sampling
deepdive.body: 改傳入視圖 size 與一張 **NoiseTexture**(`.image`)——一張預先算好、平滑隨機值的圖,用來產生有機的、隨像素變化的位移。

deepdive.title: Metal shader with noise sampling
deepdive.body: Metal 端以 `texture2d` 接收 NoiseTexture。用 position 與 size 算出 **uv**(相對位置),建立 repeat 模式的 sampler 取樣 noise;noise 的**紅、綠通道**各含不同雜訊模式,組成二維 offset,縮放後加到 position 取樣原圖,使影像產生輕微扭轉。

deepdive.title: Metal shader with domain warping
deepdive.body: 進一步**取樣兩次 noise**:第一次得到初始 offset `q`,再在被 `q` 位移過的 uv 位置取樣第二次,得到流動的有機團塊。這個分層雜訊技巧就是知名的 **domain warping**,sample app 附 preview 可自行調參。

deepdive.title: Driving animation with time
deepdive.body: shader 是 **stateless**——沒有前一幀記憶,輸出只取決於參數,因此要動畫就得傳入隨時間變化的值。**`TimelineView`** 正是需要的 pipe,以 `.animation` schedule 每幀觸發並帶 timestamp。

deepdive.title: SwiftUI layer effect with static visual
deepdive.body: 目前的 shader 效果雖酷但仍是**靜止**的,因為沒有任何隨時間變化的輸入,凸顯了需要引入 time pipe 才能讓它動起來。

deepdive.title: SwiftUI layer effect with animated visual
deepdive.body: 用 `TimelineView(.animation)` 算出 `elapsed = timeline.date.timeIntervalSince(startDate)`,把它以 `.float(elapsed)` 傳進 shader,加到取樣 noise 的位置上,圖樣便開始流動——這就是 time 驅動的 shader 動畫。

deepdive.title: Time-synced transcript view
deepdive.body: 轉到逐字稿:同樣要把 time 加進來,讓目前播放的那一行被高亮並置中於 scroll view。

deepdive.title: Basic transcript view
deepdive.body: 起點是熟悉的 SwiftUI:`ScrollView` 內一個 `LazyVStack`,以 `ForEach` 對每行逐字稿放一個 `Text`,每行各自是獨立 view。

deepdive.title: Time-synced transcript view
deepdive.body: 用 `PlaybackState` 的 timestamp 判斷 current line(用 `transcriptLineStyle(isCurrent:)` 讓目前行清晰、其餘淡出),再以 **`onChange`** 監看 `currentLineIndex` 變化,透過 **`ScrollViewReader`** 的 `scrollTo(i, anchor: .center)` 讓目前行保持置中。

deepdive.title: Floating timestamps with alignment guides
deepdive.body: 聚焦目前行旁的小時間戳。每行都在 `.overlay` 裡放了 timestamp,但只有 current line 的會顯示,如此不干擾版面、隨時待命。這個子視圖貼在容器邊緣的需求,無法用 `offset`(需同時知道兩視圖大小)解決,引出 alignment。

deepdive.title: Overlay with center alignment
deepdive.body: 解釋 alignment:每個視圖都有由兩軸定義的對齊點,布局系統用它定位。當 subview 放進 overlay,預設用 **center alignment** 把兩者對齊——就像一根針同時穿過兩視圖的對齊點,把它們釘在一起。

deepdive.title: Overlay with bottom leading alignment
deepdive.body: 把 overlay 的 alignment 改成 **`.bottomLeading`**,針改穿過兩視圖的 bottom-leading 點並鎖在那裡。此時布局系統向 subview 詢問它的 bottom-leading 對齊點。

deepdive.title: Overlay with alignment guide override
deepdive.body: 目標是讓 subview 的**上緣貼齊容器的下緣**。用 **`alignmentGuide(.bottom) { $0[.top] }`** 覆寫:當布局系統詢問 bottom 對齊時,改回傳該 subview 的 top,於是針依此點穿過。純語意覆寫即達成,無需手動 offset;此 API 還可定義自訂 alignment,closure 提供 `ViewDimensions` 以依實際大小計算。

deepdive.title: Creative pipelines
deepdive.body: 回顧:把設計拆成層、為每層找對的 API 把原始資料變成 view,每一階段的輸出餵給下一階段,這種串接就是 **creative pipeline**。但這只是此 app 的選擇——換成陀螺儀輸入、漣漪 shader、或自由 canvas 前景,就得到完全不同結果,**API 相同,你餵什麼、怎麼接才是你的創意**。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 鼓勵觀眾下載 sample project,動手調整 shader、改 noise、調速度、換圖,並在自己 app 中尋找「一個小視覺效果能帶來大不同」的機會——串起這些管子,簡單的東西很快就變得進階。

summary_en: Presented by Haotian from the UI Frameworks team, the core idea is that **SwiftUI's advanced effects are about composition, not complexity**. He frames a SwiftUI app as a **pipeline** — data flows through a series of standard "pipes" (modifiers and APIs), each of which works on its own, and you connect, branch, or merge them; that's where creativity happens. The running example is a podcast app whose bare-bones transcript view is reworked into something like Apple Music's live lyrics, with animated cover art and a time-synced scrolling transcript.

There are two main threads: background and foreground. The background uses a **shader** to turn the cover art into a visual effect: soften it with **`.blur`**, then apply a Metal `backgroundWarp` shader via **`.layerEffect`** (the most flexible of the three shader effects, able to sample the whole layer). It progresses from a plain sample, to a **`float2` offset**, to a **NoiseTexture** (using the red/green channels as a per-pixel organic offset), to a second sample producing **domain warping** with flowing organic blobs; finally, because shaders are stateless, a **`TimelineView(.animation)`** feeds in elapsed time each frame to make it move.

The foreground is a time-synced transcript. A `ScrollView` + `LazyVStack` lays out each `Text`, the playback timestamp decides the current line (bold and clear, the rest faded), and **`onChange`** with **`ScrollViewReader`**'s `scrollTo(anchor: .center)` keeps it centered. The floating timestamp is solved with **alignment**: place the timestamp in an **`.overlay`**, switch to `.bottomLeading`, then use **`alignmentGuide`** to override the subview's bottom to its own top — purely semantically pinning the subview's top edge to the container's bottom edge, with no manual offset.

The practical takeaway: these effects all come from composing simple pipes, and they work across Apple devices. The same pipeline with different inputs (gyroscope instead of audio), a different shader (ripple instead of twist), or a different foreground (a freeform canvas instead of a scroll view) yields something entirely different — the APIs are the same; **what you feed in and how you connect them is yours**. Download the sample project and experiment with the shader, noise, and speed.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Haotian sets the theme: SwiftUI's advanced effects are really a **pipeline** — data flows through a series of standard pipes that each work on their own, and you connect, branch, or merge them. **The "advanced" lies in the construction, not the complexity.** The roadmap: break down a design, build advanced effects, then apply them via a creative pipeline.

deepdive_en.title: Design breakdown
deepdive_en.body: Using a homemade podcast app, the goal is to turn a bare-bones transcript into something like Apple Music's live lyrics. The key insight: the existing UI **already contains all the data** (cover art, playback info, transcript). The question isn't what data is needed but how to **transform** it — the cover art feeds a shader pipe merged with a time pipe for dynamic visuals; the transcript feeds the same time pipe for synced scrolling.

deepdive_en.title: Cover art and shader effects
deepdive_en.body: Starting with the cover art. The raw material is just an image, and because it will sit behind the transcript it must first be tamed so it doesn't compete, then have shader magic applied.

deepdive_en.title: Cover art image
deepdive_en.body: The most basic starting point: `Image("CoverArt")`, simply displaying the raw cover image as the material for all subsequent transformations.

deepdive_en.title: Blurred cover art image
deepdive_en.body: A **`.blur(radius: 30)`** softens the cover so it recedes and doesn't compete with the foreground transcript. The talk then explains what a shader is: after the GPU rasterizes vectors into pixels, a shader program runs on the GPU to decide each pixel's color, executing **per-pixel in parallel with no awareness of neighbors**.

deepdive_en.title: Applying layer effect in SwiftUI
deepdive_en.body: Introduces the three shader effects: **colorEffect** (transforms each pixel's color, good for black-and-white), **distortionEffect** (changes the sampled position, good for geometric effects like shear), and **layerEffect** (the most flexible, providing the whole layer to sample neighbors or the entire region, good for blur). This use case picks **layerEffect**, applying `ShaderLibrary.backgroundWarp()` inside a `GeometryReader`.

deepdive_en.title: Writing layer effect shader in Metal
deepdive_en.body: The Metal `backgroundWarp`, marked `[[stitchable]]`, first just does `layer.sample(position)` to return the same image — but it's a shader you can now build on.

deepdive_en.title: Metal shader with offset parameter
deepdive_en.body: A **`float2 offset`** parameter is added, changing to `layer.sample(position + offset)` — telling SwiftUI "I want this position's color to follow that position's color," so the sampled position can be shifted.

deepdive_en.title: SwiftUI layer effect with offset parameter
deepdive_en.body: The SwiftUI side passes `.float2(.init(x: 0, y: 0))`. At zero offset the image is unchanged; increasing it makes every pixel sample with the same shift, uniformly translating the whole image.

deepdive_en.title: SwiftUI layer effect with full-width offset
deepdive_en.body: The offset becomes `.float2(.init(x: proxy.size.width, y: 0))`, shifting by the full view width. But because the **offset is uniform**, you only get a fixed-pattern shift lacking organic variation — something that varies per pixel is needed.

deepdive_en.title: SwiftUI layer effect with noise sampling
deepdive_en.body: The view size and a **NoiseTexture** (`.image`) are passed in — a pre-computed image of smooth random values used to produce organic, per-pixel variation.

deepdive_en.title: Metal shader with noise sampling
deepdive_en.body: The Metal side receives the NoiseTexture as `texture2d`. It computes a **uv** (relative position) from position and size, makes a repeat-mode sampler to sample the noise; the **red and green channels** each hold a different noise pattern, forming a 2D offset that's scaled and added to position to sample the original — twisting the image slightly.

deepdive_en.title: Metal shader with domain warping
deepdive_en.body: Going further, the noise is **sampled twice**: the first gives an initial offset `q`, then a second sample is taken at the uv shifted by `q`, yielding flowing organic blobs. This layered-noise technique is the well-known **domain warping**, and the sample app ships a preview to tweak parameters.

deepdive_en.title: Driving animation with time
deepdive_en.body: Shaders are **stateless** — no memory of the previous frame, output depends only on parameters — so animation requires passing a value that changes over time. **`TimelineView`** is exactly the pipe needed, firing each frame with a timestamp on the `.animation` schedule.

deepdive_en.title: SwiftUI layer effect with static visual
deepdive_en.body: The current shader effect, though cool, is still **frozen** because nothing time-varying drives it, underscoring the need to connect the time pipe to make it move.

deepdive_en.title: SwiftUI layer effect with animated visual
deepdive_en.body: Using `TimelineView(.animation)`, `elapsed = timeline.date.timeIntervalSince(startDate)` is computed and passed into the shader as `.float(elapsed)`, added to the noise-sampling position so the pattern starts flowing — shader animation driven by time.

deepdive_en.title: Time-synced transcript view
deepdive_en.body: Switching to the transcript: time must be added here too, so the currently playing line is highlighted and centered in the scroll view.

deepdive_en.title: Basic transcript view
deepdive_en.body: The starting point is familiar SwiftUI: a `LazyVStack` inside a `ScrollView`, with `ForEach` placing a `Text` per transcript line, each its own view.

deepdive_en.title: Time-synced transcript view
deepdive_en.body: A `PlaybackState` timestamp determines the current line (styled with `transcriptLineStyle(isCurrent:)` so it's clear and the rest fade), and **`onChange`** watches `currentLineIndex`, using **`ScrollViewReader`**'s `scrollTo(i, anchor: .center)` to keep the current line centered.

deepdive_en.title: Floating timestamps with alignment guides
deepdive_en.body: Focusing on the small timestamp by the current line. Every line has a timestamp in its `.overlay`, but only the current one is visible so it doesn't interfere with layout — always there, waiting. Pinning this subview to the container's edge can't be done with `offset` (which needs both views' sizes), motivating alignment.

deepdive_en.title: Overlay with center alignment
deepdive_en.body: Explains alignment: every view has an alignment point defined by both axes, which the layout system uses to position it. When a subview goes into an overlay, the default **center alignment** lines them up — like a pin punching through both views' alignment points to hold them together.

deepdive_en.title: Overlay with bottom leading alignment
deepdive_en.body: Changing the overlay's alignment to **`.bottomLeading`** makes the pin go through each view's bottom-leading point and lock there. The layout system then asks the subview for its bottom-leading alignment point.

deepdive_en.title: Overlay with alignment guide override
deepdive_en.body: The goal is the subview's **top edge touching the container's bottom edge**. The override **`alignmentGuide(.bottom) { $0[.top] }`** makes the subview return its top when asked for its bottom, so the pin punches through there. A purely semantic override achieves it with no manual offset; the API also supports custom alignments, with the closure giving `ViewDimensions` to compute points from actual size.

deepdive_en.title: Creative pipelines
deepdive_en.body: Recap: take a design, break it into layers, find the right API per layer to turn raw data into views, and feed each stage's output into the next — that chaining is a **creative pipeline**. But these were this app's choices — swap in gyroscope input, a ripple shader, or a freeform canvas foreground and you get something entirely different. **The APIs are the same; what you feed in and how you connect them is yours.**

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Viewers are encouraged to download the sample project and experiment — tweak the shader, change the noise, adjust the speed, try a different image — and to look for spots in their own app where a small visual effect makes a big difference. Connecting these pipes turns something simple into something advanced surprisingly fast.

title: Meet Core AI
gloss: 認識 Core AI
takeaway: Core AI 是 Apple 全新的裝置端 AI 模型部署框架，從 PyTorch 轉檔到 Swift 推論一條龍。
chapters: Convert a PyTorch model to Core AI
Input features for the snake model
Add KV cache buffers to PyTorch module
Update forward pass to read/write KV caches
Store KV cache NDArrays in ModelPlayer
Pass state views to inference function

points.text: **Core AI** 是 Apple 全新的裝置端 AI 模型部署框架，涵蓋從轉檔、整合到推論的完整生態。
用 Python 的 **coreai_torch.TorchConverter** 把 PyTorch 模型轉成 **.aimodel** 資產，並可驗證轉檔前後的數值一致性。
App 端以 **AIModel** 載入模型、**InferenceFunction** 取得推論函式，並用 **NDArray** 餵入與取出資料。
為 Transformer 加上 **KV cache** 狀態並重新轉檔，可顯著優化逐 token 的推論效能。
透過 **AIModelCache** 檢查快取並用 **AIModel.specialize** 預先特化模型，搭配 Instruments 進行效能剖析。

audience: 想把 **PyTorch 模型部署到 Apple 裝置端執行**、追求效能與低延遲的 ML 與 App 開發者。
gloss_en: Meet Core AI
takeaway_en: Core AI is Apple's new on-device AI model deployment framework, end to end from PyTorch conversion to Swift inference.

points_en.text: **Core AI** is Apple's new on-device AI model deployment framework, covering the full ecosystem from conversion to integration to inference.
Use Python's **coreai_torch.TorchConverter** to convert PyTorch models into **.aimodel** assets, and verify numerical consistency before and after conversion.
On the app side, load the model with **AIModel**, get the inference function with **InferenceFunction**, and feed data in and out with **NDArray**.
Adding **KV cache** state to a Transformer and re-converting can significantly optimize per-token inference performance.
Inspect the cache with **AIModelCache** and pre-specialize models with **AIModel.specialize**, profiling performance with Instruments.

audience_en: ML and app developers **who want to deploy PyTorch models to run on-device on Apple platforms** and care about performance and low latency.
summary: **Core AI** 是 Apple 全新的端側 AI 推論框架，也是驅動 on-device **Apple Intelligence** 的同一套引擎，如今開放給開發者使用。它從零為現代 AI 工作負載打造，能在 **CPU、GPU、Neural Engine** 上提供高效能推論，並且完全在裝置本地執行，沒有伺服器、也沒有 per-token 成本。Core AI 不只是一個框架，而是一整套涵蓋模型部署生命週期的技術，從模型最佳化、轉換、除錯到整合進 app，全程支援 AI 開發所需的快速迭代節奏。

本場以一個雙人貪食蛇遊戲為例，其中一條蛇由 Core AI 執行的模型操控。流程從 **Python/PyTorch** 端開始：用 **coreai-torch** 套件搭配 `torch.export`（並以 **dynamic_shapes** 標記動態序列長度）將模型匯出，再經 **TorchConverter** 轉成 `.aimodel` 資產；轉換後還能透過 Core AI 的 Python bindings 跑數值驗證，確認與原始 PyTorch 輸出的誤差在容許範圍內。進到 Xcode 後，可直接開啟 `.aimodel` 檢視模型大小、運算分布與函式簽章。

在 app 端，Core AI 提供現代化且漸進揭露的 **Swift API**：以 **AIModel** 載入模型、取得 **InferenceFunction**，用 **NDArray** 承載多維輸入輸出，再呼叫 `run` 執行推論。其中 **NDArray.MutableView** 等 non-escapable 型別在不犧牲效能的前提下提供記憶體安全。當遊戲序列愈來愈長導致推論變慢時（transformer 的二次方時間複雜度），講者透過 **States**（KV cache）解法：把 key/value 快取宣告為模型狀態（PyTorch 端用 `register_buffer`、轉換時加 `state_names`），讓快取在推論中就地讀寫，避免重算並省去傳入完整歷史，使延遲不再隨步數膨脹。

最後介紹進階能力：**Core AI Debugger** 可視覺化模型、檢視中間 tensor 並追溯回 Python 原始碼，配合 Instruments 與 debug gauge 找效能問題。重點概念是 **specialization**——出貨的是可跨裝置執行的來源表示，實際載入時須針對裝置特化並快取，首次可能耗時，建議透過 **AIModelCache** 檢查快取或用 `AIModel.specialize` 預先特化，避免卡在使用者互動流程；亦可在開發機做 ahead-of-time 編譯縮短時間。此外還有 **Core AI Models** repository、AI skills 與可接上 **Foundation Models** 的高階模型函式庫可運用。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: 由 Core AI 團隊工程師 **Ben** 開場，說明 AI 正以前所未有的速度演進，**Core AI** 就是用來駕馭這股動能、在 Apple 平台上打造進階 AI 功能的框架。他點出 Core AI 是驅動 on-device **Apple Intelligence** 的推論引擎，現在開放給開發者，並預告本場將涵蓋模型轉換、整合、效能最佳化與其他實用功能。

deepdive.title: What is Core AI
deepdive.body: 定義 **Core AI** 是 Apple 端側 AI 執行的新一代演進，從零為現代工作負載打造，能跨 **CPU、GPU、Neural Engine** 提供高速推論，並配備兼顧效能與記憶體安全的現代 **Swift API**。它與既有 **Python/PyTorch** 工作流自然銜接，支援模型特化、custom GPU kernels 與全新工具鏈（AOT 編譯、專屬 Instruments、可視化 Debugger），可從小型 speaker diarization 模型一路擴展到 70B 參數的 LLM，全部本地執行且無 per-token 成本。

deepdive.title: Model conversion
deepdive.body: 以一個雙人貪食蛇遊戲示範完整流程：其中一條蛇由模型操控，每個時間步看到描述棋盤狀態的特徵並累積成歷史，再預測最佳移動方向。講者用 AI coding assistant 在 PyTorch 快速搭出 **SnakeTransformer**，並以樸素模擬產生訓練資料，強調貪食蛇雖簡單，但所用工具與 API 可一路擴展到更大型用例。

deepdive.title: Convert a PyTorch model to Core AI
deepdive.body: 示範用 **coreai-torch** 套件轉換：先載入訓練好的 checkpoint 與樣本輸入，再以 `torch.export` 匯出並透過 **dynamic_shapes** 指定序列長度為動態（避免被固定成樣本長度 5），接著用 Core AI 的 decomposition table 跑 `run_decompositions`。最後執行 **TorchConverter** 指定輸入輸出名稱，將模型存成 `.aimodel` 資產。

deepdive.title: Verify converted model numerics
deepdive.body: 在離開 Python 環境前，用 Core AI 的 Python bindings 驗證轉換後模型與原始 PyTorch 的數值一致性。做法是載入兩邊模型、準備相同的貪食蛇輸入分別跑過 PyTorch module 與 Core AI **InferenceFunction**，再 assert 兩者輸出差距小於可接受的門檻（如 0.01）。

deepdive.title: App integration
deepdive.body: 進到 Xcode，直接開啟 `.aimodel` 檔即可看到模型大小、運算分布等 metadata，**Functions** 分頁則顯示每個函式的精確簽章。此模型只有一個函式，輸入棋盤特徵、輸出代表移動方向的 logits；**NDArray** 維度中的問號代表動態形狀，對應先前以動態序列長度轉換的設定。

deepdive.title: Core AI framework core types
deepdive.body: 介紹框架的核心型別與漸進揭露設計：**AIModel** 由 `.aimodel` 的 URL 初始化，用來檢視與載入一或多個 inference function；**InferenceFunction** 是代表單一已載入計算圖的可執行物件；**NDArray** 承載多維輸入輸出資料。並強調採用 non-escapable 等現代 Swift 語言特性，在不犧牲效能的前提下提供記憶體安全的 API。

deepdive.title: Initialize ModelPlayer with AIModel
deepdive.body: 建立 **ModelPlayer** 型別，在 app 初始化時以模型檔 URL 建構：載入 **AIModel** 並從中取得名為 main 的 **InferenceFunction**。這類 AIModel 與 InferenceFunction 物件通常在準備 AI 功能時（例如 app 啟動階段）就建好，以便後續重複使用。

deepdive.title: Run inference with NDArray inputs
deepdive.body: ModelPlayer 遵循自訂的 **SnakePlayer** 協定，核心是 `chooseAction`：先建立二維 float32 的 **NDArray**（第一維為當前序列長度、第二維為固定 hidden dimension），用 `writeFeatures` 搭配 **NDArray.MutableView** 安全高效地寫入特徵。接著 `run` 執行推論、取出 logits NDArray，再以其 view 挑選對應 logit 最大的方向作為下一步動作。

deepdive.title: Input features for the snake model
deepdive.body: 說明 `writeFeatures` 寫入的特徵內容：AI 蛇頭到四面牆的正規化距離、到最近食物的相對 X/Y 距離、以 one-hot 編碼的當前方向（四個元素）、到對手蛇的正規化距離，以及對手蛇的方向。這些特徵共同描述了每個時間步的棋盤狀態。

deepdive.title: Profiling with Instruments
deepdive.body: 實測讓兩條蛇都由模型操控，發現遊戲愈到後面愈慢。用 Xcode 新的 Core AI **Instruments** 觀察，可見推論區間隨時間明顯變長、延遲增加。原因是 transformer 對序列長度有二次方時間複雜度，而遊戲中序列長度會隨每一步移動持續增長。

deepdive.title: Optimizing performance
deepdive.body: 提出最佳化方向：transformer 每次序列變長都會為所有元素重算 key/value embeddings，常見對策是快取已算過的 keys/values 而非每次重算。在 Core AI 中可用 **States**——既被讀取、又在推論中就地更新的輸入——把 KV cache 變成模型狀態，如此既免重算，也不必每次傳入完整歷史，後續每步只需提供最新棋盤的新特徵。

deepdive.title: Add KV cache buffers to PyTorch module
deepdive.body: 回到 PyTorch 端的 authoring 程式碼，在 transformer module 內以 `register_buffer` 新增 key 與 value cache 張量。使用 register_buffer 的用意是讓匯出的 torch program 把這些張量視為可變 buffer，之後便能被 Core AI 轉換成 **States**。

deepdive.title: Update forward pass to read/write KV caches
deepdive.body: 在 module 的 `forward` 中加入實際使用快取的邏輯：逐層從 `k_cache`/`v_cache` 讀出先前的 keys/values，對新 token 計算 q/k/v 並在有效前綴上做注意力，再把更新後的 keys/values 寫回快取（以 `copy_` 就地更新堆疊後的張量）。

deepdive.title: Re-convert model with state names
deepdive.body: 沿用先前的轉換程式碼重新轉換模型，但這次在 `torch.export` 傳入新增的 `position_ids` 輸入，並在 **TorchConverter** 呼叫中加上 **state_names** 參數（如 keyCache、valueCache）來指定新狀態引數的名稱，最後同樣存成 `.aimodel`。

deepdive.title: Store KV cache NDArrays in ModelPlayer
deepdive.body: 更新 app 程式碼以配合新函式簽章：在 **ModelPlayer** 中新增 keyCache 與 valueCache 兩個 **NDArray** 屬性作為每次推論要傳入的狀態引數，並以 transformer 預期的形狀（layers、最大 context 長度、hidden dim）初始化。模型轉換時設定快取為涵蓋最大可能 context 長度的固定大小。

deepdive.title: Pass state views to inference function
deepdive.body: 推論時建立 **InferenceFunction.MutableViews** 集合，分別 insert keyCache 與 valueCache 的可變 view，再透過 `run` 的 **states** 參數傳入，使快取在每次推論中被讀取並就地更新。重跑後遊戲維持穩定速度不再變慢，Instruments 也確認推論延遲的增長速率大幅趨緩。

deepdive.title: Additional features
deepdive.body: 介紹貪食蛇未用到但實用的功能。**coreai-torch** 直接轉換雖簡單，但若需更多控制，Core AI Python 套件還支援直接以 Core AI API authoring 模型、針對 Apple Silicon 最佳化、以 **Metal 4** 定義 custom kernels（詳見 model authoring 與最佳化專場）。除錯方面，**Core AI Debugger** 可視覺化模型、檢視中間 tensor 值並追溯回 Python 原始碼，Xcode 中的 Core AI debug gauge 則即時顯示 Core AI 活動。

deepdive.title: Specialization
deepdive.body: 解釋出貨的 AI 模型是可在任何 Apple 裝置執行的來源表示，但實際載入前必須針對當前裝置做 **specialization** 並快取。對非常大的模型，首次特化可能相當耗時，雖然後續從快取載入很快，這段首次延遲仍需事先規劃，且建議避免讓特化發生在使用者互動流程中。

deepdive.title: Check model cache before loading
deepdive.body: Core AI 提供對 app 預設模型快取的程式化存取：透過 **AIModelCache** 嘗試取得模型，若回傳 nil 代表尚未特化、需要先特化。可用此來把功能 gate 住，或在主執行緒提示使用者「正在準備 AI 功能，可能需要稍候」。

deepdive.title: Request model specialization
deepdive.body: 可用 `AIModel.specialize` 明確請求特化，與載入動作脫鉤，例如在下載完資產後或使用者開啟某功能時預先特化好。**SpecializationOptions** 可配置最佳化方式；**AIModelCache** 還能刪除不需要的項目、控制快取保存政策，甚至在同一 app group 的多個 app 間共享快取。特化過程含 compilation 與產生 device/OS 綁定的可執行 artifacts 兩步，其中 compilation 佔多數延遲，可透過開發機 ahead-of-time 編譯顯著縮短裝置端工作量。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 總結 **Core AI** 在所有 Apple Silicon 上可用，與既有 Python 工具緊密整合、提供現代 Swift 框架高效執行模型，並附帶最先進的除錯工具。並指向 **Core AI Models** repository：內含可一鍵轉換最佳化的熱門模型、Core AI 相關 AI skills，以及含內建低階推論最佳化的 Swift 套件，其中還提供可接上 **Foundation Models** 框架的 Core AI Language model API，讓開發者帶入自訂模型與取樣策略。

summary_en: **Core AI** is Apple's new on-device AI inference framework, the same engine that powers on-device **Apple Intelligence**, now opened up for developers. Built from the ground up for modern AI workloads, it delivers high-performance inference across the **CPU, GPU, and Neural Engine**, running entirely on-device with no server and no per-token cost. It is more than a framework, it is a full set of technologies spanning the model deployment lifecycle, from optimization and conversion to debugging and app integration, all tuned for the fast iteration that building AI features requires.

The session uses a two-player snake game where one snake is driven by a Core AI model. The flow starts in **Python/PyTorch**: the model is exported with `torch.export` (marking the sequence length as dynamic via **dynamic_shapes**) and converted to a `.aimodel` asset using **TorchConverter** from the **coreai-torch** package, with numerics verified against the original PyTorch output via Core AI's Python bindings. In Xcode you can open the `.aimodel` directly to inspect model size, op distribution, and function signatures.

On the app side, Core AI offers a modern, progressively disclosing **Swift API**: load the model with **AIModel**, get an **InferenceFunction**, carry multi-dimensional data in **NDArray**, and call `run`. Non-escapable types like **NDArray.MutableView** provide memory safety without sacrificing performance. When the growing sequence makes inference slow (transformer quadratic time complexity), the speaker uses **States** to implement a KV cache: key/value caches are declared as model state (`register_buffer` in PyTorch, `state_names` at conversion) and read/written in-place during inference, avoiding recomputation and the need to pass the full history, so latency stops ballooning with each step.

Finally, the talk covers advanced capabilities: the **Core AI Debugger** visualizes the model, inspects intermediate tensors, and traces ops back to Python source, alongside Instruments and a debug gauge. A key concept is **specialization**, the shipped model is a portable source representation that must be specialized and cached for the device on first load, which can be slow, so use **AIModelCache** to check the cache or `AIModel.specialize` to prepare ahead of time and keep it out of user-interactive flows; ahead-of-time compilation on your dev machine reduces this further. The **Core AI Models** repository, AI skills, and higher-level libraries that plug into **Foundation Models** round out the ecosystem.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Core AI engineer **Ben** opens by noting AI is advancing faster than ever and that **Core AI** is built to harness that momentum for advanced AI features on Apple platforms. He points out Core AI is the inference engine powering on-device **Apple Intelligence**, now available to developers, and previews the agenda: model conversion, app integration, performance optimization, and additional useful features.

deepdive_en.title: What is Core AI
deepdive_en.body: Defines **Core AI** as the next evolution of on-device AI execution on Apple, built from the ground up for modern workloads, delivering fast inference across **CPU, GPU, and Neural Engine** with a modern, memory-safe **Swift API**. It fits existing **Python/PyTorch** workflows and supports specialization, custom GPU kernels, and a new toolchain (AOT compilation, dedicated Instruments, a visual Debugger), scaling from small speaker diarization models up to a 70B-parameter LLM, all running locally with no per-token cost.

deepdive_en.title: Model conversion
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates the full flow with a two-player snake game where one snake is model-driven: at each step it sees features describing the board, accumulates a history, and predicts the best direction. The speaker sketched a **SnakeTransformer** quickly in PyTorch with an AI coding assistant and trained it on naively simulated data, noting that although snake is simple, the same tools and APIs scale to far larger use cases.

deepdive_en.title: Convert a PyTorch model to Core AI
deepdive_en.body: Shows conversion with the **coreai-torch** package: load the trained checkpoint and a sample input, export via `torch.export` while using **dynamic_shapes** to mark the sequence length as dynamic (so it isn't traced at the static sample length of 5), then run `run_decompositions` with Core AI's decomposition table. Finally **TorchConverter** is run with named inputs/outputs and the model is saved as a `.aimodel` asset.

deepdive_en.title: Verify converted model numerics
deepdive_en.body: Before leaving Python, the converted model's numerics are validated against the original PyTorch using Core AI's Python bindings. Both models are loaded, the same snake input is run through the PyTorch module and the Core AI **InferenceFunction**, and a sufficiently small delta (e.g. 0.01) between outputs is asserted.

deepdive_en.title: App integration
deepdive_en.body: In Xcode, opening the `.aimodel` file shows model size, op distribution, and other metadata, while the **Functions** tab shows each function's exact signature. This model has a single function taking board features as input and producing direction logits; the question marks in **NDArray** dimensions denote dynamic shapes, matching the dynamic sequence length used at conversion.

deepdive_en.title: Core AI framework core types
deepdive_en.body: Introduces the core types and progressive disclosure: **AIModel** is initialized from a `.aimodel` URL and used to inspect and load one or more inference functions; **InferenceFunction** is the runnable object representing a single loaded compute graph; **NDArray** holds multi-dimensional input/output data. The API leans on modern Swift features like non-escapable types to stay memory-safe without sacrificing performance.

deepdive_en.title: Initialize ModelPlayer with AIModel
deepdive_en.body: Creates a **ModelPlayer** type constructed at app init with the model file URL: it builds the **AIModel** and loads the main **InferenceFunction** from it. These AIModel and InferenceFunction objects are typically created when preparing the AI feature (for example at app startup) so they can be reused.

deepdive_en.title: Run inference with NDArray inputs
deepdive_en.body: ModelPlayer conforms to a custom **SnakePlayer** protocol whose key method is `chooseAction`: it creates a 2D float32 **NDArray** (first dim the current sequence length, second the fixed hidden dimension) and writes features via `writeFeatures` using a safe, efficient **NDArray.MutableView**. It then `run`s inference, extracts the logits NDArray, and picks the direction with the largest corresponding logit from its view.

deepdive_en.title: Input features for the snake model
deepdive_en.body: Explains the features `writeFeatures` writes: the AI snake head's normalized distance to all walls, the relative X/Y distance to the nearest food, four elements one-hot encoding the current direction, the normalized distance to the other snake, and the opponent's direction. Together these describe the board state at each time step.

deepdive_en.title: Profiling with Instruments
deepdive_en.body: Running with both snakes model-driven, the game slows down over time. Using the new Core AI **Instruments**, the inference intervals are seen growing noticeably larger, meaning rising latency. This makes sense because transformers have quadratic time complexity in sequence length, and the game's sequence grows with every move.

deepdive_en.title: Optimizing performance
deepdive_en.body: Proposes the fix: each longer input makes the transformer recompute key/value embeddings for the whole sequence, so a common strategy is to cache previously computed keys/values rather than recompute. In Core AI this is done with **States**, inputs that are both read and updated in-place during inference; making the KV caches states avoids recomputation and removes the need to pass the full history, so each later step only needs the latest board's new features.

deepdive_en.title: Add KV cache buffers to PyTorch module
deepdive_en.body: Back in the PyTorch authoring code, key and value cache tensors are added inside the transformer module via `register_buffer`. Using register_buffer ensures the exported torch program treats them as mutable buffers, which Core AI will later convert into **States**.

deepdive_en.title: Update forward pass to read/write KV caches
deepdive_en.body: The module's `forward` is updated to actually use the caches: per layer it reads previous keys/values from `k_cache`/`v_cache`, computes q/k/v for the new token and attends over the valid prefix, then writes the updated keys/values back into the caches (with `copy_` on the stacked tensors).

deepdive_en.title: Re-convert model with state names
deepdive_en.body: The same conversion code is rerun, now passing a new `position_ids` input to `torch.export` and adding the **state_names** argument (e.g. keyCache, valueCache) to the **TorchConverter** call to name the new state arguments, finally saving the `.aimodel` again.

deepdive_en.title: Store KV cache NDArrays in ModelPlayer
deepdive_en.body: The app code is updated for the new signature: **ModelPlayer** gains keyCache and valueCache **NDArray** properties to pass as state arguments on each inference, initialized with the transformer's expected shape (layers, max context length, hidden dim). The model was converted so the caches are always a fixed size for a maximum possible context length.

deepdive_en.title: Pass state views to inference function
deepdive_en.body: At inference time an **InferenceFunction.MutableViews** collection is built, inserting mutable views of keyCache and valueCache, and passed as the **states** argument of `run`, so the caches are read and updated in-place each inference. After this the game holds a steady speed, and Instruments confirms inference latency now grows much more slowly.

deepdive_en.title: Additional features
deepdive_en.body: Highlights features unused in the snake game but broadly useful. Direct **coreai-torch** conversion is simple, but for more control the Core AI Python package also supports authoring models directly with Core AI APIs, optimizing for Apple Silicon, and defining custom kernels with **Metal 4** (see the model authoring and optimization talk). For debugging, the **Core AI Debugger** visualizes the model, inspects intermediate tensor values, and traces ops back to Python source, while Xcode's Core AI debug gauge streams live activity.

deepdive_en.title: Specialization
deepdive_en.body: Explains the shipped AI model is a source representation runnable on any Apple device, but before loading it must be **specialized** for the current device and cached. For very large models the first specialization can take significant time, and although later loads from cache are fast, that first-time cost must be planned for and should be kept out of user-interactive flows.

deepdive_en.title: Check model cache before loading
deepdive_en.body: Core AI gives programmatic access to the app's default model cache via **AIModelCache**: request the model from it, and if nil is returned it isn't present and needs specialization. This can gate features or inform users on the main thread that the app is preparing AI features and they may need to wait.

deepdive_en.title: Request model specialization
deepdive_en.body: You can explicitly request specialization with `AIModel.specialize`, decoupled from loading, for example after downloading assets or when a user opts into a feature. **SpecializationOptions** configures how the model is optimized; **AIModelCache** can also delete unneeded entries, control retention policy, and even share a cache across apps in the same app group. Specialization involves compilation plus generating device/OS-bound executable artifacts, with compilation incurring most of the latency, which ahead-of-time compilation on the dev machine can significantly reduce.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Wraps up that **Core AI** is available on all Apple Silicon, integrates tightly with familiar Python tools, provides a modern Swift framework for efficient inference, and ships state-of-the-art debugging tools. It points to the **Core AI Models** repository: popular models a single command away from being converted and optimized, Core AI AI skills, and a Swift package with model-family libraries that bake in low-level inference optimizations, including a Core AI Language model API that plugs into the **Foundation Models** framework for custom models and sampling strategies.

title: Dive into Core AI model authoring and optimization
gloss: 深入 Core AI 模型編寫與最佳化
takeaway: 用全新的 Core AI 框架走完自訂模型部署流程:從 PyTorch 轉換、最佳化、除錯,到寫自訂 Metal kernel 與重新編寫模型,部署到 Apple silicon。
chapters: Convert, optimize and run inference with Core AI
Define a SiLU Metal kernel with PyTorch reference
Use a custom Metal kernel and convert with TorchConverter

points.text: 全新 **Core AI 框架**提供 Apple silicon 上**完整的自訂模型部署工作流**。
**Python 工作流**:用 torch.export 匯出模型,再以 coreai_torch.TorchConverter 轉成 Core AI 並 optimize()、存成 .aimodel。
在裝置端以 **AIModel.load 載入 .aimodel**、load_function 取得函式並執行 inference(NDArray 輸入)。
提供 **Core AI Debugger** 協助檢視與診斷模型,並有 model optimization 段落講最佳化技巧。
進階可寫**自訂 Metal kernel(TorchMetalKernel,如 fused SiLU)**,經 register_custom_kernels 把 MSL 整合進 asset,並支援 model re-authoring。

audience: **要把自訂機器學習模型最佳化並部署到 Apple silicon、熟悉 PyTorch 的 ML 工程師。**
gloss_en: Dive into Core AI model authoring and optimization
takeaway_en: Walk through the full custom model deployment workflow with the new Core AI framework: from PyTorch conversion, optimization, and debugging to writing custom Metal kernels and re-authoring models, deployed to Apple silicon.

points_en.text: The new **Core AI framework** provides a **complete custom model deployment workflow** on Apple silicon.
**Python workflow**: export the model with torch.export, then convert it to Core AI with coreai_torch.TorchConverter, optimize(), and save as .aimodel.
On device, **load the .aimodel with AIModel.load**, get a function with load_function, and run inference (with NDArray inputs).
Provides the **Core AI Debugger** to help inspect and diagnose models, plus a model optimization section covering optimization techniques.
For advanced cases, write a **custom Metal kernel (TorchMetalKernel, such as a fused SiLU)**, integrate the MSL into the asset via register_custom_kernels, and support model re-authoring.

audience_en: **ML engineers familiar with PyTorch who need to optimize and deploy custom machine learning models to Apple silicon.**
summary: 這場由 Core AI 團隊的 Sachin 與 Nicole 主講，聚焦 **Core AI** 的 Python 生態系，帶你把自訂模型完整部署到 Apple Silicon——從轉換、最佳化、除錯到進階改寫。Core AI 是涵蓋整個模型部署生命週期的技術套件；本場介紹各種 Python 函式庫與工具，以及全新的 **Core AI Debugger**。若你用過 **Core ML**，整套以 Python／**PyTorch** 為中心的流程會相當熟悉。

起點是 **coreai-models** 開源儲存庫，內含可直接執行 LLM 的 Swift package、各種使用情境的範例模型、可重用元件，以及一組 **Core AI skills**——把這些 skills 裝進你的 coding assistant，就能像專家一樣上手 Core AI（本場多數程式碼正是與 agent 協作產出）。基本流程以 `pip install coreai-torch` 安裝後，把 PyTorch 的 **exported program**（`torch.export`）交給 **TorchConverter** 轉成 Core AI program，再 `optimize()` 並存成可在 Apple Silicon 執行的 **.aimodel** asset，最後直接從 Python 載入 function 做推論。

最佳化以 **coreai-opt** 進行 config-driven 壓縮，支援 int4／int8／FP4／FP8 與彈性 granularity，也提供校準資料或 quantization aware training 的量化 API。講者以 8.5 億參數的 **SAM3** 影像分割模型示範，用 `presets.w4`（4-bit per-channel）把 3GB 模型壓到約 430MB，但有一朵被遮蔽的花漏偵測了——問題出在對每一層都套用同樣激進壓縮。接著 Nicole 用 **Core AI Debugger** 這個獨立 app 把模型以圖形化結構檢視、在真實硬體上執行，並透過新的 **save intermediates** API 與 baseline 比對 **PSNR**，找出大量低分 sync point 集中在只占 4% 參數的 detector decoder，於是改成讓量化忽略 detector，便在數分鐘內恢復 baseline 品質且維持小體積。

最後是進階改寫。除了把多個 op **fuse** 成單一 kernel dispatch、沿用 Core AI 內建的快速 primitive（如 Scaled Dot Product Attention），還能用 **custom Metal 4 kernel**：以 MSL 寫 kernel、提供 PyTorch reference，透過 **TorchMetalKernel** 註冊後，MSL 會直接內嵌進 asset 隨模型發行。更進一步的 **model re-authoring** 則為特定目標（尤其 iOS）重寫整個模型——採用 static shapes、channels-first layout、convolutional 投影、KV cache in-place 更新等模式，並輔以嚴謹的單元／整合測試。講者把 SAM3 改寫成 image_encode／text_encode／detect 三個獨立 function，搭配 4-bit palettization 壓縮兩個 encoder、保留未壓縮的 detector，換 prompt 時只需重跑 text encoder 與 detector，第二次推論快了 76%。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: 由 Core AI 工程師 Sachin 開場（稍後 Nicole 加入），說明本場聚焦 **Core AI** 的 Python 生態系，帶你把模型高效部署到 Apple Silicon。Core AI 涵蓋從最佳化、轉換到除錯與整合的完整部署生命週期；你將認識各種 Python 函式庫與工具，以及可成為工作流核心的 **Core AI Debugger**。

deepdive.title: Models and skills
deepdive.body: 介紹生態系前沿的 **coreai-models** 開源儲存庫：內含可在 app 中執行 LLM 的 Swift package、針對各種情境工程化的範例模型與可重用元件，以及一組 **Core AI skills**。把這些 skills 裝進你慣用的 coding assistant，它便能依你鎖定的硬體與限制把高階構想轉成清楚的部署計畫，讓你像專家一樣運用 Core AI——本場多數程式碼正是與 agent 協作產出。

deepdive.title: Python workflow
deepdive.body: 說明以 **coreai-torch** 為核心的入口：`pip install coreai-torch` 會同時裝上 coreai 與 coreai-torch。你把 PyTorch 的 **exported program** 交給它即可直接轉成 Core AI 模型，並支援把多個模型組成單一 artifact、為特定 op 註冊 custom lowering、內嵌 **Metal 4** kernel，最後 specialize 成最佳化 asset 並完全從 Python 在 Apple Silicon 上執行。

deepdive.title: Convert, optimize and run inference with Core AI
deepdive.body: 以一個兩層 linear 加 relu 的 MLP 走過完整流程：先用 **`torch.export`** 傳入模型與 example_input 取得 **exported_program**（含完整計算圖、權重、shapes），再以 **TorchConverter** 搭配 input／output 名稱轉成 core_ai program，`optimize()` 後存成 **.aimodel** asset。要推論只需載入 function 並傳入「名稱對 numpy tensor」的字典即可，整個轉換、最佳化、執行都在 Python 完成。

deepdive.title: Model optimization
deepdive.body: 以 8.5 億參數的 **SAM3**（image encoder＋text encoder 占 96% 參數，再加 DETR detector 與 mask decoder）示範 **coreai-opt** 的 config-driven 壓縮，支援 int4／int8／FP4／FP8 與彈性 granularity。轉換 helper 會以 Core AI 的 decomposition table 保留 attention 等高階語意，並可用 coreai-opt 轉 16-bit。baseline 32-bit 模型逾 3GB，用 **`presets.w4`**（EAGER 模式、4-bit per-channel）壓到約 430MB 後，卻有一朵被遮蔽的花漏偵測——因為對每一層都套同樣激進壓縮。

deepdive.title: Core AI Debugger
deepdive.body: Nicole 介紹獨立 app **Core AI Debugger**：可用圖形化檢視模型結構、在真實硬體上執行、並對照 reference run 驗證推論正確性。它以 PyTorch module 分組 operations、structure viewer 顯示連結與執行順序、source viewer 對應原始 Python 行。她用新的 **save intermediates** API 抓取 baseline 各 op 的中間 tensor，再以 **PSNR** 比對 sync point，發現低分集中在僅占 4% 參數的 **detector decoder**，於是改讓量化忽略 detector，數分鐘內恢復 baseline 品質且維持極小體積。

deepdive.title: Advanced authoring
deepdive.body: Sachin 回來談進階模型改寫：把目光深入到定義輸入到輸出計算圖的 PyTorch source 本身，調整它在硬體上的執行方式。最簡單的形式是把一組 op **fuse** 成單一 kernel dispatch；Core AI 已內建如 **Scaled Dot Product Attention** 等重運算的快速 kernel 與 primitive，範例可在 coreai-models 儲存庫找到。

deepdive.title: Custom Metal kernels
deepdive.body: 若想更高度客製，Core AI 支援 **custom Metal 4 kernel**。流程上為 coreai-torch 加入第二個輸入——以 **MSL（Metal Shading Language）** 撰寫的 kernel 原始碼；converter 同時吃 PyTorch 模型與 kernel，把兩者打包成單一 asset，MSL 直接內嵌、隨模型一起發行。

deepdive.title: Define a SiLU Metal kernel with PyTorch reference
deepdive.body: 以 **SiLU**（Sigmoid Linear Unit，生成式 transformer 常見激活函數）為例：先用 `x * torch.sigmoid(x)` 定義 torch.export 追蹤所見的 **PyTorch reference**，再以 MSL 實作一個每 thread 處理一個元素、在 GPU 上算 fused activation 的 element-wise kernel。最後以 **TorchMetalKernel** 註冊，給定 Metal source、PyTorch reference 與輸入輸出名稱（此例為 x 與 y，與 MSL 中使用的名稱一致）。

deepdive.title: Use a custom Metal kernel and convert with TorchConverter
deepdive.body: 在模型中像呼叫一般 Python function 一樣使用此 kernel：傳入輸入、指定 thread grid 即可，並對每次實例化傳入 **result_shapes**，讓 Core AI 在 dynamic shape 下也能從輸入推導輸出 shape。轉換時先以 **`register_custom_kernels`** 向 TorchConverter 註冊，再 add exported program；Metal source 會直接嵌入 asset，kernel 隨模型同行。更多高效 Metal kernel 寫法見「Optimize custom machine learning operations with Metal tensors」。

deepdive.title: Model re-authoring
deepdive.body: 比 fuse 更進一步的 **model re-authoring**：為特定目標（尤其 iOS）重寫整個模型，可能更換 operations、採用新的 tensor layout、甚至改變模型介面。手法包含用預定義 pattern 告知 Core AI 特定概念（如 LLM 的 **KV cache in-place 更新**），以及採用 **static tensor shapes**、**channels-first** layout 與 convolutional op pattern 以善用底層 primitive。講者把 SAM3 拆成 image_encode／text_encode／detect 三個獨立 function，對兩個 encoder 套 4-bit palettization（**KMeansPalettizer**）、保留未壓縮 detector，並把影像由 1008 縮到 336 以在 iPhone 執行；換 prompt 時只重跑 text encoder 與 detector，第二次推論快了 76%，並強調 module 與 model 層級的嚴謹測試。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 總結今日可立即著手的事：用 Core AI 的 Python 函式庫轉換 PyTorch 模型、以 **coreai-opt** 最佳化、需要看清模型內部時用 **Core AI Debugger**、以 **coreai-models** 的範例為基礎，並把 **Core AI Skills** 接進你慣用的 AI agent，讓它像專家一樣協助你運用這個新框架。

summary_en: Presented by Sachin and Nicole from the Core AI team, this session zooms in on **Core AI**'s Python ecosystem and walks through deploying a custom model end-to-end on Apple Silicon—from conversion and optimization to debugging and advanced authoring. Core AI is a complete suite covering the model deployment lifecycle; the talk introduces the Python libraries and tools plus the new **Core AI Debugger**. If you've used **Core ML** before, this Python/**PyTorch**-centric flow will feel familiar.

The starting point is the open-source **coreai-models** repository: a Swift package for running LLMs in your app, example models for various use cases, reusable components, and a set of **Core AI skills** you install into your coding assistant to use Core AI like an expert from day one (most of the talk's code was co-developed with an agent). The basic flow: after `pip install coreai-torch`, hand a PyTorch **exported program** (`torch.export`) to the **TorchConverter** to get a Core AI program, call `optimize()`, save an **.aimodel** asset that runs on Apple Silicon, and load a function to run inference directly from Python.

Optimization uses **coreai-opt** for config-driven compression—supporting int4/int8/FP4/FP8 and flexible granularity, plus quantization APIs that work with calibration data or quantization-aware training. The driving example is the 850-million-parameter **SAM3** segmentation model: `presets.w4` (4-bit per-channel) shrinks a 3GB model to ~430MB, but one occluded flower goes undetected because the same aggressive compression was applied to every layer. Nicole then uses the standalone **Core AI Debugger** app to visualize the model graph, run on real hardware, and—via the new **save intermediates** API—compare against the baseline by **PSNR**, finding the low-scoring sync points concentrated in the detector decoder, which holds only 4% of parameters; ignoring the detector during quantization restores baseline quality in minutes while staying tiny.

Finally, advanced authoring. Beyond **fusing** ops into a single kernel dispatch and reusing Core AI's built-in fast primitives (like Scaled Dot Product Attention), you can write a **custom Metal 4 kernel**: author the kernel in MSL, provide a PyTorch reference, register it via **TorchMetalKernel**, and the MSL is embedded directly into the asset and ships with the model. Going further, **model re-authoring** rewrites the whole model for a specific target (especially iOS) using static shapes, channels-first layouts, convolutional projections, and in-place KV-cache updates, backed by rigorous module- and model-level testing. The speaker re-authors SAM3 into three independent functions—image_encode, text_encode, and detect—compressing the two encoders with 4-bit palettization while leaving the detector uncompressed; swapping the prompt only re-runs the text encoder and detector, making the second inference 76% faster.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Core AI engineer Sachin opens (Nicole joins later), framing the session around **Core AI**'s Python ecosystem and deploying models efficiently on Apple Silicon. Core AI spans the full deployment lifecycle—from optimization and conversion to debugging and integration—and you'll meet its Python libraries and tools plus the **Core AI Debugger**, which can become an integral part of the workflow.

deepdive_en.title: Models and skills
deepdive_en.body: Introduces the open-source **coreai-models** repository at the forefront of the ecosystem: a Swift package for running LLMs in your app, example models engineered for various use cases, reusable components, and a set of **Core AI skills**. Installed into your coding assistant, the skills turn high-level ideas into a clear deployment plan based on your target hardware and constraints—most of the talk's code was co-developed with an agent using them.

deepdive_en.title: Python workflow
deepdive_en.body: Describes the **coreai-torch**-centered entry point: `pip install coreai-torch` installs both coreai and coreai-torch. You hand it a PyTorch **exported program** and it converts directly to a Core AI model, with advanced features to assemble multiple models into one artifact, register custom lowerings for specific ops, inline **Metal 4** kernels, and finally specialize into optimized assets that run natively on Apple Silicon entirely from Python.

deepdive_en.title: Convert, optimize and run inference with Core AI
deepdive_en.body: Walks a two-layer-linear-plus-relu MLP through the whole pipeline: **`torch.export`** with the model and an example_input yields an **exported_program** (full graph, weights, shapes), then **TorchConverter** with input/output names converts to a core_ai program, which is `optimize()`d and saved as an **.aimodel** asset. Inference just needs a function loaded from the program and a dictionary mapping input names to numpy tensors—conversion, optimization, and execution all from Python.

deepdive_en.title: Model optimization
deepdive_en.body: Uses the 850M-parameter **SAM3** (image and text encoders are 96% of parameters, plus a DETR detector and mask decoder) to showcase **coreai-opt**'s config-driven compression with int4/int8/FP4/FP8 and flexible granularity. The conversion helper runs decompositions with Core AI's custom table to preserve high-level semantics like attention and can cast to 16-bit. The 32-bit baseline exceeds 3GB; **`presets.w4`** (EAGER mode, 4-bit per-channel) shrinks it to ~430MB, but one occluded flower goes undetected—because the same aggressive compression hit every layer.

deepdive_en.title: Core AI Debugger
deepdive_en.body: Nicole introduces the standalone **Core AI Debugger**: visualize model structure as a graph, execute on specific hardware for true runtime results, and validate inference against a reference run. Operations are grouped by PyTorch module; the structure viewer shows connectivity and execution order, and the source viewer grounds you in the original Python. Using the new **save intermediates** API to capture baseline tensors, she compares sync points by **PSNR**, finds the low-scoring ones concentrated in the **detector decoder** (only 4% of parameters), and changes the scheme to ignore the detector—restoring baseline quality in minutes while staying a fraction of the size.

deepdive_en.title: Advanced authoring
deepdive_en.body: Sachin returns to advanced re-authoring: zooming into the PyTorch source itself—the graph of computations from inputs to outputs—and tuning how it runs on hardware. The simplest form is **fusing** a group of ops into a single kernel dispatch. Core AI already ships fast kernels and primitives for heavy operations like **Scaled Dot Product Attention** common in Transformers, with examples in the coreai-models repository.

deepdive_en.title: Custom Metal kernels
deepdive_en.body: For deeper customization, Core AI supports **custom Metal 4 kernels**. This adds a second input to coreai-torch—your kernel's source written in **MSL (Metal Shading Language)**. The converter takes both the PyTorch model and the kernel and bundles them into a single asset, with the MSL embedded right inside so it ships with the model.

deepdive_en.title: Define a SiLU Metal kernel with PyTorch reference
deepdive_en.body: Uses **SiLU** (Sigmoid Linear Unit, a common activation in generative transformers) as the example: first a **PyTorch reference** `x * torch.sigmoid(x)` that torch.export sees during tracing, then an element-wise MSL kernel (one thread per element) computing the fused activation on the GPU. It's registered as a **TorchMetalKernel** with the Metal source, PyTorch reference, and input/output names (here x and y, matching the names used in the MSL).

deepdive_en.title: Use a custom Metal kernel and convert with TorchConverter
deepdive_en.body: The kernel is called like any Python function—pass the input and specify the thread grid—and each instantiation passes **result_shapes** so Core AI can bake in output-shape computation for dynamic-shaped inputs. At conversion you **`register_custom_kernels`** with the TorchConverter, then add the exported program; the Metal source is embedded directly in the asset so the kernel travels with the model. See "Optimize custom machine learning operations with Metal tensors" for efficient kernel writing.

deepdive_en.title: Model re-authoring
deepdive_en.body: Beyond fusing, **model re-authoring** rewrites the entire model for a specific target (especially iOS), possibly swapping operations, adopting new tensor layouts, and changing interfaces. Techniques include predefined patterns that tell Core AI about a concept (like **in-place KV-cache updates** in LLMs) and using **static tensor shapes**, **channels-first** layouts, and convolutional op patterns to leverage native primitives. The speaker splits SAM3 into three independent functions—image_encode, text_encode, detect—applies 4-bit palettization (**KMeansPalettizer**) to the two encoders while leaving the detector uncompressed, and shrinks the image from 1008 to 336 for iPhone; swapping the prompt re-runs only the text encoder and detector, making the second inference 76% faster, with rigorous module- and model-level testing emphasized.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Wraps up with what you can do today: convert PyTorch models with Core AI's Python libraries, optimize with **coreai-opt**, use the **Core AI Debugger** when you need to see inside the model, build on the examples in **coreai-models**, and plug **Core AI Skills** into your favorite AI agent to leverage the new framework like an expert.

title: Integrate on-device AI models into your app using Core AI
gloss: 用 Core AI 把裝置端 AI 模型整合進你的 App
takeaway: 用 Core AI 取得並執行一系列為 Apple silicon 最佳化的開源模型（如 Qwen、Mistral、SAM3），透過 FoundationModels 介面在裝置端推論，並用 AOT 編譯加速部署。
chapters: Getting models with the Core AI models repository
Load and run SAM3 image segmentation
Load a language model and create a session
Compile a Core AI model ahead of time

points.text: **Core AI** 提供一系列為 **Apple silicon 最佳化的開源模型**（Qwen、Mistral、SAM3 等），可透過 Core AI models repository 取得。
影像分割用 `CoreAIImageSegmenter`（SAM3）以文字 prompt 取得遮罩；語言模型用 `CoreAILanguageModel` 建立 `LanguageModelSession`。
Core AI 語言模型可直接搭配 **`FoundationModels` 的 `@Generable`** 產生結構化輸出，重用既有的 Foundation Models API。
可用 **AOT（ahead-of-time）編譯**（`xcrun coreai-build compile`）預先編譯模型以降低特化延遲，並支援跨平台部署。

audience: **想在裝置端整合開源大型語言模型或視覺模型、又希望沿用 Foundation Models 開發體驗的開發者**。
gloss_en: Integrate on-device AI models with Core AI
takeaway_en: Use Core AI to obtain and run a collection of open-source models optimized for Apple silicon (such as Qwen, Mistral, SAM3), inferring on-device through the FoundationModels interface and accelerating deployment with AOT compilation.

points_en.text: **Core AI** offers a collection of **open-source models optimized for Apple silicon** (Qwen, Mistral, SAM3, and more), available through the Core AI models repository.
For image segmentation, use `CoreAIImageSegmenter` (SAM3) to obtain masks from a text prompt; for language models, use `CoreAILanguageModel` to create a `LanguageModelSession`.
Core AI language models work directly with **`FoundationModels`' `@Generable`** to produce structured output, reusing your existing Foundation Models API.
Use **AOT (ahead-of-time) compilation** (`xcrun coreai-build compile`) to precompile models and reduce specialization latency, with support for cross-platform deployment.

audience_en: **Developers who want to integrate open-source large language or vision models on-device while keeping the Foundation Models development experience**.
summary: Core AI 團隊的 Carina 示範如何用 **Core AI** 把熱門開源模型（Qwen、Mistral、SAM3 等）整合進 app，並完全在裝置上執行——資料不離開裝置、無伺服器、無 token 費用、無雲端延遲。貫穿全場的範例是一個相機式語言學習 app：使用者對著物件拍照並輸入提示，app 用視覺模型把物件從場景裡分割出來當作字卡圖，再用語言模型生成翻譯、例句與英文釋義。

在**模型探索**上，講者把問題拆成兩個小於 10 億參數的小模型：影像分割用 **SAM 3**（vision-transformer，依提示精準分割物件），多語言生成用 **Qwen 0.6B**（支援 119 種語言、具推理能力可生成情境例句）。取得模型有兩條路：用 Core AI PyTorch extensions 與 optimization 套件自行轉換，或直接到 **Core AI Models repository** 取得已轉成 Core AI 格式（`.aimodel`）並附轉換腳本與平台變體的熱門模型。

**整合**部分，repo 還提供一個 Swift package（runtime libraries），把 SAM3 的文字編碼、mask 抽取與標註等前後處理抽象掉，讓你只需呼叫乾淨的 Swift API。語言模型則只要一行 `CoreAILanguageModel(resourcesAt:)` 載入，再用熟悉的 **`LanguageModelSession`**（與 Apple 內建模型相同的 FoundationModels API）來 `respond(to:)`，並支援串流與用 **`@Generable`** 做結構化輸出（VocabCard）。透過新的 Core AI Instruments，講者發現首次載入慢在 **specialization**（為裝置準備模型執行）。

**部署**策略強調：作為既有 app 的更新，功能要可被發現但非必要。模型約 1GB，因此改用 **Background Assets** 在使用者真的想試時才下載，並在 first-run experience 把 specialization 移出互動流程。更進一步用 **`coreai-build`** 在開發機做 **ahead-of-time（AOT）編譯**，把最耗時的 compilation 預先完成，使用者裝置上只需少量特化即可快速完成。最後示範**多平台**：同一份程式碼搬到 macOS，因記憶體與算力更充裕，可換用更大的 Qwen3 8B 變體做批次處理、生成 pinyin 與課程規劃。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: Core AI 團隊的 Carina 開場，介紹 **Core AI** 是把進階裝置端 AI 能力帶進 app 的新技術集合，特色是資料不離開裝置、無伺服器、無 token 費用、無雲端延遲。建議先看「Meet Core AI」了解設計理念。

deepdive.title: App concept: camera-based vocab learning
deepdive.body: 提出範例 app 概念：學生對著生活中的物件拍照並輸入提示，app 即時把該物件從場景中拉出並生成該語言的字卡（翻譯、例句、英文釋義），完全在裝置上執行，先以中文為起點。

deepdive.title: Model discovery
deepdive.body: 定義三項需求：內容（廚房／街道／辦公室等真實場景）、語言（架構需支援多語言）、裝置限制（小儲存與記憶體佔用）。結論是把問題拆成兩個專用小模型，各自小於 10 億參數，以兼顧品質、體積與可獨立升級。

deepdive.title: Getting models with the Core AI models repository
deepdive.body: 說明取得模型的兩條路：用 **Core AI PyTorch extensions** 自行從 PyTorch 轉換並可搭配 optimization 壓縮，或直接到 **Core AI Models repository** 取用已轉成 Core AI 格式的熱門模型（含 SAM 3 與 Qwen 家族）及其 export recipe。

deepdive.title: Integration
deepdive.body: 在 Xcode 中檢視匯出的 `.aimodel`（SAM3 為 623MB，targets iOS/macOS 27.0），其 Functions tab 顯示 imageEncode、detect 等以 tensor 為介面的函式，凸顯直接使用需大量前後處理，引出 repo 提供的 runtime libraries。

deepdive.title: Writing the Swift integration code
deepdive.body: 示範把 coreai-models 加為 Swift Package 並選用 CoreAILM 與 CoreAISegmentation，runtime library 把文字編碼、mask 抽取與標註抽象掉，讓你只呼叫乾淨的 Swift API。

deepdive.title: Load and run SAM3 image segmentation
deepdive.body: 用 `CoreAIImageSegmenter` 從磁碟載入 SAM 3，呼叫 `segment(image:prompt:)` 以文字提示（如 "flower"）做分割，再取出最佳 segmentation mask 當作字卡圖。

deepdive.title: Load a language model and create a session
deepdive.body: 語言模型只要一行 `CoreAILanguageModel(resourcesAt:)` 即完成資產載入、引擎建立與 tokenizer 設定。注意這裡 import 的是 **FoundationModels**，並用同一個 `LanguageModelSession` API，只是換成自己的模型。

deepdive.title: Generate structured output with @Generable
deepdive.body: 用 **`@Generable`** macro 描述 VocabCard 的欄位（word、translation、example sentence），以 guided generation 讓模型可靠地填入型別化欄位，而非自由形式文字。

deepdive.title: Diagnosing model specialization latency
deepdive.body: 示範首次拍照時轉圈很久，用新的 **Core AI Instruments** 追蹤發現有 model load 事件與龐大的 **specialization** 子事件。specialization 是為裝置準備模型執行的過程，大型模型首次會耗時，之後從快取載入則很快。

deepdive.title: Deployment
deepdive.body: 規劃部署策略：作為既有 app 的更新，功能要可被發現但非必要。發現模型若直接打包會讓下載多出超過 1GB，因此用 first-run experience 介紹功能，並用按鈕在使用者想試時才觸發下載。

deepdive.title: Ahead-of-time (AOT) compilation
deepdive.body: 說明 specialization 含 compilation 與產生 device 專屬可執行 artifact 兩步，compilation 最耗時。Core AI toolchain 可在開發機**預先**做 compilation，產生已編譯模型，使用者裝置上只剩少量特化工作。

deepdive.title: Compile a Core AI model ahead of time
deepdive.body: 用 **`coreai-build compile`** 指令把模型針對特定裝置架構預先編譯，並為每個編譯版本建立 background asset；app 端加少量程式碼偵測裝置架構並下載對應 asset，使準備時間大幅縮短。詳見 developer.apple.com 的相關文章。

deepdive.title: iOS demo
deepdive.body: 在 iOS 上實機示範：對著旅途收集的石頭、朋友贈送的木片、妹妹的向日葵拍照，模型生成例句並存入收藏；因 AOT 編譯，準備步驟大幅縮短，後續推論用快取 asset 達到無縫體驗。

deepdive.title: Multiplatform
deepdive.body: 把功能帶到 macOS：重用同一份程式碼，加上批次處理層一次處理整個資料夾的照片；因記憶體與算力更充裕，可換用更大的 **Qwen3 8B** 變體取得更好推理與更高品質輸出，甚至生成 pinyin 並把整類詞彙排成由淺入深的課程。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 總結 Core AI 讓你打造多平台、資料不離開裝置、無伺服器、無 token 費用、無雲端延遲的 app 體驗，並表示模型與工具都已就緒，鼓勵動手在裝置上打造強大且私密的智慧功能。

summary_en: Carina from the Core AI team shows how to integrate popular open-source models (Qwen, Mistral, SAM3, and more) into an app with **Core AI**, running entirely on device — data never leaves the device, with no server, no per-token cost, and no cloud latency. The running example is a camera-based language-learning app: the user points the camera at an object and types a prompt, a vision model segments the object out of the scene for the card graphic, and a language model generates the translation, example sentence, and English meaning.

For **model discovery**, the problem is split into two sub-billion-parameter models: **SAM 3** (a vision transformer) for promptable image segmentation, and **Qwen 0.6B** for multilingual generation (119 languages, with reasoning for contextual examples). There are two paths to get models: convert them yourself with the Core AI PyTorch extensions and optimization packages, or grab them ready-made from the **Core AI Models repository** in Core AI format (`.aimodel`) with conversion recipes and optional platform variants.

For **integration**, the repo also ships a Swift package of runtime libraries that abstract away SAM3's text encoding, mask extraction, and labeling, so you just call a clean Swift API. The language model loads in one line — `CoreAILanguageModel(resourcesAt:)` — then you use the familiar **`LanguageModelSession`** (the same FoundationModels API as Apple's built-in model) to `respond(to:)`, with streaming and structured output via **`@Generable`** (a VocabCard). Using the new Core AI Instruments, the presenter finds the slow first load is **specialization** (preparing the model to run on the device).

The **deployment** strategy stresses making the feature discoverable but not required as an app update. Since the models add over 1GB, it uses **Background Assets** to download only when the user opts in, and a first-run experience to move specialization out of the interactive flow. Going further, **`coreai-build`** does **ahead-of-time (AOT) compilation** on the dev machine so the most expensive compilation is done up front, leaving only light specialization on-device. Finally, **multiplatform**: the same code runs on macOS, where more memory and compute allow a larger Qwen3 8B variant for batch processing, pinyin generation, and curriculum planning.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Carina from the Core AI team opens, introducing **Core AI** as a new set of technologies for advanced on-device AI in apps, where data never leaves the device, with no server, no per-token cost, and no cloud latency. Recommends watching 'Meet Core AI' for the design philosophy.

deepdive_en.title: App concept: camera-based vocab learning
deepdive_en.body: Pitches the example app: a student photographs a real-world object and types a prompt, and the app pulls that object out of the scene and generates a vocab card (translation, example, English meaning) entirely on device, starting with Mandarin Chinese.

deepdive_en.title: Model discovery
deepdive_en.body: Defines three requirements: content (real-world scenes like kitchens, streets, offices), languages (architecture supporting multiple languages), and device constraints (small storage and memory footprint). The conclusion is to decompose into two task-specific sub-billion-parameter models for quality, size, and independent upgrades.

deepdive_en.title: Getting models with the Core AI models repository
deepdive_en.body: Two paths to obtain models: convert from PyTorch with the **Core AI PyTorch extensions** (optionally compressed via the optimization package), or pull ready-converted popular models (SAM 3, Qwen family) and their export recipes from the **Core AI Models repository**.

deepdive_en.title: Integration
deepdive_en.body: Inspects the exported `.aimodel` in Xcode (SAM3 is 623MB, targets iOS/macOS 27.0); its Functions tab shows tensor-interface functions like imageEncode and detect, highlighting the heavy pre/post-processing direct use would require — motivating the repo's runtime libraries.

deepdive_en.title: Writing the Swift integration code
deepdive_en.body: Adds coreai-models as a Swift Package and selects CoreAILM and CoreAISegmentation; the runtime libraries abstract text encoding, mask extraction, and labeling so you just call a clean Swift API.

deepdive_en.title: Load and run SAM3 image segmentation
deepdive_en.body: Uses `CoreAIImageSegmenter` to load SAM 3 from disk, calls `segment(image:prompt:)` with a text prompt (e.g. "flower"), and extracts the best segmentation mask as the card graphic.

deepdive_en.title: Load a language model and create a session
deepdive_en.body: The language model loads in one line — `CoreAILanguageModel(resourcesAt:)` — handling asset loading, engine creation, and tokenizer setup. Note the import is **FoundationModels**, using the same `LanguageModelSession` API, just with your own model.

deepdive_en.title: Generate structured output with @Generable
deepdive_en.body: Uses the **`@Generable`** macro to describe a VocabCard's fields (word, translation, example sentence), so guided generation reliably fills typed fields instead of producing free-form text.

deepdive_en.title: Diagnosing model specialization latency
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates a long spinner on first photo; the new **Core AI Instruments** trace reveals a model load event with a large **specialization** sub-event. Specialization prepares a model to run on device, is slow the first time for large models, but fast from cache afterward.

deepdive_en.title: Deployment
deepdive_en.body: Plans the deployment strategy: as an app update, the feature should be discoverable but not required. Bundling the models would add over 1GB, so a first-run experience introduces the feature and a button triggers the download only if the user wants to try it.

deepdive_en.title: Ahead-of-time (AOT) compilation
deepdive_en.body: Explains specialization has two steps — compilation and generating device-specific executable artifacts — with compilation being the most expensive. The Core AI toolchain can do compilation **ahead of time** on the dev machine, leaving only light specialization on the user's device.

deepdive_en.title: Compile a Core AI model ahead of time
deepdive_en.body: Uses the **`coreai-build compile`** command to pre-compile the model for specific device architectures and creates a background asset per compiled model; a little app code detects the device architecture and requests the right asset, sharply cutting preparation time. See the article on developer.apple.com.

deepdive_en.title: iOS demo
deepdive_en.body: Live iOS demo: photographs travel rocks, a friend's piece of wood, and a sister's sunflower; the model produces example usage saved to the collection. Thanks to AOT compilation the preparation step is much shorter, and later inferences use the cached asset for a seamless experience.

deepdive_en.title: Multiplatform
deepdive_en.body: Brings the feature to macOS: reuses the same code, adds a batch-processing layer to handle a whole folder of photos at once, and — with more memory and compute — steps up to a larger **Qwen3 8B** variant for better reasoning, higher-quality output, pinyin generation, and sequencing a whole word category into a structured curriculum.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Wraps up: Core AI enables a multiplatform app experience where user data never leaves the device, with no server, no per-token cost, and no cloud latency. The models and tools are ready — go build powerful, private on-device intelligence.

title: Explore numerical computing in Swift with MLX
gloss: 用 MLX 探索 Swift 的數值計算
takeaway: **MLX Swift** 把 NumPy 風格的陣列運算原生帶進 Swift，消除機器學習開發的跨語言摩擦並善用 Apple 晶片。
chapters: MLX Swift and the Apple ecosystem
The full MLX toolkit and ecosystem

points.text: **MLX Swift** 提供 NumPy 風格的 `MLXArray` 與向量化運算，讓數值計算原生寫在 Swift 裡。
以 Mandelbrot 為例，展示從 scalar 逐點迴圈改寫成**陣列式（array）**運算的巨大簡化與加速。
用 `conv2d` 做 Jacobi 迭代解熱傳導，再以 **SOR（Successive Over-Relaxation）** 加速收斂。
透過 **自動微分（`grad`）** 進行曲線擬合，以梯度下降更新參數。
MLX 採**延遲求值**，需以 `eval()` 強制計算，並串接完整的 MLX 工具鏈與生態系。

audience: **想在 Swift 中做數值計算或機器學習**、需善用 Apple 晶片的開發者與研究者。
gloss_en: Explore numerical computing in Swift with MLX
takeaway_en: **MLX Swift** brings NumPy-style array computing natively to Swift, eliminating cross-language friction in machine learning development and making full use of Apple silicon.

points_en.text: **MLX Swift** provides a NumPy-style `MLXArray` and vectorized operations, letting you write numerical computing natively in Swift.
Using Mandelbrot as an example, shows the dramatic simplification and speedup of rewriting a scalar point-by-point loop into **array** operations.
Solve heat conduction with Jacobi iteration using `conv2d`, then accelerate convergence with **SOR (Successive Over-Relaxation)**.
Perform curve fitting via **automatic differentiation (`grad`)**, updating parameters with gradient descent.
MLX uses **lazy evaluation**, requiring `eval()` to force computation, and connects to the full MLX toolchain and ecosystem.

audience_en: Developers and researchers who want to **do numerical computing or machine learning in Swift** while making full use of Apple silicon.
summary: David Koski 介紹 **MLX Swift**：把 NumPy 風格的數值計算原生帶進 Swift，消除跨語言摩擦。數值計算（科學計算）用於化學、物理、金融模擬、音訊與訊號處理、渲染與光線追蹤，乃至大規模梯度下降所支撐的機器學習訓練。Apple 平台已有豐富生態（Accelerate、BNNS、Metal Performance Shaders、Swift Numerics），而當你的主要目標是「寫出貼近數學、又顧及效能」的程式碼時，MLX Swift 是理想選擇。

MLX Swift 以 **n 維陣列**為核心抽象，API 與 NumPy 高度相似，多數 NumPy 程式碼只需少量改動即可轉換。關鍵特性是 **lazy evaluation**：對 array 的運算建立 compute graph，直到呼叫 `eval` 或讀值才執行。這也使得兩件事成為可能——**自動 GPU 執行**與 **automatic differentiation（`grad`）**。整個 MLX 生態皆為 MIT 授權的開源專案。

講者以三個範例展示「把數學翻成程式碼」的便利：**Mandelbrot 集合**——純 Swift 需逐 pixel 在 CPU 上迴圈，MLX Swift 則在整個複數網格上一次套用 `z = z*z + c`，預設用 GPU，可快上約 10 倍且程式更短；**熱分布穩態**——Jacobi iteration 以 `conv2d` 套用 stencil、用 `which` 處理邊界條件，再用 **Successive Over-Relaxation（SOR）** 搭配 red/black checkerboard 的就地更新與最佳 omega 加速收斂；**曲線擬合**——定義 loss（MSE）後用 `grad` 取得自動微分梯度，跑梯度下降，毋須手寫導數。

最後講者說明 MLX 涵蓋完整數值計算工具箱（線性代數、FFT、N 維卷積、reductions、scans、indexing、亂數等），並有健全生態：核心 `mlx-swift`、語言模型的 `mlx-swift-lm`、範例的 `mlx-swift-examples`，皆可用 Swift Package Manager 安裝。MLX 同時有 Swift、Python、C++、C 四種前端，共享相同概念與 lazy evaluation 模型，因此可在 Python 原型、在 Swift 出貨。鼓勵大家試用並貢獻。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: David Koski 開場定義**數值計算**（亦稱數值分析／科學計算）：用演算法解難以符號或手算的數學問題，應用涵蓋化學、物理、金融模擬、音訊訊號處理、渲染與光線追蹤，以及作為機器學習訓練基礎的大規模梯度下降。

deepdive.title: MLX Swift and the Apple ecosystem
deepdive.body: 盤點 Apple 既有數值計算生態：**Accelerate**（CPU 向量原語）、**BNNS**（神經網路積木層）、**Metal Performance Shaders**（GPU kernel）、**Swift Numerics**（Complex 與泛型數值協定）。當主要目標是寫貼近數學又顧效能的程式碼時，MLX Swift 最合適。

deepdive.title: MLX Swift
deepdive.body: 以 power iteration 為例展示 MLX Swift：`.T` 取轉置、`matmul` 做矩陣乘、`norm` 取 L2 norm，程式讀起來就像數學。並點出關鍵的 **lazy evaluation**——運算建立 compute graph，呼叫 `eval` 或讀值才執行；迴圈內每步 `eval` 讓 graph 保持精簡。

deepdive.title: Mandelbrot
deepdive.body: 介紹 **Mandelbrot 集合**作為陣列計算的絕佳範例：對複數平面每個點 c 迭代 `z = z² + c`，若 magnitude 不超過 2 則屬於集合（塗黑），否則依逃逸速度上色。是把函式套用到大型網格的典型場景。

deepdive.title: Mandelbrot set in plain Swift (scalar)
deepdive.body: 純 Swift scalar 版：逐 pixel 迴圈跑 Mandelbrot 迭代並檢查發散，雖然 idiomatic，但充斥與問題無關的 bookkeeping，且只在 CPU 上一次處理一個點。

deepdive.title: Mandelbrot set in MLX Swift (array)
deepdive.body: MLX Swift 版：先建好複數網格 c，迴圈只有兩行——`z = z * z + c` 一次套用到所有點、再計數仍 bounded 的迭代次數。是數學的直接翻譯，預設用 GPU，程式更小更簡單。

deepdive.title: Heat distribution
deepdive.body: 下個範例是房間熱分布穩態：把溫度建模成 2D 網格，每次迭代用 stencil 平均鄰居值，反覆直到穩態。因為更新只看小鄰域且每點配方相同，這正是一個 convolution。

deepdive.title: Jacobi iteration with conv2d
deepdive.body: 示範 **Jacobi iteration** 的 MLX Swift 核心：kernel 把四鄰各 0.25、中心與角為 0 的 stencil 寫出來；迴圈兩行——`conv2d` 一次套用 stencil，`which` 以 elementwise ternary 套用邊界條件（熱源／牆保持固定值，其餘取卷積新值）。

deepdive.title: Faster convergence with SOR
deepdive.body: 說明 Jacobi 計算快但收斂慢（約需 N² 次迭代）。引出 **Successive Over-Relaxation（SOR）**：用相同 kernel 但加上 omega 參數，朝變化方向過衝以更快到達，過衝會在迭代中修正；最佳 omega 可使收斂降到 N 次。

deepdive.title: Successive Over-Relaxation (SOR)
deepdive.body: SOR 程式：先依網格大小算最佳 omega，再用 red/black **checkerboard** masks 交替更新——MLX 通常產生新陣列而非就地更新，但棋盤式交替處理可達到就地效果（黑格更新時其紅格鄰居已是新值）。視覺上 SOR 以漣漪狀快速填滿，需放慢 100 倍才看得清。

deepdive.title: Curve fitting
deepdive.body: 第三個範例翻轉方向：已有資料點（輸出），要找出產生它們的參數。先決定函式結構（此處用二次多項式得拋物線），目標是最小化 loss——輸出與實際資料差的均方。這正是訓練每個 ML 模型的核心概念縮影。

deepdive.title: Curve fitting with automatic differentiation
deepdive.body: 用 MLX Swift 的關鍵 function transformation **`grad`** 做 automatic differentiation：定義 f 與 loss（MSE），把 loss 轉成回傳對參數的精確梯度的函式，毋須手寫導數；最佳化迴圈每步算梯度、走一小步、`eval` 沖掉 compute graph。若需更多可用 SGD、Adam、RMSprop 等。

deepdive.title: The full MLX toolkit and ecosystem
deepdive.body: MLX 涵蓋完整數值計算工具箱：線性代數、FFT、N 維卷積、reductions、scans、indexing、亂數等。生態包含 `mlx-swift`、`mlx-swift-lm`、`mlx-swift-examples`（本場範例會放這），皆可用 SwiftPM 幾行安裝。MLX 亦有 Swift／Python／C++／C 四前端共享相同概念，可 Python 原型、Swift 出貨。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 鼓勵大家試用 `mlx-swift` 與 `mlx-swift-examples`（含 LLM 整合、stable diffusion、訓練與微調等範例），並參與貢獻——修開放 issue 或新增範例程式。

summary_en: David Koski introduces **MLX Swift**: bringing NumPy-style numerical computing natively to Swift to eliminate cross-language friction. Numerical (scientific) computing powers simulations in chemistry, physics, and finance, audio and signal processing, rendering and ray tracing, and the large-scale gradient descent behind machine-learning training. Apple platforms already have a rich ecosystem (Accelerate, BNNS, Metal Performance Shaders, Swift Numerics), and MLX Swift is the right reach when your primary goal is writing math-like code with an eye on performance.

MLX Swift uses **n-dimensional arrays** as its central abstraction, with an API very close to NumPy — most NumPy code translates with minimal changes. The key feature is **lazy evaluation**: operations build a compute graph and nothing runs until you call `eval` or read a value. This is what makes **automatic GPU execution** and **automatic differentiation (`grad`)** possible. The whole MLX ecosystem is open source under an MIT license.
