Three examples show how easily math becomes code: **the Mandelbrot set** — plain Swift loops pixel-by-pixel on the CPU, while MLX Swift applies `z = z*z + c` across the whole complex grid at once, defaults to GPU, and can run ~10x faster in less code; **heat-distribution steady state** — Jacobi iteration applies a stencil via `conv2d` with `which` for boundary conditions, then **Successive Over-Relaxation (SOR)** uses a red/black checkerboard for in-place updates and an optimal omega to converge faster; and **curve fitting** — define a loss (MSE), get gradients via automatic differentiation with `grad`, and run gradient descent with no hand-written derivatives.

Finally, MLX covers the full numerical-computing toolkit (linear algebra, FFTs, N-dimensional convolutions, reductions, scans, indexing, random numbers, and more) with a healthy ecosystem: core `mlx-swift`, `mlx-swift-lm` for language models, and `mlx-swift-examples`, all installable via Swift Package Manager. MLX also has four front-ends — Swift, Python, C++, and C — sharing the same concepts and lazy-evaluation model, so you can prototype in Python and ship in Swift. The talk encourages trying it and contributing.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: David Koski opens by defining **numerical computing** (numerical analysis / scientific computing): algorithms to solve math problems impractical to do symbolically or by hand, spanning chemistry, physics, finance simulations, audio/signal processing, rendering and ray tracing, and the large-scale gradient descent underpinning ML training.

deepdive_en.title: MLX Swift and the Apple ecosystem
deepdive_en.body: Surveys Apple's existing numerical ecosystem: **Accelerate** (CPU vector primitives), **BNNS** (neural-network building blocks), **Metal Performance Shaders** (GPU kernels), and **Swift Numerics** (Complex and generic numeric protocols). MLX Swift fits best when the primary goal is math-like code with performance in mind.

deepdive_en.title: MLX Swift
deepdive_en.body: Walks through MLX Swift via power iteration: `.T` for transpose, `matmul` for matrix multiply, `norm` for the L2 norm — the code reads like the math. Highlights the key **lazy evaluation**: operations build a compute graph and run only on `eval` or read; calling `eval` each loop iteration keeps the graph small.

deepdive_en.title: Mandelbrot
deepdive_en.body: Introduces the **Mandelbrot set** as an ideal array-computing showcase: for each point c, iterate `z = z² + c`; if the magnitude never exceeds 2 it's in the set (black), otherwise colored by escape speed — a classic apply-a-function-over-a-grid case.

deepdive_en.title: Mandelbrot set in plain Swift (scalar)
deepdive_en.body: Plain scalar Swift loops over every pixel running the Mandelbrot iteration and checking divergence; idiomatic, but full of problem-irrelevant bookkeeping and processing one point at a time on the CPU.

deepdive_en.title: Mandelbrot set in MLX Swift (array)
deepdive_en.body: The MLX Swift version sets up a complex grid c, then the loop is two lines — `z = z * z + c` applied to all points at once, then counting bounded iterations. A direct translation of the math, defaulting to the GPU, in smaller, simpler code.

deepdive_en.title: Heat distribution
deepdive_en.body: The next example is steady-state heat in a room: model temperature as a 2D grid, each iteration averaging neighbors with a stencil, repeated until steady state. Because the update is a small same-recipe neighborhood, it's exactly a convolution.

deepdive_en.title: Jacobi iteration with conv2d
deepdive_en.body: Shows the **Jacobi iteration** core in MLX Swift: the kernel writes out the stencil (0.25 on each of four neighbors, zeros on center/corners); the loop is two lines — `conv2d` applies the stencil at once, and `which` (an elementwise ternary) applies boundary conditions (keep fixed value at sources/walls, take the convolution elsewhere).

deepdive_en.title: Faster convergence with SOR
deepdive_en.body: Notes Jacobi is fast to compute but slow to converge (~N² iterations). Introduces **Successive Over-Relaxation (SOR)**: same kernel plus an omega parameter that overshoots toward the change to get there faster, with the overshoot correcting over iterations; an optimal omega cuts convergence to N iterations.

deepdive_en.title: Successive Over-Relaxation (SOR)
deepdive_en.body: SOR code: compute the optimal omega from grid size, then use red/black **checkerboard** masks to update alternating cells — MLX usually produces new arrays, but the checkerboard alternation achieves the in-place effect (black cells update with already-fresh red neighbors). Visually SOR fills with a striking ripple, slowed 100x to be visible.

deepdive_en.title: Curve fitting
deepdive_en.body: The third example flips direction: you have data points (outputs) and want the parameters that produce them. Choose the function structure (here a quadratic, giving a parabola), and minimize the loss — the mean squared difference between output and data. This is the core idea behind training every ML model, in miniature.

deepdive_en.title: Curve fitting with automatic differentiation
deepdive_en.body: Uses MLX Swift's key function transformation **`grad`** for automatic differentiation: define f and the loss (MSE), transform loss into a function returning the exact gradient w.r.t. parameters — no hand-written derivatives; the optimization loop evaluates the gradient, takes a small step, and `eval`s to flush the graph. For more, MLX has SGD, Adam, RMSprop, and others.

deepdive_en.title: The full MLX toolkit and ecosystem
deepdive_en.body: MLX covers the full numerical toolkit: linear algebra, FFTs, N-dimensional convolutions, reductions, scans, indexing, random numbers, and more. The ecosystem includes `mlx-swift`, `mlx-swift-lm`, and `mlx-swift-examples` (where this session's examples will live), all installable in a few lines via SwiftPM. MLX also has Swift/Python/C++/C front-ends sharing the same concepts, so you can prototype in Python and ship in Swift.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Encourages trying `mlx-swift` and `mlx-swift-examples` (with examples for LLM integration, stable diffusion, training and fine-tuning) and contributing — fixing open issues or adding new example programs.

title: Optimize custom machine learning operations with Metal tensors
gloss: 用 Metal tensors 最佳化自訂機器學習運算
takeaway: 運用 Metal Tensor API 與 MPP Tensor Ops，以量化張量與 cooperative tensor 打造高效能的自訂 ML 運算核心。
chapters: Declare a multi-plane tensor with scale factors
MSL type aliases for an MXFP8 tensor handle
Declare an inline MXFP8 tensor on the stack
Slice tensors and run a quantized matmul
Reuse cooperative tensor as matmul input
Integrating custom ops into Core AI

points.text: 介紹 Apple 的 ML 軟體堆疊，並說明 **Metal Tensor API** 與 MPP Tensor Ops 的定位。
用 **MTLTensor** 搭配量化資料型別（如 MetalFloat8E4M3）管理量化資料。
透過 **auxiliary plane** 宣告帶 scale factors 的 multi-plane tensor，支援 MXFP8 區塊量化。
以 **matmul2d** 執行量化矩陣乘法，TensorOps 會自動處理反量化。
用 **cooperative tensor** 與 map_iterator 打造 SoftMax 等進階運算，並可整合進 Core AI。

audience: 撰寫 **自訂 Metal ML 核心或高效能推論運算** 的進階圖形與機器學習開發者。
gloss_en: Optimize custom machine learning operations with Metal tensors
takeaway_en: Use the Metal Tensor API and MPP Tensor Ops with quantized tensors and cooperative tensors to build high-performance custom ML compute kernels.

points_en.text: Introduces Apple's ML software stack and explains where the **Metal Tensor API** and MPP Tensor Ops fit in.
Use **MTLTensor** with quantized data types (such as MetalFloat8E4M3) to manage quantized data.
Declare a multi-plane tensor with scale factors via an **auxiliary plane** to support MXFP8 block quantization.
Use **matmul2d** to perform quantized matrix multiplication; TensorOps handles dequantization automatically.
Use a **cooperative tensor** with map_iterator to build advanced operations like SoftMax, and integrate them into Core AI.

audience_en: Advanced graphics and machine learning developers writing **custom Metal ML kernels or high-performance inference operations**.
summary: 這場由 GPU 軟體工程師 Shiyao 主講，主題是如何用 **Metal tensors** 與 **TensorOps**（Metal Performance Primitives 的一部分）寫出高效能的自訂 ML kernel。整個 Apple ML 軟體堆疊從高階的 **Core AI**、**MLX**，到較底層的 **Metal Performance Shaders**，最終都建立在 **MPP** 與 **TensorOps** 之上。會想下探到 Metal 層的理由通常是：ML 研究進展飛快，你想實作能掛進 Core AI 的自訂運算，或正在為 MLX、llama.cpp 等框架貢獻 kernel。TensorOps 是一套 Metal Shading Language API，會自動利用各世代 Apple Silicon GPU 的硬體加速，特別是 M5 晶片中位於每個 shader core 內的 **neural accelerator**。

第一大主題是**量化資料**的最佳實務。現代模型越來越大，推論階段通常受記憶體頻寬限制，因此壓縮權重變得必要。標準做法是**量化**：把高精度權重降為低精度型別（例如 16-bit 降到 4-bit），並搭配 **scale factors** 把量化值還原回原始範圍。TensorOps 除了 16/32-bit 浮點外，現也原生支援量化型別——macOS/iOS 26 加入 4/8-bit 整數，27 再擴充到 4/8-bit 浮點與 2-bit 整數。建立量化 tensor 與一般 tensor 幾乎相同，只要在 descriptor 指定量化 `dataType`；scale 則透過 **auxiliary scale plane**（支援 FP8 E8M0 block-wise 格式）打包進同一個 `MTLTensor`。在 kernel 內用 type alias 宣告 `scales_plane` 與量化 tensor 型別後，呼叫 `slice` 切出 tile，再丟給 `matmul2d`，TensorOps 會**自動處理 dequantization**。

第二大主題是用 TensorOps 打造像 **FlashAttention** 這樣的進階自訂運算。Attention 的流程是先做 Q×K 矩陣相乘、對中間矩陣的列做 SoftMax、再乘上 V；FlashAttention 把這些融合成單一 kernel。實作上要用 **execution_simdgroup** scope 讓每個 simd group 擁有完整的列，如此計算 SoftMax 時不必跨 simd group 交換資料。中間結果存進 **cooperative tensor**（分散在參與執行緒的私有 register），避免寫回記憶體；列縮減用 `reduce_rows`，再以 `map_iterator` 對應兩個不同形狀 cooperative tensor 的元素來算 SoftMax。macOS 27 起 cooperative tensor 可直接當作下一個 matmul 的輸入（先用 `is_compatible_as_left_input` 檢查相容性，不相容才透過 threadgroup memory 轉換）。最後示範用 Core AI 把這個自訂 FlashAttention kernel 整合進 **Sam3** 影像分割模型，完成端到端推論。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: GPU 軟體工程師 Shiyao 開場，預告本場會帶大家認識 **Metal tensors**，並學會用 **TensorOps** 寫出最佳化的自訂 ML kernel。重點放在量化資料的處理，以及打造像 FlashAttention 這類進階運算。

deepdive.title: Apple's ML software stack
deepdive.body: 說明 Apple 各層 ML 軟體堆疊：高階的 **Core AI**、**MLX** 讓你用最少程式碼部署模型，較低階的 **Metal Performance Shaders** 提供高效能 kernel，而這些全都建立在 **Metal Performance Primitives** 與 **TensorOps** 之上。會想下探 Metal 層，通常是為了實作能掛進高階框架的自訂運算、為 MLX/llama.cpp 等框架貢獻 kernel，或開發 Metal 應用。TensorOps 會自動利用各世代 GPU 的硬體加速，特別是 M5 每個 shader core 內專為密集 compute-bound 工作（如 LLM 的 prefill 階段）設計的 **neural accelerator**。

deepdive.title: Managing quantized data
deepdive.body: 點出現代模型越來越大、推論受**記憶體頻寬**限制，因此壓縮權重變得必要。標準做法是**量化**：把高精度權重（如 16-bit half）降為低精度型別（如 4-bit），再配上 **scale factors** 把量化值還原回原始範圍。TensorOps 已原生支援多種量化型別——26 版加入 4/8-bit 整數，27 版再擴充 4/8-bit 浮點與 2-bit 整數。

deepdive.title: Create a quantized MTLTensor
deepdive.body: 建立量化 tensor 與一般 tensor 幾乎相同：照常填好 descriptor 屬性，只要把 `dataType` 設成量化型別（例如 `MTLTensorDataTypeMetalFloat8E4M3`），再呼叫 `newTensorWithDescriptor` 即可。這只是處理量化的**元素資料**部分，scale factors 留待後續說明。

deepdive.title: Multi-plane tensors
deepdive.body: macOS/iOS 27 起，單一 `MTLTensor` 物件可用額外的 **scale plane** 把 scales 與量化資料一起表示。此 plane 支援熱門的 **FP8 E8M0** block-wise scale factor 格式，scale plane 的每個元素對應 data plane 中的一個 block。量化資料、scales 與 metadata 全部打包進同一個 tensor 物件。

deepdive.title: Declare a multi-plane tensor with scale factors
deepdive.body: 示範宣告 scale plane 的步驟：先建立 `MTLTensorAuxiliaryPlaneDescriptor`，填入 `dataType`（如 `MetalFloat8UE8M0`）與 `blockFactors`（例如 32×1）；再建立 auxiliary plane map 指定此 plane 為 **scales**；最後把 map 透過 `auxiliaryPlanes` 掛到原本的 tensor descriptor 上。

deepdive.title: Quantized matrix multiplication
deepdive.body: 矩陣乘法是 ML 工作的核心運算，LLM 推論時會做數百萬次。基本做法是把輸入矩陣切成較小的 **tile**，再用 TensorOps 做 tile-wise 相乘，以最大化平行度並讓資料留在 cache。配合量化能進一步減少記憶體流量、把更大的模型塞進記憶體。

deepdive.title: MSL type aliases for an MXFP8 tensor handle
deepdive.body: 在 kernel 內綁定 tensor 前，先用 **type alias** 宣告型別會更清楚。這裡宣告一個 `fp8_e8m0` 資料型別、block size 32×1 的 `scales_plane`（即每 32 個元素共用一個 scale），再宣告指定 FP8 資料型別並帶上該 scales_plane 的完整 tensor 型別，最後綁定到 buffer binding point。

deepdive.title: Declare an inline MXFP8 tensor on the stack
deepdive.body: 如果不想在 host 端建立完整的 `MTLTensor`，可以直接在 shader 的 **stack** 上建立暫時 tensor。語法幾乎一樣，只要把 tag 從 `tensor_handle` 換成 **`tensor_inline`**，再把 buffer 指標與其他 metadata 傳給 tensor 建構子即可。

deepdive.title: Slice tensors and run a quantized matmul
deepdive.body: 把問題分給多個 threadgroup 以增加平行度：用 threadgroup ID 對輸入與輸出 tensor 呼叫 `slice`，**data 與 scales plane 會依 block size 同步被切**。接著設定 `matmul2d_descriptor`（tile 尺寸等參數）、建立指定 simdgroup 數的 `matmul2d` op，再把量化 tensor 傳入，TensorOps 會**自動完成 dequantization**。

deepdive.title: Building advanced ops
deepdive.body: 進階主題：用 TensorOps 打造更複雜的完整自訂運算。以 **Attention** 為例——它是每個 transformer（含 LLM）的核心：先把 Q、K 兩矩陣相乘，再對中間矩陣的列做 **SoftMax** reduction，最後乘上第三個矩陣 V。熱門的 **FlashAttention** 演算法把這些步驟融合進單一 kernel。

deepdive.title: Set up simdgroup-scoped QxK multiplication
deepdive.body: 要實作 FlashAttention，先設定自訂的 simd group 對應，讓**每個 simd group 擁有中間矩陣的完整列**，如此算 SoftMax 時無需跨 simd group 交換資料。透過 **`execution_simdgroup`** scope 讓每個 simd group 獨立平行做矩陣乘法，用 simd group ID 切出 Q/K/V 的 tile，並用 **cooperative tensor** 儲存 Q×K 的結果，以便不寫回記憶體就接到下一步。

deepdive.title: Compute row-wise reduction for SoftMax
deepdive.body: 計算 SoftMax 需要對 cooperative tensor 做幾次 reduction。TensorOps 提供 **`reduce_rows`** 函式，讓執行緒彼此交換資料來算出每一列的最大值，結果回傳到另一個 cooperative tensor。這裡用 `max` 的 reduction operation，初始值設為負無限大。

deepdive.title: Compute element-wise SoftMax with map_iterator
deepdive.body: 由於 Q×K tile 與 row-max 兩個 cooperative tensor 形狀不同，TensorOps 提供 **`map_iterator`** 來對應：給定指向 2D tensor 元素的 iterator，回傳指向對應 reduction 目的元素的 iterator。做法是用 iterator 走訪 2D cooperative tensor，對每個元素 `map_iterator` 找到其 row max，再解參考相減並取 `exp`，把 SoftMax 結果寫回 cooperative tensor。

deepdive.title: Reuse cooperative tensor as matmul input
deepdive.body: 現在要把這個 cooperative tensor 乘上 V。macOS 26 時必須先存到 threadgroup memory，但 27 起可**直接把 cooperative tensor 當作 matmul 的輸入**：呼叫 `get_left_input_cooperative_tensor`。要注意並非每個 cooperative tensor 都能重用——layout 可能因資料型別等因素而異，所以要先用 **`is_compatible_as_left_input`** 檢查；若不相容，就透過 threadgroup memory 存取以轉成正確 layout，但無論哪種路徑，`op.run` 的呼叫都一樣。

deepdive.title: Integrating custom ops into Core AI
deepdive.body: **Core AI** 提供工具讓 Python 開發者把 PyTorch 模型轉成 Core AI 模型，並支援自訂 Metal kernel。講者依「Deep Dive into Core AI Model authoring and Optimization」的步驟，把自訂 FlashAttention kernel 整合進 **Sam3** 影像分割模型：在 Python 中以字串定義 kernel body 並註冊 `TorchMetalKernel`，替換掉預設的 huggingface attention，再從 PyTorch 匯出成最佳化的 Core AI 資產。最後示範以圖片加文字 prompt（標出所有汽車像素）做 promptable 概念分割，結果正確把車子標成藍色，證明 kernel 已完整整合。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 總結今天涵蓋的工具：從量化資料型別，到 cooperative tensors、reductions 等進階 TensorOps 功能，再到與 Core AI 的整合。建議進一步查閱 **Metal Performance Primitives** 文件與 programming guide，並下載 TensorOps 範例程式碼，同時參考相關的 Core AI 與 Metal 場次。

summary_en: Presented by GPU Software Engineer Shiyao, this session covers how to write high-performance custom ML kernels using **Metal tensors** and **TensorOps** (part of Metal Performance Primitives). Apple's entire ML software stack — from high-level **Core AI** and **MLX** down to **Metal Performance Shaders** — ultimately builds on **MPP** and **TensorOps**. You'd drop down to the Metal level when ML research moves fast and you want to implement custom operations that plug into Core AI, or when contributing kernels to frameworks like MLX or llama.cpp. TensorOps is a Metal Shading Language API that automatically exploits hardware acceleration across all Apple Silicon GPU generations, especially the **neural accelerator** inside each shader core of the M5 chip.

The first major topic is best practices for **quantized data**. Models keep growing and inference is typically memory-bandwidth bound, so compressing weights becomes necessary. The standard approach is **quantization** — reducing high-precision weights to lower-precision types (e.g. 16-bit down to 4-bit), paired with **scale factors** to map values back to the original range. Beyond 16/32-bit floats, TensorOps now natively supports quantized types: 4/8-bit integers in macOS/iOS 26, and 4/8-bit floats plus 2-bit integers in 27. Creating a quantized tensor is nearly identical to a regular one — just specify a quantized `dataType` in the descriptor; scales are packed into the same `MTLTensor` as an **auxiliary scale plane** (supporting the FP8 E8M0 block-wise format). In the kernel you declare type aliases for the `scales_plane` and quantized tensor, call `slice` to extract tiles, and hand them to `matmul2d`, which **handles dequantization automatically**.

The second major topic is building advanced custom operations like **FlashAttention** with TensorOps. Attention multiplies Q×K, computes SoftMax over the rows of the intermediate matrix, then multiplies by V; FlashAttention fuses all of this into a single kernel. The implementation uses the **execution_simdgroup** scope so each simd group owns complete rows, avoiding cross-simdgroup data exchange during SoftMax. Intermediate results live in a **cooperative tensor** (distributed across participating threads' private registers) to avoid writing to memory; row reductions use `reduce_rows`, and `map_iterator` maps elements between two differently shaped cooperative tensors to compute SoftMax. Since macOS 27, a cooperative tensor can feed directly into the next matmul (check with `is_compatible_as_left_input`; only fall back through threadgroup memory if incompatible). Finally, the session integrates this custom FlashAttention kernel into a **Sam3** image segmentation model via Core AI for end-to-end inference.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: GPU Software Engineer Shiyao opens by previewing an exploration of **Metal tensors** and how to write optimized custom ML kernels with **TensorOps**. The focus is on working with quantized data and building advanced operations like FlashAttention.

deepdive_en.title: Apple's ML software stack
deepdive_en.body: Lays out Apple's layered ML stack: high-level **Core AI** and **MLX** for deploying models with minimal code, lower-level **Metal Performance Shaders** for high-performance kernels, all built on **Metal Performance Primitives** and **TensorOps**. Reasons to work at the Metal level include implementing custom ops that plug into higher frameworks, contributing kernels to MLX/llama.cpp, or building a Metal app. TensorOps automatically uses hardware acceleration across GPU generations, notably the M5 **neural accelerator** in each shader core, designed for dense compute-bound work like an LLM's prefill stage.

deepdive_en.title: Managing quantized data
deepdive_en.body: Notes that models keep growing and inference is **memory-bandwidth bound**, making weight compression necessary. The standard approach is **quantization** — reducing high-precision weights (e.g. 16-bit half) to lower precision (e.g. 4-bit), paired with **scale factors** to restore the original range. TensorOps natively supports many quantized types — 4/8-bit integers added in 26, with 4/8-bit floats and 2-bit integers in 27.

deepdive_en.title: Create a quantized MTLTensor
deepdive_en.body: Creating a quantized tensor is nearly identical to a regular one: fill in descriptor properties as usual but set `dataType` to a quantized type (e.g. `MTLTensorDataTypeMetalFloat8E4M3`), then call `newTensorWithDescriptor`. This handles the quantized **element data**; scale factors are covered next.

deepdive_en.title: Multi-plane tensors
deepdive_en.body: Starting in macOS/iOS 27, a single `MTLTensor` can represent scales alongside quantized data via an additional **scale plane**. This plane supports the popular **FP8 E8M0** block-wise scale factor format, where each scale-plane element applies to a block of data-plane elements. Quantized data, scales, and metadata are all packed into one tensor object.

deepdive_en.title: Declare a multi-plane tensor with scale factors
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates declaring the scale plane: create an `MTLTensorAuxiliaryPlaneDescriptor`, set its `dataType` (e.g. `MetalFloat8UE8M0`) and `blockFactors` (e.g. 32×1); build an auxiliary plane map specifying the plane is for **scales**; then attach the map to the original tensor descriptor via `auxiliaryPlanes`.

deepdive_en.title: Quantized matrix multiplication
deepdive_en.body: Matrix multiplication is the core ML operation — LLMs perform millions per inference. The basic approach slices input matrices into smaller **tiles** and performs tile-wise multiplications with TensorOps to maximize parallelism and keep data in cache. Quantization further reduces memory traffic and fits larger models in memory.

deepdive_en.title: MSL type aliases for an MXFP8 tensor handle
deepdive_en.body: Before binding tensors in the kernel, defining **type aliases** up front helps. Here a `scales_plane` is declared with `fp8_e8m0` data type and a 32×1 block size (every 32 elements share one scale), then a full tensor type specifying an FP8 data type along with that scales_plane, finally bound to a buffer binding point.

deepdive_en.title: Declare an inline MXFP8 tensor on the stack
deepdive_en.body: If you don't want to create a full `MTLTensor` on the host, you can build a temporary tensor right on the shader's **stack**. The syntax is almost identical — just swap the tag `tensor_handle` for **`tensor_inline`** and pass buffer pointers plus other metadata to the tensor constructor.

deepdive_en.title: Slice tensors and run a quantized matmul
deepdive_en.body: Divide the problem across many threadgroups for parallelism: call `slice` on input and output tensors using the threadgroup ID, and **both data and scales planes are sliced together** per the block size. Then set up the `matmul2d_descriptor` (tile sizes, etc.), create a `matmul2d` op specifying the number of simdgroups, and pass in the quantized tensors — TensorOps **handles dequantization for you**.

deepdive_en.title: Building advanced ops
deepdive_en.body: Advanced topic: building a fuller, more complex custom operation with TensorOps. Using **Attention** as the example — core to every transformer including LLMs: multiply matrices Q and K, compute **SoftMax** via reductions on the rows of the intermediate matrix, then multiply by a third matrix V. The popular **FlashAttention** algorithm fuses all these into a single kernel.

deepdive_en.title: Set up simdgroup-scoped QxK multiplication
deepdive_en.body: To implement FlashAttention, set up a custom simd group mapping so **each simd group owns complete rows** of the intermediate matrix, letting SoftMax be computed without exchanging data between simd groups. The **`execution_simdgroup`** scope makes each simd group perform an independent matmul in parallel; use the simd group ID to slice Q/K/V tiles, and store the Q×K result in a **cooperative tensor** to feed the next step without writing to memory.

deepdive_en.title: Compute row-wise reduction for SoftMax
deepdive_en.body: Computing SoftMax needs a couple of reductions on the cooperative tensor. TensorOps provides **`reduce_rows`**, where threads exchange data to compute the max for each row, returning the result in another cooperative tensor. Here the `max` reduction operation is used with an initial value of negative infinity.

deepdive_en.title: Compute element-wise SoftMax with map_iterator
deepdive_en.body: Because the Q×K tile and the row-max cooperative tensors have different shapes, TensorOps provides **`map_iterator`** to bridge them: given an iterator to a 2D tensor element, it returns one pointing to the corresponding reduction-destination element. Loop over the 2D cooperative tensor with iterators, `map_iterator` each element to its row max, then dereference, subtract, and `exp` to compute SoftMax, storing the result back.

deepdive_en.title: Reuse cooperative tensor as matmul input
deepdive_en.body: Now multiply this cooperative tensor by V. In macOS 26 you'd first store it to threadgroup memory, but since 27 you can **use a cooperative tensor directly as a matmul input** via `get_left_input_cooperative_tensor`. Not every cooperative tensor can be reused — layouts may differ by data type and other factors — so check first with **`is_compatible_as_left_input`**; if incompatible, store and reload through threadgroup memory to convert layout, though either way the `op.run` call is the same.

deepdive_en.title: Integrating custom ops into Core AI
deepdive_en.body: **Core AI** provides tools for Python developers to convert PyTorch models to Core AI models, with support for custom Metal kernels. Following the "Deep Dive into Core AI Model authoring and Optimization" steps, the speaker integrates the custom FlashAttention kernel into a **Sam3** image segmentation model: defining the kernel body as a string in Python and registering a `TorchMetalKernel`, replacing the default huggingface attention, then exporting from PyTorch as an optimized Core AI asset. A demo runs promptable concept segmentation on an image with text (labeling all car pixels), correctly highlighting the car in blue — proving the kernel is fully integrated.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Recaps the tools covered: from quantized data types to advanced TensorOps features like cooperative tensors and reductions, to Core AI integration. Suggests exploring the **Metal Performance Primitives** documentation and programming guide, downloading the TensorOps sample code, and checking related Core AI and Metal sessions.

summary: 由 Foundation Models 框架團隊工程師 Eric Gourlaouen 主講，介紹在 macOS 上運用 **Apple Foundation Models** 的全新方式。WWDC25 推出的 Foundation Models 框架原本只能從 Swift 程式碼存取；macOS 27／iOS 27 帶來 image 輸入與 server model 支援，而本場重點是兩個新管道：macOS 27 內建的 **fm 命令列工具**，以及全新的 **Foundation Models Python SDK**。兩者都無需 API key、無雲端 API 成本，且 API 風格與 Swift 框架高度相似。

**fm CLI** 隨 macOS 27 預裝、直接在 Terminal 使用。`fm` 列出可用指令：`fm respond` 一次性 prompt 並回傳輸出（適合腳本，支援 `--model` 切換 Private Cloud Compute、`--image` 帶入影像、`--schema` 套用結構化輸出）、`fm chat` 啟動互動式對話（含 `/model` 切到 PCC、`/save` 存檔續談等指令）、`fm schema` 建立 schema。預設用裝置端模型（永遠可用），也可切到能力更強但有用量限制的 **Private Cloud Compute** 模型。講者示範用 fm 寫自動化腳本整理檔案：先列出工作目錄檔案，用 `fm schema object` 定義含 final／draft 兩個清單的結構，再用 `fm respond --schema` 讓模型把雜亂檔名分類成草稿與定稿，腳本據此把定稿備份、草稿移到封存碟。

**Python SDK** 讓你從 Python 程式碼存取裝置端模型，需 Python 3.10+、安裝 Xcode、Apple Silicon Mac，用 `pip` 安裝。它涵蓋框架核心功能：text／image 輸入、串流回應、tool calling 與 guided generation，且 API 與 Swift 幾乎一致——建立 `LanguageModelSession`、呼叫 `session.respond`、用 **`@fm.generable`** decorator 定義結構化輸出並傳給 `fm.respond` 的 generating 參數、定義 tool 供模型呼叫。對偏好 Python 的機器學習工程師特別友善。

Python SDK 最大好處是能輕鬆接上 Python 生態系。講者以「預測使用者下一筆雜貨訂單」功能做 case study：在 **Jupyter Notebook** 中先用大型 server model 產生評估資料（含 input 與期望 output），對三種不同 prompt（極簡、較詳細、最完整規則）各跑出 output 存進 **Pandas DataFrame**，再用第三方 server model 當 **judge** 依準則評分，最後用 **matplotlib** 畫圖比較。圖表顯示：過於詳細的 prompt 易超出 context window 而出錯、較簡略的 prompt 易多加品項與幻覺、詳細的則易漏掉應有品項——據此快速在 notebook 內迭代 prompt，無需重 build 整個專案。Swift 開發者則可用 Xcode 27 的 Evaluations 框架。

deepdive.body: 案例：設計「預測使用者下一筆要加入購物車的品項」功能，需確保預測可靠地基於歷史訂單、並考量購物車既有品項。先用大型 server model 產生評估資料（input 與期望 output），準備三種不同 prompt 的實作（極簡、較詳細、含規則清單最完整），對每筆評估資料各跑出 output 存進 **Pandas DataFrame**，再用 server model 當 **judge** 依準則評分、存回 DataFrame，最後用 **matplotlib** 畫圖。圖表顯示詳細 prompt 易達 context window 上限而生錯、簡略 prompt 易多加與幻覺品項、詳細的易漏品項，據此在 notebook 快速迭代。

summary_en: Presented by Foundation Models framework engineer Eric Gourlaouen, this session introduces new ways to use **Apple Foundation Models** on macOS. The framework introduced at WWDC25 was previously accessible only from Swift; macOS 27/iOS 27 add image inputs and server-model support, and this session focuses on two new channels: the **fm command line tool** preinstalled on macOS 27, and a new **Foundation Models Python SDK**. Both need no API key and incur no cloud API costs, and their APIs closely mirror the Swift framework.

The **fm CLI** ships with macOS 27 and runs in Terminal. Typing `fm` lists commands: `fm respond` for one-shot prompting that returns output (great for scripts, supporting `--model` to switch to Private Cloud Compute, `--image` to include an image, and `--schema` for structured output), `fm chat` for an interactive conversation (with `/model` to switch to PCC, `/save` to resume later, etc.), and `fm schema` to create a schema. By default it uses the on-device model (always available), but you can switch to the more capable **Private Cloud Compute** model (with usage limits). The presenter automates file cleanup with fm: list the working directory, define a structure with two lists (final/draft) via `fm schema object`, then use `fm respond --schema` to classify messy filenames into drafts and finals, with the script backing up finals and moving drafts to an archive disk.

The **Python SDK** gives Python code access to the on-device model, requiring Python 3.10+, Xcode installed, and an Apple Silicon Mac, installed via `pip`. It covers the framework's core features—text/image inputs, streaming responses, tool calling, and guided generation—and the API is nearly identical to Swift: create a `LanguageModelSession`, call `session.respond`, define structured output with the **`@fm.generable`** decorator passed to `fm.respond`'s generating argument, and define tools for the model to call. It's especially friendly to ML engineers who prefer Python.

The SDK's biggest benefit is easy integration with the Python ecosystem. The presenter's case study—predicting a user's next grocery order—runs in a **Jupyter Notebook**: first generate evaluation data (inputs and expected outputs) with a large server model, run three different prompts (minimal, more descriptive, most comprehensive with rules) to produce outputs stored in a **Pandas DataFrame**, score each with a third-party server model as a **judge**, and chart the results with **matplotlib**. The charts show that overly detailed prompts tend to hit the context window and error, less detailed prompts tend to add excess and hallucinated items, and detailed ones tend to miss expected items—letting you iterate quickly right in the notebook without rebuilding the whole project. Swift developers can instead use Xcode 27's Evaluations framework.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Framework engineer Eric opens. WWDC25 introduced the **Foundation Models** framework (with guided generation and tool calling) for prompting the on-device Apple Foundation Model in apps. macOS 27/iOS 27 add image inputs in prompts and access to server models. The framework needs no API key and incurs no cloud costs, but until now was accessible only from Swift.

deepdive_en.title: Introducing the fm CLI and Python SDK
deepdive_en.body: Announces two new ways to access Apple Foundation Models on macOS: the **fm command line tool** built into macOS 27 (great for quickly testing prompts in Terminal or for automation), and the **Foundation Models Python SDK** (supporting tool calling and guided generation, with a Swift-like API, easy for ML engineers to use in Python and build evaluation pipelines).

deepdive_en.title: Command line tool
deepdive_en.body: Dives into the **fm** CLI: preinstalled with macOS 27, typing `fm` in Terminal lists commands—`respond` (prompt and respond), `chat` (interactive interface), `schema` (create a schema), and more. Demos `fm chat` conversing with the on-device model, switching to **Private Cloud Compute** via `/model`, and `/save` to resume later; for inline responses (as in scripts) use `fm respond`.

deepdive_en.title: fm respond and structured output
deepdive_en.body: Covers `fm respond` options: `--model` to use the PCC model, `--image` to include an image. The on-device model is the default (always available); the PCC model is bigger and better on complex problems but has usage limits. You can build a schema with `fm schema object` and use it via `fm respond --schema` for structured output.

deepdive_en.title: Prompt the on-device model with fm respond
deepdive_en.body: Demos the most basic use: run `fm respond` with a prompt in Terminal and shortly get the model's response. Use `--help` to see all options.

deepdive_en.title: Automating file management with fm
deepdive_en.body: Poses a practical problem: a presentation folder is full of drafts, and you want to keep only finals, back them up, and move old ones to an archive disk—as a re-runnable script. Calling a language model from the script via fm sorts drafts from finals even when the names are messy and hard to sort predictably.

deepdive_en.title: Sort files with fm respond and a schema
deepdive_en.body: Walks through the script: load the working directory's file list, define structured output with two lists (final and draft files) via `fm schema object`, then use `fm respond --schema` with a prompt to classify. `fm respond` outputs the model-generated JSON result, which the script uses to copy finals to backup and move drafts to the archive.

deepdive_en.title: Python SDK
deepdive_en.body: Turns to the **Python SDK**: accessing the on-device Apple Foundation Models from Python code, covering prompting (text/image inputs), streaming, guided generation, and tool calling. Those familiar with the Swift framework will pick up the API and abstractions quickly.

deepdive_en.title: Install the Foundation Models Python SDK
deepdive_en.body: Install requirements: Python 3.10 or later, Xcode installed, and an Apple Silicon Mac, via `pip` (or another package manager). The SDK includes the framework's core features, and the API and abstractions feel familiar to Swift users.

deepdive_en.title: Prompting, tool calling and guided generation
deepdive_en.body: Using a grocery-ordering app to evaluate prompt accuracy, prototype in Python before implementing in Swift. Overviews three capabilities: prompting the model, defining tools the model can call (e.g., fetch recent orders for personalization), and guided generation to constrain structured output.

deepdive_en.title: Create a session and respond to a prompt
deepdive_en.body: Just like Swift: create a `LanguageModelSession` (optionally passing instructions), call `session.respond` with a prompt, and the method's result holds the model's output.

deepdive_en.title: Define a Tool for the language model
deepdive_en.body: As in the Swift framework, you can expose tools to the model to interact with the user's context. For example, define a tool the model can call to fetch the last few orders so it can provide more personalized information.

deepdive_en.title: Generate structured output with @fm.generable
deepdive_en.body: Use the **`@fm.generable`** decorator to define the desired output structure (such as an `ItemsSuggestion` object) and pass it to `fm.respond`'s generating argument, applying guided generation to ensure the model's output matches that structure.

deepdive_en.title: Building an evaluation pipeline in Python
deepdive_en.body: Case study: designing a feature that predicts items to add to the user's cart, ensuring predictions reliably reflect previous orders and account for items already in the cart. First generate evaluation data (inputs and expected outputs) with a large server model, prepare three implementations with different prompts (minimal, more descriptive, most comprehensive with a rules list), run outputs for each input into a **Pandas DataFrame**, score with a server model as a **judge** saved back to the DataFrame, then chart with **matplotlib**. Charts show detailed prompts hit the context window and error, minimal ones add excess and hallucinated items, and detailed ones miss items—iterating quickly in the notebook.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Recaps the new channels and gives next steps: first explore fm's options and features in Terminal; then learn the Python SDK from its GitHub repo (with example snippets and docs); finally build an evaluation pipeline—think of a model use, find working prompts, and quantify effectiveness against an evaluation dataset.

title: Improve your prompts by hill-climbing with Evaluations
gloss: 用評估爬坡法改進你的提示詞
takeaway: 用比較式評估（Evaluation）為提示詞建立基準、以 Cohen's kappa 校準模型評審與人類，再逐步迭代改進提示與選擇模型。
chapters: The alignment dataset, extracted to JSON
The judge alignment evaluation: dataset, subject, evaluator
Few-shot worked examples in the judge prompt
Adding few-shot examples to the judge

Going beyond prompts: adding a tool

points.text: 用**比較式評估（Evaluation）**搭配 **ScoreDimension** 與 **ModelJudgeEvaluator** 為提示詞建立可量化基準，逐步**爬坡（hill-climbing）**改進。
以 **Cohen's kappa** 量測模型評審與人類專家之間的**漂移（drift）**，並用對齊資料集校準評審提示。
用 **.evaluates** 把評估包進 **Swift Testing** 套件，以 **#expect** 設定對齊門檻並做校準測試。
比較控制組與實驗組的評審提示，並透過**少樣本範例（few-shot examples）**精修評分維度。
超越單純調提示：為 **BookTaggingService** 加入 **BookLookupTool**（Tool 協定），在同一套件中比較有無工具的差異。

audience: **用 Foundation Models 開發功能、想系統化評估與改進提示詞**並挑選合適模型的開發者。
gloss_en: Improve your prompts by hill-climbing with Evaluations
takeaway_en: Use comparative Evaluation to baseline your prompts, calibrate the model judge against humans with Cohen's kappa, then iteratively improve prompts and select models.

points_en.text: Use **comparative Evaluation** with **ScoreDimension** and **ModelJudgeEvaluator** to build a quantifiable baseline for your prompts and improve them step by step through **hill-climbing**.
Measure the **drift** between the model judge and human experts with **Cohen's kappa**, and calibrate the judge prompt using an alignment dataset.
Use **.evaluates** to wrap evaluations into a **Swift Testing** suite, setting alignment thresholds and running calibration tests with **#expect**.
Compare control and experimental judge prompts, and refine score dimensions with **few-shot examples**.
Go beyond simply tuning prompts: add a **BookLookupTool** (Tool protocol) to **BookTaggingService**, and compare results with and without the tool in the same suite.

audience_en: Developers **building features with Foundation Models who want to systematically evaluate and improve their prompts** and pick the right model.
summary: 這場由 Evaluations 框架團隊的 Marcus 主講，核心是 **hill-climbing**（爬坡）這套迭代改善流程：以 develop → run → analyze 為循環，用評估分數當作指南，一次只改一個變數，把每次迭代當成一場**科學實驗**（control 對照組 vs experimental 實驗組）來思考。範例是 Book Tracker 的標籤產生功能——它用 on-device model 依讀者書評產生標籤，但常產出像 poignant（讀者情緒）或 quiet-steadiness（直接抄自書評、不利搜尋）這類不理想的標籤。

整場最關鍵的洞見是 **drift**（漂移）：當 **model judge** 與人類專家對同一批樣本評分時，若兩者傾向不一致，平均分數會隨資料集成長而越拉越遠，最終讓你無法判斷功能是否被正確評估。講者指出單純用 **accuracy** 不夠，因為資料集分數分布不均（樣本多為高品質），judge 只要傾向給高分就會「看似對齊」。解法是引入 **Cohen's kappa**——以 accuracy 減去隨機巧合一致的機率、再除以「有意一致」的可能性，得出真正的 alignment 分數；統計學上 0.6 代表有意義的一致水準。

技術實作上，講者示範用 **Evaluations 框架** 寫一個 judge 對齊評估，由 dataset、subject、evaluators、aggregation 四部分組成：dataset 重用先前評估產生的 Xcode 附件（summary/tag pairs）並加上專家評分，subject 直接回傳已生成的標籤，evaluator 沿用同一個 **ModelJudgeEvaluator**，aggregation 則以自訂方法計算 Cohen's kappa 及各 **ScoreDimension** 的 mean 與 standard deviation。對齊不足時就回到 develop 階段改進 judge 的 prompt：先加入 app 情境與好壞標籤範例，再細化 relevance／usefulness 的 **scoring dimensions**，最後補上少量 **few-shot worked examples**（刻意保持精簡以避免 overfit），在 Xcode 27 的並排 **comparison view** 中比對 control 與 experimental 的結果。

最後，講者示範**超越 prompt** 的改善方式：為標籤服務新增一個 **BookLookupTool**，讓模型能依書評中的角色、場景、引文等線索查出書名與作者，藉此取得更多上下文。做法是讓 `BookTaggingService.generateTags` 多收一個 `tools` 參數（預設空陣列、不影響舊評估），再寫一個帶 tool 的新評估，於同一個 suite 中比較「有 tool」與「無 tool」的品質差異。實務心法：一次只改一個變數、失敗的實驗和成功的一樣有價值、保持實驗的創造力（prompt、tool、模型、dataset、aggregation、evaluator 都可調），並持續留意 drift——讓 judge 與你對齊，才能在資料集成長時持續取得可信的訊號。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: Evaluations 框架團隊的 Marcus 開場，說明 AI 功能難以驗證在所有情況下是否如預期運作，因此推出 **Evaluations 框架**。核心方法是 **hill-climbing**：develop（做出想衡量的改動）→ run（執行評估）→ analyze（分析結果）的迭代循環，並強調有效的爬坡還需要一點「科學思維」。本場聚焦在「對已有評估管線進行爬坡」，若還沒建好管線，建議先看 "Meet the Evaluations framework"。

deepdive.title: BookTracker's tagging problem
deepdive.body: 以 **Book Tracker** 為例，其 tagging service 用模型依讀者書評產生標籤。講者示範問題：Little Women 出現 poignant 這類描述讀者**感受**而非書本內容的標籤，以及 quiet-steadiness 這種直接抄自書評、日後搜尋幾乎用不到的標籤。結論是標籤產生器沒有想像中好，而這正是 hill-climbing 的起點。

deepdive.title: The BookTaggingEvaluation
deepdive.body: 檢視既有的 **BookTaggingEvaluation**，重點看品質如何被評判。質性面由 **score dimensions** 捕捉：**Relevance** 衡量標籤多能代表書本的情節、主題等資訊，**Usefulness** 衡量標籤作為搜尋詞的好壞。**ModelJudgeEvaluator** 用這些維度加上一段 prompt 為每組標籤評分。講者計畫把 Treasure Island 與 Little Women 兩本書加進資料集再觀察結果。

deepdive.title: Refined Relevance & Usefulness score dimensions
deepdive.body: 細看 **ScoreDimension** 的定義：Relevance 區分「書本屬性」（如 suspenseful）與「讀者反應」（如 exhausted），並把標錯 genre 視為嚴重失敗；Usefulness 要求標籤當作 library shelf label——夠廣能讓多本書共用、又夠精確能縮小搜尋，排除自創詞、角色名與過度籠統的字。兩者皆用 1–4 的 **numeric scale** 並對每個分數給出明確判準。

deepdive.title: Analyzing the evaluation results
deepdive.body: 進入 analyze 階段，用 Xcode 新的 **evaluations report** 檢視上次執行結果，頂部是 aggregate metric charts、下方是結果表，並開啟 Assistant Editor 比對模型產出與自己預期的標籤。講者對 Treasure Island 給 relevance 4、usefulness 2，但 judge 卻給 usefulness 4；Little Women 也出現同樣分歧，顯示自己與 model judge 的評分有明顯落差。

deepdive.title: Drift between judge and human
deepdive.body: 把模型與人類評分的落差定義為 **drift**，並解釋其危害：假設 10 個樣本由 judge 與人各評 1–4 分再取平均，若兩者傾向不一致，平均分會彼此發散；隨資料集成長，drift 會越來越寬，最終難以判斷功能是否被正確評估。解方是把 judge 對齊到專家的判斷。

deepdive.title: Measuring drift with Cohen's kappa
deepdive.body: 討論如何量化 drift。最直觀是對齊兩者評分算出 **accuracy**（一致百分比），但它只在每個分數等機率出現時才可靠；實際資料集分布不均（多為高品質、人類傾向給高分），judge 也傾向給高分就會「假性對齊」，放到更大資料集仍會 drift。因此需要一個能考慮加權分布與運氣巧合的替代方案。

deepdive.title: The alignment dataset, extracted to JSON
deepdive.body: 為了讓 judge 與人類評同一批資料，講者重用先前評估的產物：因為評估在測試中執行，Xcode 產生了含所有評估資料的 attachment，可從中抽取 summary 與 tag pairs 成 JSON。接著在每筆加上自己的專家評分，這份檔案就成為對齊評估的輸入。

deepdive.title: Building a judge alignment evaluation
deepdive.body: 說明對齊評估由四個元件構成：**dataset**、**subject**、**evaluators**、以及結果的 **aggregation**。重點在於 judge 與人必須評估**完全相同**的資料集，才能公平比較兩者的評分傾向。

deepdive.title: The judge alignment evaluation: dataset, subject, evaluator
deepdive.body: 逐一實作：dataset 載入抽取出的 summary/tag pairs；subject 因標籤已生成，直接回傳既有標籤而非重新呼叫 API；evaluator 則沿用與 book-tags 評估**完全相同**的 ModelJudgeEvaluator，讓 judge 在此給出它的評分。

deepdive.title: Cohen's kappa aggregation
deepdive.body: 在 aggregation 階段比較自己與 judge 的評分，用自訂 aggregation method 計算 **Cohen's kappa**：以 accuracy 減去兩者隨機一致的機率，再除以隨機一致的反面（即有意一致的機率），得出 alignment。除了 kappa，也一併算出每個 score dimension 的 **mean** 與 **standard deviation**，方便觀察 judge 分數的升降趨勢。

deepdive.title: The judge calibration test
deepdive.body: 用 Swift Testing 設定測試，期望 relevance 與 usefulness 的 alignment 分數都大於 **0.6**（統計學上代表有意義的一致水準）。執行後測試**失敗**，代表期望未達成，於是再次進入 analyze 階段檢視細節。

deepdive.title: Analyzing alignment failures
deepdive.body: 在 evaluation report 中發現 relevance 與 usefulness 對齊分數都偏低。開 Assistant 細看樣本：Frankenstein 的 judge 與人分歧很大（judge 竟認為 self-help、self-improvement 相關）；The Ramakien 則在 usefulness 上分歧，visual-dimension、quaint-dignity 等標籤過度具體。講者判斷問題在於 judge 的 prompt 缺乏足夠 context。

deepdive.title: The experimental judge prompt
deepdive.body: 改進方向是寫一個新 prompt 來和現行 prompt 比較。借用科學實驗概念：**control group** 用原本的 judge prompt 當基準，**experimental group** 用改寫後更詳盡的 prompt——先給 judge 關於 app 與評判對象的 context，再給好標籤的範例與辨識壞標籤的方式。

deepdive.title: Comparative evaluation: control vs experimental
deepdive.body: 把兩個評估放進同一 test suite 一起執行並比較。結果 relevance 的 alignment 改善、但 usefulness 大幅下滑；測試仍未通過。講者決定**保留**這次 prompt 改動，把下一輪焦點放在改善 usefulness——體現「一次處理一個 trade-off」的爬坡精神。

deepdive.title: Refining the scoring dimensions
deepdive.body: 用 Xcode 的 comparison view 並排檢視，發現 Picture of Dorian Gray 的 usefulness 分歧大、experimental judge 的分數全是 2 或 3，判得太嚴。為了只變動一個變數，講者先把 experimental 的 prompt 套回 baseline，再單獨修改 scoring dimensions：relevance 加強需要 genre 標籤、usefulness 則更嚴格看待過度具體的標籤。重跑後兩者分數都大幅優於 baseline。

deepdive.title: Few-shot worked examples in the judge prompt
deepdive.body: 雖然已改善但仍未達標。細看 Moby Dick 的 relevance 開始對齊、usefulness 仍需加強，而 Frankenstein 持續讓 judge 出錯。講者判斷 judge 需要一些「自己如何評分」的範例，好讓它依照同一套標準的 pattern 來評判。

deepdive.title: Adding few-shot examples to the judge
deepdive.body: 重寫主 judge prompt，加入更多功能目標說明以 ground 模型，再寫出數個評分範例（worked examples A–F，附上 librarian 給的 Relevance/Usefulness 分數）。刻意只給**少量**範例，避免清單過長導致 overfit 對齊分數而誤判 judge 已對齊。重跑後分數終於超過期望值、測試通過，得以退出爬坡循環。

deepdive.title: The BookLookupTool
deepdive.body: 開始示範超越 prompt 的改善：因標籤用 on-device model 生成（讓使用者隨處皆可用），講者想給模型更多書本 context。Book Tracker 已存有作者與書名，於是建立 **BookLookupTool**，依書評中的角色、場景、引文、情節等 distinguishing details 查出書名與作者；加 tool 本身也是一種 hill-climbing。

deepdive.title: BookTaggingService with a tools parameter
deepdive.body: 為了比較「有 tool」與「無 tool」的品質，修改 **BookTaggingService**，讓 generateTags 多收一個 `tools` 參數並預設為**空陣列**——如此既能傳入新 tool，又能讓既有評估完全不必改動。session 也用 `permissiveContentTransformations` guardrails 建立 LanguageModelSession。

deepdive.title: Evaluation with the lookup tool
deepdive.body: 寫一個新評估 BookTaggingWithLookupEvaluation，內容與原評估**完全相同**，唯一差別是在 subject 中把 `BookLookupTool()` 傳入 tools 陣列。dataset、evaluators、aggregation 全部沿用，確保比較公平。

deepdive.title: Compare with/without the tool in one suite
deepdive.body: 定義兩個評估實例（一個不帶 tool、一個帶 tool）放進同一 suite 執行比較。帶 tool 的服務通過了所有期望、且整體表現較佳，看來可以準備出貨。

deepdive.title: Going beyond prompts: adding a tool
deepdive.body: 但講者指出兩個隱憂：Book Tracker 的 dataset 只有 13 對書評，無法涵蓋使用者可能提交的多樣性；而且觀察到 tool 並未在所有該被呼叫的情境被呼叫，缺乏驗證 tool 是否在正確時機被使用的方法。框架對這兩點都有解，詳見 "Create robust evaluations for agentic apps"（tool call evaluators 與 Sample Generator API）。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 總結爬坡四大心法：一次只改一個變數、把每次迭代當科學實驗來隔離變因；過程需要時間，失敗的實驗和成功的一樣有價值；好實驗需要創造力，instructions、tools、模型、dataset、aggregation、evaluator 全都可調；最後務必留意 **drift**——對齊良好的 model judge 能比人類更快產生評分，在資料集成長時持續提供可信訊號。並提供 Book Tracker app 與對齊評估的範例與文件連結。

summary_en: Hosted by Marcus from the Evaluations framework team, this session centers on **hill-climbing**: an iterative develop → run → analyze loop that uses evaluation scores as a guide, changing one variable at a time and treating every iteration like a **science experiment** with a control group and an experimental group. The running example is Book Tracker's tag generator, which uses an on-device model to produce tags from a reader's review but often emits poor ones like poignant (a reader emotion) or quiet-steadiness (lifted straight from the review and useless for search).

The key insight is **drift**: when a **model judge** and a human expert rate the same samples but tend to disagree, their averaged scores diverge further as the dataset grows, until you can no longer tell whether your feature is being evaluated correctly. Plain **accuracy** isn't enough, because datasets skew toward high-quality samples, so a judge that simply tends to score high can look aligned while still drifting on larger data. The fix is **Cohen's kappa** — accuracy minus the chance of coincidental agreement, divided by the chance of intentional agreement — yielding a true alignment score, where 0.6 is considered a meaningful level of agreement.

Implementation-wise, the speaker writes a judge-alignment evaluation with the **Evaluations framework**, composed of dataset, subject, evaluators, and aggregation: the dataset reuses the Xcode attachment from a prior run (summary/tag pairs) annotated with expert ratings, the subject simply returns the already-generated tags, the evaluator reuses the same **ModelJudgeEvaluator**, and a custom aggregation computes Cohen's kappa plus the mean and standard deviation of each **ScoreDimension**. When alignment falls short, he returns to develop and improves the judge's prompt — adding app context and good/bad tag examples, refining the relevance/usefulness **scoring dimensions**, and finally adding a few **few-shot worked examples** (kept small to avoid overfitting) — comparing control vs experimental side by side in Xcode 27's new comparison view.

Finally he shows how to improve a feature **beyond prompts** by adding a **BookLookupTool** that resolves a book's title and author from clues in the review (character names, settings, quoted lines), giving the model more context. He adds a `tools` parameter to `BookTaggingService.generateTags` defaulting to an empty array (so existing evaluations are untouched), then writes a new evaluation passing the tool, and compares with-tool vs without-tool in one suite. The practical takeaways: change one variable at a time, treat failed experiments as just as informative as successful ones, stay creative (prompt, tools, model, dataset, aggregation, evaluator are all fair game), and watch for drift — keeping the judge aligned yields trustworthy signal as the dataset grows.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Marcus from the Evaluations framework team opens by noting how hard it is to verify that an AI feature behaves as expected in all cases, motivating the **Evaluations framework**. Its core method is **hill-climbing**: an iterative loop of develop (make a change you want to measure), run (execute the evaluation), and analyze (understand the results), with the reminder that effective hill-climbing also takes some scientific thinking. The session assumes you already have an evaluation pipeline; if not, watch "Meet the Evaluations framework" first.

deepdive_en.title: BookTracker's tagging problem
deepdive_en.body: Using **Book Tracker** as the example, its tagging service generates tags from reader reviews. The speaker shows the problem: Little Women yields poignant (describing the reader's **feelings**, not the book) and quiet-steadiness (lifted from the review and nearly useless for later search). The conclusion is that the tag generator isn't as good as it could be — which is exactly where hill-climbing begins.

deepdive_en.title: The BookTaggingEvaluation
deepdive_en.body: He reviews the existing **BookTaggingEvaluation**, focusing on how quality is judged. The qualitative side is captured by **score dimensions**: **Relevance** measures how well tags represent the book's plot and themes, and **Usefulness** measures how good the tags are as search terms. A **ModelJudgeEvaluator** uses those dimensions plus a prompt to score each tag set. The plan is to add Treasure Island and Little Women to the dataset and inspect the results.

deepdive_en.title: Refined Relevance & Usefulness score dimensions
deepdive_en.body: A closer look at the **ScoreDimension** definitions: Relevance distinguishes book properties (e.g. suspenseful) from reader reactions (e.g. exhausted) and treats a mislabeled genre as a serious failure; Usefulness requires tags to act as library shelf labels — broad enough to group several books, specific enough to narrow a search — excluding made-up phrases, character names, and overly generic words. Both use a 1–4 numeric scale with explicit criteria per score.

deepdive_en.title: Analyzing the evaluation results
deepdive_en.body: In the analyze phase he uses Xcode's new **evaluations report** to inspect the last run — aggregate metric charts on top, a results table below — and opens the Assistant Editor to compare model output against his expected tags. He'd score Treasure Island relevance 4, usefulness 2, but the judge gave usefulness 4; Little Women shows the same divergence, revealing a clear gap between his ratings and the model judge's.

deepdive_en.title: Drift between judge and human
deepdive_en.body: He names the model-vs-human gap **drift** and explains its danger: with 10 samples each rated 1–4 by a judge and a person, if the two tend to disagree their averages diverge, and as the dataset grows drift widens until you can't tell whether the feature is properly evaluated. The remedy is to align the judge to the expert's opinion.

deepdive_en.title: Measuring drift with Cohen's kappa
deepdive_en.body: How to quantify drift: the obvious approach is **accuracy** (percent agreement), but it's only reliable when every score is equally likely; real datasets are skewed (mostly high-quality, humans rate high), so a judge that also rates high looks falsely aligned and still drifts on larger data. So an alternative is needed that accounts for the weighted distribution and the chance of lucky agreement.

deepdive_en.title: The alignment dataset, extracted to JSON
deepdive_en.body: To have judge and human rate the same data, he reuses the prior run's output: because the evaluation ran in a test, Xcode produced an attachment with all the evaluation data, from which he extracts summary and tag pairs into JSON. He then adds his expert ratings to each entry, and this file becomes the input to the alignment evaluation.

deepdive_en.title: Building a judge alignment evaluation
deepdive_en.body: He explains the alignment evaluation has four components: **dataset**, **subject**, **evaluators**, and **aggregation** of results. The crucial point is that the judge and the human must evaluate the exact same dataset so their rating tendencies can be compared fairly.

deepdive_en.title: The judge alignment evaluation: dataset, subject, evaluator
deepdive_en.body: Implementing each piece: the dataset loads the extracted summary/tag pairs; the subject simply returns the already-generated tags rather than re-calling the API; and the evaluator reuses the **exact same** ModelJudgeEvaluator as the book-tags evaluation, which is where the judge produces its rating.

deepdive_en.title: Cohen's kappa aggregation
deepdive_en.body: In aggregation he compares his ratings against the judge's via a custom method computing **Cohen's kappa**: start from accuracy, subtract the chance of random agreement, then divide by the inverse of random agreement (the chance of intentional agreement). Alongside kappa he also computes each score dimension's **mean** and **standard deviation** to track whether the judge's scores rise or fall.

deepdive_en.title: The judge calibration test
deepdive_en.body: Using Swift Testing he sets an expectation that both relevance and usefulness alignment exceed **0.6** (statistically a meaningful level of agreement). The test **fails**, meaning the expectation isn't met, so he returns to the analyze phase to inspect the details.

deepdive_en.title: Analyzing alignment failures
deepdive_en.body: The report shows both relevance and usefulness alignment are low. In the Assistant he inspects samples: Frankenstein has a large gap (the judge even thinks self-help and self-improvement are relevant), and The Ramakien diverges on usefulness with overly specific tags like visual-dimension and quaint-dignity. He concludes the judge's prompt lacks sufficient context.

deepdive_en.title: The experimental judge prompt
deepdive_en.body: The improvement is to write a new prompt and compare it against the current one, borrowing the science-experiment idea: the **control group** uses the original judge prompt as baseline, while the **experimental group** uses a more thorough prompt — first giving the judge context about the app and what it's judging, then examples of good tags and ways to identify bad ones.

deepdive_en.title: Comparative evaluation: control vs experimental
deepdive_en.body: Both evaluations run in one test suite for comparison. Relevance alignment improves but usefulness drops considerably, and the test still doesn't pass. He decides to **keep** this prompt change and focus the next round on improving usefulness — embodying the hill-climbing habit of handling one trade-off at a time.

deepdive_en.title: Refining the scoring dimensions
deepdive_en.body: Using Xcode's comparison view he spots a big usefulness gap on Picture of Dorian Gray, with the experimental judge scoring everything 2 or 3 — too harsh. To change only one variable, he first applies the experimental prompt back into the baseline, then modifies the scoring dimensions alone: relevance emphasizes needing a genre tag, usefulness becomes more critical of overly specific tags. The rerun shows both scores greatly improved over baseline.

deepdive_en.title: Few-shot worked examples in the judge prompt
deepdive_en.body: Improved but still short of the goal. Inspecting Moby Dick shows relevance aligning while usefulness still needs work, and Frankenstein keeps tripping up the judge. He concludes the judge needs examples of how he himself rates, giving it a pattern to judge by his scale.

deepdive_en.title: Adding few-shot examples to the judge
deepdive_en.body: He reworks the main judge prompt with more detail about the feature's goal to ground the model, then writes several worked examples (A–F, each with the librarian's Relevance/Usefulness scores). He deliberately uses only a **few** examples to avoid overfitting the alignment score, which would mask whether the judge is truly aligned. The rerun finally exceeds the expected value and the test passes, so he can exit the loop.

deepdive_en.title: The BookLookupTool
deepdive_en.body: He moves beyond prompts: since tags are generated on-device (so users can tag books anywhere), he wants to give the model more context. Book Tracker already stores the author and title, so he builds a **BookLookupTool** that resolves a book's title and author from distinguishing details in the review — character names, settings, quoted lines, plot points. Adding the tool is itself a form of hill-climbing.

deepdive_en.title: BookTaggingService with a tools parameter
deepdive_en.body: To compare with-tool vs without-tool quality, he modifies **BookTaggingService** so generateTags takes a `tools` parameter defaulting to an **empty array** — letting him pass the new tool while leaving existing evaluations unchanged. The session is built with `permissiveContentTransformations` guardrails on the LanguageModelSession.

deepdive_en.title: Evaluation with the lookup tool
deepdive_en.body: He writes a new evaluation, BookTaggingWithLookupEvaluation, identical to the original except that its subject passes `BookLookupTool()` in the tools array. The dataset, evaluators, and aggregation are all reused to keep the comparison fair.

deepdive_en.title: Compare with/without the tool in one suite
deepdive_en.body: He defines two evaluation instances — one without the tool, one with — and runs them in the same suite to compare. The tool-using service meets all expectations and performs better overall, so things look ready to ship.

deepdive_en.title: Going beyond prompts: adding a tool
deepdive_en.body: But he flags two concerns: Book Tracker's dataset has only 13 review pairs, too few to cover the variety users might submit, and the tool isn't being called in every situation it should be, with no way to verify it fires at the right moments. The framework addresses both — see "Create robust evaluations for agentic apps" for tool-call evaluators and the Sample Generator API.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: He recaps four lessons: change one thing at a time and treat each iteration as a science experiment to isolate variables; the process takes time and failed experiments tell you as much as successful ones; good experiments need creativity — instructions, tools, models, dataset, aggregation, and evaluators are all fair game; and finally watch out for **drift**, since a well-tuned model judge rates far faster than humans and keeps providing useful signal as the dataset grows. Links to the Book Tracker app, the alignment evaluations, and the docs are provided.

title: Build live production tools for Apple Immersive Video
gloss: 為 Apple Immersive Video 打造直播製作工具
takeaway: 了解如何封裝沉浸式影片、空間音訊與場景中繼資料，並透過即時媒體傳輸與 VideoToolbox 壓縮設定打造 Apple Immersive Video 的直播製作流程。
chapters: Set compression properties for vexu metadata

points.text: 概覽 **Apple Immersive Video** 的直播製作流程，並說明沉浸式直播與一般直播的差異。
介紹沉浸式直播格式，整合沉浸式影片、**spatial audio** 與場景中繼資料。
說明 **real-time media transport** 以及錄製與播放的處理方式。
透過 **VideoToolbox** 設定壓縮屬性 **kVTCompressionPropertyKey_ProjectionKind** 為 AppleImmersiveVideo 來寫入 vexu 中繼資料。

audience: 適合**從事沉浸式影片直播製作、需要封裝與傳輸 Apple Immersive Video 的開發者與工程團隊**。
gloss_en: Build live production tools for Apple Immersive Video
takeaway_en: Learn how to package immersive video, spatial audio, and scene metadata, and build a live production workflow for Apple Immersive Video using real-time media transport and VideoToolbox compression settings.

points_en.text: Overviews the live production workflow for **Apple Immersive Video** and explains how immersive live broadcasts differ from ordinary ones.
Introduces the immersive live format, combining immersive video, **spatial audio**, and scene metadata.
Explains **real-time media transport** and how recording and playback are handled.
Write vexu metadata by setting the **VideoToolbox** compression property **kVTCompressionPropertyKey_ProjectionKind** to AppleImmersiveVideo.

audience_en: **Developers and engineering teams working on immersive video live production who need to package and transport Apple Immersive Video.**
summary: 這場由 Apple Immersive Video Live Engineering 團隊主講，背景是 Apple 今年首度把 LA Lakers 球賽以 **Apple Immersive Video** 即時串流進 Apple Vision Pro（透過 Spectrum SportsNet 與 NBA app）。講者的目標是啟發大家打造下一代沉浸式直播工具與工作流程，並先用一段時間說明傳統直播製作管線（production domain 與 delivery domain），介紹攝影機、圖卡、replay、video switcher、麥克風、audio console，以及把所有設備串在一起的中央 media router，作為理解沉浸式製作的基礎。

接著講者點出沉浸式直播與傳統 2D 製作的根本差異：為了符合人眼視覺敏銳度，影像解析度是一般 2D 製作的 **32 倍**且以兩倍幀率產製，音訊則改用最多可達 64 聲道以上的 **ASAF（Apple Spatial Audio Format）**。這些龐大的格式與品質需求讓傳統工具與傳輸方式無法直接沿用，必須重建整套工作流程。為此他歸納三個關鍵概念：一套媒體格式標準、一套即時傳輸方法，以及錄製與播放回放（playout）的機制。

媒體格式由三個既有標準組合而成：影像是串流的 **ProRes** 影格（而非未壓縮影格，且 Apple Silicon 對 ProRes 處理特別最佳化）、音訊是承載高階 ambisonics 與 spatial audio objects 的未壓縮 PCM（即 ASAF）、metadata 則是每影格的 JSON 物件，描述鏡頭校正、創意事件、空間音訊行為等。傳輸層採用業界標準 **SMPTE 2110**：壓縮影像走 **2110-22**（左右眼以兩個獨立 essence 包在同一 stream，免去 frame packing 或雙串流管理）、ASAF 音訊走 **2110-30**、JSON metadata 走 **2110-41**。

錄製與回放是直播的核心能力，傳統 2D 工作流程因反覆編解碼會累積世代損失，但沉浸式格式因「全部都已是 ProRes」而免去額外編解碼——同一批 ProRes 影格直接複製進 MOV 檔再讀回 2110 串流，全程零品質損失。實作上以 AVFoundation 的 **AVAssetWriter** 寫入影像、音訊與 MEBX metadata 軌；寫影像軌時要在 `AVVideoCompressionPropertiesKey` 設定新的 VideoToolbox 常數 `kVTProjectionKind_AppleImmersiveVideo`，加上正確的 vexu 靜態 metadata；metadata 則需先反序列化、解析後，用 visionOS 26 引入的 **Immersive Media Support（IMS）** 框架建立 lens calibration、camera ID 等物件並與影音同步寫入。實務上鼓勵以 AVFoundation、VideoToolbox、AudioToolbox 與 IMS 自行打造工具，並深入 SMPTE 2110 把工具串成完整直播工作流程。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: 由 Apple Immersive Video Live Engineering 團隊負責人 Jared King 開場，以今年首度把 LA Lakers 球賽即時串流進 **Apple Vision Pro** 的案例切入，說明沉浸式攝影機讓球迷坐進難以企及的座位、資料驅動圖卡強化賽事、**spatial audio** 把觀眾包進現場人聲中。背後是 Apple 自建的直播平台。講者把目標定為啟發大家打造下一代沉浸式工具與直播體驗。

deepdive.title: Live production overview
deepdive.body: 先建立直播管線的整體圖像：影音與資料在 **production domain** 被擷取與創意製作，再於 **delivery domain** 編碼並即時串流給觀眾。規模可大可小，從 TV 攝影棚、轉播車到 podcast 工作室或小型音樂場館皆然，但目標一致——即時把製作好的內容傳給觀眾。本場聚焦 production domain 的獨特之處。

deepdive.title: What makes immersive live different
deepdive.body: 逐一介紹製作工作流程中的創意工具：多台 **live cameras** 捕捉不同角度、**graphics** 鍵控疊加下三分之一字幕或計分板、**replay** 系統錄影與回放、**video switcher** 讓操作員切換鏡頭並疊圖產出最終創意串流。音訊端由麥克風收音、**audio console** 把各音源混成最終的 mix。所有工具都透過中央 **media router** 像統一網路層般彼此交換訊號。

deepdive.title: Immersive live format
deepdive.body: 點出沉浸式與 2D 製作分道揚鑣的關鍵在於 fidelity 與 presence：影像解析度是 2D 製作的 **32 倍**並以兩倍幀率產製以匹配人眼視覺敏銳度，音訊以 **ASAF** 取代立體聲或 5.1，可含 **64 聲道以上**。這些龐大格式讓傳統工具與傳輸方式無法支撐，因此必須重建整套工作流程，並歸納出格式標準、即時傳輸、錄製回放三大主題。

deepdive.title: Real-time media transport
deepdive.body: 說明任何製作中設備分為輸出、輸入、兩者兼具三類，全部須對齊統一格式才能透過 media router 即時交換。媒體格式由三個既有標準合成：串流 **ProRes** 影格（在畫質與頻寬間取得平衡，且 Apple Silicon 已最佳化）、承載高階 ambisonics 與 audio objects 的 PCM（即 ASAF）、每影格 JSON metadata（鏡頭校正、創意事件等）。傳輸採 **SMPTE 2110**：壓縮影像走 **2110-22**（左右眼為兩個獨立 essence 同包一 stream，免 frame packing）、ASAF 走 **2110-30**、JSON 走 **2110-41**。

deepdive.title: Recording and playback
deepdive.body: 傳統 2D 工作流程反覆編解碼會累積世代損失，對沉浸式體驗影響尤甚；但因沉浸式格式「全部已是 **ProRes**」，錄製到磁碟無需額外編解碼，同一批 ProRes 影格直接複製進 MOV 再讀回 2110 串流，全程不被觸碰、零品質損失。實務上一段內容可被攝影、傳輸、錄製、剪輯並反覆 live 播出而品質不變。播放時所有流程反向操作，從 MOV 各軌讀出影音與 metadata 再送回 2110 輸出。

deepdive.title: Set compression properties for vexu metadata
deepdive.body: 說明以 AVFoundation 的 **AVAssetWriter** 把影像寫入 QuickTime MOV 影像軌、PCM 音訊寫入音訊軌、JSON 寫入 **MEBX** metadata 軌。寫影像軌時要在 `AVVideoCompressionPropertiesKey` 設定新的 VideoToolbox 常數 **`kVTProjectionKind_AppleImmersiveVideo`**，為檔案加上正確的 **vexu** 靜態 metadata 將其標記為 immersive。JSON 須先反序列化解析後，以 visionOS 26 引入的 **Immersive Media Support（IMS）** 框架建立 lens calibration、camera ID 等物件並與影音同步寫入。

summary_en: Presented by Apple's Immersive Video Live Engineering team, this session is grounded in a milestone: Apple streamed select LA Lakers games live into Apple Vision Pro this year (via the Spectrum SportsNet and NBA apps), placing fans courtside with immersive cameras, data-driven graphics, and crowd-enveloping **spatial audio**. The speaker's goal is to inspire developers to build the next generation of immersive production tools, starting with a primer on the traditional live pipeline split into a **production domain** and a **delivery domain**, and the creative tools within it: cameras, graphics, replay, the video switcher, microphones, audio consoles, and the central **media router** that ties every device together.

He then explains how immersive live diverges from traditional 2D production. To match human visual acuity, video resolution is **32 times** that of a typical 2D broadcast and runs at twice the frame rate, while audio moves to **ASAF (Apple Spatial Audio Format)** mixes carrying 64 or more channels. These massive formats break traditional tools and transports, forcing an entirely rebuilt workflow. Three key concepts anchor it: a media format standard, a real-time transport method, and a record/playout mechanism.

The media format combines three existing standards: streamed **ProRes** frames for video (not uncompressed frames, and Apple Silicon is optimized for ProRes), uncompressed PCM carrying high-order ambisonics and spatial audio objects for ASAF, and per-frame JSON metadata describing lens calibrations, creative events, and spatial audio behavior. Transport rides on the industry-standard **SMPTE 2110**: compressed video as **2110-22** (left and right eye as two separate essences inside one stream, eliminating frame packing and dual-stream management), ASAF audio as **2110-30**, and JSON metadata as **2110-41**.

Recording and playback are core to any broadcast. Traditional 2D workflows accumulate generational loss through repeated encode/decode cycles, but the immersive format avoids this because everything is already **ProRes**: the same frames are copied straight into MOV files and read back into 2110 streams, untouched and lossless. In practice this is done with AVFoundation's **AVAssetWriter** for video, audio, and MEBX metadata tracks. When writing the video track, set the new VideoToolbox constant `kVTProjectionKind_AppleImmersiveVideo` in `AVVideoCompressionPropertiesKey` to add the correct vexu static metadata. The streamed JSON must be deserialized and parsed, then turned into lens calibration objects, camera IDs, and other metadata via the **Immersive Media Support (IMS)** framework introduced in visionOS 26, written in sync with the audio and video. Developers are encouraged to build their own tools with AVFoundation, VideoToolbox, AudioToolbox, and IMS, and to go deeper on SMPTE 2110 to wire tools into a real live workflow.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Jared King, who leads the Apple Immersive Video Live Engineering team, opens with this year's first live streaming of LA Lakers games into **Apple Vision Pro**, noting how immersive cameras gave fans unreachable seats, data-driven graphics augmented the action, and **spatial audio** placed viewers inside the roaring crowd. Behind it all was a live broadcast platform built by Apple. His stated goal is to inspire developers to build the next generation of immersive tools and live experiences.

deepdive_en.title: Live production overview
deepdive_en.body: He frames the overall pipeline: video, audio, and data are captured and creatively produced in the **production domain**, then encoded and streamed live to viewers in the **delivery domain**. Productions scale from TV studios and broadcast trucks to podcast studios and small venues, but the goal is the same — capture, produce, and transmit live content in real time. The session concentrates on what makes the production domain unique for immersive.

deepdive_en.title: What makes immersive live different
deepdive_en.body: He walks through the creative tools of a production workflow: multiple **live cameras** for different angles, **graphics** keyed over video (lower thirds, scoreboards), **replay** systems for recording and playout, and a **video switcher** for cutting between cameras and overlaying graphics into the final stream. On the audio side, microphones capture sources and **audio consoles** blend them into the final mix. Every tool exchanges signals through a central **media router** acting as a unified network layer.

deepdive_en.title: Immersive live format
deepdive_en.body: The divergence from 2D production hinges on fidelity and presence: video resolution is **32 times** that of a typical 2D broadcast and produced at twice the frame rate to match human visual acuity, while audio uses **ASAF** instead of stereo or 5.1, supporting **64 or more channels**. These massive formats and quality requirements mean traditional tools and transports can't keep up, so an entirely different workflow is required — distilled into format standard, real-time transport, and record/playback.

deepdive_en.title: Real-time media transport
deepdive_en.body: Every device falls into three classes — output, ingest, or both — and all must agree on a unified format to exchange content through the media router in real time. That format fuses three standards: streamed **ProRes** frames (balancing quality and bandwidth, with Apple Silicon optimized for ProRes), PCM carrying high-order ambisonics and audio objects (ASAF), and per-frame JSON metadata. Transport uses **SMPTE 2110**: compressed video as **2110-22** (left and right eye as two separate essences in one stream, no frame packing), ASAF as **2110-30**, and JSON as **2110-41**.

deepdive_en.title: Recording and playback
deepdive_en.body: Traditional 2D workflows lose quality through repeated encode/decode cycles, which compound as generational loss and hurt the immersive experience. Because the immersive format is already **ProRes** end to end, recording to disk needs no extra encode or decode — the same frames are copied directly into MOV files and read back into 2110 streams during playout, untouched. In practice, a clip can be captured, transported, recorded, edited, and replayed live on repeat with no quality impact. On playback every step is reversed: media types are read from their MOV tracks and retransmitted into 2110 output streams.

deepdive_en.title: Set compression properties for vexu metadata
deepdive_en.body: Video is written to QuickTime MOV video tracks with AVFoundation's **AVAssetWriter**, PCM audio into the audio tracks, and JSON into **MEBX** metadata tracks. When writing the video track, set the new VideoToolbox constant **`kVTProjectionKind_AppleImmersiveVideo`** in `AVVideoCompressionPropertiesKey` so the file gets the correct **vexu** static metadata signaling it as immersive. The streamed JSON must first be deserialized and parsed, then turned into lens calibration objects, camera IDs, and other metadata using the **Immersive Media Support (IMS)** framework introduced in visionOS 26, written in sync with the audio and video.

title: Bring an LLM provider to the Foundation Models framework

透過實作 **LanguageModel** 與 **LanguageModelExecutor** 協定，把新模型接入 Foundation Models 框架。
以 **prewarm／respond** 管理模型資源，並把 **Transcript** 條目對應成模型訊息。

audience: **想把自家或第三方 LLM 整合進 Apple Foundation Models 框架的開發者與模型供應商**。
gloss_en: Bring an LLM provider to the Foundation Models framework
takeaway_en: Implement LanguageModel and LanguageModelExecutor to bring your own or open-source LLMs into Foundation Models, streaming tokens, mapping the Transcript, handling errors, and supporting custom segments and server-side tools.

points_en.text: Choose from multiple model sources: on-device, **Private Cloud Compute**, Core AI, or open-source **MLX** models from HuggingFace.
Bring new models into the Foundation Models framework by implementing the **LanguageModel** and **LanguageModelExecutor** protocols.
Manage model resources with **prewarm / respond**, and map **Transcript** entries into model messages.
**Stream tokens and metadata** through a channel and report usage; throw a **LanguageModelError** when a request can't be satisfied.
Support **custom Transcript segments** and **server-side tools** (such as web search) to extend response content.

audience_en: **Developers and model providers who want to integrate their own or third-party LLMs into Apple's Foundation Models framework**.
summary: 這場由 Machine Learning Research 團隊的 Christopher Webb 主講，核心訊息是 **Foundation Models** 框架不再只服務 Apple 的內建模型，而是開放給「幾乎任何 LLM」——本地或伺服器端皆可。除了重新打造、更聰明且能直接吃影像的 **System Language Model**，框架還新增了具推理與 32K context 的 **Private Cloud Compute**、可吃 ANE 跑本地模型的 **Core AI**，以及解鎖 Hugging Face 上數千個社群模型的 **MLX**。關鍵在於這些都建立在一個全新的公開協定上，因此 Anthropic（Claude）與 Google（Gemini）很快也會以各自的 Swift package 擴充框架。對 app 開發者而言重點是：不論用哪個模型，呼叫方式完全一樣——只要換掉 model 物件即可。

對「模型提供者」而言，把模型帶進框架分成四步：**packaging、protocol、authentication、customization**。打包建議用 Swift Package Manager，並儘量支援 iOS／macOS／visionOS／watchOS（甚至因框架開源而支援 Linux），同時謹慎控制 dependencies，因為每個相依都是使用者要下載的位元組；發佈只需打一個 git tag。協定是模型與框架之間的橋樑，分兩塊：**`LanguageModel`** 描述模型（capabilities 與 executorConfiguration），**`LanguageModelExecutor`** 才是真正幹活的地方（init、prewarm、respond）。框架會用 model 提供的 **Configuration**（Hashable）作為查找鍵，在每個 session 的 executor store 中快取對應的 executor，相同 configuration 解析到同一個 executor。

executor 的工作是把對話 **Transcript**（六種 entry：instructions、prompt、toolCalls、toolOutput、response、reasoning 等）翻譯成模型原生的 message 格式，並從每個 request 讀出 **ContextOptions**（reasoning level、schema）與 **GenerationOptions**（sampling、temperature、最大 token 數）。回傳時透過 channel 串流事件，且有刻意的順序：先送 metadata（model／request ID 供 logging）、再送 usage（prompt token 計數），最後逐 token 送 textDelta 讓使用者看到逐字浮現。stateful 整合（KV cache 或持久連線）可比對新舊 transcript，只處理 append 的新內容，若 entry 被刪改則回退到分歧點。當模型無法滿足開發者意圖時，原則是「能近似就近似、不能就 throw」，框架提供內建 **`LanguageModelError`**（context 溢位、rate limit、refusal 等），僅在只有你的服務才會發生的失敗時才自訂 error。

authentication 部分強調讓開發者「容易做對的事」：別只收 API key 字串，改提供 token provider 或登入流程，並用 **Keychain** 安全保存 token；雲端模型還應做 **device attestation**（見「Secure your apps with App Attest」）。最後是 customization：可用 response metadata 附帶 tokensPerSecond 等資訊、用 **custom segments** 擴充協定支援新模態（如音訊），並為 web search、程式碼執行、圖片生成等 **server-side tools** 設計三種揭露層級——僅回傳答案、附帶 citation metadata，或透過 custom segment 把工具的結構化產出整個攤給 app。講者也提醒，鏈上每個人都要清楚模型的隱私特性（on-device 與 cloud 差異極大）。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: 由 Machine Learning Research 團隊工程師 Christopher Webb 開場，宣布 **Foundation Models** 框架從只提供 Apple 內建模型，擴大到能搭配「幾乎任何 LLM」，本地或伺服器端皆可。內建 **System Language Model** 已重新打造，更聰明、更擅長指令遵循、並能直接在 prompt 吃影像。另新增 **Private Cloud Compute**（含推理與 32K context）、可用 ANE 的 **Core AI**、以及解鎖 Hugging Face 社群模型的 **MLX**。

deepdive.title: Choose a language model
deepdive.body: 因為這些選項都建立在全新的公開協定上，開發者能用同一套框架引進前沿模型；**Anthropic 的 Claude** 與 **Google 的 Gemini** 很快會以各自的 Swift package 擴充框架。預覽顯示用法極簡：建立 on-device model、傳進 session、呼叫 respond；要更多算力換成 **Private Cloud Compute**、要出貨自家模型把 **Core AI** 指向資源、要試開源模型則傳入 model ID。所有模型都遵循同一個 **LanguageModel** 協定，因此能輕易互換並取得 Dynamic Profiles 等功能。

deepdive.title: Packaging
deepdive.body: 把模型帶進框架共四步：**packaging、protocol、authentication、customization**。本段先談打包——一個精心設計的 Swift package 能讓開發者輕鬆上手。

deepdive.title: Configure Package.swift for your model package
deepdive.body: 建議用 **Swift Package Manager**，讓開發者把你的 package 直接加為 app 的相依。要考慮支援哪些平台——框架支援 iOS／macOS／visionOS／watchOS，建議比照辦理，且因框架開源也可考慮支援 **Linux**（伺服器端 Swift）。每個 **dependency** 都是使用者要下載的位元組，務必謹慎；發佈只需建立一個 **git tag**，因 SPM 去中心化，你的 repo URL 就是發行管道。

deepdive.title: Protocol
deepdive.body: 協定是你的模型與 Foundation Models 框架之間的橋樑，是把模型接進來的核心步驟。

deepdive.title: LanguageModel and LanguageModelExecutor protocols
deepdive.body: 協定分兩塊：**`LanguageModel`** 向框架描述模型——透過 capabilities 宣告能力，並提供框架建立 executor 所需的 configuration；**`LanguageModelExecutor`** 是真正幹活的地方，有吃 Configuration 的 init、用於事先準備資源的 prewarm，以及把生成串流回 session 的 respond。**Configuration** 是連接兩者的關鍵：Model 提供它、框架用它來建構 executor。

deepdive.title: Implement LanguageModel and Executor conformances
deepdive.body: 每個 session 持有一個 **executor store**：當 Model 到來，框架用其 configuration 查 store，沒有對應的 executor 就新建並存入。因 **Configuration 是 Hashable**，相同 configuration 會解析到同一個 executor，不同的則各有一個——查找鍵是 configuration 而非 model。程式上 LanguageModel 宣告 capabilities 並回傳 configuration，executor 才負責載入權重、管理資源與串流 token；session 釋放時 store 連同所有 executor 自動釋放、deinit 執行、權重釋放、連線關閉，開發者無需自寫拆解程式。

deepdive.title: Manage model resources with prewarm and respond
deepdive.body: executor 還有 **prewarm**：在 request 抵達前，開發者可請框架預熱，讓你預先做昂貴設定（載入權重、開啟連線）以免拖慢首個回應。一種作法是把設定放進一個只載入一次並快取的私有 helper，prewarm 提前呼叫它；但 **prewarm 不保證執行**，無論如何權重都只載入一次，而像伺服器後端這種無昂貴設定的模型，prewarm 可直接是 no-op。

deepdive.title: Map Transcript entries to model messages
deepdive.body: respond 被呼叫時，executor 居中把 **Transcript**（至今的對話，由一連串 entry 組成）翻譯成推論引擎能讀的原生 message，回傳時再反向翻譯串回 session。Foundation Models 定義六種 entry 類型，模型則有自己的 role；executor 的工作就是兩者間映射，例如把 instructions／prompt／response 對到 system／user／assistant，把 toolCalls、toolOutput、reasoning 都對到 assistant（若模型有專屬 tool role 也可改路由過去）。

deepdive.title: Read generation and context options from the request
deepdive.body: 每個 request 除了歷史，還帶有開發者對「該如何回應」的意圖，由兩個屬性表達：**ContextOptions** 控制進到 prompt 的內容（如 reasoning level 或 response schema），**GenerationOptions** 控制解碼迴圈（sampling 策略、temperature、最大回應長度）。在 respond 內把兩種 options 從 request 取出，於呼叫模型時一併傳入。

deepdive.title: Stream tokens and metadata through the channel
deepdive.body: 回應端透過 channel 送出事件，每個 chunk（token 或 tool-call 片段）成為一個 textDelta、toolCallDelta 等事件，框架寫入 transcript；一次性與串流 API 都以串流實作，one-shot 只是內部收集 deltas。順序是刻意的：先送 **metadata**（model／request ID 供 logging 與除錯）、再送 **usage**（prompt token 計數供計費），最後每產生一個 token 就立刻送 **textDelta**，讓使用者看到回應逐字浮現而非一次全出。

deepdive.title: Honor the developer's intent or throw
deepdive.body: stateful 整合（持有 KV cache 或持久 session）能靠框架依 configuration 快取 executor 來保存跨呼叫的工作。executor 每次都收到完整 transcript，可比對新舊：多半只是 append 了新 entry，便可保留既有狀態只處理新增；若發現 entry 被刪改（如開發者裁修舊內容），則回退到分歧點重算。當模型無法完全照辦時——能近似就近似、honor 開發者意圖，無法時就 **throw**（例如 token 預算太小無法滿足 schema 的必填欄位）。

deepdive.title: Built-in errors that any model can throw
deepdive.body: Foundation Models 提供內建的 **`LanguageModelError`** 涵蓋常見情況：context window 溢位、rate limit、refusal、guardrail violation、unsupportedCapability、unsupportedTranscriptContent、timeout 等。丟出其中之一，任何用過框架的開發者都已知道如何處理。

deepdive.title: Handle errors from your model executor
deepdive.body: 當內建錯誤不夠用時可自訂 error 類型——有些失敗只在你的服務情境中才有意義（訂閱層級、帳號狀態、功能授權），有意義的 case 名稱能讓開發者一接到就明白發生什麼。但每個自訂錯誤都是開發者要額外學習、catch、處理的負擔，因此能用內建 **LanguageModelError** 就優先用，自訂留給只有你的服務才會產生的失敗。

deepdive.title: Authentication
deepdive.body: 你身為 package 作者的任務是讓開發者「容易做對的事」。若 init 只收 API key 字串，開發者會走捷徑；應改提供 **token provider 或登入流程**。若你的 package 代開發者取得 access token，務必用 **Keychain** 安全保存。憑證只是一半，另一半是 **device attestation**——若要出貨雲端模型 package，建議深入「Secure your apps with App Attest」，了解驗證裝置、攔截被竄改的 build、簽署 payload 與運用 Apple 詐欺訊號。

deepdive.title: Customization
deepdive.body: 完成打包、協定、authentication 後就有了基礎扎實的 package，接著是差異化。協定保留空間讓你圍繞只有你的模型才有的能力來形塑 **LanguageModelSession**——從附加 response metadata，一路到定義全新的模態。

deepdive.title: Attach custom metadata to responses
deepdive.body: **Response metadata** 是輕量選項，可在回應上附加額外資訊並給開發者清楚的存取方式。範例中串流結束後 executor 透過 channel 送出 **tokensPerSecond** 與 **timeToFirstToken**。底層 metadata 就是個字典，可裝字串、數字等內建型別；建議提供工具或文件（清楚的 key、typed accessor）讓開發者好用。

deepdive.title: Define and use custom Transcript segments
deepdive.body: 當需要比字典更有彈性時，**custom segments** 是答案：定義新的 segment 型別、在 executor 接收、再經同一條 channel 串回結果，開發者全程不必離開 LanguageModelSession。因 custom segment 須符合 **PromptRepresentable**，開發者能像文字一樣直接放進 prompt（範例為 `AudioSegment`）；segment ID 決定你是新增 segment 還是更新一個已開始串流的 segment，讓你完全掌控結果如何串入 app。這也是新模態（音訊、影片）進來時的 typed、結構化途徑。

deepdive.title: Implement server-side tools in your model
deepdive.body: **Server-side tools** 是模型自行執行的能力（web search、程式碼執行、圖片生成）：開發者建構模型時帶入想要的工具，executor 每次 request 都透過 model 收到。揭露分三層：最簡單是私下執行工具、只把答案串回（工具痕跡留在 executor 內）；其次是讓 text delta 帶上 metadata（如 citation），與文字一併 forward；最完整是用 **custom segment** 把工具的結構化產出整個攤給 app。透過這一條 channel，你 forward 的事件、附加的 metadata 與設計的 custom segment，共同決定使用你 package 的 app 能向使用者呈現什麼。

deepdive.title: Next steps
