deepdive.body: 提醒鏈上每個人都要清楚模型背後的隱私特性——**on-device 與 cloud 模型的隱私特性截然不同**，使用者有權知道用的是哪一種。並推薦延伸 session：「Integrate On-Device AI Models into Your App Using Core AI」、「Build with the new Apple Foundation Model on Private Cloud Compute」、「Build agentic app experiences with the Foundation Models framework」。講者期待看到蓬勃的 LanguageModel package 生態。

summary_en: Presented by Christopher Webb of the Machine Learning Research team, the core message is that the **Foundation Models** framework no longer serves only Apple's built-in model — it now works with nearly any LLM, local or server-based. Beyond a rebuilt **System Language Model** that's smarter, better at instruction following, and accepts images directly in prompts, the framework adds **Private Cloud Compute** (with reasoning and a 32K context window), **Core AI** for running local models efficiently on the ANE, and **MLX** to unlock thousands of community models on Hugging Face. Because all of these are built on a brand-new public protocol, Anthropic (Claude) and Google (Gemini) will soon extend the framework with their own Swift packages. For app developers the key point is that whichever model you use, you call it the same way — you just swap the model object.

For model providers, bringing a model into the framework takes four steps: **packaging, protocol, authentication, and customization**. Packaging is done with Swift Package Manager, ideally supporting iOS/macOS/visionOS/watchOS (and even Linux since the framework is open source), while keeping dependencies minimal because every dependency is bytes shipped to users; publishing is just a git tag. The protocol is the bridge and has two pieces: **`LanguageModel`** describes the model (capabilities and executorConfiguration), while **`LanguageModelExecutor`** does the real work (init, prewarm, respond). The framework uses the model's **Configuration** (which is Hashable) as a lookup key to cache an executor per configuration in each session's executor store, so the same configuration resolves to the same executor.

The executor's job is to translate the conversation **Transcript** (six entry types: instructions, prompt, toolCalls, toolOutput, response, reasoning) into the model's native message format, and to read **ContextOptions** (reasoning level, schema) and **GenerationOptions** (sampling, temperature, max tokens) from each request. Responses stream back through a channel in a deliberate order: first metadata (model/request IDs for logging), then usage (prompt token counts), then per-token textDeltas so users see the response appear word-by-word. Stateful integrations (holding a KV cache or persistent connection) can diff the new transcript against the saved one and process only appended entries, invalidating back to the divergence point if entries were removed or modified. When the model can't satisfy the developer's intent, the rule is approximate where you can and otherwise throw, using the built-in **`LanguageModelError`** (context overflow, rate limits, refusals, and more), reserving custom errors for failures only your service can produce.

On authentication, the emphasis is making it easy for developers to do the right thing: don't take a bare API key string — offer a token provider or sign-in flow, and persist tokens securely with **Keychain**; cloud models should also do **device attestation** (see "Secure your apps with App Attest"). Finally, customization: attach response metadata such as tokensPerSecond, use **custom segments** to extend the protocol for new modalities like audio, and design **server-side tools** (web search, code execution, image generation) with three levels of disclosure — return only the answer, attach citation metadata, or surface the tool's structured output via a custom segment. The speaker also stresses that everyone in the chain should understand the privacy characteristics of the model behind a package, since on-device and cloud models differ greatly.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Christopher Webb, an engineer on the Machine Learning Research team, opens by announcing that the **Foundation Models** framework now works with nearly any LLM, local or server-based, instead of only Apple's built-in model. The on-device **System Language Model** has been rebuilt to be smarter, better at instruction following, and able to accept images directly in prompts. Three more options join it: **Private Cloud Compute** (with reasoning and a 32K context window), **Core AI** to run local models on the ANE, and **MLX** to unlock community models on Hugging Face.

deepdive_en.title: Choose a language model
deepdive_en.body: Because these options are built on a brand-new public protocol, developers can bring frontier models into their apps with the same framework, and **Anthropic's Claude** and **Google's Gemini** will soon extend it with their own Swift packages. A preview shows how simple usage is: create an on-device model, pass it into a session, call respond; swap to **Private Cloud Compute** for more horsepower, point **Core AI** at your resources to ship your own model, or pass a model ID to try open-source models. Every model conforms to the same **LanguageModel** protocol, so models swap easily and unlock features like Dynamic Profiles.

deepdive_en.title: Packaging
deepdive_en.body: Bringing a model into the framework takes four steps: **packaging, protocol, authentication, and customization**. This section starts with packaging — a well-crafted Swift package makes it easy for developers to get started.

deepdive_en.title: Configure Package.swift for your model package
deepdive_en.body: Use **Swift Package Manager** so developers can add your package as a dependency. Decide which platforms to support — the framework supports iOS/macOS/visionOS/watchOS, and you should do the same, with **Linux** worth considering since the framework is open source and useful for server-side Swift. Every **dependency** is bytes shipped to users, so choose carefully; publishing is as easy as creating a **git tag**, and because SPM is decentralized your repo URL is your distribution channel.

deepdive_en.title: Protocol
deepdive_en.body: The protocol is the bridge between your model and the Foundation Models framework, and is the core step in connecting a model into it.

deepdive_en.title: LanguageModel and LanguageModelExecutor protocols
deepdive_en.body: The protocol has two pieces: **`LanguageModel`** describes the model to the framework — declaring what it can do via capabilities and providing the configuration the framework needs to set up the executor — while **`LanguageModelExecutor`** is where the work happens, with an init that takes a Configuration, a prewarm for preparing resources ahead of time, and a respond that streams generation back to the session. The **Configuration** is the link between the two: the Model provides it and the framework uses it to construct the executor.

deepdive_en.title: Implement LanguageModel and Executor conformances
deepdive_en.body: Each session holds an **executor store**: when a Model arrives, the framework checks the store by its configuration and, if there's no match, creates and stores a new executor. Because **Configuration is Hashable**, the same configuration resolves to the same executor while a different one gets its own — the lookup key is the configuration, not the model. In code, LanguageModel declares capabilities and returns a configuration, while the executor loads weights, manages resources, and streams tokens; when the session deallocates, the store and every stored executor are released automatically, with deinit running, weights freed, and connections closed — no teardown code needed.

deepdive_en.title: Manage model resources with prewarm and respond
deepdive_en.body: The executor also has **prewarm**: before a request arrives, the developer can ask the framework to prewarm so you can do expensive setup (loading weights, opening connections) ahead of the first response. One approach puts that setup in a private helper that loads weights once and caches them, with prewarm calling it eagerly; but **prewarm isn't guaranteed to run**, weights load exactly once either way, and for a server-backed model with no expensive setup prewarm can simply be a no-op.

deepdive_en.title: Map Transcript entries to model messages
deepdive_en.body: When respond is called, the executor sits in the middle, translating the **Transcript** (the conversation so far, a sequence of entries) into messages your inference engine understands, then running the same translation in reverse to stream back to the session. Foundation Models defines six entry types and your model defines its own roles; the executor maps between them — for example instructions/prompt/response to system/user/assistant, and toolCalls, toolOutput, and reasoning all to assistant (routing to a dedicated tool role instead if your model has one).

deepdive_en.title: Read generation and context options from the request
deepdive_en.body: Beyond history, every request carries the developer's intent for how the model should respond via two properties: **ContextOptions** control what goes into the prompt (like reasoning level or a response schema), and **GenerationOptions** control the decoder loop (sampling strategy, temperature, maximum response length). Inside respond you pull both out of the request and pass them along when calling the model.

deepdive_en.title: Stream tokens and metadata through the channel
deepdive_en.body: On the response side, each chunk the inference engine emits (a token or tool-call fragment) becomes an event — a textDelta, a toolCallDelta — which the framework writes to the transcript; both one-shot and streaming APIs are implemented as streaming, with one-shot just collecting deltas internally. The order is deliberate: first a **metadata** update (model and request IDs for logging and debugging), then a **usage** update (prompt token counts for accounting), then a **textDelta** the moment each token arrives so users see the response appear word-by-word rather than all at once.

deepdive_en.title: Honor the developer's intent or throw
deepdive_en.body: Stateful integrations (holding a KV cache or persistent session) can preserve work across calls thanks to the framework caching executors by configuration. The executor receives the full transcript every call and diffs new against saved: usually entries are just appended, so you keep existing state and process only the new; if entries were removed or modified (e.g., the developer trims older context) you invalidate back to where they diverge. When the model can't do exactly what's asked, approximate and honor the intent where possible, and otherwise **throw** (for example when the token budget is too small to satisfy a schema's required fields).

deepdive_en.title: Built-in errors that any model can throw
deepdive_en.body: Foundation Models ships a built-in **`LanguageModelError`** covering common cases: context window overflows, rate limits, refusals, guardrail violations, unsupportedCapability, unsupportedTranscriptContent, timeouts, and more. Throw one of these and any developer who's used the framework already knows how to handle it.

deepdive_en.title: Handle errors from your model executor
deepdive_en.body: When the built-in cases don't cover your situation, define your own error type — some failures only make sense in your service's context (subscription tiers, account states, feature provisioning), and a purpose-built case name carries the intent so a developer catching it knows exactly what happened. But each custom error is a new case developers must learn, catch, and handle, so prefer a built-in **LanguageModelError** when it fits and save custom ones for failures only your service can produce.

deepdive_en.title: Authentication
deepdive_en.body: As a package author your job is to make it easy for developers to do the right thing. If your initializer takes an API key string, developers take the path of least resistance, so offer a **token provider or sign-in flow** instead. If your package fetches access tokens on developers' behalf, persist them securely with **Keychain**. Credentials are half the story; the other half is **device attestation** — if you ship a cloud-based model package, dig into "Secure your apps with App Attest" to verify the device, catch tampered builds, sign payloads, and use Apple's fraud signal.

deepdive_en.title: Customization
deepdive_en.body: Having packaged the model, implemented the protocol, and handled authentication, you have a solid package with the fundamentals covered — now it's time to differentiate. The protocol gives you room to shape **LanguageModelSession** around abilities only your model offers, from attaching response metadata all the way to defining entirely new modalities.

deepdive_en.title: Attach custom metadata to responses
deepdive_en.body: **Response metadata** is a lightweight way to attach extra information to responses and give developers clear ways to access it. In the example, after streaming completes the executor sends **tokensPerSecond** and **timeToFirstToken** through the channel. Underneath, metadata is just a dictionary of strings, numbers, and other built-in types, and you should provide utilities or documentation — clear keys, typed accessors — to make it easy to work with.

deepdive_en.title: Define and use custom Transcript segments
deepdive_en.body: When you need more flexibility than a dictionary, **custom segments** are the answer: define a new segment type, receive it in the executor, and stream results back through the same channel, with the developer never leaving LanguageModelSession. Because custom segments must be **PromptRepresentable**, developers can pass them directly in prompts just like text (the example is an `AudioSegment`); the segment ID controls whether you're adding a new segment or updating one you've already started streaming, giving full control over how results stream into the app — and a typed, structured path for new modalities like audio or video.

deepdive_en.title: Implement server-side tools in your model
deepdive_en.body: **Server-side tools** are capabilities the model runs itself (web search, code execution, image generation): the developer constructs the model with the tools they want and the executor receives them through the model on every request. Disclosure comes in three levels — run the tool privately and stream only the answer (its work stays inside the executor), or attach metadata like a citation to a text delta and forward both, or surface the tool's structured output via a **custom segment**. Through this one channel, the events you forward, the metadata you attach, and the custom segments you design shape what apps using your package can show their users.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: A final reminder that everyone in the chain should understand the privacy implications of the model behind a package — **on-device and cloud models have very different privacy characteristics**, and users deserve to know which they're getting. The talk points to follow-up sessions: "Integrate On-Device AI Models into Your App Using Core AI," "Build with the new Apple Foundation Model on Private Cloud Compute," and "Build agentic app experiences with the Foundation Models framework," closing with hope for a thriving ecosystem of LanguageModel packages.

title: Support the Center Stage front camera in your iOS app
gloss: 在 iOS App 中支援人物居中前置鏡頭
takeaway: 用 AVCapture 的動態長寬比與智慧取景 API，讓你的相機 App 支援 iPhone 17 等機型的 Center Stage 前置鏡頭。
chapters: Support Center Stage for video calls

points.text: 在 iPhone 17、iPhone 17 Pro 與 iPhone Air 上，以 **builtInUltraWideCamera** 前置鏡頭支援 Center Stage 拍照。
用 **supportedDynamicAspectRatios** 與 **setDynamicAspectRatio** 在拍攝中切換 4:3 等**動態長寬比**。
透過 **smartFramingMonitor** 觀察 **recommendedFraming**，自動調整長寬比與 **videoZoomFactor** 完成智慧取景。
需處理**感光元件方向補償（sensor orientation compensation）**，確保畫面方向正確。
錄影與視訊通話情境可用 **centerStageControlMode = .cooperative** 與 **isCenterStageEnabled** 開啟 Center Stage。

audience: 開發 **iOS 相機或視訊 App、想支援前置鏡頭 Center Stage 與智慧取景**的開發者。
gloss_en: Support the Center Stage front camera in your iOS app
takeaway_en: Use AVCapture's dynamic aspect ratio and smart framing APIs to support the Center Stage front camera on devices like iPhone 17 in your camera app.

points_en.text: On iPhone 17, iPhone 17 Pro, and iPhone Air, support Center Stage photo capture with the **builtInUltraWideCamera** front camera.
Use **supportedDynamicAspectRatios** and **setDynamicAspectRatio** to switch **dynamic aspect ratios** like 4:3 during capture.
Observe **recommendedFraming** via **smartFramingMonitor** to automatically adjust the aspect ratio and **videoZoomFactor** for smart framing.
Handle **sensor orientation compensation** to ensure the image is oriented correctly.
For video recording and video calling, enable Center Stage with **centerStageControlMode = .cooperative** and **isCenterStageEnabled**.

audience_en: Developers building **iOS camera or video apps who want to support front-camera Center Stage and smart framing**.
summary: iPhone 17、iPhone Air 與 iPhone 17 Pro 上的 **Center Stage 前置鏡頭**徹底改變了自拍與視訊通話的取景方式。傳統前鏡頭感光元件是 4x3 比例，框景會受手機方向限制；新的前鏡頭改採**正方形感光元件**搭配 **95 度超廣角鏡頭**（iPhone 前鏡頭史上最廣），讓你不用旋轉手機就能拍出直幅或橫幅自拍，握持更穩、視線接觸也更自然。本場以 **AVCapture** API 為主軸，示範如何在自己的 app 裡支援這顆鏡頭的照片、錄影與視訊通話體驗。

照片取景的核心是 **Auto Zoom 與 Auto Rotate**，由兩個 API 組成。基礎是 iOS 26 新增的 **dynamicAspectRatio**：在不重建 capture session、不中斷預覽的前提下，從正方形感光元件即時裁切出你要的比例（支援 3x4、4x3、9x16、16x9、1x1），可用來實作「點一下旋轉」按鈕。建立在它之上的是 **AVCaptureSmartFramingMonitor**，會依臉部與視線偵測週期性給出含 aspectRatio 與 zoomFactor 的取景建議，app 透過 KVO 觀察 `recommendedFraming` 後套用，達成有人加入或離開鏡頭時自動縮放與旋轉；此監視器僅在 4032 照片格式下提供建議。鏡頭選取一律使用 `.builtInUltraWideCamera`、`.front` 的 discovery session。

照片部分還需注意**感光元件方向補償**：新前鏡頭改以 Portrait 方向安裝，與過去的 Landscape Left 不同。**AVCapturePhotoOutput** 預設會自動旋轉照片並更新 EXIF，讓輸出與舊機種一致，因此沿用既有旋轉值即可；但補償只套用於 HEIC、JPEG 與未壓縮處理過的照片，永遠不套用於 Bayer RAW 或 Apple ProRAW，且可用 `cameraSensorOrientationCompensationEnabled` 控制（建議測試關閉以求最佳效能）。

錄影與視訊通話同樣受惠。錄影可用 dynamicAspectRatio「點一下旋轉」，但因 QuickTime 軌道要求所有 sample 尺寸一致，改變比例時會自動停止錄影（改用 **AVCaptureVideoDataOutput** 搭 **AVAssetWriter** 可用完成 timestamp 無縫接續），並支援臉部感知的 **cinematicExtended** 穩定模式。視訊通話方面，若 app 已使用 VoIP 背景模式則自動支援 Center Stage；否則可採用 Center Stage API，先設定 `centerStageControlMode`（cooperative 或 app）再開啟 `isCenterStageEnabled`，並可把 AVCaptureConnection 的 `preferredVideoStabilizationMode` 設為 `lowLatency` 取得即時低延遲穩定。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: 由 Camera Software 團隊工程師 Tracy 開場，點出自拍取景的痛點（自拍棒、找手臂長的朋友幫忙）。**Center Stage 前置鏡頭**搭載於 iPhone 17、iPhone Air 與 iPhone 17 Pro，能更彈性地框住畫面。全場路線為：先總覽鏡頭特性，再講照片、錄影與視訊通話三種情境的 API。

deepdive.title: Center Stage front camera
deepdive.body: 說明硬體本質：傳統前鏡頭是 **4x3 感光元件**，框景受手機方向限制；新鏡頭改用**正方形感光元件**，可自由選任意比例，直幅或橫幅自拍都不必旋轉手機，握持更穩、視線更自然。再搭配 **95 度超廣角鏡頭**（iPhone 前鏡頭最廣視野），有利於團體自拍、影片穩定與通話置中。

deepdive.title: Center Stage for photos
deepdive.body: 進入照片取景主題，核心是 **Auto Zoom 與 Auto Rotate**：結合正方形感光元件、廣角與自動臉部／視線偵測，鏡頭會智慧調整方向並在窄景與廣景間切換。以實例示範朋友 Karen 加入時畫面自動拉遠、更多人入鏡時自動旋轉，並預告接下來會講 capture session 設定、dynamic aspect ratio 與 smart framing monitor 兩個 API，最後是感光元件方向補償。

deepdive.title: Capture session setup
deepdive.body: 說明典型照片拍攝設定：建立 **AVCaptureSession**，以 `.builtInUltraWideCamera` 取得前鏡頭並建立 **AVCaptureDeviceInput**，加入 **AVCaptureVideoPreviewLayer** 取得預覽、加入 **AVCapturePhotoOutput** 接收照片。加入 input/output 時 session 會在相容媒體型別間隱含建立 **AVCaptureConnection**。

deepdive.title: Dynamic aspect ratio
deepdive.body: 介紹 iOS 26 新增的 **dynamicAspectRatio** 屬性，是手動與自動取景的共同基礎：設定後相機直接從正方形感光元件裁切出指定比例，不必重建 session 或中斷預覽，切換無縫快速。支援格式須為前置 `.builtInUltraWideCamera` 的正方形格式，解析度 1280 至 4032，提供 3x4、4x3、9x16、16x9、1x1 五種比例；其中 4032 照片格式只支援 3x4 與 4x3 以取得最高解析度。

deepdive.title: Support dynamic aspect ratio
deepdive.body: 以「點一下旋轉」按鈕示範實作：用 **AVCaptureDevice.DiscoverySession** 指定 `.builtInUltraWideCamera` 與 `.front` 取得唯一裝置，遍歷 `format.supportedDynamicAspectRatios` 找到支援 4x3 的格式並設為 `activeFormat`。鎖定設定後呼叫 `setDynamicAspectRatio(.ratio4x3)`，回傳值為變更生效的第一個 buffer **timestamp**。

deepdive.title: Smart framing monitor
deepdive.body: 介紹 iOS 26 的 **AVCaptureSmartFramingMonitor**，與 dynamicAspectRatio 協作，依自動臉部與視線偵測週期性提供取景建議。每筆建議含 **aspectRatio 與 zoomFactor**，app 可套用或忽略；由於專為照片拍攝設計，僅在 **4032 照片格式**下提供建議。

deepdive.title: Support smart framing monitor
deepdive.body: 示範監視器設定流程：找到同時支援目標比例與 smart framing 的格式並設為 activeFormat，取得 `smartFramingMonitor` 並把 `enabledFramings` 設為 `supportedFramings`（也可只取子集，如 4x3 的窄／廣兩種）。接著以 **KVO** 觀察 `recommendedFraming`，於回呼中先設 aspectRatio 再設 zoomFactor 以求預覽平滑過渡，可隨時 `startMonitoring`；關閉自動取景時則註銷觀察並 `stopMonitoring`。

deepdive.title: Sensor orientation compensation
deepdive.body: 說明方向差異：過去前鏡頭感光元件以 Landscape Left 安裝，直拍照片會帶 EXIF 旋轉 270 度標記；新鏡頭改以 **Portrait 方向**安裝，若沿用舊旋轉值照片可能歪斜。**AVCapturePhotoOutput** 預設自動補償（實體旋轉並更新 EXIF，輸出維持 landscape left），但僅套用於 **HEIC、JPEG 與未壓縮處理照片**，絕不套用於 Bayer RAW 或 Apple ProRAW，並可用 `cameraSensorOrientationCompensationEnabled` 控制，建議測試關閉以求效能。

deepdive.title: Center Stage for video recordings
deepdive.body: 錄影同樣可用 dynamicAspectRatio「點一下旋轉」，但 QuickTime 軌道要求所有 sample 尺寸一致，故改變比例時錄影會自動停止。用 **AVCaptureMovieFileOutput** 時會自動停錄；用 **AVCaptureVideoDataOutput** 搭 **AVAssetWriter** 則可用 `setDynamicAspectRatio` 的完成 timestamp 結束目前錄影並以新比例接續。錄影也受惠於臉部感知的 **cinematicExtended** 與 **cinematicExtendedEnhanced** 穩定模式。

deepdive.title: Center Stage for video calls
deepdive.body: 以 FaceTime 為例示範朋友加入時鏡頭自動拉廣納入兩人。若 app 使用 **VoIP 背景模式**，Center Stage 已自動支援，使用者可從控制中心的視訊效果直接開啟；如同 Portrait、Studio Light 等系統視訊效果，Center Stage 是以行程為單位啟用，啟用後套用到 app 內任何支援的鏡頭。

deepdive.title: Support Center Stage for video calls
deepdive.body: 說明未用 VoIP 背景模式時如何採用 Center Stage API：視訊通話通常用 video data output 串流取得 buffer，先找支援格式並設為 active format，再設定 `centerStageControlMode`（**cooperative** 讓 app 內按鈕也能控制，或 **app**），最後設 `isCenterStageEnabled = true`。另介紹 iOS 26 的即時低延遲穩定，把 AVCaptureConnection 的 `preferredVideoStabilizationMode` 設為 **lowLatency** 即可，預設為關閉。

summary_en: The **Center Stage front camera** on iPhone 17, iPhone Air, and iPhone 17 Pro changes how people take selfies and make video calls. Traditional front sensors are 4x3, so framing depends on phone orientation; the new camera uses a **square image sensor** paired with a **95-degree wide lens** (the widest on any iPhone front camera), letting you shoot portrait or landscape selfies without rotating the phone, with a more secure grip and more natural eye contact. The session walks through the **AVCapture** APIs to support this camera for photos, video recordings, and video calls.

Photo framing centers on **Auto Zoom and Auto Rotate**, built from two APIs. The foundation is iOS 26's **dynamicAspectRatio**: it crops your chosen ratio (3x4, 4x3, 9x16, 16x9, 1x1) out of the square sensor without rebuilding the session or interrupting preview, ideal for a Tap to Rotate button. On top of that sits **AVCaptureSmartFramingMonitor**, which uses face and gaze detection to periodically recommend a framing (aspectRatio plus zoomFactor); the app key-value observes `recommendedFraming` and applies it to auto-zoom and auto-rotate as people enter or leave the shot. The monitor only provides recommendations on the 4032 photo format, and the camera is always selected via a `.builtInUltraWideCamera`, `.front` discovery session.

Photos also require **sensor orientation compensation**: the new front sensor is mounted in Portrait rather than the old Landscape Left. **AVCapturePhotoOutput** automatically rotates photos and updates EXIF by default so output matches older devices, letting you keep your existing rotation values. Compensation applies only to HEIC, JPEG, and uncompressed processed photos, never to Bayer RAW or Apple ProRAW, and can be controlled via `cameraSensorOrientationCompensationEnabled` (test with it off for best performance).

Recordings and video calls benefit too. Recording supports Tap to Rotate via dynamicAspectRatio, but since QuickTime tracks require uniform sample dimensions, changing the ratio stops recording automatically (use **AVCaptureVideoDataOutput** with **AVAssetWriter** plus the completion timestamp to stitch segments seamlessly), and face-aware **cinematicExtended** stabilization is available. For video calls, apps using the VoIP background mode get Center Stage automatically; otherwise adopt the Center Stage API by setting `centerStageControlMode` (cooperative or app) then `isCenterStageEnabled`, and set the AVCaptureConnection's `preferredVideoStabilizationMode` to `lowLatency` for real-time low-latency stabilization.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Tracy, an engineer on the Camera Software team, opens by naming the pain of selfie framing (selfie sticks, friends with long arms). The **Center Stage front camera** on iPhone 17, iPhone Air, and iPhone 17 Pro gives more flexibility in framing. The roadmap: overview the camera, then cover the APIs for photos, video recordings, and video calls.

deepdive_en.title: Center Stage front camera
deepdive_en.body: Explains the hardware: traditional front cameras use a **4x3 sensor** whose framing is constrained by phone orientation, while the new camera has a **square image sensor** that lets you pick any aspect ratio, shooting portrait or landscape without rotating the phone for a more secure one-handed grip and natural eye contact. It is paired with a **95-degree field-of-view lens** (the widest of any iPhone front camera), helping with group selfies, video stabilization, and staying centered on calls.

deepdive_en.title: Center Stage for photos
deepdive_en.body: Begins the photo topic, where the key feature is **Auto Zoom and Auto Rotate**: combining the square sensor, wide field of view, and automatic face and gaze detection, the camera adapts its orientation and switches between narrow and wide views. A live demo shows the frame zooming out as Karen joins and rotating as more friends enter, then previews the agenda: capture session setup, the dynamic aspect ratio and smart framing monitor APIs, and finally sensor orientation compensation.

deepdive_en.title: Capture session setup
deepdive_en.body: Walks through a typical photo setup: create an **AVCaptureSession**, find the front camera via `.builtInUltraWideCamera` and create an **AVCaptureDeviceInput**, add an **AVCaptureVideoPreviewLayer** for preview and an **AVCapturePhotoOutput** to receive photos. As inputs and outputs are added, the session implicitly forms **AVCaptureConnections** between compatible media types.

deepdive_en.title: Dynamic aspect ratio
deepdive_en.body: Introduces iOS 26's **dynamicAspectRatio** property, the building block for both manual and automatic framing: setting it crops the chosen ratio out of the square sensor without rebuilding the session or interrupting preview, making the switch seamless and quick. Supported formats require the front `.builtInUltraWideCamera`, are square, span resolutions 1280 to 4032, and offer five ratios (3x4, 4x3, 9x16, 16x9, 1x1); the 4032 photo format only supports 3x4 and 4x3 for the highest photo resolution.

deepdive_en.title: Support dynamic aspect ratio
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates implementing a Tap to Rotate button: use an **AVCaptureDevice.DiscoverySession** with `.builtInUltraWideCamera` and `.front` to get the single device, iterate `format.supportedDynamicAspectRatios` to find a 4x3 format, and set it as `activeFormat`. After locking for configuration, call `setDynamicAspectRatio(.ratio4x3)`, which returns the **timestamp** of the first buffer where the change takes effect.

deepdive_en.title: Smart framing monitor
deepdive_en.body: Introduces iOS 26's **AVCaptureSmartFramingMonitor**, which works alongside dynamicAspectRatio to give periodic framing recommendations based on automatic face and gaze detection. Each recommendation contains an **aspectRatio and a zoomFactor** the app can apply or ignore; because it is designed for photo capture, it only provides recommendations on the **4032 photo format**.

deepdive_en.title: Support smart framing monitor
deepdive_en.body: Shows the monitor setup: find a format supporting both the desired ratios and smart framing and set it as the active format, get the `smartFramingMonitor`, and set `enabledFramings` to `supportedFramings` (or a subset such as 4x3 narrow and wide). Then **key-value observe** `recommendedFraming`, applying it by setting aspectRatio first then zoomFactor for a smooth preview transition; you can `startMonitoring` at any time, and unregister the observation plus `stopMonitoring` when turning automatic framing off.

deepdive_en.title: Sensor orientation compensation
deepdive_en.body: Explains the orientation difference: older front sensors were mounted Landscape Left, so a portrait selfie carried an EXIF tag to rotate 270 degrees, whereas the new sensor is mounted in **Portrait**, so reusing old rotation values can make photos appear sideways. **AVCapturePhotoOutput** compensates by default (physically rotating and updating EXIF so output stays landscape left), but only for **HEIC, JPEG, and uncompressed processed photos**, never Bayer RAW or Apple ProRAW; control it via `cameraSensorOrientationCompensationEnabled` and test with it off for best performance.

deepdive_en.title: Center Stage for video recordings
deepdive_en.body: Recording also supports Tap to Rotate via dynamicAspectRatio, but QuickTime tracks require all samples to share dimensions, so changing the ratio stops recording automatically. With **AVCaptureMovieFileOutput** recording stops automatically; with **AVCaptureVideoDataOutput** plus **AVAssetWriter** you can use the `setDynamicAspectRatio` completion timestamp to end the current recording and start a new one. Recordings also benefit from face-aware **cinematicExtended** and **cinematicExtendedEnhanced** stabilization modes.

deepdive_en.title: Center Stage for video calls
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates a FaceTime call where the camera widens to include a friend who joins. Apps using the **VoIP background mode** already support Center Stage, which people can turn on from Control Center's Video Effects; like other system video effects (Portrait, Studio Light), Center Stage is enabled per process and, once active, applies to any supported camera in the app.

deepdive_en.title: Support Center Stage for video calls
deepdive_en.body: Shows how apps not using the VoIP background mode adopt the Center Stage API: video calling apps typically use a video data output stream, so find a supported format and set it as active, set `centerStageControlMode` (**cooperative** so an in-app button can also control it, or **app**), then set `isCenterStageEnabled = true`. It also covers iOS 26's real-time low-latency stabilization, enabled by setting the AVCaptureConnection's `preferredVideoStabilizationMode` to **lowLatency** (off by default).

title: Explore advanced App Intents features for Siri and Apple Intelligence
gloss: 探索 Siri 與 Apple Intelligence 的進階 App Intents 功能
takeaway: 用進階 App Intents 打磨與 Siri/Apple Intelligence 的整合:自訂對話與澄清提問、視覺片段回應、互動捐贈、語意索引、結構化搜尋與螢幕內容感知。
chapters: Ask a clarifying question within an inten
Re-run Siri search in your app

points.text: 自訂 Siri 回應:用 **ProvidesDialog 的 IntentDialog** 給出完整/簡短對話,並可用 **$param.requestValue** 在 intent 中向使用者**反問澄清問題**。
視覺回應:強化 **DisplayRepresentation**(title/subtitle/image),並以 **ShowsSnippetView** 回傳自訂 snippet 視圖。
用 **IntentDonationManager.donate** 捐贈互動(含參數與結果),讓 Siri 學習使用者偏好。
語意整合:用 **IndexedEntity + CSSearchableIndex** 建語意索引,用 **IntentValueQuery** 做結構化搜尋,並以 .system.searchInApp 把 Siri 搜尋導回 App 內。
**螢幕內容感知(onscreen awareness)**:用 **EntityIdentifier / appEntityIdentifier** 在 NSUserActivity、視圖、清單、通知、Now Playing、AlarmKit 等處標註螢幕上的實體。

audience: **已導入 App Intents、想把 Siri 與 Apple Intelligence 整合做到更深(澄清提問、語意索引、螢幕感知)的開發者。**
gloss_en: Explore advanced App Intents features for Siri and Apple Intelligence
takeaway_en: Use advanced App Intents to polish your Siri/Apple Intelligence integration: custom dialog and clarifying questions, visual snippet responses, interaction donations, semantic indexing, structured search, and onscreen awareness.

points_en.text: Customize Siri responses: use **ProvidesDialog's IntentDialog** to give full/short dialog, and use **$param.requestValue** to **ask the user a clarifying question** within the intent.
Visual responses: enhance **DisplayRepresentation** (title/subtitle/image), and return a custom snippet view with **ShowsSnippetView**.
Use **IntentDonationManager.donate** to donate interactions (including parameters and results) so Siri learns user preferences.

Semantic integration: build a semantic index with **IndexedEntity + CSSearchableIndex**, do structured search with **IntentValueQuery**, and route Siri search back into your app with .system.searchInApp.
**Onscreen awareness**: use **EntityIdentifier / appEntityIdentifier** to annotate onscreen entities across NSUserActivity, views, lists, notifications, Now Playing, AlarmKit, and more.

audience_en: **Developers who have already adopted App Intents and want to deepen their Siri and Apple Intelligence integration (clarifying questions, semantic indexing, onscreen awareness).**
summary: 本場帶你超越 **App Intents** 的基礎，讓 app 在 **Siri** 與 **Apple Intelligence** 裡的體驗更精緻、更個人化，也更像你 app 自己的樣子。內容假設你已具備 App Intents 與 App Schemas 的基本概念，並以三個範例 app 貫穿全場：音樂播放與計時器的 CosmoTunes、訊息 app UnicornChat、行事曆 app CometCal。整體分三大主題：塑造 Siri 對話、讓內容更容易被找到、以及把系統各處的整合串連起來。

第一部分聚焦**塑造 Siri 對話**。透過 `ProvidesDialog` 回傳含 full 與 supporting 字串的 **IntentDialog**，讓回覆符合 app 個性（例如把歌曲叫 track、播放清單叫 mix tape），其中 full 字串要能在 AirPods 等純語音裝置上獨立成立。可在 perform 中用 `requestValue` 適時提出**澄清問題**；用 **DisplayRepresentation**（title／subtitle／image）與 `ShowsSnippetView` 自訂視覺呈現。**Interaction Donations** 則是把使用者在 app UI 內的操作（如送出訊息）以符合 schema 的 intent 捐贈給系統，讓 Apple Intelligence 學習偏好；最後在執行有副作用的 intent 前，可讓符合 **OwnershipProvidingEntity** 的實體回報 ownership 狀態，使 Siri 在更新公開或共享內容時適時要求確認。

第二部分讓 Siri **找得到你的內容**，有三條路徑。採用 **IndexedEntity** 並以 `CSSearchableIndex.indexAppEntities` 寫入 **Spotlight 語意索引**，依網域可獲得語意搜尋；並記得在內容新增、變更、刪除時同步維護索引（可用新的 **IndexedEntityQuery** 支援重新索引）。若資料量大或變動頻繁無法事先索引，改用 **IntentValueQuery**：接收系統的結構化搜尋輸入（如 AudioSearch，含 searchQuery／unspecified／url 等 criteria），並可回傳多種實體型別。要把結果顯示在自家搜尋介面，則採用 `.system.searchInApp` schema，由 intent 的 perform 在 app 內呈現結果。

第三部分是**畫面感知與系統整合**。**Onscreen awareness** 讓 Siri 把畫面上看得到的內容對應到可理解的實體與動作，解析「播放第三個」「那段對話」這類指稱：用 **NSUserActivity** 標註單一主要內容、用 **View Entity annotation**（`appEntityIdentifier`）標註多項中的一項、用 **Collection annotation** 處理清單與集合、用 custom canvas view annotation 處理非標準子視圖。再以 component-based display representation query 讓 Siri 只取文字表示、快速理解畫面。最後把實體標註延伸到既有系統整合：**UserNotifications**、**Now Playing**（依最具體到最不具體排序）與 **AlarmKit**，都用同一套 `appEntityIdentifiers` 模式（注意不可用 TransientAppEntity），讓人能在通知、播放中與鬧鐘等各處對你的內容採取行動。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: 由 App Intents 團隊工程師 Antonio Cancio 開場，目標是把 app 在 **Siri** 與 **Apple Intelligence** 的體驗推進到「精緻、個人化、明顯是你 app 樣子」的層次。本場假設已懂 App Intents 與 App Schemas 基礎，並介紹三個貫穿範例 app：CosmoTunes、UnicornChat、CometCal，可下載原始碼跟著操作。

deepdive.title: Customize how Siri responds
deepdive.body: 說明 Siri 已負責理解自然語言、選對動作、產生回覆，而 **App Intents** 讓你塑造它做什麼、精煉它怎麼回應，讓 app 個性展現出來。以 CosmoTunes 的 `AddToPlaylistIntent` 為例，先在 perform 中加入歌曲並回傳空的 IntentResult，代表交由 Siri 處理回覆。

deepdive.title: Custom dialog response
deepdive.body: 為讓回覆貼近 app 用語（歌曲叫 track、清單叫 mix tape），在 perform 加上 **ProvidesDialog** 協定，並回傳含 **full 與 supporting** 兩種字串的 **IntentDialog**。Siri 可用 supporting 字串搭配 UI，並在 AirPods 等純語音裝置朗讀 full 字串，因此 full 必須能獨立描述發生了什麼事。

deepdive.title: Ask a clarifying question within an inten
deepdive.body: 示範在 intent 執行中提出**澄清問題**：CosmoTunes 可建立會啟停播放的計時器，採用含必填與選填參數的 schema。若已有計時器在跑，便在未提供 label 時用 `$label.requestValue(...)` 請使用者為新計時器命名，以避免混淆；其他如選單選擇或確認等對話請求可參考範例與文件。

deepdive.title: Visual responses
deepdive.body: 說明實體的 display representation 與回應中的自訂視圖，是在對話旁呈現資訊並彰顯 app 識別的好機會。這些視覺可用於建立／更新實體的回應、在相似實體間請使用者選擇、回答 app 內容相關問題，Spotlight 與 Shortcuts 也會用到。

deepdive.title: Enhanced DisplayRepresentation
deepdive.body: 教你定義更豐富的 **DisplayRepresentation**：基本只需 title，但可加上 **subtitle 與 image** 讓呈現更完整。以 SongEntity 為例提供 artwork 圖片，當人問起 app 內歌曲時 Siri 即可顯示，藉此精煉實體在系統各處的視覺識別。

deepdive.title: Return a custom snippet view
deepdive.body: 回到 `AddToPlaylistIntent`，在 perform 加上 **ShowsSnippetView** 回傳型別，即可回傳含 SwiftUI 視圖（如 PlaylistSnippetView）的 IntentResult，以熟悉色彩顯示播放清單細節。講者提醒：審慎決定哪裡值得客製化，確保回覆在所有平台（含純語音裝置）都準確自然，並少用澄清問題以免造成摩擦。

deepdive.title: Interaction donations
deepdive.body: 引入 **Interaction Donations**：系統已知道人透過 Siri 或 Shortcuts 的互動，但 Apple Intelligence 無法從 app UI 內的操作學習，除非你協助。每筆捐贈是「人在 app UI 做了某動作」的提示，系統以符合 schema 的 App Intent 存入暫時的 transcript，給 Siri 更聰明判斷的脈絡。

deepdive.title: Donate a UI interaction
deepdive.body: 以 UnicornChat 示範：ConversationView 與 sendMessage intent 共用同一個送訊息 helper，於是在 helper 加上 `donateIntent` 參數區分來源（只需捐贈 UI 互動，Siri 互動系統已會學習）。接著建立 intent、填入參數與結果，再透過 **IntentDonationManager** 捐贈，讓系統學到使用者何時偏好用 UnicornChat；此模式也讓 Siri 掌握 app 中進行中的活動（如 Maps 的 NavigationSession、Clock 的碼錶起停）。提醒：捐贈須真實反映使用者行為，過度捐贈系統可能忽略。

deepdive.title: Confirmations and entity ownership
deepdive.body: 說明 Siri 蒐集完參數、準備呼叫 intent 前的最後一步是**確認**，可讓人知情並避免 LLM 帶來的非預期副作用。對有意義副作用的 intent（如取消行程）Siri 會自動確認；對更新已公開或與他人共享內容的 intent 更應確認（更新私人事件可能不確認，更新有與會者的 Crew Lunch 則可能確認）。

deepdive.title: Declare entity ownership for confirmations
deepdive.body: 教你以新的 **OwnershipProvidingEntity** 協定告訴 Siri 實體已被公開或共享。Siri 預設假設實體屬個人私有、可能略過確認；只對人能在 app 中共享或公開的實體加上此協定並提供 ownership 狀態（如有與會者則為 .shared），且每次系統索取實體時保持狀態最新，Siri 也會用稍早自訂的 display representation 作為確認視覺。

deepdive.title: Index entities with IndexedEntity
deepdive.body: 進入讓 Siri「找到內容」主題，先談語意索引。CosmoTunes 的播放清單都在裝置本機，採用 **IndexedEntity** 即可讓 Apple Intelligence 找到它們，並用 `CSSearchableIndex.indexAppEntities` 寫入 Spotlight 語意索引。

deepdive.title: Semantic index with IndexedEntity
deepdive.body: 示範索引後即可「在 CosmoTunes 播放我的 WWDC 播放清單」並在 Spotlight 搜尋。依 App Intents 網域，Spotlight 索引可提供**語意搜尋**——依意義而非完全關鍵字理解實體。強調維護索引同樣關鍵：新增時索引、關鍵屬性變更時更新、刪除時移除；可採用新的 **IndexedEntityQuery** 支援重新索引（若已用 Core Spotlight 層級 API 則不需另定義）。

deepdive.title: Structured search with IntentValueQuery
deepdive.body: 說明若資料量大、在伺服器或變動太頻繁而無法事先索引（如 CosmoTunes 選擇索引播放清單但不索引歌曲），可改用 **IntentValueQuery**，仍讓人能用 Siri 播放歌曲。

deepdive.title: Structured search with IntentValueQuer
deepdive.body: 深入 **IntentValueQuery**：類似 EntityQuery，但差別在 app 收到系統的**結構化搜尋輸入**且可回傳多種實體型別。Siri 為 PlayAudioIntent 的 audioEntity 參數呼叫此 query 並帶入 **AudioSearch**，其 `.criteria` 描述查詢：`.searchQuery` 含相關語句、`.unspecified`（如「播放 CosmoTunes」）直接播放先前喜歡的歌、還有 `.url` 處理連結指稱；回傳的 AudioEntity 是含歌曲與播放清單的 UnionValue。

deepdive.title: Re-run Siri search in your app
deepdive.body: 說明有時人不是要動作、只想找東西（如「顯示 CosmoTunes 裡的跑步播放清單」）。Siri 預設會列出實體結果，但若想用自家精心打造的搜尋介面呈現，可採用系統的 **searchInApp** schema。

deepdive.title: In-app search
deepdive.body: iOS 17 推出的 system search schema 現更名為 **`.system.searchInApp`**，屬 System App Schema 網域，讓人不論採用哪些其他網域、甚至未索引實體，都能用 Siri 在 app 內搜尋。Siri 以它搜尋的同一字串呼叫此 intent，perform 方法便設定 searchText 與分頁、在 app 內找到並顯示結果。

deepdive.title: Onscreen awareness
deepdive.body: 引入 **Onscreen awareness**：把畫面上看得到的內容連到系統可理解的結構化資訊與動作，讓 Siri 解析「播放第三個」「那段對話」等指稱。Siri 預設只懂畫面像素中的文字（無法對顯示的 track 採取行動，也可能說不出未顯示的歌手），採用相關 API 才能提供畫面上有哪些實體、位於何處的脈絡。

deepdive.title: Onscreen awareness annotations
deepdive.body: 示範起手式：用 **NSUserActivity** 的 `.userActivity` 標註代表主要內容的視圖（如 NowPlayingView 整個畫面就是當前播放項），用 **View Entity annotation** 的 `.appEntityIdentifier` 標註多項中的一項（如 AlbumView 同時顯示專輯與曲目）。UIKit 與 AppKit 同樣支援所有 onscreen awareness API。

deepdive.title: Component-based display representation query
deepdive.body: 說明畫面一次顯示多個實體時，Siri 需快速判斷它們是否與請求相關，否則可能改問或播錯。稍早自訂的 display representation 可幫上忙：在 PlaylistQuery 實作 `displayRepresentations(for:requestedComponents:)`，讓 Siri 只查實體的**文字表示**，跳過從資料庫取完整內容的開銷。此段也涵蓋處理清單與集合的 **Collection annotation**（`appEntityIdentifier(forSelectionType:)`，系統延遲取得識別碼、可發現已選但捲出畫面的實體）與 custom canvas view annotation（如 PianoRollView 的非標準子視圖）。

deepdive.title: Leverage existing integrations
deepdive.body: 說明除了畫面之外，app 已與系統其他部分緊密整合，可把實體連到既有整合給 Siri 更多脈絡。app 實體像是一種通用語言，讓 Siri 不只懂畫面、也懂其他系統整合與時間敏感事件如何與你的內容相關。

deepdive.title: Entity annotations on system integrations
deepdive.body: 示範把實體標註延伸到三個既有整合，皆用同一套 **entity annotations** 模式。**UserNotifications**：把訊息的 EntityIdentifier 指派給 UNMutableNotificationContent 的 `appEntityIdentifiers`，讓 AirPods 朗讀通知時能直接回覆。**Now Playing**：把歌曲、歌手、播放清單實體依最具體到最不具體加入，支援「播放現場版」。**AlarmKit**：在 AlarmConfiguration 的 `appEntityIdentifier` 加單一識別碼以對響鈴鬧鐘採取行動。注意這三種 API 都不能用 TransientAppEntity（暫時實體無持久識別碼）。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 總結建議的下一步：先自訂 entity display representation（系統各處都會用到），再把實體加入語意索引並持續維護，接著考慮以 IntentValueQuery 與 in-app search 讓實體可被 Siri 取用，並為視圖、活動與既有系統整合加上實體標註，最後捐贈 UI 互動以更個人化。並指向 App Schemas 的 Code-Along 與相關範例專案。

summary_en: This session takes you beyond the basics of **App Intents** so your app feels polished, personal, and unmistakably yours in **Siri** and **Apple Intelligence**. It assumes a basic understanding of App Intents and App Schemas and runs through three sample apps: CosmoTunes (music, alarms, timers), UnicornChat (messaging), and CometCal (calendar). The plan has three parts: shaping the Siri conversation, making your content easier to find, and connecting existing system integrations.

Part one shapes the **Siri conversation**. Adopt `ProvidesDialog` and return an **IntentDialog** with full and supporting strings so responses match your app's personality (calling songs tracks and playlists mix tapes), where the full string must stand on its own for voice-only devices like AirPods. Ask a **clarifying question** mid-perform with `requestValue`, and customize visuals via **DisplayRepresentation** (title/subtitle/image) and `ShowsSnippetView`. **Interaction Donations** donate UI actions (such as sending a message) as schema-conforming intents so Apple Intelligence can learn preferences, and before intents with side effects, entities conforming to **OwnershipProvidingEntity** report their ownership state so Siri confirms when updating public or shared content.

Part two helps Siri **find your content** via three paths. Adopt **IndexedEntity** and call `CSSearchableIndex.indexAppEntities` to populate the **Spotlight semantic index** (semantic search depending on domain), keeping the index updated as content is added, changed, or removed (support reindexing with the new **IndexedEntityQuery**). When data is large or changes too often to index ahead of time, use **IntentValueQuery**: it receives a structured search input from the system (e.g. AudioSearch with searchQuery/unspecified/url criteria) and can return multiple entity types. To show results in your own search UI, adopt the `.system.searchInApp` schema, whose perform method presents results in the app.

Part three covers **onscreen awareness and system integrations**. Onscreen awareness connects what's visible on screen to entities and actions the system understands, resolving references like "play the third one" or "that conversation": use **NSUserActivity** for a single primary item, the **View Entity annotation** (`appEntityIdentifier`) for one item among many, **Collection annotation** for lists and collections, and a custom canvas view annotation for non-standard subviews. A component-based display representation query lets Siri query just the text representation to understand the screen quickly. Finally, extend entity annotations to existing integrations: **UserNotifications**, **Now Playing** (ordered most to least specific), and **AlarmKit**, all using the same `appEntityIdentifiers` pattern (TransientAppEntity is not allowed), so people can act on your content wherever they encounter it.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Antonio Cancio, an App Intents engineer, opens with the goal of taking your app's experience in **Siri** and **Apple Intelligence** beyond the basics to feel polished, personal, and unmistakably yours. The talk assumes familiarity with App Intents and App Schemas and introduces three sample apps to follow along with: CosmoTunes, UnicornChat, and CometCal.

deepdive_en.title: Customize how Siri responds
deepdive_en.body: Notes that Siri already understands natural language, picks the right action, and crafts a response, while **App Intents** lets you shape what it does and refine how it responds so your app's personality shows. Using CosmoTunes' `AddToPlaylistIntent`, the perform method first adds the song and returns an empty IntentResult, telling Siri to handle the response.

deepdive_en.title: Custom dialog response
deepdive_en.body: To make responses match the app's vocabulary (tracks and mix tapes), the perform method adopts **ProvidesDialog** and returns an **IntentDialog** with both **full and supporting** strings. Siri can show the supporting string with UI and read the full string on voice-only devices like AirPods, so the full string must describe what happened on its own.

deepdive_en.title: Ask a clarifying question within an inten
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates asking a **clarifying question** while the intent runs: CosmoTunes timers that start or stop playback adopt a schema with required and optional parameters. If a timer is already running, it calls `$label.requestValue(...)` to ask the person to name the new timer when no label was provided; other dialog requests (choosing from a list, confirmations) are covered in the sample and docs.

deepdive_en.title: Visual responses
deepdive_en.body: Explains that entity display representations and custom views in responses are a great opportunity to present information visually and surface the app's identity alongside the dialog. They're used in responses when entities are created or updated, when asking someone to choose between similar entities, and when answering questions about content, and Spotlight and Shortcuts use them too.

deepdive_en.title: Enhanced DisplayRepresentation
deepdive_en.body: Shows defining a richer **DisplayRepresentation**: a basic one needs just a title, but adding a **subtitle and image** makes it fuller. The SongEntity example provides artwork that Siri can show when people ask about songs, refining the visual identity of entities across the system.

deepdive_en.title: Return a custom snippet view
deepdive_en.body: Back in `AddToPlaylistIntent`, adding the **ShowsSnippetView** return type lets the perform method return an IntentResult with a SwiftUI view (like PlaylistSnippetView) showing playlist details in familiar colors. The speaker advises deciding where customization actually makes sense, ensuring responses are accurate and natural on all platforms including voice-only devices, and asking clarifying questions sparingly to avoid friction.

deepdive_en.title: Interaction donations
deepdive_en.body: Introduces **Interaction Donations**: the system already knows about Siri and Shortcuts interactions, but Apple Intelligence can't learn from actions taken through the app's own UI without your help. Each donation is a hint that a person took a specific action in your UI, stored by the system as a schema-conforming App Intent in a temporary transcript that gives Siri context for smarter decisions.

deepdive_en.title: Donate a UI interaction
deepdive_en.body: Using UnicornChat: ConversationView and the sendMessage intent share the same send helper, so a `donateIntent` parameter is added to distinguish the caller (only UI interactions need donating, since Siri interactions are already learned). It then creates the intent, populates parameters and result, and donates via **IntentDonationManager** so the system learns when the person prefers UnicornChat; the pattern also keeps Siri aware of ongoing activities (Maps NavigationSession, Clock stopwatches). Donations must reflect real behavior, as excessive donations may be ignored.

deepdive_en.title: Confirmations and entity ownership
deepdive_en.body: Explains that once Siri has gathered parameters and is ready to call your intent, the final step is **confirmation**, keeping people informed and protecting against the unintended side effects that are a known LLM risk. Siri can automatically confirm intents with meaningful side effects (like canceling a trip), and confirmation matters even more for updates to content made public or shared (it may skip a private event but confirm updating a Crew Lunch with attendees).

deepdive_en.title: Declare entity ownership for confirmations
deepdive_en.body: Shows conforming relevant entities to the new **OwnershipProvidingEntity** protocol to tell Siri an entity is public or shared. Siri assumes entities are private by default and may skip confirmations, so only add the protocol to entities people can share or make public, provide the ownership state (e.g. .shared when there are attendees), and keep it current whenever the system requests the entity; Siri can reuse the earlier display representations as confirmation visuals.

deepdive_en.title: Index entities with IndexedEntity
deepdive_en.body: Begins the "help Siri find content" topic with the semantic index. CosmoTunes playlists are all on device, so adopting **IndexedEntity** and calling `CSSearchableIndex.indexAppEntities` populates the Spotlight semantic index so Apple Intelligence can find them.

deepdive_en.title: Semantic index with IndexedEntity
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates that once indexed you can say "Play my WWDC playlist in CosmoTunes" and search in Spotlight. Depending on the App Intents domain, Spotlight indexing provides **semantic search** that understands entities by meaning, not just exact keywords. It stresses maintaining the index: index on add, update when key properties change, delete on removal; support reindexing with the new **IndexedEntityQuery** (not needed if you already reindex via Core Spotlight-level APIs).

deepdive_en.title: Structured search with IntentValueQuery
deepdive_en.body: Explains that when data is large, server-side, or changes too frequently to index ahead of time (CosmoTunes indexes playlists but not songs), you can reach for an **IntentValueQuery** to still let people play songs with Siri.

deepdive_en.title: Structured search with IntentValueQuer
deepdive_en.body: Dives into **IntentValueQuery**: similar to EntityQuery, but the app receives a **structured search input** from the system and can return more than one entity type. Siri calls it for the PlayAudioIntent's audioEntity parameter with an **AudioSearch** whose `.criteria` describes the query: `.searchQuery` holds the relevant phrase, `.unspecified` ("Play CosmoTunes") plays previously liked songs, and `.url` handles link references; the returned AudioEntity is a UnionValue of songs and playlists.

deepdive_en.title: Re-run Siri search in your app
deepdive_en.body: Notes that sometimes people just want to find something rather than act ("Show me running playlists in CosmoTunes"). Siri shows a list of entity results by default, but to present them in your own crafted search experience you can adopt the system **searchInApp** schema.

deepdive_en.title: In-app search
deepdive_en.body: The iOS 17 system search schema is now named **`.system.searchInApp`**, part of the System App Schema domain, letting people search in your app with Siri regardless of which other domains you adopt and even without indexed entities. Siri calls the intent with the same string it searched, and the perform method sets the search text and tab to find and show the results in the app.

deepdive_en.title: Onscreen awareness
deepdive_en.body: Introduces **onscreen awareness**: connecting what's visible on screen to structured information and actions the system understands so Siri can resolve references like "play the third one" or "that conversation." By default Siri only understands text in the pixels (it can't act on shown tracks and may not know an off-screen artist), so adopting these APIs provides context on which entities are on screen and where.

deepdive_en.title: Onscreen awareness annotations
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates the starting points: use **NSUserActivity** (`.userActivity`) on the view representing primary content (NowPlayingView is a whole screen dedicated to the current item) and the **View Entity annotation** (`.appEntityIdentifier`) when an entity is one item among many (AlbumView shows both the album and its tracks). UIKit and AppKit support all of the onscreen awareness APIs too.

deepdive_en.title: Component-based display representation query
deepdive_en.body: Explains that when many entities show at once, Siri must quickly judge whether they relate to a request or it may ask to clarify or play the wrong thing. The earlier display representations help: implementing `displayRepresentations(for:requestedComponents:)` on PlaylistQuery lets Siri query just the **text representation**, skipping the cost of fetching full content from the database. This section also covers the **Collection annotation** for lists (`appEntityIdentifier(forSelectionType:)`, with lazy identifier fetching that finds selected, scrolled-off entities) and the custom canvas view annotation for non-standard subviews like PianoRollView.

deepdive_en.title: Leverage existing integrations
deepdive_en.body: Notes that beyond the UI, the app already integrates closely with other parts of the system, and connecting entities to those existing integrations gives Siri more context. App entities act as a universal language so Siri understands not just what's on screen but how other system integrations and time-sensitive events relate to your content.

deepdive_en.title: Entity annotations on system integrations
deepdive_en.body: Adds entity annotations to three existing integrations using the same **entity annotations** pattern. **UserNotifications**: assign the message's EntityIdentifier to UNMutableNotificationContent's `appEntityIdentifiers` so a notification announced on AirPods can be replied to. **Now Playing**: add song, artist, and playlist entities ordered most to least specific, enabling "Play the live version." **AlarmKit**: add a single EntityIdentifier to AlarmConfiguration's `appEntityIdentifier` to act on firing alarms. None of these three APIs allow TransientAppEntity, which has no persistent identifier.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Summarizes recommended next steps: start by customizing entity display representations (used across the system), then add entities to the semantic index and keep it updated, consider making entities accessible via IntentValueQuery and in-app search, annotate views, activities, and existing integrations with entities, and finally donate UI interactions for a more personalized experience. It points to the App Schemas Code-Along and the sample projects.

title: Code-along: Make your app available to Siri
gloss: 程式碼實作：讓你的 App 可被 Siri 使用
takeaway: 跟著 Xcode 專案一步步採用 App Schemas 與 App Intents，建立日曆、出席者與事件等 entity，讓使用者能用 Siri 開啟、建立、更新與刪除事件。

points.text: 這是一場 **code-along**，跟著實際 Xcode 專案採用 **App Schemas**，讓 App 的功能可被 Siri 觸發。
逐步建立 **CalendarEntity、AttendeeEntity 與 EventEntity** 等 App Intents entity，作為 Siri 操作的資料模型。
示範用 **OpenIntent 開啟事件**並加入**畫面感知（onscreen awareness）**，讓 Siri 理解使用者當下看到的內容。
完整涵蓋以 Siri **建立、更新與刪除事件**的流程，並加入**自訂 snippet view** 呈現結果。

audience: **想讓 App 深度整合 Siri、跟著動手實作 App Intents 與 App Schemas 的開發者**。
gloss_en: Code-along: Make your app available to Siri
takeaway_en: Follow along in an Xcode project to adopt App Schemas and App Intents step by step, creating calendar, attendee, and event entities so users can open, create, update, and delete events with Siri.

points_en.text: This is a **code-along** that follows a real Xcode project to adopt **App Schemas**, making your app's features available to Siri.
Builds App Intents entities step by step, including **CalendarEntity, AttendeeEntity, and EventEntity**, as the data model for Siri operations.
Demonstrates using **OpenIntent to open an event** and adding **onscreen awareness** so Siri understands what the user is currently looking at.
Fully covers **creating, updating, and deleting events** with Siri, and adds a **custom snippet view** to present the results.

audience_en: **Developers who want deep Siri integration and want to follow along implementing App Intents and App Schemas hands-on**.
summary: 由 Swift Intelligence Frameworks 團隊工程師 Justin 主講的 code-along，逐步把一個名為 **CometCal** 的 SwiftUI 行事曆 app 變得「可被 Siri 使用」。願景是：對 Siri 說「誰會來野餐？」就能查到出席名單、說「移到 11:30」就能改時間、說「傳訊息給所有人」就能通知、問「我需要帶什麼？」「開車過去要多久？」都能直接得到答案。這一切由 Apple Intelligence 透過 **App Intents** 框架達成，核心關鍵字是 **App Schemas**——以 Siri 早已理解的結構描述 app 的內容與動作，無需訓練語句或自寫 NLP。

第一階段是讓 Siri **理解內容**，依序建立三個 entity。**CalendarEntity** 用 `calendar_calendar` snippet 帶出 `@AppEntity` 結構，id 設為 UUID，conform **`IndexedEntity`** 以便用 Spotlight 語意索引被捐贈（donate）；在 query 中用 `@Dependency` 注入 main-actor 的 `CalendarManager`，並 conform `EnumerableEntityQuery` 提供 `allEntities`。關鍵是在 `CalendarManager` 的 create／update／delete 中用 `CSSearchableIndex` 的 `indexAppEntities`／`deleteAppEntities` **捐贈與移除** entity。**AttendeeEntity** 改 conform **`TransientAppEntity`**（暫時、無需 id、不被查詢，因 attendee 代表某事件中的參與而非人本身），用到 `IntentPerson` 型別與兩個 schema 化 `@AppEnum`（status、type）。**EventEntity** 是核心、conform `IndexedEntity`，組合了 CalendarEntity 與 AttendeeEntity 陣列，並處理 recurrence（`Calendar.RecurrenceRule`）與 location／alarm 的 **union value**。

第二階段讓 Siri 能**導覽與感知畫面**。**`OpenEventIntent`** conform `system.open` schema，以 EventEntity 為 target 呼叫 NavigationManager 導到該事件，讓在 Siri/Spotlight 點事件能直接開到詳情頁。**Onscreen awareness** 只需兩個 view modifier：在事件列表用 `.appEntityIdentifier` 把每列對應到 entity、在詳情頁用 `.userActivity` 帶 `EntityIdentifier` 標示當前單一事件，如此就能對 Siri 說「開那第三個事件」或「email 這個事件裡的人」而不必念出標題。

第三階段給 Siri **行動能力**。三個 intent 皆用對應 snippet（`calendar_createEvent`／`updateEvent`／`deleteEvent`）以 `@AppIntent` macro 生成，perform 流程一致：把參數解析成資料層能懂的形式、執行動作、回傳 entity。Update intent 多數參數為 optional，靠 `IntentParameter` 的 **`valueState`**（`.set` 帶值＝更新、`.set` 帶 nil＝清除、`.unset`＝不在請求中）分辨「不改」與「清空」。Delete 最簡單，Siri 會自動處理確認對話與多筆消歧。最後用 **snippet view**（回傳型別加 `ShowsSnippetView` 並傳入自訂 SwiftUI view）把 Siri 預設結果卡換成有 app 風格的自訂卡片。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: 由 Swift Intelligence Frameworks 團隊的 Justin 開場，以一段與 Siri 的對話情境（查野餐出席者、改時間、傳訊息、問要帶什麼、問車程）描繪本場目標：把現有 app 變得可被 Siri 使用。說明 Siri 由 Apple Intelligence 驅動，開發者透過 **App Intents** 框架讓 app 內容與動作出現在 Siri 等系統體驗中，並指引可先看 App Schemas 與 Get to know App Intents 的基礎影片。

deepdive.title: App Schemas and the plan
deepdive.body: 介紹範例專案 **CometCal**（SwiftUI 行事曆，原本只能用螢幕操作），計畫讓 Siri 能理解內容並採取動作。關鍵是 **App Schemas**：以 Siri 已理解的結構描述 entity、action 與輸出，無需訓練語句或自寫 NLP。Schema 依 **domain** 組織，calendar domain 涵蓋 events、calendars、attendees 與相關動作。

deepdive.title: Build the CalendarEntity
deepdive.body: 建立 **CalendarEntity**：新檔 import AppIntents，輸入 `calendar_` 由 Xcode autocomplete 選 `calendar_calendar` snippet 帶出 `@AppEntity`、屬性、DisplayRepresentation 與 query stub。把 id 設為 UUID 對應資料模型，conform **`IndexedEntity`** 以用 Spotlight 語意索引被捐贈、讓 Siri 依名稱／屬性／脈絡解析。query 中用 `@Dependency` 注入 main-actor 的 `CalendarManager`、conform `EnumerableEntityQuery` 加 `allEntities`，DisplayRepresentation 設標題與系統圖示。

deepdive.title: Build the AttendeeEntity
deepdive.body: 建立 **AttendeeEntity**，用 `calendar_attendee` snippet。與 CalendarEntity 不同，它 conform **`TransientAppEntity`**——暫時、無需唯一 id、不被查詢；因為 attendee 代表某人在特定事件的參與而非人本身，獨立索引會在 Spotlight 產生重複結果。用到系統標準的 **`IntentPerson`** 型別（含姓名與聯絡資訊，方便跨 app 分享如把 email 傳給 Mail），以及兩個 schema 化 `@AppEnum`：用 `calendar_attendeeStatus` 與 `calendar_attendeeType` snippet 建立 status 與 type。

deepdive.title: Build the EventEntity
deepdive.body: 建立核心的 **EventEntity**，用 `calendar_event` snippet 並 conform `IndexedEntity`，讓 Siri 能搜尋標題（「crew lunch 何時？」）或 note 內容（「哪些事件提到 oxygen？」）。schema 定義哪些屬性必填／選填（title、startDate 必填；travelTime、virtualLocation 不用可不設）；非 schema 但模型有的屬性（如 isFavorite）也可加。它組合 **CalendarEntity** 與 **AttendeeEntity 陣列**，recurrence 用 Foundation 的 `Calendar.RecurrenceRule` 互轉 app 的 frequency enum，location／alarm 則用 **union value**（location 可為 GeoToolbox 的 PlaceDescriptor 或 String；alarm 可為 Duration 或 Date），並有 EventEntityStatus 等 schema 化 enum。

deepdive.title: Open events with OpenIntent
deepdive.body: 內容層完成後，Siri 已能回答事件相關問題（如「流星派對快到了嗎？」「峰值觀賞時間？」），但點結果只會開到主畫面。於是加入 **`OpenEventIntent`**：conform `system.open` schema、以 EventEntity 為 target、呼叫 NavigationManager 導到該事件。當有人在 Spotlight／Siri 點事件或請 Siri 開啟時系統會呼叫它，現在點事件即直達詳情頁。

deepdive.title: Onscreen awareness
deepdive.body: 加入 **onscreen awareness** 讓對話更自然（如「email 這個事件的人」不必念標題），只需兩個 view modifier：在 CalendarListView 對 list 加 **`.appEntityIdentifier`** 為每個 event entity 帶 EntityIdentifier，連結列表與其 entity；在事件詳情頁加 **`.userActivity`** 帶 EntityIdentifier 標示當前單一事件，讓 Siri 解析到正在檢視的那一個。示範「開那第三個事件」與「email 這個事件的人請他帶巧克力與棉花糖」。

deepdive.title: Create events with Siri
deepdive.body: 進入動作層，先做建立事件。用 `calendar_createEvent` snippet 生成帶 `@AppIntent` macro、schema 必填參數與 perform stub 的 intent。填好型別、加 `@Dependency` 的 `CalendarManager`，perform 標 `@MainActor`、回傳型別設 EventEntity。一般模式：把參數（如從 union value 取 location、轉換 recurrence）解析成資料層能懂的形式、呼叫 createEvent、回傳 EventEntity。示範對 Siri 說在 Lunar Orbit Log 建立 6/15 早上 8 點的 Zero Gravity Yoga。

deepdive.title: Update events
deepdive.body: 做 **UpdateEventIntent**（`calendar_updateEvent` snippet）。結構類似 create，但多數參數為 optional（使用者可能只改一兩項），event 由 Siri 解析、其餘選填。perform 同樣解析有提供的參數再交給 CalendarManager 的 updateEvent。示範以多輪對話改時間、改週期、換 calendar、取消重複。

deepdive.title: Custom snippet views
deepdive.body: 更新後 Siri 顯示預設結果卡，CometCal 想要更有風格的。預設卡由 DisplayRepresentation 建構，**snippet view** 可換成自訂 SwiftUI view。在 UpdateEventIntent 的 perform 回傳型別加 **`ShowsSnippetView`**，並在回傳時傳入接受 EventEntity 的 `EventSnippetView`（宇宙漸層、深藍背景、星形圖示）；同法可用於 create 等回傳結果的 intent。提醒保持輕量。

deepdive.title: Delete events
deepdive.body: 做最後也最簡單的 **DeleteEventIntent**：只有 event 與 recurring 事件的 optional span，perform 找到事件並刪除。Siri 會自動在刪除前處理**確認對話**，並在多筆事件符合時自動**消歧**。示範刪派對與依日期刪事件、以及「算了，不要」的取消。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 總結：三個 entity、三個 intent 加上少量 snippet，就把 CometCal 從只能用螢幕變成可語音操作。下一步：下載 CometCal 範例專案探索完整實作、瀏覽 App Intents 文件了解所有 App Schemas 與 domain、用 AppIntentsTesting 框架寫測試、並看「Explore advanced App Intents features for Siri and Apple Intelligence」深入未涵蓋的進階主題。

summary_en: This code-along, presented by Swift Intelligence Frameworks engineer Justin, steps through making a SwiftUI calendar app called **CometCal** available to Siri. The vision: asking Siri 'Who's coming to my picnic?' surfaces the guest list, 'Move it to 11:30' changes the time, 'Text everyone going' notifies them, and 'What did I need to bring?' / 'How long will it take to drive there?' get direct answers. All of this is achieved through Apple Intelligence via the **App Intents** framework, with the key concept being **App Schemas**—describing the app's content and actions in structures Siri already understands, with no training phrases and no custom NLP.

The first phase makes Siri **understand content** by building three entities. **CalendarEntity** uses the `calendar_calendar` snippet for an `@AppEntity` structure, sets id to UUID, and conforms to **`IndexedEntity`** so it can be donated via the Spotlight semantic index; its query injects a main-actor `CalendarManager` with `@Dependency` and conforms to `EnumerableEntityQuery` for `allEntities`. Crucially, the `CalendarManager`'s create/update/delete **donate and remove** entities using `CSSearchableIndex`'s `indexAppEntities`/`deleteAppEntities`. **AttendeeEntity** instead conforms to **`TransientAppEntity`** (temporary, no id, not queried, since an attendee represents participation in an event, not the person), using the `IntentPerson` type and two schematized `@AppEnum`s (status, type). **EventEntity** is the core, conforms to `IndexedEntity`, composes a CalendarEntity and an array of AttendeeEntity, and handles recurrence (`Calendar.RecurrenceRule`) and **union values** for location/alarms.

The second phase gives Siri **navigation and onscreen awareness**. **`OpenEventIntent`** conforms to the `system.open` schema, takes an EventEntity as its target, and calls the NavigationManager to navigate to that event, so tapping an event in Siri/Spotlight opens straight to its detail view. **Onscreen awareness** takes just two view modifiers: `.appEntityIdentifier` on the event list to map each row to its entity, and `.userActivity` with an `EntityIdentifier` on the detail view to mark the single onscreen event—so you can say 'open that third event' or 'email the people in this event' without naming the title.

The third phase gives Siri the ability to **act**. Three intents are generated from their snippets (`calendar_createEvent`/`updateEvent`/`deleteEvent`) with the `@AppIntent` macro, following the same perform pattern: resolve parameters into something the data layer understands, perform the action, and return an entity. The update intent's mostly-optional parameters use `IntentParameter`'s **`valueState`** (`.set` with a value = update, `.set` with nil = clear, `.unset` = not part of the request) to distinguish 'don't change' from 'remove'. Delete is the simplest—Siri automatically handles the confirmation dialog and disambiguation. Finally, **snippet views** (add `ShowsSnippetView` to the return type and pass a custom SwiftUI view) replace Siri's default result card with an on-brand one.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Swift Intelligence Frameworks engineer Justin opens with a Siri conversation scenario (checking picnic attendees, changing the time, texting everyone, asking what to bring, asking the drive time) framing the goal: make an existing app available to Siri. Siri is powered by Apple Intelligence, and developers integrate through the **App Intents** framework so app content and actions appear in Siri and other system experiences; he points to the App Schemas and Get to know App Intents foundational videos.

deepdive_en.title: App Schemas and the plan
deepdive_en.body: Introduces the sample project **CometCal** (a SwiftUI calendar, previously screen-only) and the plan to let Siri understand content and take actions. The key is **App Schemas**: describing entities, actions, and outputs in structures Siri already understands, with no training phrases or custom NLP. Schemas are organized into **domains**, and the calendar domain covers events, calendars, attendees, and their actions.

deepdive_en.title: Build the CalendarEntity
deepdive_en.body: Builds **CalendarEntity**: a new file imports AppIntents, and typing `calendar_` lets Xcode autocomplete the `calendar_calendar` snippet with `@AppEntity`, properties, DisplayRepresentation, and a query stub. Set id to UUID to match the model and conform to **`IndexedEntity`** so it can be donated via the Spotlight semantic index and resolved by name/property/context. The query injects a main-actor `CalendarManager` via `@Dependency`, conforms to `EnumerableEntityQuery` with `allEntities`, and DisplayRepresentation sets the title and a system image.

deepdive_en.title: Build the AttendeeEntity
deepdive_en.body: Builds **AttendeeEntity** with the `calendar_attendee` snippet. Unlike CalendarEntity, it conforms to **`TransientAppEntity`**—temporary, no unique id, not queried—because an attendee represents a person's participation in a specific event, not the person, and indexing each separately would duplicate Spotlight results. It uses the system-standard **`IntentPerson`** type (name and contact info, handy for sharing across apps like sending an email to Mail) and two schematized `@AppEnum`s: status and type via the `calendar_attendeeStatus` and `calendar_attendeeType` snippets.

deepdive_en.title: Build the EventEntity
deepdive_en.body: Builds the core **EventEntity** with the `calendar_event` snippet, conforming to `IndexedEntity` so Siri can search the title ('when is my crew lunch?') or note content ('what events mention oxygen?'). The schema defines required vs optional properties (title, startDate required; travelTime, virtualLocation can stay unset); non-schema model properties like isFavorite can be added. It composes a **CalendarEntity** and an **array of AttendeeEntity**, with recurrence converting to/from Foundation's `Calendar.RecurrenceRule`, and **union values** for location/alarms (location is a GeoToolbox PlaceDescriptor or String; alarm is a Duration or Date), plus schematized enums like EventEntityStatus.

deepdive_en.title: Open events with OpenIntent
deepdive_en.body: With the content layer done, Siri answers event questions (e.g., 'is the Meteor Shower Party soon?', 'peak viewing time?'), but tapping a result only opens the main screen. So add **`OpenEventIntent`**: conform to the `system.open` schema, take an EventEntity target, and call the NavigationManager to navigate to that event. The system calls it when someone taps an event in Spotlight/Siri or asks Siri to open one, so tapping now lands on the detail view.

deepdive_en.title: Onscreen awareness
deepdive_en.body: Adds **onscreen awareness** for more natural conversation (e.g., 'email the people in this event' without the title), via two view modifiers: on CalendarListView's list, add **`.appEntityIdentifier`** with an EntityIdentifier for each event entity to connect the list to its entities; on the detail view, add **`.userActivity`** with an EntityIdentifier marking the single onscreen event so Siri resolves the one being viewed. Demos 'open that third event' and 'email the people in this event and ask someone to bring chocolate and marshmallows'.

deepdive_en.title: Create events with Siri
deepdive_en.body: Enters the action layer with creating events. The `calendar_createEvent` snippet scaffolds an intent with the `@AppIntent` macro, the schema's required parameters, and a perform stub. Fill in types, add a `@Dependency` `CalendarManager`, mark perform `@MainActor`, and set EventEntity as the return type. The general pattern: resolve parameters (e.g., extract location from a union value, convert recurrence) into data-layer terms, call createEvent, and return an EventEntity. Demos asking Siri to create Zero Gravity Yoga in the Lunar Orbit Log for June 15th, 8am.

deepdive_en.title: Update events
deepdive_en.body: Builds **UpdateEventIntent** (`calendar_updateEvent` snippet). Similar to create, but most parameters are optional (someone may change just one or two things); the event is what Siri resolves, the rest optional. Perform resolves each provided parameter then passes everything to CalendarManager's updateEvent. Demos multi-turn changes to time, recurrence, calendar, and turning off repeat.

deepdive_en.title: Custom snippet views
deepdive_en.body: After updates Siri shows a default result card, but CometCal wants more personality. The default card is built from the DisplayRepresentation; a **snippet view** replaces it with a custom SwiftUI view. Add **`ShowsSnippetView`** to UpdateEventIntent's perform return type and pass an `EventSnippetView` (cosmic gradient, dark blue background, star icon) that takes an EventEntity; the same works for any intent returning a result, like create. Keep it lightweight.

deepdive_en.title: Delete events
deepdive_en.body: Builds the last and simplest **DeleteEventIntent**: just the event and an optional span for recurring events; perform finds and deletes the event. Siri automatically handles the **confirmation dialog** before deletion and **disambiguates** when more than one event matches. Demos deleting a party, deleting an event by date, and an 'actually, never mind' cancellation.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Recap: three entities, three intents, and a few snippets take CometCal from screen-bound to voice-piloted. Next steps: download the CometCal sample project to explore the full implementation, browse the App Intents documentation for all App Schemas and domains, write tests with the AppIntentsTesting framework, and watch 'Explore advanced App Intents features for Siri and Apple Intelligence' for advanced topics not covered here.

title: Discover new capabilities in the App Intents framework
gloss: 探索 App Intents 框架的新能力
takeaway: App Intents 新增 **ValueRepresentation、EntityCollection、SyncableEntity、LongRunningIntent 與 ExecutionTargets**，讓 intent 更快、更彈性也更貼近情境。
chapters: Share entities across apps with ValueRepresentation
Handle large entity sets with EntityCollection
Use entities across devices with SyncableEntity
Make entity IDs stable with SyncableEntity
Run beyond 30 s with LongRunningIntent + CancellableIntent
Target the right process with ExecutionTargets
Control which process runs your intent with ExecutionTargets

points.text: 用 **`ValueRepresentation`** 分享結構化實體（如以 `PlaceDescriptor` 表示地點），可用 key-path 大幅減少程式碼。
以 **`EntityCollection`** 取代 `[Entity]` 高效處理大量實體，只在需要時取用識別碼。
透過 **`SyncableEntity`** 與 `SyncableEntityIdentifier` 讓實體 ID 跨裝置穩定一致。
用 `LongRunningIntent` 搭配 `CancellableIntent` 讓 intent 執行**超過 30 秒**並回報進度、可取消。
以 **`ExecutionTargets`** 指定 intent 執行於主 App、App Intents extension 或 widget extension。

audience: **已採用 App Intents、想用進階功能提升彈性與效能**的 iOS 開發者。
gloss_en: Discover new capabilities in the App Intents framework
takeaway_en: App Intents adds **ValueRepresentation, EntityCollection, SyncableEntity, LongRunningIntent, and ExecutionTargets**, making intents faster, more flexible, and more relevant.

points_en.text: Use **`ValueRepresentation`** to share structured entities (such as representing a place with `PlaceDescriptor`), with key paths to greatly reduce code.
Use **`EntityCollection`** instead of `[Entity]` to efficiently handle large numbers of entities, fetching identifiers only when needed.
Keep entity IDs stable and consistent across devices with **`SyncableEntity`** and `SyncableEntityIdentifier`.
Use `LongRunningIntent` with `CancellableIntent` to let an intent run **longer than 30 seconds** while reporting progress and being cancellable.
Use **`ExecutionTargets`** to specify whether an intent runs in the main app, an App Intents extension, or a widget extension.

audience_en: iOS developers who **have already adopted App Intents and want to use advanced features to improve flexibility and performance**.
summary: **App Intents** 是讓 app 把自身動作與內容表達給系統其他部分（Siri、Shortcuts、Spotlight、Widgets）的框架，也是 **Apple Intelligence** 的核心支柱。本場由 App Intents 團隊的 Moe 介紹 2027 版本中、由開發者需求驅動的新能力，主軸聚焦三大領域：entities、更豐富的 parameter 型別，以及 intent 的執行控制。內容延續 WWDC25 的 Landmarks 旅遊追蹤範例 app 來逐步示範。

在 entities 方面，新增 **ValueRepresentation** 讓 entity 能把如座標等結構化資料（透過 GeoToolbox 的 **PlaceDescriptor**）分享給像 Maps 這類需要結構化資訊的 app，補足既有 file/data representation 只適用已知格式的限制。**RelevantEntities** 讓你主動告訴系統某些 entity 在特定情境（如開始跑步）下相關，補足 Spotlight 索引與 interaction donation 都無法涵蓋「全新、從未被搜尋或使用過的內容」的缺口。針對效能，**EntityCollection** 只傳遞 entity 識別碼而非完整解析的 entities，讓批次處理上千筆 entity 從緩慢變為近乎即時。**SyncableEntity** 則為跨裝置的 Siri 對話提供穩定 ID，搭配 **SyncableEntityIdentifier** 把 local 與 stable ID 配對。

在 parameter 型別上，框架為更多原生型別（如 **Duration**、**PersonNameComponents**）提供內建 picker、Siri 理解與在地化，免去自製選擇器。**@UnionValue** 巨集讓單一 parameter 能接受多種型別——以 enum 每個 case 包裝不同 entity 型別，自動產生型別資訊、case metadata 與 picker 支援，並可在 Widgets、Shortcuts 等所有 intent 出現之處運作。

在執行控制上，**LongRunningIntent** 突破 intent 預設 30 秒上限、管理背景任務生命週期，並把進度自動呈現為 **Live Activity**（須回報 progress）；搭配 **CancellableIntent** 可在使用者取消、系統逾時或需回收資源時，透過 onCancel 優雅清理。**ExecutionTargets** 則讓你明確指定 intent 該在哪個 process 執行（主 app、App Intents extension、WidgetKit extension 或其組合），覆寫系統的預設啟發式選擇——例如把寫入操作鎖定在主 app 以避免多 process 寫同一資料而衝突。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: 由 App Intents 團隊工程師 **Moe** 開場，說明 **App Intents** 是把 app 動作與內容自然且深度整合地表達給系統的框架，橫跨 Siri、Shortcuts、Spotlight、Widgets，並已成為 **Apple Intelligence** 的關鍵支柱。預告 2027 版本帶來更多控制、彈性與更順暢的開發體驗，涵蓋 entities、原生型別與 union values、以及執行控制三大主題，並以 WWDC25 的 Landmarks 旅遊追蹤 app 為基礎延伸。

deepdive.title: Share structured entities with ValueRepresentation
deepdive.body: 說明使用者會在 app 間移動，但 entity（如 landmark）原本只活在自己的 app 裡。既有的 Transferable file/data representation 適用 PDF、影像等已知格式，卻無法承載沒有檔案格式的結構化型別（如座標），導致「取得到該地點的路線（交給 Maps）」這類需求行不通。

deepdive.title: Share entities across apps with ValueRepresentation
deepdive.body: **ValueRepresentation** 是新的 representation 型別，可分享系統已理解的結構化型別。範例在 **LandmarkEntity** 既有 Transferable 旁加上 ValueRepresentation，把座標與名稱匯出為 GeoToolbox 的 **PlaceDescriptor**（內含 Maps 導航所需的座標與 metadata）；若 entity 已有 PlaceDescriptor 的 @Property，更可直接用 key-path 省去 closure。如此一來 shortcut 執行時 landmark 便以 PlaceDescriptor 流向 Maps 並開啟導航。

deepdive.title: Register relevant entities with RelevantEntities
deepdive.body: 以音樂 app CosmoTunes 的全新高節奏跑步歌單為例，提出如何讓它出現在 Fitness app 設定跑步時的建議清單。既有兩種讓內容曝光的方式——用 **Spotlight** 索引內容（也是 Siri 檢索的主要途徑），以及透過 **IntentDonationManager** 做 interaction donation 讓系統學習使用模式——但全新歌單因從未被搜尋或播放，兩者都無法涵蓋。

deepdive.title: Register relevant entities with RelevantEntities
deepdive.body: **RelevantEntities** 讓你主動向系統建議 entity 並提供相關情境。做法是先選出相關 entity（跑步歌單），建立 context 告訴系統這些歌單在開始跑步時相關，再呼叫 `updateEntities` 註冊，系統便會在對的情境下把它們當建議浮現，即使從未被播放過。entity 會保持註冊直到移除，可針對特定 context 或全部 context 清除。並總結三者取捨：Spotlight 用於可搜尋與 Siri 檢索、donation 用於教系統學使用模式、RelevantEntities 用於提示特定情境下相關的內容。

deepdive.title: Handle entities efficiently with EntityCollection
deepdive.body: 回到旅遊追蹤 app，新增讓使用者儲存自己旅遊照片的相簿，並定義帶 photos app schema 的 **PhotoEntity**，以及一個用關鍵字為照片加標籤的 intent。隨著照片庫變大，發現一次標記大量照片比預期慢，引出對問題成因的探討。

deepdive.title: Handle large entity sets with EntityCollection
deepdive.body: 問題根源在於 App Intents 在 intent 執行前會解析每個 entity（呼叫 entity query 填滿所有屬性），即使這個標籤 intent 只需要 entity ID，仍會解析成千上萬個 photo entity。**EntityCollection** 解法是儲存 entity 識別碼陣列而非完整解析的 entities，將 @Parameter 改為 EntityCollection 後系統只把識別碼傳給 perform，用 `photos.identifiers` 直接更新資料模型；實測標記 1000 張照片由緩慢變為近乎即時。

deepdive.title: Use entities across devices with SyncableEntity
deepdive.body: 2027 版本讓 Siri 能跨裝置延續對話，entity 也要能參與其中。問題在於 entity 的 ID 常是各裝置本地產生，同一 entity 在不同裝置會有不同 ID，導致在 iPhone 加入相簿的照片，換到另一裝置請 Siri 加標籤時可能找不到。Siri 跨裝置引用 entity 需要一個處處相同的 **stableID**（可來自伺服器或 CloudKit record ID）。

deepdive.title: Make entity IDs stable with SyncableEntity
deepdive.body: **SyncableEntity** 用來向系統宣告 entity 的 ID 是穩定、可跨裝置使用的。採用方式是讓 entity 遵循 SyncableEntity 協定：若 ID 本就跨裝置相同（如伺服器 UUID 或 CloudKit record ID）即可直接使用；若用的是本地識別碼（如 CoreData row ID），則以 **SyncableEntityIdentifier** 把 local 與 stable ID 配成單一 ID，裝置上用 local、跨裝置時系統用 stable。

deepdive.title: Richer parameter types
deepdive.body: 說明宣告 @Parameter 即可免費獲得原生 picker、Siri 理解與在地化，而此次把同樣支援擴展到更多原生型別。新增對 **Duration** 的原生支援（不必再自製時間選擇器）、用 **PersonNameComponents** 取代純字串做結構化姓名輸入等，每個型別都附帶原生 picker，並在 Siri、Shortcuts、Widgets 等 intent 出現處皆可運作。

deepdive.title: Accept multiple types with @UnionValue
deepdive.body: 說明 union value 是一個 Swift enum、每個 case 包裝不同型別，讓單一 parameter 能代表多個選項之一。以同時擁有 landmarks 與旅遊照片的需求為例，想用單一 widget 同時顯示相簿或 landmark collection 的照片，**@UnionValue** 對輸入 parameter 的支援正好讓一個 widget 涵蓋兩者。

deepdive.title: Union value parameters
deepdive.body: 示範以 **@UnionValue** 巨集將 enum 定義為 union value，兩個 case 分別包裝 LandmarkCollectionEntity 與 PhotoAlbumEntity；巨集自動產生型別資訊、case metadata 與 picker 支援。並用 **typeDisplayRepresentation** 設定整體型別標籤、**caseDisplayRepresentations** 對應各 case 在 picker 顯示的名稱，且此能力不限 Widgets，在 Shortcuts 等所有 intent 出現之處皆可運作。

deepdive.title: Extend execution with LongRunningIntent
deepdive.body: 指出 intent 從任何系統介面執行時只有 30 秒可完成，對多數日常動作足夠但非全部。以「不開 app 就把旅遊照片上傳到共享相簿」的上傳 intent 為例，大照片上傳因超過 30 秒上限而持續失敗，引出對 LongRunningIntent 的需求。

deepdive.title: Run beyond 30 s with LongRunningIntent + CancellableIntent
deepdive.body: **LongRunningIntent** 讓 intent 突破 30 秒上限並管理 app 背景任務生命週期，進度會自動以 **Live Activity** 呈現；它建構於 ProgressReportingIntent 之上，須回報 progress（範例以 performBackgroundTask 包裝工作、計算 chunk 數並逐塊更新進度）。Live Activity 上有停止鈕讓使用者隨時取消，而 **CancellableIntent** 透過 onCancel handler 在取消、逾時或系統回收資源時取得原因並優雅清理部分上傳。LongRunningIntent 在支援裝置上亦支援背景 GPU 存取（需加入對應 entitlement）。

deepdive.title: Target the right process with ExecutionTargets
deepdive.body: 說明隨 app 成長，intent 可能被移到 Widget extension 或 App Intents extension 等輕量獨立 process，且常把 intent、entity、query 放進共享 Swift package 供 app 與 extension 匯入。此時系統需依啟發式（如 app 已在執行就偏好 app、否則啟動 extension）決定由哪個 process 執行，但這未必正確——例如想在 widget 加最愛按鈕，但兩個 process 同時寫同一資料庫會衝突，故 widget 設唯讀、寫入交由主 app。

deepdive.title: Control which process runs your intent with ExecutionTargets
