deepdive.body: **ExecutionTargets** 讓你明確告訴系統哪個 process 該執行 intent：可指定主 app、appIntentsExtension、widgetKitExtension 或任意組合（透過 `allowedExecutionTargets`），藉此覆寫系統的啟發式選擇。例如寫入操作鎖定 `.main`、獨立下載走 extension、純顯示走 widget extension，或允許多個目標讓系統自選。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 總結建議的後續行動：為 entity 加上 **ValueRepresentation** 以攜帶結構化資料跨 app、用 **RelevantEntities** 向系統註冊相關內容、採用 **EntityCollection** 加速大量 entity 的處理、為需超過 30 秒的 intent 加上 **LongRunningIntent**。並指向「Code-along: Make your app available to Siri」以逐步建構 Siri 體驗，以及用 **AppIntentsTesting** 框架測試 intent 的相關專場。

summary_en: **App Intents** is the framework that exposes your app's actions and content to the rest of the system (Siri, Shortcuts, Spotlight, Widgets) and is now a core pillar of **Apple Intelligence**. App Intents engineer Moe introduces the new, feature-request-driven capabilities in the 2027 releases, focused on three areas: entities, richer parameter types, and intent execution control. The session builds on the WWDC25 Landmarks travel tracking sample app to demonstrate each step.

On entities, the new **ValueRepresentation** lets an entity share structured data such as coordinates (via GeoToolbox's **PlaceDescriptor**) with apps like Maps that need structured info, filling the gap left by file/data representations that only work for known formats. **RelevantEntities** lets you proactively tell the system which entities are relevant in a context (like starting a run), covering brand-new content that Spotlight indexing and interaction donation can't reach because it was never searched or used. For performance, **EntityCollection** passes only entity identifiers instead of fully resolved entities, turning batch operations over thousands of entities from slow to nearly instant. **SyncableEntity** provides stable IDs for cross-device Siri conversations, pairing local and stable IDs with **SyncableEntityIdentifier**.

For parameter types, the framework adds native pickers, Siri understanding, and localization to more native types (like **Duration** and **PersonNameComponents**), removing the need for custom pickers. The **@UnionValue** macro lets a single parameter accept multiple types, an enum whose cases each wrap a different entity type, with type info, case metadata, and picker support generated automatically, working everywhere your intent does including Widgets and Shortcuts.

For execution control, **LongRunningIntent** breaks past the default 30-second limit, manages the app's background task lifecycle, and surfaces progress automatically as a **Live Activity** (it must report progress); paired with **CancellableIntent**, an onCancel handler cleans up gracefully when the user cancels, the system times out, or resources are reclaimed. **ExecutionTargets** lets you specify exactly which process runs an intent (main app, App Intents extension, WidgetKit extension, or a combination), overriding the system's heuristics, for example pinning write operations to the main app to avoid conflicts from multiple processes writing the same data.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: App Intents engineer **Moe** opens by describing **App Intents** as the framework that expresses your app's actions and content naturally and deeply across Siri, Shortcuts, Spotlight, and Widgets, now a key pillar of **Apple Intelligence**. He previews the 2027 releases bringing more control, flexibility, and a smoother developer experience across three themes, entities, native types and union values, and execution control, building on the WWDC25 Landmarks travel tracking app.

deepdive_en.title: Share structured entities with ValueRepresentation
deepdive_en.body: Explains that people move between apps but entities (like a landmark) originally live only inside their own app. Existing Transferable file/data representations work for known formats like PDFs and images but can't carry structured types with no file format (such as coordinates), so a need like getting directions to a landmark (handing it to Maps) doesn't work.

deepdive_en.title: Share entities across apps with ValueRepresentation
deepdive_en.body: **ValueRepresentation** is a new representation type for sharing structured types the system already understands. The example adds a ValueRepresentation alongside **LandmarkEntity**'s existing Transferable, exporting the coordinate and name as GeoToolbox's **PlaceDescriptor** (carrying the coordinates and metadata Maps needs to navigate); if the entity already has a PlaceDescriptor @Property, a key-path replaces the closure entirely. Running the shortcut then flows the landmark to Maps as a PlaceDescriptor and opens directions.

deepdive_en.title: Register relevant entities with RelevantEntities
deepdive_en.body: Using the CosmoTunes music app's brand-new high-tempo running playlist, the question is how to get it into the Fitness app's suggestions when someone sets up a run. The two existing ways to surface content, indexing with **Spotlight** (also the primary path for Siri retrieval) and interaction donation via **IntentDonationManager** so the system learns patterns, both miss the new playlist since it was never searched or played.

deepdive_en.title: Register relevant entities with RelevantEntities
deepdive_en.body: **RelevantEntities** lets you proactively suggest entities and provide context for when they're relevant. You identify the relevant entities (running playlists), create a context telling the system they're relevant when someone starts a run, then call `updateEntities` to register them, and the system surfaces them as suggestions in the right context even if never played. Entities stay registered until removed, per context or across all contexts. The talk summarizes the tradeoff: Spotlight for searchable/Siri-retrievable content, donation to teach usage patterns, and RelevantEntities to hint context-specific relevance.

deepdive_en.title: Handle entities efficiently with EntityCollection
deepdive_en.body: Back in the travel tracking app, a photo album lets people save their own travel photos, with a **PhotoEntity** defined using the photos app schema, plus an intent to tag photos by keyword. As the library grew, tagging many photos at once turned out slower than expected, motivating a look at why.

deepdive_en.title: Handle large entity sets with EntityCollection
deepdive_en.body: The cause is that App Intents resolves every entity before an intent runs (calling the entity query to populate all properties), so even though the tagging intent only needs the entity ID, it resolves thousands of photo entities. **EntityCollection** stores an array of entity identifiers instead of fully resolved entities; switching the @Parameter to EntityCollection makes the system pass just identifiers to perform, using `photos.identifiers` directly, and tagging 1000 photos went from slow to almost instant.

deepdive_en.title: Use entities across devices with SyncableEntity
deepdive_en.body: The 2027 releases let Siri continue conversations across devices, and entities should take part. The challenge is that entity IDs are often generated locally per device, so the same entity ends up with different IDs, meaning a photo added to an album on iPhone might not be findable when asking Siri to tag it on another device. Cross-device referencing needs a **stableID** that's the same everywhere, from a server or CloudKit record ID.

deepdive_en.title: Make entity IDs stable with SyncableEntity
deepdive_en.body: **SyncableEntity** declares to the system that an entity's ID is stable and usable across devices. To adopt it, conform the entity to SyncableEntity: if the ID is already the same across devices (a server UUID or CloudKit record ID) no further change is needed; if you use local identifiers (like CoreData row IDs), **SyncableEntityIdentifier** pairs a local and a stable ID into one, using the local ID on-device and the stable one across devices.

deepdive_en.title: Richer parameter types
deepdive_en.body: Declaring a @Parameter gives you a native picker, Siri understanding, and localization for free, and this support is now extended to more native types. New native support for **Duration** removes the need for custom time pickers, **PersonNameComponents** enables structured name input instead of a plain string, and more, each getting a native picker and working everywhere the intent does, Siri, Shortcuts, and Widgets.

deepdive_en.title: Accept multiple types with @UnionValue
deepdive_en.body: A union value is a Swift enum whose cases each wrap a different type, letting one parameter represent one of several options. With both landmarks and travel photos in the app, the goal is a single widget showing photos from either a photo album or a landmark collection, and **@UnionValue** support for input parameters lets one widget cover both.

deepdive_en.title: Union value parameters
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates defining a union value enum with the **@UnionValue** macro, with cases wrapping LandmarkCollectionEntity and PhotoAlbumEntity; the macro generates type information, case metadata, and picker support. **typeDisplayRepresentation** sets the overall type label and **caseDisplayRepresentations** maps each case to its picker name, and this isn't limited to Widgets, working everywhere the intent does including Shortcuts.

deepdive_en.title: Extend execution with LongRunningIntent
deepdive_en.body: Notes that an intent run from any system surface has only 30 seconds to finish, fine for most everyday actions but not all. With an upload intent to share travel photos to a shared album without opening the app, large photos kept failing because the upload couldn't finish within 30 seconds, motivating LongRunningIntent.

deepdive_en.title: Run beyond 30 s with LongRunningIntent + CancellableIntent
deepdive_en.body: **LongRunningIntent** lets an intent run past the 30-second limit and manages the app's background task lifecycle, with progress shown automatically as a **Live Activity**; built on ProgressReportingIntent, it requires reporting progress (the example wraps work in performBackgroundTask, computes chunk counts, and updates progress per chunk). The Live Activity has a stop button to cancel anytime, and **CancellableIntent**'s onCancel handler receives the reason to clean up partial uploads on cancel, timeout, or resource reclamation. LongRunningIntent also supports background GPU access on supported devices (requiring the corresponding entitlement).

deepdive_en.title: Target the right process with ExecutionTargets
deepdive_en.body: As an app grows, intents may move into lightweight separate processes like a Widget extension or App Intents extension, with intents, entities, and queries often living in a shared Swift package imported by the app and extensions. The system then decides which process runs each intent via heuristics (prefer the app if running, otherwise launch the extension), but that isn't always right, for example a favorite button in a widget where two processes writing the same data store would conflict, so the widget gets read-only access and the main app handles writes.

deepdive_en.title: Control which process runs your intent with ExecutionTargets
deepdive_en.body: **ExecutionTargets** lets you tell the system exactly which process runs an intent: target the main app, appIntentsExtension, widgetKitExtension, or any combination (via `allowedExecutionTargets`), overriding the system's heuristics. For example pin a write operation to `.main`, run a standalone download in the extension, a display-only intent in the widget extension, or allow multiple targets so the system chooses.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Summarizes recommended next steps: add **ValueRepresentation** so entities carry structured data across apps, register relevant content with **RelevantEntities**, adopt **EntityCollection** to speed up intents over many entities, and add **LongRunningIntent** for any intent needing more than 30 seconds. It points to "Code-along: Make your app available to Siri" for building the Siri experience step by step, and the **AppIntentsTesting** framework session for testing intents.

title: Secure your app: mitigate risks to agentic features
gloss: 保護你的 App：降低 agentic 功能的風險
takeaway: 針對間接提示注入進行威脅建模，並用工具確認、spotlighting、redaction 與 App Intents 驗證政策來保護 agentic 功能。

points.text: 解析 **間接提示注入（indirect prompt injection）** 帶來的資料外洩與非預期行為風險。
以 **威脅建模** 區分高風險工具（如有財務影響的下單）與會回傳不可信資料的工具。
用 **onToolCall** 在執行高風險工具前要求使用者確認，避免未授權動作。
透過 **historyTransform** 對不可信工具輸出做 spotlighting 標記與 PII redaction。
為 App Intents 設定 **authenticationPolicy（.requiresAuthentication）**，保護刪除等敏感操作。

audience: 正在 App 中加入 **LLM 工具呼叫或 agentic 功能**、需要把關安全性的開發者。
gloss_en: Secure your app: mitigate risks to agentic features
takeaway_en: Threat-model indirect prompt injection and protect agentic features with tool confirmation, spotlighting, redaction, and App Intents authentication policies.

points_en.text: Breaks down the data-exfiltration and unintended-action risks posed by **indirect prompt injection**.
Use **threat modeling** to distinguish high-risk tools (such as placing an order with financial impact) from tools that return untrusted data.
Use **onToolCall** to require user confirmation before running high-risk tools, preventing unauthorized actions.
Use **historyTransform** to apply spotlighting tags and PII redaction to untrusted tool output.
Set an **authenticationPolicy (.requiresAuthentication)** for App Intents to protect sensitive operations like deletion.

audience_en: Developers adding **LLM tool calls or agentic features** to their app who need to enforce security.
summary: 本場由 Willy 與 Akshay 主講，主題是辨識並緩解 app 中 **agentic 功能**帶來的新安全風險。當 LLM 成為 app 的關鍵元件、能依使用者請求與額外 context 執行一或多個動作後再回應，它就引入一個強大但**可能被騙**的機率引擎。講者明確界定範圍：不談 model safety、不談 guardrail 繞過，而是聚焦於**外部攻擊者**試圖破壞你的應用。攻擊者覬覦 app 的原因在於它可能持有敏感資料、執行金流交易、存取麥克風／相機等系統資源，甚至控制實體裝置。

核心風險是 **indirect prompt injection**（間接提示注入）：嵌在提供給模型之額外 context 或 tool 結果中、意圖改變控制流的指令。以虛構社群 app **Loose Leaf** 的「Organize a tea party」功能為例——它從多處取得 context（行事曆、好友動態）並能代使用者呼叫多個帶副作用的動作。注入可造成兩種效果：**data poisoning**（影響動作的參數，如把訊息改送給攻擊者）與 **action poisoning**（影響執行哪個動作，如把摘要 email 改成把內容附在攻擊者網址後開啟）。對應 Simon Willison 的 **Lethal Trifecta**：同時具備存取私密資料、接觸不可信內容、能對外通訊（可泛化為任何有副作用的動作）時風險最高。講者強調 prompt injection 仍是活躍研究領域，目前最佳做法是評估風險並設法緩解。

緩解前先做 **threat modeling**：對 agentic loop 的輸入（prompt）做資料流分析，找出所有不可信 context 來源（凡來自外部實體者皆為攻擊面，如行事曆邀請與好友動態）；再檢視 agent 可用的動作與其副作用（OrderTea 有金流風險、PostAndFetchPublicFeed 有資料外洩風險、BrewingTimer 的 label 可能被寫入後續攻擊指令、Delete Photo 有資料遺失風險）。緩解應**優先採用確定性（deterministic）手段**（安全保證易稽核），其次才是機率性手段；可在 prompt 層（redact PII、spotlighting 標示不可信內容）或動作執行階段（使用者確認、要求裝置解鎖）設檢查點。

Akshay 接著示範平台上的具體 API。**Foundation Models** 端用 **lifecycle event modifiers** 在 agent 執行中注入安全檢查點：**`onToolCall`** 在工具實際執行前觸發，丟錯即可阻止執行——適合對 OrderTea 這類有金流影響的工具強制使用者確認；**`historyTransform`** 在 transcript 送入推論前觸發，可對不可信的 tool 輸出加上 **spotlighting** 分隔標籤、或把敏感資料 **redact** 成佔位字串（注意轉換僅限當次推論、需重複套用，昂貴轉換則用 `@SessionProperty` 持久化）。**App Intents** 端：當 intent 採用 schema 而成為 Siri 工具時，系統以**風險導向、情境化的確認機制**——結合 intent 的風險 metadata（隨採用的 schema 自動指派，依副作用判定）與動態系統狀態決定是否需要確認（連 createTimer 這種看似無害、但 label 可被注入的也會被情境化評估）；並用 **authentication policy**（`.requiresAuthentication`）防範鎖定畫面攻擊，schema 有預設政策、可覆寫但只能更嚴格。下一步：建立威脅模型、找出不可信 context、依副作用評估各動作風險，再用兩個框架實作最適緩解。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: Willy 開場：隨 LLM 普及，許多 app 用它打造智慧功能而使 LLM 成為關鍵元件——可依使用者請求與額外 context 執行一或多個動作後再回應。但這引入一個強大卻**可能被騙**的機率引擎。明確界定範圍：不談 model safety 與 guardrail 繞過，而聚焦於**外部攻擊者**破壞你的應用；後半由 Akshay 講平台上可用的具體 API。

deepdive.title: Risks
deepdive.body: 說明攻擊者為何鎖定你的 app：它可能持有敏感資料、執行金流、存取麥克風／相機、甚至控制實體裝置。以虛構社群 app **Loose Leaf** 的「Organize a tea party」為例（查行事曆找時間、依好友 profile 決定邀請與茶款、並下單），點出兩個性質：從多處取得 context、能代使用者呼叫帶副作用的動作。由此帶出 **indirect prompt injection**——嵌在額外 context 或 tool 結果中、意圖改變控制流的指令（如行事曆事件內含刪除使用者資料的指令）。

deepdive.title: Threat modeling
deepdive.body: 進入威脅建模：對 agentic loop 的輸入（prompt）做資料流分析，找出構成 prompt 的資料來源並指認哪些**不可信**（凡來自外部實體者皆為攻擊面）。Loose Leaf 的來源含 instructions、使用者 prompt、額外 context（過往訂單、茶譜、行事曆、好友動態），其中**行事曆內容與好友動態**被判為不可信（任何人都能寄行事曆邀請或在動態發文）。接著檢視動作與副作用：OrderTea 有金流風險、PostAndFetchPublicFeed 有資料外洩風險、BrewingTimer 的 label 可被寫入後續攻擊指令、Delete Photo 有資料遺失風險。並對應 Simon Willison 的 **Lethal Trifecta**（私密資料＋不可信內容＋對外通訊／任何副作用）。

deepdive.title: Implementing mitigations
deepdive.body: 概述緩解原則：**優先採用確定性（deterministic）緩解**作為基線，因其安全保證較易稽核與推理；鑑於模型能力快速演進，也可輔以機率性緩解。可在 prompt 層或動作執行階段設檢查點，Apple 設計 Siri AI 時也用了其中部分手段。

deepdive.title: Foundation Models
deepdive.body: Akshay 接手，聚焦 Foundation Models 框架，將以 **lifecycle event modifier** API 注入安全 guardrail（假設讀者已具基本認識）。先為 Loose Leaf 建立簡單 agent。

deepdive.title: Tools
deepdive.body: 定義工具：符合 Tool 協定、指定 name／description／Arguments（模型靠這些 metadata 理解用途與呼叫方式）並提供實作。示範 OrderTea 工具與 PostAndFetchPublicFeed 工具（會把訊息貼到公開動態並取回新貼文）。

deepdive.title: Profile
deepdive.body: 建立 **Profile**：加入模型 instructions 與剛定義的工具，再附上 session properties（如指定使用哪個模型，此處用 on-device 模型）。此 Profile 用來實例化 LanguageModelSession，供 agentic loop 使用。

deepdive.title: Session
deepdive.body: 有了基本 agent 後開始注入安全政策：用 **lifecycle event modifiers**——這些 callback 會在 session 執行的特定生命週期點**確定性地**觸發，故可作為實作安全政策的檢查點。接著介紹其中兩個。

deepdive.title: Confirmation via onToolCall
deepdive.body: 第一個 modifier 是 **`onToolCall`**：保證在 LLM 輸出 tool call、executor 實際執行工具**之前**觸發；若此 callback 丟錯，工具就不會執行、控制權立即回到迴圈，因此是強制**確認**的最佳位置。範例對有金流影響的 OrderTea 加上 onToolCall：先判斷是否為該工具，是則向使用者確認，未確認就丟錯阻止執行。只在這一處加確認邏輯，就能涵蓋所有 tool call。

deepdive.title: Spotlighting via historyTransform
deepdive.body: 第二個 modifier **`historyTransform`** 在 transcript 送入推論前觸發（新請求與每次迴圈迭代皆會），轉換 transcript 尾端。因 PostAndFetchPublicFeed 會回傳公開動態（攻擊者易在此植入注入），需以特殊標籤標示為不可信：在 callback 中只針對該工具的 toolOutput entry、逐 segment 加上 **spotlighting** 分隔標籤（範例用角括號），其餘 entry 原樣複製。

deepdive.title: Redaction via historyTransform
deepdive.body: 同樣的 historyTransform 思路也可用於 **redaction**：把 `delimit()` 換成把敏感資料替換為佔位字串的 redaction 函式即可。重點提醒：轉換後的 entry 僅限**當次推論迭代**、下次推論不可見，必須重複套用；若想持久化昂貴的轉換，改用 `@SessionProperty` 註記做有狀態的 history 轉換。並指出框架還有更多 modifier 與可自製、可打包重用的 profile modifier。

deepdive.title: App Intents
deepdive.body: 切換到 **App Intents**：它讓 app 整合 Apple Intelligence 與 Siri、Spotlight、Shortcuts 等系統體驗。當 App Intent 採用 intent schema（如 DeletePhotoIntent 採用 photos 領域的 deleteAssets schema），它就成為 Siri 模型可用的工具——但因由模型決定呼叫哪個 intent，prompt injection 可能濫用你的 app 做資料外洩等惡意目的（如在外部 context 下擅自執行 Delete Photo）。系統提供多種 guardrail，將介紹 confirmations 與 lock-screen authentication 兩者。

deepdive.title: Intent authentication policy
deepdive.body: 講 lock screen authentication：Siri 可在鎖定畫面互動，意味著實體持有鎖定裝置的攻擊者可能透過 Siri 觸發你的 intent，主要緩解是在執行高風險動作前要求解鎖。自訂 App Intent 可設 **`authenticationPolicy`**（如把 destructive 的 DeletePhotoIntent 設為 `.requiresAuthentication`）。先前也談到 confirmation：系統以風險導向、情境化機制，結合靜態風險 metadata（隨採用的 schema 自動指派、依副作用判定，如 deleteAssets 屬 destructive）與動態系統狀態決定是否確認，連 createTimer 這種 label 可被注入的也會被情境評估。

deepdive.title: Schema authentication policy
deepdive.body: 當 @AppIntent 採用 schema 時情況略有不同：schema 有依其敏感度與處理資料而內部設定的**預設 authenticationPolicy**，會自動指派給你的 intent；你可覆寫，但**只能更嚴格**（設更弱會得到 build error 並提示最低允許政策）。小結：認證是鎖定畫面攻擊的重要緩解，請依鎖定畫面行為檢視你的 intent。最後 Willy 總結下一步：建立威脅模型、找出 prompt 中不可信 context、依副作用判定各動作風險，再用 Foundation Models 與 App Intents 框架實作最適緩解。

summary_en: Presented by Willy and Akshay, this session is about identifying and mitigating new security risks from **agentic features** in your app. When an LLM becomes a key component that can execute one or more actions on the user's request plus extra context before responding, it introduces a powerful but **trickable** probabilistic engine. The speakers explicitly scope out model safety and guardrail circumvention, focusing instead on an **external attacker** trying to compromise your app. Attackers target apps because they may hold sensitive data, perform financial transactions, access system resources like the microphone or camera, or even control physical devices.

The core risk is **indirect prompt injection**: instructions embedded in extra context or tool results provided to the model, intended to redirect control flow. Using the fictional social app **Loose Leaf** and its 'Organize a tea party' feature—which pulls context from multiple places (calendar, friend feed) and can call multiple side-effecting actions on the user's behalf—the talk shows two effects: **data poisoning** (influencing an action's parameters, e.g., redirecting a message to the attacker) and **action poisoning** (influencing which action runs, e.g., turning 'summarize an email' into opening an attacker URL with the email appended). This maps to Simon Willison's **Lethal Trifecta**: risk is highest when an agent has access to private data, exposure to untrusted content, and the ability to communicate externally (generalizable to any side-effecting action). The speakers stress prompt injection is an active research area, so the best approach is to assess and mitigate risk.

Before mitigating, do **threat modeling**: a data-flow analysis of the agentic loop's input (the prompt) to find all untrusted context sources (anything from an external entity is attack surface, like calendar invites and the friend feed), then examine the actions available and their side effects (OrderTea has financial risk, PostAndFetchPublicFeed has data-exfiltration risk, BrewingTimer's label can be written with future attack instructions, Delete Photo has data-loss risk). Mitigations should **favor deterministic approaches** (easier to audit) over probabilistic ones, with checkpoints at the prompt level (redact PII, spotlighting untrusted content) or the action-execution stage (user confirmation, requiring an unlocked device).

Akshay then demonstrates concrete platform APIs. On **Foundation Models**, use **lifecycle event modifiers** to inject security checkpoints into agent execution: **`onToolCall`** fires before a tool actually runs, and throwing an error blocks it—perfect for forcing user confirmation on financially impactful tools like OrderTea; **`historyTransform`** fires before the transcript is rendered to the model, letting you add **spotlighting** delimiters around untrusted tool output or **redact** sensitive data to a placeholder (note transforms are scoped to the current inference and must be reapplied; use `@SessionProperty` to persist expensive ones). On **App Intents**: when an intent adopts a schema and becomes a Siri tool, the system uses a **risk-based, contextual confirmation** mechanism—combining the intent's risk metadata (auto-assigned by the adopted schema based on side effects) with dynamic system state to decide if confirmation is needed (even createTimer, whose label can be injected, is evaluated contextually); and **authentication policy** (`.requiresAuthentication`) guards against lock-screen attacks, with schemas providing defaults you can override only to be stricter. Next steps: build a threat model, find untrusted context, rate each action's risk by side effects, then implement the best mitigations with both frameworks.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Willy opens: as LLMs become commonplace, many apps use them for intelligent features, making the LLM a key component that can execute one or more actions on the user's request plus extra context before responding—introducing a powerful but **trickable** probabilistic engine. He scopes out model safety and guardrail circumvention, focusing on an **external attacker** compromising your app; Akshay covers concrete platform APIs in the second half.

deepdive_en.title: Risks
deepdive_en.body: Explains why attackers target your app: it may hold sensitive data, perform financial transactions, access the mic/camera, or control physical devices. The fictional **Loose Leaf** app's 'Organize a tea party' (check calendar for timing, choose invitees and teas from friend profiles, place orders) highlights two properties: it pulls context from many places and can call side-effecting actions on the user's behalf. This introduces **indirect prompt injection**—instructions embedded in extra context or tool results to redirect control flow (e.g., a calendar event with instructions to delete user data).

deepdive_en.title: Threat modeling
deepdive_en.body: Enters threat modeling: a data-flow analysis of the loop's input (the prompt) to find its data sources and identify which are **untrusted** (anything from an external entity is attack surface). Loose Leaf's sources include instructions, the user prompt, and extra context (past orders, recipes, calendar, friend feed), with **calendar content and the friend feed** deemed untrusted (anyone can send an invite or post). It then examines actions and side effects: OrderTea (financial), PostAndFetchPublicFeed (data exfiltration), BrewingTimer's label (can carry future attack instructions), Delete Photo (data loss)—mapping to Simon Willison's **Lethal Trifecta** (private data + untrusted content + external communication/any side effect).

deepdive_en.title: Implementing mitigations
deepdive_en.body: Overviews the principle: **favor deterministic mitigations** as a baseline because their guarantees are easier to audit and reason about, supplemented by probabilistic ones given fast-moving model capabilities. Checkpoints can be added at the prompt level or the action-execution stage—some of which Apple used designing Siri AI.

deepdive_en.title: Foundation Models
deepdive_en.body: Akshay takes over, focusing on Foundation Models and using its **lifecycle event modifier** API to inject security guardrails (assuming basic familiarity). He first builds a simple agent for Loose Leaf.

deepdive_en.title: Tools
deepdive_en.body: Defines tools: conform to the Tool protocol, specify name/description/Arguments (metadata the model uses to understand purpose and how to call), and provide an implementation. Shows an OrderTea tool and a PostAndFetchPublicFeed tool (posts a message to the public feed and retrieves new posts).

deepdive_en.title: Profile
deepdive_en.body: Builds a **Profile**: add model instructions and the defined tools, then attach session properties (like which model—here the on-device model). This Profile instantiates a LanguageModelSession for use in an agentic loop.

deepdive_en.title: Session
deepdive_en.body: With a basic agent, injects security policy via **lifecycle event modifiers**—callbacks that **deterministically** trigger at certain lifecycle points, usable as security-policy checkpoints. Two are introduced next.

deepdive_en.title: Confirmation via onToolCall
deepdive_en.body: The first modifier, **`onToolCall`**, is guaranteed to fire after the LLM outputs a tool call but **before** the executor runs it; if the callback throws, the tool never runs and control returns to the loop—making it the perfect place for **confirmation**. The example adds onToolCall for the financially impactful OrderTea: check if it's that tool, and if so ask the user to confirm, throwing to block execution if they decline. Adding confirmation at this one point covers all tool calls.

deepdive_en.title: Spotlighting via historyTransform
deepdive_en.body: The second modifier, **`historyTransform`**, fires before the transcript is rendered to the model (on new requests and each loop iteration), transforming the transcript's tail. Since PostAndFetchPublicFeed returns a public feed (easy to inject into), demarcate it as untrusted: in the callback, focus only on that tool's toolOutput entries, add **spotlighting** delimiters per segment (angle brackets in the example), and copy all other entries unmodified.

deepdive_en.title: Redaction via historyTransform
deepdive_en.body: The same historyTransform idea applies to **redaction**: swap `delimit()` for a redaction function that replaces sensitive data with a placeholder. Key reminder: transformed entries are scoped to the **current inference iteration** only and aren't visible to the next call, so reapply them; to persist expensive transformations, use the `@SessionProperty` annotation. Notes the framework has many more modifiers and lets you build reusable custom profile modifiers.

deepdive_en.title: App Intents
deepdive_en.body: Switches to **App Intents**, which integrate apps with Apple Intelligence and system experiences like Siri, Spotlight, and Shortcuts. When an App Intent adopts an intent schema (e.g., DeletePhotoIntent adopting the photos deleteAssets schema), it becomes a tool for the Siri model—but since the model decides which intent to call, a prompt injection can misuse the app for data exfiltration or other goals (e.g., running Delete Photo under external context). The system offers several guardrails; confirmations and lock-screen authentication are covered.

deepdive_en.title: Intent authentication policy
deepdive_en.body: On lock-screen authentication: Siri works on the lock screen, so an attacker with physical possession of a locked device could invoke your intent via Siri—the main mitigation is requiring the device to be unlocked before risky actions. Custom App Intents can set **`authenticationPolicy`** (e.g., the destructive DeletePhotoIntent set to `.requiresAuthentication`). Earlier, confirmations: the system uses a risk-based, contextual mechanism combining static risk metadata (auto-assigned by the adopted schema based on side effects, e.g., deleteAssets is destructive) with dynamic system state to decide on confirmation, even evaluating createTimer (whose label can be injected) contextually.

deepdive_en.title: Schema authentication policy
deepdive_en.body: When an @AppIntent adopts a schema, it's slightly different: schemas have a **default authenticationPolicy** set internally based on sensitivity and data handled, automatically assigned to your intent; you can override it but **only to be stricter** (a weaker policy yields a build error citing the minimum allowed). Recap: authentication is an important mitigation for lock-screen attacks—review your intents with lock-screen behavior in mind. Willy closes with next steps: build a threat model, find untrusted context in the prompt, rate each action's risk by side effects, then implement the best mitigations with the Foundation Models and App Intents frameworks.

title: Bringing Cyberpunk 2077 to Mac
gloss: 將《電馭叛客 2077》帶上 Mac
takeaway: CD PROJEKT RED 分享如何運用 Game Porting Toolkit 將《電馭叛客 2077》移植到 macOS，並透過「For this Mac」預設樹立 AAA 遊戲新標竿。
chapters: How we brought it to Mac
What we did to stand out

points.text: **CD PROJEKT RED** 分享將 AAA 大作《電馭叛客 2077》移植至 **macOS** 的幕後歷程與決策。
說明**為何要登上 Mac**，以及整體的移植策略與工程流程。
使用 **Game Porting Toolkit** 進行可行性評估，加速從 Windows 到 Mac 的移植。
推出 **「For this Mac」預設**，依機型自動最佳化畫質設定，做出與眾不同的體驗。

audience: **遊戲開發者與想將大型遊戲移植到 macOS** 的工作室，特別是關注 AAA 等級效能與最佳化者。
gloss_en: Bringing Cyberpunk 2077 to Mac
takeaway_en: CD PROJEKT RED shares how they used the Game Porting Toolkit to bring Cyberpunk 2077 to macOS, setting a new bar for AAA gaming with the "For this Mac" preset.

points_en.text: **CD PROJEKT RED** shares the behind-the-scenes story and decisions of porting the AAA blockbuster Cyberpunk 2077 to **macOS**.
Explains **why bring it to the Mac**, along with the overall porting strategy and engineering process.
Uses the **Game Porting Toolkit** for feasibility assessment, accelerating the port from Windows to Mac.
Introduces the **"For this Mac" preset**, which automatically optimizes graphics settings per model to deliver a distinctive experience.

audience_en: **Game developers and studios looking to port large games to macOS**, especially those focused on AAA-class performance and optimization.
summary: Apple Game Performance 團隊的 Garrett Austin 與 CD PROJEKT RED 副遊戲總監 Paweł Sasko，分享如何把 **Cyberpunk 2077: Ultimate Edition** 帶上 Mac，並成為 macOS 上 AAA 遊戲的新標竿。Cyberpunk 2077 是設定在 Night City 的開放世界 RPG，無讀取畫面、海量資料持續處理，混合光照無處不在，並支援 ray tracing 與 path tracing；它從一開始就以可擴展（scaleable）為設計，這在移植 Mac 時幫了大忙。

團隊為自己訂下三項品質標準：維持視覺保真與遊戲識別（光照、材質）、在重 CPU/GPU 場景下的穩定效能，以及讓體驗感覺原生的收尾。實際開發前，先用 **Game Porting Toolkit** 在 macOS 的轉譯環境評估 Windows build，目的不是最終效能數字，而是了解 frame time 花在哪、瓶頸在 CPU 還是 GPU、該優先處理什麼。評估時從三個角度看資料：引擎內 profiler 的統計 frame time、**Metal HUD**、以及依執行緒拆解的引擎內部 profiling。訊號顯示高階硬體上 GPU 健康，重度遊玩則受 CPU 壓力影響；live shader translation 與 audio middleware 等問題在轉為 native binary 後解決。

production roadmap 分為：把 Mac 變成真正目標（native build、資料管線、架構橋接與單元測試）、用 **Metal API** 與 **Metal shader converter** 取得可玩 build、再加上原生功能、最佳化與打磨。Metal 後端逐步從單元測試、靜態場景到動態場景帶起；效能擴展靠 **MetalFX Upscaling** 搭配 **Dynamic Resolution Scaling**，以較低內部解析度重建高解析輸出。亮點是 **"For this Mac"** preset：偵測硬體並自動設定最佳設定（目標 30 或 60 FPS、MetalFX+DRS、解析度上下界、VSync、依顯示器能力開 HDR），讓玩家首次啟動即獲穩定體驗。

團隊還採用多項平台原生功能：用 NSNotification 回應 app 切換與顯示變更（如 `NSWindowDidChangeOcclusionStateNotification` 在背景時暫停 render）、Game Mode 自動啟用、Game Controller framework 支援第三方控制器與 Magic Mouse/trackpad、透過 Apple 的 **EDR** pipeline 用 `maximumExtendedDynamicRangeColorComponentValue` 自動校準 HDR、用 AVAudioEngine 的 `listenerHeadTrackingEnabled` 為 AirPods 啟用頭部追蹤的 spatial audio，以及 iCloud Drive 與跨平台存檔。成果是榮獲 Apple 2025 App Store Awards 的 Mac 年度遊戲。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: Apple Game Performance 團隊的 Garrett Austin 開場，介紹特別來賓——CD PROJEKT RED 副遊戲總監 Paweł Sasko，將分享把 **Cyberpunk 2077: Ultimate Edition** 帶上 Mac 的歷程，並善用平台特性、在多種 Mac 上提供良好效能。

deepdive.title: What is Cyberpunk 2077
deepdive.body: 說明 Cyberpunk 2077 是設定在 Night City、扮演傭兵 V 的開放世界 RPG：龐大世界、無讀取畫面、海量資料持續處理。大量 CPU 壓力來自人群、交通、AI、物理、動畫與任務；混合光照無處不在，並支援 ray tracing 與 path tracing 等隨 GPU 能力擴展的進階模式。

deepdive.title: Why bring it to Mac
deepdive.body: 說明帶上 Mac 的理由：CD PROJEKT RED 在 Apple 平台有長久歷史，隨 Apple silicon 演進，硬體能力已足以在認真的品質水準上承載 Cyberpunk 規模的遊戲，並能觸及更多玩家。

deepdive.title: How we brought it to Mac
deepdive.body: 訂出三項品質標準：維持視覺保真與遊戲識別（光照、材質）、在重 CPU/GPU 場景（大量人群、screen space reflections、密集區域駕駛、戰鬥）下的穩定效能，以及讓體驗感覺原生的收尾。

deepdive.title: Game Porting Toolkit evaluation
deepdive.body: 正式寫 native 程式碼前，用 **Game Porting Toolkit** 在 macOS 轉譯環境評估 Windows build，取得「是否可行、壓力在哪、該先做什麼」的洞見。以預設 hotspot 序列從三角度看資料：引擎 profiler 的統計 frame time、**Metal HUD**、依執行緒拆解的內部 profiling。高階硬體 GPU 健康，重度遊玩受 CPU 壓力；live shader translation 與 audio middleware 等為評估環境 artifact，轉 native 後解決。

deepdive.title: What we did to stand out
deepdive.body: 帶出讓 Mac 版脫穎而出的收尾：預設設定（首次啟動的樣貌）、用平台原生功能差異化，以及整體體驗打磨。

deepdive.title: "For this Mac" preset
deepdive.body: introduces **"For this Mac"** preset：偵測 Mac 硬體並自動配置最佳設定，讓任何支援的 Mac 一啟動即獲穩定起點。流程包含為每台裝置挑選維持影像保真的設定、目標 30 或 60 FPS、用 MetalFX+Dynamic Resolution Scaling 並調最小/最大解析度、設定輸出解析度與 VSync、依顯示器能力開 HDR，再逐項調校。示範以 M5 Max MacBook Pro 載入 Dogtown 的 Black Market 重場景，於 out-of-box 設定下穩定 60 FPS，並聊到把創辦人掃描進遊戲的彩蛋。最後總結採用 windowing/app 切換、控制器、顯示與音訊、雲端存檔等平台原生功能：用 `NSWindowDidChangeOcclusionStateNotification` 在背景暫停 render、用 `NSApplicationDidChangeScreenParametersNotification` 與 `NSWindowDidChangeScreenNotification` 回應顯示變更、用 resign/become key 通知切換游標；Game Mode 自動啟用以提高 CPU/GPU 優先權並降低無線延遲；Game Controller framework 支援第三方控制器與 Magic Mouse/trackpad；透過 EDR 以 `maximumExtendedDynamicRangeColorComponentValue` 自動校準 HDR、以 `maximumPotential...` 大於 2.0 自動開 HDR；用 AVAudioEngine 的 `listenerHeadTrackingEnabled` 為 AirPods 啟用頭追 spatial audio；並支援 iCloud Drive 與跨平台存檔。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: Garrett 收尾，鼓勵試用 Game Porting Toolkit 評估環境（無需程式碼、設定快速）、用 Metal HUD 評估效能，並透過優化設定與啟用 EDR、AirPods 頭追 spatial audio 等原生功能打造出色首次啟動體驗。並推薦「Speedrun your game port with agentic coding」與「Find and fix performance issues in your Metal games」兩場延伸。

summary_en: Apple's Game Performance team (Garrett Austin) and CD PROJEKT RED's Associate Game Director (Paweł Sasko) share how they brought **Cyberpunk 2077: Ultimate Edition** to Mac, setting a new standard for AAA gaming on macOS. Cyberpunk 2077 is an open-world RPG set in Night City with no loading screens, constant heavy data processing, mixed lighting everywhere, and support for ray tracing and path tracing; it was designed from the start to be scaleable, which helped greatly on Mac.

The team set three quality bars: preserving visual fidelity and the game's identity (lighting, materials), stable performance in heavy CPU/GPU scenes, and finishing touches that feel native. Before writing native code, they used the **Game Porting Toolkit** to evaluate the Windows build in a translated environment on macOS — the goal was information (where frame time goes, CPU vs. GPU pressure, what to build first), not final numbers. They looked at data three ways: in-engine profiler frame-time stats, the **Metal HUD**, and per-thread engine profiling. Signals showed healthy GPU on high-spec hardware, with CPU pressure in heavy gameplay; live shader translation and audio middleware artifacts were resolved once native.

The production roadmap: make Mac a real target (native builds, data pipeline, architecture bridge with unit tests), reach a playable build with the **Metal API** and **Metal shader converter**, then add native features, optimize, and polish. The Metal backend was brought up incrementally from unit tests to stationary then dynamic scenes; performance scaling relied on **MetalFX Upscaling** with **Dynamic Resolution Scaling**, rendering at a lower internal resolution and reconstructing a higher-resolution output. The highlight is the **"For this Mac"** preset: it detects the hardware and auto-configures the best settings (target 30 or 60 FPS, MetalFX+DRS, resolution bounds, VSync, HDR per display capability) so players get a stable experience on first launch.

The team also adopted many platform-native features: NSNotifications for app switching and display changes (e.g. `NSWindowDidChangeOcclusionStateNotification` to pause rendering in the background), automatic Game Mode, the Game Controller framework for third-party controllers and Magic Mouse/trackpad, automatic HDR calibration via Apple's **EDR** pipeline using `maximumExtendedDynamicRangeColorComponentValue`, head-tracked spatial audio for AirPods via AVAudioEngine's `listenerHeadTrackingEnabled`, and iCloud Drive plus cross-platform saves. The result earned Mac Game of the Year at Apple's 2025 App Store Awards.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Apple Game Performance's Garrett Austin opens, introducing special guest Paweł Sasko, Associate Game Director at CD PROJEKT RED, who will share bringing **Cyberpunk 2077: Ultimate Edition** to Mac while leveraging platform features and delivering good performance across many Macs.

deepdive_en.title: What is Cyberpunk 2077
deepdive_en.body: Describes Cyberpunk 2077 as an open-world RPG set in Night City as mercenary V: a massive world, no loading screens, constant heavy data processing. Much CPU pressure comes from crowds, traffic, AI, physics, animation, and quests; mixed lighting is everywhere, with ray tracing and path tracing scaling with GPU capability.

deepdive_en.title: Why bring it to Mac
deepdive_en.body: Explains the reasons: CD PROJEKT RED has a long history on Apple platforms, and as Apple silicon evolved, hardware became capable enough to carry a Cyberpunk-scale game at a serious quality level — and reach more players.

deepdive_en.title: How we brought it to Mac
deepdive_en.body: Sets three quality bars: preserving visual fidelity and the game's identity (lighting, materials), stable performance in heavy CPU/GPU scenes (large crowds, screen-space reflections, dense-area driving, combat), and finishing touches that feel native.

deepdive_en.title: Game Porting Toolkit evaluation
deepdive_en.body: Before native code, they used the **Game Porting Toolkit** to evaluate the Windows build in a translated macOS environment for insight on feasibility, pressure points, and what to build first. Predetermined hotspot sequences were viewed three ways: engine profiler frame-time stats, the **Metal HUD**, and per-thread internal profiling. GPU was healthy on high-spec hardware, with CPU pressure in heavy gameplay; live shader translation and audio middleware were evaluation-environment artifacts resolved once native.

deepdive_en.title: What we did to stand out
deepdive_en.body: Introduces the finishing work that makes the Mac version stand out: default settings (how it looks on first launch), differentiating with platform-native features, and overall polish.

deepdive_en.title: "For this Mac" preset
deepdive_en.body: Introduces the **"For this Mac"** preset: it detects the Mac's hardware and auto-configures the best settings so any supported Mac gets a stable starting point on launch. The process picks fidelity-preserving settings per device, targets 30 or 60 FPS, uses MetalFX+Dynamic Resolution Scaling with tuned min/max resolution, sets output resolution and VSync, and enables HDR per display capability, then tunes each setting. The demo loads Dogtown's Black Market on an M5 Max MacBook Pro at a steady 60 FPS out of the box, with an easter egg of the founders scanned in. It then covers platform-native features: `NSWindowDidChangeOcclusionStateNotification` to pause rendering in the background; `NSApplicationDidChangeScreenParametersNotification` and `NSWindowDidChangeScreenNotification` for display changes; resign/become-key notifications for cursor handling; automatic Game Mode for CPU/GPU priority and lower wireless latency; the Game Controller framework for third-party controllers and Magic Mouse/trackpad; automatic HDR calibration via EDR using `maximumExtendedDynamicRangeColorComponentValue` and auto-enabling HDR when `maximumPotential...` exceeds 2.0; head-tracked spatial audio for AirPods via AVAudioEngine's `listenerHeadTrackingEnabled`; and iCloud Drive with cross-platform saves.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Garrett closes, encouraging trying the Game Porting Toolkit evaluation environment (no code, fast setup), using Metal HUD to evaluate performance, and building a great first-launch experience with optimized settings and native features like EDR and AirPods head-tracked spatial audio. Recommends 'Speedrun your game port with agentic coding' and 'Find and fix performance issues in your Metal games'.

title: Speedrun your game port with agentic coding
gloss: 用代理式編碼加速遊戲移植
takeaway: 用 Game Porting Toolkit 4 的新代理式技能，大幅加速把遊戲移植到 Apple 平台，並把 D3D12 對應到 Metal 4。
chapters: Map D3D12 states to Metal 4 stages

points.text: **Game Porting Toolkit 4** 新增**代理式技能（agentic skills）**，可大幅加速遊戲移植到 Apple 平台的歷程。
透過 **/plugin** 安裝 game-porting-skills，並導入移植助理工作流程，處理視窗化與**影格節奏（frame pacing）**。
用 **Metal 4** 算繪場景：登錄資源 residency、查詢 argument buffer 位移，並把 **D3D12** 狀態對應到 Metal 4 階段。
用 **IRShaderReflection** 查詢著色器參數數量，並借助 GPU 命令列工具除錯。
整合遊戲控制器與 **MetalFX**，完善移植後的輸入與升頻體驗。

audience: **要把 Windows/D3D12 遊戲移植到 Apple 平台**、想用 AI 代理加速移植與 Metal 4 轉換的遊戲開發者。
gloss_en: Speedrun your game port with agentic coding
takeaway_en: Use the new agentic skills in Game Porting Toolkit 4 to dramatically accelerate porting your game to Apple platforms, and map D3D12 to Metal 4.

points_en.text: **Game Porting Toolkit 4** adds **agentic skills** that can dramatically accelerate the journey of porting games to Apple platforms.
Install game-porting-skills via **/plugin** and adopt the porting-assistant workflow to handle windowing and **frame pacing**.
Render scenes with **Metal 4**: register resource residency, query argument buffer offsets, and map **D3D12** state to Metal 4 stages.
Use **IRShaderReflection** to query shader parameter counts, and debug with the help of GPU command-line tools.
Integrate game controllers and **MetalFX** to round out input and upscaling for the ported experience.

audience_en: Game developers who **want to port Windows/D3D12 games to Apple platforms** and use AI agents to accelerate the port and the Metal 4 conversion.
summary: 這場由 Metal 生態系團隊的 David Srour 主講，核心訊息是：coding agent 正在徹底改變遊戲移植的方式，過去需要數月的手動平台工作，現在能在極短時間內完成。**Game Porting Toolkit 4** 帶來全新的 **agentic skills**，讓你的 coding agent 具備把遊戲移植到 Apple 平台所需的專業知識，速度與品質都遠勝以往。整個工具組分成三類：提供技術指引的 **expert skills**、提供結構化流程的 **workflow skills**，以及把兩者串起來的 **porting assistant** 代理人。

porting assistant 採用 discover、plan、execute／validate 的三階段方法論。**discover** 會分析你的程式碼庫、從評估環境抓取 ground truth 參考擷取，並詢問你的偏好；接著與你一起規劃 **milestone** 目標（因為整套遊戲通常太大，無法一次完成）；每個 milestone 執行時會自動載入必要的 expert skills，不依賴模型是否「想到」要用，最後再透過 validation 多點檢查清單（app 是否啟動、Metal validation、螢幕擷取比對 ground truth、anti-pattern 審查、記憶體問題等）逐項把關。講者以移植 Microsoft 的 D3D12 開源引擎 **MiniEngine** 從 Windows 到 macOS 為例，全程使用 **Claude Code**。

移植過程依序攻克數個目標：以 **Metal display link** 驅動 render loop 的視窗與 frame pacing；用 **Metal 4** 的顯式記憶體管理與全新 command 結構帶起 renderer（包含把資源註冊到 **residency set**、從 **Metal shader converter** runtime 查詢 argument buffer offset、把 D3D12 狀態映射到 Metal 4 的 producer-consumer barrier 模型、用 shader reflection 查出真正的參數數量）；再加上 **GCController** 的遊戲控制器支援；以及 **MetalFX** 的 temporal upscaling 與 frame interpolation。每個環節 skill 都會擋下常見的反模式，避免無聲無息的渲染錯誤。

實務上最重要的突破是 **macOS 27** 推出的命令列工具 **gpucapture** 與 **gpudebug**，讓 agent 能完全自主地擷取並分析 GPU frame trace（檢查資源綁定、constants、資料流向），把除錯從「猜測」變成「系統化定位」。Metal HUD 也擴充了 MetalFX 的除錯能力（exposure、jitter scatter plot、可即時覆寫 motion vector scale）。講者最後把同一套 skills 套用到生產級引擎 **Godot**，幾天內就讓 Metal 4 backend 跑起來，證明此方法可擴展到大型專案。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: 由 Metal 生態系團隊的 David Srour 開場，點出 coding agent 正在根本性地改變軟體開發方式，遊戲移植也不例外。過去需要數月的手動平台工作，如今透過 **Game Porting Toolkit 4** 的全新 **agentic skills**，能在極短時間內以更高品質完成，因為這些 skill 替 agent 補上了移植到 Apple 平台所需的專業知識。

deepdive.title: Porting assistant workflow
deepdive.body: 說明 porting assistant 的三階段方法論：**discover** 分析程式碼庫、抓取評估環境的 ground truth 擷取並詢問偏好；接著規劃 **milestone** 目標，把龐大的移植拆成可單場完成的單位；每個 milestone 自動載入必要的 expert skills，不依賴模型自行決定，最後以 **validation** 多點檢查清單逐項把關。agent 還會跨 milestone 儲存所學，避免知識在不同 session 間遺失。

deepdive.title: Install Game Porting Toolkit skills
deepdive.body: skills 與 assistant 以 plugin 形式提供，來自 GitHub 上的 **Game Porting Toolkit marketplace**。流程是先 `add` marketplace、再 `install` plugin，所有 skill 隨即就緒。若不確定下一步該做什麼，可直接詢問 porting assistant，它會引導你走過結構化的 discovery 與 planning 流程。

deepdive.title: Windowing and frame pacing
deepdive.body: windowing 與 frame pacing 這個 milestone 需要數個 skill 協同運作：window skill 負責視窗建立與生命週期、translating to Metal 映射 D3D12 的 swap chain 概念、presenting drawables 處理 frame pacing、metal-cpp 教導正確的 Metal 物件生命週期。技術上用 **Metal display link** 驅動 render loop、處理 focus／fullscreen 事件、最佳化 layer 的解析度與 color space，並善用 **direct-to-display** 降低延遲、妥善管理 drawable 生命週期避免卡頓。最終成果是平滑的 color clear 動畫與穩定的 frame pacing。

deepdive.title: Scene rendering with Metal 4
deepdive.body: 用 **Metal 4** 帶起 renderer，鎖定 lighting、shadows、SSAO 與 tone mapping 作為 first playable。scene rendering 拆成三個 milestone：GPU resources、shader pipelines、command encoding。resources skill 教導該用哪些 storage mode（含 Apple silicon tile 架構專屬選項）、constants 透過 buffer 傳遞的配置模式，shader pipeline／converter skill 把 HLSL shader 接上 Metal 的綁定模型，synchronization skill 提供 pass 之間的同步模式。

deepdive.title: Register resources for residency
deepdive.body: 示範 resources skill 如何教 agent 在使用前、且要在 application 中更早的時機，就把資源註冊進 **residency set**，確保 GPU 需要時每個資源都可存取。對照組顯示：沒有 skill 時 agent 不知道這個步驟存在，雖然程式能編譯，但 GPU 無法如預期讀取 texture，導致渲染結果錯誤。

deepdive.title: Query argument buffer offsets
deepdive.body: 示範 shader pipeline／converter skill 教 agent 從 **Metal shader converter** runtime 查詢 argument buffer offset，以確保與 shader 期望的版面一致。對照組顯示：沒有 skill 時 agent 會沿用 MiniEngine 以 index 乘 size 計算 offset 的舊做法，但 Metal shader converter 的版面可能不同，導致 offset 錯誤——沒有錯誤訊息，只有不正確的渲染。

deepdive.title: Map D3D12 states to Metal 4 stages
deepdive.body: 示範 synchronization skill 教 agent 把 D3D12 狀態映射到 **Metal 4** 的 producer-consumer 模型，從一開始就實作正確的同步。Metal 4 採用完全顯式的同步，單一 command buffer 內的多個 encoder 之間需要適當的 barrier。對照組顯示：沒有 skill 時 agent 只會在 encoder 邊界放上寬鬆的 blanket barrier，簡單情況或許可行，但隨著渲染管線變複雜會無聲無息地壞掉。

deepdive.title: Query shader reflection parameter count
deepdive.body: 示範 shader converter skill 教 agent 利用 **Metal shader converter** 的 reflection 查詢 shader 實際的參數數量。對照組顯示：沒有 skill 時 agent 沿用引擎原本的 5 個 root parameter，但 Metal shader converter 從 HLSL shader 判定版面其實只宣告 4 個，這個不符會把 sampler table 推到錯誤的 offset，造成渲染異常。

deepdive.title: Debugging with GPU command-line tools
deepdive.body: **macOS 27** 推出支援完全自主 agent 工作流的命令列工具：**gpucapture** 擷取 GPU frame、**gpudebug** 分析擷取。在 debugging rendering issues skill 的結構化方法論下，agent 從視覺症狀（lighting 錯誤、牆面 texture 被拉伸）出發，擷取 GPU trace 並檢查資源綁定、constants、資料流向，系統化地定位偏離 ground truth 之處並修正。validation 階段再次用這些工具比對 dispatch 呼叫、pipeline 與 dispatch 維度，把原本繁瑣的人工比對自動化。

deepdive.title: Game controllers and MetalFX
deepdive.body: controller skill 涵蓋 **GCController** 探索、input 模型與從 Windows API 的移植：相較於 XInput 固定的版面，skill 教 agent 改為查詢每個 controller 實際支援的能力與輸入，並提供正確的連線／斷線處理。接著整合 **MetalFX**：upscaling skill 處理 jitter（pixel space）、motion vector 規模與 history reprojection，frame interpolation skill 設定專屬 present thread 與精確時序。Metal HUD 在 macOS 27 擴充了 exposure、jitter scatter plot 與可即時覆寫的 motion vector scale，協助除錯整合問題。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 總結 **Game Porting Toolkit 4** 的 agentic skills 如何加速把遊戲帶到 Apple 平台：porting assistant 提供結構化方法、skills 結合知識與最佳實務。講者最後展示把同一套 skills 套用到生產級引擎 **Godot**（在既有 Metal 3 backend 旁加上 Metal 4），幾天內就跑起來，證明可擴展到大型專案。行動建議是下載安裝 skills、在自己的遊戲程式碼庫上試用、並讓 porting assistant 引導整個移植流程。

summary_en: Presented by David Srour of the Metal Ecosystem Team, the core message is that coding agents are fundamentally changing how games get ported: work that used to take months of manual platform effort can now happen in a fraction of the time. **Game Porting Toolkit 4** introduces new **agentic skills** that give your coding agent the platform expertise it needs to port your game to Apple platforms, with both speed and quality far beyond before. The toolkit has three parts: **expert skills** that provide technical guidance, **workflow skills** that provide a structured approach, and the **porting assistant** agent that ties them together.

The porting assistant follows a three-stage methodology of discover, plan, and execute/validate. **Discover** analyzes your codebase, grabs ground-truth reference captures from the evaluation environment, and asks about your preferences; then you plan **milestones** together (since a whole title is too large for one session); each milestone automatically loads the necessary expert skills rather than relying on the model to choose them, and finally a validation checklist (does the app launch, Metal validation, screen captures compared against ground truth, anti-pattern review, memory issues, and more) checks each milestone. The demo ports Microsoft's D3D12 open-source engine **MiniEngine** from Windows to macOS, entirely with **Claude Code**.

The port works through several goals in order: window and frame pacing driven by a **Metal display link**; bringing up the renderer with **Metal 4**'s explicit memory management and new command structure (registering resources in a **residency set**, querying argument buffer offsets from the **Metal shader converter** runtime, mapping D3D12 states to Metal 4's producer-consumer barrier model, and using shader reflection to find the real parameter count); adding **GCController** gamepad support; and integrating **MetalFX** temporal upscaling and frame interpolation. At each step the skills act as guardrails that catch common anti-patterns and silent rendering bugs.

The most important practical breakthrough is **macOS 27**'s command-line tools **gpucapture** and **gpudebug**, which let the agent fully autonomously capture and analyze a GPU frame trace (inspecting resource bindings, constants, and data flow), turning debugging from guesswork into systematic root-causing. The Metal HUD also gains MetalFX debugging features (exposure, a jitter scatter plot, and live overrides of motion vector scale). Finally, the same skills are applied to the production-grade **Godot** engine, getting a Metal 4 backend running in a few days, proving the approach scales beyond small engines.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: David Srour of the Metal Ecosystem Team opens by noting that coding agents are fundamentally changing software development, and game porting is no different. What used to take months of manual platform work can now happen far faster and with better quality through **Game Porting Toolkit 4**'s new **agentic skills**, which give the agent the expertise needed to port games to Apple platforms.

deepdive_en.title: Porting assistant workflow
deepdive_en.body: The porting assistant's three-stage methodology: **discover** analyzes the codebase, grabs ground-truth captures from the evaluation environment, and asks about preferences; then **milestone** goals are planned to break a huge port into single-session units; each milestone automatically loads the necessary expert skills rather than relying on the model, and a **validation** checklist verifies each one. The agent also stores what it learns across milestones so knowledge isn't lost between sessions.

deepdive_en.title: Install Game Porting Toolkit skills
deepdive_en.body: The skills and assistant ship as a plugin from the **Game Porting Toolkit marketplace** on GitHub. You first add the marketplace, then install the plugin, and all skills are ready. If you're unsure what to do next, just ask the porting assistant and it will guide you through the structured discovery and planning workflow.

deepdive_en.title: Windowing and frame pacing
deepdive_en.body: The windowing and frame pacing milestone needs several skills working together: the window skill for window creation and lifecycle, translating-to-Metal for mapping D3D12's swap chain concepts, presenting-drawables for frame pacing, and metal-cpp for correct Metal object lifetimes. Technically it sets up a **Metal display link** for the render loop, handles focus/fullscreen events, optimizes layer resolution and color space, and leverages **direct-to-display** for lower latency while managing drawable lifetimes to avoid stuttering. The result is a smooth color-clear animation with steady frame pacing.

deepdive_en.title: Scene rendering with Metal 4
deepdive_en.body: Bringing up the renderer with **Metal 4**, targeting lighting, shadows, SSAO and tone mapping for first playable. Scene rendering splits into three milestones: GPU resources, shader pipelines, and command encoding. The resources skill teaches which storage modes to use (including options specific to Apple silicon's tile architecture) and the allocation pattern for constants passed through buffers, the shader pipeline/converter skills wire HLSL shaders through Metal's binding model, and the synchronization skill provides the patterns between passes.

deepdive_en.title: Register resources for residency
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates the resources skill teaching the agent to register resources in a **residency set** before use, much earlier in the application, so every resource is accessible when the GPU needs it. Without the skill the agent doesn't know this step is needed; the code compiles, but the GPU can't read the texture as expected, causing incorrect results.

deepdive_en.title: Query argument buffer offsets
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates the shader pipeline/converter skill teaching the agent to query argument buffer offsets from the **Metal shader converter** runtime so they match what the shader expects. Without the skill the agent copies MiniEngine's pattern of index-times-size, but the Metal shader converter layout can differ, making the offsets wrong — no error, just incorrect rendering.

deepdive_en.title: Map D3D12 states to Metal 4 stages
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates the synchronization skill teaching the agent to map D3D12 states to **Metal 4**'s producer-consumer model, implementing correct synchronization from the start. Metal 4 uses fully explicit synchronization, and multiple encoders in one command buffer need proper barriers. Without the skill the agent resorts to broad blanket barriers at encoder boundaries, which may work for simple cases but can silently break as the pipeline grows more complex.

deepdive_en.title: Query shader reflection parameter count
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates the shader converter skill teaching the agent to use **Metal shader converter**'s reflection to query the shader's actual parameter count. Without the skill the agent carries over the engine's original 5 root parameters, but the converter determines from the HLSL shader that only 4 are declared; that mismatch shifts the sampler table to the wrong offset and breaks rendering.

deepdive_en.title: Debugging with GPU command-line tools
deepdive_en.body: **macOS 27** introduces command-line tools for fully autonomous agent workflows: **gpucapture** to capture a GPU frame and **gpudebug** to analyze it. Guided by the debugging-rendering-issues skill's structured methodology, the agent starts from visual symptoms (wrong lighting, stretched wall textures), captures a GPU trace, inspects resource bindings, constants and data flow, and systematically traces where things diverge from ground truth before fixing it. Validation reuses these tools to compare dispatch calls, pipelines and dispatch dimensions, automating what was previously tedious manual comparison.

deepdive_en.title: Game controllers and MetalFX
deepdive_en.body: The controller skill covers **GCController** discovery, the input model, and porting from Windows APIs: rather than XInput's fixed layout, it teaches the agent to query what each controller actually supports and to handle connect/disconnect gracefully. Then **MetalFX** integration: the upscaling skill handles jitter in pixel space, motion vector scale and conventions, MIP bias and history reprojection, while the frame interpolation skill sets up a dedicated present thread and precise timing. The Metal HUD in macOS 27 adds exposure, a jitter scatter plot, and live overrides of motion vector scale to help debug the integration.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Recaps how **Game Porting Toolkit 4**'s agentic skills accelerate bringing games to Apple platforms: the porting assistant provides a structured approach and the skills combine knowledge with best practices. The talk closes by applying the same skills to the production-grade **Godot** engine (adding Metal 4 alongside its existing Metal 3 backend), getting it running in a few days and proving the approach scales. The call to action is to download and install the skills, try them on your own game's codebase, and let the porting assistant guide the process.

title: Make your game great with touch
gloss: 用觸控讓你的遊戲更出色
takeaway: 運用 TCTouchController 打造彈性的觸控版面與流暢互動，依情境動態調整按鈕與搖桿，並以自訂內容提供豐富回饋，為遊戲設計出色的觸控操作。
chapters: Create a standard circular button B
Update contents for button B based on context
Hide left thumbstick when not touched
Show power options as touch controls
Use the left half of the screen for character movement
Calculate thumbstick tilt magnitude to trigger sprint
Replace right thumbstick with a touchpad
Collapse two QTE buttons into one
Use button B to aim, move, and release power
Add a halo effect with custom TCControlContents

points.text: 以 **TCTouchController** 與各種 descriptor 設定觸控控制項，並比較 GCController 的 polling 與 change handlers 兩種輸入方式。
設計**彈性版面**：以 anchor 與 offset 並考量 safe area 配置按鈕，例如標準圓形的 button B。
打造**流暢互動**：依情境更換按鈕圖示、在未觸碰時隱藏搖桿、動態顯示拾取按鈕或能力轉盤。
用螢幕左半 colliderShape 控制角色移動、計算搖桿傾斜量觸發衝刺，並以 **TCTouchpadDescriptor** 取代右搖桿。
透過自訂 **TCControlContents**（如為搖桿加上光暈圖層）提供豐富的視覺回饋。

audience: 適合**在 Apple 平台開發遊戲、想為觸控螢幕設計優質操作體驗的遊戲開發者**。
gloss_en: Make your game great with touch
takeaway_en: Use TCTouchController to build flexible touch layouts and fluid interactions, adjusting buttons and sticks dynamically by context, and provide rich feedback with custom content to design great touch controls for your game.

points_en.text: Set up touch controls with **TCTouchController** and various descriptors, and compare GCController's two input approaches: polling versus change handlers.
Design a **flexible layout**: position buttons with anchors and offsets while accounting for the safe area, such as a standard circular button B.
Build **fluid interactions**: swap button icons by context, hide the stick when not being touched, and dynamically show a pickup button or ability wheel.
Use a colliderShape over the left half of the screen to control character movement, compute the stick's tilt amount to trigger a sprint, and replace the right stick with **TCTouchpadDescriptor**.
Provide rich visual feedback through custom **TCControlContents** (such as adding a glow layer to a stick).

audience_en: **Game developers building on Apple platforms who want to design great controls for touchscreens.**
summary: 這場由 Game Technology 團隊主講，主題是如何用全新的 **Touch Controller 框架**為遊戲打造出色的觸控操作。前提是：玩家會隨時隨地在 iPhone 上玩你的遊戲，但臨時起意時手邊不一定有實體控制器，因此優秀的觸控操作至關重要。Touch Controller 建立在既有的 **Game Controller 框架**之上——當啟用觸控控制時，它會以一個 **`GCController`** 物件呈現，所以你可以像對待任何控制器一樣 poll 狀態或設 value-changed handler，已支援實體控制器的遊戲幾乎不必改動遊戲邏輯。整場以講者的遊戲為例，依序示範：設定觸控控制器、設計彈性版面、打造流暢互動、提供豐富回饋。

**設定**：從 descriptor 建立 `TCTouchController` 並用 `connect` 啟用（自動啟用 game controller 邏輯），在 UIView 覆寫 `touchesBegan`／`touchesEnded`／`touchesMoved` 轉呼叫對應的 handle 函式通知控制器，並在 Metal renderer 中用 render API 把控制項畫到畫面上。**彈性版面**是關鍵：框架為每個版面提供 **九個 anchor point**，控制項以相對 anchor 的 offset 擺放，可把相關控制項群組成 section 共用同一 anchor，讓裝置形狀改變時各 section 維持一致的大小與距離。同時要設計**全螢幕**體驗、用 UIView 的 `safeAreaInsets` 避開圓角、home indicator 與 Dynamic Island，並把控制項放在拇指附近（常用）與螢幕頂端（不常用如選單），避開角色與移動／攝影機輸入區。

**流暢互動**強調讓控制項感覺原生於觸控。用動態控制項：換 system asset 的名稱讓 button B 顯示實際動作（如打擊、火球、水滴）的圖示，並在 context 改變時更新；用 `hidesWhenNotPressed`（thumbstick）或 `isEnabled = false`（按鈕）在動作不可用時整個隱藏，pickup 按鈕則因位置會變而用「加入／移除」並每次更新位置。觸控控制項可同時作為輸入與輸出——直接把可用的招式顯示成觸控控制項（power wheel）取代 overlay，並在三秒無選擇時自動消失。移動方面：把 thumbstick 的 `colliderShape` 設為 `leftSide`／`rightSide` 讓半個螢幕都能感測；把衝刺併入 thumbstick 本身、用**傾斜幅度（tilt magnitude）**判定（小幅正常、大幅衝刺），免去第二根手指;並用 **`TCTouchpad`**（label 設 rightThumbstick、`reportsRelativeValues = true`）取代右 thumbstick 控制攝影機，兼顧速度與精準、無過度旋轉。

**重新設計複雜操作**：把需多指的 QTE（如同時按 L1+R1 又推 thumbstick 脫困）**併成單一 QTE 按鈕**，因位置固定故用 `isEnabled` 顯示／隱藏；把瞄準與發射這類「瞄準—移動—放開」**合併成單一動作按鈕**——在 button B 的 valueChangedHandler 依按壓狀態呼叫 releasePower，並在 `touchesMoved` 中於 button B 按住時擷取原始 touch delta 做按住拖曳瞄準。**豐富回饋**方面，每個觸控控制項都應有可見的按下狀態（框架預設處理：thumbstick 隨移動動畫、按鈕按下高亮）；要更進一步可手動建立 **`TCControlContents`**（本質是一疊圖層 array），例如把 halo Metal 材質做成的光環 `TCControlImage` 疊在標準背景上，衝刺啟動時換上、結束時還原，給玩家強烈的視覺指示。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: Game Technology 團隊的 Keyi Yu 開場，說明用 **Game Porting Toolkit 4** 把 Mac 遊戲移植到 iOS 很直接，但玩家臨時起意在 iPhone 上玩時不一定有實體控制器，因此**出色的觸控操作**至關重要。以 Black Salt Games 的 Dredge 為例,並預告以自己的遊戲示範四步驟：設定觸控控制器、彈性版面、流暢互動、豐富回饋。

deepdive.title: Set up a touch controller
deepdive.body: 說明 **Touch Controller 框架**建立在 Game Controller 框架之上，把支援延伸到觸控輸入。它含豐富的按鈕型別與行為、每個按鈕外觀可自訂、並直接整合 Metal 以求最高效能；啟用後以一個 **`GCController`** 物件呈現，可像其他控制器一樣 poll 或設 handler。

deepdive.title: GCController polling vs. change handlers
deepdive.body: 回顧 Game Controller 框架核心：對 `GCController` 連接／斷開的通知反應，然後 poll 活躍裝置的輸入狀態，或設 value-changed handler 在狀態改變時收到通知。實作好遊戲邏輯後即可在其上加觸控控制。

deepdive.title: Set up a TCTouchController
deepdive.body: 示範設定：從 descriptor 建立 `TCTouchController`、用 `connect` API 啟用（自動啟用 game controller 邏輯），在 UIView 覆寫 `touchesBegan`／`touchesEnded`／`touchesMoved` 並轉呼叫對應 handle 函式通知控制器，在 Metal renderer 用 render API 渲染所有控制項，最後設好 polling 與 valueChangedHandler。

deepdive.title: Design flexible layouts
deepdive.body: 強調**彈性版面**讓遊戲在任何螢幕尺寸都舒適。框架為每個版面提供 **九個 anchor point**，控制項以相對 anchor 的 offset 擺放,可把相關控制項群組成 section 共用同一 anchor，使裝置形狀改變時各 section 維持一致大小與距離。並要設計**全螢幕**、用 `safeAreaInsets` 避開圓角、home indicator 與 Dynamic Island，把常用控制放拇指附近、不常用（如選單）放頂端，避開角色與移動／攝影機區。

deepdive.title: Create a standard circular button B
deepdive.body: 示範建立標準圓形 button B：初始化 `TCButtonDescriptor`、把 label 設為 `TCControlLabel.buttonB` 對應實體控制器的 B 鍵（因此免寫額外遊戲邏輯）、anchor 在 bottomRight 並設固定 offset、設定視覺內容、呼叫 `addButton`，並用 `safeAreaInsets` 調整 offset 以免被裁切。

deepdive.title: Design fluid interactions
deepdive.body: 指出一對一照搬實體控制器會讓畫面雜亂、控制項互相爭空間，本節要清理並設計感覺原生於觸控的控制，因為流暢自然的互動能讓玩家沉浸。

deepdive.title: Change icon image
deepdive.body: 用**動態控制項**：因螢幕控制項外觀可隨時改，換 system asset 名稱讓 button B 不顯示 buttonB 而顯示實際動作（打擊）的圖示。換掉所有 asset 後版面更直覺，玩家不必查設定或看提示就知道每個控制項的功能。

deepdive.title: Update contents for button B based on context
deepdive.body: 當控制項行為隨 context 改變時應更新圖示：button B 除預設打擊外還可代表火球或水招，因此選招時圖示換成火焰或水滴。做法是寫一個更新 button B 內容的 helper，在 cyclePower 中以對應 symbolName 呼叫它。

deepdive.title: Hide left thumbstick when not touched
deepdive.body: 當動作不相關時就整個從螢幕移除，別留下無法使用的控制項。thumbstick 在未被觸碰時隱藏只要在建立時設 `hidesWhenNotPressed = true`；其他按鈕則設 `isEnabled = false` 來隱藏。

deepdive.title: Show/hide the pick-up button
deepdive.body: pickup 按鈕較特別：它要出現在需撿拾物品的旁邊，因此每次顯示時更新位置，要關閉時則整個從 touchController **移除**。隱藏 thumbstick、pickup 與 QTE 按鈕後畫面乾淨許多。

deepdive.title: Show power options as touch controls
deepdive.body: 觸控控制項可同時作為輸入與輸出——與其顯示 overlay 再循環切換招式，不如直接把招式顯示成觸控控制項。在 buttonX 的 press handler 直接開啟 power wheel 控制項，在 openPowerWheel 依目前可用招式加入各控制項並設 value-changed handler，且因不常用故三秒無選擇即自動消失。

deepdive.title: Use the left half of the screen for character movement
deepdive.body: 角色與攝影機移動需流暢。實體 thumbstick 尺寸固定，但觸控不受限,且玩家感覺不到手指相對控制項的位置，故應盡量擴大輸入區。把 `colliderShape` 設為 `leftSide` 或 `rightSide`，讓 thumbstick 取得整個半邊螢幕的觸控偵測。

deepdive.title: Calculate thumbstick tilt magnitude to trigger sprint
deepdive.body: 衝刺原本要按住 thumbstick 又同時移動，觸控上等於要兩指很難做。解法是把 thumbstick 按鈕功能內嵌進 thumbstick，用**傾斜幅度**判定：小幅正常、大幅衝刺。在 `pollInput()` 讀 `GCController` 的 leftThumbstick 取 tilt 值並做 magnitude 檢查，玩家用單一 thumbstick 即可衝刺。

deepdive.title: Replace right thumbstick with a touchpad
deepdive.body: 直接把右 thumbstick 對應攝影機會過度旋轉且遲鈍，**touchpad** 兼顧速度與精準、無延遲或起止漂移。用 **`TCTouchpad`**：初始化 descriptor、label 設 rightThumbstick 以對應既有攝影機邏輯、colliderShape 設 rightSide 覆蓋右半螢幕、`reportsRelativeValues = true` 讓任意位置觸碰皆可用，再加入 touchController，且無可見控制項佔畫面。

deepdive.title: Collapse two QTE buttons into one
deepdive.body: 處理複雜組合的第一例 QTE：大魔王凍結角色時需按住 L1+R1 脫困又用左 thumbstick 移動，兩指難管。解法是把兩鍵**併成單一 QTE 按鈕**並在事件外整個隱藏；因位置固定（不像 pickup 變位置），用 `isEnabled` 顯示／隱藏而非每次加移除。

deepdive.title: Use button B to aim, move, and release power
deepdive.body: 第二例瞄準發招原需多於兩指同時瞄準、移動、放開。解法是把瞄準與發射**合併成單一動作按鈕**：移除瞄準與發射按鈕，在 button B 的 valueChangedHandler 依按壓狀態呼叫 releasePower，並在 `touchesMoved` 中於 button B 按住時擷取原始 touch delta 做按住拖曳瞄準，放開即發火球，互動順暢許多。

deepdive.title: Provide rich feedback
deepdive.body: 玩家能觸碰任何地方，因此清楚的觸碰回饋很重要。每個觸控控制項都應有可見按下狀態，而框架預設已處理：thumbstick 隨移動動畫、按鈕按下高亮。但在視覺繁忙的遊戲中可能想要更強的自訂視覺回饋。

deepdive.title: Add a halo effect with custom TCControlContents
deepdive.body: 因衝刺時回饋不足，加一個圍繞左 thumbstick 外圈的發光光環。手動建立 **`TCControlContents`**：用 halo Metal 材質產生略大於背景的 halo `TCControlImage`，把它疊在標準背景圖層之上（`TCControlContents` 本質是一疊圖層 array），衝刺啟動時換上含光環的版本、結束時還原,讓「衝刺模式」一目了然。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 總結整體成果：從實體控制器一對一照搬的雜亂畫面，到清楚易用的觸控版面——左 thumbstick 觸碰才現、pickup 按鈕有物品才現、右半螢幕為攝影機 touchpad 無過度旋轉、按鈕選招、按住拖曳單鍵瞄準發招、衝刺指示。鼓勵用 **Touch Controller 框架**設計優秀觸控操作，並建議搭配「Design great interfaces for handheld games」等延伸內容。

summary_en: Presented by the Game Technology team, this session is about crafting great touch controls for games with the new **Touch Controller framework**. The premise: players will jump into your game on iPhone anywhere, anytime, but in spontaneous moments they may not have a physical controller—so great touch controls matter. Touch Controller builds on the existing **Game Controller framework**—when enabled, it shows up as a **`GCController`** object, so you poll its state or set value-changed handlers just like any controller, meaning games that already support physical controllers barely change their game logic. Using the presenter's game, it walks through setting up a touch controller, designing flexible layouts, building fluid interactions, and providing rich feedback.

**Setup**: create a `TCTouchController` from a descriptor and enable it with `connect` (which auto-enables game controller logic), override `touchesBegan`/`touchesEnded`/`touchesMoved` in the UIView to forward to the matching handle functions, and render controls on screen with the render API in the Metal renderer. **Flexible layout** is key: the framework gives **nine anchor points** per layout, controls are placed by offset relative to an anchor, and related controls can be grouped into a section sharing one anchor so each stays at a consistent size and distance as the device shape changes. Design for **fullscreen**, use a UIView's `safeAreaInsets` to avoid rounded corners, the home indicator, and the Dynamic Island, and place controls near the thumbs (frequent) and at the top (infrequent, like menus), away from the character and movement/camera input areas.

**Fluid interactions** focus on making controls feel native to touch. Use dynamic controls: change a system asset's name so button B shows the actual action's icon (strike, fireball, water) and update it as context changes; hide controls entirely when unavailable via `hidesWhenNotPressed` (thumbsticks) or `isEnabled = false` (buttons), while the pickup button is added/removed with its position updated each time. Touch controls serve as both input and output—show available powers directly as touch controls (a power wheel) instead of an overlay, auto-dismissing after three seconds. For movement: set a thumbstick's `colliderShape` to `leftSide`/`rightSide` so half the screen senses touch; fold sprint into the thumbstick itself using **tilt magnitude** (small = normal, large = sprint) to avoid a second finger; and replace the right thumbstick with a **`TCTouchpad`** (label set to rightThumbstick, `reportsRelativeValues = true`) for camera control with speed and precision and no over-rotation.

**Redesigning complex controls**: collapse a multi-finger QTE (holding L1+R1 while moving the thumbstick to break free) into a **single QTE button**, shown/hidden via `isEnabled` since its position is fixed; combine aim-and-release into a **single action button**—call releasePower from button B's valueChangedHandler based on pressed state, and capture the raw touch delta in `touchesMoved` while button B is held for hold-and-drag aiming. For **rich feedback**, every control should have a visible pressed state (handled by default: thumbsticks animate, buttons highlight); to go further, build **`TCControlContents`** manually (essentially an array of layers)—e.g., stack a halo `TCControlImage` from a halo Metal texture over the standard background, swapping it in when sprint is active and reverting when not, for a strong visual indicator.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Game Technology team's Keyi Yu opens, noting porting Mac games to iOS is straightforward with **Game Porting Toolkit 4**, but players jumping into a game on iPhone may not have a physical controller, so **great touch controls** matter. Cites Dredge by Black Salt Games and previews four steps demoed on her own game: set up a touch controller, flexible layouts, fluid interactions, and rich feedback.

deepdive_en.title: Set up a touch controller
deepdive_en.body: Explains the **Touch Controller framework** builds on the Game Controller framework, extending support to touch input. It includes a rich set of button types and behaviors, each button's appearance is customizable, and it integrates with Metal for top performance; when enabled it appears as a **`GCController`** so you poll or set handlers like any controller.

deepdive_en.title: GCController polling vs. change handlers
deepdive_en.body: Reviews the Game Controller core: react to `GCController` connect/disconnect notifications, then poll active devices' input state or set value-changed handlers for updates. With game logic implemented on GCController, you're ready to layer touch controls on top.

deepdive_en.title: Set up a TCTouchController
deepdive_en.body: Shows setup: create a `TCTouchController` from a descriptor, enable it with the `connect` API (auto-enabling game controller logic), override `touchesBegan`/`touchesEnded`/`touchesMoved` in the UIView to forward to matching handle functions, render all controls with the render API in the Metal renderer, and set up polling and a valueChangedHandler.

deepdive_en.title: Design flexible layouts
deepdive_en.body: Stresses **flexible layout** so the game feels comfortable on any screen size. The framework provides **nine anchor points** per layout; controls are placed by offset relative to an anchor, and related controls can share one anchor in a section so each stays at a consistent size and distance as the device shape changes. Also design for **fullscreen**, use `safeAreaInsets` to avoid rounded corners, the home indicator, and the Dynamic Island, placing frequent controls near the thumbs and infrequent ones (menus) at the top, away from the character and movement/camera areas.

deepdive_en.title: Create a standard circular button B
deepdive_en.body: Demos a standard circular button B: initialize a `TCButtonDescriptor`, set its label to `TCControlLabel.buttonB` to map to the physical B (so no extra game logic), anchor in bottomRight with a fixed offset, set visual contents, call `addButton`, and adjust the offset with `safeAreaInsets` to avoid clipping.

deepdive_en.title: Design fluid interactions
deepdive_en.body: Notes a one-to-one mapping from a physical controller clutters the screen with controls competing for space; this section cleans that up and designs controls that feel native to touch, since fluid, natural interactions immerse players.

deepdive_en.title: Change icon image
deepdive_en.body: Uses **dynamic controls**: since on-screen control appearance can change, swap the system asset name so button B shows the actual action's (strike) icon instead of 'buttonB'. After swapping all assets, the layout is more intuitive and players know each control's function without checking settings or hints.

deepdive_en.title: Update contents for button B based on context
deepdive_en.body: When a control's behavior changes with context, update its icon: besides strike, button B can be fireball or water, so the icon becomes a flame or water drop when that power is selected. A helper updates button B's contents, called in cyclePower with the right symbolName per power.

deepdive_en.title: Hide left thumbstick when not touched
deepdive_en.body: When an action is irrelevant, remove it from the screen entirely rather than leaving unusable controls. Hide a thumbstick when untouched by setting `hidesWhenNotPressed = true` at creation; hide other buttons by setting `isEnabled = false`.

deepdive_en.title: Show/hide the pick-up button
deepdive_en.body: The pickup button is special: it should appear next to the item to pick up, so its position is updated each time it's shown, and when dismissed it's **removed** from the touchController entirely. After hiding the thumbsticks, pickup, and QTE buttons, the screen is much cleaner.

deepdive_en.title: Show power options as touch controls
deepdive_en.body: Touch controls serve as both input and output—rather than an overlay cycling through actions, show available powers directly as touch controls. In buttonX's press handler, open the power wheel controls directly; in openPowerWheel, add each available power with a value-changed handler, auto-dismissing after three seconds since they're used infrequently.

deepdive_en.title: Use the left half of the screen for character movement
deepdive_en.body: Character and camera movement must feel smooth. Physical thumbsticks have a fixed size, but touch isn't bound by that, and players can't feel their finger's position relative to a control, so expand the input area. Set `colliderShape` to `leftSide` or `rightSide` to give the thumbstick the entire half of the screen for touch detection.

deepdive_en.title: Calculate thumbstick tilt magnitude to trigger sprint
deepdive_en.body: Sprinting originally meant holding the thumbstick while moving it—two fingers on touch, which is hard. The fix embeds the thumbstick button's function into the thumbstick and uses **tilt magnitude**: small = normal, large = sprint. In `pollInput()`, read `GCController`'s leftThumbstick, get the tilt, and do a magnitude check, so players sprint with a single thumbstick.

deepdive_en.title: Replace right thumbstick with a touchpad
deepdive_en.body: Mapping the right thumbstick directly to the camera causes over-rotation and feels sluggish; a **touchpad** gives speed and precision with no latency or drift. Use **`TCTouchpad`**: initialize the descriptor, set label to rightThumbstick to map to existing camera logic, colliderShape to rightSide to cover the right half, `reportsRelativeValues = true` so it works wherever the player touches, then add it to the touchController—with no visible control cluttering the screen.

deepdive_en.title: Collapse two QTE buttons into one
deepdive_en.body: The first complex-combo case is a QTE: when the boss freezes the character, hold L1+R1 to break free while moving with the left thumbstick—hard with two fingers. The fix collapses the two buttons into a **single QTE button** and hides it when the event isn't happening; since its position is fixed (unlike pickup), use `isEnabled` to show/hide rather than add/remove each time.

deepdive_en.title: Use button B to aim, move, and release power
deepdive_en.body: The second case, aim-to-release, originally needed more than two fingers to aim, move, and release at once. The fix combines aim and release into a **single action button**: remove the aim and release buttons, call releasePower from button B's valueChangedHandler based on pressed state, and capture the raw touch delta in `touchesMoved` while button B is held for hold-and-drag aiming—releasing fires the fireball, much smoother.

deepdive_en.title: Provide rich feedback
deepdive_en.body: Since players can touch anywhere, clear feedback matters. Every control should have a visible pressed state, and the framework handles this by default: thumbsticks animate as they move and buttons highlight when pressed. But in a visually busy game you may want stronger custom visual feedback.

deepdive_en.title: Add a halo effect with custom TCControlContents
deepdive_en.body: Since sprinting gave little feedback, add a glowing halo around the left thumbstick's outer ring. Build **`TCControlContents`** manually: generate a halo `TCControlImage` from a halo Metal texture, slightly larger than the background, and stack it over the standard background layers (`TCControlContents` is essentially an array of layers), swapping in the haloed version when sprint is active and reverting when not, making sprint mode immediately clear.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Summarizes the overall result: from a cluttered one-to-one mapping of a physical controller to a clear, easy-to-use touch layout—the left thumbstick appears on touch, the pickup button appears when an item is nearby, the right half is a camera touchpad with no over-rotation, buttons pick powers, a single button hold-and-drag aims and releases, and a sprint indicator helps. Encourages designing great touch controls with the **Touch Controller framework** and points to talks like 'Design great interfaces for handheld games.'

title: Build real-time neural rendering pipelines with Metal
gloss: 用 Metal 打造即時神經渲染管線
takeaway: 用 Metal 4 將機器學習整合進即時渲染管線，透過 MetalFX 降噪、相機運動向量與內嵌神經網路（tensorOps）提升畫質與效能。
chapters: Deploy custom ML networks with Metal 4

points.text: 用 **Metal 4** 把機器學習整合進**即時渲染管線**，提供實務導入建議。
採用 **MetalFX Denoising** 降噪，提升渲染畫面品質。
在 shader 中計算**僅相機（camera-only）運動向量**，並扣除前後幀的 jitter 子像素偏移。
以 Metal 4 **部署自訂 ML 網路**，整合進渲染流程。
透過 **tensorOps** 把神經網路**內嵌（inline）**到 shader 中執行。

audience: **開發高效能遊戲與即時 3D 渲染的 Metal 開發者**，想把 ML 導入渲染管線的人。
gloss_en: Build real-time neural rendering pipelines with Metal
takeaway_en: Integrate machine learning into a real-time rendering pipeline with Metal 4, improving quality and performance through MetalFX denoising, camera motion vectors, and inline neural networks (tensorOps).

points_en.text: Integrate machine learning into a **real-time rendering pipeline** with **Metal 4**, with practical adoption recommendations.
Use **MetalFX Denoising** to reduce noise and improve rendered frame quality.
