summary: 由 StoreKit 團隊的 Sam 主講，這場介紹在 Apple 平台打造遊戲的三組新工具：**Background Assets** 的更新、全新的 **Unity 外掛**（StoreKit 與 Background Assets），以及在 App Store 與 Apple Games app 上強化遊戲曝光。以一款內容豐富的遊戲 The Coast 為例：與其一次下載所有音訊、影片、貼圖與 ML 模型佔用儲存空間，**Managed Background Assets** 會在需要時自動下載 asset pack，省下玩家的時間與空間；App Store 上的 app 更可享每 app 最高 **200 GB** 的 Apple 託管資產（含在開發者計畫會員資格內）。

iOS 27 的重點是 **localized asset packs**：系統會依玩家在「設定」選的偏好語言，只下載該語言的資產，大幅縮減下載量；若無對應語言則自動 fallback 到最接近的語言（如 English-UK 缺則用 English-US，Spanish 缺且無區域變體則退回主要語言 English）。作法是在 asset pack manifest JSON 加上 **`language`** 標籤。若你在 Steam 上以 depots 管理資產，可用 **`xcrun ba-package convert`**（傳入 asset pack ID、語言 ID、download policy 與 Steam manifest）把 depot 轉成 asset pack manifest，再用 `ba-package` 把 manifest 產生為 **`.aar`** asset pack archive；該工具即將支援 Linux 與 Windows。

Unity 開發者現可用兩個新加入 Apple 外掛家族的外掛——**StoreKit** 與 **Background Assets**（已於 GitHub 提供，用既有 Python 腳本建置，需 Xcode 27、Python 3、Unity 2022 LTS 以上）。它們以 C# API 橋接底層原生框架：StoreKit 提供 `Product.FetchProducts` 取得商品、`Purchase()` 顯示系統付款表單，購買後檢查 `IsVerified` 並 `Finish()`，並用 **`Transaction.Updates`** 序列監聽交易（consumable 內聯處理，non-consumable 與訂閱以 **`CurrentEntitlements`** 為真實來源）；Background Assets 外掛則用 `AssetPackManager` 取得 manifest、以 `DownloadStatusUpdatesAsync` 回報進度、用 `EnsureLocalAvailabilityOfAssetPackAsync` 確保本地可用。測試可用 Xcode 的 StoreKit Testing 與 **Background Assets mock server**（執行時自動啟動），以及 sandbox testing。最後，提交時可為產品頁 header 與搜尋結果加入新視覺素材（也會出現在 Apple Games app），iOS 27 重新設計的付款表單在橫向也運作良好。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: StoreKit 團隊的 Sam 開場，預告三大主題：**Background Assets** 更新、新的 **Unity 外掛**，以及在 App Store 與 Apple Games app 強化曝光，目標是協助打造 Apple 平台上最棒的遊戲。

deepdive.title: Background Assets
deepdive.body: 以遊戲 The Coast 為例：與其一次下載所有音訊、影片、紋理與 ML 模型，**Managed Background Assets** 在需要時自動下載 asset pack，省下玩家時間與儲存空間。App Store 上的 app 可享每 app 最高 **200 GB** Apple 託管資產，含在開發者計畫會員內，自 iOS/iPadOS/macOS/tvOS/visionOS 26 起提供。

deepdive.title: Localized asset packs
deepdive.body: iOS 27 的 **localized asset packs** 依玩家在設定選的偏好語言只下載該語言資產，大幅縮減下載量。若未提供對應語言則 **fallback** 到最接近者（English-UK→English-US；Spanish 無變體則退回主要語言 English）。

deepdive.title: Asset pack manifest for a localized asset pack
deepdive.body: 支援 localized asset packs 的作法是在 asset pack manifest JSON 加上 **`language`** 標籤（如 "en-US"），其餘欄位含 assetPackID、downloadPolicy、fileSelectors、platforms 等。

deepdive.title: Convert Steam depots to asset packs
deepdive.body: 若在 Steam 以 **depots** 管理資產，現可更容易把 Steam depots 轉成 asset packs 在 Apple 平台發行。

deepdive.title: Convert a Steam depot to an asset pack manifest
deepdive.body: 在 macOS 裝 Xcode 27 後執行 **`xcrun ba-package convert`**，傳入 asset pack ID、語言 ID、download policy 與 Steam manifest 建置腳本，輸出 asset pack manifest。該工具即將支援 Linux 與 Windows。

deepdive.title: Convert an asset pack manifest to an asset pack archive
deepdive.body: 有了 manifest 後，再次以 **`ba-package`** 用該 manifest 作輸入，產生 **`.aar`** asset pack archive，即可在遊戲中使用。

deepdive.title: Unity plug-ins
deepdive.body: 宣布兩個加入 Apple Unity 外掛家族的新外掛：**Background Assets** 與 **StoreKit**（已在 GitHub 提供）。用與其他 Apple Unity 外掛相同的 Python 腳本建置；兩者皆以 **C# API** 橋接底層原生框架，需 Xcode 27、Python 3、Unity 2022 LTS 以上。

deepdive.title: StoreKit and Background Assets sample code
deepdive.body: 外掛裝好後在 Unity editor 開啟遊戲；採用 **StoreKit** 即可透過 App Store 安全的商務平台向全球玩家提供 In-App Purchases。

deepdive.title: Fetch and purchase products with the StoreKit plug-in
deepdive.body: C# 版 StoreKit 用 **`Product.FetchProducts`** 取得並陳列商品，用 **`Purchase()`** 顯示系統付款表單；購買後檢查 `PurchaseResult` 成功且 `IsVerified`，交付內容後呼叫 **`Finish()`** 完成交易。

deepdive.title: Listen for Transaction updates with the StoreKit plug-in
deepdive.body: 用 **`Transaction.Updates`** 序列在整個生命週期監聽交易（任何在 app 外或其他裝置建立／更新的交易都會發出）。**consumable** 檢查是否被撤銷後內聯授權；**non-consumable 與訂閱** 則以 **`CurrentEntitlements`** 為真實來源（已過濾退款／撤銷／過期），確認 verified 後授權，最後 `Finish()`。

deepdive.title: Download asset packs with the Background Assets plug-in
deepdive.body: 玩家購買內容後，用 Background Assets 外掛確保 asset pack 本地可用再供應內容：用 **`AssetPackManager.GetManifestAsync`** 取 manifest 與 asset pack，用 **`DownloadStatusUpdatesAsync`** 迭代回報下載進度更新 UI，再用 **`EnsureLocalAvailabilityOfAssetPackAsync`** 確保本地可用。匯出到 Xcode 後可用 Xcode 的 StoreKit Testing 與 **Background Assets mock server**（執行時自動啟動）及 sandbox testing 進行測試。

deepdive.title: Game presence
deepdive.body: 提交遊戲時可為產品頁 header 與搜尋結果加入新的圖像與影片素材，讓遊戲更突出；這些素材也會出現在 **Apple Games app**。詳見「Enhance your presence on the App Store」（WWDC26）。iOS 27 重新設計的系統付款表單在橫向模式也運作良好，玩家可邊解鎖內容邊繼續遊戲。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 總結後續步驟：在 App Store Connect 上傳 localized 版本的 asset packs 進一步縮減 app 大小、安裝新的 Apple Unity 外掛把原生 Managed Background Assets 與 StoreKit 帶入 Unity 遊戲，並規劃用新的圖像／影片素材在 App Store 與 Apple Games app 突顯遊戲特色。

summary_en: Presented by Sam from the StoreKit team, this session covers three new tools for building games on Apple platforms: updates to **Background Assets**, new **Unity plug-ins** (StoreKit and Background Assets), and enhancing your game's presence on the App Store and Apple Games app. Using a content-packed game called The Coast: rather than downloading all audio, video, textures, and ML models upfront and taking up storage, **Managed Background Assets** automatically downloads asset packs when needed, saving players time and space; apps on the App Store can also use up to **200 GB** of Apple-hosted assets per app, included in the Developer Program membership.

The iOS 27 highlight is **localized asset packs**: the system delivers only the assets for the player's preferred language selected in Settings, greatly reducing download size, and automatically falls back to the closest language match if none is provided (English-UK falls back to English-US; Spanish with no regional variant falls back to the primary language English). You enable this by adding a **`language`** tag to the asset pack manifest JSON. If you manage assets as Steam depots, use **`xcrun ba-package convert`** (passing the asset pack ID, language ID, download policy, and Steam manifest) to convert a depot to an asset pack manifest, then run `ba-package` to produce an **`.aar`** asset pack archive; the tool is coming soon to Linux and Windows.

Unity developers can now use two plug-ins newly joining Apple's plug-in portfolio—**StoreKit** and **Background Assets** (available on GitHub, built with the existing Python script, requiring Xcode 27, Python 3, Unity 2022 LTS or later). They expose C# APIs bridging the underlying native frameworks: StoreKit provides `Product.FetchProducts` to fetch products, `Purchase()` to show the system payment sheet, checking `IsVerified` and calling `Finish()` after purchase, and listening to transactions via the **`Transaction.Updates`** sequence (handle consumables inline, with **`CurrentEntitlements`** as the source of truth for non-consumables and subscriptions); the Background Assets plug-in uses `AssetPackManager` to get the manifest, `DownloadStatusUpdatesAsync` to report progress, and `EnsureLocalAvailabilityOfAssetPackAsync` to ensure local availability. Test with Xcode's StoreKit Testing and the **Background Assets mock server** (auto-starting at run time), plus sandbox testing. Finally, on submission you can add new visuals to your product page header and search results (which also appear in the Apple Games app), and iOS 27's redesigned payment sheet works great in landscape.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Sam from the StoreKit team opens by previewing three topics: **Background Assets** updates, new **Unity plug-ins**, and enhancing presence on the App Store and Apple Games app, all aimed at helping create the best games on Apple platforms.

deepdive_en.title: Background Assets
deepdive_en.body: Using the game The Coast: rather than downloading all audio, video, textures, and ML models upfront, **Managed Background Assets** downloads asset packs automatically when needed, saving players time and storage. App Store apps can use up to **200 GB** of Apple-hosted assets per app, included in the Developer Program, available since iOS/iPadOS/macOS/tvOS/visionOS 26.

deepdive_en.title: Localized asset packs
deepdive_en.body: iOS 27's **localized asset packs** deliver only the player's preferred-language assets selected in Settings, greatly reducing download size. If a language isn't provided, the system **falls back** to the closest match (English-UK → English-US; Spanish with no variant falls back to the primary language English).

deepdive_en.title: Asset pack manifest for a localized asset pack
deepdive_en.body: To support localized asset packs, add a **`language`** tag (e.g. "en-US") to the asset pack manifest JSON, alongside fields like assetPackID, downloadPolicy, fileSelectors, and platforms.

deepdive_en.title: Convert Steam depots to asset packs
deepdive_en.body: If you manage assets with **depots** on Steam, you can now more easily convert Steam depots to asset packs to distribute on Apple platforms.

deepdive_en.title: Convert a Steam depot to an asset pack manifest
deepdive_en.body: On macOS with Xcode 27 installed, run **`xcrun ba-package convert`**, passing the asset pack ID, language ID, download policy, and the Steam manifest build script, to output an asset pack manifest. The tool is coming soon to Linux and Windows.

deepdive_en.title: Convert an asset pack manifest to an asset pack archive
deepdive_en.body: With the manifest created, run **`ba-package`** again using that manifest as input to produce an **`.aar`** asset pack archive, ready to use in your game.

deepdive_en.title: Unity plug-ins
deepdive_en.body: Announces two new plug-ins joining the Apple Unity portfolio: **Background Assets** and **StoreKit** (available on GitHub). Build them with the same Python script as other Apple Unity plug-ins; both expose a **C# API** bridging the native framework, requiring Xcode 27, Python 3, and Unity 2022 LTS or later.

deepdive_en.title: StoreKit and Background Assets sample code
deepdive_en.body: Once installed, open the game in the Unity editor; adopting **StoreKit** lets you offer In-App Purchases to players worldwide through the App Store's safe, trusted commerce platform.

deepdive_en.title: Fetch and purchase products with the StoreKit plug-in
deepdive_en.body: The C# StoreKit uses **`Product.FetchProducts`** to fetch and merchandise products and **`Purchase()`** to show the system payment sheet; after purchase, check that `PurchaseResult` succeeded and `IsVerified`, deliver the content, then call **`Finish()`** to complete the transaction.

deepdive_en.title: Listen for Transaction updates with the StoreKit plug-in
deepdive_en.body: Use the **`Transaction.Updates`** sequence to listen for transactions throughout the lifecycle (any created/updated outside the app or on other devices). For **consumables**, check for revocation then grant access inline; for **non-consumables and subscriptions**, **`CurrentEntitlements`** is the source of truth (already filtering refunded/revoked/expired), grant access once verified, then `Finish()`.

deepdive_en.title: Download asset packs with the Background Assets plug-in
deepdive_en.body: After a player buys content, use the Background Assets plug-in to ensure the asset pack is locally available before serving content: use **`AssetPackManager.GetManifestAsync`** to get the manifest and asset pack, iterate **`DownloadStatusUpdatesAsync`** to report progress in the UI, then **`EnsureLocalAvailabilityOfAssetPackAsync`**. After exporting to Xcode, test with Xcode's StoreKit Testing and the **Background Assets mock server** (auto-starting at run time) plus sandbox testing.

deepdive_en.title: Game presence
deepdive_en.body: When submitting, add new image and video assets to your product page header and search results to stand out; these also appear in the **Apple Games app**. See 'Enhance your presence on the App Store' (WWDC26). iOS 27's redesigned system payment sheet works great in landscape, so players can unlock content and keep gaming.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Summarizes next steps: upload localized versions of asset packs in App Store Connect to further reduce app size, install the new Apple Unity plug-ins to bring native Managed Background Assets and StoreKit to your Unity game, and plan to highlight features with new image/video assets on the App Store and Apple Games app.

title: Meet Trust Insights
gloss: 認識 Trust Insights
takeaway: 全新的 Trust Insights 框架以隱私保護方式評估使用者是否正遭社交詐騙或脅迫，協助 App 在風險情境中增加保護摩擦。

points.text: **Trust Insights** 是全新框架，以**隱私保護**方式協助偵測使用者是否正遭**社交詐騙或脅迫**。
透過 **InsightEvaluator** 先 requestAuthorization 取得授權，再用 **IsLikelyBeingCoachedInsight** 請求評估。
結果為 .unknown／.medium／.high 等風險等級，App 可據此調整流程（例如增加確認步驟）。
需以 **reportConsumption**（如 .usedIncreasedFriction）提供**即時消費回饋**，並遵循隱私與最佳實務。

audience: **開發金融、轉帳或通訊類 App**、希望保護使用者免於社交工程詐騙與脅迫的工程師。
gloss_en: Meet Trust Insights
takeaway_en: The new Trust Insights framework assesses, in a privacy-preserving way, whether a user is being socially scammed or coerced, helping apps add protective friction in risky situations.

points_en.text: **Trust Insights** is a new framework that helps detect, in a **privacy-preserving** way, whether a user is being **socially scammed or coerced**.
Use **InsightEvaluator** to first requestAuthorization for permission, then request an assessment with **IsLikelyBeingCoachedInsight**.
Results are risk levels such as .unknown/.medium/.high, so the app can adjust its flow accordingly (for example, adding a confirmation step).
You must provide **real-time consumption feedback** via **reportConsumption** (such as .usedIncreasedFriction) and follow privacy and best practices.

audience_en: **Engineers building finance, money-transfer, or messaging apps** who want to protect users from social-engineering scams and coercion.
summary: 這場由 Apple 工程經理 Mike Armstrong 主講，介紹 iOS 27 全新框架 **Trust Insights**，用來偵測並回應針對「人」而非「系統」的**社交工程**攻擊。社交詐騙鎖定的是人的心理弱點：使用者可能在被施壓、恐嚇或欺騙下，完成一個技術上完全合法的操作，而 app 本身根本分辨不出這是真實意圖還是被脅迫的結果。常見的脅迫模式包括假冒技術支援誘導遠端存取、冒充銀行／政府／執法機關套取敏感資訊，以及利用親情、結合 AI deepfake 的家庭緊急詐騙。最棘手的是**即時教唆（real-time coaching）**——攻擊者透過電話或訊息一步步引導受害者親自操作，使得 MFA、生物辨識等既有防護全部失效，因為動手的正是使用者本人。

Trust Insights 提供一種全新的訊號：**行為脈絡（behavioral context）**，用來區分自由意志下的操作與被脅迫的行為。框架結合裝置端與雲端基礎設施，但整合完全是 client-side 的 Swift API。整合流程是：在 Xcode 宣告 entitlement 後 `import TrustInsights`，建立含所需 insight 的 parameter pack（須指定 schema、modelVersion 可選），再透過 `InsightEvaluator.InsightContext` 指定 **operationCategory** 與要請求的 evaluations。operationCategory 告訴系統使用者在做哪類動作、決定套用哪套模型邏輯，共有五類：**payment、account、resourceUse、communication、other**。接著建立 `InsightEvaluator`、檢查授權（使用者可完全掌控），最後非同步呼叫 `requestEvaluation`——這需要網路連線、可能耗時數秒，因此應安排在動畫或過場畫面等適當時機。

以 `IsLikelyBeingCoachedInsight` 為例，結果有三種值：**unknown**（無詐騙風險證據，但不可解讀為低風險）、**medium**（有部分教唆風險證據，可考慮增加摩擦或額外驗證）、**high**（顯著風險，應在使用者繼續前告知）。回饋是整合的必要環節：必須對每次 evaluation 呼叫 **`reportConsumption`** 回報 app 如何回應（六種值如 `usedIncreasedFriction`、`notUsedNotNeeded` 等），否則 app 可能被 rate-limit；另有 offline feedback，透過 **Apple Business Register** 的 server-to-server API 在事後（可能數天到數月）回報確認為詐騙的案例，以協助模型改進。

**隱私**是整套設計的核心：採資料最小化，裝置端資料就地處理、評估後立即丟棄，僅單一輸出值離開裝置，最終結果可能再結合 Apple Account 訊號與 velocity check。框架分析的是互動模式、時間、脈絡與基本感測資料，**絕不**觸及 Photos、Messages、Mail 的內容；使用者可在設定中關閉，且關閉後有冷卻期以保護被教唆關閉的受害者。**最佳實踐**包括：把 Trust Insights 整合進既有風險與決策邏輯而非當成唯一依據、在高價值金流／不可逆操作／權限授予／敏感資料分享等關鍵時刻才呼叫、絕不把 unknown 或缺值當成低風險，並完整處理 evaluation 與 insight 兩層各自不同的錯誤。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: Apple 工程經理 Mike Armstrong 開場說明 **Trust Insights** 用來偵測並回應**社交工程**威脅——這類攻擊鎖定人而非系統，利用心理而非技術漏洞。他列舉三大脅迫模式：假冒技術支援誘導遠端存取、冒充銀行／政府／執法機關套取資訊，以及結合 AI deepfake 的家庭緊急詐騙。核心難題是**即時教唆**：使用者在攻擊者引導下親自、經授權地完成操作，使 MFA 與生物辨識失效，因此需要能判斷「是否出於自由意志」的全新訊號，且此訊號必須兼顧隱私。

deepdive.title: Generating insights
deepdive.body: 進入整合流程，說明 Trust Insights 結合裝置與雲端，但整合完全是 client-side 的 Swift API。第一步是設定：產生 insight 需要 **entitlement**，要在 Xcode 為 app target 宣告該 capability。

deepdive.title: Generating insights
deepdive.body: `import TrustInsights` 後建立含所請求 insight 的 parameter pack（**schema** 必填、**modelVersion** 選填，同時指定當前與先前版本可支援模型治理與驗證）。透過 `InsightEvaluator.InsightContext` 指定 **operationCategory** 與 evaluations，類別共五種：**payment**（資產／金錢交換，含遊戲內購）、**account**（更新帳戶或安全資訊）、**resourceUse**（昂貴或受限的基礎設施如 AI 推論）、**communication**（傳訊、送出表單、簽署文件）與 **other**（後備）。接著建立 `InsightEvaluator`、檢查授權（使用者可完全掌控），再非同步呼叫 **`requestEvaluation`**——需網路、可能耗時數秒，宜安排在動畫或過場時機；開發時打到 sandbox，上架後改用 production 模型，並可用 Xcode build scheme 覆寫值與錯誤來測試。

deepdive.title: Handling results for IsLikelyBeingCoachedInsight
deepdive.body: 回應每個請求對應一個結果。以 `IsLikelyBeingCoachedInsight` 為例有三種值：**unknown**（無詐騙風險證據，但不可當作低風險）、**medium**（有部分教唆風險證據，可考慮加摩擦、額外驗證或調整風險評分）、**high**（顯著風險，應在使用者繼續前告知）。並強調需獨立處理 evaluation 層與 insight 層兩種不同意義的錯誤。

deepdive.title: Feedback requirements
deepdive.body: 說明整合需要兩種回饋：即時 consumption feedback（回報 app 對 insight 的回應方式）與 offline feedback（事後發現交易其實為詐騙時回報）。背後是一套精密的 ML 模型，裝置端資料就地處理、評估後立即丟棄，僅單一輸出值離開裝置，最終可能再納入 Apple Account 訊號與 velocity check。

deepdive.title: Real-time consumption feedback
deepdive.body: 對每次 evaluation 結果呼叫 **`reportConsumption`** 提交即時回饋，此呼叫為強制；若省略 app 可能被 rate-limit。六種值：**usedReducedFriction**、**usedUnchangedFriction**、**usedIncreasedFriction**（增加檢查，但不建議僅憑 insight 直接封鎖）、**notUsedNotNeeded**（使用者取消）、**notUsedError**（技術失敗如結果太晚到）與 **usedEvaluationOnly**。offline label 對模型改進至關重要：經 **Apple Business Register** 的 server-to-server API、依含 insight identifier 的 schema 提交確認詐騙案例，且不得夾帶 PII 等多餘資訊、需對殘留值施以隱私保護以防 fingerprinting；offline 提交非必要但能強化整體生態。

deepdive.title: Privacy
deepdive.body: **資料最小化**是 Trust Insights 的核心：只處理必要資料、輸入立即丟棄、所有裝置來源資料都留在裝置上。框架分析的是互動模式、時間、脈絡與基本感測資料，**絕不**觸及 Photos、Messages、Mail 的內容，這些裝置衍生訊號也不與 Apple 或第三方分享。使用者在設定中有完整控制權可關閉，且關閉後可能有**冷卻期**，以保護那些被教唆去關閉此功能的受害者；app 應查詢授權狀態以確認使用者是否已啟用。

deepdive.title: Best practices
deepdive.body: 以實例說明：使用者正設定一筆大額轉帳給自稱是家人主治醫師的對象，app 在背景請求了 trust insight，**medium** 結果促使 app 顯示警告並對交易加入延遲；也可改為伺服器端處理、加入人工審查或調整風險而不打斷使用者。建議在最有價值的時刻才呼叫：高價值金流（如 P2P 付款）、不可逆操作（如刪除帳戶、匯出個資）、權限授予（如遠端存取、新裝置授權）與敏感資料分享。其他要點：把 Trust Insights 整合進既有風險邏輯而非當成唯一依據、善用跨版本模型抽樣、各層分別處理錯誤、**絕不**把 unknown 或缺值當成低風險，並務必在 app 內提交即時回饋以避免 rate limit、盡量透過 Apple Business Register 貢獻 offline 詐騙標籤。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 結語呼籲找出 app 中 Trust Insights 能與既有邏輯協同保護使用者的關鍵時刻，依最佳實踐與文件採用框架，並到 **Apple Business Register** 註冊以了解 Partner Data Services。並推薦關注 **App Attest**（驗證伺服器請求來自合法 app 實例），鼓勵此刻透過 Feedback Assistant 對框架、能力或高流量使用案例提供回饋。

summary_en: Presented by Apple Engineering Manager Mike Armstrong, this session introduces **Trust Insights**, a new framework in iOS 27 for detecting and responding to **social engineering** attacks that target people rather than systems. Social scams exploit human psychology: users may be pressured, frightened, or deceived into performing an action that is technically legitimate, and the app itself cannot tell genuine intent from coerced intent apart. Common coercion patterns include tech-support scams that prompt remote access, authority impersonation of banks, government, or law enforcement to collect sensitive data, and family-emergency fraud increasingly using AI deepfakes. The hardest case is **real-time coaching**—attackers guide victims step by step to act themselves, defeating MFA and biometrics because the user is the one acting.

Trust Insights provides a new signal—**behavioral context**—to distinguish freely-made actions from coerced ones. The framework combines on-device and cloud infrastructure, but integration is entirely client-side via a Swift API. The flow: declare an entitlement in Xcode, `import TrustInsights`, build a parameter pack of requested insights (schema required, modelVersion optional), then specify the **operationCategory** and evaluations through `InsightEvaluator.InsightContext`. The operation category tells the system what kind of action the user is taking and which model logic applies; five exist: **payment, account, resourceUse, communication, other**. You then create an `InsightEvaluator`, check authorization (the user has full control), and asynchronously call `requestEvaluation`—which needs Internet, can take a couple of seconds, and should be placed during animations or interstitials.

For `IsLikelyBeingCoachedInsight`, results take three values: **unknown** (no evidence of scam risk, but not to be read as low risk), **medium** (some coaching-risk evidence; consider friction or extra verification), and **high** (significant risk; inform the user before proceeding). Feedback is mandatory: call **`reportConsumption`** on every evaluation to report how the app responded (six values such as `usedIncreasedFriction` and `notUsedNotNeeded`), or risk being rate-limited. Offline feedback is submitted later—days to months afterward—via a server-to-server API through **Apple Business Register** for transactions confirmed as fraud, helping improve the model.

**Privacy** is foundational: data minimization means device-sourced inputs are processed locally and discarded immediately, with only a single output value leaving the device, possibly combined with Apple Account signals and velocity checks. The framework analyzes interaction patterns, timing, context, and basic sensor data—**never** content in Photos, Messages, or Mail. Users can disable it in Settings, with a cooldown to protect those coached into turning it off. **Best practices**: integrate Trust Insights into existing risk and decision logic rather than treating it as the sole factor, call it only at the moments that matter (high-value financial transactions, irreversible actions, permission grants, sensitive data sharing), never treat unknown or a missing value as low risk, and handle the distinct evaluation-level and insight-level errors separately.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Apple Engineering Manager Mike Armstrong opens by explaining that **Trust Insights** detects and responds to **social engineering** threats—attacks that target people not systems, exploiting psychology rather than technical flaws. He lists three coercion patterns: tech-support scams prompting remote access, authority impersonation of banks/government/law enforcement, and family-emergency fraud using AI deepfakes. The core difficulty is **real-time coaching**: users act themselves, authenticated and legitimately, defeating MFA and biometrics—so a new signal is needed to tell whether they're acting freely, and it must preserve privacy.

deepdive_en.title: Generating insights
deepdive_en.body: He begins the integration, noting Trust Insights combines device and cloud but integrates entirely client-side via Swift. The first step is configuration: generating insights requires an **entitlement**, declared as a capability on the app target in Xcode.

deepdive_en.title: Generating insights
deepdive_en.body: After `import TrustInsights`, build a parameter pack of requested insights (**schema** required, **modelVersion** optional—specifying current and prior versions supports model governance and validation). Through `InsightEvaluator.InsightContext` you set **operationCategory** and evaluations; five categories exist: **payment** (asset/money exchange, including IAP), **account** (updating account or security info), **resourceUse** (costly or constrained infrastructure such as AI inference), **communication** (messaging, form submission, document signing), and **other** (fallback). Then create an `InsightEvaluator`, check authorization (the user has full control), and asynchronously call **`requestEvaluation`**—it needs Internet, can take seconds, and is best placed during animations or interstitials; development hits a sandbox, distribution uses production models, and Xcode build schemes can override values and errors for testing.

deepdive_en.title: Handling results for IsLikelyBeingCoachedInsight
deepdive_en.body: The response has one result per requested evaluation. For `IsLikelyBeingCoachedInsight` there are three values: **unknown** (no scam-risk evidence, but not to be interpreted as low risk), **medium** (some coaching-risk evidence; consider friction, extra verification, or adjusting risk scoring), and **high** (significant risk; inform the user before proceeding). He stresses handling evaluation-level and insight-level errors independently, as they carry different meaning.

deepdive_en.title: Feedback requirements
deepdive_en.body: Two kinds of feedback complete the integration: real-time consumption feedback reporting how the app responded, and offline feedback for transactions that later prove fraudulent. Behind the three values is a sophisticated ML model; device-sourced data is processed locally and discarded immediately, with only a single output value leaving the device, which may incorporate Apple Account signals and velocity checks.

deepdive_en.title: Real-time consumption feedback
deepdive_en.body: Submit real-time feedback by calling **`reportConsumption`** on each evaluation result—mandatory per request, or the app may be rate-limited. Six values: **usedReducedFriction**, **usedUnchangedFriction**, **usedIncreasedFriction** (added checks, though blocking solely on an insight is discouraged), **notUsedNotNeeded** (user cancelled), **notUsedError** (technical failure such as a late result), and **usedEvaluationOnly**. Offline labels are vital for model improvement: submitted via a server-to-server API through **Apple Business Register** using a schema with the original insight identifier, excluding PII and applying privacy-preserving techniques against fingerprinting—optional but strengthening the ecosystem.

deepdive_en.title: Privacy
deepdive_en.body: **Data minimization** is central: only what's needed is processed, inputs are discarded immediately, and all device-sourced data stays on the device. The framework analyzes interaction patterns, timing, context, and basic sensor data—**never** content in Photos, Messages, or Mail—and none of these signals are shared with Apple or third parties. Users have full control to disable it in Settings, with a possible **cooldown** afterward to protect victims coached into turning it off; apps should query authorization status to check whether it's enabled.

deepdive_en.title: Best practices
deepdive_en.body: He gives an example: a user sets up a large transfer to someone claiming to be a family member's doctor; the app requested a trust insight in the background, and the **medium** result prompts it to show a warning and add a delay—alternatively handled server-side, with manual review, or by adjusting risk without disruption. Call it at the moments of most value: high-value financial transactions (P2P payments), irreversible actions (account deletion, data export), permission grants (remote access, new device authorization), and sensitive data sharing. Other points: integrate Trust Insights into existing risk logic rather than as the sole factor, sample model versions over time, handle each error level, **never** treat unknown or a missing value as low risk, and submit real-time feedback in-app to avoid rate limits while contributing offline fraud labels via Apple Business Register.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: He closes by urging developers to identify the moments where Trust Insights can work alongside existing logic to protect users, adopt the framework per best practices and documentation, and register on **Apple Business Register** to learn about Partner Data Services. He points to **App Attest** for verifying server requests come from legitimate app instances, and encourages submitting feedback now via Feedback Assistant on the framework, its capabilities, or high-volume use cases.

title: Inside Apple Intelligence and Xcode: Special Presentation
gloss: 深入 Apple Intelligence 與 Xcode：特別發表
takeaway: 在 Steve Jobs Theater 一次掌握 Xcode 27、App Intents、Foundation Models、Core AI 與 MLX 等 Apple Intelligence 與開發工具的最新進展。

points.text: 於 Steve Jobs Theater 舉行的特別發表，總覽 **Apple Intelligence** 與 **Xcode** 的最新進展。
介紹 **Xcode 27** 如何加速開發流程，是本場的重點段落之一。
說明 **App Intents** 與 **Foundation Models framework** 如何把智慧功能帶進你的 App。
涵蓋 **Core AI** 與 **MLX**，介紹底層 AI 能力與在 Apple 裝置上執行模型的方案。

audience: **想一次掌握 Apple Intelligence 與開發工具走向**的所有 Apple 平台開發者。
gloss_en: Inside Apple Intelligence and Xcode: Special Presentation
takeaway_en: At Steve Jobs Theater, get caught up all at once on the latest advancements in Apple Intelligence and developer tools, including Xcode 27, App Intents, Foundation Models, Core AI, and MLX.

points_en.text: A special presentation held at Steve Jobs Theater, surveying the latest advancements in **Apple Intelligence** and **Xcode**.
Introduces how **Xcode 27** accelerates the development workflow, one of the session's key segments.
Explains how **App Intents** and the **Foundation Models framework** bring intelligent features into your app.
Covers **Core AI** and **MLX**, introducing the underlying AI capabilities and ways to run models on Apple devices.

audience_en: All Apple platform developers who **want to get caught up all at once on the direction of Apple Intelligence and developer tools**.
summary: 這是一場在 **Steve Jobs Theater** 舉行的特別發表，主題環繞 **Apple Intelligence** 與 **Xcode** 的最新進展，目標是讓開發者了解如何運用 Apple 的裝置端智慧與升級後的開發工具來加速開發流程。內容從歡迎開場，貫穿 Xcode 27、App Intents、Foundation Models framework、Core AI 到 MLX，最後收尾於後續行動建議，整體像是一份把「智慧」如何滲透進整個開發與執行環節的全景導覽。
工具鏈方面，**Xcode 27** 是這場的重心之一，強調把生成式與輔助式的智慧能力直接整合進 IDE，讓寫程式、理解程式碼與除錯都更省力。緊接著的 **App Intents** 則把焦點移到讓 app 的功能被系統與智慧層理解、調用，使 Siri、Spotlight 等入口能更深度地驅動 app 行為。
在模型與執行層，**Foundation Models framework** 提供了直接在裝置上呼叫 Apple 大型語言模型的途徑，讓開發者以隱私優先、離線可用的方式把生成能力嵌入 app；**Core AI** 與 **MLX** 則分別代表系統層的 AI 基礎建設，以及在 Apple Silicon 上做機器學習研究與自訂模型訓練／推論的高效框架。
整體訊息很明確：Apple 正把智慧能力從系統一路延伸到開發工具與自訂模型，**Foundation Models**、**App Intents**、**Core AI** 與 **MLX** 構成一套可組合的堆疊。實務上的下一步，是評估自家 app 哪些環節能用裝置端模型強化、用 App Intents 暴露關鍵功能，並善用 Xcode 27 的智慧輔助加速落地。

deepdive.title: Welcome
deepdive.body: 在 **Steve Jobs Theater** 的開場歡迎，為這場 **Apple Intelligence** 與 **Xcode** 的特別發表定調，預告將涵蓋從開發工具到裝置端模型的多項進展。主軸是說明這些能力如何串連起來，協助開發者加速開發流程。

deepdive.title: Xcode 27
deepdive.body: 聚焦 **Xcode 27** 如何把智慧輔助能力整合進 IDE，讓撰寫、理解與除錯程式碼更有效率。重點在於把生成式與輔助式工具帶到開發者日常的工作流程中。

deepdive.title: App Intents
deepdive.body: 介紹 **App Intents** 如何讓 app 的核心功能被系統與智慧層理解與調用，串接 Siri、Spotlight 等系統入口。透過清楚定義 intents，app 能更深度地參與裝置端的智慧體驗。

deepdive.title: Foundation Models framework
deepdive.body: 說明 **Foundation Models framework** 讓開發者直接在裝置上呼叫 Apple 的大型語言模型，以隱私優先、離線可用的方式把生成能力嵌入 app。這是把 Apple Intelligence 落地到第三方 app 的關鍵途徑。

deepdive.title: Core AI
deepdive.body: 介紹 **Core AI** 作為系統層的 AI 基礎建設，承載並協調裝置上的智慧能力。重點在於它如何為上層的 Foundation Models 與 app 功能提供統一的基礎。

deepdive.title: MLX
deepdive.body: 聚焦 **MLX** 這套針對 **Apple Silicon** 最佳化的機器學習框架，支援在 Mac 上做研究、訓練與推論。它讓開發者能高效地實驗與部署自訂模型。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 收尾整理後續行動建議，引導開發者評估哪些 app 環節適合導入裝置端模型與 **App Intents**，並善用 **Xcode 27** 的智慧輔助。鼓勵把這套可組合的智慧堆疊實際應用到自家專案。

summary_en: This is a special presentation held in the **Steve Jobs Theater**, centered on the latest advancements in **Apple Intelligence** and **Xcode**, aimed at showing developers how to use Apple's on-device intelligence and upgraded tooling to accelerate their workflows. It runs from a welcome opening through Xcode 27, App Intents, the Foundation Models framework, Core AI, and MLX, closing with next steps — a panoramic tour of how intelligence threads through the entire development and runtime stack.

On the tooling side, **Xcode 27** is a key focus, emphasizing how generative and assistive intelligence is integrated directly into the IDE to make writing, understanding, and debugging code easier. **App Intents** then shifts the focus to making an app's capabilities understandable and invocable by the system and the intelligence layer, so entry points like Siri and Spotlight can drive app behavior more deeply.

At the model and runtime layer, the **Foundation Models framework** provides a path to call Apple's large language models directly on device, letting developers embed generative capabilities in a privacy-first, offline-capable way; **Core AI** and **MLX** represent the system-level AI foundation and an efficient framework for machine learning research and custom model training/inference on Apple Silicon, respectively.

The overall message is clear: Apple is extending intelligence from the system all the way into developer tools and custom models, with **Foundation Models**, **App Intents**, **Core AI**, and **MLX** forming a composable stack. Practically, the next step is to assess which parts of your app can be enhanced with on-device models, expose key functionality via App Intents, and use Xcode 27's intelligent assistance to ship faster.

deepdive_en.title: Welcome
deepdive_en.body: An opening welcome in the **Steve Jobs Theater** sets the stage for this special presentation on **Apple Intelligence** and **Xcode**, previewing advancements spanning from developer tools to on-device models. The throughline is how these capabilities connect to help developers accelerate their workflows.

deepdive_en.title: Xcode 27
deepdive_en.body: Focuses on how **Xcode 27** integrates intelligent assistance into the IDE to make writing, understanding, and debugging code more efficient. The emphasis is on bringing generative and assistive tooling into developers' day-to-day workflow.

deepdive_en.title: App Intents
deepdive_en.body: Introduces how **App Intents** make an app's core capabilities understandable and invocable by the system and the intelligence layer, connecting entry points like Siri and Spotlight. By clearly defining intents, an app can participate more deeply in the device's intelligent experiences.

deepdive_en.title: Foundation Models framework
deepdive_en.body: Explains how the **Foundation Models framework** lets developers call Apple's large language models directly on device, embedding generative capabilities in a privacy-first, offline-capable way. This is the key path for bringing Apple Intelligence into third-party apps.

deepdive_en.title: Core AI
deepdive_en.body: Introduces **Core AI** as the system-level AI foundation that hosts and coordinates on-device intelligence. The focus is on how it provides a unified base for the higher-level Foundation Models and app features.

deepdive_en.title: MLX
deepdive_en.body: Focuses on **MLX**, a machine learning framework optimized for **Apple Silicon** that supports research, training, and inference on the Mac. It enables developers to experiment with and deploy custom models efficiently.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Wraps up with next-step guidance, encouraging developers to assess which parts of their apps suit on-device models and **App Intents**, and to leverage **Xcode 27**'s intelligent assistance. It motivates applying this composable intelligence stack to real projects.

title: Find and fix performance issues in your Metal games
gloss: 找出並修復 Metal 遊戲的效能問題
takeaway: 用 metalperftrace 收集與分析 Metal 效能追蹤，搭配 StateReporting 將指標對應到遊戲狀態，並以 MetricKit 蒐集實機現場資料，精準定位效能瓶頸。
chapters: Filter by process and emit JSON
Include full state transitions in overview

points.text: 用命令列工具 **metalperftrace** 收集效能追蹤，可指定最近時段或明確時間範圍。
以 **overview** 檢視 FPS、Frame Time、On-GPU Time 等指標，並可依 process 過濾與輸出 JSON。
透過 **StateReporting** 的 **SRStateReporter** 回報狀態轉換與中繼資料，把效能指標對應到遊戲情境（如關卡、畫質）。
用 **--include-state-transitions** 與 **--aggregate** 依狀態彙總指標，找出哪些情境最耗效能。
搭配 **MetricKit** 蒐集使用者實機的現場效能資料，補足實驗室外的真實表現。

audience: 適合**開發 Metal 遊戲、需要診斷與優化 GPU 與整體效能的遊戲與圖形開發者**。
gloss_en: Find and fix performance issues in your Metal games
takeaway_en: Use metalperftrace to collect and analyze Metal performance traces, pair it with StateReporting to map metrics to game state, and gather on-device field data with MetricKit to pinpoint performance bottlenecks.

points_en.text: Collect performance traces with the command-line tool **metalperftrace**, targeting either a recent window or an explicit time range.
Use **overview** to inspect metrics like FPS, Frame Time, and On-GPU Time, with the ability to filter by process and output JSON.
Report state transitions and metadata via **StateReporting**'s **SRStateReporter** to map performance metrics to game context (such as level or quality settings).
Use **--include-state-transitions** and **--aggregate** to summarize metrics by state and find which contexts cost the most performance.
Pair with **MetricKit** to gather real on-device field performance data, filling in the gaps beyond the lab.

audience_en: **Game and graphics developers building Metal games who need to diagnose and optimize GPU and overall performance.**
summary: 本場由 Metal Tools 團隊主講，目標是幫你在**長時間遊戲 session** 中快速蒐集並定位效能問題，交付一致而流暢的幀率。打磨流暢體驗是個循環：在各種裝置與形態上實測、蒐集效能資料、分析、找出問題、修復，再重來。玩家連玩數小時時諸多條件會變（裝置升溫導致 thermal state 變化、調整畫質設定、在不同關卡與戰鬥間移動），因此必須跨多種情境長時間量測。講者依序介紹可用的 **Metal performance metrics**、蒐集與分析長時間 trace 的新工具、用 **StateReporting** 為 trace 加上脈絡，以及出貨後用 **MetricKit** 蒐集現場資料。

**Metric** 方面，Metal Tools 提供 FPS、GPU time、frame interval 等時序指標，以及 layer sizes、composition mode、MetalFX 等顯示相關指標。**Metal Performance HUD** 能在遊戲畫面上即時疊加顯示這些指標、可自訂或選 preset，但無法長時間儲存。要拿到細節就得蒐集長時間 **trace**：桌上實測可用 Instruments 的 **Game Performance Overview** 範本（擷取彙總的 Metal 指標與 Time Profiler CPU 取樣）。更強的是——系統其實**一直在背景記錄**並保存 Metal 效能與資源使用指標達數日，因此長 session 結束後仍能**回溯（look-back）蒐集**。macOS 用新 CLI 工具 **`metalperftrace collect --last`**（如近 5 小時）或指定起訖時間；iOS 需一次性在開發者設定啟用 Performance Trace、設定回溯時長、並把 Performance Trace 按鈕加到控制中心，玩完一按即蒐集，完成後可傳到 Mac 分析。

**分析** trace：macOS 可用 `metalperftrace overview` 印出（或 `--json` 輸出）每個 process 的資源使用統計與各 layer 的 Metal 指標（如平均記憶體約 2.1GB、平均 FPS 約 60，及 frame/GPU time 的統計值），JSON 適合餵 regression 腳本或 AI agent 自動分流；也可用 Instruments 在時間軸上視覺化，偏離過多的數值會以顏色標示，可框選時間範圍即時彙總（範例某段平均 FPS 掉到 26、GPU 使用率很低）。但光看平均 FPS 缺乏可行動的**脈絡**——不知掉幀那刻遊戲在做什麼。

解法是新 API **StateReporting**，用四個概念描述遊戲隨時間的狀態：**domain**（代表某功能領域的有限狀態機，如 level、graphics、network），各 domain 同時只處於一個 **state**（含 label、不可變的 stable metadata、可變的 volatile metadata），玩家進度推進時在 state 間 transition。把多個 domain 疊到時間軸上，就能立即看出 FPS 下降對應的脈絡（例如畫質切到 High 時平均 FPS 只剩約 24）。API 支援 Swift 與 Objective-C，用 `reportTransition`（帶 label 與 stableMetadata）回報狀態、`reportVolatileMetadataUpdate` 更新動態值，並與 HUD、metalperftrace（`--include-state-transitions`、可依 state 彙總指標）、Instruments（在 Points of Interest 為每個 domain 建 track）緊密整合。最佳實務：domain 彼此正交、勿在單一 domain 塞太多維度、transition 頻率勿過高（過高會被系統節流）、並用工具確認狀態正確。出貨後則靠 **MetricKit**——它每日把含 Metal 幀率（且可依 StateReporting 狀態分組）的效能與電力 metrics、以及記憶體例外等 diagnostics 送回遊戲 process，讓你在現場持續監控並定位問題。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: Metal Tools 團隊工程師 Ruiwei 開場：流暢一致的幀率是給玩家最重要的體驗之一，而維持整段 session 的流暢是關鍵。打磨流暢是個循環——跨多裝置與形態實測、蒐集資料、分析、找問題、修復、再來。玩家連玩數小時時 thermal state、畫質設定、關卡與戰鬥都會變，故須跨多情境長時間量測。預告將依序講 Metal 指標、長時間 trace 的蒐集與分析、用 StateReporting 加脈絡、以及出貨後用 MetricKit 蒐集現場資料。

deepdive.title: Metal performance metrics
deepdive.body: 介紹 Metal Tools 提供的各類指標作為比較不同 session 的基準：時序類如 frames per second、GPU time、frame interval 反映幀的節奏與 GPU 利用率；顯示相關如 layer sizes、composition mode、MetalFX 指標則用來確認顯示設定正確。**Metal Performance HUD** 能在遊戲內容上疊加顯示 FPS、記憶體、frame interval 等，可在設定面板逐項開關或選 preset，適合開發中快速掌握。

deepdive.title: Trace collection
deepdive.body: 指出 HUD 雖好但無法長時間儲存指標，容易忘記掉幀發生在哪裡，要拿細節就得蒐集長時間 **trace**。桌上實測可用 Instruments 的 **Game Performance Overview** 範本：擷取彙總的 Metal 效能指標與 Time Profiler CPU 取樣，可從 Instruments 啟動遊戲或附加到已執行的 session，按錄製即可，適合數分鐘以上的 session。

deepdive.title: Collect a trace with metalperftrace
deepdive.body: 揭示更強大之處：遊戲執行時系統**一直在記錄並保存** Metal 效能與資源使用指標（彙總與選用的 per-frame，如 CPU、GPU、FPS、Memory）達數日，因此長 session 結束後仍能**回溯蒐集**。macOS 用新 CLI 工具 `metalperftrace collect` 並傳 `--last`（如近 5 小時）或指定起訖時間，無需額外設定。

deepdive.title: Analyze performance traces
deepdive.body: 蒐集完進入分析：macOS 可用 `metalperftrace` 印出或匯出指標概觀，或在 Instruments 中視覺化探索。兩者皆會示範。

deepdive.title: Print a trace overview
deepdive.body: 用 `metalperftrace overview` 加 trace 檔印出整體效能：報告對每個 process 分兩段——資源使用統計（記憶體、CPU time、disk activity）與各 layer 的 Metal 指標。範例該 session 平均記憶體約 2.1GB、平均 FPS 約 60，並含 frame time 與 on-GPU time 的統計值，快速給出整體概況。

deepdive.title: Filter by process and emit JSON
deepdive.body: 若 trace 含多個遊戲 session 或 Metal app，可用 predicate 只印出指定 process 的資料；亦可加 `--json` 讓 metalperftrace 輸出結構化格式，方便餵入 regression 測試腳本或 AI agent 自動分流潛在效能問題。Instruments 也能開啟並視覺化 trace 做更深入分析：資料畫在時間軸上、偏離過多者以不同顏色標示（如某段 FPS 掉幀標為黃色），詳情視圖顯示各指標的 min／max／平均／標準差，可框選時間範圍即時更新（範例該段平均 FPS 掉到 26、GPU 使用率很低）。

deepdive.title: Contextualize with StateReporting
deepdive.body: 點出挑戰：知道掉幀約在第 12 分鐘，卻不知那時遊戲在做什麼——光看平均 FPS 缺乏可行動脈絡。為此引入新 API **StateReporting**，用四個核心概念描述遊戲隨時間的行為與狀態：**domain**（代表某功能領域的有限狀態機，如追蹤玩家進度的 level domain），各 domain 同時只處於一個 **state**（以 label 起始，可含不可變的 **stable metadata** 與會變的 **volatile metadata**），玩家推進時在 state 間 transition。可定義多個 domain（level、graphics、network），疊到時間軸後即能立即看出需改進處。並給出 Swift／Objective-C 範例：建立 domain（反向 DNS 字串）、取得 reporter，用 `reportTransition`（帶 label 與選用 stableMetadata）回報狀態，用 `reportVolatileMetadataUpdate` 在不轉換狀態下更新動態值。

deepdive.title: Include full state transitions in overview
deepdive.body: StateReporting 與所有工具緊密整合。在 **Metal Performance HUD**，state domain 清單會出現在指標設定分頁，啟用後疊加層會顯示 label、stable 與 volatile metadata（範例回報 level 狀態：biome 與 id 為 stable、玩家位置為每秒一次的 volatile），是檢查 StateReporting 採用最直接的方式。在 `metalperftrace` 印 overview 時，報告會列出 domain、transition 數與最後已知狀態；加 `--include-state-transitions` 則印出含起訖時間戳的完整狀態清單。

deepdive.title: Aggregate metrics by state
deepdive.body: metalperftrace 還能**依狀態自動彙總指標**：可對所有 domain 與 transition、特定 domain 的所有 transition、或某 domain 內特定 state label 彙總。例如想看畫質設為 High 時的平均 FPS，就請它彙總 graphics domain 的「High」label——報告顯示該狀態的詳情、作用時長與其他 domain 的重疊狀態（範例 High 時平均 FPS 僅約 24）。要更視覺化可在 Instruments 開啟：每個 domain 會在 Points of Interest 各成一條 track，繪出 state transition 與 volatile 更新，可選個別狀態檢視 metadata，結合 Metal 指標即可確認幀率隨畫質切到 High 而開始下降。

deepdive.title: Collect field data with MetricKit
deepdive.body: 工具不止於上市前。**MetricKit** 提供 metrics 與 diagnostics 兩類資料，讓遊戲在 process 內直接取得電力與效能報告：玩家遊玩時於背景持續蒐集、每日交付一份報告。macOS／iOS 27 起 MetricKit 揭露 Metal 幀率（及大量其他效能與電力指標），並可**依 StateReporting 狀態分組**幀率（範例報告含整體平均幀率，並依 level domain 各狀態細分）。這些資料送到遊戲 process 可做本機分析、或打包做離線彙總，以在現場監控效能、找出可調查修復的問題。MetricKit 也提供 diagnostics（如記憶體例外）幫你定位是哪段程式造成問題。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 收尾回顧：iOS／macOS 27 中 Metal 效能指標一直被系統記錄，可回溯蒐集橫跨數小時數日的指標，並用 metalperftrace 與 Instruments 分析；新 **StateReporting** API 可為 trace 加脈絡，出貨後 **MetricKit** 從玩家裝置送回 metrics 與 diagnostics。並列出採用 StateReporting 的最佳實務：先審慎設計 domain 與 state（各 domain 應彼此正交、勿在單一 domain 塞太多維度）、勿有過多 transition（StateReporting 為長期脈絡而設、非高頻狀態變化，過高會被系統節流而丟失資訊）、並用 HUD 與 Instruments 確認狀態正確。建議從設計遊戲中最重要的 domain（level、graphics、network）開始回報，並整合 MetricKit 蒐集每日報告。

summary_en: Presented by the Metal Tools team, this session helps you quickly collect and pinpoint performance issues across **long game sessions** to deliver a consistent, smooth frame rate. Polishing smoothness is a cycle: play-test on many devices and form factors, collect performance data, analyze, identify issues, fix, and repeat. Over hours of play many conditions change (the device heats up and thermal state shifts, players adjust graphics settings, they move between levels and fights), so you must measure across many scenarios over long periods. The talk covers the available **Metal performance metrics**, new tools for collecting and analyzing long traces, **StateReporting** to contextualize traces, and **MetricKit** for collecting field data after shipping.

On **metrics**, Metal Tools provides timing metrics like FPS, GPU time, and frame interval, plus display-related ones like layer sizes, composition mode, and MetalFX. The **Metal Performance HUD** overlays these live on the game, customizable or via presets, but can't store them over long durations. For detail you need long **traces**: at the desk, use Instruments' **Game Performance Overview** template (aggregated Metal metrics plus Time Profiler CPU samples). More powerfully, the system is **always recording** and saving Metal performance and resource metrics for days, so you can **look back and collect** after a long session ends. On macOS, use the new CLI tool **`metalperftrace collect --last`** (e.g., the last 5 hours) or an explicit time range; on iOS, a one-time setup enables Performance Trace in developer settings, sets the look-back duration, and adds the Performance Trace button to Control Center—tap after playing to collect, then transfer to a Mac.

To **analyze** a trace, macOS can `metalperftrace overview` to print (or `--json` to emit) per-process resource-usage stats and per-layer Metal metrics (e.g., average memory ~2.1GB, average FPS ~60, plus stats for frame and GPU time), with JSON ideal for feeding regression scripts or AI agents for auto-triage. Or open it in Instruments for a timeline visualization where deviating values are color-highlighted and you can select a range for live aggregation (one stretch averaged 26 FPS with very low GPU usage). But average FPS alone lacks actionable **context**—you don't know what the game was doing when the drop happened.

The fix is the new **StateReporting** API, describing the game's state over time with four concepts: a **domain** (a finite state machine for an area of functionality, like level, graphics, network), each in one **state** at a time (with a label, immutable stable metadata, and mutable volatile metadata), transitioning between states as the player progresses. Overlaying multiple domains on the timeline immediately reveals the context of an FPS drop (e.g., average FPS of only ~24 when graphics is High). The API supports Swift and Objective-C, using `reportTransition` (with label and stableMetadata) and `reportVolatileMetadataUpdate`, and integrates tightly with the HUD, metalperftrace (`--include-state-transitions`, aggregate metrics by state), and Instruments (a track per domain in Points of Interest). Best practices: keep domains orthogonal, don't pack too many dimensions into one domain, don't transition too frequently (the system throttles excessive rates), and verify states with the tools. After shipping, **MetricKit** delivers daily performance and power metrics (Metal frame rate, grouped by StateReporting state) plus diagnostics like memory exceptions to your game process for ongoing field monitoring and triage.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Metal Tools engineer Ruiwei opens: a smooth, consistent frame rate is one of the most important things for players, and maintaining it across a whole session is key. Polishing smoothness is a cycle—play-test across devices and form factors, collect data, analyze, identify issues, fix, repeat. Over hours of play, thermal state, graphics settings, and levels/fights all change, so you must measure across scenarios over long periods. He previews covering Metal metrics, collecting and analyzing long traces, adding context with StateReporting, and collecting field data with MetricKit after shipping.

deepdive_en.title: Metal performance metrics
deepdive_en.body: Introduces Metal Tools metrics as a baseline for comparing sessions: timing metrics like frames per second, GPU time, and frame interval reflect frame pacing and GPU utilization; display-related ones like layer sizes, composition mode, and MetalFX metrics confirm display settings are correct. The **Metal Performance HUD** overlays FPS, memory, and frame interval on game content, with a config panel to toggle each metric or pick a preset—great for a quick read during development.

deepdive_en.title: Trace collection
deepdive_en.body: Notes the HUD can't store metrics over long durations and it's easy to forget where drops happened, so you need long **traces** for detail. At the desk, use Instruments' **Game Performance Overview** template: it captures aggregated Metal metrics and Time Profiler CPU samples, can start the game from Instruments or attach to a running session, and records on a click—ideal for sessions of minutes or longer.

deepdive_en.title: Collect a trace with metalperftrace
deepdive_en.body: Reveals the powerful part: while the game runs, the system is **always recording and saving** Metal performance and resource metrics (aggregated and optional per-frame, like CPU, GPU, FPS, Memory) for days, so you can **look back and collect** after a long session ends. On macOS, the new CLI tool `metalperftrace collect` with `--last` (e.g., the last 5 hours) or an explicit start/end range does this with no extra configuration.

deepdive_en.title: Analyze performance traces
deepdive_en.body: After collecting, on to analysis: on macOS you can print or export an overview of metrics with `metalperftrace`, or open traces in Instruments to explore visually. Both are demonstrated.

deepdive_en.title: Print a trace overview
deepdive_en.body: Run `metalperftrace overview` with a trace file to print overall performance: per process the report has two sections—resource-usage stats (memory, CPU time, disk activity) and per-layer Metal metrics. In the example, average memory is ~2.1GB and average FPS ~60, with statistical values for frame time and on-GPU time, giving a quick overall picture.

deepdive_en.title: Filter by process and emit JSON
deepdive_en.body: If a trace has multiple sessions or Metal apps, a predicate prints data for a specific process; `--json` emits structured output ideal for regression scripts or AI agents to auto-triage issues. Instruments can also open and visualize traces for deeper analysis: data is plotted on a timeline with deviating values color-highlighted (e.g., an FPS drop marked yellow), the detail view shows min/max/average/standard deviation per metric, and selecting a range updates the aggregation live (one stretch averaged 26 FPS with very low GPU usage).

deepdive_en.title: Contextualize with StateReporting
deepdive_en.body: Highlights the challenge: knowing the drop happened around the 12-minute mark but not what the game was doing—average FPS lacks actionable context. Introduces the new **StateReporting** API with four core concepts: a **domain** (a finite state machine for an area of functionality, like a level domain tracking player progress), each in one **state** at a time (starting with a label, with optional immutable **stable metadata** and mutable **volatile metadata**), transitioning between states as the player progresses. You can define multiple domains (level, graphics, network) and overlay them to immediately spot areas to improve. The Swift/Objective-C example creates a domain (reverse-DNS string), gets a reporter, reports state with `reportTransition` (label plus optional stableMetadata), and updates dynamic values with `reportVolatileMetadataUpdate` without transitioning.

deepdive_en.title: Include full state transitions in overview
deepdive_en.body: StateReporting integrates tightly with all tools. In the **Metal Performance HUD**, the list of state domains appears in the metrics config tab, and enabling them shows the label and stable/volatile metadata (the example reports level state with biome and id as stable and player position as volatile updated once per second)—the most direct way to check adoption. In `metalperftrace` overview, the report lists domains, transition counts, and the last known state; `--include-state-transitions` prints the full list with start/end timestamps.

deepdive_en.title: Aggregate metrics by state
deepdive_en.body: metalperftrace can also **aggregate metrics by state automatically**: across all domains and transitions, all transitions for a specific domain, or a specific state label within a domain. For example, to see average FPS when graphics is High, aggregate the 'High' label of the graphics domain—the report shows state details, how long it was active, and overlapping states in other domains (average FPS only ~24 when High). For a visual look, open the trace in Instruments: each domain becomes a track in Points of Interest graphing transitions and volatile updates, with selectable states showing metadata, and combined with Metal metrics it confirms the frame rate started dropping as graphics changed to High.

deepdive_en.title: Collect field data with MetricKit
deepdive_en.body: The tools don't stop at launch. **MetricKit** provides metrics and diagnostics, giving the game in-process access to power and performance reports: it collects in the background as players play and delivers a daily report. In macOS/iOS 27, MetricKit exposes Metal frame rate (plus many other performance and power metrics) and can **group frame rate by StateReporting state** (the example report has overall average frame rate broken down by states in the level domain). These can be analyzed locally or packaged for off-device aggregation to monitor field performance and find issues; MetricKit also provides diagnostics (like memory exceptions) to identify which code path caused a problem.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Recaps: in iOS/macOS 27 Metal performance metrics are always recorded by the system, so you can look back and collect metrics spanning hours and days and analyze with metalperftrace and Instruments; the new **StateReporting** API adds context, and after shipping **MetricKit** sends back metrics and diagnostics from player devices. It lists StateReporting best practices: carefully design orthogonal domains and states (don't pack too many dimensions into one), don't have too many transitions (it's for long-term context, not high-frequency changes—the system throttles excessive rates and loses information), and verify states with the HUD and Instruments. Start by reporting the domains that matter most (level, graphics, network) and integrate MetricKit for daily reports.

title: Discover container machines
gloss: 認識 container machines
takeaway: container machine 是 Container 新增的工具，在 Mac 上提供輕量、可持續存在的 Linux 環境，可建立、執行指令並進入互動式 shell。

points.text: **container machine** 是 Container 內建的新工具，在 Mac 上提供**輕量且可持續存在的 Linux 環境**。
說明背後的**容器化（Containerization）**機制與**設計原則**。
可用 `container machine create --name demo --set-default alpine` **建立新的 container machine**。
用 `container machine run` 執行指令（如 echo、uname），或**進入互動式 shell**。
以 `container machine list` 列出現有環境，並可在其中**執行應用程式**。

audience: **需要在 Mac 上跑 Linux 環境的開發者**，想用輕量持久容器做開發或測試的人。
gloss_en: Discover container machines
takeaway_en: A container machine is a new tool in Container that provides a lightweight, persistent Linux environment on Mac, where you can create it, run commands, and enter an interactive shell.

points_en.text: A **container machine** is a new built-in tool in Container that provides a **lightweight, persistent Linux environment** on Mac.
Explains the underlying **Containerization** mechanism and its **design principles**.
Use `container machine create --name demo --set-default alpine` to **create a new container machine**.
Use `container machine run` to run commands (such as echo, uname), or **enter an interactive shell**.
List existing environments with `container machine list`, and **run applications** inside them.

audience_en: **Developers who need to run a Linux environment on Mac** and want to use lightweight, persistent containers for development or testing.
summary: Michael 介紹建立在 **Containerization**（一個聚焦安全、隱私與效能、用於在 macOS 上執行 Linux container 的 Swift 框架）之上的新功能 **Container machine**：在 Mac 上提供一個高度整合、持久的輕量 Linux 環境。它像 container 一樣快速輕量，又像 virtual machine 一樣持久，並透過 host 整合讓使用起來感覺原生於 macOS。

回顧 WWDC 25 開源的 Containerization：它提供 storage、networking、execution 與 Linux init system 的 API，為每個 container 提供 **VM 等級隔離**且具備 sub-second 啟動；隨附開源的 container 工具提供 image 建立、散布與生命週期管理的 CLI。Container machine 的設計原則是：快速輕量、易於管理、提供持久性可重複造訪，以及感覺像 macOS 的延伸。快速建立讓多個專案各有專屬環境，避免相依與 toolchain 衝突；持久環境讓你能隨開發週期逐步加入工具。

Container machine 是 container 工具的一級功能，使用與 container 相同的 **OCI image 格式**（demo 用 alpine）。每個 Container machine 在自己的輕量 VM 中執行，具狀態並能保存你在其中所做的修改，可依需要 start/stop 並從上次離開處接續。透過 **自動 user mapping、共享檔案系統，以及在任何終端機位置都能進入 Linux 環境**，它提供從 macOS 到 Linux 再返回的順暢轉換。

Demo 涵蓋：`container machine create --set-default` 建立並設為預設、`container machine run` 執行指令（`uname` 在 Mac 印 Darwin、在 Container machine 印 Linux）、自動鏡射使用者名稱與當前工作目錄、無參數 run 進入互動 shell、`container machine list` 列出名稱/IP/資源。最後以一個 **Vapor** web server 範例展示跨平台工作流：在 Mac 用 Xcode 編輯（含用 Icon Composer 改 icon），在 Container machine（已裝 Swift toolchain）編譯執行，並把 Vapor 設為監聽 Container machine 的外部 IP，再從 Mac 的 Safari 以 IP:8080 存取——檔案修改透過目錄共享即時可見，重新整理頁面即看到更新的 icon。鼓勵到 GitHub 下載最新 container 工具試用。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: Michael 開場介紹建立在 **Containerization** 之上的新功能 **Container machine**：在 Mac 上提供一個高度整合的 Linux 環境，像 container 一樣快速輕量、像 VM 一樣持久，並透過 host 整合讓使用感覺原生於 macOS。

deepdive.title: Containerization
deepdive.body: 回顧 WWDC 25 開源的 **Containerization**——用於在 macOS 上執行 Linux container 的 Swift 框架，提供 storage、networking、execution 與 Linux init system 的 API，為每個 container 提供 **VM 等級隔離**且具 sub-second 啟動；隨附的 container 工具提供 image 建立、散布與生命週期管理。詳見「Meet Containerization」。

deepdive.title: Design principles
deepdive.body: 說明 Container machine 的設計原則：快速輕量以融入既有工作流、在 macOS 與 Linux 間切換要容易、能快速自訂與建立新環境（讓多專案各有專屬環境避免相依衝突）、提供持久性以隨開發週期加入工具，並感覺像既有工作流的延伸。

deepdive.title: Container machine
deepdive.body: 說明 Container machine 如何改善跨平台工作流：每個都跑在自己的輕量 VM、使用與 container 相同的 image 格式、是 container 工具的一級功能且 UX 熟悉；具狀態並保存修改，並透過自動 user mapping、共享檔案系統與隨處進入 Linux 環境的能力提供順暢轉換。

deepdive.title: Demo
deepdive.body: 進入 demo 段落，開始實際操作 Container machine 的各項指令與工作流。

deepdive.title: Viewing container machine commands
deepdive.body: 執行 `container machine` 顯示可用動作總覽，包含 create、run、stop 等。

deepdive.title: Creating a new container machine
deepdive.body: 用 `container machine create` 提供名稱並以 `--set-default` 設為預設機器（之後指令免再帶名稱）。Container machine 使用與 container 相同的 **OCI image**，demo 採用常見的 alpine。

deepdive.title: Echo hi
deepdive.body: 用 `container machine run` 在 Container machine 內執行 `echo hi` 指令，驗證可在其中執行命令。

deepdive.title: Running uname
deepdive.body: 執行 `uname`：在 macOS 印出 Darwin，而 `container machine run uname` 印出 Linux，反映其實際執行環境。

deepdive.title: Start interactive shell
deepdive.body: 無額外參數的 `container machine run` 啟動互動 session。Container machine 自動鏡射 Mac 的使用者名稱與當前工作目錄，因此在內執行 `whoami` 與 `pwd` 回傳與 Mac 相同的結果，帶來無縫體驗。

deepdive.title: List container machines
deepdive.body: 用 `container machine list` 顯示所有 Container machine 的名稱、IP 位址與資源資訊；講者複製 IP 供稍後使用。

deepdive.title: Start interactive shell
deepdive.body: 以 `container machine run` 啟動互動 shell 進入已安裝 Swift toolchain 的環境，透過自動目錄共享，所有專案檔案（Package.swift、原始碼、Public 目錄）皆可用。

deepdive.title: Run the application
deepdive.body: 以 **Vapor** web server 示範跨平台工作流：因 Container machine 有隔離網路，需在 Xcode 把 Vapor 設定的 hostname 設為 Container machine 的 IP；此 Mac 上的編輯透過共享立即可用。編譯執行後從 Safari 以 IP:8080 存取網站；再用 Icon Composer 改 icon 並覆寫，無需複製檔案，重新整理頁面即見更新。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 總結 Container machine 結合 container 的易用與速度及 VM 的持久性，無縫整合讓 Linux 環境像 Mac 的延伸，鼓勵到 GitHub 下載最新 container 工具試用並回饋。

summary_en: Michael introduces **Container machine**, a new feature built on top of **Containerization** (a Swift framework for running Linux containers on macOS focused on security, privacy, and performance): a highly integrated, persistent, lightweight Linux environment on Mac. It's fast and lightweight like a container, persistent like a virtual machine, and — thanks to host integrations — feels native to macOS.

It reviews Containerization, open-sourced at WWDC 25: it provides APIs for storage, networking, execution, and a Linux init system, giving each container **VM-based isolation** with sub-second start times, alongside the open-source container tool for image creation, distribution, and lifecycle management. Container machine's design principles are: fast and lightweight, simple to manage, persistent so you can revisit over time, and feeling like an extension of macOS. Quick creation lets each project have its own environment without dependency or toolchain conflicts, and persistence lets you add tools over the development lifecycle.

Container machine is a first-class feature of the container tool and uses the same **OCI image format** as containers (the demo uses alpine). Each one runs in its own lightweight VM, is stateful, and persists the modifications you make, so you can start/stop projects and continue where you left off. With **automatic user mapping, shared filesystem support, and the ability to enter the Linux environment from anywhere in a terminal**, it provides a smooth transition from macOS into Linux and back.

The demo covers `container machine create --set-default` to create and set a default, `container machine run` to execute commands (`uname` prints Darwin on Mac but Linux inside the machine), automatic mirroring of username and working directory, `container machine run` with no args for an interactive shell, and `container machine list` for name/IP/resources. It ends with a **Vapor** web server showing a cross-platform workflow: edit on Mac in Xcode (including changing the icon in Icon Composer), build and run inside the Container machine (with the Swift toolchain installed), set Vapor to listen on the machine's external IP, and access it from Safari on the Mac at IP:8080 — file edits are instantly visible via directory sharing, and refreshing shows the updated icon. It encourages downloading the latest container tool from GitHub.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: Michael opens, introducing **Container machine**, a new feature built on **Containerization**: a highly integrated Linux environment on Mac that's fast and lightweight like a container, persistent like a VM, and — via host integrations — feels native to macOS.

deepdive_en.title: Containerization
deepdive_en.body: Reviews **Containerization**, open-sourced at WWDC 25 — a Swift framework for running Linux containers on macOS with APIs for storage, networking, execution, and a Linux init system, giving each container **VM-based isolation** with sub-second starts; the accompanying container tool handles image creation, distribution, and lifecycle. See 'Meet Containerization'.

deepdive_en.title: Design principles
deepdive_en.body: Lays out the design principles: fast and lightweight to fit existing workflows, easy switching between macOS and Linux, quick customization and creation of new environments (so multiple projects each get a dedicated one without conflicts), persistence to add tools over time, and feeling like an extension of the existing workflow.

deepdive_en.title: Container machine
deepdive_en.body: Explains how Container machine improves cross-platform workflows: each runs in its own lightweight VM, uses the same image format as containers, is a first-class container-tool feature with familiar UX, is stateful and persists modifications, and provides a smooth transition via automatic user mapping, shared filesystem, and entering the Linux environment from anywhere.

deepdive_en.title: Demo
deepdive_en.body: Begins the demo section, moving into hands-on use of Container machine's commands and workflow.

deepdive_en.title: Viewing container machine commands
deepdive_en.body: Running `container machine` shows an overview of available actions, including create, run, and stop.

deepdive_en.title: Creating a new container machine
deepdive_en.body: Uses `container machine create` with a name and `--set-default` to set it as the default machine (so later commands omit the name). Container machine uses the same **OCI images** as containers; the demo uses the common alpine image.

deepdive_en.title: Echo hi
deepdive_en.body: Uses `container machine run` to execute `echo hi` inside the machine, verifying commands can run within it.

deepdive_en.title: Running uname
deepdive_en.body: Runs `uname`: on macOS it prints Darwin, while `container machine run uname` prints Linux, reflecting the runtime environment.

deepdive_en.title: Start interactive shell
deepdive_en.body: `container machine run` with no extra arguments starts an interactive session. Container machine automatically mirrors the Mac's username and current working directory, so `whoami` and `pwd` inside return the same results as the Mac, for a seamless experience.

deepdive_en.title: List container machines
deepdive_en.body: Uses `container machine list` to display each machine's name, IP address, and resource info; the presenter copies the IP for later use.

deepdive_en.title: Start interactive shell
deepdive_en.body: Starts an interactive shell with `container machine run` into an environment that has the Swift toolchain installed; thanks to automatic directory sharing, all project files (Package.swift, source, Public directory) are available.

deepdive_en.title: Run the application
deepdive_en.body: Demonstrates a cross-platform workflow with a **Vapor** web server: because the machine has an isolated network, Vapor's hostname is set in Xcode to the machine's IP; the Mac edit is instantly available via sharing. After compiling and running, the site is accessed from Safari at IP:8080; changing the icon in Icon Composer and overwriting it requires no file copy, and refreshing shows the update.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: Wraps up: Container machine combines the usability and speed of containers with the persistence of a VM, with seamless integrations making the Linux environment feel like an extension of the Mac. Encourages downloading the latest container tool from GitHub and sharing feedback.

title: Offer subscriptions to groups and organizations
gloss: 向群組與組織提供訂閱

audience_en: App Store developers and business teams who want to **sell subscriptions to teams, enterprises, or institutions**.
summary: 本場由 Apple 商務團隊的 Andrew 主講,說明如何把訂閱販售給群組與組織。訂閱已成為持續提供價值的重要方式,但有時訂閱者希望讓自己的社交群組、團隊或公司一起使用你的 app(例如公司想替剪輯團隊購買影片軟體,或跑步社團想互相督促)。為此 Apple 推出兩條全新途徑:在 app 內進行的 **Group Purchases**,以及透過 **Apple Business Manager** 與 **Apple School Manager** 的 **volume purchasing**(大量採購)。前者適合小型團隊或社交群組,後者則適合具規模與管理、身分需求的組織,可用既有的 device management service 以分配 app 的相同流程指派席次。

在可用性方面,這些新選項適用於所有使用 **StoreKit 2** 的自動續訂訂閱,對多數新舊訂閱預設為開啟;若訂閱已啟用 **Family Sharing**,則預設為退出(opted-out),讓你自行掌控兩種選項如何運作。你可在 **App Store Connect** 中調整,例如讓某訂閱僅在 Apple School Manager 上架以針對驗證過的教育機構制定特定價格,或完全關閉對群組與組織的販售(但仍可賣給個人)。

在定價上,預設每個席次以 App Store Connect 的現行價格出售;若要提供大量折扣,可使用全新的 **volume pricing** 配置,最多設定 5 個價格區間(price bands),完全掌控每個區間所需數量與價格。講者以三個區間為例:前 20 席每月每席 $19.99、第 21–40 席降為 $13.99、第 41 席以上為 $10.99,在購買 50 席的情境下平均每席約比基礎價降低 20%,藉此鼓勵買方涵蓋更大群組並整合採購。

在購買與席次管理上,**volume purchasing** 由 Apple Business/School Manager 顯示訂閱並處理購買,你只需確保訂閱對組織開放;**group purchases** 則由你自建 app 內 UI 觸發 **StoreKit 2** 購買流程,取得所需席次數後傳入購買請求。購買完成後,volume purchasing 由組織透過 device management service 指派席次,group purchases 則產生 **邀請連結** 供初始購買者分享。預設提供內建的席次管理系統(處理邀請連結、追蹤接受與指派、以及取消等生命週期);若已有自家系統,則可透過新的 **App Store Server API** 端點整合自訂邀請流程與群組成員查詢。

deepdive.title: Introduction
deepdive.body: Apple 商務團隊的 **Andrew** 說明訂閱是持續提供價值的好方式,但訂閱者有時希望讓社交群組、團隊或公司一起使用 app。為此 Apple 推出兩條購買與管理途徑:在 app 內的 **Group Purchases**(如同今日的 in-app purchase,但一次購買多個席次,再以邀請連結分享),以及透過 **Apple Business Manager** 與 **Apple School Manager** 的 **volume purchasing**,讓組織以分配 app 的相同工作流程,經 device management service 大規模指派席次。

deepdive.title: Availability
deepdive.body: 這些新選項適用於所有使用 **StoreKit 2** 的自動續訂訂閱,對多數新舊訂閱預設開啟;若已啟用 **Family Sharing** 則預設退出,讓你掌控兩者如何並存。在 **App Store Connect** 中可調整:例如讓訂閱僅於 **Apple School Manager** 上架以針對驗證過的教育機構制定價格,或完全關閉對群組與組織的販售(此時仍可賣給個人)。

deepdive.title: Pricing
deepdive.body: 預設每個席次以現行價格出售;要提供大量折扣可使用新的 **volume pricing**,最多設 5 個價格區間並完全掌控數量門檻與價格。講者示範三個區間:前 20 席每月每席 **$19.99**、第 21–40 席 **$13.99**、第 41 席以上 **$10.99**;在 50 席的購買情境下平均每席約比基礎價降低 **20%**,藉此鼓勵買方涵蓋更大群組並整合採購,設定直接在 App Store Connect 完成。

deepdive.title: Purchasing
deepdive.body: **volume purchasing** 由 Apple Business/School Manager 顯示訂閱並處理購買,你只需確保訂閱對組織開放。**group purchases** 則需自建 app 內 UI 觸發 **StoreKit 2** 購買流程,並在 merchandising 中凸顯群組購買的價值,接著取得顧客所需的席次數,傳入 StoreKit 2 購買請求。

deepdive.title: Seat Management
deepdive.body: 購買後,**volume purchasing** 由組織透過 device management service 以指派 app 的相同方式分配席次,適合大規模且確保由組織擁有與管理;**group purchases** 則為初始購買者產生 **邀請連結** 供分享。當任一類型完成指派,App Store 會為每位成員建立交易,你便可授予存取權。

deepdive.title: Next steps
deepdive.body: 預設的內建席次管理系統會處理邀請連結產生、成員接受與指派追蹤,以及取消等生命週期管理;若已有自家邀請與成員管理系統,可透過新的 **App Store Server API** 端點整合自訂邀請流程,並以群組管理端點查詢單一顧客所屬的所有群組與群組中所有成員。講者最後提醒:務必改用 **StoreKit 2**(這是必要條件),並重新評估可用性、定價策略與可加入的協作體驗。

summary_en: Presented by Andrew from Apple's commerce team, this session explains how to offer subscriptions to groups and organizations. Subscriptions are a great way to deliver continuous value, but sometimes a subscriber wants to get their social group, team, or company onto your app (for example, a company buying video editing software for its editors, or a run club keeping each other accountable). To address this, Apple introduces two new paths: **Group Purchases** made within your app, and **volume purchasing** through **Apple Business Manager** and **Apple School Manager**. The former suits small teams or social groups, while the latter suits organizations with scale and management/identity needs, who can assign seats through the same device management service workflows they already use to distribute apps.

On availability, these options apply to all auto-renewable subscriptions using **StoreKit 2** and are on by default for most new and existing subscriptions; if a subscription has **Family Sharing** enabled it is opted-out by default so you control how the two work together. You can adjust this in **App Store Connect**, for example making a subscription available only on Apple School Manager to create plans with specific pricing for verified educational institutions, or turning off selling to groups and organizations entirely (while still selling to individuals).

For pricing, every seat sells at the current App Store Connect price by default; to offer bulk discounts you can use the new **volume pricing** configuration with up to 5 price bands and full control over quantities and prices. The presenter's example uses three bands: $19.99 per seat per month for the first 20 seats, $13.99 for seats 21–40, and $10.99 for seat 41 and above, so a 50-seat purchase brings the average cost per seat down about 20% from the base price, incentivizing buyers to cover larger groups and consolidate purchasing.

For purchasing and seat management, **volume purchasing** has Apple Business/School Manager display the subscriptions and handle the purchase, so you only need to make the subscription available to organizations; **group purchases** require your own in-app UI to trigger the **StoreKit 2** purchase flow, passing in the requested seat count. After purchase, volume purchasing lets the organization assign seats via a device management service, while group purchases generate an **invitation link** for the initial purchaser to share. A built-in seat management system handles invitation links, acceptance/assignment tracking, and lifecycle events like cancellations by default; if you already have your own system, you can integrate custom invitation flows and query group membership through new **App Store Server API** endpoints.

deepdive_en.title: Introduction
deepdive_en.body: **Andrew** from Apple's commerce team explains that subscriptions are a great way to deliver continuous value, but subscribers sometimes want their social group, team, or company on the app. Apple introduces two paths to purchase and manage: **Group Purchases** within the app (like an in-app purchase today, but buying multiple seats and sharing an invite link), and **volume purchasing** through **Apple Business Manager** and **Apple School Manager**, where organizations assign seats at scale via a device management service using the same workflows they use to distribute apps.

deepdive_en.title: Availability
deepdive_en.body: These options apply to all auto-renewable subscriptions using **StoreKit 2** and are on by default for most new and existing subscriptions; if **Family Sharing** is enabled they are opted-out by default so you control how both coexist. In **App Store Connect** you can adjust this, for example making a subscription available only on **Apple School Manager** to price for verified educational institutions, or turning off selling to groups and organizations entirely (while still selling to individuals).

deepdive_en.title: Pricing
deepdive_en.body: By default every seat sells at the current price; to offer bulk discounts you can use the new **volume pricing** with up to 5 price bands and full control over quantity thresholds and prices. The presenter demonstrates three bands: **$19.99** per seat per month for the first 20 seats, **$13.99** for seats 21–40, and **$10.99** for seat 41 and above; for a 50-seat purchase the average per-seat cost drops about **20%** from the base price, encouraging buyers to cover larger groups and consolidate purchasing, all configured in App Store Connect.

deepdive_en.title: Purchasing
deepdive_en.body: **volume purchasing** has Apple Business/School Manager display the subscriptions and handle the purchase, so you just need to make the subscription available to organizations. **group purchases** require building your own in-app UI to trigger the **StoreKit 2** purchase flow, highlighting the value of a group purchase during merchandising, then getting the customer's requested seat count and passing it into the StoreKit 2 purchase request.

deepdive_en.title: Seat Management
deepdive_en.body: After purchase, **volume purchasing** lets the organization assign seats via a device management service the same way they assign apps, ideal for large scale and ensuring org ownership; **group purchases** generate an **invitation link** for the initial purchaser to share. When assignments complete from either type, the App Store assigns a transaction for each member so you can grant them access.

deepdive_en.title: Next steps
deepdive_en.body: The default built-in seat management system handles invitation link generation, member acceptance and assignment tracking, and lifecycle management like cancellations; if you already have your own invitation and member system, you can integrate custom invitation flows via new **App Store Server API** endpoints and use group management endpoints to query all groups a customer is in and all members in a group. The presenter closes by urging developers to move to **StoreKit 2** (a requirement) and to reconsider availability, pricing strategy, and collaborative experiences they could add.

title: Supercharge your spatial workflows with Reality Composer Pro 3
gloss: 用 Reality Composer Pro 3 強化你的空間工作流
takeaway: 完全在 Reality Composer Pro 3 內就能用 Animation Graph、Behavior Tree、Script Graph、Navigation Mesh、Compute Graph 與強化的 Shader Graph 打造豐富互動與視覺效果。

points.text: **完全在 Reality Composer Pro 內**就能打造豐富互動與絢麗視覺效果,不必離開編輯器。
**Animation Graph 與 Behavior Tree** 讓你以視覺化方式編排動畫與行為邏輯。
**Script Graph** 提供節點式腳本,搭配 **Navigation Mesh** 處理空間中的移動與尋路。
新增 **Compute Graph**,可在編輯器內做運算密集的處理。
**Shader Graph 強化**,提升材質與視覺效果的表現力。

audience: **想完全在 Reality Composer Pro 3 內完成互動、動畫與視覺效果的 visionOS 創作者與開發者。**
gloss_en: Supercharge your spatial workflows with Reality Composer Pro 3
takeaway_en: Build rich interactivity and stunning visual effects entirely within Reality Composer Pro 3 using Animation Graph, Behavior Tree, Script Graph, Navigation Mesh, Compute Graph, and an enhanced Shader Graph.

points_en.text: Build rich interactivity and stunning visual effects **entirely within Reality Composer Pro**, without leaving the editor.
**Animation Graph and Behavior Tree** let you orchestrate animation and behavior logic visually.
**Script Graph** provides node-based scripting, paired with **Navigation Mesh** for movement and pathfinding in space.
Adds **Compute Graph**, enabling compute-intensive processing within the editor.
